DEFINITION: alpha; the first letter of the Greek alphabet.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first.
USAGE: Alpha. Often used (usually an, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from aneu) in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of hama).

BDAG.en: Alpha (the first letter of the Greek alphabet).
BDAG.pt: Alfa (a primeira letra do alfabeto grego).

DEFINITION: Aaron, son of Amram and Jochebed, brother of Moses.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Aharown); Aaron, the brother of Moses.

DEFINITION: Abaddon, Destroyer (i.e. Destroying Angel) or place of destruction (personified).
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('abaddown); a destroying angel.

DEFINITION: not burdensome, bringing no weight or oppression upon.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and baros; weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome.

DEFINITION: Abba, father.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin ('ab); father as a vocative.

DEFINITION: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Hebel); Abel, the son of Adam.

DEFINITION: Abijah, (a) a king, son of Rehoboam, (b) founder of the eighth class of priests.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Abiyah); Abijah, the name of two Israelites.

DEFINITION: Abiathar, a priest in King David's time.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Ebyathar); Abiathar, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: the Abilenian territory, the territory of Abila (in Syria), a small principality in the mountains of Damascus.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (compare 'abel); Abilene, a region of Syria.

DEFINITION: Abiud, son of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Abiyhuwd); Abihud, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: Abraham, progenitor of the Hebrew race.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Abraham); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch.
USAGE: Abraham. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.)

BDAG.en: Abraham; patriarch of Israel, bearer of the promise, friend of God, and model of faith.
BDAG.pt: Abraão; patriarca de Israel, portador da promessa, amigo de Deus e modelo de fé.

DEFINITION: the abyss, unfathomable depth, an especially Jewish conception, the home of the dead and of evil spirits.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a variation of buthos; depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss".

BDAG.en: immense depth, abyss; a transcendent place associated with the dead and hostile powers, netherworld, abode of the dead, dungeon.
BDAG.pt: profundidade imensa, abismo; um lugar transcendente associado aos mortos e poderes hostis, submundo, morada dos mortos, masmorra.

DEFINITION: Agabus, a Christian prophet.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (compare Chagab); Agabus, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Agabus, a Christian prophet from Judea.
BDAG.pt: Ágabo, um profeta cristão da Judeia.

DEFINITION: to work that which is good, perform good deeds.
ORIGIN: From agathos and ergon; to work good.

BDAG.en: to do that which benefits others, do good, confer benefits.
BDAG.pt: fazer o que beneficia os outros, fazer o bem, conferir benefícios.

DEFINITION: to do that which is good.
ORIGIN: From agathopoios; to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty).

BDAG.en: to do that which is beneficial to another, do good, be benevolent, be helpful; to meet a high level of exemplary conduct, do what is right, be a good citizen.
BDAG.pt: fazer o que é benéfico para o outro, fazer o bem, ser benevolente, ser prestativo; atingir um alto nível de conduta exemplar, fazer o que é certo, ser um bom cidadão.

DEFINITION: the doing of that which is good, well-doing.
ORIGIN: From agathopoios; well-doing, i.e. Virtue.

BDAG.en: engagement in doing what is good, doing good as a mark of exceptional merit.
BDAG.pt: empenho na prática do bem, fazer o bem como marca de mérito excepcional.

DEFINITION: a doer of that which is good.
ORIGIN: From agathos and poieo; a well-doer, i.e. Virtuous.

BDAG.en: beneficent, doing good, upright; as a substantive, one who does good, is a good citizen.
BDAG.pt: benéfico, fazendo o bem, íntegro; como substantivo, aquele que faz o bem, é um bom cidadão.

DEFINITION: intrinsically good, good in nature, good whether it be seen to be so or not, the widest and most colorless of all words with this meaning.
ORIGIN: A primary word; "good" (in any sense, often as noun).
USAGE: benefit, good(-s, things), well. Compare kalos.

BDAG.en: good, useful, beneficial, kind, generous, upright; also used as a substantive for 'the good', 'good things', 'possessions', 'benefactions', or 'good deeds'.
BDAG.pt: bom, útil, benéfico, bondoso, generoso, íntegro; também usado como substantivo para 'o bem', 'coisas boas', 'possessões', 'benefícios' ou 'boas ações'.

DEFINITION: intrinsic goodness, especially as a personal quality, with stress on the kindly (rather than the righteous) side of goodness.
ORIGIN: From agathos; goodness, i.e. Virtue or beneficence.

BDAG.en: positive moral quality characterized especially by interest in the welfare of others; goodness, generosity.
BDAG.pt: qualidade moral positiva caracterizada especialmente pelo interesse no bem-estar dos outros; bondade, generosidade.

DEFINITION: wild joy, ecstatic delight, exultation, exhilaration.
ORIGIN: From agalliao; exultation; specially, welcome.

BDAG.en: exultation, joy, gladness; a piercing exclamation of joy.
BDAG.pt: exultação, alegria, júbilo; uma exclamação vibrante de alegria.

DEFINITION: to exult, rejoice greatly.
ORIGIN: From agan (much) and hallomai; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. Exult.
USAGE: be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly).

BDAG.en: to be exceedingly joyful, exult, be glad, overjoyed
BDAG.pt: estar extremamente alegre, exultar, regozijar-se, estar cheio de alegria

DEFINITION: unmarried, of a person not in a state of wedlock, whether he or she has formerly been married or not.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and gamos; unmarried.

BDAG.en: unmarried man or woman
BDAG.pt: solteiro, não casado (referente a homem ou mulher)

DEFINITION: to grieve much, to be indignant.
ORIGIN: From agan (much) and achthos (grief; akin to the base of agkale); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant.
USAGE: be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation.

BDAG.en: be indignant against what is assumed to be wrong, be aroused, indignant, angry
BDAG.pt: ficar indignado contra o que se presume estar errado, sentir-se ofendido, indignado ou zangado

DEFINITION: feeling of anger, indignation, vexation.
ORIGIN: From aganakteo; indignation.

BDAG.en: indignation.
BDAG.pt: indignação.

DEFINITION: to love, wish well to, take pleasure in, long for; denotes the love of reason, esteem.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from agan (much); to love (in a social or moral sense).

BDAG.en: to have a warm regard for and interest in another, cherish, have affection for, love; to have high esteem for or satisfaction with something, to take pleasure in, long for, or wish for; to practice or express love, prove one’s love.
BDAG.pt: ter um profundo apreço e interesse por outro, estimar, ter afeição, amar; ter alta estima ou satisfação com algo, ter prazer em, desejar ou querer; praticar ou expressar amor, provar o amor de alguém.

DEFINITION: love, benevolence, good will, esteem; plur: love-feasts.
ORIGIN: From agapao; love, i.e. Affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast.

BDAG.en: The quality of warm regard for and interest in another; esteem, affection, regard, love (without limitation to very intimate relationships, and very seldom in general Greek of sexual attraction). Also, a common meal eaten by early Christians for fostering mutual affection and concern; a fellowship meal, a love-feast (agape).
BDAG.pt: A qualidade de consideração calorosa e interesse pelo outro; estima, afeição, consideração, amor (sem limitação a relacionamentos muito íntimos, e muito raramente no grego geral de atração sexual). Também, uma refeição comum comida pelos primeiros cristãos para fomentar a afeição e preocupação mútua; uma refeição de comunhão, uma festa do amor (ágape).

DEFINITION: loved, beloved, with two special applications: the Beloved, a title of the Messiah (Christ), as beloved beyond all others by the God who sent Him; of Christians, as beloved by God, Christ, and one another.
ORIGIN: From agapao; beloved.

BDAG.en: Pertaining to one who is in a very special relationship with another; only, only beloved (especially in reference to an only son). Also, pertaining to one who is dearly loved, dear, beloved, prized, valued (indicating a close relationship, such as between parent and child).
BDAG.pt: Relacionado a alguém que está em um relacionamento muito especial com outro; único, unigênito, amado (especialmente em referência a um filho único). Também, relacionado a alguém que é muito querido, amado, prezado, valorizado (indicando um relacionamento próximo, como entre pais e filhos).

DEFINITION: Hagar, the servant of Sarah, concubine of Abraham.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Hagar); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham.

BDAG.en: Hagar, a concubine of Abraham, mother of Ishmael; taken allegorically by Paul as a type of Judaism.
BDAG.pt: Agar, uma concubina de Abraão, mãe de Ismael; tomada alegoricamente por Paulo como um tipo do Judaísmo.

DEFINITION: to impress (into service), send (on an errand).
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (compare 'iggra'); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service.

BDAG.en: To requisition or press into service; to force or compel someone to perform a task (originally of the official post).
BDAG.pt: Requisitar ou recrutar para serviço obrigatório; forçar ou compelir alguém a realizar uma tarefa (originalmente referente ao serviço postal oficial).

DEFINITION: a vessel, flask.
ORIGIN: From aggos (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of agkale); a receptacle.

BDAG.en: vessel, flask, container; figuratively, the body as the home of spirits.
BDAG.pt: vaso, frasco, recipiente; figurativamente, o corpo como morada de espíritos.

DEFINITION: a message.
ORIGIN: From aggelos; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept.

BDAG.en: A message, good news; an instruction or directive.
BDAG.pt: Mensagem, boa notícia; uma instrução ou diretriz.

DEFINITION: a messenger, generally a (supernatural) messenger from God, an angel, conveying news or behests from God to men.
ORIGIN: From aggello (probably derived from ago; compare agele) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor.

BDAG.en: messenger; an envoy, one who is sent; a transcendent power who carries out various missions or tasks, an angel, a spirit-being; an evil spirit.
BDAG.pt: mensageiro; um enviado, alguém que é mandado; um poder transcendente que executa várias missões ou tarefas, um anjo, um ser espiritual; um espírito maligno.

DEFINITION: come!.
ORIGIN: Imperative of ago; properly, lead, i.e. Come on.

BDAG.en: present impv. of ἄγω, used as an interjection, come!
BDAG.pt: imperativo presente de ἄγω, usado como interjeição: vem!, vinde!

DEFINITION: a flock, herd.
ORIGIN: From ago (compare aggelos); a drove.

BDAG.en: herd (usually of swine)
BDAG.pt: manada, rebanho (geralmente de porcos)

DEFINITION: of unrecorded genealogy, whose descent cannot be traced.
ORIGIN: From a (as negative particle) and genealogeo; unregistered as to birth.

BDAG.en: without genealogy, of Melchizedek (with 'without father' and 'without mother').
BDAG.pt: sem genealogia, referente a Melquisedeque (com 'sem pai' e 'sem mãe').

DEFINITION: lit: without family, hence: ignoble, base.
ORIGIN: From a (as negative particle) and genos; properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble.

BDAG.en: not of noble birth (ignobilis), but also in the more general sense base, low, insignificant.
BDAG.pt: não de nascimento nobre (ignóbil), mas também no sentido mais geral: baixo, humilde, insignificante.

DEFINITION: to make holy, treat as holy, set apart as holy, sanctify, hallow, purify.
ORIGIN: From hagios; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate.

BDAG.en: To set aside something or make it suitable for ritual purposes, consecrate, dedicate. To include a person in the inner circle of what is holy, consecrate, dedicate, sanctify, often by baptism or sacrifice; to dedicate oneself as an offering. To treat as holy, reverence. To purify, eliminating what is incompatible with holiness.
BDAG.pt: Separar algo ou torná-lo adequado para propósitos rituais, consagrar, dedicar. Incluir uma pessoa no círculo íntimo do que é sagrado, consagrar, dedicar, santificar, muitas vezes por batismo ou sacrifício; dedicar-se como oferta. Tratar como sagrado, reverenciar. Purificar, eliminando o que é incompatível com a santidade.

DEFINITION: the process of making or becoming holy, set apart, sanctification, holiness, consecration.
ORIGIN: From hagiazo; properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier.

BDAG.en: personal dedication to the interests of the deity, holiness, consecration, sanctification; the use in a moral sense for a process or, more often, its result (the state of being made holy) is peculiar to our literature.
BDAG.pt: dedicação pessoal aos interesses da divindade, santidade, consagração, santificação; o uso em sentido moral para um processo ou, mais frequentemente, seu resultado (o estado de ser feito santo) é peculiar à nossa literatura.

DEFINITION: holy place, sanctuary.
ORIGIN: Neuter of hagios; a sacred thing (i.e. Spot).

BDAG.en: That which is holy; a holy thing (e.g., sacrificial meat); sanctuary.
BDAG.pt: Aquilo que é santo; uma coisa santa (ex: carne sacrificial); santuário.

DEFINITION: set apart by (or for) God, holy, sacred.
ORIGIN: From hagos (an awful thing) (compare hagnos, thalpo); sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated).

BDAG.en: Originally a cultic concept: of the quality possessed by things and persons that could approach a divinity. As an adjective, pertaining to being dedicated or consecrated to the service of God; in a cultic sense, dedicated to God, holy, sacred, reserved for God and God's service (of things and places). Also used of human beings consecrated to God, holy, pure, reverent (prophets, apostles, Christians, etc.), and of transcendent beings (angels), of Christ, and of God.
BDAG.pt: Originalmente um conceito cúltico: da qualidade possuída por coisas e pessoas que podiam se aproximar de uma divindade. Como adjetivo, pertinente a ser dedicado ou consagrado ao serviço de Deus; em sentido cúltico, dedicado a Deus, santo, sagrado, reservado para Deus e Seu serviço (de coisas e lugares). Também usado para seres humanos consagrados a Deus, santos, puros, reverentes (profetas, apóstolos, cristãos, etc.), e para seres transcendentais (anjos), de Cristo e de Deus.

DEFINITION: holiness, sanctity, as an abstract quality.
ORIGIN: From hagios; sanctity (i.e. Properly, the state).

BDAG.en: Holiness; the quality of being holy, moral purity, holy character.
BDAG.pt: Santidade; a qualidade de ser santo, pureza moral, caráter santo.

DEFINITION: a holy or sanctified state.
ORIGIN: From hagios; sacredness (i.e. Properly, the quality).

BDAG.en: Holiness; a state of being holy or perfected in holiness.
BDAG.pt: Santidade; um estado de ser santo ou aperfeiçoado em santidade.

DEFINITION: an arm, especially as bent to receive a burden.
ORIGIN: From agkos (a bend, "ache"); an arm (as curved).

BDAG.en: the arm bent as to receive someth., arm; to take into one’s arms.
BDAG.pt: o braço dobrado para receber algo, braço; tomar nos braços.

DEFINITION: a fish-hook.
ORIGIN: From the same as agkale; a hook (as bent).

BDAG.en: Fishhook; also figuratively, something that entangles or ensnares, like the 'fishhooks of error'.
BDAG.pt: Anzol; também figurativamente, algo que emaranha ou prende, como os 'anzóis do erro'.

DEFINITION: an anchor.
ORIGIN: From the same as agkale; an "anchor" (as crooked).

BDAG.en: anchor; used literally of a ship's anchor and figuratively of hope
BDAG.pt: âncora; usado literalmente para a âncora de um navio e figuradamente para a esperança

DEFINITION: uncarded, undressed.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and the same as gnapheus; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth).

BDAG.en: pert. to cloth fresh from the weaver’s loom, not fulled, unshrunken, unsized, new.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a tecido fresco do tear do tecelão, não batido, não encolhido, não engomado, novo.

DEFINITION: purity, chastity.
ORIGIN: From hagnos; cleanliness (the quality), i.e. (specially) chastity.

BDAG.en: The quality of moral purity, purity; of a pure mind, specifically chastity.
BDAG.pt: A qualidade de pureza moral, pureza; de uma mente pura, especificamente castidade.

DEFINITION: to cleanse, purify, either ceremonially, actually, or morally.
ORIGIN: From hagnos; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally).

BDAG.en: to purify or cleanse and so make acceptable for cultic use, purify; to cause to be morally pure, purify; to set oneself apart in dedication, to dedicate oneself.
BDAG.pt: purificar ou limpar e assim tornar aceitável para uso cultual, purificar; tornar moralmente puro, purificar; separar-se em dedicação, dedicar-se.

DEFINITION: (ceremonial) purification.
ORIGIN: From hagnizo; a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration.

BDAG.en: the process of making someth. cultically acceptable, purification; the process of being morally purified, purification.
BDAG.pt: o processo de tornar algo cultualmente aceitável, purificação; o processo de ser moralmente purificado, purificação.

DEFINITION: to not know, be ignorant of (a person, thing, or fact), sometimes with the idea of willful ignorance.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and noieo; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination).
USAGE: (be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown.

BDAG.en: to be uninformed about, not to know, be ignorant (of); to pay little or no attention to, not to recognize, disregard, ignore; to fail to understand; to be unaware about one’s wrongdoing, lapse/do wrong/sin unintentionally.
BDAG.pt: estar desinformado sobre, não saber, ser ignorante (de); dar pouca ou nenhuma atenção, não reconhecer, desconsiderar, ignorar; não conseguir entender; não ter consciência de sua má conduta, falhar/agir mal/pecar involuntariamente.

DEFINITION: an offence committed through ignorance, an error due to (willful or culpable) ignorance.
ORIGIN: From agnoeo; a thing ignored, i.e. Shortcoming.

BDAG.en: a sin committed in ignorance or unintentionally
BDAG.pt: um pecado cometido em ignorância ou de forma não intencional

DEFINITION: ignorance, inadvertence, sometimes with the idea of willful blindness.
ORIGIN: From agnoeo; ignorance (properly, the quality).

BDAG.en: lack of information about someth., ignorance; spec. lack of information that may result in reprehensible conduct, ignorance, unawareness, lack of discernment; almost equivalent to sin (unintentional moral lapses).
BDAG.pt: falta de informação sobre algo, ignorância; especificamente falta de informação que pode resultar em conduta repreensível, ignorância, falta de consciência, falta de discernimento; quase equivalente a pecado (falhas morais involuntárias).

DEFINITION: (originally, in a condition prepared for worship), pure (either ethically, or ritually, ceremonially), chaste.
ORIGIN: From the same as hagios; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect.

BDAG.en: pure, holy; originally a cultic attribute of divinity, later transferred to a moral sense; chaste, innocent.
BDAG.pt: puro, santo; originalmente um atributo cúltico da divindade, posteriormente transferido para um sentido moral; casto, inocente.

DEFINITION: purity, chastity.
ORIGIN: From hagnos; cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively) blamelessness.

BDAG.en: purity, sincerity.
BDAG.pt: pureza, sinceridade.

DEFINITION: purely, sincerely, with pure motives, honestly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from hagnos; purely, i.e. Honestly.

BDAG.en: purely, sincerely; not from mixed motives.
BDAG.pt: puramente, sinceramente; sem segundas intenções.

DEFINITION: ignorance; specifically: willful ignorance.
ORIGIN: From a (as negative particle) and gnosis; ignorance (properly, the state).

BDAG.en: ignorance, specifically a lack of religious experience or spiritual discernment; ignorant talk
BDAG.pt: ignorância, especificamente falta de experiência religiosa ou discernimento espiritual; fala ignorante

DEFINITION: unknown, unknowable.
ORIGIN: From a (as negative particle) and gnostos; unknown.

BDAG.en: unknown, pertaining to that which is unknown due to lack of information
BDAG.pt: desconhecido, pertencente àquilo que não se conhece por falta de informação

DEFINITION: market-place, forum, public place of assembly.
ORIGIN: From ageiro (to gather; probably akin to egeiro); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare.

BDAG.en: market place; the center of public life, a scene of public events and lawsuits.
BDAG.pt: praça do mercado; mercado, o centro da vida pública e local de eventos públicos e processos judiciais.

DEFINITION: to buy in the marketplace, purchase.
ORIGIN: From agora; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem.

BDAG.en: to buy or purchase; to secure the rights to someone by paying a price, acquire as property (especially of believers for whom Christ paid the price with his blood).
BDAG.pt: comprar ou adquirir; assegurar os direitos sobre alguém mediante o pagamento de um preço, adquirir como propriedade (especialmente em relação aos crentes por quem Cristo pagou o preço com seu sangue).

DEFINITION: a lounger in the market-place, perhaps with the idea of agitator.
ORIGIN: From agora; relating to the market-place, i.e. Forensic (times); by implication, vulgar.

BDAG.en: pertaining to a market; as a noun: market people, rabble; court days or legal sessions.
BDAG.pt: referente ao mercado; como substantivo: gente do mercado, turba ou plebe; dias de tribunal ou sessões judiciais.

DEFINITION: catching, a catch.
ORIGIN: From ago; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish).

BDAG.en: the act of catching or hunting; that which is caught, a catch.
BDAG.pt: o ato de apanhar, pescar ou caçar; aquilo que é pego, uma captura ou presa.

DEFINITION: unlettered, illiterate, uneducated, perhaps with the narrower idea: unacquainted with Rabbinic teaching.
ORIGIN: From a (as negative particle) and gramma; unlettered, i.e. Illiterate.

BDAG.en: unable to write, illiterate, uneducated; lacking in legal or formal proficiency.
BDAG.pt: analfabeto, sem instrução, incapaz de escrever; sem proficiência formal ou jurídica.

DEFINITION: to spend the night in the open, bivouac.
ORIGIN: From agros and auleo (in the sense of aule); to camp out.

BDAG.en: to live out of doors, to live in the open field (especially of shepherds).
BDAG.pt: viver ao ar livre, habitar no campo (especialmente referente a pastores).

DEFINITION: to catch, take by hunting.
ORIGIN: From agra; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap.

BDAG.en: to catch; figuratively: to catch someone unawares or trap them in a statement.
BDAG.pt: apanhar, caçar; figuradamente: apanhar alguém desprevenido ou enredar alguém em uma declaração.

DEFINITION: a wild olive tree, oleaster.
ORIGIN: From agrios and elaia; an oleaster.

BDAG.en: a wild olive tree; pertaining to or growing from a wild olive tree.
BDAG.pt: oliveira brava; referente a ou proveniente de uma oliveira brava.

DEFINITION: living in the fields, wild, savage, fierce.
ORIGIN: From agros; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce).

BDAG.en: Pertaining to a natural state, wild (of plants, animals); wild in appearance (of persons); untamed, uncontrolled, savage, fierce (of desires); cruelty; stormy (of natural phenomena).
BDAG.pt: Relativo a um estado natural, selvagem (de plantas, animais); de aparência selvagem (de pessoas); indomado, descontrolado, selvagem, feroz (de desejos); crueldade; tempestuoso (de fenómenos naturais).

DEFINITION: Agrippa, the name of two descendant of Herod the Great.
ORIGIN: Apparently from agrios and hippos; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods.

BDAG.en: Agrippa, name of various political figures, specifically Herod Agrippa I and Herod Agrippa II.
BDAG.pt: Agripa, nome de várias figuras políticas, especificamente Herodes Agripa I e Herodes Agripa II.

DEFINITION: a field, especially as bearing a crop; the country, lands, property in land, a country estate.
ORIGIN: From ago; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. Hamlet.
USAGE: country, farm, piece of ground, land.

BDAG.en: field, land, countryside; open country as opposed to city; property used for farming purposes, farm, estate; arable land
BDAG.pt: campo, terra, zona rural; campo aberto em contraste com a cidade; propriedade agrícola, fazenda, herdade; terra cultivável

DEFINITION: to be not asleep, be awake; especially: to be watchful, careful.
ORIGIN: Ultimately from a (as negative particle) and hupnos; to be sleepless, i.e. Keep awake.

BDAG.en: to keep oneself awake, be awake; to be vigilant, alert, or on guard against peril; to be alertly concerned about, look after, care for
BDAG.pt: manter-se acordado, estar desperto; ser vigilante, estar alerta ou em guarda contra o perigo; preocupar-se atentamente, cuidar de, zelar por

DEFINITION: the state of being awake (at night), sleeplessness, watching.
ORIGIN: From agrupneo; sleeplessness, i.e. A keeping awake.

BDAG.en: Sleeplessness; the state of being alertly concerned, care (figurative extension).

DEFINITION: brotherhood (in the collective sense), the members of the Christian Church, Christendom.

DEFINITION: unceasing, unremitting.

DEFINITION: lavishness, lavish generosity, abundance, bounty.

USAGE: could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak.

DEFINITION: Athenian, belonging to Athens.

DEFINITION: to engage, compete, in an (athletic) contest.

BDAG.pt: torneio, luta (figurativamente falando de tentações e sofrimentos)

DEFINITION: to lose heart, be despondent, be disheartened.

BDAG.pt: ficar desanimado a ponto de perder a motivação, ficar desalentado, perder o ânimo, ficar desmoralizado

DEFINITION: (sometimes: unpunished), guiltless, innocent.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of tithemi (meaning a penalty); not guilty.

BDAG.en: innocent; be innocent of (something)

DEFINITION: of a goat.
ORIGIN: From aix (a goat); belonging to a goat.

DEFINITION: sea-coast, (sandy) beach; shore (of sea or lake), land.

DEFINITION: Egyptian.

DEFINITION: Egypt, the land of the Nile.

DEFINITION: eternal, everlasting.

BDAG.pt: eterno

DEFINITION: a sense of shame.

DEFINITION: an Ethiopian, Abyssinian.
ORIGIN: From aitho (to scorch) and ops (the face, from optanomai); an Æthiopian (as a blackamoor).

BDAG.en: Ethiopian
BDAG.pt: etíope

DEFINITION: blood (especially as shed).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred.

BDAG.pt: sangue (como componente básico de um organismo; constituindo a vida de um indivíduo, sangue vital; a cor vermelha (apocalíptica) que indica desastre)

DEFINITION: Aeneas, a paralytic cured by Peter.

DEFINITION: a riddle, an enigma.

BDAG.pt: aquilo que requer agudeza especial para entender porque é expresso de maneira enigmática, enigma; modo indireto de comunicação

DEFINITION: praise (noun).

BDAG.en: praise

DEFINITION: to perceive, understand.
