ORIGIN: From aischros and kerdos (gain); sordid.

BDAG.en: shamelessly greedy for money, avaricious, fond of dishonest gain.
BDAG.pt: descaradamente ávido por dinheiro, avarento, afeiçoado a ganhos desonestos.

DEFINITION: greedily, in a spirit of eagerness for base gain.
ORIGIN: Adverb from aischrokerdes; sordidly.

BDAG.en: in fondness for dishonest gain, greedily.
BDAG.pt: em afeição a ganhos desonestos, avidamente.

DEFINITION: filthy speech, foul language.
ORIGIN: From aischros and logos; vile conversation.

BDAG.en: speech of a kind that is generally considered in poor taste, obscene speech, dirty talk; scurrilous talk.
BDAG.pt: fala de um tipo geralmente considerada de mau gosto, fala obscena, linguagem suja; conversa difamatória.

DEFINITION: shame.
ORIGIN: Neuter of aischros; a shameful thing, i.e. Indecorum.

DEFINITION: base, disgraceful.
ORIGIN: From the same as aischunomai; shameful, i.e. Base (specially, venal).

BDAG.en: pert. to being socially or morally unacceptable, shameful, base; disgraceful.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser social ou moralmente inaceitável, vergonhoso, vil; vergonhoso.

DEFINITION: obscenity, indecency, baseness.
ORIGIN: From aischros; shamefulness, i.e. Obscenity.

BDAG.en: behavior that flouts social and moral standards, shamefulness, obscenity.
BDAG.pt: comportamento que desafia os padrões sociais e morais, vergonha, obscenidade.

DEFINITION: shame, shamefacedness, shameful deeds.
ORIGIN: From aischunomai; shame or disgrace (abstractly or concretely).

BDAG.en: a sensitivity respecting possibility of dishonor, modesty, shame (a feeling that one has); an experience of ignominy that comes to someone, shame, disgrace; commission of something shameful, a shameful deed.
BDAG.pt: uma sensibilidade em relação à possibilidade de desonra, modéstia, vergonha (um sentimento que se tem); uma experiência de ignomínia que acontece a alguém, vergonha, desgraça; comissão de algo vergonhoso, um ato vergonhoso.

DEFINITION: to be ashamed, be put to shame.
ORIGIN: From aischos (disfigurement, i.e. Disgrace); to feel shame (for oneself).

DEFINITION: to ask, request, petition, demand.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; to ask (in genitive case).
USAGE: ask, beg, call for, crave, desire, require. Compare punthanomai.

BDAG.en: to ask for, with a claim on receipt of an answer, ask, ask for, demand; to request something from someone.
BDAG.pt: pedir, com direito a receber uma resposta, pedir, solicitar, exigir; pedir algo a alguém.

DEFINITION: a petition, request.
ORIGIN: From aiteo; a thing asked or (abstractly) an asking.

BDAG.en: request
BDAG.pt: pedido, requerimento

DEFINITION: a cause, reason, excuse; a charge, accusation; guilt; circumstances, case.
ORIGIN: From the same as aiteo; a cause (as if asked for), i.e. (logical) reason (motive, matter), (legal) crime (alleged or proved).

BDAG.en: 1 that which is responsible for a condition, cause, reason; 2 the actual state of affairs, case, circumstance, relationship; 3 a basis for legal action, legal t.t. a charge, ground for complaint
BDAG.pt: 1 aquilo que é responsável por uma condição, causa, razão; 2 o estado real das coisas, caso, circunstância, relacionamento; 3 uma base para ação legal, uma acusação, motivo de queixa

DEFINITION: a charge, accusation.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of aitia; a thing charged.

BDAG.en: charge, complaint
BDAG.pt: acusação, queixa

DEFINITION: cause, crime, guilt, criminality.
ORIGIN: Neuter of aitios; a reason or crime (like aitia).

DEFINITION: the cause, author; the culprit, the accused; the crime.
ORIGIN: From the same as aiteo; causative, i.e. (concretely) a causer.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being the cause of someth., in our lit. only subst. a the one who is the cause, source; b neut. cause, reason; 2 ground for legal action.
BDAG.pt: 1 pertencente a ser a causa de algo, apenas em nosso texto como substantivo: a quem é a causa, fonte; b neutro causa, razão; 2 base para ação legal.

DEFINITION: unexpected, sudden.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and phaino (compare exaiphnes) (meaning non-apparent); unexpected, i.e. (adverbially) suddenly.

BDAG.en: sudden
BDAG.pt: súbito, repentino

DEFINITION: captivity; a captive multitude.
ORIGIN: From aichmalotos; captivity.

BDAG.en: 1 state of captivity, captivity, mostly in war; 2 abstr. for concr. a captured military force, prisoners of war, captives
BDAG.pt: 1 estado de cativeiro, cativeiro, principalmente em guerra; 2 abstrato para concreto: uma força militar capturada, prisioneiros de guerra, cativos

DEFINITION: to take captive, captivate.
ORIGIN: From aichmalotos; to capture (like aichmalotizo).

BDAG.en: to capture in war, capture, take captive, fig.
BDAG.pt: capturar em guerra, capturar, levar cativo, figurativamente

DEFINITION: to take captive (in war); to subdue, ensnare.
ORIGIN: From aichmalotos; to make captive.
USAGE: lead away captive, bring into captivity.

BDAG.en: 1 to cause someone to become a prisoner of war a lit. take captive; b fig. make captive; 2 gain control of, in which case connotes carry away=mislead, deceive
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer com que alguém se torne prisioneiro de guerra: capturar literalmente; b figurativamente: tornar cativo; 2 tomar controle de, no qual conota levar embora = enganar, iludir

DEFINITION: a captive (in war), a prisoner.
ORIGIN: From aichme (a spear) and a derivative of the same as halosis; properly, a prisoner of war, i.e. (genitive case) a captive.

BDAG.en: captive
BDAG.pt: cativo

DEFINITION: an age, a cycle (of time), especially of the present age as contrasted with the future age, and of one of a series of ages stretching to infinity.
ORIGIN: From the same as aei; properly, an age; by extension, perpetuity (also past); by implication, the world; specially (Jewish) a Messianic period (present or future).
USAGE: age, course, eternal, (for) ever(-more), (n-)ever, (beginning of the, while the) world (began, without end). Compare chronos.

BDAG.en: a long period of time, the past, earliest times; time to come (eternity); the world as a spatial concept; a segment of time as a particular unit of history, age (present age, age to come)
BDAG.pt: um longo período de tempo, o passado, tempos mais antigos; tempo futuro (eternidade); o mundo como conceito espacial; um segmento de tempo como unidade particular da história, era (era presente, era vindoura)

DEFINITION: age-long, and therefore: practically eternal, unending; partaking of the character of that which lasts for an age, as contrasted with that which is brief and fleeting.
ORIGIN: From aion; perpetual (also used of past time, or past and future as well).

BDAG.en: eternal, pertaining to a long period of time, or unending duration
BDAG.pt: eterno, pertencente a um longo período de tempo ou duração sem fim

DEFINITION: uncleanness, impurity.
ORIGIN: From akathartos; impurity (the quality), physically or morally.

BDAG.en: uncleanness, filth, moral corruption, vileness (especially sexual sins)
BDAG.pt: imundície, sujeira, corrupção moral, vileza (especialmente pecados sexuais)

DEFINITION: filthiness.
ORIGIN: From akathartos; impurity (the state), morally.

BDAG.en: uncleanness (a rare reading/form)
BDAG.pt: imundície (uma leitura/forma rara)

DEFINITION: unclean, impure.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of kathairo (meaning cleansed); impure (ceremonially, morally (lewd) or specially, (demonic)).

BDAG.en: impure, unclean (cultic sense); morally impure, unclean (moral sense)
BDAG.pt: impuro, imundo (sentido cultual); moralmente impuro, sujo (sentido moral)

DEFINITION: to be without a suitable opportunity.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and kairos (meaning unseasonable); to be inopportune (for oneself), i.e. To fail of a proper occasion.

BDAG.en: to lack an opportune time for doing something, have no opportunity, have no time abs.
BDAG.pt: carecer de um momento oportuno para fazer algo, não ter oportunidade, não ter tempo absoluto.

DEFINITION: unseasonably, out of due season, inopportunely.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the same as akaireomai; inopportunely.

BDAG.en: untimely
BDAG.pt: intempestivamente

DEFINITION: innocent, guileless, simple.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and kakos; not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting.

BDAG.en: innocent, guileless
BDAG.pt: inocente, ingênuo.

DEFINITION: a thorn-bush, prickly plant; a thorn.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as akmen; a thorn.

BDAG.en: thorn-plant, common weed (e.g., Ononis spinosa); thornbush
BDAG.pt: planta espinhosa, erva daninha comum; silva espinhosa

DEFINITION: made of thorns.
ORIGIN: From akantha; thorny.

BDAG.en: thorny
BDAG.pt: espinhoso.

DEFINITION: unfruitful, barren, profitless.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and karpos; barren (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: unfruitful, fruitless (literal); useless, unproductive (figurative)
BDAG.pt: não frutífero, infrutífero (literal); inútil, improdutivo (figurado)

DEFINITION: not open to just rebuke; irreprehensible.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of kataginosko; unblamable.

BDAG.en: not condemned, beyond reproach
BDAG.pt: não condenado, irrepreensível.

DEFINITION: unveiled, uncovered.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of kata and kalupto; unveiled.

BDAG.en: uncovered
BDAG.pt: descoberto, sem cobertura

DEFINITION: uncondemned, not yet tried.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of katakrino; without (legal) trial.

BDAG.en: uncondemned, without due process
BDAG.pt: não condenado, sem o devido processo legal.

DEFINITION: indissoluble, that cannot be broken up.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of kataluo; indissoluble, i.e. (figuratively) permanent.

BDAG.en: indestructible, endless
BDAG.pt: indestrutível, sem fim.

DEFINITION: not ceasing from, not abandoning (giving up).
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of katapauo; unrefraining.

BDAG.en: unceasing, restless
BDAG.pt: incessante, inquieto.

DEFINITION: disturbance, upheaval, revolution, almost anarchy, first in the political, and thence in the moral sphere.
ORIGIN: From akatastatos; instability, i.e. Disorder.

BDAG.en: unsettled state of affairs, disturbance, tumult; opposition to established authority, disorder, unruliness
BDAG.pt: estado de coisas instável, perturbação, tumulto; oposição à autoridade estabelecida, desordem, indisciplina.

DEFINITION: unsettled, unstable (though these are hardly strong enough equivalents), almost anarchic.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of kathistemi; inconstant.

BDAG.en: unstable, restless, of vacillating persons
BDAG.pt: instável, inquieto, de pessoas vacilantes.

DEFINITION: unrestrainable, unruly, untamable.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of katecho; unrestrainable.

BDAG.en: uncontrollable
BDAG.pt: incontrolável.

DEFINITION: Hakeldama, a field apparantly located south of the valley of Hinnom.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood; corresponding to kathairesis and exapatao); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem.

DEFINITION: (lit: unmixed) simple, unsophisticated, sincere, blameless.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of kerannumi; unmixed, i.e. (figuratively) innocent.

BDAG.en: pure, innocent
BDAG.pt: puro, inocente.

DEFINITION: unbent, unyielding, resolute, firm.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and klino; not leaning, i.e. (figuratively) firm.

BDAG.en: without wavering
BDAG.pt: sem vacilar.

DEFINITION: to reach maturity, become ripe, be in full vigor.
ORIGIN: From the same as akmen; to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature.

BDAG.en: to bloom (fig. of the best time of life)
BDAG.pt: florescer (figurado para a melhor fase da vida).

DEFINITION: at the present point of time.
ORIGIN: Accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to ake (a point) and meaning the same; adverbially, just now, i.e. Still.

BDAG.en: extension of time up to and beyond a certain point, even yet, still
BDAG.pt: extensão de tempo até e além de um certo ponto, ainda, ainda assim

DEFINITION: hearing, faculty of hearing, ear; report, rumor.
ORIGIN: From akouo; hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard).
USAGE: audience, ear, fame, which ye heard, hearing, preached, report, rumor.

BDAG.en: the faculty of hearing, hearing; the act of hearing, listening; the organ w. which one hears, ear; that which is heard, a fame, report, rumor; account, report, message
BDAG.pt: a faculdade de ouvir, audição; o ato de ouvir, escutar; o órgão com o qual se ouve, ouvido; aquilo que é ouvido, fama, boato, rumor; conta, relatório, mensagem

DEFINITION: to accompany, attend, follow.
ORIGIN: From a (as a particle of union) and keleuthos (a road); properly, to be in the same way with, i.e. To accompany (specially, as a disciple).

BDAG.en: to move behind someone in the same direction, come after; to follow or accompany someone who takes the lead, accompany, go along with; to follow someone as a disciple, be a disciple, follow; to comply with, follow, obey; to come after someth. else in sequence, follow, of things
BDAG.pt: mover-se atrás de alguém na mesma direção, seguir; seguir ou acompanhar alguém que lidera, acompanhar, ir junto; seguir alguém como discípulo, ser discípulo, seguir; cumprir, seguir, obedecer; vir depois de outra coisa em sequência, seguir, de coisas

DEFINITION: to hear, listen, comprehend by hearing; pass: is heard, reported.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to hear (in various senses).
USAGE: give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand.

BDAG.en: hear (as an active faculty); hear something from someone; receive news or information about something, learn about something; give careful attention to, listen to, heed; pay attention to by listening, listen to; be given a nickname or other identifying label, be called; hear and understand a message, understand
BDAG.pt: ouvir (como faculdade ativa); ouvir algo de alguém; receber notícias ou informações sobre algo, tomar conhecimento de algo; prestar atenção cuidadosa, escutar, atender; prestar atenção ouvindo, escutar; receber um apelido ou outro rótulo de identificação, ser chamado; ouvir e entender uma mensagem, compreender

DEFINITION: incontinence, intemperance (in wide sense), lack of restraint.
ORIGIN: From akrates; want of self-restraint.

BDAG.en: lack of self-control, self-indulgence
BDAG.pt: falta de autocontrole, autossatisfação/indulgência

DEFINITION: lacking self-control, powerless, inclined to excess.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and kratos; powerless, i.e. Without self-control.

BDAG.en: without self-control, dissolute
BDAG.pt: sem autocontrole, dissoluto

DEFINITION: unmixed, undiluted, pure.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of kerannumi; undiluted.

BDAG.en: unmixed (of wine); fig. of God’s anger in full strength
BDAG.pt: não misturado (de vinho); fig. de raiva de Deus em plena força

DEFINITION: strictness, accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness.
ORIGIN: From the same as akribestatos; exactness.

BDAG.en: strict conformity to a norm or standard, exactness, precision
BDAG.pt: estrita conformidade a uma norma ou padrão, exatidão, precisão

DEFINITION: most exact, strict.
ORIGIN: Superlative of akribes (a derivative of the same as akron); most exact.

DEFINITION: more perfectly.
ORIGIN: Neuter of the comparative of the same as akribestatos; (adverbially) more exactly.

DEFINITION: to learn carefully, inquire with exactness.
ORIGIN: From the same as akribestatos; to be exact, i.e. Ascertain.

BDAG.en: make detailed inquiry about someth., ascertain precisely/exactly
BDAG.pt: investigar detalhadamente algo, apurar precisamente/exatamente

DEFINITION: carefully, exactly, strictly, distinctly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the same as akribestatos; exactly.

BDAG.en: accurately, carefully, well (pert. to strict conformity to a standard or norm, w. focus on careful attention)
BDAG.pt: com precisão, cuidadosamente, bem (relativo à estrita conformidade a um padrão ou norma, com foco na atenção cuidadosa)

DEFINITION: a locust.
ORIGIN: Apparently from the same as akron; a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation).

BDAG.en: the desert locust: ‘Schistocerca gregaria’; locust, a migratory phase of the grasshopper
BDAG.pt: o gafanhoto do deserto: 'Schistocerca gregaria'; gafanhoto, uma fase migratória do gafanhoto

DEFINITION: auditorium, recitation hall, court room (for hearing cases).
ORIGIN: From akroates; an audience-room.

BDAG.en: audience hall (Lat. auditorium) of the procurator, hall of justice
BDAG.pt: salão de audiências (latim: auditorium) do procurador, salão de justiça

DEFINITION: a hearer of, a listener to.
ORIGIN: From akroaomai (to listen; apparently an intensive of akouo); a hearer (merely).

BDAG.en: a hearer
BDAG.pt: um ouvinte

DEFINITION: (a technical word of Jewish use) foreskin, prepuce: used sometimes as a slang term by Jews, of Gentiles.
ORIGIN: From akron and probably a modified form of posthe (the penis or male sexual organ); the prepuce; by implication, an uncircumcised (i.e. Gentile, figuratively, unregenerate) state or person.

BDAG.en: prepuce, foreskin; uncircumcision as a state of being; noncircumcised, gentiles
BDAG.pt: prepúcio, pele do prepúcio; incircuncisão como estado de ser; incircuncisos, gentios

DEFINITION: in the corner (of a building); subst: corner-(stone).
ORIGIN: From akron and gonia; belonging to the extreme corner.

BDAG.en: cornerstone or capstone (only fig., of Christ)
BDAG.pt: pedra angular ou pedra de fecho (somente em sentido figurado, de Cristo)

DEFINITION: (lit: top of a heap), first-fruits, spoil, treasure (taken in war).
ORIGIN: From akron and this (a heap); properly (in the plural) the top of the heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty.

BDAG.en: booty, spoils (the topmost/best part of the heap)
BDAG.pt: botim, despojos (a parte mais alta/melhor do monte)

DEFINITION: the end, extremity.
ORIGIN: Neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of akmen; the extremity.
USAGE: one end... Other, tip, top, uttermost participle.

BDAG.en: high point, top; extreme limit, end
BDAG.pt: ponto alto, cume; limite extremo, fim

DEFINITION: the Greek way of writing the Latin Aquila, a male proper name; the husband of Priscilla (Prisca), and a Jew, of a family belonging to (Sinope in ?) Pontus.
ORIGIN: Probably for Latin aquila (an eagle); Akulas, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Aquila (a Jewish artisan, husband of Priscilla, friend of Paul)
BDAG.pt: Áquila (um artesão judeu, marido de Priscila, amigo de Paulo)

DEFINITION: to annul, make of no effect, cancel.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and kuroo; to invalidate.

BDAG.en: to make void
BDAG.pt: anular, tornar nulo

DEFINITION: (characteristic of legal documents), without hindrance, freely.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of koluo; in an unhindered manner, i.e. Freely.

BDAG.en: without hindrance
BDAG.pt: sem impedimento

DEFINITION: unwilling, generally used where English would express by an adverb: unwillingly.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and hekon; unwilling.

BDAG.en: unwilling; to be translated as adv. unwillingly; sin inadvertently
BDAG.pt: relutante; traduzido como advérbio relutantemente; pecar inadvertidamente

DEFINITION: a phial or bottle of perfumed ointment, usually of alabaster.
ORIGIN: Neuter of alabastros (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone; properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material).

BDAG.en: a vase for holding perfume/ointment, often made of alabaster
BDAG.pt: um vaso para guardar perfume/unguento, frequentemente feito de alabastro

DEFINITION: boasting, show, arrogant display, ostentation; plur: occasions of ostentation.
ORIGIN: From alazon; braggadocio, i.e. (by implication) self-confidence.

BDAG.en: pretension, arrogance in word and deed, pride in one’s possessions
BDAG.pt: pretensão, arrogância em palavras e atos, orgulho das posses

DEFINITION: a boaster, one who gives one's self airs in a loud and flaunting way.
ORIGIN: From ale (vagrancy); braggart.

BDAG.en: boaster, braggart; (as adjective) boastful presumption
BDAG.pt: fanfarrão, gabarola; (como adjetivo) presunção arrogante

DEFINITION: to cry aloud, raise a war-cry; a clanging or clashing cymbal.
ORIGIN: From alale (a shout, "halloo"); to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang.

BDAG.en: to cry out loudly in wailing; (gener.) of shrill tones, to clash
BDAG.pt: gritar alto em lamento; (geral) de tons estridentes, soar (címbalo)

DEFINITION: unutterable, that baffles words, unexpressed.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of laleo; unspeakable.

BDAG.en: unexpressed, wordless (sighs too deep for words)
BDAG.pt: inexpressável, sem palavras (suspiros profundos demais para palavras)

DEFINITION: unable to speak or articulate; speechless.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and laleo; mute.

BDAG.en: mute, unable to speak; a mute person
BDAG.pt: mudo, incapaz de falar; uma pessoa muda

DEFINITION: salt.
ORIGIN: From hals; salt; figuratively, prudence.

BDAG.en: salt (as seasoning or fertilizer); fig. spiritual qualities of disciples; of speech that is winsome or witty
BDAG.pt: sal (como tempero ou fertilizante); fig. qualidades espirituais dos discípulos; de fala atraente ou espirituosa

DEFINITION: to anoint: festivally, in homage, medicinally, or in anointing the dead.
ORIGIN: From a (as particle of union) and the base of liparos; to oil (with perfume).

BDAG.en: to anoint by applying a liquid (oil or perfume); to besmear with something undesirable (figuratively)
BDAG.pt: ungir aplicando um líquido (óleo ou perfume); untar com algo indesejável (figurativamente)

DEFINITION: the cockcrow, as a period of time, between midnight and 3 a.m.
ORIGIN: From alektor and phone; cock-crow, i.e. The third night-watch.

BDAG.en: crowing of a cock, crowing of a cock (=dawn) name of the third watch of the night
BDAG.pt: canto do galo, canto do galo (=alvorada) nome da terceira vigília da noite

DEFINITION: a cock, rooster.
ORIGIN: From aleko (to ward off); a cock or male fowl.

BDAG.en: cock, rooster
BDAG.pt: galo

DEFINITION: an Alexandrian, a native (or resident) of Alexandria in Egypt.
ORIGIN: From Alexandreia (the city so called); an Alexandreian or inhabitant of Alexandria.

BDAG.en: an Alexandrian
BDAG.pt: um alexandrino

DEFINITION: Alexandrian, belonging to Alexandria in Egypt.
ORIGIN: From the same as Alexandreus; Alexandrine, or belonging to Alexandria.

BDAG.en: Alexandrian (adjective)
BDAG.pt: alexandrino (adjetivo)

DEFINITION: Alexander, a name of Greek origin, (a) son of Simon of Cyrene, (b) the High Priest's kinsman, (c) an Ephesian Jew, (d) the coppersmith.
ORIGIN: From the same as (the first part of) alektor and aner; man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man.

BDAG.en: Alexander (a name)
BDAG.pt: Alexandre (um nome)

DEFINITION: meal, flour.
ORIGIN: From aleo (to grind); flour.

BDAG.en: wheat flour used for making bread
BDAG.pt: farinha de trigo usada para fazer pão

DEFINITION: truth, but not merely truth as spoken; truth of idea, reality, sincerity, truth in the moral sphere, divine truth revealed to man, straightforwardness.
ORIGIN: From alethes; truth.

BDAG.en: truthfulness, dependability, uprightness in thought and deed; the content of what is true, truth (opp. falsehood); an actual event or state, reality
BDAG.pt: verdade, confiabilidade, retidão no pensamento e na ação; o conteúdo daquilo que é verdadeiro, verdade (oposto a falsidade); um evento ou estado real, realidade

DEFINITION: to say (speak) truth, do truth, maintain truth (the truth).
ORIGIN: From alethes; to be true (in doctrine and profession).

BDAG.en: be truthful, tell the truth to someone; (Absol.) maintain the spirit of love
BDAG.pt: ser veraz, dizer a verdade a alguém; (Absoluto) manter o espírito de amor

DEFINITION: unconcealed, true, true in fact, worthy of credit, truthful.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and lanthano; true (as not concealing).

BDAG.en: 1. pert. to being truthful and honest, truthful, righteous, honest (of persons); 2. pert. to being in accordance with fact, true (of things spoken); 3. pert. to being real, real, genuine, not imaginary
BDAG.pt: 1. referente a ser sincero e honesto, verdadeiro, justo, honesto (de pessoas); 2. referente a estar de acordo com o fato, verdadeiro (de coisas ditas); 3. referente a ser real, genuíno, autêntico, não imaginário

DEFINITION: true (lit: made of truth), real, genuine.
ORIGIN: From alethes; truthful.

BDAG.en: 1. pert. to being in accord with what is true, true, trustworthy (of God, Christ, credentials); 2. pert. to being in accordance with fact, true (of a word, testimony, judgment); 3. pert. to being real, genuine, authentic, real (of light, life, bread of Eucharist, God in contrast to other deities, true sanctuary)
BDAG.pt: 1. referente a estar em acordo com o que é verdadeiro, verdadeiro, confiável (de Deus, Cristo, credenciais); 2. referente a estar de acordo com o fato, verdadeiro (de uma palavra, testemunho, julgamento); 3. referente a ser real, genuíno, autêntico (de luz, vida, pão da Eucaristia, Deus em contraste com outras divindades, verdadeiro santuário)

DEFINITION: to grind.
ORIGIN: From the same as aleuron; to grind.

BDAG.en: grind (by hand-mill); (Fig.) used of martyrdom (being ground as God’s wheat)
BDAG.pt: moer (em moinho de mão); (Fig.) usado de martírio (ser moído como trigo de Deus)

DEFINITION: truly, really, certainly, surely.
ORIGIN: Adverb from alethes; truly.
USAGE: indeed, surely, of a surety, truly, of a (in) truth, verily, very.

BDAG.en: truly, in truth, really, actually (modifying a verb or in an attributive relation with substantives)
BDAG.pt: verdadeiramente, em verdade, realmente, de fato (modificando um verbo ou em relação atributiva com substantivos)

DEFINITION: a fisherman.
ORIGIN: From hals; a sailor (as engaged on the salt water), i.e. (by implication) a fisher.

BDAG.en: fisher (one whose occupation is catching fish); allegorically: one who catches people (disciples)
BDAG.pt: pescador (aquele cuja ocupação é pescar); alegoricamente: aquele que pesca pessoas (discípulos)

DEFINITION: to fish.
ORIGIN: From halieus; to be a fisher, i.e. (by implication) to fish.

BDAG.en: to fish
BDAG.pt: pescar

DEFINITION: to salt, sprinkle with salt (of sacrifices or of those who offer sacrifice), keep fresh and sound, and so acceptable to God.
ORIGIN: From hals; to salt.

BDAG.en: to be salted; to be seasoned/preserved (fig. to appropriate power to prevent corruption)
BDAG.pt: ser salgado; ser temperado/preservado (fig. apropriar-se do poder para evitar a corrupção)

DEFINITION: pollution, perhaps a polluted thing (especially of food).
ORIGIN: From alisgeo (to soil); (ceremonially) defilement.

BDAG.en: pollution
BDAG.pt: poluição (atos separados de impureza cerimonial)

DEFINITION: otherwise, on the other hand, but.
ORIGIN: Neuter plural of allos; properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially) contrariwise (in many relations).
USAGE: and, but (even), howbeit, indeed, nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet.

BDAG.en: but, yet, rather (adversative particle indicating contrast or transition)
BDAG.pt: mas, porém, contudo, antes (partícula adversativa indicando contraste ou transição)

DEFINITION: to change, alter, exchange, transform.
ORIGIN: From allos; to make different.

BDAG.en: to make something other or different, change, alter; to exchange one thing for another
BDAG.pt: tornar algo diferente, mudar, alterar; trocar uma coisa por outra

DEFINITION: from another place, by another way.
ORIGIN: From allos; from elsewhere.

BDAG.en: from another place
BDAG.pt: de outro lugar

DEFINITION: to speak allegorically.
ORIGIN: From allos and agoreo (to harangue (compare agora)); to allegorize.
USAGE: be an allegory (the Greek word itself).

BDAG.en: to use analogy or likeness to express something, speak allegorically
BDAG.pt: usar analogia ou semelhança para expressar algo, falar alegoricamente

DEFINITION: hallelujah, alleluia (an adoring exclamation).
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (imperative of halal and Yahh); praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation.

BDAG.en: Hallelujah (loanword, praise Yahweh)
BDAG.pt: Aleluia (palavra emprestada, louvai ao Senhor)

DEFINITION: one another, each other.
ORIGIN: Genitive plural from allos reduplicated; one another.
USAGE: each other, mutual, one another, (the other), (them-, your-)selves, (selves) together (sometimes with meta or pros).

BDAG.en: each other, one another, mutually
BDAG.pt: um ao outro, mutuamente

DEFINITION: of another nation, a foreigner.
ORIGIN: From allos and genos; foreign, i.e. Not a Jew.

BDAG.en: foreign
BDAG.pt: estrangeiro

DEFINITION: to leap, leap up; of water: to spring up, bubble up.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to jump; figuratively, to gush.

BDAG.en: to make a quick leaping movement, leap, spring up; to spring up from a source, well up, bubble up (of water)
BDAG.pt: fazer um movimento rápido de salto, saltar, brotar; de água, jorrar, borbulhar

DEFINITION: other, another (of more than two), different.
ORIGIN: A primary word; "else," i.e. Different (in many applications).

BDAG.en: other, different; another (person or thing); additional; the other (of two)
BDAG.pt: outro, diferente; outro (pessoa ou coisa); adicional; o outro (de dois)

DEFINITION: one who meddles in things alien to his calling or in matters belonging to others; factious.
ORIGIN: From allotrios and episkopos; overseeing others' affairs, i.e. A meddler (specially, in Gentile customs).

DEFINITION: belonging to another person, belonging to others, foreign, strange.
ORIGIN: From allos; another's, i.e. Not one's own; by extension foreign, not akin, hostile.

BDAG.en: belonging to another, not one’s own, strange; different in kind from other entities, different; in addition, more; the remaining one of two or more, the other of the two; hostile, enemy.
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a outro, não próprio, estranho; diferente em tipo ou espécie de outras entidades, diverso; adicional, mais; o restante de dois ou mais, o outro; hostil, inimigo.

DEFINITION: foreign, of another tribe or race.
ORIGIN: From allos and phule; foreign, i.e. (specially) Gentile.

BDAG.en: alien, foreign, hence from the Judean viewpoint=gentiles, outsiders; subst. a gentile (opposed to an Israelite/Jew); especially (as in LXX) of the Philistines, Amalekites, or Canaanites.
BDAG.pt: estranho, estrangeiro, daí, do ponto de vista judeu=gentios, de fora; como substantivo, um gentio (oposto a israelita/judeu); especialmente (como na LXX) referente aos Filisteus, Amalequitas ou Cananeus.

DEFINITION: otherwise, things that are otherwise.
ORIGIN: Adverb from allos; differently.

BDAG.en: otherwise, in another way, differently (pertaining to difference in manner or condition).
BDAG.pt: de outra forma, de outro modo, diferentemente (pertencente à diferença na maneira ou condição).

DEFINITION: to thresh (wheat).
ORIGIN: From the same as halon; to tread out grain.

BDAG.en: to thresh (grain), usually done with oxen driven over the threshing-floor.
BDAG.pt: Debulhar (grão), geralmente feito com bois que eram conduzidos sobre a eira.

DEFINITION: without reason, irrational; contrary to reason, absurd.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and logos; irrational.

BDAG.en: without reason or capacity for reason, like animals; contrary to reason, absurd.
BDAG.pt: Sem razão ou capacidade de raciocínio, como animais; contrário à razão, absurdo.

DEFINITION: aloes, the powdered fragrant aloe wood.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (compare akanthinos); aloes (the gum).

BDAG.en: aloes (an aromatic substance, likely *aloe vera* or *aloe succotrina*, used mixed with myrrh for embalming).
BDAG.pt: aloés (uma substância aromática, provavelmente *aloe vera* ou *aloe succotrina*, usada misturada com mirra para embalsamar).

DEFINITION: salt.
ORIGIN: A primary word; "salt".

BDAG.en: salt; also used figuratively (e.g., pillar of salt).
BDAG.pt: sal; também usado figurativamente (ex: pilar de sal).

DEFINITION: salty, saltine, bitter.
ORIGIN: From hals; briny.

BDAG.en: salty; of salty water (often referring to a salt spring).
BDAG.pt: Salgado; de água salgada (frequentemente referindo-se a uma fonte salina).

DEFINITION: free from pain (grief, trouble).
ORIGIN: Comparative of a compound of a (as a negative particle) and lupe; more without grief.

BDAG.en: free from anxiety.
BDAG.pt: Livre de ansiedade.

DEFINITION: a (light) chain, bond.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a fetter or manacle.

BDAG.en: chain, especially handcuffs; figuratively, imprisonment or disgrace.
BDAG.pt: corrente, especialmente algemas; figurativamente, prisão ou desgraça.

DEFINITION: profitless, unprofitable, ruinous, detrimental.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and the base of lusitelei; gainless, i.e. (by implication) pernicious.

BDAG.en: unprofitable, not covering one's expenses; can also mean harmful.
BDAG.pt: Improdutivo, que não cobre as despesas; também pode significar prejudicial.

DEFINITION: Alphaeus; apparently two persons, (a) father of Levi, and (b) father of James.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (compare Cheleph); Alphoeus, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Alphaeus (the name of two different individuals: father of Levi the tax-collector, and father of the apostle James).
BDAG.pt: Alfeu (o nome de dois indivíduos diferentes: pai de Levi o coletor de impostos, e pai do apóstolo Tiago).

DEFINITION: a threshing floor.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of heilisso; a threshing-floor (as rolled hard), i.e. (figuratively) the grain (and chaff, as just threshed).

BDAG.en: threshing floor (the surface for threshing grain); figuratively, threshed grain still lying on the floor.
BDAG.pt: Eira (a superfície para debulhar o grão); figurativamente, grão debulhado ainda sobre o chão.

DEFINITION: a fox; a fox-like, crafty person.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a fox, i.e. (figuratively) a cunning person.

BDAG.en: fox; metaphorically, a crafty person (Herod Antipas)
BDAG.pt: raposa; metaforicamente, uma pessoa astuta (Herodes Antipas)

DEFINITION: capture, capturing.
ORIGIN: From a collateral form of haireomai.

BDAG.en: capture, the catching of animals (for food).
BDAG.pt: captura, o ato de apanhar animais (para alimentação).

DEFINITION: at the same time, therewith, along with, together with.
ORIGIN: A primary particle; properly, at the "same" time, but freely used as a preposition or adverb denoting close association.

BDAG.en: at the same time, together; marker of simultaneous occurrence or association; together with
BDAG.pt: ao mesmo tempo, junto; marcador de ocorrência simultânea ou associação; juntamente com

DEFINITION: unlearned, ignorant.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and manthano; ignorant.

BDAG.en: ignorant, incompetent (referring to interpreters).
BDAG.pt: ignorante, incompetente (referindo-se a intérpretes).

DEFINITION: unfading, fadeless, enduring.
ORIGIN: From amarantos; "amaranthine", i.e. (by implication) fadeless.

BDAG.en: unfading, incorruptible (figuratively used of eternal glory or an unfading crown).
BDAG.pt: inefadigável, incorruptível (usado figurativamente da glória eterna ou uma coroa que não murcha).

DEFINITION: unfading, enduring.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of maraino; unfading, i.e. (by implication) perpetual.

BDAG.en: unfading (pertaining to not losing pristine quality, used for flowers or eternal bliss).
BDAG.pt: inefadigável (pertencente a não perder a qualidade original, usado para flores ou bem-aventurança eterna).

DEFINITION: pecar

BDAG.en: to commit a wrong, to sin (transgress against divinity, custom, or law; miss the mark, err, do wrong)
BDAG.pt: cometer um erro, pecar (transgredir contra a divindade, costume ou lei; errar o alvo, falhar, fazer o mal)

DEFINITION: a fault, sin, evil deed.
ORIGIN: From hamartano; a sin (properly concrete).

BDAG.en: an individual act sin, transgression (as moral default)
BDAG.pt: um ato individual de pecado, transgressão (como falta moral)

DEFINITION: prop: missing the mark; hence: (a) guilt, sin, (b) a fault, failure (in an ethical sense), sinful deed.
ORIGIN: From hamartano; a sin (properly abstract).

BDAG.en: a departure from human or divine standards of uprightness (sin, sinfulness); a destructive evil power (sin as a ruling power)
BDAG.pt: um desvio dos padrões humanos ou divinos de retidão (pecado, pecaminosidade); um poder maligno destrutivo (pecado como poder dominante)

DEFINITION: without witness, untestified to.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a form of martus; unattested.

DEFINITION: sinning, sinful, depraved, detestable.
ORIGIN: From hamartano; sinful, i.e. A sinner.

DEFINITION: peaceable, abstaining from fighting, not contentious.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and mache; peaceable.

DEFINITION: to mow, reap, collect.
ORIGIN: From hama; properly, to collect, i.e. (by implication) reap.

DEFINITION: amethyst (a kind of rock crystal: the best specimens are the color of unmixed wine, whence perhaps the name), believed to stave off drunkenness.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of methuo; the "amethyst" (supposed to prevent intoxication).

DEFINITION: to neglect, be careless of, disregard.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and melo; to be careless of.
USAGE: make light of, neglect, be negligent, no regard.

DEFINITION: blameless, free from fault or defect.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of memphomai; irreproachable.

DEFINITION: blamelessly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from amemptos; faultlessly.

DEFINITION: free from anxiety (though anxiety is rather too strong a word) or care.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and merimna; not anxious.

DEFINITION: immutable, unchangeable.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of metatithemi; unchangeable, or (neuter as abstract) unchangeability.

DEFINITION: immovable, firm.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of metakineo; immovable.

DEFINITION: not to be repented of, about which no change of mind can take place, not affected by change of mind.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of metamellomai; irrevocable.
USAGE: without repentance, not to be repented of.

DEFINITION: impenitent, unrepentant.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of metanoeo; unrepentant.

DEFINITION: not measurable, immeasurable, to a limitless degree.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and metron; immoderate.

DEFINITION: verily, truly, amen; at the end of sentences may be paraphrased by: So let it be.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('amen); properly, firm, i.e. (figuratively) trustworthy; adverbially, surely (often as interjection, so be it).

DEFINITION: (lit: motherless), whose mother's name is not recorded (or known).
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and meter; motherless, i.e. Of unknown maternity.

DEFINITION: undefiled, untainted, free from contamination.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of miaino; unsoiled, i.e. (figuratively) pure.

DEFINITION: Amminadab, son of Ram and father of Nahshon, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ammiynadab); Aminadab, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: sand, sandy ground.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from hama; sand (as heaped on the beach).

DEFINITION: a lamb (as a type of innocence, and with sacrificial connotation).
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a lamb.

DEFINITION: a change, an exchange; hence plur: reciprocal good deeds (services), a fitting requital.
ORIGIN: From ameibo (to exchange); requital.

DEFINITION: a vine, grape-vine.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of amphoteros and that of halon; a vine (as coiling about a support).

BDAG.en: vine, grapevine
BDAG.pt: videira, parreira

DEFINITION: a vine-dresser, gardener.
ORIGIN: From ampelos and ergon; a vine-worker, i.e. Pruner.

BDAG.en: vinedresser, gardener
BDAG.pt: viticultor, jardineiro

DEFINITION: a vineyard.
ORIGIN: From ampelos; a vineyard.

BDAG.en: vineyard
BDAG.pt: vinha, vinhedo

DEFINITION: Ampliatus (Amplias), a male member of the church at Rome, probably of the imperial household.
ORIGIN: Contracted for Latin ampliatus (enlarged); Amplias, a Roman Christian.

DEFINITION: to ward off, defend myself against, resist, defend, assist.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of a primary verb; to ward off (for oneself), i.e. Protect.

BDAG.en: to help by coming to the aid of, help, assist, defend someone
BDAG.pt: socorrer, ajudar, defender alguém

DEFINITION: prop: something thrown around; a fishing-net, drag-net.
ORIGIN: From a compound of the base of amphoteros and ballo; a (fishing) net (as thrown about the fish).

BDAG.en: a circular casting-net used in fishing, casting-net
BDAG.pt: rede de arrasto circular usada na pesca, rede de pescar

DEFINITION: to put on, clothe.
ORIGIN: From the base of amphoteros and hennumi (to invest); to enrobe.

BDAG.en: clothe, dress
BDAG.pt: vestir, trajar

DEFINITION: Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia.
ORIGIN: From the base of amphoteros and polis; a city surrounded by a river; Amphipolis, a place in Macedonia.

BDAG.en: Amphipolis (city name)
BDAG.pt: Anfípolis (nome de cidade)

DEFINITION: prop: a road around anything; the street of a village.
ORIGIN: From the base of amphoteros and hodos; a fork in the road.

BDAG.en: a city quarter, surrounded and crossed by streets, then street
BDAG.pt: um quarteirão da cidade, rodeado e cruzado por ruas, depois rua

DEFINITION: both (of two).
ORIGIN: Comparative of amphi (around); (in plural) both.

BDAG.en: both
BDAG.pt: ambos, os dois

DEFINITION: without blame or fault, unblemished.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of momaomai; unblamable.

BDAG.en: blameless, unblemished
BDAG.pt: incontestável, sem mácula, imaculado

DEFINITION: blameless, without blemish, unblemished, faultless.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and momos; unblemished (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: without blame (blemish, fault, spot), faultless, unblamable.

BDAG.en: pert. to being without defect or blemish, unblemished; pert. to being without fault and therefore morally blameless, blameless
BDAG.pt: pertencente à ausência de defeito ou mancha, imaculado; pertencente à ausência de falha e, portanto, moralmente irrepreensível, sem culpa

DEFINITION: Amon (Amos), son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Amown); Amon, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Amon, in genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Amon, na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: Amos, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Amowts); Amos, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Amos in genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Amós na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: an untranslatable word (under the circumstances, in that case, anyhow), the general effect of which is to make a statement contingent, which would otherwise be definite: it is thus regularly used with the subjunctive mood.
ORIGIN: A primary particle, denoting a supposition, wish, possibility or uncertainty.
USAGE: (what-, where-, wither-, who-)soever. Usually unexpressed except by the subjunctive or potential mood. Also contracted for ean.

BDAG.en: A particle denoting aspect of contingency, incapable of translation by a single English word; indicates that the verb's action is dependent on some circumstance or condition.
BDAG.pt: Uma partícula que denota aspecto de contingência, incapaz de ser traduzida por uma única palavra em inglês; indica que a ação do verbo depende de alguma circunstância ou condição.

DEFINITION: prep. Rare in NT; prop: upwards, up; among, between; in turn; apiece, by; as a prefix: up, to, anew, back.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition and adverb; properly, up; but (by extension) used (distributively) severally, or (locally) at (etc.).
USAGE: and, apiece, by, each, every (man), in, through. In compounds (as a prefix) it often means (by implication) repetition, intensity, reversal, etc.

BDAG.en: prep. with acc. (Hom.+), lit. 'up, up to'; rare in later Gk. 1 ἀνὰμέσον in a position in the middle among, in the midst of... b of pers. between... 2 ἀνὰμέρος following in sequence, in turn... 3 distributive, w. numbers, each, apiece...
BDAG.pt: Preposição com acusativo (Hom.+), literalmente 'para cima, até'; raro no grego posterior. 1 ἀνὰμέσον em uma posição no meio, entre... b de pessoas, entre... 2 ἀνὰμέρος sucessivamente, em turno... 3 distributivo, com números, cada um, por vez...

DEFINITION: a step, a flight of steps; the well-known stairs leading up from the temple to the tower of Antonia at Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: From anabaino (compare bathmos); a stairway.

BDAG.en: step, pl. flight of stairs. Of the stairs that led fr. the temple court to the tower Antonia
BDAG.pt: degrau, escadaria (plural). Referente às escadas que conduziam do pátio do templo à torre Antônia

DEFINITION: to go up, mount, ascend; of things: to rise, spring up, come up.
ORIGIN: From ana and the base of basis; to go up (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: arise, ascend (up), climb (go, grow, rise, spring) up, come (up).

BDAG.en: to be in motion upward, go up, ascend; of movement in a direction without special focus on making an ascent; Esp. of the road to Jerusalem, located on high ground; of the journey to Judea; Of ships, embark, get (into); Abs. he went up again; of any upward movement ascend, go up (to heaven); Climb up; Repres. a passive (a burden ‘is laid’); of things: smoke, rocks, stones, of vines that cling to elm trees climb up; Of plants also come up; Prayers ascend to heaven; Fig. a report came up to the tribune; the priesthood went to Simeon; Semitism: lit. ‘to arise in the heart’ enter one’s mind
BDAG.pt: estar em movimento ascendente, subir, ascender; de movimento em uma direção sem foco especial em subir; Especialmente da estrada para Jerusalém, localizada em terreno elevado; Da jornada à Judeia; De navios, embarcar, entrar; Absoluto, ele subiu novamente; De qualquer movimento ascendente ascender, subir (para o céu); Subir; Representa um passivo (um fardo 'é posto'); De coisas: fumaça, rochas, pedras, de videiras que se agarram a árvores de olmo subir; De plantas também brotar; Orações sobem ao céu; Fig., um relatório chegou ao tribuno; o sacerdócio foi para Simeão; Semitismo: literalmente, 'erguer-se no coração' vir à mente

DEFINITION: to postpone, defer, especially: to postpone the trial of.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ana and ballo; to put off (for oneself).

BDAG.en: 2 aor. act. ... mid. 'put off'... mid. in the only instance in our lit., and as legal t.t. adjourn a trial, etc.... remand someone, adjourn (his trial)...
BDAG.pt: 2. aoristo ativo... médio 'adiar'... médio na única ocorrência em nossa literatura, e como termo legal: adiar um julgamento, etc.... adiar alguém, suspender (seu julgamento)...

DEFINITION: to draw up, as a net to shore.
ORIGIN: From ana and a derivative of the base of basis; to cause to go up, i.e. Haul (a net).

BDAG.en: bring up of a net...
BDAG.pt: Trazer para cima (no caso de uma rede)...

DEFINITION: to look up, recover sight.
ORIGIN: From ana and blepo; to look up; by implication, to recover sight.

BDAG.en: to direct one’s vision upward, look up, lit.; Look up; to gain sight, whether for the first time or again, regain sight, gain sight (of blind persons, who were formerly able to see, regain sight; of one born blind receive sight, become able to see); fig., of inward sight
BDAG.pt: dirigir a visão para cima, olhar para cima, literalmente; Olhar para cima; ganhar a visão, seja pela primeira vez ou novamente, recuperar a visão, ganhar a visão (de pessoas cegas que antes podiam ver, recuperam a visão; de alguém nascido cego receber a visão, tornar-se capaz de ver); fig., de visão interior

DEFINITION: recovery of sight.
ORIGIN: From anablepo; restoration of sight.

BDAG.en: recovery of sight
BDAG.pt: recuperação da visão

DEFINITION: to shout upwards, cry out, raise voice.
ORIGIN: From ana and boao; to halloo.

BDAG.en: cry out
BDAG.pt: gritar

DEFINITION: postponement, delay, putting off.
ORIGIN: From anaballomai; a putting off.

BDAG.en: ‘delay’; legal t.t. postponement
BDAG.pt: 'atraso'; termo legal de adiamento

DEFINITION: to bring back word, report; to announce, declare.
ORIGIN: From ana and the base of aggelos; to announce (in detail).
USAGE: declare, rehearse, report, show, speak, tell.

BDAG.en: to carry back information, to report, of pers. returning fr. a place; gener. to provide information, disclose, announce, proclaim, teach; Of a report to officials; Of proclamation of what is to come in the future through the Spirit; Of Jesus; Of didactic speaking: preach
BDAG.pt: trazer de volta informações, relatar, de pessoas voltando de um lugar; geralmente fornecer informações, revelar, anunciar, proclamar, ensinar; De um relatório a autoridades; De proclamação do que está por vir no futuro através do Espírito; De Jesus; De falar didaticamente: pregar

DEFINITION: to beget again, beget into a new life.
ORIGIN: From ana and gennao; to beget or (by extension) bear (again).

BDAG.en: beget again, cause to be born again (fig. of the spiritual rebirth of Christians)
BDAG.pt: gerar novamente, fazer nascer de novo (metaf. do renascimento espiritual dos cristãos)

DEFINITION: to read, know again, know certainly, recognize, discern.
ORIGIN: From ana and ginosko; to know again, i.e. (by extension) to read.

DEFINITION: to force, compel, constrain, urge.
ORIGIN: From anagke; to necessitate.

BDAG.en: to compel someone to act in a particular manner, compel, force, of inner and outer compulsion; strongly urge/invite, urge upon, press
BDAG.pt: compelir alguém a agir de uma maneira particular, forçar, de compulsão interna e externa; exortar/convidar fortemente, instar, pressionar

DEFINITION: necessary, essential, intimate, right, proper.
ORIGIN: From anagke; necessary; by implication, close (of kin).

BDAG.en: necessary (as meeting need); intimate, as Lat. necessarius of relatives and friends
BDAG.pt: necessário (como suprindo uma necessidade); íntimo, como o latim *necessarius* de parentes e amigos

DEFINITION: by way of compulsion, unwillingly, by force, necessarily.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of anagkazo; compulsorily.

BDAG.en: by compulsion (opposed to willingly)
BDAG.pt: por compulsão (em oposição a voluntariamente)

DEFINITION: necessity, constraint, compulsion; there is need to; force, violence.
ORIGIN: From ana and the base of agkale; constraint (literally or figuratively); by implication, distress.
USAGE: distress, must needs, (of) necessity(-sary), needeth, needful.

BDAG.en: necessity or constraint as inherent in the nature of things, necessity, pressure of any kind, a divine dispensation, some hoped-for advantage, custom, duty, etc.; a state of distress or trouble, distress, calamity, pressure; (concr.) compulsion by forcible means, torture
BDAG.pt: necessidade ou constrangimento inerente à natureza das coisas, necessidade, pressão de qualquer tipo, uma dispensa divina, alguma vantagem esperada, costume, dever, etc.; um estado de aflição ou problema, aflição, calamidade, pressão; (concreto) coerção por meios forçados, tortura

DEFINITION: to recognize; pass: to be made known, cause myself to be recognized.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ana and gnorizo; to make (oneself) known.

BDAG.en: learn to know again, become reacquainted, see again; be recognized
BDAG.pt: conhecer novamente, familiarizar-se novamente, ver de novo; ser reconhecido

DEFINITION: recognition, reading; public reading (of the law and prophets in synagogue or church).
ORIGIN: From anaginosko; (the act of) reading.

BDAG.en: the process of reading something written, reading (of public reading, of the reading of the law and prophets in the synagogue); the content of what is read, reading
BDAG.pt: o processo de ler algo escrito, leitura (de leitura pública, da leitura da lei e dos profetas na sinagoga); o conteúdo do que é lido, leitura

DEFINITION: to lead up, bring up, offer, produce, put to sea, set sail.
ORIGIN: From ana and ago; to lead up; by extension to bring out; specially, to sail away.
USAGE: bring (again, forth, up again), depart, launch (forth), lead (up), loose, offer, sail, set forth, take up.

BDAG.en: to lead or bring from a lower to a higher point, lead, bring up; bring up for judicial process, bring before; to bring an offering, offer up; (nautical) to begin to go by boat, put out to sea; to put back into a former state or condition, restore, bring back (figuratively)
BDAG.pt: conduzir ou trazer de um ponto mais baixo para um mais alto, guiar, trazer para cima; levar a um processo judicial, apresentar; trazer uma oferta, oferecer; (náutico) começar a ir de barco, zarpar; restaurar a um estado ou condição anterior, restabelecer, trazer de volta (figurado)

DEFINITION: to show forth, show clearly; hence: to proclaim (a person's appointment to an office), appoint.
ORIGIN: From ana and deiknuo; to exhibit, i.e. (by implication) to indicate, appoint.

BDAG.en: to make someth. known by clear indication, show clearly, reveal someth. hidden; to assign to a task or position, appoint, commission
BDAG.pt: tornar algo conhecido por clara indicação, mostrar claramente, revelar algo escondido; designar para uma tarefa ou posição, nomear, comissionar

DEFINITION: the proclamation of an appointment (to an office); perhaps rather admission to membership of a society.
ORIGIN: From anadeiknumi; (the act of) exhibition.

BDAG.en: commissioning, installation (public recognition of an appointed official)
BDAG.pt: comissionamento, instalação (reconhecimento público de um oficial nomeado)

DEFINITION: to welcome, receive kindly; to undertake, assume the responsibility of.
ORIGIN: From ana and dechomai; to entertain (as a guest).

BDAG.en: to experience something by being accepting, accept, receive; to extend hospitality to, receive, welcome of guests
BDAG.pt: experimentar algo ao ser aceitador, aceitar, receber; estender hospitalidade, receber, acolher convidados

DEFINITION: to send up, deliver, hand over, yield.
ORIGIN: From ana and didomi; to hand over.

BDAG.en: deliver, hand over
BDAG.pt: entregar, passar

DEFINITION: to come to life again, revive, regain life.
ORIGIN: To recover life (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to come to life out of a condition of death (literally be resurrected); figuratively be alive
BDAG.pt: voltar à vida a partir de uma condição de morte (literalmente ser ressuscitado); figurativamente estar vivo

DEFINITION: to seek out, search for (implying the difficulty of the task).
ORIGIN: From ana and zeteo; to search out.

BDAG.en: to try to locate by search, look, search for someone
BDAG.pt: tentar localizar por busca, procurar, buscar alguém

DEFINITION: to gird up, brace up (with a view to active exertion); a metaphor from the girding of the flowing tunic, to prevent its hampering one in active work.
ORIGIN: From ana and zonnumi; to gird afresh.

BDAG.en: to bind up, gird up, lit. of long garments to facilitate work or walking; then fig. prepared for action
BDAG.pt: atar, cingir, literalmente de vestes longas para facilitar o trabalho ou a caminhada; depois, figurativamente, preparar-se para a ação

DEFINITION: to stir up the fire, fan the flame of.
ORIGIN: From ana and a compound of the base of zoon and pur; to re-enkindle.

BDAG.en: to cause to begin again, rekindle (fig.); to take on new life, kindle into flame
BDAG.pt: fazer começar de novo, reavivar (fig.); ganhar nova vida, incendiar-se

DEFINITION: to thrive or flourish again, revive.
ORIGIN: From ana and thallo (to flourish); to revive.

BDAG.en: to be in a state identical with a previous state, grow up again, bloom again; cause to grow/bloom again
BDAG.pt: estar em um estado idêntico a um estado anterior, crescer novamente, florescer novamente; fazer crescer/florescer novamente

DEFINITION: a votive offering, a thing devoted to God; a curse, the thing cursed.
ORIGIN: From anatithemai; a (religious) ban or (concretely) excommunicated (thing or person).

BDAG.en: that which is dedicated as a votive offering, a votive offering set up in a temple; that which has been cursed, cursed, accursed; the content that is expressed in a curse, a curse
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é dedicado como oferta votiva, uma oferenda votiva posta em um templo; aquilo que foi amaldiçoado, amaldiçoado, maldito; o conteúdo expresso em uma maldição, uma maldição

DEFINITION: to curse, invoke curses, devote to destruction.
ORIGIN: From anathema; to declare or vow under penalty of execration.
USAGE: (bind under a) curse, bind with an oath.

BDAG.en: to invoke consequences if what one says is not true; put under a curse; curse
BDAG.pt: invocar consequências se o que se diz não for verdade; colocar sob maldição; amaldiçoar

DEFINITION: to look at attentively, gaze at, consider.
ORIGIN: From ana and theoreo; to look again (i.e. Attentively) at (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to examine someth. carefully, look carefully at; to give careful thought to, consider, of spiritual things
BDAG.pt: examinar algo cuidadosamente, olhar atentamente; dar pensamento cuidadoso, considerar, de coisas espirituais

DEFINITION: an offering dedicated (hung up in a temple) by a worshipper; a gift or offering consecrated to God.
ORIGIN: From anatithemai (like anathema, but in a good sense); a votive offering.

BDAG.en: a dedication to a deity, votive offering
BDAG.pt: uma dedicação a uma divindade, oferenda votiva

DEFINITION: shamelessness, shameless persistence (e.g. in greed).
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle (compare aneu)) and aidos; impudence, i.e. (by implication) importunity.

BDAG.en: lack of sensitivity to what is proper, carelessness about the good opinion of others, shamelessness, impertinence, impudence, ignoring of convention
BDAG.pt: falta de sensibilidade ao que é apropriado, desconsideração pela boa opinião dos outros, descaramento, impertinência, audácia, ignorar a convenção

DEFINITION: taking away (of life), killing, slaying, murder.
ORIGIN: From anaireo; (the act of) killing.

BDAG.en: murder, killing
BDAG.pt: assassinato, morte (por violência)

DEFINITION: to take up, take away the life of, make an end of, murder.
ORIGIN: From ana and (the active of) haireomai; to take up, i.e. Adopt; by implication, to take away (violently), i.e. Abolish, murder.
USAGE: put to death, kill, slay, take away, take up.

BDAG.en: 1 to remove or take away, take away of things. Do away with, abolish. Take up a martyr’s bones. 2 to get rid of by execution, do away with, destroy, of persons (mostly of killing by violence, in battle, by execution, murder, or assassination). commit suicide. Of execution. Of the destruction of the Lawless One. 3 mid. to take up for oneself, take up, claim (for oneself)
BDAG.pt: 1 remover ou levar embora, tirar coisas. Abolir, anular. Recolher ossos de mártir. 2 livrar-se por execução, destruir, de pessoas (principalmente matar por violência, em batalha, por execução, assassinato ou morte súbita). cometer suicídio. De execução. Da destruição do Ímpio. 3 médio. tomar para si, resgatar, reivindicar (para si)

DEFINITION: guiltless, innocent.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and aitios (in the sense of aitia); innocent.

BDAG.en: innocent
BDAG.pt: inocente

DEFINITION: to set up, to sit up.
ORIGIN: From ana and kathizo; properly, to set up, i.e. (reflexively) to sit up.

BDAG.en: to sit up from a reclining position, sit up, sit upright
BDAG.pt: sentar-se de uma posição reclinada, sentar-se, sentar-se ereto

DEFINITION: to make fresh again, renew, restore.
ORIGIN: From ana and a derivative of kainos; to restore.

BDAG.en: renew, restore
BDAG.pt: renovar, restaurar

DEFINITION: to renew, make new again.
ORIGIN: From ana and a derivative of kainos; to renovate.

BDAG.en: renew only in Paul, in pass., and fig. of the spiritual rebirth of the Christian
BDAG.pt: renovar, somente em Paulo, na voz passiva e figuradamente do renascimento espiritual do cristão

DEFINITION: renewing; a renewal or change of heart and life.
ORIGIN: From anakainoo; renovation.

BDAG.en: renewal; of a person’s spiritual rebirth
BDAG.pt: renovação; do renascimento espiritual de uma pessoa

DEFINITION: to unveil, uncover.
ORIGIN: From ana (in the sense of reversal) and kalupto; to unveil.

BDAG.en: uncover, unveil
BDAG.pt: descobrir, desvendar

DEFINITION: to bend or turn back; to return.
ORIGIN: From ana and kampto; to turn back.

BDAG.en: 1 intr. to go back to a point or area from which an entity has departed, return. fig. of a religious greeting it will return to you. 2 to return to a former way of thinking, turn back again
BDAG.pt: 1 intransitivo. retornar a um ponto ou área de onde uma entidade partiu, voltar. figurado, de uma saudação religiosa, retornará a você. 2 retornar a um modo de pensar anterior, voltar atrás

DEFINITION: to recline, especially at a dinner-table.
ORIGIN: From ana and keimai; to recline (as a corpse or at a meal).
USAGE: guest, lean, lie, sit (down, at meat), at the table.

BDAG.en: 1 gener. lie, recline. 2 otherw. always of reclining at table, equals dine
BDAG.pt: 1 em geral. estar deitado, estar reclinado. 2 de outra forma, sempre reclinado à mesa, ou seja, jantar

DEFINITION: to sum up, summarize, recapitulate, gather up in one.
ORIGIN: From ana and kephalaioo (in its original sense); to sum up.
USAGE: briefly comprehend, gather together in one.

BDAG.en: 1 used of literary or rhetorical summation sum up, recapitulate. 2 of a mathematical total sum up, complete the total
BDAG.pt: 1 usado em sumarização literária ou retórica: resumir, recapitular. 2 de um total matemático: somar, completar o total

DEFINITION: to lay upon, lean against, lay down, make to recline; pass: to lie back, recline.
ORIGIN: From ana and klino; to lean back.

BDAG.en: 1 to cause someone to lie down, to lay down, lay, put to bed; 2 to cause to recline at a meal, place as guest; Pass. lie down, recline at a meal
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer alguém deitar-se, deitar, pôr na cama; 2 fazer alguém reclinar-se a uma refeição, colocar como convidado; Passivo deitar-se, reclinar-se para comer

DEFINITION: hinder.
ORIGIN: From ana and kopto; to beat back, i.e. Check.

BDAG.en: hinder, restrain. Of desires restrain. mid. abstain
BDAG.pt: impedir, conter. De desejos: refrear. médio: abster-se

DEFINITION: to shout aloud, cry out.
ORIGIN: From ana and krazo; to scream up (aloud).

BDAG.en: cry out
BDAG.pt: gritar, clamar

DEFINITION: to examine, inquire into, investigate, question.
ORIGIN: From ana and krino; properly, to scrutinize, i.e. (by implication) investigate, interrogate, determine.
USAGE: ask, question, discern, examine, judge, search.

BDAG.en: 1 to engage in careful study of a question, question, examine; 2 to conduct a judicial hearing, hear a case, question; 3 to examine with a view to finding fault, judge, call to account, discern
BDAG.pt: 1 engajar-se em estudo cuidadoso de uma questão, perguntar, examinar; 2 conduzir uma audiência judicial, ouvir um caso, interrogar; 3 examinar com o intuito de encontrar falhas, julgar, pedir contas, discernir

DEFINITION: judicial examination, preliminary inquiry.
ORIGIN: From anakrino; a (judicial) investigation.

BDAG.en: a judicial hearing, investigation, hearing, esp. preliminary hearing
BDAG.pt: uma audiência judicial, investigação, audição, especialmente audiência preliminar

DEFINITION: to raise myself, look up, be elated.
ORIGIN: From ana (in the sense of reversal) and kupto; to unbend, i.e. Rise; figuratively, be elated.

BDAG.en: 1 to raise oneself up to an erect position, stand erect, straighten oneself, lit.; 2 to take heart in expectation of deliverance, stand tall, fig.
BDAG.pt: 1 levantar-se para uma posição ereta, ficar de pé, endireitar-se, literalmente; 2 tomar ânimo na expectativa de livramento, ficar de pé, figurativamente

DEFINITION: to take up, raise; to pick up, take on board; to carry off, lead away.
ORIGIN: From ana and lambano; to take up.

BDAG.en: 1 to lift up and carry away, take up; 2 to take up in order to carry, take up; 3 to make someth. one’s own by taking, take to one’s self, adopt; 4 take someone along on a journey, take along of a travel companion; 5 take up someth. for scrutiny, take in hand
BDAG.pt: 1 levantar e levar embora, levar; 2 pegar para carregar, pegar; 3 tornar algo seu ao tomar, assumir, adotar; 4 levar alguém em uma jornada, levar como companheiro de viagem; 5 pegar algo para exame, tomar a seu cargo

DEFINITION: a taking up, lifting up.
ORIGIN: From analambano; ascension.

DEFINITION: to destroy, annihilate, expend, consume.
ORIGIN: From ana and a form of the alternate of haireomai; properly, to use up, i.e. Destroy.

BDAG.en: to do away with someth. completely by using up, destroy, consume; Fig., of annihilation
BDAG.pt: destruir completamente algo pelo uso, consumir, esgotar; Figurado, de aniquilação

DEFINITION: proportion, measure, analogy.
ORIGIN: From a compound of ana and logos; proportion.

BDAG.en: a state of right relationship involving proportion, proportion; in right relationship to, in agreement w., or in proportion to
BDAG.pt: um estado de relacionamento correto envolvendo proporção, proporção; em relacionamento correto com, em acordo com, ou em proporção a

DEFINITION: to think upon, consider attentively.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from analogia; to estimate, i.e. (figuratively) contemplate.

BDAG.en: to reason with careful deliberation, consider
BDAG.pt: raciocinar com deliberação cuidadosa, considerar

DEFINITION: saltless, tasteless, flat.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and hals; saltless, i.e. Insipid.

BDAG.en: without salt, deprived of its salt content
BDAG.pt: sem sal, privado de seu teor de sal

DEFINITION: a loosing, departing, departure (from this life); (Probably a metaphor from the yoking and unyoking of transport animals).
ORIGIN: From analuo; departure.

BDAG.en: lit. ‘loosing up’; then, like our ‘breaking up’, departure; euphem., of departure from life, death
BDAG.pt: lit. ‘desatar’; depois, como nosso ‘despedida’, partida; eufemisticamente, de partida da vida, morte

DEFINITION: to unloose, unloose for departure, depart, return.
ORIGIN: From ana and luo; to break up, i.e. Depart (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: trans. loose, untie; intr. depart, return; Fig., depart (euphemistic for die)
BDAG.pt: transitivo soltar, desatar; intransitivo partir, regressar; Figurado, partir (eufemismo para morrer)

DEFINITION: without blame, faultless, unerring.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of hamartano; sinless.

BDAG.en: without sin, i.e. not having sinned
BDAG.pt: sem pecado, ou seja, não tendo pecado

DEFINITION: to await (one whose coming is expected).
ORIGIN: From ana and meno; to await.

BDAG.en: wait for, expect someone or something, esp. the Messiah; Fig., of time
BDAG.pt: esperar por, aguardar alguém ou algo, especialmente o Messias; Figurado, de tempo

DEFINITION: to remind, admonish, be reminded, remind myself; pass: to remember, recall.
ORIGIN: From ana and mimnesko; to remind; (reflexively) to recollect.
USAGE: call to mind, (bring to, call to, put in), remember(-brance).

BDAG.en: remind someone of something; Pass. be reminded, remember
BDAG.pt: lembrar alguém de algo; Passivo ser lembrado, recordar

DEFINITION: a recalling, remembrance, memory.
ORIGIN: From anamimnesko; recollection.

BDAG.en: reminder, remembrance of something; in the account of the Eucharist in remembrance (memory) of me
BDAG.pt: lembrete, recordação de algo; na narração da Eucaristia em memória de mim

DEFINITION: to renew; mid: to renew myself, be renewed.
ORIGIN: From ana and a derivative of neos; to renovate, i.e. Reform.

BDAG.en: 1 trans. renew; 2 intr. become young again
BDAG.pt: 1 trans. renovar; 2 intr. rejuvenescer

DEFINITION: to return to soberness, regain one's senses.
ORIGIN: From ana and nepho; to become sober again, i.e. (figuratively) regain (one's) senses.

BDAG.en: come to one’s senses again
BDAG.pt: voltar a si, recobrar o juízo

DEFINITION: Ananias, (a) husband of Sapphira, a member of the early church at Jerusalem, (b) a member of the church at Damascus, (c) the high priest at Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Chananyah); Ananias, the name of three Israelites.

BDAG.en: Ananias (proper name)
BDAG.pt: Ananias (nome próprio)

DEFINITION: indisputable, undeniable, not to be contradicted.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of anti and rheo; indisputable.

BDAG.en: not to be contradicted, undeniable
BDAG.pt: incontestável, inegável

DEFINITION: without contradiction, without hesitation, promptly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from anantirrhetos; promptly.

BDAG.en: without raising any objection
BDAG.pt: sem levantar qualquer objeção

DEFINITION: unworthy, inadequate.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and axios; unfit.

BDAG.en: unworthy
BDAG.pt: indigno

DEFINITION: unworthily, in an unworthy manner.
ORIGIN: Adverb from anaxios; irreverently.

BDAG.en: in an unworthy/careless manner (of the Eucharist)
BDAG.pt: de maneira indigna/descuidada (da Eucaristia)

DEFINITION: rest, cessation from labor, refreshment.
ORIGIN: From anapano; intermission; by implication, recreation.

BDAG.en: 1 cessation from an activity; 2 cessation from wearisome activity for the sake of rest, rest, relief; 3 a location for resting, resting-place
BDAG.pt: 1 cessação de uma atividade; 2 cessação de atividade fatigante em prol de descanso, repouso, alívio; 3 um lugar para repousar, local de descanso

DEFINITION: to give rest, give intermission from labor, by implication refresh.
ORIGIN: From ana and pauo; (reflexively) to repose (literally or figuratively (be exempt), remain); by implication, to refresh.

BDAG.en: cause to rest, give (someone) rest, refresh, revive; to bring something to a conclusion, end, conclude, finish; to take one’s rest, rest; to settle on an object, rest upon.
BDAG.pt: causar repouso, dar descanso (a alguém), refrescar, reavivar; concluir, terminar, finalizar algo; descansar, repousar; pousar sobre um objeto, repousar sobre.

DEFINITION: to persuade, incite, seduce, tempt.
ORIGIN: From ana and peitho; to incite.

BDAG.en: to move someone to do something by persuasion, induce.
BDAG.pt: persuadir alguém a fazer algo, induzir.

DEFINITION: to send up (to a higher tribunal), send back.
ORIGIN: From ana and pempo; to send up or back.

BDAG.en: to send up from a lower position to a higher, send up toward heaven; to send on to someone in authority, send (up); to send back to a previous location, send back.
BDAG.pt: enviar de uma posição inferior para uma superior, enviar para cima em direção ao céu; enviar a alguém em autoridade, mandar (acima); enviar de volta a um local anterior, mandar de volta.

DEFINITION: crippled, maimed.
ORIGIN: From ana (in the sense of intensity) and peros (maimed); crippled.

BDAG.en: a cripple.
BDAG.pt: um aleijado, um coxo.

DEFINITION: to lie down, recline (at a dinner-table), fall back upon (the breast of another person reclining at dinner).
ORIGIN: From ana and pipto; to fall back, i.e. Lie down, lean back.

BDAG.en: to recline on a couch to eat, lie down, recline, esp. at a meal; to lean while reclining at a meal, lean, lean back.
BDAG.pt: reclinar-se num divã para comer, deitar-se, recostar-se, especialmente durante uma refeição; apoiar-se ao reclinar-se durante uma refeição, inclinar-se, encostar-se.

DEFINITION: to fill up, make up, complete the measure of, fulfill, carry out the commands (provisions, etc.) of.
ORIGIN: From ana and pleroo; to complete; by implication, to occupy, supply; figuratively, to accomplish (by coincidence ot obedience).

BDAG.en: to complete the quantity of something, make complete; to carry out an agreement or obligation, fulfill; to supply what is lacking, fill a gap, replace; to occupy a place, occupy, fill.
BDAG.pt: completar a quantidade de algo, tornar completo; executar um acordo ou obrigação, cumprir; suprir o que falta, preencher uma lacuna, substituir; ocupar um lugar, ocupar, preencher.

DEFINITION: without (ground of) defense, indefensible, inexcusable.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of apologeomai; indefensible.

BDAG.en: without excuse, inexcusable.
BDAG.pt: sem desculpa, inexcusável.

DEFINITION: to unroll, roll back, unfold.
ORIGIN: From ana (in the sense of reversal) and ptusso; to unroll (a scroll or volume).

BDAG.en: unroll of a book in scroll form.
BDAG.pt: desenrolar um livro em formato de rolo.

DEFINITION: to kindle, set on fire, light.
ORIGIN: From ana and hapto; to enkindle.

BDAG.en: kindle.
BDAG.pt: acender, incendiar.

DEFINITION: uncountable, innumerable, that cannot be numbered.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of arithmeo; unnumbered, i.e. Without number.

BDAG.en: innumerable of the grains of sand on the seashore.
BDAG.pt: inumerável (referente aos grãos de areia na praia).

DEFINITION: to shake up, stir up, excite.
ORIGIN: From ana and seio; figuratively, to excite.

BDAG.en: to cause to be disturbed, stir up, disturb, upset, incite.
BDAG.pt: causar perturbação, agitar, perturbar, abalar, incitar.

DEFINITION: to pervert, subvert, dismantle, unsettle, overthrow, destroy.
ORIGIN: From ana (in the sense of reversal) and a derivative of skeuos; properly, to pack up (baggage), i.e. (by implication, and figuratively) to upset.

BDAG.en: lit. ‘tear down, dismantle’ then fig. to cause inward distress, upset, unsettle.
BDAG.pt: literalmente 'desmontar, desmantelar', depois figurativamente causar angústia interior, perturbar, abalar.

DEFINITION: to drag up, pull up, draw up, draw out.
ORIGIN: From ana and spao; to take up or extricate.

BDAG.en: draw/pull up. Of the sheet, which Peter saw in his vision (lifted up to heaven).
BDAG.pt: puxar/levantar (algo). Referente ao lençol que Pedro viu em sua visão (elevado ao céu).

DEFINITION: a standing up, a resurrection, a raising up, rising.
ORIGIN: From anistemi; a standing up again, i.e. (literally) a resurrection from death (individual, genitive case or by implication, (its author)), or (figuratively) a (moral) recovery (of spiritual truth).
USAGE: raised to life again, resurrection, rise from the dead, that should rise, rising again.

BDAG.en: a change for the better in status, rising up, rise; resurrection from the dead, resurrection
BDAG.pt: uma mudança de status para melhor, levantar-se, ascensão; ressurreição dentre os mortos, ressurreição

DEFINITION: (perhaps a political metaphor), to turn upside down, upset, unsettle.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of anistemi (in the sense of removal); properly, to drive out of home, i.e. (by implication) to disturb (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: trouble, turn upside down, make an uproar.

BDAG.en: to upset the stability of a pers. or group, disturb, trouble, upset
BDAG.pt: abalara estabilidade de uma pessoa ou grupo, perturbar, incomodar, transtornar

DEFINITION: to impede, crucify (again).

BDAG.en: build someth. up again after it has fallen, rebuild, restore; become erect from a bent position, straighten up
BDAG.pt: reconstruir algo depois que caiu, restaurar; tornar-se ereto de uma posição curvada, endireitar

DEFINITION: unholy, profane.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and hosios; wicked.

BDAG.en: unholy; wicked, revolting to God or to a well-minded person
BDAG.pt: profano, ímpio; perverso, revoltante para Deus ou para uma pessoa de bom senso

DEFINITION: forbearance, suspense or delay (of punishment), patience.
ORIGIN: From anechomai; self-restraint, i.e. Tolerance.

BDAG.en: a state of respite from someth. onerous or disagreeable, relief; a temporary cessation, pause; the act of being forbearing, forbearance, clemency, tolerance
BDAG.pt: um estado de alívio de algo oneroso ou desagradável, repouso; uma cessação temporária, pausa; o ato de ser tolerante, paciência, clemência, tolerância

DEFINITION: to resist, strive against, contend.
ORIGIN: From anti and agonizomai; to struggle against (figuratively) ("antagonize").

BDAG.en: to struggle against sin
BDAG.pt: lutar contra o pecado

DEFINITION: an exchange, purchasing price.
ORIGIN: From a compound of anti and allasso; an equivalent or ransom.

BDAG.en: something given in exchange; compensation
BDAG.pt: algo dado em troca; compensação

DEFINITION: to fill up in place of someone else, complete, supply.
ORIGIN: From anti and anapleroo; to supplement.

BDAG.en: take one’s turn in filling up someth., fill up on one’s part, supplement
BDAG.pt: fazer a sua parte em completar algo, completar por sua vez, suplementar

DEFINITION: to give back as an equivalent, recompense.
ORIGIN: From anti and apodidomi; to requite (good or evil).

BDAG.en: to practice reciprocity with respect to an obligation, repay, pay back, requite; to exact retribution, repay, pay back
BDAG.pt: praticar reciprocidade em relação a uma obrigação, retribuir, pagar de volta, recompensar; exigir retribuição, pagar de volta

DEFINITION: a gift in return (for another), a return, recompense, requital.
ORIGIN: From antapodidomi; a requital (properly, the thing).

BDAG.en: that which is given in requital for a benefit, repayment, reward; that which is given in return for behavior, recompense (as punishment); recompense (neutrally, of the last judgment)
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é dado em retribuição por um benefício, pagamento, recompensa; aquilo que é dado em retorno por um comportamento, compensação (como punição); recompensa (neutramente, do juízo final)

DEFINITION: a reward, recompense.
ORIGIN: From antapodidomi; requital (properly, the act).

BDAG.en: that which is given to someone in exchange for what has been done, repaying, reward; day of recompense of divine judgment
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é dado a alguém em troca do que foi feito, retribuição, recompensa; dia de retribuição do juízo divino

DEFINITION: to contradict, reply against, give a hostile answer.
ORIGIN: From anti and apokrinomai; to contradict or dispute.

BDAG.en: to answer in turn
BDAG.pt: responder por sua vez

DEFINITION: to speak or say in opposition, contradict (oppose, resist).
ORIGIN: From anti and epo; to refute or deny.

BDAG.en: to say someth. in reply, say in return, contradict someone
BDAG.pt: dizer algo em resposta, dizer em troca, contradizer alguém

DEFINITION: trans: to hold against; intrans: to withstand; mid: to hold out against, hold firmly to, cleave to.
ORIGIN: From anti and the middle voice of echo; to hold oneself opposite to, i.e. (by implication) adhere to; by extension to care for.

DEFINITION: (a) instead of, in return for, over against, opposite, in exchange for, as a substitute for, (b) on behalf, (c) wherefore, because.
ORIGIN: A primary particle; opposite, i.e. Instead or because of (rarely in addition to).
USAGE: for, in the room of. Often used in composition to denote contrast, requital, substitution, correspondence, etc.

BDAG.en: indicating replacement (instead of, in place of); indicating equivalence (for, as, in place of); indicating intervention (in behalf of, for someone); indicating reason (because of, for the purpose of); indicating result (wherefore, therefore, so then)
BDAG.pt: indicando substituição (em vez de, no lugar de); indicando equivalência (por, como, no lugar de); indicando intervenção (em favor de, para alguém); indicando razão (por causa de, com o propósito de); indicando resultado (portanto, por conseguinte)

DEFINITION: to throw at in opposition, exchange (words) with, perhaps: to compare.
ORIGIN: From anti and ballo; to bandy.
