BDAG.pt: partícula de transição/inferência (ilativa); 1 marcador de uma inferência feita com base no que precede (assim, então, consequentemente); b frequentemente em perguntas que tiram uma inferência do que precede; 2 para expressar resultado (então, como resultado); 3 para expressar algo tentador, talvez, concebivelmente

DEFINITION: an untranslatable interrogative particle implying anxiety or impatience.
ORIGIN: A form of ara, denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed.

BDAG.en: interrog. particle introducing direct questions (marker of a tone of suspense or impatience in interrogation)
BDAG.pt: partícula interrogativa que introduz perguntas diretas (marcador de um tom de suspense ou impaciência na interrogação)

DEFINITION: Arabia, a peninsula of Asia near Africa.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ( Arab); Arabia, a region of Asia.

BDAG.en: Arabia as a geogr. concept includes the territory west of Mesopotamia, east and south of Syria and Palestine, to the isthmus of Suez.
BDAG.pt: Arábia como conceito geográfico, inclui o território a oeste da Mesopotâmia, a leste e sul da Síria e Palestina, até o istmo de Suez.

DEFINITION: Ram, son of Hezron and father of Amminadab.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ram); Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Aram (in genealogy of Jesus)
BDAG.pt: Aram (na genealogia de Jesus)

DEFINITION: unsewn, without seam.
ORIGIN: From Arabia; an Arab or native of Arabia.

BDAG.en: an Arab
BDAG.pt: um Árabe

DEFINITION: to linger, delay, be idle.
ORIGIN: From argos; to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay.

BDAG.en: to stop doing something, slack off, become idle
BDAG.pt: cessar de fazer algo, diminuir o ritmo, tornar-se ocioso

DEFINITION: idle, lazy, thoughtless, unprofitable, injurious.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and ergon; inactive, i.e. Unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being without anything to do, unemployed, idle. 2 pert. to being unwilling to work, idle, lazy. 3 pert. to being unproductive, useless, worthless
BDAG.pt: 1 referente a estar sem nada para fazer, desempregado, ocioso. 2 referente a estar relutante em trabalhar, ocioso, preguiçoso. 3 referente a ser improdutivo, inútil, sem valor

DEFINITION: made of silver.
ORIGIN: From arguros; made of silver.

BDAG.en: made of silver, silver
BDAG.pt: feito de prata, prateado

DEFINITION: silver, a piece of silver, a shekel, money in general.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of arguros; silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. Drachma or shekel).

BDAG.en: 1 the precious metal known as silver, silver. 2 silver used as money, silver money, money gener.
BDAG.pt: 1 o metal precioso conhecido como prata, prata. 2 prata usada como dinheiro, dinheiro em prata, dinheiro em geral

DEFINITION: (lit: silver-cutter), a silversmith.
ORIGIN: From arguros and kopto; a beater (i.e. Worker) of silver.

BDAG.en: silversmith
BDAG.pt: prateiro

DEFINITION: silver as a metal.
ORIGIN: From argos (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or coin).

BDAG.en: 1 silver as a commodity, silver. 2 money made of silver, silver money, silver
BDAG.pt: 1 prata como mercadoria, prata. 2 dinheiro feito de prata, moeda de prata, prata

DEFINITION: Areopagus, or Mar's Hill, an open space on a hill in Athens where the supreme court was held.
ORIGIN: From Ares (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of pegnumi; rock of Ares, a place in Athens.

BDAG.en: the Areopagus or Hill of Ares
BDAG.pt: o Areópago ou Colina de Ares

DEFINITION: member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite.
ORIGIN: From Areios Pagos; an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill.

BDAG.en: Areopagite, member of the council or court of the Areopagus
BDAG.pt: Areopagita, membro do conselho ou tribunal do Areópago

DEFINITION: a desire to please, pleasing.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of aresko; complaisance.

BDAG.en: desire to do something that produces satisfaction, desire to please, obsequiousness (mostly pejorative); exceptional public service or expression of devotion (favorable)
BDAG.pt: desejo de fazer algo que produza satisfação, desejo de agradar, obsequiosidade (na maioria das vezes pejorativo); serviço público excepcional ou expressão de devoção (favorável)

DEFINITION: to please, with the idea of willing service rendered to others; hence almost: to serve.
ORIGIN: Probably from airo (through the idea of exciting emotion); to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so).

BDAG.en: to act in a fawning manner, win favor, please, flatter; to give pleasure/satisfaction, please, accommodate (often reflecting reciprocity in the Mediterranean world; pleasing God/Lord)
BDAG.pt: agir de maneira bajuladora, ganhar favor, agradar, bajular; dar prazer/satisfação, agradar, acomodar (muitas vezes refletindo reciprocidade no mundo mediterrâneo; agradar a Deus/Senhor)

DEFINITION: pleasing, satisfactory, acceptable.
ORIGIN: From aresko; agreeable; by implication, fit.

BDAG.en: pertaining to being satisfying, pleasing (e.g., doing what is pleasing to God)
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que é satisfatório, agradável (ex: fazer o que agrada a Deus)

DEFINITION: Aretas IV, King of the Nabataeans.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin; Aretas, an Arabian.

BDAG.en: Aretas (a name borne by Nabataean kings)
BDAG.pt: Areta (um nome usado por reis nabateus)

DEFINITION: goodness, a gracious act, virtue, uprightness.
ORIGIN: From the same as arrhen; properly, manliness (valor), i.e. Excellence (intrinsic or attributed).

BDAG.en: consummate ‘excellence’ or ‘merit’ within a social context, uncommon character worthy of praise, excellence of character, exceptional civic virtue; manifestation of divine power, miracle.
BDAG.pt: ‘Excelência’ consumada ou ‘mérito’ dentro de um contexto social; caráter incomum digno de louvor, excelência de caráter, virtude cívica excepcional; manifestação de poder divino, milagre.

DEFINITION: a lamb, sheep.
ORIGIN: Perhaps the same as arrhen; a lamb (as a male).

BDAG.en: lamb (as an animal for slaughter); used as a type of weakness (like lambs among wolves)
BDAG.pt: cordeiro (como animal para abate); usado como tipo de fraqueza (como cordeiros entre lobos)

DEFINITION: to number, count.
ORIGIN: From arithmos; to enumerate or count.

BDAG.en: count.
BDAG.pt: contar.

DEFINITION: a number, total.
ORIGIN: From airo; a number (as reckoned up).

BDAG.en: a cardinal number; a numerical total, number, total (including reference to numerology, e.g., 666)
BDAG.pt: um número cardinal; um total numérico, número, soma (incluindo referência à numerologia, ex: 666)

DEFINITION: Arimathea, probably a city near Jer.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ramah); Arimathaea (or Ramah), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Arimathea, a city in Judea; home of Joseph.
BDAG.pt: Arimateia, uma cidade na Judeia; lar de José.

DEFINITION: Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica in Macedonia.
ORIGIN: From the same as ariston and archo; best ruling; Aristarchus, a Macedonian.

BDAG.en: Aristarchus (of Thessalonica, companion of Paul)
BDAG.pt: Aristarchus (de Tessalônica, companheiro de Paulo)

DEFINITION: to breakfast, to take a meal.
ORIGIN: From ariston; to take the principle meal.

BDAG.en: to eat breakfast; to eat a meal, dine
BDAG.pt: tomar o café da manhã; comer uma refeição, jantar

DEFINITION: better, left, on the left.
ORIGIN: Apparently a comparative of the same as ariston; the left hand (as second-best).

BDAG.en: left (opp. to right), the left hand, the left side.
BDAG.pt: esquerdo (oposto a direito), a mão esquerda, o lado esquerdo.

DEFINITION: "best-counseling", Aristobulus, a Christian at Rome.
ORIGIN: From the same as ariston and boule; best counselling; Aristoboulus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Aristobulus; οἱ ἐκ τῶν Ἀριστοβούλου those who belong to (the household of) A. Ro 16:10.
BDAG.pt: Aristóbulo; οἱ ἐκ τῶν Ἀριστοβούλου aqueles que pertencem (à casa) de A. Ro 16:10.

DEFINITION: breakfast or a mid-day meal.
ORIGIN: Apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as arrhen; the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from eri ("early")), i.e. Luncheon.

BDAG.en: In early Gk. meal eaten early in the day (later called ἀκράτισμα, from the custom of dipping bread in wine), then the noon meal. 1 breakfast... 2 noon meal... and meal gener.
BDAG.pt: No grego antigo, refeição comida no início do dia (mais tarde chamada ἀκράτισμα, pelo costume de molhar pão em vinho), depois a refeição do meio-dia. 1 café da manhã... 2 refeição do meio-dia... e refeição em geral.

DEFINITION: sufficient, enough.
ORIGIN: From arkeo; satisfactory.

BDAG.en: enough, sufficient, adequate.
BDAG.pt: suficiente, bastante, adequado.

DEFINITION: to keep off, assist; to suffice; pass: to be satisfied.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to airo through the idea of raising a barrier); properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory).
USAGE: be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient.

BDAG.en: 1 act. be enough, sufficient, adequate... 2 pass. be satisfied/content w. someth.
BDAG.pt: 1 ativo ser suficiente, bastar, ser adequado... 2 passivo estar satisfeito/contente com algo.

DEFINITION: a bear.
ORIGIN: Probably from arkeo; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity).

BDAG.en: a bear Rv 13:2 (Da 7:5).
BDAG.pt: um urso (Rv 13:2; Dn 7:5).

DEFINITION: a chariot, vehicle.
ORIGIN: Probably from airo (perhaps with a (as a particle of union) prefixed); a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare harmos)).

BDAG.en: carriage, a traveling-chariot; especially a war-chariot.
BDAG.pt: carruagem, um carro de viagem; especialmente um carro de guerra.

DEFINITION: Har-Magedon.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (har and Mgiddown); Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a symbolic name.

DEFINITION: to fit, join; mid: (the middle indicating deep personal interest) to espouse, betroth; mid: to take a wife, give in marriage.
ORIGIN: From harmos; to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth).

BDAG.en: 1 to be appropriate as part of a whole, fit, fit in intr.... 2 to bring into close association, join trans.... Of betrothal and marriage join or give in marriage, betroth.
BDAG.pt: 1 ser apropriado como parte de um todo, caber, ajustar-se (intransitivo)... 2 juntar em estreita associação, unir (transitivo)... No que diz respeito a noivado e casamento: unir ou dar em casamento, noivar.

DEFINITION: a joint of the body.
ORIGIN: From the same as harma; an articulation (of the body).

BDAG.en: joint.
BDAG.pt: junta, articulação.

DEFINITION: (a) to deny (a statement), (b) to repudiate (a person, or belief).
ORIGIN: Perhaps from a (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of rheo; to contradict, i.e. Disavow, reject, abnegate.

BDAG.en: to refuse consent to something, refuse, disdain; to state that something is not true, deny; to disclaim association with a person or event, deny, repudiate, disown; to refuse to pay any attention to, disregard, renounce; to deny, disregard oneself (be untrue to oneself)
BDAG.pt: recusar consentimento a algo, recusar, desprezar; declarar que algo não é verdade, negar; negar associação com uma pessoa ou evento, repudiar, renegar; recusar dar atenção, desconsiderar, renunciar; negar-se a si mesmo (ser infiel a si mesmo)

DEFINITION: (originally: a little lamb, but diminutive force was lost), a lamb.
ORIGIN: Diminutive from aren; a lambkin.

BDAG.en: a sheep of any age, sheep, lamb, in our lit. only in imagery: in Rv a designation of Christ... of the Christian community.
BDAG.pt: uma ovelha de qualquer idade, ovelha, cordeiro; na nossa literatura, apenas em imagens: em Apocalipse, uma designação de Cristo... da comunidade cristã.

DEFINITION: to plow.
ORIGIN: From arotron; to plow.

BDAG.en: to plow
BDAG.pt: lavrar, arar

DEFINITION: a plow.
ORIGIN: From aroo (to till); a plow.

BDAG.en: a plow.
BDAG.pt: um arado.

DEFINITION: the act of plundering; plunder, spoil, robbery.
ORIGIN: From harpazo; pillage (properly abstract).

BDAG.en: the act of seizure, robbery, plunder; the product of seizure, what has been stolen, plunder; the inner state of mind that leads to seizure, greediness, rapacity
BDAG.pt: o ato de apreensão, roubo, pilhagem; o produto da apreensão, aquilo que foi roubado, despojo; o estado mental interior que leva à apreensão, cobiça, rapacidade

DEFINITION: spoil, an object of eager desire, a prize.
ORIGIN: From harpazo; plunder (properly concrete).

BDAG.en: a violent seizure of property, robbery; something to which one can claim or assert title by gripping or grasping, something claimed (prize, gain); (mystical) rapture (less probable)
BDAG.pt: uma apreensão violenta de propriedade, roubo; algo a que se pode reivindicar título agarrando ou segurando, algo reivindicado (prêmio, ganho); (rapto místico) (menos provável)

DEFINITION: to seize, snatch, obtain by robbery.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of haireomai; to seize (in various applications).
USAGE: catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force).

BDAG.en: to snatch, seize, i.e. take suddenly and vehemently, or take away (steal, carry off, drag away); to grab or seize suddenly so as to remove or gain control, snatch/take away forcefully; (of rescue from threatening danger); (passive) be caught up; to grasp something quickly, eagerly, with desire
BDAG.pt: arrebatamento, apoderar-se, isto é, tomar de repente e veementemente, ou levar embora (roubar, carregar, arrastar); agarrar ou tomar de repente para remover ou ganhar controle, arrebatar/levar à força; (resgate de perigo ameaçador); (passivo) ser arrebatado; agarrar algo rápida, ansiosamente, com desejo

DEFINITION: rapacious, ravenous; a robber, an extortioner.
ORIGIN: From harpazo; rapacious.

BDAG.en: rapacious, ravenous; robber, swindler or rogue (subst.)
BDAG.pt: rapaz, voraz; ladrão, vigarista ou patife (substantivo)

DEFINITION: an earnest, earnest-money, a large part of the payment, given in advance as a security that the whole will be paid afterwards.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (arabown); a pledge, i.e. Part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest.

BDAG.en: payment of part of a purchase price in advance, first installment, deposit, down payment, pledge, which secures a legal claim or validates a contract; figuratively, a guarantee or first installment of the Spirit.
BDAG.pt: pagamento de parte de um preço de compra adiantado, primeira parcela, depósito, sinal, penhor, que assegura um direito legal ou valida um contrato; figurativamente, garantia ou primeira parcela do Espírito.

DEFINITION: without seam, of a single piece.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as rhaphis; unsewed, i.e. Of a single piece.

BDAG.en: seamless
BDAG.pt: sem costura

DEFINITION: male, man.
ORIGIN: Arsen (ar'-sane) probably from airo; male (as stronger for lifting).

BDAG.en: male (opposed to female); used as a substantive for males.
BDAG.pt: masculino (oposto a feminino); usado como substantivo para designar homens.

DEFINITION: not to be uttered (because too sacred), secret, unspeakable, unspoken.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and the same as rhetos; unsaid, i.e. (by implication) inexpressible.

BDAG.en: inexpressible (beyond human powers); or not to be spoken (holy, sacred).
BDAG.pt: inexprimível (além das capacidades humanas); ou não deve ser dito (santo, sagrado).

DEFINITION: infirm, sick, ill, feeble, sickly.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of rhonnumi; infirm.

BDAG.en: sick, ill, literally powerless.
BDAG.pt: doente, enfermo, literalmente sem força.

DEFINITION: a male engaging in same-gender sexual activity; a sodomite, pederast.
ORIGIN: From arrhen and koite; a sodomite.
USAGE: abuser of (that defile) self with mankind.

BDAG.en: a male who engages in sexual activity with a person of his own sex; pederast, one who assumes the dominant role in same-sex activity.
BDAG.pt: um homem que se envolve em atividade sexual com uma pessoa do seu próprio sexo; pederasta, aquele que assume o papel dominante em atividade homossexual.

DEFINITION: "gift of Artemis", Artemas, a friend of the apostle Paul.
ORIGIN: Contracted from a compound of Artemis and doron; gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian.

BDAG.en: Artemas, a friend of Paul.
BDAG.pt: Artemas, um amigo de Paulo.

DEFINITION: Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus, typifying fertility (she had no relation with the other Artemis, the maiden huntress, to whom corresponded the Latin Diana).
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as artemon; prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities.

BDAG.en: Artemis, a deity whose worship was widespread (Diana is her Roman name).
BDAG.pt: Ártemis, uma divindade cujo culto era generalizado (Diana é o seu nome romano).

DEFINITION: something hung up or fastened, a foresail.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of arti; properly, something ready (or else more remotely from airo (compare artos); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel.

BDAG.en: prob. foresail.
BDAG.pt: provavelmente vela de proa.

DEFINITION: now, just now, at this moment.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of airo (compare artos) through the idea of suspension; just now.
USAGE: this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present.

BDAG.en: temporal adverb: 1. ref. to the immediate past, just (now). 2. ref. to the immediate present, at once, immediately, now. 3. later Gk. uses ἄ. as ref. to the present in general, now, at the present time.
BDAG.pt: advérbio temporal: 1. referente ao passado imediato, acabara de. 2. referente ao presente imediato, de uma vez, imediatamente, agora. 3. o grego posterior usa ἄ. como referência ao presente em geral, agora, no tempo presente.

DEFINITION: newly begotten, newly born.
ORIGIN: From arti and gennetos; just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert.

BDAG.en: newborn
BDAG.pt: recém-nascido

DEFINITION: perfect, complete, fitted, ready.
ORIGIN: From arti; fresh, i.e. (by implication) complete.

BDAG.en: pert. to being well fitted for some function, complete, capable, proficient=able to meet all demands
BDAG.pt: relativo a estar bem ajustado para alguma função, completo, capaz, proficiente=capaz de satisfazer todas as exigências

DEFINITION: bread, a loaf, food.
ORIGIN: From airo; bread (as raised) or a loaf.

BDAG.en: 1. a baked product produced fr. a cereal grain, bread, loaf of bread; also bread-offering; also of the bread of the eucharist; also any kind of food or nourishment, food gener. 2. means of support, support, livelihood. 3. reward for labor, reward, proceeds.
BDAG.pt: 1. um produto assado produzido a partir de um cereal, pão, pão em forma de rosca; também oferta de pão; também do pão da eucaristia; também qualquer tipo de alimento ou sustento, comida em geral. 2. meio de subsistência, suporte, modo de vida. 3. recompensa pelo trabalho, remuneração, rendimento.

DEFINITION: prop: to arrange, make ready; to season, flavor.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of airo; to prepare, i.e. Spice (with stimulating condiments).

BDAG.en: gener. ‘prepare’ w. connotation of skillful use of material. Of food preparation to add condiments to someth., season, salt.
BDAG.pt: em geral, ‘preparar’ com a conotação de uso hábil do material. Na preparação de alimentos, adicionar condimentos a algo, temperar, salgar.

DEFINITION: Arphaxad, a son of Shem and an ancestor of Christ.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Arpakshad); Arphaxad, a post-diluvian patriarch.

BDAG.en: Arphaxad, son of Shem (Gen 10:22, 24), in genealogy of Jesus Lk 3:36.
BDAG.pt: Arfaxade, filho de Sem (Gênesis 10:22, 24), na genealogia de Jesus (Lucas 3:36).

DEFINITION: a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel.
ORIGIN: From archo and aggelos; a chief angel.

BDAG.en: a member of the higher ranks in the celestial hierarchy, chief angel, archangel
BDAG.pt: um membro dos escalões superiores na hierarquia celestial, anjo principal, arcanjo.

DEFINITION: original, primitive, ancient.
ORIGIN: From arche; original or primeval.

BDAG.en: pert. to what has existed from the beginning or for a long time, old; pert. to what was in former times, long ago, ancient; the ancients, people of ancient times, of old; what is old
BDAG.pt: relativo ao que existe desde o início ou por muito tempo, antigo; relativo ao que era em tempos passados, há muito tempo, antigo; os antigos, pessoas de tempos antigos, de outrora; aquilo que é antigo

DEFINITION: Archelaus, Herod Archelaus, son and successor of Herod to, reigned over Judea from 4 B.C. to A.D. 6 and died before A.D. 18.
ORIGIN: From archo and Laodikeus; people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish king.

BDAG.en: Archelaus, ... in NT, the son of Herod I, ethnarch of Judaea, Idumaea and Samaria fr. his father’s death in 4 b.c. to a.d. 6, when he was deposed by Emperor Augustus
BDAG.pt: Herodes Arquelau, ... no NT, o filho de Herodes I, etnarca da Judeia, Idumeia e Samaria, desde a morte de seu pai em 4 a.C. até 6 d.C., quando foi deposto pelo Imperador Augusto.

DEFINITION: (a) rule (kingly or magisterial), (b) plur: in a quasi-personal sense, almost: rulers, magistrates, (c) beginning.
ORIGIN: From archomai; (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank).
USAGE: beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule.

BDAG.en: 1 the commencement of something as an action, process, or state of being, beginning, i.e. a point of time at the beginning of a duration... 2 one with whom a process begins, beginning fig., of persons... 3 the first cause, the beginning... 4 a point at which two surfaces or lines meet, corner... 5 a basis for further understanding, beginning... 6 an authority figure who initiates activity or process, ruler, authority... 7 the sphere of one’s official activity, rule, office, or better domain, sphere of influence
BDAG.pt: 1 o começo de algo como uma ação, processo ou estado de ser, início, ou seja, um ponto no tempo no começo de uma duração... 2 aquele com quem um processo começa, início figurado, de pessoas... 3 a primeira causa, o princípio... 4 um ponto onde duas superfícies ou linhas se encontram, canto... 5 uma base para maior compreensão, o princípio... 6 uma figura de autoridade que inicia uma atividade ou processo, governante, autoridade... 7 a esfera da atividade oficial, governo, cargo de alguém, ou melhor, domínio, esfera de influência.

DEFINITION: originator, author, founder, prince, leader.
ORIGIN: From arche and ago; a chief leader.

BDAG.en: 1 one who has a preeminent position, leader, ruler, prince... 2 one who begins something that is first in a series, thereby providing impetus for further developments... 3 one who begins or originates, hence the recipient of special esteem in the Gr-Rom. world, originator, founder
BDAG.pt: 1 aquele que tem uma posição de destaque, líder, governante, príncipe... 2 aquele que inicia algo que é o primeiro em uma série, fornecendo assim um ímpeto para desenvolvimentos futuros... 3 aquele que começa ou origina, daí o destinatário de estima especial no mundo greco-romano, originador, fundador.

DEFINITION: high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs.
ORIGIN: From arche and a derivative of hieros; high-priestly.

BDAG.en: highpriestly (pertaining to the high priest's family).
BDAG.pt: sumo sacerdotal (pertencente à família do sumo sacerdote).

DEFINITION: high priest, chief priest.
ORIGIN: From arche and hiereus; the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest.
USAGE: chief (high) priest, chief of the priests.

BDAG.en: one who serves as head priest, high priest (of a gentile or Israelite, sometimes president of the Sanhedrin); by fig. extension, of Christ, who serves as high priest by atoning for the sins of humans; a priest of high rank, chief priest (in Israel’s cultic life, often plural to denote members of the Sanhedrin belonging to highpriestly families).
BDAG.pt: aquele que serve como sumo sacerdote (de um gentio ou israelita, às vezes presidente do Sinédrio); por extensão figurada, de Cristo, que serve como sumo sacerdote expiando os pecados dos humanos; um sacerdote de alta patente, principal sacerdote (na vida cultual de Israel, frequentemente no plural para designar membros do Sinédrio que pertenciam a famílias de sumos sacerdotes).

DEFINITION: the chief shepherd.
ORIGIN: From arche and poimen; a head shepherd.

BDAG.en: chief shepherd (of Christ).
BDAG.pt: chefe dos pastores (de Cristo).

DEFINITION: "horse-ruler", Archippus, a Christian at Colossae.
ORIGIN: From arche and hippos; horse-ruler; Archippus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Archippus (a common name), a Christian in Colossae
BDAG.pt: Arquípo (um nome comum), um cristão em Colossos

DEFINITION: a leader of the synagogue, a leader connected with the synagogue: sometimes there was only one, and the name was in some cases merely honorary.
ORIGIN: From arche and sunagoge; director of the synagogue services.

BDAG.en: leader/president of a synagogue, an official whose duty it was esp. to take care of the physical arrangements for the worship services.
BDAG.pt: líder/presidente de uma sinagoga, um oficial cuja função era especialmente cuidar dos arranjos físicos para os cultos.

DEFINITION: master-builder, architect.
ORIGIN: From arche and tekton; a chief constructor, i.e. "architect".

BDAG.en: master builder
BDAG.pt: mestre construtor

DEFINITION: head of a custom-house, chief tax-gatherer or publican.
ORIGIN: From arche and telones; a principle tax-gatherer.

BDAG.en: chief tax collector.
BDAG.pt: chefe dos cobradores de impostos.

DEFINITION: master of ceremonies at a dinner, master of the feast.
ORIGIN: From arche and a compound of treis and klino (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches); director of the entertainment.

BDAG.en: head waiter, butler (the slave who was responsible for managing a banquet).
BDAG.pt: copeiro-chefe, mordomo (o escravo responsável por gerenciar um banquete).

DEFINITION: commence, rule.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of archo (through the implication, of precedence); to commence (in order of time).

DEFINITION: to rule, to begin.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to be first (in political rank or power).

BDAG.en: to rule or govern, w. implication of special status; to initiate an action, process, or state of being, begin (mid.).
BDAG.pt: governar ou reinar, com implicação de status especial; iniciar uma ação, processo ou estado de ser, começar (meio).

DEFINITION: a ruler, governor, leader, leading man; with the Jews, an official member (a member of the executive) of the assembly of elders.
ORIGIN: Present participle of archo; a first (in rank or power).

BDAG.en: one who is in a position of leadership, esp. in a civic capacity: ruler, lord, prince; one who has administrative authority, leader, official.
BDAG.pt: aquele que está em posição de liderança, especialmente em capacidade cívica: governante, senhor, príncipe; aquele que tem autoridade administrativa, líder, oficial.

DEFINITION: spice, perfume.
ORIGIN: From airo (in the sense of sending off scent); an aromatic.

BDAG.en: any kind of fragrant substance, fragrant spice/salve/oil/perfume, esp. used in embalming the dead
BDAG.pt: qualquer tipo de substância fragrante, especiaria/bálsamo/óleo/perfume fragrante, especialmente usado no embalsamamento dos mortos

DEFINITION: Asa, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah about 900 B.C. for 41 years.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Aca'); Asa, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: unshaken, immovable.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of saleuo; unshaken, i.e. (by implication) immovable (figuratively).

BDAG.en: not being subject to movement, immovable; not subject to alteration of essential nature or being, unshakable, enduring.
BDAG.pt: não sujeito a movimento, imóvel; não sujeito à alteração da natureza ou ser essencial, inabalável, duradouro.

DEFINITION: inextinguishable, unquenchable.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of sbennumi; not extinguished, i.e. (by implication) perpetual.

BDAG.en: of something whose state of being cannot be nullified or stopped: of fire inextinguishable; of lime that has not been disintegrated by addition of water: unslaked lime.
BDAG.pt: de algo cujo estado de ser não pode ser anulado ou parado: de fogo inextinguível; de cal que não foi desintegrada pela adição de água: cal virgem.

DEFINITION: impiety, irreverence, ungodliness, wickedness.
ORIGIN: From asebes; impiety, i.e. (by implication) wickedness.

BDAG.en: a lack of reverence for deity and hallowed institutions as displayed in sacrilegious words and deeds: impiety.
BDAG.pt: uma falta de reverência à divindade e às instituições santificadas, manifestada em palavras e atos sacrílegos: impiedade.

DEFINITION: to be impious, to be ungodly.
ORIGIN: From asebes; to be (by implied act) impious or wicked.
USAGE: commit (live, that after should live) ungodly.

BDAG.en: to violate the norms of a proper or professed relation to deity, act impiously
BDAG.pt: violar as normas de uma relação própria ou professada com a divindade, agir impiedosamente

DEFINITION: impious, ungodly, wicked.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of sebomai; irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked.

BDAG.en: pert. to violating norms for a proper relation to deity, irreverent, impious, ungodly.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à violação das normas para uma relação adequada com a divindade, irreverente, ímpio, profano.

DEFINITION: (outrageous conduct, conduct shocking to public decency, a wanton violence), wantonness, lewdness.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a presumed selges (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other vices).

BDAG.en: lack of self-constraint which involves one in conduct that violates all bounds of what is socially acceptable, self-abandonment, licentiousness.
BDAG.pt: falta de autocontrole que envolve alguém em conduta que viola todos os limites do que é socialmente aceitável, autoabandono, licenciosidade.

DEFINITION: (lit: unmarked, unstamped), undistinguished, obscure, unknown.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and the base of semaino; unmarked, i.e. (figuratively) ignoble.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being unmarked, insignificant, unimportant; 2 of words or statements whose meaning or intent is not readily grasped, obscure, unclear
BDAG.pt: 1. Relativo a não ter marca, insignificante, sem importância; 2. De palavras ou declarações cujo significado ou intenção não são facilmente compreendidos, obscuro, pouco claro.

DEFINITION: Asher, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the Twelve Tribes.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Asher); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe.

BDAG.en: Asher son of Jacob, ancestor of the tribe to which the prophet Anna belonged.
BDAG.pt: Aser, filho de Jacó, ancestral da tribo à qual pertencia a profetisa Ana.

DEFINITION: want of strength, weakness, illness, suffering, calamity, frailty.
ORIGIN: From asthenes; feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty.

BDAG.en: 1 a state of debilitating illness, sickness, disease; 2 incapacity for someth. or experience of limitation, weakness a gener.; 3 lack of confidence or feeling of inadequacy, weakness.
BDAG.pt: 1. Um estado de doença debilitante, enfermidade, moléstia; 2. Incapacidade para algo ou experiência de limitação, fraqueza em geral; 3. Falta de confiança ou sentimento de inadequação, fraqueza.

DEFINITION: to be weak (physically: then morally), to be sick.
ORIGIN: From asthenes; to be feeble (in any sense).
USAGE: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.

BDAG.en: 1 to suffer a debilitating illness, be sick; 2 to experience some personal incapacity or limitation, be weak; 3 to experience lack of material necessities, be in need
BDAG.pt: 1. Sofrer uma doença debilitante, estar doente; 2. Experimentar alguma incapacidade pessoal ou limitação, ser fraco; 3. Experimentar falta de necessidades materiais, estar em necessidade.

DEFINITION: weakness, infirmity, doubt, hesitation.
ORIGIN: From astheneo; a scruple of conscience.

BDAG.en: weakness; pl., of conscientious scruples caused by weakness of faith
BDAG.pt: Fraqueza; no plural, escrúpulos de consciência causados pela fraqueza da fé.

DEFINITION: (lit: not strong), (a) weak (physically, or morally), (b) infirm, sick.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and the base of sthenoo; strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral).
USAGE: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing).

BDAG.en: weak, powerless; 1. sick, ill; 2. experiencing some incapacity or limitation, weak (of physical weakness; also applied to the flesh, woman, physical presence); of spirit beings that can do nothing; of relative ineffectiveness (weak, feeble, ineffectual); of the inner life: helpless in a moral sense; weakness in faith; without influence.
BDAG.pt: fraco, sem poder; 1. doente, enfermo; 2. experimentando alguma incapacidade ou limitação, fraco (de fraqueza física; também aplicado à carne, mulher, presença física); de seres espirituais que nada podem fazer; de ineficácia relativa (fraco, desprovido de vigor, ineficaz); da vida interior: indefeso num sentido moral; fraqueza na fé; sem influência.

DEFINITION: the Roman province of Asia, roughly the western third of Asia Minor.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore.

BDAG.en: Asia, a Rom. province in western Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Ásia, uma província romana na Ásia Menor ocidental.

DEFINITION: belonging to the Roman province Asia.
ORIGIN: From Asia; an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia.

BDAG.en: a person from the Roman province of Asia, Asian
BDAG.pt: Uma pessoa da província romana da Ásia, asiático.

DEFINITION: an Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome and the Emperor in the Roman province Asia.
ORIGIN: From Asia and arche; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Asiarch, plainly equiv. to the ἀρχιερεὺς Ἀσίας
BDAG.pt: Asiarca, claramente equivalente ao sumo sacerdote da Ásia.

DEFINITION: either: lack or wheat, lack of food (the literal meaning), or: abstinence from food, a fast, loss of appetite, sea-sickness (the extended meaning).
ORIGIN: From asitos; fasting (the state).

BDAG.en: lack of appetite
BDAG.pt: Falta de apetite.

DEFINITION: without eating, fasting.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and sitos; without (taking) food.

BDAG.en: without eating, fasting
BDAG.pt: Sem comer, em jejum.

DEFINITION: to train, practice, exercise.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as skeuos; to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive).

BDAG.en: to apply oneself w. commitment to some activity, practice, engage in
BDAG.pt: Aplicar-se com dedicação a alguma atividade, praticar, engajar-se.

DEFINITION: a wine-skin, leather bottle.
ORIGIN: From the same as askeo; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle.

BDAG.en: a leather bag, esp. wine-skin
BDAG.pt: Um odre de couro, especialmente de vinho.

DEFINITION: joyfully, with delight, gladly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of the base of hedone; with pleasure.

BDAG.en: gladly (to receive someone gladly).
BDAG.pt: alegremente (receber alguém com prazer).

DEFINITION: unskilled, unwise, foolish.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and sophos; unwise.

BDAG.en: lacking proper discernment, unwise, foolish.
BDAG.pt: falta de discernimento apropriado, insensato, tolo.

DEFINITION: to greet, salute, pay respects to, welcome.
ORIGIN: From a (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of spao; to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome.

BDAG.en: greet, welcome; to engage in hospitable recognition; to express happiness about the arrival of something (welcome, greet).
BDAG.pt: saudar, dar boas-vindas; engajar-se em reconhecimento hospitaleiro; expressar felicidade pela chegada de algo (acolher, saudar).

DEFINITION: a greeting, salutation.
ORIGIN: From aspazomai; a greeting (in person or by letter).

BDAG.en: greeting (personal salutations or written greetings).
BDAG.pt: saudação (saudações pessoais ou correspondências escritas).

DEFINITION: unstained, undefiled, spotless, pure.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and spiloo; unblemished (physically or morally).

BDAG.en: spotless, without defect (of outward condition); pure, without fault (of inward character); unspotted by the world.
BDAG.pt: imaculado, sem defeito (de condição exterior); puro, sem culpa (de caráter interior); sem mácula pelo mundo.

DEFINITION: an asp (hooded-snake, cobra).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp".

BDAG.en: 'asp, Egyptian cobra', generally of venomous snakes (venom of asps).
BDAG.pt: 'áspide, cobra egípcia', geralmente de serpentes venenosas (veneno de áspides).

DEFINITION: without libation, without truce, admitting of no truce.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of spendo; literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless.

BDAG.en: unwilling to negotiate a solution, irreconcilable.
BDAG.pt: indisposto a negociar uma solução, irreconciliável.

DEFINITION: a small coin equal to the tenth part of a drachma.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin.

BDAG.en: assarion, a Roman copper coin (worth very little).
BDAG.pt: assário, uma moeda de cobre romana (de pouco valor).

DEFINITION: nearer, close by.
ORIGIN: Neuter comparative of the base of eggus; more nearly, i.e. Very near.

BDAG.en: nearer, close
BDAG.pt: mais perto, próximo

DEFINITION: Assos, a port of Mysia, in the Roman province Asia.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia minor.

DEFINITION: to be unsettled, have no fixed abode, lead a vagabond life.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of histemi; to be non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless.

BDAG.en: to be without a permanent residence, be unsettled, be homeless
BDAG.pt: não ter residência fixa, ser instável, ser sem-abrigo

DEFINITION: (lit: belonging to the city; then: witty, clever), elegant, pretty, fair, fine, beautiful.
ORIGIN: From astu (a city); urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome.

BDAG.en: befitting a city (urbanus), good breeding, refinement, handsome, well-bred
BDAG.pt: apropriado para uma cidade (urbano), boa criação, refinamento, bonito, bem-educado

DEFINITION: a star.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of stronnumi; a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: a luminous body (other than the sun) visible in the sky, star, single star, planet
BDAG.pt: um corpo luminoso (exceto o sol) visível no céu, estrela, estrela singular, planeta

DEFINITION: (lit: unpropped), unsteady, unstable, unsettled.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of sterizo; unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating.

BDAG.en: unstable, weak (persons)
BDAG.pt: instável, fraco (pessoas)

DEFINITION: unloving, devoid of affection.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of stergo (to cherish affectionately); hard-hearted towards kindred.

BDAG.en: hardhearted, unfeeling, without regard for others (lacking good feelings)
BDAG.pt: insensível, impiedoso, sem consideração pelos outros (carente de bons sentimentos)

DEFINITION: to miss the mark, miss aim, make a false aim, fail.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and stoichos (an aim); to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth.

BDAG.en: 'miss the mark', go astray by departing from moral or spiritual standards, miss, fail, deviate, depart
BDAG.pt: 'errar o alvo', desviar-se dos padrões morais ou espirituais, falhar, desviar, afastar-se

DEFINITION: a flash of lightning, brightness, luster.
ORIGIN: From astrapto; lightning; by analogy, glare.

BDAG.en: lightning illuminating the whole sky; proceeding from God’s throne; accompanying cosmic phenomena; type of the greatest speed and brilliance; fiery lightning; of a lamp light.
BDAG.pt: Relâmpago que ilumina todo o céu; procedente do trono de Deus; acompanhando fenômenos cósmicos; tipo de velocidade e brilho máximos; relâmpago de fogo; luz de lâmpada.

DEFINITION: to flash (with, then like, lightning), be lustrous.
ORIGIN: Probably from aster; to flash as lightning.

BDAG.en: flash, gleam; lightning flashing; of clothing gleam like lightning.
BDAG.pt: Fagulhar, brilhar; relâmpago cintilante; de vestes que brilham como relâmpago.

DEFINITION: a star.
ORIGIN: Neuter from aster; properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial).

BDAG.en: star, constellation, also single star; w. sun and moon; normally showing sailors the way at night; typical of a large number; the constellation of the god Raphain; of the harmonious stellar movements created by God.
BDAG.pt: Estrela, constelação, também estrela única; com sol e lua; normalmente guiando os marinheiros à noite; típico de grande número; a constelação do deus Reifã; do movimento harmonioso das estrelas criado por Deus.

DEFINITION: "incomparable", Asyncritus, a Christian at Rome.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of sugkrino; incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Asyncritus (Proper Name).
BDAG.pt: Asíncrito (Nome Próprio).

DEFINITION: dissonant, discordant; met: at variance.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and sumphonos; inharmonious (figuratively).

BDAG.en: 'discordant'; in disagreement w.; they disagreed w. each other.
BDAG.pt: Discordante; em desacordo com; eles discordaram um do outro.

DEFINITION: unintelligent, without wisdom, unwise, undiscerning (implying probably moral defect).
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and sunetos; unintelligent; by implication, wicked.

BDAG.en: void of understanding, senseless, foolish, implying also a lack of high moral quality; senseless, faithless; without understanding of the future; foolish.
BDAG.pt: Sem entendimento, insensato, tolo, implicando também falta de qualidade moral elevada; insensatos, infiéis; sem entendimento do futuro; tolo.

DEFINITION: not covenanting, untrue to an agreement, treacherous.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of suntithemai; properly, not agreed, i.e. Treacherous to compacts.

BDAG.en: pert. to such as renege on their word, faithless (does not keep an agreement)
BDAG.pt: pertencente àqueles que renunciam à sua palavra, infiel (não cumpre um acordo)

DEFINITION: safety, security, reliability, firmness.
ORIGIN: From asphales; security (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: security against stumbling/falling; a stable and salutary circumstance, safety, security; stability of idea or statement, certainty, truth; detention that restricts movement, security; securely locked.
BDAG.pt: Segurança contra tropeçar/cair; uma circunstância estável e salvadora, segurança; estabilidade de ideia ou afirmação, certeza, verdade; detenção que restringe o movimento, segurança; trancado com segurança.

DEFINITION: (lit: unfailing), safe, reliable, trustworthy, certain, sure.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail"); secure (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: pert. to being stable, firm (anchor); the sure foundation; fig. pert. to expression that ensures certainty about someth., certain; pert. to being in someone’s best interest, safe, secure.
BDAG.pt: Pertencente ao que é estável, firme (âncora); o fundamento seguro; fig. pertencente à expressão que garante certeza sobre algo, certo; pertencente ao melhor interesse de alguém, seguro.

DEFINITION: to make safe (secure, fast).
ORIGIN: From asphales; to render secure.

BDAG.en: to ensure security by preventive measures; fasten, secure; make secure, against tampering; to cause to be safe, safeguard, watch over
BDAG.pt: assegurar a segurança por meio de medidas preventivas; prender, fixar; tornar seguro, contra adulteração; fazer com que esteja seguro, salvaguardar, vigiar

DEFINITION: safely, securely, assuredly, certainly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from asphales; securely (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: securely, guard someone securely; lead away under guard; assuredly, certainly, of intellectual and emotive aspects.
BDAG.pt: Seguramente, guardar alguém seguramente; levar sob custódia; com certeza, certamente, quanto aos aspectos intelectuais e emotivos.

DEFINITION: to act improperly, be unseemly, behave unbecomingly (or even dishonorably); perhaps: to consider (something) unseemly.
ORIGIN: From askemon; to be (i.e. Act) unbecoming.

BDAG.en: behave disgracefully, dishonorably, indecently; if anyone thinks he is behaving dishonorably toward his fianceé.
BDAG.pt: Comportar-se de forma vergonhosa, desonrosa, indecente; se alguém pensa que está se comportando desonrosamente com sua noiva.

DEFINITION: unseemly behavior, unseemliness, indecency, shame, nakedness, an indecent (lewd) act.
ORIGIN: From askemon; an indecency; by implication, the pudenda.

BDAG.en: behavior that elicits disgrace, shameless deed; appearance that deviates from a standard, unbecoming appearance, abnormality, embarrassing condition; a state of disgrace, disgracefulness, associated w. nakedness; someth. considered too private for public exposure, nakedness (euphem.= genitals)
BDAG.pt: comportamento que provoca desgraça, ato vergonhoso; aparência que se desvia de um padrão, aparência inadequada, anormalidade, condição embaraçosa; um estado de desgraça, indignidade, associado à nudez; algo considerado muito privado para exposição pública, nudez (eufemismo = genitais)

DEFINITION: shapeless, unseemly.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of echo (in the sense of its congener schema); properly, shapeless, i.e. (figuratively) inelegant.

BDAG.en: ‘shameful, unpresentable, indecent’, or ‘unmentionable’, opp. εὐσχήμων; applied esp. to sexual matters; the unpresentable parts i.e. those that elicit special modesty, genitalia
BDAG.pt: 'vergonhoso, apresentável, indecente', ou 'impronunciável', oposto a εὐσχήμων; aplicado especialmente a assuntos sexuais; as partes não apresentáveis, isto é, aquelas que provocam modéstia especial, genitália

DEFINITION: wantonness, profligacy, wastefulness.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of sozo; properly, unsavedness, i.e. (by implication) profligacy.

BDAG.en: wastefulness; reckless abandon, debauchery, dissipation, profligacy, esp. exhibited in convivial gatherings; debauchery; wild living; flood of dissipation.
BDAG.pt: Desperdício; abandono irresponsável, libertinagem, dissipação, prodigalidade, especialmente exibido em reuniões sociais; libertinagem; vida desregrada; torrente de dissipação.

DEFINITION: prodigally, with prodigal living, wastefully.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the same as asotia; dissolutely.

BDAG.en: wastefully, prodigally (of a spendthrift lifestyle)
BDAG.pt: desperdiçadamente, prodigamente (de um estilo de vida esbanjador)

DEFINITION: (lit: to march out of order; then: to riot, rebel), behave disorderly, neglect duty, be careless (or idle) in habits.
ORIGIN: From ataktos; to be (i.e. Act) irregular.

BDAG.en: to violate prescribed or recognized order, behave inappropriately; not treat in a free-wheeling manner; to support his claim, he states that he ‘worked night and day so as not to be a burden to them’
BDAG.pt: violar a ordem prescrita ou reconhecida, comportar-se inadequadamente; não tratar de maneira irrestrita; para sustentar sua alegação, ele afirma que 'trabalhou noite e dia para não ser um fardo para eles'

DEFINITION: (lit: out of order), disorderly, slack (in performance of duty).
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of tasso; unarranged, i.e. (by implication) insubordinate (religiously).

BDAG.en: ‘not in the proper order’; disorderly, insubordinate; undisciplined impulse
BDAG.pt: 'fora da ordem apropriada'; desordenado, insubordinado; impulso indisciplinado

DEFINITION: in a disorderly manner, irregularly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from ataktos, irregularly (morally).

BDAG.en: in defiance of good order, disorderly, holding religious services without regard to established times arbitrarily; behave irresponsibly apparently without respect for established custom or received instruction, as the qualifying clause and… of us indicates; freeloading, sponging
BDAG.pt: em desafio à boa ordem, desordenadamente, realizando serviços religiosos sem levar em conta os tempos estabelecidos arbitrariamente; comportar-se irresponsavelmente aparentemente sem respeito ao costume estabelecido ou instrução recebida, como indica a cláusula qualificadora e... de nós; aproveitando-se, parasitando

DEFINITION: childless.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and teknon; childless.

BDAG.en: childless
BDAG.pt: sem filhos, estéril

DEFINITION: to direct gaze, look steadily.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a particle of union) and teino (to stretch); to gaze intently.
USAGE: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes.

BDAG.en: look intently at, stare at something or someone
BDAG.pt: olhar atentamente, fixar o olhar em algo ou alguém

DEFINITION: apart from, without.
ORIGIN: A particle probably akin to aneu; aloof, i.e. Apart from (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: without; apart fr. the crowd; without a purse; without God, apart fr. God’s will
BDAG.pt: sem; à parte da multidão; sem bolsa; sem Deus, à parte da vontade de Deus

DEFINITION: to disgrace, treat disgracefully, dishonor, insult; to despise.
ORIGIN: From atimos; to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat.
USAGE: despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.

BDAG.en: deprive someone of honor or respect, to dishonor/shame, an especially grievous offense in the strongly honor-shame oriented Semitic and Gr-Rom. societies
BDAG.pt: privar alguém de honra ou respeito, desonrar/envergonhar, uma ofensa especialmente grave nas sociedades semíticas e greco-romanas fortemente orientadas pela honra e vergonha

DEFINITION: disgrace, dishonor; a dishonorable use.
ORIGIN: From atimos; infamy, i.e. (subjectively) comparative indignity, (objectively) disgrace.

BDAG.en: a state of dishonor or disrespect, dishonor; a disaster in Gr-Rom. society; of things, a vessel to which no special value is attached (for ordinary use); shameful passions (=passions that disgrace a pers.); it is a disgrace for him; in humiliation
BDAG.pt: um estado de desonra ou desrespeito, desonra; um desastre na sociedade Greco-Romana; de coisas, um vaso ao qual não se atribui valor especial (para uso comum); paixões vergonhosas (=paixões que desonram uma pessoa); é uma desgraça para ele; em humilhação

DEFINITION: without honor, dishonored.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and time; (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured.
USAGE: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree).

BDAG.en: pert. to being without honor or respect, dishonored, despised, of pers. in disrepute; pert. to being considered relatively unimportant, insignificant of things that do not elicit special admiration or attention, comp. held in less esteem (of parts of the body)
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar sem honra ou respeito, desonrado, desprezado, de pessoas em descrédito; pertencente a ser considerado relativamente sem importância, insignificante de coisas que não despertam admiração ou atenção especial, comparado a ter menos estima (de partes do corpo)

DEFINITION: to dishonor, treat shamefully.
ORIGIN: From atimos; used like atimazo, to maltreat.

BDAG.en: Mng. same as ἀτιμάζω (q.v.); be disgraced
BDAG.pt: Significado igual a ἀτιμάζω (ver); ser desgraçado

DEFINITION: breath, steam, vapor.
ORIGIN: From the same as aer; mist.

BDAG.en: vapor; smoky vapor (like that of a volcanic eruption); typical of what passes away; steam that rises from a pot, typical of nothingness
BDAG.pt: vapor; vapor esfumaçado (como o de uma erupção vulcânica); típico do que desaparece; vapor que sobe de uma panela, típico do nada

DEFINITION: (lit: that cannot be cut), an indivisible part of time, a moment.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and the base of tomoteros; uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time).

BDAG.en: ‘uncut’; then of someth. that is viewed as such a unit that it cannot be cut, esp. because of smallness (e.g. particle of matter, uncompounded word) indivisible; used of time by Aristot. (Phys. 236a, 6 ἐν ἀτόμῳ) in a moment
BDAG.pt: 'não cortado'; então de algo visto como uma unidade que não pode ser cortada, especialmente por causa de pequenez (ex. partícula de matéria, palavra não composta) indivisível; usado de tempo por Aristóteles (Física 236a, 6 ἐν ἀτόμῳ) em um momento

DEFINITION: (lit: out of place, unusual, unbecoming), improper, unrighteous, perverse.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and topos; out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked.

BDAG.en: from the perception of something ‘not in its proper place’, ‘out of place’, it is but a short step to the metaph. sense of something that is ‘unusual’, i.e. does not correspond to normal expectation; 2 pertaining to being behaviorally out of place, evil, wrong, improper
BDAG.pt: da percepção de algo 'fora do lugar apropriado', 'fora do lugar', é um pequeno passo para o sentido metafórico de algo que é 'incomum', ou seja, não corresponde à expectativa normal; 2 relativo a ser comportamentalmente fora do lugar, mau, errado, impróprio

DEFINITION: Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia.
ORIGIN: From Attalos (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in Pamphylia.

BDAG.en: Attalia, a seaport in Pamphylia
BDAG.pt: Atália, um porto marítimo na Panfília

DEFINITION: to flash, gleam, shine forth, appear white, bright; but perhaps: to see, see clearly, discern.
ORIGIN: From auge; to beam forth (figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 see (related to brightness or clarity); 2 intr. shine forth
BDAG.pt: 1 ver (relacionado ao brilho ou clareza); 2 intransitivo brilhar

DEFINITION: brightness, daylight, dawn.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn.

BDAG.en: dawn (lit. ‘light’ esp. ‘daylight’)
BDAG.pt: alvorada (literalmente 'luz', especialmente 'luz do dia')

DEFINITION: Augustus, a title conferred on the first Roman Emperor, C. Iulius Octauianus, denoting sanctity (almost divinity).
ORIGIN: From Latin ("august"); Augustus, a title of the Roman emperor.

BDAG.en: Augustus, title given Octavian, first Rom. emperor
BDAG.pt: Augusto, título dado a Otaviano, o primeiro imperador romano

DEFINITION: self-satisfied, arrogant, stubborn.
ORIGIN: From autos and the base of hedone; self-pleasing, i.e. Arrogant.

BDAG.en: self-willed, stubborn, arrogant
BDAG.pt: obstinado, teimoso, arrogante

DEFINITION: self-chosen, of one's own accord.
ORIGIN: From autos and the same as hairetizo; self-chosen, i.e. (by implication) voluntary.
USAGE: of own accord, willing of self.

BDAG.en: pertaining to being self-chosen, of one’s own accord
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser autônomo/auto-escolhido, de livre e espontânea vontade

DEFINITION: to domineer, govern, have mastery over.
ORIGIN: From a compound of autos and an obsolete hentes (a worker); to act of oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate.

BDAG.en: to assume a stance of independent authority, give orders to, dictate to
BDAG.pt: assumir uma postura de autoridade independente, dar ordens a, ditar a

DEFINITION: to play the flute, pipe.
ORIGIN: From aulos; to play the flute.

BDAG.en: to play the flute (for someone, to dance)
BDAG.pt: tocar a flauta (para alguém, para dançar)

DEFINITION: court-yard, fore-court, sheep-fold; but it may be understood as: palace, house.
ORIGIN: From the same as aer; a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a mansion.

BDAG.en: an area open to the sky, freq. surrounded by buildings... enclosed open space, courtyard
BDAG.pt: uma área aberta para o céu, frequentemente cercada por edifícios... espaço aberto cercado, pátio

DEFINITION: a flute player.
ORIGIN: From auleo; a flute-player.

BDAG.en: flutist for festive occasions or for mourning
BDAG.pt: flautista para ocasiões festivas ou para luto

DEFINITION: to lodge in the open, lodge, pass the night.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from aule; to pass the night (properly, in the open air).

BDAG.en: orig. of spending the night in the courtyard, then also of temporary lodging, with context indicating whether outdoors ('bivouac') or indoors; gener. to have a temporary sleeping arrangement, spend the night; to have housing, without special ref. to nighttime, live, stay
BDAG.pt: originalmente de passar a noite no pátio (αὐλή), então também de alojamento temporário, com contexto indicando se ao ar livre ('acampar') ou em local coberto; em geral, ter um arranjo temporário para dormir, passar a noite; ter moradia, sem referência especial à noite, morar, ficar

DEFINITION: a pipe, flute.
ORIGIN: From the same as aer; a flute (as blown).

BDAG.en: flute
BDAG.pt: flauta

DEFINITION: (a) to cause to increase, become greater (b) to increase, grow.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow ("wax"), i.e. Enlarge (literal or figurative, active or passive).

DEFINITION: increasing, increase, growth.
ORIGIN: From auzano; growth.

BDAG.en: growth, increase; to cause growth
BDAG.pt: crescimento, aumento; causar crescimento

DEFINITION: tomorrow.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the same as aer (meaning a breeze, i.e. The morning air); properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of hemera) to-morrow.

BDAG.en: next day; a brief time lapse without ref. to a nocturnal period, soon, in a short time
BDAG.pt: o dia seguinte; um breve lapso de tempo sem referência a um período noturno, logo, em pouco tempo

DEFINITION: grim, severe, strict, exacting, harsh, rigid.
ORIGIN: From a (presumed) derivative of the same as aer (meaning blown); rough (properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe.

BDAG.en: pert. to being strict in requirement, punctilious, strict, used esp. of persons who practice rigid personal discipline or are strict in the supervision of others
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser rigoroso na exigência, pontual, severo, usado especialmente de pessoas que praticam disciplina pessoal rígida ou são rigorosas na supervisão de outros

DEFINITION: self-sufficiency, independence, contentment.
ORIGIN: From autarkes; self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence.

BDAG.en: self-sufficiency in the sense of 'independence', then generally 'sufficiency', external state of having what is adequate, sufficiency, a competence; internal state of being content w. one’s circumstances, contentment, self-sufficiency
BDAG.pt: autossuficiência no sentido de 'independência', depois genericamente 'suficiência', estado externo de ter o que é adequado, suficiência, competência; estado interno de estar contente com as próprias circunstâncias, contentamento, autossuficiência

DEFINITION: self-sufficient, contented, satisfied, independent.
ORIGIN: From autos and arkeo; self-complacent, i.e. Contented.

BDAG.en: content, self-sufficient
BDAG.pt: contente, autossuficiente

DEFINITION: (perhaps a new coinage), self-condemned.
ORIGIN: From autos and a derivative or katakrino; self-condemned.

BDAG.en: self-condemned
BDAG.pt: autocondenado

DEFINITION: acting of one's own will, of its own accord.
ORIGIN: From autos and the same as maten; self-moved ("automatic"), i.e. Spontaneous.

BDAG.en: pert. to something that happens without visible cause, by itself
BDAG.pt: pertencente a algo que acontece sem causa visível, por si mesmo

DEFINITION: an eye-witness.
ORIGIN: From autos and optanomai; self-seeing, i.e. An eye-witness.

BDAG.en: eyewitness
BDAG.pt: testemunha ocular

DEFINITION: (1) self (emphatic) (2) he, she, it (used for the third person pronoun) (3) the same.
ORIGIN: From the particle au (perhaps akin to the base of aer through the idea of a baffling wind) (backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the comparative heautou) of the third person, and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons.
USAGE: her, it(-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy-)self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at, - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which. Compare hautou.

BDAG.en: reflexive pronoun: 'self'; intensive marker, setting an item off from everything else through emphasis and contrast, self, used in all persons, genders, and numbers; of bodily presence, come in person; of one whose action is independent or significant without ref. to something else; of one viewed as a solitary figure '(be) by oneself, alone'
BDAG.pt: pronome reflexivo: 'próprio/a'; marcador intensivo, separando um item de todo o resto através de ênfase e contraste, eu mesmo/você mesmo/ele mesmo, usado em todas as pessoas, gêneros e números; de presença corporal, vir pessoalmente; de alguém cuja ação é independente ou significativa sem referência a outra coisa; de alguém visto como figura solitária '(estar) por si mesmo, sozinho'

DEFINITION: there, here.
ORIGIN: Genitive (i.e. Possessive) of autos, used as an adverb of location; properly, belonging to the same spot, i.e. In this (or that) place.

BDAG.en: here (designating a position relatively near or far)
BDAG.pt: aqui (designando uma posição relativamente próxima ou distante)

DEFINITION: her own, his own, their own, themselves, they.
ORIGIN: Contracted for heautou; self (in some oblique case or reflexively, relation).
USAGE: her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them(-selves), they.

BDAG.en: here (designating a position relatively near or far)
BDAG.pt: aqui (designando uma posição relativamente próxima ou distante)

DEFINITION: with one's own hand.
ORIGIN: From autos and cheir; self-handed, i.e. Doing personally.

BDAG.en: with one's own hand.
BDAG.pt: com as próprias mãos.

DEFINITION: (poetical, lit: dry and parched; then: squalid and rough), dingy, murky, obscure, dark, funereal.
ORIGIN: From auchmos (probably from a base akin to that of aer) (dust, as dried by wind); properly, dirty, i.e. (by implication) obscure.

BDAG.en: dry, dark or gloomy (of a place); very dreary.
BDAG.pt: seco, escuro ou sombrio (de um lugar); muito desolador/lúgubre.

DEFINITION: to take from, take away.
ORIGIN: From apo and haireomai; to remove (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to detach by force, take away, remove, cut off; to cause a state or condition to cease, take away, do away with; to deprive by taking.
BDAG.pt: desprender à força, tirar, remover, cortar; fazer cessar um estado ou condição, tirar, eliminar; privar ao tomar/retirar.

DEFINITION: invisible, unseen, hidden.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and phaino; non-apparent).

BDAG.en: invisible, hidden
BDAG.pt: invisível, escondido

DEFINITION: to cause to disappear, hide, remove; to disfigure (probably by leaving unwashed for a long period), destroy.
ORIGIN: From aphanes; to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed).

BDAG.en: to cause something to disappear, destroy, perish; to cause to become unrecognizable through change in appearance, render invisible/unrecognizable
BDAG.pt: fazer algo desaparecer, destruir, perecer; fazer com que se torne irreconhecível através de mudança de aparência, tornar invisível/irreconhecível

DEFINITION: disappearing, disappearance, obliteration.
ORIGIN: From aphanizo; disappearance, i.e. (figuratively) abrogation.

BDAG.en: the condition of being no longer visible, frequently in the transferred sense destruction.
BDAG.pt: a condição de não ser mais visível, frequentemente no sentido figurado de destruição.

DEFINITION: disappearing, invisible, hidden.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of phaino; non-manifested, i.e. Invisible.

BDAG.en: invisible; vanish.
BDAG.pt: invisível; desaparecer/evaporar-se.

DEFINITION: a place of sitting apart, a privy, drain.
ORIGIN: From a compound of apo and the base of hedraios; a place of sitting apart, i.e. A privy.

BDAG.en: toilet, latrine.
BDAG.pt: vaso sanitário, latrina.

DEFINITION: severity, severe treatment.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and pheidomai; unsparingness, i.e. Austerity (asceticism).

BDAG.en: from 'spare nothing', hence lavishness or severe treatment (asceticism of the body)
BDAG.pt: de 'não poupar nada', daí extravagância ou tratamento severo (ascetismo do corpo)

DEFINITION: simplicity, sincerity.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a (as a negative particle) and phellos (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, i.e. (figuratively) simplicity.

BDAG.en: simplicity of heart
BDAG.pt: simplicidade de coração

DEFINITION: a sending away, a letting go, a release, pardon, complete forgiveness.
ORIGIN: From aphiemi; freedom; (figuratively) pardon.

BDAG.en: the act of freeing and liberating from something that confines, release from captivity; the act of freeing from an obligation, guilt, or punishment, pardon, cancellation; forgiveness of sins i.e. cancellation of the guilt of sin
BDAG.pt: o ato de libertar e soltar de algo que confina, libertação da cativeiro; o ato de libertar de uma obrigação, culpa ou punição, perdão, cancelamento; perdão dos pecados, ou seja, cancelamento da culpa do pecado

DEFINITION: a band, fastening (hence, possibly: a ligament), joint.
ORIGIN: From haptomai; probably a ligament (as fastening).

BDAG.en: ligament, lit. ‘joint, connection’
BDAG.pt: ligamento, literalmente 'articulação, conexão'

DEFINITION: indestructibility, incorruptibility; hence: immortality.
ORIGIN: From aphthartos; incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence; (figuratively) genuineness.

BDAG.en: the state of not being subject to decay/dissolution/interruption, incorruptibility, immortality
BDAG.pt: o estado de não estar sujeito à decomposição/dissolução/interrupção, incorruptibilidade, imortalidade

DEFINITION: indestructible, imperishable, incorruptible; hence: immortal.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of phtheiro; undecaying (in essence or continuance).

BDAG.en: imperishable, incorruptible, immortal (pert. to imperviousness to corruption and death)
BDAG.pt: imperecível, incorruptível, imortal (relativo à impermeabilidade à corrupção e à morte)

DEFINITION: (a) to send away, (b) to let go, release, permit to depart, (c) to remit, forgive, (d) to permit, suffer.
ORIGIN: From apo and hiemi (to send; an intensive form of eimi, to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow).
USAGE: cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up.

BDAG.en: Gener., to cause someone or someth. to undergo separation. 1 to dismiss or release someone or someth. from a place or one’s presence; b w. imperson. obj. give up, emit obj. the spirit; c in a legal sense divorce wife. 2 to release from legal or moral obligation or consequence, cancel, remit, pardon the loan, a debt. Also of remission of the guilt (debt) of sin, in OT and NT predom. in sense of divine forgiveness. 3 to move away, w. implication of causing a separation, leave, depart from a lit. of pers. or physical things as obj.; b fig. of imperson. obj. give up, abandon; leave (behind) to go on to someth. else; neglect also omit what is more important in the law. 4 to have someth. continue or remain in a place. Leave standing/leaving. Leave (behind) w. pers. obj. as orphans. 5 to convey a sense of distancing through an allowable margin of freedom, leave it to someone to do something, let, let go, allow, tolerate.
BDAG.pt: De modo geral, fazer com que alguém ou algo sofra separação. 1 dispensar ou libertar alguém ou algo de um lugar ou da presença de alguém; b com objeto impessoal, desistir, emitir objeto o espírito; c em sentido legal, divorciar a esposa. 2 libertar de obrigação ou consequência legal ou moral, cancelar, remeter, perdoar o empréstimo, uma dívida. Também de remissão da culpa (dívida) do pecado, no Antigo Testamento e no Novo Testamento predominantemente no sentido de perdão divino. 3 afastar, com a implicação de causar separação, deixar, partir de um literal de pessoa ou coisas físicas como objeto; b figurado de objeto impessoal desistir, abandonar; deixar (para trás) para prosseguir para outra coisa; negligenciar também omitir o que é mais importante na lei. 4 fazer com que algo continue ou permaneça em um lugar. Deixar parado/deixado. Deixar (para trás) com objeto pessoal como órfãos. 5 transmitir um senso de distanciamento através de uma margem permissível de liberdade, deixar a critério de alguém fazer algo, permitir, soltar, deixar, tolerar.

DEFINITION: to arrive at, reach, come to.
ORIGIN: From apo and the base of hikanos; to go (i.e. Spread) forth (by rumor).

BDAG.en: to arrive at a certain point, reach (the central mng. ‘come to’ in ref. to physical space is not used in the NT) of a report εἴς τινα someone the report of your obedience has reached (become known to) everyone. With ref. to passage of time so that some of them (the healed) remained alive to our own time.
BDAG.pt: chegar a um certo ponto, alcançar (o sentido central de ‘vir a’ em referência ao espaço físico não é usado no NT) de um relatório a alguém o relatório de sua obediência alcançou (tornou-se conhecido por) todos. Com referência à passagem do tempo, de modo que alguns deles (os curados) permaneceram vivos até o nosso tempo.

DEFINITION: not loving that which is good.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and philagathos; hostile to virtue.
USAGE: despiser of those that are good.

BDAG.en: pert. to lack of generous interest in the public good, without interest in the (public) good.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à falta de interesse generoso no bem público, sem interesse no bem (público).

DEFINITION: not loving money, not avaricious.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and philarguros; unavaricious.
USAGE: without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.

BDAG.en: not loving money, not greedy.
BDAG.pt: não amar o dinheiro, não ser ávido por dinheiro (não avarento).

DEFINITION: arrival, by implication departure.
ORIGIN: From aphikneomai; properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication) departure.

BDAG.en: arrival (usu. of ‘arrival’; in our lit. the point from which one moves is emphasized departure)
BDAG.pt: Chegada (geralmente de ‘chegada’; na nossa literatura, o ponto de onde se parte é enfatizada como partida).

DEFINITION: to make to stand away, draw away, repel, take up a position away from, withdraw from, leave, abstain from.
ORIGIN: From apo and histemi; to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc..
USAGE: depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self.

BDAG.en: of action that results in the distancing of pers. or thing from pers., thing, place, or condition. 1 to cause someone to move from a reference point, trans., in our lit. in ref. to altering allegiance cause to revolt, mislead. 2 to distance oneself from some pers. or thing (mid. forms, and 2 aor., pf., and plupf. act.) intrans. a go away, withdraw; Desert someone; Fall away; b keep away; Fig. of moral conduct abstain.
BDAG.pt: de ação que resulta no distanciamento de pessoa ou coisa de pessoa, coisa, lugar ou condição. 1 fazer com que alguém se afaste de um ponto de referência, trans., em nossa literatura em referência a alterar aliança, causar revolta, desviar. 2 afastar-se de alguma pessoa ou coisa (formas médias, e 2 aor., pf., e plupf. ativo) intrans. a ir embora, retirar-se; Desertar alguém; Cair (desviar-se); b manter-se afastado; Fig. de conduta moral abster-se.

DEFINITION: suddenly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from aphanes (contraction); unawares, i.e. Unexpectedly.

BDAG.en: adv. pert. to a very brief interval between a state or event that precedes and one that follows, of a sudden, suddenly. Immediately, at once.
BDAG.pt: adv. pertencente a um intervalo muito breve entre um estado ou evento que precede e um que se segue, de repente, subitamente. Imediatamente, de uma vez.

DEFINITION: fearlessly, shamelessly, securely, tranquilly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a compound of a (as a negative particle) and phobos; fearlessly.

BDAG.en: adv. of ἄφοβος ‘without fear’ pert. to being without fear of what might happen, fearlessly; without cause to be afraid.
BDAG.pt: adv. de ἄφοβος ‘sem medo’ pertencente a não ter medo do que pode acontecer, destemidamente; sem motivo para ter medo.

DEFINITION: to assimilate, make like to.
ORIGIN: From apo and homoioo; to assimilate closely.

BDAG.en: make like/similar pass. become like, in past tenses be like, resemble.
BDAG.pt: tornar como/semelhante pass. tornar-se como, em tempos passados ser como, assemelhar-se.

DEFINITION: to look away from (something else) to, see distinctly.
ORIGIN: From apo and horao; to consider attentively.

BDAG.en: 1 to direct one’s attention without distraction, fix one’s eyes trustingly on someone. 2 to develop more precise knowledge about someth. in the offing, determine, see.
BDAG.pt: 1 direcionar a atenção sem distração, fixar os olhos com confiança em alguém. 2 desenvolver conhecimento mais preciso sobre algo iminente, determinar, ver.

DEFINITION: to mark off by boundaries from, set apart.
ORIGIN: From apo and horizo; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.

BDAG.en: to mark off or set apart as if by a line or boundary. 1 to remove one party from other parties so as to discourage or eliminate contact, separate, take away. Exclude, excommunicate. Pass., w. middle mng. be separate. 2 to select one pers. out of a group for a purpose, set apart, appoint.
BDAG.pt: demarcar ou separar como se por uma linha ou limite. 1 afastar uma parte de outras para desencorajar ou eliminar contato, separar, retirar. Excluir, excomungar. Na voz passiva, com sentido médio, estar separado. 2 selecionar uma pessoa de um grupo para um propósito, apartar, nomear.

DEFINITION: (a) a starting, a start, (b) cause, occasion, opportunity.
ORIGIN: From a compound of apo and hormao; a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively) an opportunity.

BDAG.en: a base or circumstance from which other action becomes possible, the starting-point or base of operations for an expedition, then gener. the resources needed to carry through an undertaking, occasion, opportunity for someth.
BDAG.pt: uma base ou circunstância a partir da qual outra ação se torna possível, o ponto de partida ou base de operações para uma expedição, depois geralmente os recursos necessários para realizar um empreendimento, ocasião, oportunidade para algo.

DEFINITION: to foam (at the mouth), froth.
ORIGIN: From aphros; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy).

BDAG.en: to produce a foam, foam (at the mouth) of a sick person, prob. in an epileptic seizure.
BDAG.pt: produzir espuma, babar (espuma na boca) de uma pessoa doente, provavelmente em uma crise epiléptica.

DEFINITION: foam, froth.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. Slaver.

BDAG.en: a frothy mass, foam (only of froth appearing at the mouth in epileptic seizures)
BDAG.pt: Uma massa espumosa, espuma (apenas da espuma que aparece na boca em convulsões epilépticas).

DEFINITION: want of sense, foolishness, impiety, wickedness.
ORIGIN: From aphron; senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness.

BDAG.en: the state of lack of prudence or good judgment, foolishness, lack of sense, moral and intellectual
BDAG.pt: O estado de falta de prudência ou bom senso, tolice, falta de sentido, moral e intelectual.

DEFINITION: senseless, foolish, inconsiderate.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and phren; properly, mindless, i.e. Stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving.

BDAG.en: pert. to lack of prudence or good judgment, foolish, ignorant
BDAG.pt: Pertencente à falta de prudência ou bom senso, tolo, ignorante.

DEFINITION: to fall asleep.
ORIGIN: From a compound of apo and hupnos; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber.

BDAG.en: fall asleep, drop off to sleep
BDAG.pt: Adormecer, cair no sono.

DEFINITION: soundless, voiceless, speechless, dumb.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and phone; voiceless, i.e. Mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning.

BDAG.en: pert. to making no sound with vocal chords, silent, mute; incapable of vocal utterance, mute of inanimate obj.; incapable of human speech, speechless
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a não emitir som com as cordas vocais, silencioso, mudo; incapaz de emissão vocal, mudo em objetos inanimados; incapaz de fala humana, sem fala.

DEFINITION: Ahaz, son of Jotham and father of Hezekiah.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Achaz); Achaz, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Ahaz, a king of Judah.
BDAG.pt: Acaz, um rei de Judá.

DEFINITION: the Roman Province Achaia, governed by a proconsul, and practically conterminous with modern Greece before 1912.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe.

BDAG.en: Achaia in NT the Rom. province created 146 b.c., including the most important parts of Greece, i.e. Attica, Boeotia (perh. Epirus) and the Peloponnese.
BDAG.pt: Acaia no NT, a província romana criada em 146 a.C., incluindo as partes mais importantes da Grécia, ou seja, Ática, Beócia (perto do Épiro) e o Peloponeso.

DEFINITION: "an Achaian", Achaicus, a Christian at Corinth.
ORIGIN: From Achaia; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Achaicus a Christian at Corinth.
BDAG.pt: Acáico, um cristão em Corinto.

DEFINITION: ungrateful, ungracious, unpleasing.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of charizomai; thankless, i.e. Ungrateful.

BDAG.en: ungrateful
BDAG.pt: ingrato

DEFINITION: Achim, son of Zadok and father of Eliud.
ORIGIN: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare Yowqiym); Achim, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: not made with hands.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and cheiropoietos; unmanufactured, i.e. Inartificial.

BDAG.en: not made by (human) hand. Of circumcision
BDAG.pt: não feito por mão (humana). Referente à circuncisão

DEFINITION: a mist, dimness, darkening.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract.

BDAG.en: 1 lit. someth. that comes upon one like a fog and obscures vision, mist. 2 fig. someth. that beclouds one’s understanding, mistiness
BDAG.pt: 1 lit. algo que vem como uma névoa e obscurece a visão, névoa. 2 fig. algo que obscurece o entendimento, neblina mental

DEFINITION: unprofitable, useless, unworthy.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and a derivative of chre (compare chreia); useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious.

BDAG.en: pert. to being of no use or profit, useless, worthless
BDAG.pt: pertencente a não ter utilidade ou proveito, inútil, sem valor

DEFINITION: (lit: to become sour, to turn, of milk), to be good for nothing, render useless; met: to become corrupt.
ORIGIN: From achreios; to render useless, i.e. Spoil.

BDAG.en: Pass. 1 make useless, outwardly, in symbolism. 2 of becoming a liability to society because of moral depravity become depraved, worthless of pers.
BDAG.pt: Passivo. 1 tornar inútil, externamente, em simbolismo. 2 tornar-se um fardo para a sociedade devido à depravação moral, tornar-se depravado, inútil de pessoas.

DEFINITION: unprofitable, useless, detrimental.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and chrestos; inefficient, i.e. (by implication) detrimental.
