BDAG.en: pert. to not serving any beneficial purpose, useless, worthless
BDAG.pt: pertencente a não servir a nenhum propósito benéfico, inútil, sem valor

DEFINITION: as far as, up to, until, during.
ORIGIN: Or achris akh'-rece; akin to akron (through the idea of a terminus); (of time) until or (of place) up to.
USAGE: as far as, for, in(-to), till, (even, un-)to, until, while. Compare mechri.

BDAG.en: a function word used to indicate an interval between two points (marker of continuous extent of time: until; marker of extension up to a certain point: as far as)
BDAG.pt: uma palavra funcional usada para indicar um intervalo entre dois pontos (marcador de extensão contínua de tempo: até; marcador de extensão até um certo ponto: até onde)

DEFINITION: chaff.
ORIGIN: Perhaps remotely from cheo (to shed forth); chaff (as diffusive).

BDAG.en: the husks of grain, chaff
BDAG.pt: as cascas do grão, palha/jó

DEFINITION: not guilty of falsehood, truthful.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and pseudos; veracious.

BDAG.en: free fr. all deceit, truthful, trustworthy
BDAG.pt: livre de todo engano, verdadeiro, digno de confiança

DEFINITION: wormwood.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity).

DEFINITION: lifeless, inanimate.
ORIGIN: From a (as a negative particle) and psuche; lifeless, i.e. Inanimate (mechanical).

BDAG.en: inanimate, lifeless
BDAG.pt: inanimado, sem vida

DEFINITION: Baal, chief deity of the Phoenicians and other Semitic nations.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ba'al); Baal, a Phoenician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry).

BDAG.en: Baal, a deity worshipped by the Semites generally, bitterly opposed by Elijah and later Hebrew prophets, [with the phrase] bow the knee before B.
BDAG.pt: Baal, uma divindade adorada pelos Semitas em geral, amargamente combatida por Elias e pelos profetas hebreus posteriores, [com a expressão] dobrar o joelho diante de B.

DEFINITION: (a) Babylon, the ancient city on the Euphrates, to which the people of Jerusalem, etc., were transported, (b) hence allegorically of Rome, from the point of view of the Christian people.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Babel); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldaea (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny)).

BDAG.en: Babylon, capital of Babylonia; also used for the country, [with the phrase] deportation to Babylonia. Among Israelites Rome began to take on the name and many of the characteristics of Babylon as a world-power hostile to God, denounced by the prophets. So also in 1 Peter 5:13. The association with Rome is preferred by most for Revelation, where B. is always called the Great (e.g., the Great City).
BDAG.pt: Babilônia, capital da Babilônia; também usada para o país, [com a expressão] deportação para a Babilônia. Entre os israelitas, Roma começou a assumir o nome e muitas das características da Babilônia como potência mundial hostil a Deus, denunciada pelos profetas. Assim também em 1 Pedro 5:13. A associação com Roma é preferida pela maioria para o Apocalipse, onde B. é sempre chamada a Grande (ex: a Grande Cidade).

DEFINITION: a step (of a stairway); hence: a stage in a career, a position.
ORIGIN: From the same as bathos; a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of dignity).

BDAG.en: a structured rest for the foot marking a stage in ascending or descending, step; a stage in intellectual or spiritual progress, grade, rank
BDAG.pt: um apoio estruturado para o pé que marca uma etapa na subida ou descida, degrau; uma etapa no progresso intelectual ou espiritual, grau, patente

DEFINITION: depth; deep water; met: fullness, immensity; an extreme degree; profundities, deep-laid plans.
ORIGIN: From the same as bathus; profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent; (figuratively) mystery.

BDAG.en: The space or distance beneath a surface, depth. Something nonphysical perceived to be so remote that it is difficult to assess, depth figuratively (e.g., extreme poverty; inexhaustibility of wealth; depths of divine knowledge; depths of God).
BDAG.pt: O espaço ou distância abaixo de uma superfície, profundidade. Algo não físico percebido como tão remoto que é difícil de avaliar, profundidade figurativamente (ex: pobreza extrema; inesgotabilidade da riqueza; profundezas do conhecimento divino; profundezas de Deus).

DEFINITION: to deepen, excavate.
ORIGIN: From bathus; to deepen.

BDAG.en: make deep and intransitively go down deep, dug deep.
BDAG.pt: tornar profundo e intransitivamente ir fundo, cavou profundamente.

DEFINITION: deep (lit. and met.); in the depths of the early morning, while still very early; profound.
ORIGIN: From the base of basis; profound (as going down), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: Pertaining to distance beneath a surface, deep (of a well). Pertaining to something nonphysical perceived to be so remote that it is difficult to assess, deep (e.g., the hidden depths of Satan). Pertaining to an extreme point on a scale of extent: profound, of sleep. At the extreme of, very, exceedingly (e.g., very early in the morning).
BDAG.pt: Pertencente à distância abaixo de uma superfície, profundo (de um poço). Pertencente a algo não físico percebido como tão remoto que é difícil de avaliar, profundo (ex: as profundezas ocultas de Satanás). Pertencente a um ponto extremo numa escala de extensão: profundo, de sono. No extremo de, muito, excessivamente (ex: muito cedo pela manhã).

DEFINITION: a palm branch.
ORIGIN: A diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of basis; a palm twig (as going out far).

BDAG.en: palm branch.
BDAG.pt: ramo de palmeira.

DEFINITION: Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates, a soothsayer in the Old Testament.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Bil'am); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher).

BDAG.en: Balaam, a seer. Viewed as a typical deceiver and false prophet.
BDAG.pt: Balaão, um vidente. Visto como um enganador típico e falso profeta.

DEFINITION: Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Balaq); Balak, a Moabite.

BDAG.en: Balak, a Moabite king, involved with Balaam.
BDAG.pt: Balak, um rei moabita, envolvido com Balaão.

DEFINITION: a purse, money-bag.
ORIGIN: Probably remotely from ballo (as a depository); a pouch (for money).

DEFINITION: lançar, jogar

BDAG.en: Generally to put something into motion by throwing. To cause to move from one location to another through forceful motion, throw (e.g., scatter seed, cast lots). To force out of or into a place, throw (away), drive out, expel (e.g., throw into prison). To put or place something in a location, put, place, apply, lay, bring (e.g., put money into the treasury; pour wine into skins).
BDAG.pt: Geralmente colocar algo em movimento através do arremesso. Fazer mover-se de um lugar para outro através de movimento forçado, lançar (ex: espalhar semente, lançar sortes). Forçar para fora ou para um lugar, jogar (fora), expulsar (ex: lançar na prisão). Colocar ou dispor algo em um local, pôr, colocar, aplicar, deitar, trazer (ex: colocar dinheiro no tesouro; verter vinho em odres).

DEFINITION: lit: to dip, submerge, but specifically of ceremonial dipping; to baptize.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of bapto; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. Fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism.

BDAG.en: In our literature only in ritual or ceremonial sense: 1. wash ceremonially for purpose of purification, wash, purify; 2. to use water in a rite for purpose of renewing or establishing a relationship w. God, plunge, dip, wash, baptize; 3. to cause someone to have an extraordinary experience akin to an initiatory water-rite, to plunge, baptize.
BDAG.pt: Em nossa literatura apenas em sentido ritual ou cerimonial: 1. lavar cerimonialmente com o propósito de purificação, lavar, purificar; 2. usar água em um rito com o propósito de renovar ou estabelecer um relacionamento com Deus, mergulhar, imergir, lavar, batizar; 3. causar em alguém uma experiência extraordinária semelhante a um rito iniciático de água, mergulhar, batizar.

DEFINITION: (the result of) a dipping or sinking.
ORIGIN: From baptizo; baptism (technically or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1. the ceremonious use of water for purpose of renewing or establishing a relationship w. God, plunging, dipping, washing, water-rite, baptism; 2. an extraordinary experience akin to an initiatory purification rite, a plunge, a baptism.
BDAG.pt: 1. o uso cerimonioso da água com o propósito de renovar ou estabelecer um relacionamento com Deus, imersão, mergulho, lavagem, rito de água, batismo; 2. uma experiência extraordinária semelhante a um rito iniciático de purificação, um mergulho, um batismo.

DEFINITION: dipping, washing (of a ceremonial character).
ORIGIN: From baptizo; ablution (ceremonial or Christian).

BDAG.en: 1. water-rite for purpose of purification, washing, cleansing, of dishes; 2. water-rite for purpose of renewing or establishing a relationship w. God, plunging experience, baptism burial with Christ in baptism.
BDAG.pt: 1. rito de água com o propósito de purificação, lavagem, limpeza, de pratos; 2. rito de água com o propósito de renovar ou estabelecer um relacionamento com Deus, experiência de imersão, batismo, sepultamento com Cristo no batismo.

DEFINITION: the baptizer, the Baptist, epithet used only of John, the son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, forerunner of Jesus.
ORIGIN: From baptizo; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner.

BDAG.en: Baptist, Baptizer, surname of John
BDAG.pt: Batista, Batizador, sobrenome de João

DEFINITION: (a) to dip, (b) to dye.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to whelm, i.e. Cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye).

BDAG.en: to dip something in a liquid, dip, dip in
BDAG.pt: mergulhar algo em um líquido, mergulhar, molhar em

DEFINITION: "son of Abba", Barabbas, the Israelite robber released instead of Christ.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (dikaiosis and Abba); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Barabbas = ‘son of Abba’ (Billerb, I 1031). 1 the prisoner released by Pilate
BDAG.pt: Barrabás = 'filho de Abba'. 1 o prisioneiro libertado por Pilatos

DEFINITION: Barak, one of the judges of Israel.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Baraq); Barak, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Barak, an Israelite general (Judg 4f), mentioned w. other heroes
BDAG.pt: Barak, um general israelita, mencionado com outros heróis

DEFINITION: Barachiah; his identity is uncertain, perhaps father of the Zechariah killed by the Zealots in the last Jewish War.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Berekyah); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Barachiah, name of the father of a certain Zechariah (Gk. Zacharias), who was killed in the temple
BDAG.pt: Barachias, nome do pai de um certo Zacarias, que foi morto no templo

DEFINITION: a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin; as adj: foreign.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e. Non-Greek).

BDAG.en: gener. pert. to what is foreign (esp. from the perspective of one who knows Greek and is familiar w. Hellenic culture) ‘non-Hellenic’ 1 w. focus on strangeness of language: pert. to using a language that is unintelligible to outsiders, foreign-speaking, of foreign tongue adj. or noun 2 w. focus on non-Hellenic association: pert. to not speaking Greek or participating in Gk. culture a adj. not Hellenic b subst. a non-Hellene, foreigner
BDAG.pt: Geralmente pertence ao que é estrangeiro (especialmente da perspectiva de quem conhece o grego e está familiarizado com a cultura helênica) 'não-helênico'. 1 com foco na estranheza da linguagem: pertence ao uso de uma língua incompreensível para os de fora, falante de língua estrangeira, de língua estrangeira (adjetivo ou substantivo). 2 com foco na associação não-helênica: pertence a não falar grego ou não participar da cultura grega. a adjetivo não helênico. b substantivo um não-heleno, estrangeiro.

DEFINITION: to weight, load, burden, lit. and met.
ORIGIN: From barus; to weigh down (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to press down as if with a weight, weigh down, burden a of physical weariness. b of a mental or psychological condition. Of minds that lose their alertness in drunkenness. Of misfortune or injustice.
BDAG.pt: Pressionar como se com um peso, pesar, sobrecarregar. a de cansaço físico. b de uma condição mental ou psicológica. De mentes que perdem sua agilidade na embriaguez. De infortúnio ou injustiça.

DEFINITION: heavily, with difficulty.
ORIGIN: Adverb from barus; heavily (figuratively).

BDAG.en: with difficulty ἀκούειν be hard of hearing
BDAG.pt: Com dificuldade. Ouvir ser de audição difícil (duro de ouvido).

DEFINITION: Bartholomew, surname of Nathanael, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (bar and Talmay); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomoeus, a Christian apostle.

BDAG.en: Bartholomew, name of one of the 12 apostles
BDAG.pt: Bartolomeu, nome de um dos 12 apóstolos.

DEFINITION: Bar-Jesus, the name of the magician and false prophet at Paphos in Cyprus; he is also called Elymas.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (bar and Yhowshuwa'); son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: Bar-Jonas, son of Jonas, the surname of Simon Peter.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (diakoneo and Malchos); son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: Barnabas, a Cypriote Jew, uncle of John Mark; his other name was Joseph.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (diakoneo and tacha); son of Nabas (i.e. Prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Barnabas, a Levite fr. Cyprus, whose first name was Joseph, uncle of John Mark and freq. cited in association w. Paul
BDAG.pt: Barnabé, um levita do Chipre, cujo primeiro nome era José, tio de João Marcos e frequentemente citado em associação com Paulo.

DEFINITION: a weight, burden, lit. or met.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as basis (through the notion of going down; compare bathos); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority.

BDAG.en: gener. ‘weight, burden’; in our lit. only fig. 1 experience of someth. that is particularly oppressive, burden 2 influence that someone enjoys or claims, claim of importance 3 a high point in a scale of evaluation, fullness
BDAG.pt: Geralmente 'peso, fardo'; em nossa literatura apenas figurado. 1 experiência de algo particularmente opressivo, fardo. 2 influência que alguém desfruta ou reivindica, alegação de importância. 3 um ponto alto em uma escala de avaliação, plenitude.

DEFINITION: "son of Sabba", Barsabbas, the surname of two Israelites Christian.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (bar and probably tsba'); son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites.

DEFINITION: "son of Timaeus", Bartimaeus, a beggar.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (diakoneo and kruphe); son of Timoeus (or the unclean); Bar-timoeus, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Bartimaeus (name of a blind man, where ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου explains it).
BDAG.pt: Bartimeu (nome de um cego, onde ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου o explica).

DEFINITION: overcharge.
ORIGIN: From barus; to burden (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to cause pressure through something weighty, burden, weigh down; weigh down with chains.
BDAG.pt: causar pressão por algo pesado, sobrecarregar, pesar; sobrecarregar com correntes.

DEFINITION: heavy, weighty, burdensome, lit. and met; violent, oppressive.
ORIGIN: From the same as baros; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave.

BDAG.en: gener. ‘heavy’, in our lit. in imagery and metaphors pert. esp. to things or pers. that are burdensome because of demands or threats. 1 pert. to being relatively weighty, heavy, regulations, rules, and legal matters 2 pert. to being a source of difficulty or trouble because of demands made. 3 pert. to being important because of unusual significance. 4 pert. to being of unbearable temperament, fierce, cruel, savage
BDAG.pt: Geralmente 'pesado', em nossa literatura em imagens e metáforas pert. especialmente a coisas ou pessoas que são onerosas devido a exigências ou ameaças. 1 pert. a ser relativamente pesado, regulamentos, regras e questões legais. 2 pert. a ser uma fonte de dificuldade ou problema devido às exigências feitas. 3 pert. a ser importante devido a um significado incomum. 4 pert. a ter um temperamento insuportável, feroz, cruel, selvagem.

DEFINITION: of great value.
ORIGIN: From barus and time; highly valuable.

BDAG.en: pert. to being of great value, very expensive, very precious
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a ser de grande valor, muito caro, muito precioso.

DEFINITION: to examine, as by torture; to torment; to buffet, as of waves.
ORIGIN: From basanos; to torture.

BDAG.en: to subject to punitive judicial procedure, torture; to subject to severe distress, torment, harass (a boat harassed by the waves; in diseases; of birth pangs; of Jesus as a threat to evil spirits; prophetic testimony as a source of annoyance).
BDAG.pt: submeter a procedimento judicial punitivo, tortura; submeter a aflição severa, tormento, assédio (um barco atormentado pelas ondas; em doenças; de dores de parto; de Jesus como ameaça aos espíritos malignos; testemunho profético como fonte de aborrecimento).

DEFINITION: torture, torment.
ORIGIN: From basanizo; torture.

BDAG.en: 1 infliction of severe suffering or pain associated with torture or torment, tormenting, torture 2 the severe pain experienced through torture, torment
BDAG.pt: 1 infligir sofrimento ou dor severa associada à tortura ou tormento, atormentar, tortura. 2 a dor severa experimentada através da tortura, tormento.

DEFINITION: one who tortures, a tormentor, jailor.
ORIGIN: From basanizo; a torturer.

BDAG.en: guard in a prison, freq. under orders to torture prisoners, oppressive jailer
BDAG.pt: Guarda em uma prisão, frequentemente sob ordens para torturar prisioneiros, carcereiro opressor.

DEFINITION: a touchstone (a dark stone used in testing metals), examination by torture, torture.
ORIGIN: Perhaps remotely from the same as basis (through the notion of going to the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture.

BDAG.en: severe pain occasioned by punitive torture, torture, torment (of the tortures in the nether world; descriptive of place in the nether world); general severe pain caused by something oppressive, severe pain, torment (of diseases).
BDAG.pt: dor severa causada por tortura punitiva, tortura, tormento (das torturas no submundo; descritivo do lugar no submundo); dor severa geral causada por algo opressivo, dor severa, tormento (de doenças).

DEFINITION: kingship, sovereignty, authority, rule, especially of God, both in the world, and in the hearts of men; hence: kingdom, in the concrete sense.
ORIGIN: From basileus; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: the act of ruling, kingship, royal power, royal rule (especially of God's rule, the royal reign of God, chiefly an eschatological concept, usually rendered ‘kingdom of God’); the greatest blessings conceivable are found in the kingdom; participation in its benefits; prerequisite for participation is repentance/becoming like children.
BDAG.pt: o ato de governar, realeza, poder real, domínio real (especialmente o domínio de Deus, o reinado real de Deus, principalmente um conceito escatológico, geralmente traduzido como ‘reino de Deus’); as maiores bênçãos concebíveis são encontradas no reino; participação em seus benefícios; pré-requisito para participação é arrependimento/tornar-se como crianças.

DEFINITION: king's court.
ORIGIN: Neuter of basileios; a palace.

DEFINITION: courtiers, palaces, a body of kings, royal.
ORIGIN: From basileus; kingly (in nature).

BDAG.en: pert. to a king, royal; used as a noun, the (royal) palace
BDAG.pt: pertencente a um rei, real; usado como substantivo, o (palácio) real

DEFINITION: a king, ruler, but in some passages clearly to be translated: emperor.
ORIGIN: Probably from basis (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively).

BDAG.en: have become kings
BDAG.pt: se tornaram reis

DEFINITION: (a) to rule, reign, (b) to reign over.
ORIGIN: From basileus; to rule (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to exercise authority at a royal level, be king, rule; to obtain royal power, become king
BDAG.pt: exercer autoridade a nível real, ser rei, reinar; obter poder real, tornar-se rei

DEFINITION: connected with a king, royal, regal, (a) an officer in the service of the king, (b) the king's country.
ORIGIN: From basileus; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent.

BDAG.en: royal; of a king’s official robe; royal robe; royal law; the king’s country; on the royal road; royal mark
BDAG.pt: real; da veste oficial de um rei; veste real; lei real; território do rei; na estrada real; marca real

DEFINITION: a queen.
ORIGIN: Feminine from basileuo; a queen.

BDAG.en: a female ruler within a specific area and with authority to pass her ruling power on to a successor, queen
BDAG.pt: uma governante feminina dentro de uma área específica e com autoridade para transmitir seu poder de governar a um sucessor, rainha

DEFINITION: a step; hence: a foot.
ORIGIN: From baino (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot.

BDAG.en: in various senses relating to ‘step’ but in our lit. that with which one steps, usually of the area below the ankle, foot
BDAG.pt: em vários sentidos relacionados a 'passo', mas em nossa literatura, aquilo com que se pisa, geralmente a área abaixo do tornozelo, pé

DEFINITION: to give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower.
ORIGIN: Akin to phasko; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations).

BDAG.en: to exert an evil influence through the eye, bewitch, as with the ‘evil eye'; to be resentful of someth. enjoyed by another, envy
BDAG.pt: exercer uma influência maligna através do olho, enfeitiçar, como com o 'mau-olhado'; sentir ressentimento por algo desfrutado por outro, invejar

DEFINITION: (a) to carry, bear, (b) to carry (take) away.
ORIGIN: Perhaps remotely derived from the base of basis (through the idea of removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.).

BDAG.en: pick up, take up; sustain a burden, carry, bear (a physical object, heaven, a cross, drugs, animals); be carried; be pregnant; bearing anything burdensome (a cross, legal requirements, Christian conduct); bear up under, endure (misfortune, evil, divine mysteries, weaknesses, judgment); carry, bear (marks, the name/message of Jesus); carry away, remove (a corpse, sandals); remove (disease); take surreptitiously, pilfer, steal
BDAG.pt: pegar, levantar; sustentar um fardo, carregar, suportar (um objeto físico, o céu, uma cruz, drogas, animais); ser carregado; estar grávida; carregar qualquer coisa onerosa (uma cruz, requisitos legais, conduta cristã); aguentar, suportar (infortúnio, mal, mistérios divinos, fraquezas, julgamento); carregar, portar (marcas, o nome/mensagem de Jesus); levar embora, remover (um cadáver, sandálias); remover (doença); pegar sorrateiramente, furtar, roubar

DEFINITION: a thorn bush or bramble.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub.

BDAG.en: a Hebr. liquid measure ‘bath’, jug
BDAG.pt: Uma medida líquida hebraica, 'bat', jarra.

DEFINITION: a bath, a liquid measure among the Jews, containing 72 sextarii, that is, between eight and nine gallons.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (bath); a bath, or measure for liquids.

BDAG.en: a Hebr. liquid measure ‘bath’, jug
BDAG.pt: Uma medida líquida hebraica, 'bat', jarra.

DEFINITION: a frog.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a frog.

BDAG.en: frog
BDAG.pt: Sapo, rã.

DEFINITION: to chatter, be long-winded, utter empty words, stammer, repeat.
ORIGIN: From Battos (a proverbial stammerer) and logos; to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously.

DEFINITION: an abominable thing, an accursed thing.
ORIGIN: From bdelusso; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry.

BDAG.en: something that causes revulsion or extreme disgust, a 'loathsome, detestable thing'; something disgusting that arouses wrath, loathsome thing; detestable in the sight of God; something that is totally defiling, abomination, pollutant
BDAG.pt: algo que causa repulsa ou extremo nojo, uma 'coisa nojenta, detestável'; algo nojento que provoca ira, coisa detestável; detestável à vista de Deus; algo totalmente contaminante, abominação, poluente

DEFINITION: abominable, detestable.
ORIGIN: From bdelusso; detestable, i.e. (specially) idolatrous.

BDAG.en: abhorrent, detestable (pertaining to a person or thing that stirs up feelings of repugnance)
BDAG.pt: aborrecível, detestável (relativo a uma pessoa ou coisa que provoca sentimentos de repugnância)

DEFINITION: to abhor, detest, loathe.
ORIGIN: From a (presumed) derivative of bdeo (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry).

BDAG.en: to detest something because it is utterly offensive or loathsome, abhor, detest (cult images)
BDAG.pt: detestar algo porque é totalmente ofensivo ou nojento, abominar, detestar (imagens de culto)

DEFINITION: firm, steadfast, enduring, sure, certain.
ORIGIN: From the base of basis (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: relating to stability: ‘firm, permanent’; of something that can be relied on not to cause disappointment, reliable; pert. to having continuity or being unwavering and persistent, abiding; pert. to having validity over a period of time, in force, valid
BDAG.pt: Relativo à estabilidade: 'firme, permanente'; de algo em que se pode confiar para não desapontar, confiável; relativo a ter continuidade ou ser inabalável e persistente, duradouro; relativo a ter validade por um período de tempo, em vigor, válido.

DEFINITION: to confirm, ratify, secure, establish; pass: to guarantee.
ORIGIN: From bebaios; to stabilitate (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to put something beyond doubt, confirm, establish; to prove promises reliable, fulfill (them); to make a person firm in commitment, establish, strengthen.
BDAG.pt: tornar algo fora de dúvida, confirmar, estabelecer; provar que as promessas são confiáveis, cumpri-las; tornar uma pessoa firme no compromisso, estabelecer, fortalecer.

DEFINITION: confirmation, ratification, establishment.
ORIGIN: From bebaioo; stabiliment.

BDAG.en: process of establishing or confirming something, confirmation, validation
BDAG.pt: Processo de estabelecer ou confirmar algo, confirmação, validação.

DEFINITION: permitted to be trodden, by implication unhallowed.
ORIGIN: From the base of basis and belos (a threshold); accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked.

BDAG.en: pert. to being gener. public, in NT not in a ritualistic sense; pert. to being accessible to everyone and therefore devoid of real significance, pointless, worthless; of pers. pert. to being worldly as opp. to having an interest in transcendent matters, totally worldly
BDAG.pt: Relativo a ser geralmente público, no NT não em sentido ritualístico; relativo a ser acessível a todos e, portanto, destituído de significado real, sem sentido, sem valor; de pessoas, relativo a ser mundano em oposição a ter interesse em assuntos transcendentais, totalmente mundano.

DEFINITION: to profane, pollute, violate.
ORIGIN: From bebelos; to desecrate.

BDAG.en: to cause someth. highly revered to become identified with the commonplace, violate sanctity, desecrate, profane
BDAG.pt: Fazer com que algo altamente reverenciado se identifique com o comum, violar a santidade, profanar, macular.

DEFINITION: Beelzebul, a name of Satan, the chief of evil spirits.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (by parody on Ba'al Zbuwb); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan.

BDAG.en: Beelzebul, orig. a Philistine deity; prince of hostile spirits
BDAG.pt: Belzebu, originalmente uma divindade filisteia; príncipe dos espíritos hostis.

DEFINITION: "lord of the forest", Beliar, a name of Satan.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (bliya'al); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan.

BDAG.en: Beliar (Belial), name for the devil
BDAG.pt: Belial, nome para o diabo.

DEFINITION: a missile, dart, javelin, arrow.
ORIGIN: From ballo; a missile, i.e. Spear or arrow.

BDAG.en: someth. w. a sharp point, a term used for projectiles of various kinds, in our lit. arrow
BDAG.pt: algo com uma ponta afiada, um termo usado para projéteis de vários tipos, na nossa literatura flecha/seta

DEFINITION: better; adv: very well.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of a derivative of ballo (used for the comparative of agathos); better.

BDAG.en: relatively superior, better (as in 'better than someone'); it is better to (do something).
BDAG.pt: relativamente superior, melhor (como em 'melhor que alguém'); é melhor (fazer algo).

DEFINITION: Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Binyamiyn); Benjamin, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: Bernice, daughter of Agrippa to and Kypros, and sister of M. Julius Agrippa II.
ORIGIN: From a provincial form of phero and nike; victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family.

BDAG.en: Bernice, daughter of Agrippa I and sister of Agrippa II and Drusilla
BDAG.pt: Berenice, filha de Agripa I e irmã de Agripa II e Drusila

DEFINITION: Berea, a town of the province Macedonia.
ORIGIN: Perhaps a provincial from a derivative of peran (Peroea, i.e. The region beyond the coast-line); Beroea, a place in Macedonia.

BDAG.en: Beroia, very old city in Macedonia on the river Astraeus in the province of Emathia at the foot of Mt. Bermion
BDAG.pt: Beroia, cidade muito antiga na Macedônia sobre o rio Astraeus na província de Emathia, ao pé do Monte Bermion

DEFINITION: belonging to Berea, Berean.
ORIGIN: From Beroia; a Beroeoean or native of Beroea.

BDAG.en: of or from Beroia, subst. the Beroian (of Sopater, a companion of Paul)
BDAG.pt: de ou originário de Beroia, substantivo: o habitante de Beroia (de Sopatro, um companheiro de Paulo)

DEFINITION: Bethabara.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (bayith and abarah); ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan.

BDAG.en: Bethabara, a place on the Jordan River mentioned in John's Gospel.
BDAG.pt: Betabara, um lugar no rio Jordão mencionado no Evangelho de João.

DEFINITION: (a) Bethany, the home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary, near Jerusalem, (b) Bethany, beyond Jordan.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Bethany, village near Jerusalem/home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus; also a place on the east side of the Jordan where John baptized.
BDAG.pt: Betânia, aldeia perto de Jerusalém/lar de Maria, Marta e Lázaro; também um lugar no lado leste do Jordão onde João batizava.

DEFINITION: Bethesda, name of a pool in Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare bayith and checed); house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem.

BDAG.en: Bethesda, name of a pool in Jerusalem.
BDAG.pt: Betesda, nome de um tanque em Jerusalém.

DEFINITION: "house of bread", Bethlehem, a city near Jer.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Beyth l-'Aphrah); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Bethlehem, a town in Judaea, birthplace of Benjamin and home of David, hence the birthplace of the Messiah
BDAG.pt: Belém, uma cidade na Judeia, local de nascimento de Benjamim e casa de Davi, portanto, o local de nascimento do Messias

DEFINITION: "house of fish", Bethsaida, the name of two cities on the shore of the Sea of Galilee.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare bayith and tsayad); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Bethsaida, a place north of the Sea of Galilee, home of Philip, Andrew, and Peter.
BDAG.pt: Betsaida, um lugar ao norte do Mar da Galileia, lar de Filipe, André e Pedro.

DEFINITION: Bethphage, a village in the neighborhood of Jerusalem, on the Mt. of Olives.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare bayith and pag); fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Bethphage, a place on the Mount of Olives.
BDAG.pt: Betfagé, um lugar no Monte das Oliveiras.

DEFINITION: an elevated place ascended by steps, a throne, tribunal.
ORIGIN: From the base of basis; a step, i.e. Foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. A tribunal.

BDAG.en: orig. movement by raising a step, ‘step’; then 1 a step forward made by a foot, step 2 a very limited space, step 3 a dais or platform that required steps to ascend, tribunal, Esp. judicial bench
BDAG.pt: originalmente movimento ao levantar um passo, 'passo'; então 1 um passo à frente dado por um pé, passo 2 um espaço muito limitado, passo 3 um estrado ou plataforma que exigia degraus para subir, tribunal, especialmente assento judicial

DEFINITION: a beryl, a precious stone of various colors, the best known being sea-green.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a "beryl".

BDAG.en: semiprecious stone usually of sea-green color, beryl.
BDAG.pt: pedra semipreciosa geralmente de cor verde-mar, berilo.

DEFINITION: force, violence, strength.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to bia (through the idea of vital activity); force.

BDAG.en: strength or energy brought to bear in varying degrees on things or persons, force; of violent natural forces; of persons, compulsion; a mob pressing forward.
BDAG.pt: força ou energia aplicada em graus variados a coisas ou pessoas, força; de forças naturais violentas; de pessoas, compulsão; uma multidão que avança.

DEFINITION: (a) mid: to use force, force way, come forward violently, (b) pass: to be forcibly treated, suffer violence.
ORIGIN: From bios; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized.

DEFINITION: strong, violent.
ORIGIN: From bia; violent.

BDAG.en: pert. to being violent or strong in use of force, violent, forcible. a of human force b of natural force violent, strong
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser violento ou forte no uso da força, violento, forçoso. a de força humana b de força natural, violento, forte

DEFINITION: a forceful, violent man; one who is eager in pursuit.
ORIGIN: From biazo; a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic.

BDAG.en: violent, impetuous pers. transf. sense
BDAG.pt: pessoa violenta, impetuosa, sentido transferido

DEFINITION: a little papyrus roll.
ORIGIN: A diminutive of biblion; a booklet.

BDAG.en: variant spelling of βιβλαρίδιον.
BDAG.pt: variante de grafia para βιβλαρίδιον.

DEFINITION: a papyrus roll.
ORIGIN: A diminutive of biblos; a roll.

BDAG.en: brief written message, document; certificate of divorce; long written composition, scroll, book; of the scroll of the Law; of the scroll of a prophet; of John’s gospel; of holy writings generally; book of life.
BDAG.pt: breve mensagem escrita, documento; certidão de divórcio; longa composição escrita, pergaminho, livro; do rolo da Lei; do rolo de um profeta; do evangelho de João; dos escritos sagrados em geral; livro da vida.

DEFINITION: a written book, roll, or volume, sometimes with a sacred connotation.
ORIGIN: Properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing.

BDAG.en: 'book', later esp. 'sacred, venerable book'; a specific composition or class of composition, book; a book of accounts, record-book, esp. book of life.
BDAG.pt: 'livro', mais tarde especialmente 'livro sagrado, venerável'; uma composição específica ou classe de composição, livro; um livro de contas, registro, especialmente livro da vida.

DEFINITION: to eat.
ORIGIN: A reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of bosko); to eat.

BDAG.en: to take food in through the mouth, eat, consume; of sticks be eaten, gnawed.
BDAG.pt: ingerir alimento pela boca, comer, consumir; de paus, ser comido, roído.

DEFINITION: Bithynia, a Roman province, north-west of Asia Minor and south-west of the Black Sea.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia.

BDAG.en: Bithynia, province in northern Asia Minor.
BDAG.pt: Bitínia, província na Ásia Menor setentrional.

DEFINITION: (a) life, (b) manner of life; livelihood.
ORIGIN: A primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood.

BDAG.en: 'life' in its appearance and manifestations (manner in which one’s life finds expression); life and activity associated w. it, life; resources needed to maintain life, means of subsistence, property
BDAG.pt: 'vida' em sua aparência e manifestações (maneira pela qual a vida se expressa); vida e atividade associadas a ela, vida; recursos necessários para manter a vida, meios de subsistência, propriedade

DEFINITION: to live, pass life.
ORIGIN: From bios; to spend existence.

BDAG.en: to spend one’s life, live.
BDAG.pt: passar a vida, viver.

DEFINITION: manner of life.
ORIGIN: From bioo; living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode).

BDAG.en: manner of life
BDAG.pt: maneira de viver

DEFINITION: belonging to ordinary life, worldly.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of bioo; relating to the present existence.
USAGE: of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life.

BDAG.en: pert. to daily life and living, belonging to (daily) life; ordinary (everyday) matters
BDAG.pt: pertencente à vida diária e ao viver, pertencente à vida (diária); assuntos comuns (do dia a dia)

DEFINITION: injurious, hurtful.
ORIGIN: From blapto; injurious.

BDAG.en: harmful
BDAG.pt: prejudicial, nocivo

DEFINITION: to hurt, injure.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure.

BDAG.en: to harm, injure
BDAG.pt: prejudicar, ferir

DEFINITION: intrans: to sprout; trans: to cause to sprout, make to grow up.
ORIGIN: From blastos (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit.

BDAG.en: to cause growth or to spring up as new growth; to emerge as new growth, bud, sprout
BDAG.pt: causar crescimento ou brotar como novo crescimento; emergir como novo crescimento, brotar, germinar

DEFINITION: Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa to.
ORIGIN: Perhaps the same as the base of blastano; Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa.

BDAG.en: Blastus (chamberlain of Herod Agrippa I)
BDAG.pt: Blastus (camerista de Herodes Agripa I)

DEFINITION: to speak evil against, blaspheme, use abusive or scurrilous language about (God or men).
ORIGIN: From blasphemos; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously.
USAGE: (speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil.

BDAG.en: to speak in a disrespectful way that demeans, denigrates, maligns (a in relation to humans slander, revile, defame; b in relation to transcendent or associated entities slander, revile, defame, speak irreverently/impiously/disrespectfully of or about)
BDAG.pt: falar de maneira desrespeitosa que rebaixa, denigre, difama (a em relação a humanos: caluniar, insultar, difamar; b em relação a entidades transcendentes ou associadas: caluniar, insultar, difamar, falar irreverentemente/impiedosamente/desrespeitosamente sobre)

DEFINITION: abusive or scurrilous language, blasphemy.
ORIGIN: From blasphemos; vilification (especially against God).

BDAG.en: speech that denigrates or defames, reviling, denigration, disrespect, slander (a gener., of any kind of speech that is defamatory or abusive; b specif., against)

BDAG.pt: estar cheio de algo (estado em vez de procedimento), estar repleto.

DEFINITION: a generation; if repeated twice or with another time word, practically indicates infinity of time.
ORIGIN: From (a presumed derivative of) genos; a generation; by implication, an age (the period or the persons).

BDAG.pt: termo relativo ao produto do ato de gerar, com referência especial à parentesco; descendentes de um ancestral comum, um 'clã'; o total daqueles nascidos ao mesmo tempo, geração, contemporâneos; o tempo de uma geração, era

DEFINITION: to put into a genealogy, reckon descent.

BDAG.en: to trace descent.
BDAG.pt: rastrear a descendência.

DEFINITION: the making of a pedigree, a genealogy.
ORIGIN: From the same as genealogeo; tracing by generations, i.e. "genealogy".

DEFINITION: a birthday celebration.

BDAG.pt: ancestralidade como ponto de origem, nascimento; estado de ser, existência; um relato da vida de alguém, história, vida

DEFINITION: birth.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of genea; birth.

BDAG.en: coming into being through birth, birth
BDAG.pt: vir a existir através do nascimento, nascimento

DEFINITION: to beget (of the male), (of the female) to bring forth, give birth to.
ORIGIN: From a variation of genos; to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate.
USAGE: bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring.

BDAG.en: to cause something to come into existence, primarily through procreation or parturition; to beget; to give birth to, bear; to cause something to happen, bring forth, produce
BDAG.pt: fazer com que algo venha à existência, primariamente através da procriação ou parto; gerar; dar à luz, parir; causar algo, produzir, gerar

DEFINITION: offspring, child, fruit.
ORIGIN: From gennao; offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: product of the activity expressed by γεννάω, that which is produced or born, child, offspring, brood of vipers
BDAG.pt: produto da atividade expressa por γεννάω, aquilo que é produzido ou nascido, filho, descendência, ninhada de víboras

DEFINITION: Gennesaret, a fertile district by the lake of Tiberias, which was in consequence sometimes called the Lake of Gennesaret.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (compare Kinnrowth); Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake and plain in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Gennesaret, name of the fertile plain south of Capernaum and the adjacent large lake
BDAG.pt: Genesaré, nome da planície fértil ao sul de Cafarnaum e do grande lago adjacente

DEFINITION: nativity, birth.
ORIGIN: From gennao; nativity.

BDAG.en: birth
BDAG.pt: nascimento

DEFINITION: begotten, born.
ORIGIN: From gennao; born.

BDAG.en: pert. to having been born, born; person that is born of woman=human being
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao ter nascido, nascido; pessoa que nasce de mulher = ser humano

DEFINITION: offspring, family, race, nation, kind.
ORIGIN: From ginomai; "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective).
USAGE: born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock.

BDAG.en: ancestral stock, descendant; a relatively small group with common ancestry, family, relatives; a relatively large people group, nation, people; entities united by common traits, class, kind
BDAG.pt: estirpe ancestral, descendente; um grupo relativamente pequeno com ascendência comum, família, parentes; um grupo de pessoas relativamente grande, nação, povo; entidades unidas por traços comuns, classe, tipo

DEFINITION: Gerasene, of Gerasa, a city East of the Jordan.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Girgashiy); a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the aborigines of Palestine.

BDAG.en: the Gergesene (from Gergesa, a town on the eastern shore of Lake Genessaret)
BDAG.pt: o Gergeseno (de Gergesa, uma cidade na margem leste do Mar da Galileia)

DEFINITION: the assembly or body of elders.
ORIGIN: From geron; the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrin.

BDAG.en: council of elders, esp. the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem
BDAG.pt: conselho de anciãos, especialmente o Sinédrio em Jerusalém

DEFINITION: an old man.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity (compare geras); aged.

BDAG.en: elderly/old man
BDAG.pt: homem idoso/velho

DEFINITION: (a) to taste, (b) to experience.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill).

BDAG.en: to have perception of something either by mouth or by experience, especially in reference to a relatively small quantity; to partake of something by mouth, taste; to experience something cognitively or emotionally, come to know something
BDAG.pt: ter percepção de algo pela boca ou por experiência, especialmente em referência a uma pequena quantidade; participar de algo pela boca, provar; experimentar algo cognitivamente ou emocionalmente, chegar a conhecer algo

DEFINITION: to work the soil, cultivate the earth.
ORIGIN: From georgos; to till (the soil).

BDAG.en: to cultivate; (Passive) to be tilled (land)
BDAG.pt: cultivar; (Passivo) ser lavrado (terra)

DEFINITION: a tilled field, cultivation, husbandry.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a (presumed) derivative of georgos; cultivable, i.e. A farm.

BDAG.en: an area of land used for cultivation, cultivated land, field (figuratively of a Christian congregation as God’s field)
BDAG.pt: uma área de terra usada para cultivo (em oposição a pastagem), terra cultivada, campo (figurativamente de uma congregação cristã como campo de Deus)

DEFINITION: a worker of the soil, husbandman, farmer, farm-laborer, vine-dresser.
ORIGIN: From ge and the base of ergon; a land-worker, i.e. Farmer.

BDAG.en: one who is occupied in agriculture or gardening; one who owns a farm, farmer; one who does agricultural work on a contractual basis, vine-dresser, tenant farmer
BDAG.pt: aquele que se ocupa com agricultura ou jardinagem; aquele que possui uma fazenda, agricultor; aquele que realiza trabalho agrícola sob contrato, viticultor, arrendatário

DEFINITION: the earth, soil, land, region, country, inhabitants of a region.
ORIGIN: Contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application).

BDAG.en: surface of the earth as the habitation of humanity, earth; the inhabited planet; the inhabitants of the earth, people, humanity; portions or regions of the earth, region, country; dry land as opposed to sea, land; earth-like surface that forms the bottom of a body of water, ground, bottom of the sea; earth w. ref. to limited areas and the material that forms its surface, soil, earth, receiving seed
BDAG.pt: a superfície da terra como habitação da humanidade, terra; o planeta habitado; os habitantes da terra, povo, humanidade; porções ou regiões da terra, região, país; terra seca em oposição ao mar, solo; superfície semelhante à terra que forma o fundo de um corpo de água, chão, fundo do mar; terra com referência a áreas limitadas e ao material que forma sua superfície, solo, terra, que recebe a semente

DEFINITION: old age.
ORIGIN: Akin to geron; senility.

BDAG.en: advancement in years or age w. ref. to passage of a relatively long period of time (in our lit. of pers.), old age
BDAG.pt: avanço em anos ou idade com referência à passagem de um período de tempo relativamente longo (em nossa literatura, de pessoas), velhice

DEFINITION: to become old, grow old.
ORIGIN: From geras; to be senescent.

BDAG.en: to grow old; becoming obsolete and growing old
BDAG.pt: envelhecer; tornar-se obsoleto e envelhecer

DEFINITION: to come into being, be born, become, come about, happen.
ORIGIN: A prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; to cause to be ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.).
USAGE: arise, be assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.

BDAG.en: A verb with numerous nuances relating to being and manner of being. 1. to come into being through process of birth or natural production, be born, be produced. 2. to come into existence, be made, be created, be manufactured, be performed. 3. to come into being as an event or phenomenon from a point of origin, arise, come about, develop. 4. to occur as process or result, happen, turn out, take place. 5. to experience a change in nature and so indicate entry into a new condition, become something. 6. to make a change of location in space, move.
BDAG.pt: Um verbo com inúmeras nuances relacionadas ao ser e à maneira de ser. 1. vir a existir através de processo de nascimento ou produção natural, nascer, ser produzido. 2. vir a existir, ser feito, ser criado, ser fabricado, ser realizado. 3. vir a ser como um evento ou fenômeno a partir de um ponto de origem, surgir, acontecer, desenvolver-se. 4. ocorrer como processo ou resultado, acontecer, revelar-se, ter lugar. 5. experimentar uma mudança na natureza e assim indicar a entrada em uma nova condição, tornar-se algo. 6. fazer uma mudança de localização no espaço, mover-se.

DEFINITION: to be taking in knowledge, come to know, learn; aor: to ascertained, realized.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely) in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with others not thus clearly expressed).
USAGE: allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand.

BDAG.en: to arrive at a knowledge of someone or someth., know, know about, make acquaintance of; to acquire information through some means, learn (of), ascertain, find out; to grasp the significance or meaning of someth., understand, comprehend; to be aware of someth., perceive, notice, realize; to have sexual intercourse with, have sex/marital relations with; to have come to the knowledge of, have come to know, know; to indicate that one does know, acknowledge, recognize as that which one is or claims to be
BDAG.pt: chegar a um conhecimento de alguém ou algo, saber, ter conhecimento de, tomar conhecimento de; adquirir informação por algum meio, aprender (sobre), apurar, descobrir; apreender o significado ou sentido de algo, entender, compreender; estar ciente de algo, perceber, notar, realizar; ter relações sexuais com, ter relações sexuais/conjugais com; ter chegado ao conhecimento de, ter vindo a saber, conhecer; indicar que se sabe, reconhecer, reconhecer como aquilo que se é ou se alega ser

DEFINITION: the unfermented juice of grapes; hence: sweet new wine.
ORIGIN: Akin to glukus; sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine.

BDAG.en: sweet new wine (must)
BDAG.pt: vinho novo doce (mosto)

DEFINITION: sweet.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; sweet (i.e. Not bitter nor salt).

BDAG.en: sweet of water; of honey; in imagery, of a book be sweet as honey, i.e. pleasant to read; fig. of commandments, of patience, of an exchange; superl. freq. of persons to express affection
BDAG.pt: doce (de água); de mel; em imagens, de um livro ser doce como mel, ou seja, agradável de ler; figurado, de mandamentos, de paciência, de uma troca; superlativo frequente para pessoas para expressar afeição

DEFINITION: the tongue, a language, a nation (usually distinguished by their speech).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired).

BDAG.en: organ of speech, tongue; a body of words and systems that makes up a distinctive language, language, tongue; ecstatic language, ecstatic speech, tongue
BDAG.pt: órgão da fala, língua; um corpo de palavras e sistemas que constitui uma linguagem distinta, idioma, língua; linguagem extática, fala extática, língua

DEFINITION: (a vernacular word), bag, purse; some prefer to take as: box, chest.
ORIGIN: From glossa and the base of kosmos; properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse.

BDAG.en: container for money, money-box, purse
BDAG.pt: recipiente para dinheiro, caixa de dinheiro, bolsa

ORIGIN: By variation for a derivative from knapto (to tease cloth); a cloth-dresser.

BDAG.en: specialist in the treatment of cloth, incl. fulling, carding, cleaning, bleaching (cloth refiner)
BDAG.pt: especialista no tratamento de tecidos, incluindo enfeltragem, cardagem, limpeza, branqueamento (refinador de tecidos)

DEFINITION: (lit: born in wedlock), hence: real, true, genuine; with definite article: the true, genuine element.
ORIGIN: From the same as genesia; legitimate (of birth), i.e. Genuine.

BDAG.en: one who is considered a valid member of a family, legitimate, true; pert. to possession of apparent or reputed good character or quality, genuine of things
BDAG.pt: aquele que é considerado um membro válido de uma família, legítimo, verdadeiro; referente à posse de bom caráter ou qualidade aparente ou reputada, genuíno de coisas

DEFINITION: truly, genuinely, honorably, sincerely.
ORIGIN: Adverb from gnesios; genuinely, i.e. Really.

BDAG.en: sincerely, genuinely
BDAG.pt: sinceramente, genuinamente

DEFINITION: darkness, gloom; a thick cloud.
ORIGIN: Akin to nephos; gloom (as of a storm).

BDAG.en: darkness
BDAG.pt: escuridão, trevas

DEFINITION: opinion, counsel, judgment, intention, decree.

BDAG.en: that which is purposed or intended, purpose, intention, mind, mind-set; a viewpoint or way of thinking about a matter, opinion, judgment, way of thinking; the act of expressing agreement with a body of data, approval; a declaration that expresses formal consideration of a matter, declaration, decision, resolution
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é proposto ou pretendido, propósito, intenção, mente, mentalidade; um ponto de vista ou maneira de pensar sobre um assunto, opinião, juízo, modo de pensar; o ato de expressar concordância com um corpo de dados, aprovação; uma declaração que expressa consideração formal de um assunto, declaração, decisão, resolução

DEFINITION: to make known, declare, know, discover.

BDAG.en: to cause information to become known: make known, reveal; to have information or be knowledgeable about someth., know
BDAG.pt: fazer com que a informação se torne conhecida: tornar conhecido, revelar; ter informação ou ser conhecedor de algo, saber

DEFINITION: knowledge, doctrine, wisdom.

BDAG.en: comprehension or intellectual grasp of someth., knowledge as possessed by God and humans; the content of what is known, knowledge, what is known; a dissident variety of knowledge
BDAG.pt: compreensão ou apreensão intelectual de algo, conhecimento possuído por Deus e pelos humanos; o conteúdo do que é conhecido, conhecimento, aquilo que é sabido; uma variedade dissidente de conhecimento

DEFINITION: one who knows, an expert.

BDAG.pt: aquele que é conhecedor de algo, alguém familiarizado, perito em

DEFINITION: known, an acquaintance.
ORIGIN: From ginosko; well-known.

BDAG.pt: pertencente ao ser familiar ou conhecido: conhecido; pertencente ao ser capaz de ser conhecido, inteligível

DEFINITION: to whisper, murmur, grumble (generally of smoldering discontent).

BDAG.pt: enunciado feito em tom de voz baixo (o contexto indica se o enunciado é de descontentamento ou satisfação), conversa de bastidores; aspecto negativo: queixa, desagrado, expresso em murmúrio; conversa secreta, sussurro

DEFINITION: a murmurer, grumbler.
ORIGIN: From gogguzo; a grumbler.

BDAG.en: grumbler.
BDAG.pt: resmungão.

DEFINITION: a conjuror, juggler, sorcerer; a tricky (crafty) deceiver, imposter.
ORIGIN: From goao (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter.

BDAG.en: sorcerer, conjurer; swindler, cheat, impostor (of persons who lead others into error).
BDAG.pt: feiticeiro, encantador; vigarista, trapaceiro, impostor (de pessoas que desviam da instrução correta e levam outros ao erro).

DEFINITION: Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare gulgoleth); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem.

BDAG.en: Golgotha (name of an eminence near Jerusalem, used as a place of execution) translated 'Skull Place'.
BDAG.pt: Gólgota (nome de uma elevação perto de Jerusalém, usada como local de execução), traduzido como 'Lugar da Caveira'.

DEFINITION: Gomorrah, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Amorah); Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea.

BDAG.en: Gomorrah, name of a ruined city, example of awesome divine punishment.
BDAG.pt: Gomorra, nome de uma cidade arruinada, exemplo de castigo divino terrível.

DEFINITION: a ship's freight, cargo.
ORIGIN: From gemo; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares.

BDAG.en: that which is carried by a conveyance, load, freight, cargo of a ship.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é transportado por um veículo, carga, frete, carregamento de um navio.

DEFINITION: a begetter, father; plur: parents.
ORIGIN: From the base of ginomai; a parent.

BDAG.en: parents (used only in the plural in this literature).
BDAG.pt: pais (usado apenas no plural nesta literatura).

DEFINITION: the knee.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; the "knee".

BDAG.en: knee; fig. the knees of the heart.
BDAG.pt: joelho; fig. os joelhos do coração.

DEFINITION: to fall on knees before (in supplication), supplicate, entreat.
ORIGIN: From a compound of gonu and the alternate of pipto; to fall on the knee.

BDAG.en: to kneel down (in petition or otherwise).
BDAG.pt: ajoelhar-se (em súplica ou de outra forma).

DEFINITION: a letter of the alphabet; collectively: written (revelation); (a) a written document, a letter, an epistle, (b) writings, literature, learning.
ORIGIN: From grapho; a writing, i.e. A letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning.
USAGE: bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.

BDAG.en: a unit of an alphabet (letter); a set of written characters forming a document (letter, epistle, promissory note, writing, book, esp. of the books of Moses or the OT generally).
BDAG.pt: uma unidade de um alfabeto (letra); um conjunto de caracteres escritos formando um documento (carta, epístola, nota promissória, escrito, livro, especialmente dos livros de Moisés ou do AT em geral).

ORIGIN: From gramma. A writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary.

BDAG.en: one who has special functions in connection with documents; chief executive officer of a governmental entity, secretary, clerk; an expert in matters relating to divine revelation, a specialist in the law of Moses, scribe, scholar; interpreter of teaching connected with the ministry of Jesus, scribe, instructor.
BDAG.pt: aquele que tem funções especiais em conexão com documentos; principal oficial executivo de uma entidade governamental, secretário, escrivão; um especialista em assuntos relativos à revelação divina, um especialista na lei de Moisés, escriba, erudito; intérprete do ensinamento conectado com o ministério de Jesus, escriba, instrutor.

DEFINITION: written.
ORIGIN: From grapho; inscribed (figuratively).

BDAG.en: pertaining to being set down in writing, written.
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que está escrito, escrito.

DEFINITION: (a) a writing, (b) a passage of scripture; plur: the scriptures.
ORIGIN: A document, i.e. Holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it).

BDAG.en: that which is written: 'writing'; a brief piece of writing, writing; sacred scripture, in the NT exclusively so, an individual scripture passage; scripture in its entirety (plural: the scriptures; singular: Scripture as a whole).
BDAG.pt: aquilo que está escrito: 'escrita'; um breve pedaço de escrita, escrito; escritura sagrada, no NT exclusivamente, uma passagem individual da escritura; escritura em sua totalidade (plural: as escrituras; singular: a Escritura como um todo).

DEFINITION: to write; pass: it is written, it stands written (in the scriptures).
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe.

BDAG.en: to inscribe characters on a surface, write; to express thought in writing, write down, record; of correspondence, write (to) someone; compose, write (a book, letter); to give someone directions in writing.
BDAG.pt: escrever caracteres em uma superfície, escrever; expressar o pensamento por escrito, registrar, anotar; em correspondência, escrever a alguém; compor, escrever (um livro, carta); dar instruções a alguém por escrito.

DEFINITION: belonging to old women, such as old women tell.
ORIGIN: From graus (an old woman) and eidos; crone-like, i.e. Silly.

BDAG.en: characteristic of an elderly woman, pertaining to speculative or legendary accounts that lack Christian pedagogical value.
BDAG.pt: característico de uma mulher idosa, pertencente a relatos especulativos ou lendários que carecem de valor pedagógico cristão.

DEFINITION: (a) to be awake (in the night), watch, (b) to be watchful, on the alert, vigilant.
ORIGIN: From egeiro; to keep awake, i.e. Watch (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to stay awake, be watchful; to be in constant readiness, to be on the alert; to remain fully alive, be alive (opposed to being dead).
BDAG.pt: permanecer acordado, estar vigilante; estar em constante prontidão, estar alerta; permanecer plenamente vivo, estar vivo (em oposição a estar morto).

DEFINITION: to train by physical exercise; hence: train, in the widest sense.
ORIGIN: From gumnos; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. Train (figuratively).

BDAG.en: exercise naked, train; but also fig. of mental and spiritual powers: to train, undergo discipline
BDAG.pt: exercitar-se nu, treinar; mas também figurativamente de poderes mentais e espirituais: treinar, submeter-se à disciplina

DEFINITION: (physical) exercise, in a wide sense.
ORIGIN: From gumnazo; training, i.e. (figuratively) asceticism.

BDAG.pt: treinamento, especialmente exercício físico

DEFINITION: to be poorly clad; to be habitually wearing an under-garment only.

BDAG.en: be poorly clothed (variant spelling/form)
BDAG.pt: estar mal vestido (forma/grafia variante)

DEFINITION: rarely: stark-naked; generally: wearing only the under-garment; bare, open, manifest; mere.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative).

BDAG.en: naked, stripped, bare; uncovered, bare; naked (of the soul); inadequately clothed, poorly dressed; lightly clad, without an outer garment
BDAG.pt: nu, despojado, descoberto; exposto, nu; nu (da alma); inadequadamente vestido, mal vestido; levemente vestido, sem vestimenta exterior

DEFINITION: nakedness.
ORIGIN: From gumnos; nudity (absolute or comparative).

BDAG.en: being without clothing, nakedness; being without adequate clothing, destitution, lack of sufficient clothing, destitution
BDAG.pt: estado de não ter vestimentas, nudez; estado de não ter vestimentas adequadas, carência, falta de roupa suficiente, desamparo

DEFINITION: a woman, with all a woman's weakness, a poor weak woman, a silly woman.
ORIGIN: A diminutive from gune; a little (i.e. Foolish) woman.

BDAG.en: idle/foolish/weak woman (diminutive with derogatory connotation)
BDAG.pt: mulher ociosa/tola/fraca (diminutivo com conotação depreciativa)

DEFINITION: belonging to woman, of woman, female.

BDAG.en: feminine (periphrasis for woman, wife)
BDAG.pt: feminino (peri frase para mulher, esposa)

DEFINITION: a woman, wife, lady.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of ginomai; a woman; specially, a wife.

DEFINITION: vehemently, terribly, grievously.

DEFINITION: properly: the people, especially citizens of a Greek city in popular assembly, but in NT, multitude, rabble.
ORIGIN: From deo; the public (as bound together socially).

BDAG.en: a gathering of people for any purpose, people, populace, crowd; in a Hellenistic city, a convocation of citizens called together for the purpose of transacting official business, popular assembly
BDAG.pt: um ajuntamento de pessoas para qualquer propósito, povo, população, multidão; em uma cidade helenística, uma convocação de cidadãos reunidos com o propósito de tratar de assuntos oficiais, assembleia popular

DEFINITION: public, publicly.
ORIGIN: From demos; public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in public.

BDAG.en: pert. to belonging to the state, public; pert. to being able to be known by the general public, in the open, public.
BDAG.pt: relativo a pertencer ao estado, público; relativo a poder ser conhecido pelo público em geral, aberto, público.

DEFINITION: a denarius, a small Roman silver coin.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a denarius (or ten asses).

BDAG.en: denarius, a Roman silver coin orig. c. 4.55 g; the debasement of coinage under Nero reduced it in value; it was a worker’s average daily wage
BDAG.pt: denário, uma moeda de prata romana com cerca de 4,55g; a desvalorização da cunhagem sob Nero reduziu seu valor; era o salário diário médio de um trabalhador

DEFINITION: even at that time, whenever.
ORIGIN: From de and pote; a particle of generalization; indeed, at any time.

BDAG.en: at any time; w. relative whatever
BDAG.pt: a qualquer tempo; com relativo (o que for)

DEFINITION: of course, indeed, qualifying and yet strengthening the assertion.
ORIGIN: From de and pou; a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless.

BDAG.en: a marker of emphasis, but the suffix που is rhetorically significant, for it softens the process of inference, while yet strongly asserting the conclusion, by graciously taking the auditor into the logical process, somewhat in the sense ‘one would agree, I’m sure’ of course, surely
BDAG.pt: um marcador de ênfase, mas o sufixo που é retoricamente significativo, pois suaviza o processo de inferência, ao mesmo tempo que afirma fortemente a conclusão, convidando o ouvinte ao processo lógico, algo no sentido de 'certamente concordaríamos' claro, certamente

DEFINITION: (a) gen: through, throughout, by the instrumentality of, (b) acc: through, on account of, by reason of, for the sake of, because of.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; through (in very wide applications, local, causal, or occasional).
USAGE: after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause)... Fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that, thereby, therefore, X though, through(-out), to, wherefore, with (-in). In composition it retains the same general importance.

BDAG.en: prep. w. gen. and acc.; fundamental idea is separation, esp. in the gen., with the gener. sense ‘through’; in the acc. the gener. sense also is ‘through’, but primarily with a causal focus ‘owing to’
BDAG.pt: preposição com genitivo e acusativo; a ideia fundamental é separação, especialmente no genitivo, com o sentido geral de 'através de'; no acusativo, o sentido geral também é 'através de', mas primariamente com foco causal 'devido a'

DEFINITION: to cross, pass through, step across.
ORIGIN: From dia and the base of basis; to cross.

BDAG.en: to proceed from one side to another over a geographical area, go through, cross
BDAG.pt: prosseguir de um lado para outro sobre uma área geográfica, passar, atravessar

DEFINITION: to thrust through, slander, complain of, accuse.
ORIGIN: From dia and ballo; (figuratively) to traduce.

BDAG.en: to make a complaint about a person to a third party, bring charges, inform (either justly or falsely)
BDAG.pt: fazer uma queixa sobre uma pessoa a um terceiro, apresentar acusações, informar (justa ou falsamente)

DEFINITION: to assert emphatically.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of a compound of dia and bebaioo; to confirm thoroughly (by words), i.e. Asseverate.

BDAG.en: speak confidently, insist concerning or on someth.; confirm
BDAG.pt: falar com confiança, insistir sobre ou a respeito de algo; confirmar

DEFINITION: to look through, to see clearly.
ORIGIN: From dia and blepo; to look through, i.e. Recover full vision.

BDAG.en: to stare w. eyes wide open, look intently, or open one’s eyes (wide); to be able to see clearly, see clearly
BDAG.pt: olhar fixamente com os olhos bem abertos, olhar atentamente, ou abrir os olhos (bem abertos); ser capaz de ver claramente, ver claramente

DEFINITION: (adj. used often as a noun), slanderous; with the article: the Slanderer (par excellence), the Devil.
ORIGIN: From diaballo; a traducer; specially, Satan (compare satan).

BDAG.en: one who engages in slander, slanderous; subst.: the adversary/devil (title of the principal transcendent evil being)
BDAG.pt: Aquele que se dedica à calúnia, calunioso; substantivo: o adversário/diabo (título do principal ser do mal transcendente)

DEFINITION: to announce throughout (the world), spread the news of, give notice of, teach.
ORIGIN: From dia and the base of aggelos; to herald thoroughly.

BDAG.en: to make something known far and wide, proclaim, spread the news concerning/about; to make a report, announce, report
BDAG.pt: Fazer algo conhecido amplamente, proclamar, espalhar as notícias sobre/a respeito de; fazer um relatório, anunciar, relatar

DEFINITION: to pass (of time); to continue through, intervene.
ORIGIN: From dia and ginomai; to elapse meanwhile.
USAGE: X after, be past, be spent.

BDAG.en: to pass/elapse of time
BDAG.pt: passar/decorrer do tempo

DEFINITION: to know accurately, examine, decide.
ORIGIN: From dia and ginosko; to know thoroughly, i.e. Ascertain exactly.

BDAG.en: to give careful attention (to facts or a subject) as a basis for forming a judgment, determine; to make a judicial decision, decide/hear (a case)
BDAG.pt: Prestar atenção cuidadosa (aos fatos ou a um assunto) como base para formar um julgamento, determinar; tomar uma decisão judicial, decidir/julgar (um caso)

DEFINITION: to tell abroad, make known.
ORIGIN: From graptos and gnorizo; to tell abroad.

BDAG.en: give an exact report concerning someth.
BDAG.pt: dar um relatório exato sobre algo

DEFINITION: judicial examination, decision; an act of discernment.
ORIGIN: From diaginosko; (magisterial) examination ("diagnosis").

BDAG.en: a judicial inquiry or investigation that culminates in a decision, decision
BDAG.pt: Uma investigação ou inquérito judicial que culmina em uma decisão, decisão

DEFINITION: to murmur greatly, continue murmuring.
ORIGIN: From dia and gogguzo; to complain throughout a crowd.

BDAG.en: complain, grumble (aloud)
BDAG.pt: reclamar, resmungar (em voz alta)

DEFINITION: to awake out of sleep, be thoroughly awake.
ORIGIN: From dia and gregoreuo; to waken thoroughly.

BDAG.en: keep awake; awake fully
BDAG.pt: manter-se acordado; despertar completamente

DEFINITION: (either trans. or intrans.), to spend time, pass time, live.
ORIGIN: From dia and ago; to pass time or life.

BDAG.en: spend one’s life, live
BDAG.pt: passar a vida, viver

DEFINITION: to receive in turn, receive through another.
ORIGIN: From dia and dechomai; to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed to.

BDAG.en: to receive in turn from a former possessor, receive in turn, succeed to
BDAG.pt: Receber em sucessão de um possuidor anterior, receber por sua vez, suceder a

DEFINITION: a head-wreath, crown, diadem.
ORIGIN: From a compound of dia and deo; a "diadem" (as bound about the head).

BDAG.en: band, fillet, properly the sign of royalty among the Persians, a blue band trimmed with white, on the tiara, hence a symbol of royalty, gener.: royal headband, crown
BDAG.pt: banda, faixa, propriamente o sinal de realeza entre os persas, uma faixa azul guarnecida de branco, na tiara, daí um símbolo de realeza, geralmente: faixa real, coroa

DEFINITION: to offer here and there, distribute, divide, hand over.
ORIGIN: From dia and didomi; to give throughout a crowd, i.e. Deal out; also to deliver over (as to a successor).

BDAG.en: to apportion among various parties, distribute, give
BDAG.pt: Repartir entre várias partes, distribuir, dar

DEFINITION: a successor.
ORIGIN: From diadechomai; a successor in office.

BDAG.en: one who comes next in a series, esp. of a political figure, successor
BDAG.pt: aquele que vem em seguida numa série, especialmente de uma figura política, sucessor

DEFINITION: to gird, tie around; mid: to gird round myself.
ORIGIN: From dia and zonnumi; to gird tightly.

BDAG.en: tie around. δ. ἑαυτόν tie (a towel) around oneself
BDAG.pt: amarrar em volta. δ. ἑαυτόν amarrar (uma toalha) em volta de si mesmo

DEFINITION: (a) a covenant between two parties, (b) (the ordinary, everyday sense [found a countless number of times in papyri]) a will, testament.
ORIGIN: From diatithemai; properly, a disposition, i.e. (specially) a contract (especially a devisory will).

BDAG.en: last will and testament; covenant, decree, declaration of purpose, set of regulations (as translation of LXX בְּרִית); compact, contract
BDAG.pt: Última vontade e testamento; aliança, decreto, declaração de propósito, conjunto de regulamentos (como tradução do hebraico בְּרִית no LXX); pacto, contrato

DEFINITION: division, distribution, difference, distinction.
ORIGIN: From diaireo; a distinction or (concretely) variety.

BDAG.en: a state or circumstance of being divided up; division or distribution of something to persons, apportionment; a state of difference in the nature of objects or events, difference, variety; division through violent action, tearing apart
BDAG.pt: um estado ou circunstância de estar dividido; divisão ou distribuição de algo a pessoas, rateio; um estado de diferença na natureza de objetos ou eventos, diferença, variedade; divisão através de ação violenta, rasgar

DEFINITION: to divide into parts, cut asunder, distribute.
ORIGIN: From dia and haireomai; to separate, i.e. Distribute.

BDAG.en: distribute, divide; apportion someth. to someone
BDAG.pt: distribuir, dividir; repartir algo a alguém

DEFINITION: to cleanse thoroughly.
ORIGIN: From dia and katharizo; to cleanse perfectly, i.e. (specially) winnow.

BDAG.en: clean out
BDAG.pt: limpar completamente

DEFINITION: to effectively (utterly) refute.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from dia and a compound of kata and elegcho; to prove downright, i.e. Confute.

BDAG.en: confute, overwhelm in argument
BDAG.pt: refutar, sobrecarregar em argumento

DEFINITION: to wait at table (particularly of a slave who waits on guests); to serve (generally).
ORIGIN: From diakonos; to be an attendant, i.e. Wait upon (menially or as a host, friend, or (figuratively) teacher); technically, to act as a Christian deacon.
USAGE: (ad-)minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon.

BDAG.en: to render service in a variety of ways either at someone’s behest or voluntarily and frequently with suggestion of movement; to function as an intermediary, act as go-between/agent, be at one’s service; to perform obligations; to meet an immediate need, help; to carry out official duties, minister, in cultic context; care for, take care of tables
BDAG.pt: prestar serviço de várias maneiras, seja a mando de alguém ou voluntariamente e frequentemente com sugestão de movimento; funcionar como intermediário, agir como intermediário/agente, estar a serviço de alguém; cumprir obrigações; atender a uma necessidade imediata, ajudar; cumprir deveres oficiais, ministrar, em contexto cultual; cuidar, ocupar-se das mesas

DEFINITION: waiting at table; in a wider sense: service, ministration.
ORIGIN: From diakonos; attendance (as a servant, etc.); figuratively (eleemosynary) aid, (official) service (especially of the Christian teacher, or technically of the diaconate).

BDAG.en: service rendered in an intermediary capacity, mediation, assignment; performance of a service (general service, engagement in preparations for a social event, functioning in the interest of a larger public, service/office); rendering of specific assistance, aid, support, esp. of alms and charitable giving; an administrative function, service as attendant, aide, or assistant
BDAG.pt: serviço prestado em capacidade intermediária, mediação, incumbência; desempenho de um serviço (serviço geral, envolvimento em preparativos para um evento social, funcionamento em benefício de um público maior, serviço/ofício); prestação de assistência específica, auxílio, apoio, especialmente de esmolas e doações de caridade; uma função administrativa, serviço como atendente, auxiliar ou assistente

DEFINITION: a waiter, servant; then of any one who performs any service, an administrator.
ORIGIN: Probably from an obsolete diako (to run on errands; compare dioko); an attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a deacon or deaconess).

BDAG.en: one who is busy with something in a manner that is of assistance to someone; one who serves as an intermediary in a transaction, agent, intermediary, courier; one who gets something done, at the behest of a superior, assistant to someone; one who serves as assistant in a cultic context, attendant, assistant, aide (as one identified for special ministerial service in a Christian community)
BDAG.pt: aquele que está ocupado com algo de maneira a auxiliar alguém; aquele que serve como intermediário em uma transação, agente, intermediário, mensageiro; aquele que faz algo ser feito, a mando de um superior, assistente de alguém; aquele que serve como assistente em um contexto cultual, atendente, assistente, auxiliar (como alguém identificado para um serviço ministerial especial em uma comunidade cristã)

DEFINITION: two hundred.
ORIGIN: From dis and hekaton; two hundred.

BDAG.en: two hundred.
BDAG.pt: duzentos.

DEFINITION: to hear throughout, of a judicial hearing.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from dia and akouo; to hear throughout, i.e. Patiently listen (to a prisoner's plea).

BDAG.en: to give someone an opportunity to be heard in court, give someone a hearing.
BDAG.pt: dar a alguém a oportunidade de ser ouvido em tribunal, dar audiência a alguém.

DEFINITION: to separate, distinguish, discern one thing from another; to doubt, hesitate, waver.
ORIGIN: From dia and krino; to separate thoroughly, i.e. (literally and reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose; figuratively, to discriminate (by implication, decide), or (reflexively) hesitate.
USAGE: contend, make (to) differ(-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver.

BDAG.en: to differentiate by separating, separate, arrange; to conclude that there is a difference, make a distinction, differentiate; to evaluate by paying careful attention to, evaluate, judge; to render a legal decision, judge, decide, legal t.t.; to be at variance w. someone, dispute; to be uncertain, be at odds w. oneself, doubt, waver
BDAG.pt: diferenciar separando, separar, arranjar; concluir que há uma diferença, fazer uma distinção, diferenciar; avaliar prestando atenção cuidadosa, avaliar, julgar; proferir uma decisão legal, julgar, decidir, termo legal; estar em desacordo com alguém, disputar; estar incerto, estar em conflito consigo mesmo, duvidar, vacilar

DEFINITION: distinguishing; hence: deciding, passing sentence on; the act of judgment, discernment.
ORIGIN: From diakrino; judicial estimation.

BDAG.en: the ability to distinguish and evaluate, distinguishing, differentiation; engagement in verbal conflict because of differing viewpoints, quarrel.
BDAG.pt: a capacidade de distinguir e avaliar, distinção, diferenciação; envolvimento em conflito verbal devido a pontos de vista divergentes, briga.

DEFINITION: to obstinately prevent, hinder.
ORIGIN: From dia and koluo; to hinder altogether, i.e. Utterly prohibit.

BDAG.en: to keep someth. from happening, prevent.
BDAG.pt: impedir que algo aconteça, prevenir.

DEFINITION: to converse together, talk of; of conversation passing from mouth to mouth.
ORIGIN: From dia and laleo; to talk throughout a company, i.e. Converse or (genitive case) publish.

BDAG.en: discuss, to exchange opinions or viewpoints.
BDAG.pt: discutir, trocar opiniões ou pontos de vista.

DEFINITION: to converse, address, preach, lecture; to argue, reason.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from dia and lego; to say thoroughly, i.e. Discuss (in argument or exhortation).

BDAG.en: to engage in speech interchange, converse, discuss, argue, especially of instructional discourse that frequently includes exchange of opinions; to instruct about something, inform, instruct
