BDAG.pt: engajar-se em intercâmbio de fala, conversar, discutir, argumentar, especialmente em discurso instrutivo que frequentemente inclui troca de opiniões; instruir sobre algo, informar, ensinar

DEFINITION: to cease, give over, give up.
ORIGIN: From dia and leipo; to leave off in the middle, i.e. Intermit.

BDAG.en: to desist from an action or activity, stop, cease; constantly
BDAG.pt: desistir de uma ação ou atividade, parar, cessar; constantemente

DEFINITION: language, speech, conversation, manner of speaking.
ORIGIN: From dialegomai; a (mode of) discourse, i.e. "dialect".

BDAG.en: language of a nation or a region
BDAG.pt: língua de uma nação ou de uma região

DEFINITION: to change, exchange; to reconcile, change enmity for friendship.
ORIGIN: From dia and allasso; to change thoroughly, i.e. (mentally) to conciliate.

BDAG.en: to be restored to normal relations or harmony w. someone, become reconciled
BDAG.pt: ser restaurado a relações normais ou harmonia com alguém, reconciliar-se

DEFINITION: to reason (with), debate (with), consider.
ORIGIN: From dia and logizomai; to reckon thoroughly, i.e. (genitive case) to deliberate (by reflection or discussion).
USAGE: cast in mind, consider, dispute, muse, reason, think.

BDAG.en: to think or reason carefully, consider, ponder, reason; to discuss a matter in some detail, consider and discuss, argue
BDAG.pt: pensar ou raciocinar cuidadosamente, considerar, ponderar, raciocinar; discutir um assunto em algum detalhe, considerar e discutir, argumentar

DEFINITION: a calculation, reasoning, thought, movement of thought, deliberation, plotting.
ORIGIN: From dialogizomai; discussion, i.e. (internal) consideration (by implication, purpose), or (external) debate.

BDAG.en: the process of reasoning, reasoning; content of reasoning or conclusion reached through use of reason, thought, opinion, reasoning, design; verbal exchange that takes place when conflicting ideas are expressed, dispute, argument; reasoning that gives rise to uncertainty, doubt
BDAG.pt: o processo de raciocínio, raciocínio; conteúdo do raciocínio ou conclusão alcançada através do uso da razão, pensamento, opinião, raciocínio, desígnio; intercâmbio verbal que ocorre quando ideias conflitantes são expressas, disputa, argumento; raciocínio que gera incerteza, dúvida

DEFINITION: to break up, disperse, dissolve.
ORIGIN: From dia and luo; to dissolve utterly.

BDAG.en: to break up into elements, break up, dissolve; to put an end to something, destroy; to cause a group to be broken up, disperse, scatter
BDAG.pt: quebrar em elementos, desmembrar, dissolver; pôr fim a algo, destruir; fazer com que um grupo se desfaça, dispersar, espalhar

DEFINITION: to give solemn evidence, testify (declare) solemnly.
ORIGIN: From dia and martureo; to attest or protest earnestly, or (by implication) hortatively.

BDAG.en: to make a solemn declaration about the truth of someth., testify of, bear witness to; to exhort with authority in matters of extraordinary importance, solemnly urge, exhort, warn
BDAG.pt: fazer uma declaração solene sobre a verdade de algo, testemunhar; exortar com autoridade em assuntos de importância extraordinária, urgir solenemente, exortar, advertir

DEFINITION: to strive greatly, contend fiercely.
ORIGIN: From dia and machomai; to fight fiercely (in altercation).

BDAG.en: contend sharply
BDAG.pt: contender vigorosamente

DEFINITION: to remain, continue.
ORIGIN: From dia and meno; to stay constantly (in being or relation).

BDAG.en: to continue in an activity, state, or condition, remain; continue to exist, live on; to continue in association with someone, remain continually w. someone
BDAG.pt: continuar em uma atividade, estado ou condição, permanecer; continuar a existir, viver; continuar em associação com alguém, permanecer continuamente com alguém

DEFINITION: to divide up into parts, break up; to distribute.
ORIGIN: From dia and merizo; to partition thoroughly (literally in distribution, figuratively in dissension).

BDAG.en: to divide into separate parts, divide, separate; to distribute objects to a series of persons, distribute; to be divided into opposing units, be divided
BDAG.pt: dividir em partes separadas, dividir, separar; distribuir objetos a uma série de pessoas, distribuir; ser dividido em unidades opostas, estar dividido

DEFINITION: breaking up; discord, hostility.
ORIGIN: From diamerizo; disunion (of opinion and conduct).

BDAG.en: division into partisan and contentious units, dissension, disunity
BDAG.pt: divisão em unidades partidárias e contenciosas, dissensão, desunião

DEFINITION: to divide into portions, distribute; pass: to be spread about.
ORIGIN: From dia and the base of nomos; to distribute, i.e. (of information) to disseminate.

BDAG.en: distribute
BDAG.pt: distribuir

DEFINITION: to wink at, nod to, beckon to.
ORIGIN: From dia and neuo; to nod (or express by signs) across an intervening space.

BDAG.en: to express an idea through motion of a part of the body, such as head (‘nod’), eye, or hand (‘gesture’), give a sign
BDAG.pt: expressar uma ideia através do movimento de uma parte do corpo, como a cabeça ('acenar'), olho ou mão ('gesticular'), dar um sinal

DEFINITION: a reasoning, thought, cogitation.
ORIGIN: From a compound of dia and noieo; something thought through, i.e. A sentiment.

BDAG.en: product of a thought process, thought
BDAG.pt: produto de um processo de pensamento, pensamento

DEFINITION: understanding, intellect, mind, insight.
ORIGIN: From dia and nous; deep thought, properly, the faculty (mind or its disposition), by implication, its exercise.

BDAG.en: the faculty of thinking, comprehending, and reasoning, understanding, intelligence, mind as the organ of thinking; mind as a mode of thinking, disposition, thought, mind; mind focused on objective, purpose, plan; mind as fantasizing power, imagination, in an unfavorable sense; mind in sensory aspect, sense, impulse, in a bad sense
BDAG.pt: a faculdade de pensar, compreender e raciocinar, entendimento, inteligência, mente como órgão do pensar; mente como modo de pensar, disposição, pensamento, mente; mente focada no objetivo, propósito, plano; mente como poder de fantasiar, imaginação, em sentido desfavorável; mente no aspecto sensorial, sentido, impulso, em sentido mau

DEFINITION: to open up completely.
ORIGIN: From dia and anoigo; to open thoroughly, literally (as a first-born) or figuratively (to expound).

BDAG.en: open (a womb, the heavens); fig. ears, eyes, heart, mind; explain, interpret (the Scriptures)
BDAG.pt: abrir (o ventre, os céus); figurativamente ouvidos, olhos, coração, mente; explicar, interpretar (as Escrituras)

DEFINITION: to spend the whole night.
ORIGIN: From dia and a derivative of nux; to sit up the whole night.

BDAG.en: spend the whole night
BDAG.pt: passar a noite inteira

DEFINITION: to finish, complete, accomplish fully.
ORIGIN: From dia and anuo (to effect); to accomplish thoroughly.

BDAG.en: to carry out an activity, complete; arrive (at), intr., travel (to)
BDAG.pt: realizar uma atividade, completar; chegar (a), intransitivo, viajar (para)

DEFINITION: always, continually.
ORIGIN: From dia and the genitive case of pas; through all time, i.e. (adverbially) constantly.

DEFINITION: to cross over, pass over.
ORIGIN: From dia and a derivative of the base of peran; to cross entirely.

BDAG.en: in our literature movement across the area between two sides of a geographical object, cross (over)
BDAG.pt: na nossa literatura, movimento através da área entre dois lados de um objeto geográfico, atravessar (por cima)

DEFINITION: to sail over (across).
ORIGIN: From dia and pleo; to sail through.

BDAG.en: to cross an area by ship, sail through (the sea)
BDAG.pt: atravessar uma área de navio, navegar através (o mar)

DEFINITION: to toil through, to be worn out or annoyed.
ORIGIN: From dia and a derivative of ponos; to toil through, i.e. (passively) be worried.

BDAG.en: to feel burdened as the result of someone’s provocative activity, be (greatly) disturbed, annoyed
BDAG.pt: sentir-se sobrecarregado como resultado da atividade provocadora de alguém, ficar (muito) perturbado, incomodado

DEFINITION: to pass across, journey through.
ORIGIN: From dia and poreuomai; to travel through.
USAGE: go through, journey in, pass by.

BDAG.en: of movement by way of something, go, walk through something; of movement from one part or locality to another within a geographical area, pass through
BDAG.pt: de movimento por meio de algo, ir, caminhar através de algo; de movimento de uma parte ou localidade para outra dentro de uma área geográfica, passar por

DEFINITION: to be in trouble, doubt, difficulty; to be at a loss.
ORIGIN: From dia and aporeo; to be thoroughly nonplussed.

BDAG.en: be greatly perplexed, be at a loss
BDAG.pt: ficar muito perplexo, estar sem saber o que fazer

DEFINITION: to examine thoroughly, to gain by trading.
ORIGIN: From dia and pragmateuomai; to thoroughly occupy oneself, i.e. (transitively and by implication) to earn in business.

BDAG.en: gain by trading, earn
BDAG.pt: ganhar através de comércio, lucrar

DEFINITION: (lit: to saw through), to cut to the quick (with indignation and envy).
ORIGIN: From dia and the base of prizo; to saw asunder, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate.

BDAG.en: lit., like πρίω ‘saw through, saw asunder’; fig. be cut to the quick, be infuriated
BDAG.pt: lit., como πρίω 'serrar através, serrar em pedaços'; fig. ficar profundamente ofendido, ficar enfurecido

DEFINITION: to plunder, rob thoroughly.
ORIGIN: From dia and harpazo; to seize asunder, i.e. Plunder.

BDAG.en: plunder thoroughly (a house); rob; steal someone’s livelihood; snatch away, abduct or take captive someone
BDAG.pt: saquear completamente (uma casa); roubar; roubar o sustento de alguém; arrebatar, raptar ou levar cativo alguém

DEFINITION: to tear asunder, burst, rend.
ORIGIN: From dia and rhegnumi; to tear asunder.

DEFINITION: to make clear, explain fully.
ORIGIN: From dia and saphes (clear); to clear thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) declare.

BDAG.en: to cause something to be clear to the understanding, to clarify something that is obscure, explain, lit. ‘make clear’; to inform by relating something in detail, tell plainly, tell in detail, report
BDAG.pt: fazer com que algo se torne claro para a compreensão, clarificar algo obscuro, explicar, literalmente 'tornar claro'; informar relatando algo em detalhe, contar abertamente, relatar em detalhe, reportar

DEFINITION: to blackmail, extort from, intimidate.
ORIGIN: From dia and seio; to shake thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to intimidate.

BDAG.en: extort money by force or threat of violence, extort
BDAG.pt: extorquir dinheiro à força ou com ameaça de violência, extorquir

DEFINITION: generally to separate, to winnow, to squander.
ORIGIN: From dia and skorpizo; to dissipate, i.e. (genitive case) to rout or separate; specially, to winnow; figuratively, to squander.

BDAG.en: scatter, disperse (of a flock, God’s children, the proud, on the field of battle, components of the bread of the Lord’s Supper); scatter (of seed), waste, squander (figuratively)
BDAG.pt: espalhar, dispersar (de um rebanho, dos filhos de Deus, dos orgulhosos, no campo de batalha, dos componentes do pão da Ceia do Senhor); espalhar (de semente), desperdiçar, esbanjar (figurado)

DEFINITION: to draw apart, tear asunder.
ORIGIN: From dia and spao; to draw apart, i.e. Sever or dismember.

BDAG.en: tear apart, tear up (of a possessed person breaking chains, a document); of an angry mob that Paul would be torn in pieces by them; figuratively tear apart the members of Christ, i.e. the churches
BDAG.pt: rasgar, despedaçar (de um possesso quebrando correntes, um documento); de uma turba enfurecida que Paulo seria despedaçado por eles; figurativamente rasgar os membros de Cristo, ou seja, as igrejas

DEFINITION: to sow throughout, disperse (in foreign lands).
ORIGIN: From dia and speiro; to sow throughout, i.e. (figuratively) distribute in foreign lands.

BDAG.en: scatter someone (sons of Adam); (Passive) of scattered communities (of Christians)
BDAG.pt: espalhar alguém (filhos de Adão); (Passivo) de comunidades dispersas (de cristãos)

DEFINITION: lit: scattering abroad of seed by the sower, hence: dispersion, used especially of the Jews who had migrated and were scattered over the ancient world.
ORIGIN: From diaspeiro; dispersion, i.e. (specially and concretely) the (converted) Israelite resident in Gentile countries.

BDAG.en: state or condition of being scattered, dispersion (of those who are dispersed); the place in which the dispersed are found, dispersion, diaspora; fig. of Christians who live in dispersion in the world, far from their heavenly home
BDAG.pt: estado ou condição de estar espalhado, dispersão (daqueles que estão dispersos); o lugar onde os dispersos são encontrados, dispersão, diáspora; fig. de cristãos que vivem em dispersão no mundo, longe de sua pátria celestial

DEFINITION: to give a commission (instructions), order; to admonish, prohibit.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from dia and stello; to set (oneself) apart (figuratively, distinguish), i.e. (by implication) to enjoin.

DEFINITION: an interval of time, distance.
ORIGIN: From diistemi; an interval.

BDAG.en: a space of time between events, interval
BDAG.pt: um espaço de tempo entre eventos, intervalo

DEFINITION: distinction, difference, separation.
ORIGIN: From diastellomai; a variation.

BDAG.en: difference, distinction
BDAG.pt: diferença, distinção

DEFINITION: to pervert, corrupt, oppose, distort.
ORIGIN: From dia and strepho; to distort, i.e. (figuratively) misinterpret, or (morally) corrupt.

BDAG.en: to cause to be distorted, deform (of a vessel on the potter’s wheel: become misshapen); to cause to depart from an accepted standard of oral or spiritual values, make crooked, pervert; to cause to be uncertain about a belief or to believe something different, mislead, turn away someone from something
BDAG.pt: causar que algo se torne distorcido, deformar (de um vaso no torno do oleiro: ficar disforme); causar desvio de um padrão aceito de valores orais ou espirituais, tornar torto, perverter; causar incerteza sobre uma crença ou fazer crer algo diferente, enganar, desviar alguém de algo

DEFINITION: to save (rescue) through (some danger), bring safely to, escaped to.
ORIGIN: From dia and sozo; to save thoroughly, i.e. (by implication or analogy) to cure, preserve, rescue, etc.
USAGE: bring safe, escape (safe), heal, make perfectly whole, save.

BDAG.en: to rescue or deliver from a hazard or danger, bring safely through, also save, rescue; (Passive) escape death; of sick persons be cured
BDAG.pt: resgatar ou livrar de um perigo ou risco, trazer em segurança, também salvar, resgatar; (Passivo) escapar da morte; de pessoas doentes ser curado

DEFINITION: ordaining, ordinance, disposition.
ORIGIN: From diatasso; arrangement, i.e. Institution.

BDAG.en: that which has been ordered or commanded, ordinance, direction (of God)
BDAG.pt: aquilo que foi ordenado ou comandado, ordenança, direção (de Deus)

DEFINITION: a mandate, decree, edict.
ORIGIN: From diatasso; an arrangement, i.e. (authoritative) edict.

BDAG.en: an official ordinance, edict, command (of the king)
BDAG.pt: uma ordenança oficial, édito, comando (do rei)

DEFINITION: to trouble greatly, agitate.
ORIGIN: From dia and tarasso; to disturb wholly, i.e. Agitate (with alarm).

BDAG.en: confuse, perplex (greatly)
BDAG.pt: confundir, perplexar (grandemente)

DEFINITION: to arrange thoroughly, to charge, appoint.
ORIGIN: From dia and tasso; to arrange thoroughly, i.e. (specially) institute, prescribe, etc.
USAGE: appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain.

BDAG.en: to make orderly arrangements or to cause someone to do someth. that advances one’s objective, freq. of an official nature; to put into a proper order or relationship, make arrangements; To make provisions for someone arrange (accommodations); to give (detailed) instructions as to what must be done, order; order, command (Mid.)
BDAG.pt: fazer arranjos ordenados ou fazer com que alguém faça algo que avance o objetivo de alguém, frequentemente de natureza oficial; colocar em ordem ou relacionamento apropriado, fazer arranjos; Fazer provisões para alguém, arranjar (acomodações); dar instruções (detalhadas) sobre o que deve ser feito, ordenar; ordenar, comandar (Médio)

DEFINITION: to accomplish thoroughly, to persist.
ORIGIN: From dia and teleo; to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to persist.

BDAG.en: continue, remain
BDAG.pt: continuar, permanecer

DEFINITION: to keep safe, hold fast.
ORIGIN: From dia and tereo; to watch thoroughly, i.e. (positively and transitively) to observe strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to avoid wholly.

BDAG.en: to keep someth. mentally with implication of duration, keep; to keep oneself from doing something, keep free of
BDAG.pt: manter algo mentalmente com implicação de duração, guardar; abster-se de fazer algo, manter-se livre de

DEFINITION: wherefore, why.
ORIGIN: From dia and tis; through what cause ?, i.e. Why?.

BDAG.en: See διά B2b.
BDAG.pt: Ver διά B2b.

DEFINITION: (a) to appoint, make (of a covenant), (b) to make (a will).
ORIGIN: Middle voice from dia and tithemi; to put apart, i.e. (figuratively) dispose (by assignment, compact, or bequest).

DEFINITION: to rub hard, rub away, to spend time.
ORIGIN: From dia and the base of tribos; to wear through (time), i.e. Remain.

BDAG.en: to remain or stay in a place, spend time, usually rendered stay in sense of duration, esp. when associated with place or pers.
BDAG.pt: permanecer ou ficar em um lugar, passar tempo, geralmente traduzido como ficar no sentido de duração, especialmente quando associado a lugar ou pessoa

DEFINITION: food, nourishment.
ORIGIN: From a compound of dia and trepho; nourishment.

BDAG.en: that which sustains or nourishes the body, support, sustenance; means of subsistence, food
BDAG.pt: aquilo que sustenta ou nutre o corpo, sustento, provisão; meio de subsistência, alimento

DEFINITION: to shine through, dawn (of the light coming through the shadows).
ORIGIN: From dia and augazo; to glimmer through, i.e. Break (as day).

BDAG.en: to emit light through someth.; shine through; dawn, break
BDAG.pt: emitir luz através de algo; brilhar através; amanhecer, romper

DEFINITION: through which light passes, transparent.
ORIGIN: From dia and phaino; appearing through, i.e. "diaphanous".

BDAG.en: possessing the property of being able to be seen through, transparent, pure
BDAG.pt: possuir a propriedade de poder ser visto através, transparente, puro

DEFINITION: (a) trans: to carry through, hither and thither, (b) intrans: to be different, differ, and sometimes: to surpass, excel.
ORIGIN: From dia and phero; to bear through, i.e. (literally) transport; usually to bear apart, i.e. (objectively) to toss about (figuratively, report); subjectively, to "differ", or (by implication) surpass.
USAGE: be better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent, make matter, publish, be of more value.

BDAG.en: to carry someth. through a place or structure, carry through; to cause to move from one locality to another, carry hither and yon; to be unlike, differ, be different; differ to one’s advantage fr. someone or someth., be worth more than, be superior to
BDAG.pt: carregar algo através de um lugar ou estrutura, levar através; causar movimento de um local para outro, carregar para cá e para lá; ser diferente, distinguir-se; ser diferente em vantagem de alguém ou algo, valer mais que, ser superior a

DEFINITION: to flee through, escape.
ORIGIN: From dia and pheugo; to flee through, i.e. Escape.

BDAG.en: escape
BDAG.pt: escapar

DEFINITION: to report, publish abroad.
ORIGIN: From dia and a derivative of pheme; to report thoroughly, i.e. Divulgate.
USAGE: blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame.

BDAG.en: to make extensively known by word of mouth, make generally known, spread abroad; spread widely, disseminate, advertise
BDAG.pt: tornar amplamente conhecido de boca em boca, tornar geralmente conhecido, espalhar; espalhar amplamente, disseminar, anunciar

DEFINITION: to destroy, waste; hence met: to corrupt.
ORIGIN: From diaballo and phtheiro; to rot thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to ruin (passively, decay utterly, figuratively, pervert).

BDAG.en: to cause the destruction of someth., spoil, destroy (of rust eating into iron, of moths that eat clothes); destroy persons and nations; be destroyed (of a person’s physical being, of ships, a kingdom, bodies of starving persons waste away); to cause to become morally corrupt, deprave, ruin (the earth (i.e. its people), one's mind/disposition)
BDAG.pt: causar a destruição de algo, estragar, destruir (de ferrugem corroendo ferro, de traças que comem roupas); destruir pessoas e nações; ser destruído (do ser físico de uma pessoa, de navios, de um reino, dos corpos de pessoas famintas definharem); causar a corrupção moral, depravar, arruinar (a terra (i.e. seu povo), a mente/disposição).

DEFINITION: destruction, decay, corruption.
ORIGIN: From diaphtheiro; decay.

BDAG.en: the condition or state of rotting or decaying, destruction, corruption of the body; return to decay (i.e. prob. the realm of the dead)
BDAG.pt: a condição ou estado de apodrecimento ou decadência, destruição, corrupção do corpo; retorno à decadência (i.e. provavelmente o reino dos mortos)

DEFINITION: differing, different; hence: excellent.
ORIGIN: From diaphero; varying; also surpassing.

BDAG.en: pert. to being different, w. focus on distinctiveness, different; pert. to being different, w. focus on value, outstanding, excellent
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao ser diferente, com foco na distinção, diferente; pertencente ao ser diferente, com foco no valor, notável, excelente

DEFINITION: to guard carefully, protect, defend.
ORIGIN: From dia and phulasso; to guard thoroughly, i.e. Protect.

BDAG.en: guard, protect (someone/something, of God, of angels)
BDAG.pt: guardar, proteger (alguém/algo, de Deus, de anjos)

DEFINITION: to have in hand, thus to lay hands on (violently).
ORIGIN: From dia and a derivative of cheir; to handle thoroughly, i.e. Lay violent hands upon.

DEFINITION: to separate myself from, part from, go away.
ORIGIN: From dia and the middle voice of chorizo; to remove (oneself) wholly, i.e. Retire.

DEFINITION: able to teach, apt to teach.
ORIGIN: From didaktos; instructive ("didactic").

BDAG.en: skillful in teaching
BDAG.pt: hábil em ensinar

DEFINITION: instructed, taught.
ORIGIN: From didasko; (subjectively) instructed, or (objectively) communicated by teaching.

BDAG.en: pert. to being taught, taught, instructed (as recipients of instruction); pert. to being communicated as instruction, imparted, taught
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao ser ensinado, ensinado, instruído (como receptores de instrução); pertencente ao ser comunicado como instrução, transmitido, ensinado

DEFINITION: instruction (the function or the information).
ORIGIN: From didaskalos; instruction (the function or the information).

BDAG.en: the act of teaching, teaching, instruction; that which is taught, teaching, instruction (often of the teachings of eccl. Christianity)
BDAG.pt: o ato de ensinar, ensino, instrução; aquilo que é ensinado, doutrina, instrução (frequentemente dos ensinamentos do cristianismo eclesiástico)

DEFINITION: a teacher, master.
ORIGIN: From didasko; an instructor (genitive case or specially).

BDAG.en: teacher (used also in addressing Jesus, as a designation for Jesus, or for scholars/officials in the assembly)
BDAG.pt: mestre (usado também para se dirigir a Jesus, como designação para Jesus, ou para estudiosos/oficiais na assembleia)

DEFINITION: to teach, direct, admonish.
ORIGIN: A prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb dao (to learn); to teach (in the same broad application).

BDAG.en: to tell someone what to do, tell, instruct; to provide instruction in a formal or informal setting, teach (absolutely, with person/thing as direct object, or with acc. of person and thing)
BDAG.pt: dizer a alguém o que fazer, dizer, instruir; fornecer instrução em um ambiente formal ou informal, ensinar (absolutamente, com pessoa/coisa como objeto direto, ou com acusativo de pessoa e coisa)

DEFINITION: teaching, doctrine, what is taught.
ORIGIN: From didasko; instruction (the act or the matter).

BDAG.en: 1 the activity of teaching, teaching, instruction; 2 the content of teaching, teaching, instruction
BDAG.pt: 1 a atividade de ensinar, ensino, instrução; 2 o conteúdo do ensino, doutrina, instrução

DEFINITION: a double-drachma, two drachmae, a Greek silver coin.
ORIGIN: From dis and drachme; a double drachma (didrachm).

BDAG.en: a double drachma, two-drachma piece (a coin worth two Attic drachmas, about equal to a half shekel among the Jews, and was the sum required of each person annually as the temple tax)
BDAG.pt: uma dracma dupla, moeda de duas dracmas (moeda equivalente a duas dracmas áticas, aproximadamente igual a um meio siclo entre os judeus, e era a soma exigida anualmente de cada pessoa como imposto do templo)

DEFINITION: the Twin; Didymus, the Greek name equivalent to Thomas.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from dis; double, i.e. Twin; Didymus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Didymus (as a name); lit. twin, Greek name of the apostle Thomas
BDAG.pt: Dídimo (como nome); literalmente gêmeo, nome grego do apóstolo Tomé

DEFINITION: to offer, give; to put, place.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an alternative in most of the tenses); to give (used in a very wide application, properly, or by implication, literally or figuratively; greatly modified by the connection).
USAGE: adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit, deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minister, number, offer, have power, put, receive, set, shew, smite (+ with the hand), strike (+ with the palm of the hand), suffer, take, utter, yield.

BDAG.en: to give as an expression of generosity, give, donate; to give someth. out, give, bestow, grant; to express devotion, give (glory to God); to cause to happen, produce, make, cause, give; to put something in care of another, entrust; to engage in a financial transaction (pay, render account, deposit); to appoint to special responsibility, appoint; to cause something to happen, give (knowledge, life); to bear as a natural product, yield, produce; to dedicate oneself for some purpose or cause, give up, sacrifice oneself; to cause (oneself) to go, go, venture somewhere; to use an oracular device, draw/cast lots; to grant by formal action, grant, allow; to cause to come into being, institute; to give up, give back; to proffer something, extend, offer; in many phrases relates to an activity or an abstract object (give counsel, give testimony, give an example, grant peace, inflict punishment, etc.)
BDAG.pt: dar como expressão de generosidade, dar, doar; dar algo para fora, dar, conceder, outorgar; expressar devoção, dar (glória a Deus); fazer acontecer, produzir, causar, dar; colocar algo sob os cuidados de outro, confiar; engajar-se numa transação financeira (pagar, prestar contas, depositar); nomear para uma responsabilidade especial, designar; fazer com que algo aconteça, dar (conhecimento, vida); produzir como resultado natural, render, produzir; dedicar-se a um propósito ou causa, entregar-se, sacrificar-se; fazer com que (a si mesmo) vá, ir, aventurar-se em algum lugar; usar um dispositivo oracular, sortear/lançar sortes; conceder por ação formal, permitir, autorizar; fazer vir à existência, instituir; entregar, devolver; oferecer algo, estender, apresentar; em muitas frases relaciona-se com uma atividade ou objeto abstrato (dar conselho, dar testemunho, dar um exemplo, conceder paz, infligir castigo, etc.)

DEFINITION: to wake out of sleep, arouse in general, stir up.
ORIGIN: From dia and egeiro; to wake fully; i.e. Arouse (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: wake up, arouse someone who is asleep; (passive) awaken; (figuratively) of a calm sea: was becoming aroused; arouse, stir up
BDAG.pt: acordar, despertar alguém que está dormindo; (passivo) ser despertado; (figurado) de um mar calmo: estava se agitando; despertar, instigar

DEFINITION: a meeting-place of roads, a public spot in a city.
ORIGIN: From dia and exodos; an outlet through, i.e. Probably an open square (from which roads diverge).

BDAG.en: street-crossing, the place where a main street cuts (through) the city boundary and goes (out) into the open country, outlet, way out of town; the point where a stream of water flowing underground suddenly breaks through and flows out freely, a spring
BDAG.pt: Cruzamento de rua, o lugar onde uma rua principal corta (através) do limite da cidade e sai para campo aberto, saída, caminho para fora da cidade; o ponto onde um fluxo de água subterrâneo irrompe subitamente e flui livremente, uma nascente.

DEFINITION: an explainer, an interpreter.
ORIGIN: From diermeneuo; an explainer.

BDAG.en: interpreter, translator of ecstatic speech
BDAG.pt: Intérprete, tradutor de discurso extático.

DEFINITION: to explain thoroughly, by implication to translate.
ORIGIN: From dia and hermeneuo; to explain thoroughly, by implication, to translate.

BDAG.en: to translate from one language to another, translate; to clarify someth. so as to make it understandable, explain, interpret
BDAG.pt: Traduzir de uma língua para outra, traduzir; Clarificar algo para torná-lo compreensível, explicar, interpretar.

DEFINITION: to pass through, spread (as a report).
ORIGIN: From dia and erchomai; to traverse (literally).
USAGE: come, depart, go (about, abroad, everywhere, over, through, throughout), pass (by, over, through, throughout), pierce through, travel, walk through.

BDAG.en: to move within or through an area, go (through) (travel or move about, spread; go through someth. (go or travel through; come, go; go through someth. in one’s mind, review); to pass into or through an obstacle, penetrate
BDAG.pt: Mover-se dentro ou através de uma área, ir (através) (viajar ou se mover, espalhar; atravessar algo (ir ou viajar através; vir, ir); percorrer algo na mente, rever); Passar para dentro ou através de um obstáculo, penetrar.

DEFINITION: to find by inquiry.
ORIGIN: From dia and erotao; to question throughout, i.e. Ascertain by interrogation.

BDAG.en: ask about, find by inquiry [about a house]
BDAG.pt: Perguntar sobre, descobrir por inquérito [sobre uma casa].

DEFINITION: lasting two years, two years old.
ORIGIN: From dis and etos; of two years (in age).

BDAG.en: two years old
BDAG.pt: de dois anos de idade

DEFINITION: a period of two years, two years; according to ancient practice this means any period between one and two years.
ORIGIN: From dietes; a space of two years (biennium).

BDAG.en: a span of two years, two years; a two-year period of limitation, biennium, legal and administrative t.t.
BDAG.pt: um período de dois anos, dois anos; um período de limitação de dois anos, biênio, termo legal e administrativo

DEFINITION: to relate in full, describe, narrate.
ORIGIN: From dia and hegeomai; to relate fully.

BDAG.en: to give a detailed account of someth. in words, tell, relate, describe
BDAG.pt: dar um relato detalhado de algo em palavras, contar, relatar, descrever

DEFINITION: a narrative.
ORIGIN: From diegeomai; a recital.

BDAG.en: an orderly description of facts, events, actions, or words narrative, account
BDAG.pt: uma descrição ordenada de fatos, eventos, ações ou palavras, narrativa, relato

DEFINITION: continuous, continually, unbroken.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of dia and a derivative of an alternate of phero; carried through, i.e. (adverbially with eis and ho prefixed) perpetually.

BDAG.en: pert. to being continuous, without interruption, always of time
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser contínuo, sem interrupção, sempre no tempo

DEFINITION: divided into two seas, dividing the sea (as a reef).
ORIGIN: From dis and thalassa; having two seas, i.e. A sound with a double outlet.

BDAG.en: 'with the sea on both sides' (signifying a point of land jutting out with water on both sides)
BDAG.pt: 'com o mar de ambos os lados' (significando um ponto de terra projetando-se com água em ambos os lados)

DEFINITION: to pass through (to), come through (to), pierce.
ORIGIN: From dia and the base of hikanos; to reach through, i.e. Penetrate.

BDAG.en: to move through a three-dimensional space, pierce, penetrate
BDAG.pt: mover-se através de um espaço tridimensional, perfurar, penetrar

DEFINITION: to put apart, separate, put some distance between.
ORIGIN: From dia and histemi; to stand apart, i.e. (reflexively) to remove, intervene.
USAGE: go further, be parted, after the space of.

BDAG.en: separate, divide; move from, separate from, or take leave of, go away, part; cause separation through movement, go on; mark the passage of time, pass
BDAG.pt: separar, dividir; afastar-se, separar-se, ou despedir-se, ir embora, partir; causar separação através do movimento, prosseguir; marcar a passagem do tempo, passar

DEFINITION: to assert emphatically, lean upon.
ORIGIN: From dia and a derivative of ischuros; to stout it through, i.e. Asservate.

BDAG.en: to be emphatic or resolute about someth., insist, maintain firmly
BDAG.pt: ser enfático ou resoluto sobre algo, insistir, manter firmemente

DEFINITION: just judging, just judgment.
ORIGIN: From dikaios and krisis; a just sentence.

BDAG.en: just/fair verdict
BDAG.pt: veredicto justo/equitativo

DEFINITION: just; especially, just in the eyes of God; righteous; the elect (a Jewish idea).
ORIGIN: From dike; equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent, holy (absolutely or relatively).

BDAG.en: pert. to being in accordance with high standards of rectitude, upright, just, fair; the neuter denotes that which is obligatory in view of certain requirements of justice, right, fair, equitable
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar de acordo com altos padrões de retidão, íntegro, justo, equitativo; o neutro denota aquilo que é obrigatório em vista de certos requisitos de justiça, o correto, o justo, o equitativo

DEFINITION: (usually if not always in a Jewish atmosphere), justice, justness, righteousness, righteousness of which God is the source or author, but practically: a divine righteousness.
ORIGIN: From dikaios; equity (of character or act); specially (Christian) justification.

BDAG.en: the quality of being upright; the quality, state, or practice of judicial responsibility with a focus on fairness, justice, equitableness; quality or state of juridical correctness with focus on redemptive action, righteousness; the quality or characteristic of upright behavior, uprightness, righteousness.
BDAG.pt: a qualidade de ser reto; a qualidade, estado ou prática de responsabilidade judicial com foco na imparcialidade, justiça, equidade; a qualidade ou estado de correção jurídica com foco na ação redentora, retidão; a qualidade ou característica de comportamento reto, retidão, justiça.

DEFINITION: to make righteous, defend the cause of, plead for the righteousness (innocence) of, acquit, justify; hence: to regard as righteous.
ORIGIN: From dikaios; to render (i.e. Show or regard as) just or innocent.

BDAG.en: to practice righteousness; to take up a legal cause, show justice, do justice, take up a cause; to render a favorable verdict, vindicate; to be found in the right, be free of charges; to acquit, be pronounced and treated as righteous; to cause someone to be released from personal or institutional claims, make free/pure; to demonstrate to be morally right, prove to be right.
BDAG.pt: praticar a justiça; tomar uma causa legal, demonstrar justiça, fazer justiça, tomar uma causa; proferir um veredicto favorável, vindicar; ser considerado certo, estar livre de acusações; absolver, ser declarado e tratado como justo; fazer com que alguém seja libertado de reivindicações pessoais ou institucionais, tornar livre/puro; demonstrar ser moralmente correto, provar ser justo.

DEFINITION: a thing pronounced (by God) to be righteous (just, the right); or the restoration of a criminal, a fresh chance given him; a righteous deed, an instance of perfect righteousness.
ORIGIN: From dikaioo; an equitable deed; by implication, a statute or decision.

BDAG.en: a regulation relating to just or right action, regulation, requirement, commandment; an action that meets expectations as to what is right or just, righteous deed; to clear someone of a violation.
BDAG.pt: uma regulamentação relativa a uma ação justa ou correta, regulamento, requisito, mandamento; uma ação que satisfaz as expectativas do que é certo ou justo, ato justo; libertar alguém de uma violação.

DEFINITION: righteously, justly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from dikaios; equitably.

BDAG.en: pert. to being just or right in a juridical sense, justly, in an upright manner; pert. to quality of character, thought, or behavior, correctly, justly, uprightly.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser justo ou correto em um sentido jurídico, justamente, de maneira reta; pertencente à qualidade de caráter, pensamento ou comportamento, corretamente, justamente, com retidão.

DEFINITION: acquittal, justifying, justification, a process of absolution.
ORIGIN: From dikaioo; aquittal (for Christ's sake).

BDAG.en: justification, vindication, acquittal (as a process as well as its result).
BDAG.pt: justificação, vindicação, absolvição (tanto como processo quanto como seu resultado).

DEFINITION: a judge.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of dike; a judger.

BDAG.en: one who presides over and decides cases in court, judge.
BDAG.pt: aquele que preside e decide casos em tribunal, juiz.

DEFINITION: (a) (originally: custom, usage) right, justice, (b) process of law, judicial hearing, (c) execution of sentence, punishment, penalty, (d) justice, vengeance.
ORIGIN: Probably from deiknuo; right (as self-evident), i.e. Justice (the principle, a decision, or its execution).

BDAG.en: punishment meted out as legal penalty, punishment, penalty; Justice personified as a deity.
BDAG.pt: punição aplicada como penalidade legal, castigo, penalidade; Justiça personificada como uma divindade.

DEFINITION: a fishing-net.
ORIGIN: Probably from a primary verb diko (to cast); a seine (for fishing).

BDAG.en: a generic term ‘net’, but in NT only of fishnet; for catching birds.
BDAG.pt: um termo genérico para ‘rede’, mas no NT apenas de rede de pesca; para apanhar pássaros.

DEFINITION: given to repetition, double-tongued.
ORIGIN: From dis and logos; equivocal, i.e. Telling a different story.

BDAG.en: insincere (double-talking).
BDAG.pt: insincero (de falar duas vezes/enganoso).

DEFINITION: wherefore, on which account, therefore.
ORIGIN: From dia and hos; through which thing, i.e. Consequently.

BDAG.en: inferential conjunction: therefore, for this reason
BDAG.pt: conjunção inferencial: portanto, por esta razão

DEFINITION: to journey through, go about.
ORIGIN: From dia and hodeuo; to travel through.

BDAG.en: 1 go, travel through. 2 go about, intr.
BDAG.pt: 1 ir, viajar através. 2 andar, circular (intransitivo)

DEFINITION: Dionysius, an Athenian.
ORIGIN: From Dionusos (Bacchus); reveller; Dionysius, an Athenian.

BDAG.en: Dionysius, name of an Athenian, member of the Areopagus, converted by Paul
BDAG.pt: Dionísio, nome de um ateniense, membro do Areópago, convertido por Paulo

DEFINITION: wherefore (emphatically), for which very reason.
ORIGIN: From dio and per; on which very account.

BDAG.en: inferential conj.: therefore, for this very reason
BDAG.pt: conjunção inferencial: portanto, por esta razão exata

DEFINITION: fallen from the sky.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of Zeus and the alternate of pipto; sky-fallen (i.e. An aerolite).

BDAG.en: lit. ‘fallen from Zeus’ or ‘the sky’. Orig. of meteorites viewed as heaven-sent cult objects fallen from heaven; in our lit. only as neut. subst. τὸ διοπετές the image (of Artemis) fallen fr. heaven at Ephesus
BDAG.pt: lit. ‘caído de Zeus’ ou ‘do céu’. Originalmente de meteoritos vistos como objetos de culto enviados do céu; em nossa literatura apenas como substantivo neutro τὸ διοπετές a imagem (de Ártemis) caída do céu em Éfeso

DEFINITION: amendment, improvement, reformation.
ORIGIN: From a compound of dia and a derivative of orthos, meaning to straighten thoroughly; rectification, i.e. (specially) the Messianic restauration.

BDAG.en: a process leading to a new order viewed as something yet to be realized, improvement, reformation, new order.
BDAG.pt: um processo que leva a uma nova ordem vista como algo ainda a ser realizado, melhoria, reforma, nova ordem.

DEFINITION: to dig through (as of breaking into a house).
ORIGIN: From dia and orusso; to penetrate burglariously.

BDAG.en: to break through a wall or barrier. In our lit. of a thief who digs through the (sun-dried brick) wall of a house and gains entrance, break through, break in
BDAG.pt: romper uma parede ou barreira. Em nossa literatura, de um ladrão que escava a parede (de tijolos de sol) de uma casa e entra, romper, invadir

DEFINITION: the Dioscuri, Castor and Pollux, sons of Zeus and Leda, and patrons of sailors.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of Zeus and a form of the base of korasion; sons of Jupiter, i.e. The twins Dioscuri.

BDAG.en: the Dioscuri title of Castor and Pollux, twin sons of Zeus and Leda, serving as insignia and also tutelary deities of an Alexandrian ship
BDAG.pt: o título Dióscuros de Castor e Pólux, filhos gêmeos de Zeus e Leda, servindo como insígnias e também como deuses tutelares de um navio alexandrino

DEFINITION: on the very account that, because, inasmuch as.
ORIGIN: From dia and hoti; on the very account that, or inasmuch as.

BDAG.en: conj. marker of a causal connection between two statements, because (= διὰτοῦτο ὅτι ‘for the reason that, in view of the fact that’)
BDAG.pt: conjunção. Marcador de uma conexão causal entre duas declarações, porque (= διὰτοῦτο ὅτι ‘pela razão de que, visto o fato de que’)

DEFINITION: "cherished by Zeus", Diotrephes, an opponent of the apostle John.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of Zeus and trepho; Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity.

BDAG.en: Diotrephes, a Christian, influential in his congregation
BDAG.pt: Diótrefes, um cristão, influente em sua congregação

DEFINITION: double, two-fold.
ORIGIN: From dis and (probably) the base of pleion; two-fold.

BDAG.en: double, two-fold
BDAG.pt: duplo, de duas dobras

DEFINITION: to double, render back double.
ORIGIN: From diplous; to render two-fold.

BDAG.en: to double
BDAG.pt: duplicar

DEFINITION: twice, entirely, utterly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from duo; twice.

BDAG.en: twice
BDAG.pt: duas vezes

DEFINITION: to waver, doubt, hesitate.
ORIGIN: From dis; properly, to duplicate, i.e. (mentally) to waver (in opinion).

BDAG.en: gener. ‘to be uncertain, to have second thoughts about a matter’. 1 to have doubts concerning something, doubt, waver. 2 to be uncertain about taking a particular course of action, hesitate in doubt
BDAG.pt: genericamente ‘estar incerto, ter segundas intenções sobre um assunto’. 1 ter dúvidas sobre algo, duvidar, vacilar. 2 estar incerto sobre tomar um curso de ação particular, hesitar em dúvida

DEFINITION: (lit: twain-mouthed; hence: of a sword, as a drinker of blood), two-edged.
ORIGIN: From dis and stoma; double-edged.

BDAG.en: pert. to having two edges, double-edged of a sword
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter duas arestas, de gume duplo de uma espada

DEFINITION: two thousand.
ORIGIN: From dis and chilioi; two thousand.

BDAG.en: two thousand
BDAG.pt: dois mil

DEFINITION: to strain thoroughly, strain out.
ORIGIN: From dia and hulizo hoo-lid'-zo (to filter); to strain out.

BDAG.en: filter out, strain out (fr. a liquid)
BDAG.pt: coar, filtrar (de um líquido)

DEFINITION: to cut asunder; met: to set at variance, make to be hostile.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of dis; to make apart, i.e. Sunder (figuratively, alienate).

BDAG.en: to divide in two, separate; cause a separation, separate (someone)
BDAG.pt: dividir em dois, separar; causar uma separação, separar (alguém)

DEFINITION: division, dissension, standing apart.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of dis and stasis; disunion, i.e. (figuratively) dissension.

BDAG.en: the state of being in factious opposition, dissension
BDAG.pt: o estado de estar em oposição facciosa, dissensão

DEFINITION: to cut in two, perhaps: scourge severely.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a derivative of dis and a derivative of temno (to cut); to bisect, i.e. (by extension) to flog severely.

BDAG.en: cut in two (of the dismemberment of a condemned person); figurative extension: punish w. utmost severity
BDAG.pt: cortar em dois (referente à desmembramento de um condenado); extensão figurativa: punir com a máxima severidade

DEFINITION: to thirst for, desire earnestly.
ORIGIN: From a variation of dipsos; to thirst for (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to have a desire for liquid, be thirsty, suffer from thirst; to have a strong desire to attain some goal, thirst, i.e. long for something
BDAG.pt: ter desejo de líquido, ter sede, sofrer de sede; ter um forte desejo de alcançar algum objetivo, ansiar, isto é, desejar algo

DEFINITION: thirst.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; thirst.

BDAG.en: thirst
BDAG.pt: sede

DEFINITION: (lit: of two souls, of two selves), double-minded, wavering.
ORIGIN: From dis and psuche; two-spirited, i.e. Vacillating (in opinion or purpose).

BDAG.en: double-minded, pert. to being uncertain about the truth of someth., doubting, hesitating
BDAG.pt: de coração duplo (double-minded), pertencente a estar incerto sobre a verdade de algo, duvidoso, hesitante

DEFINITION: chase, pursuit; persecution.
ORIGIN: From dioko; persecution.

BDAG.en: a program or process designed to harass and oppress someone, persecution (only for reasons of belief in our lit.)
BDAG.pt: um programa ou processo destinado a assediar e oprimir alguém, perseguição (apenas por motivos de crença em nossa literatura)

DEFINITION: a persecutor.
ORIGIN: From dioko; a persecutor.

BDAG.en: persecutor
BDAG.pt: perseguidor

DEFINITION: to put to flight, pursue, by implication to persecute.
ORIGIN: A prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb dio (to flee; compare the base of deilos and diakonos); to pursue (literally or figuratively); by implication, to persecute.
USAGE: ensue, follow (after), given to, (suffer) persecute(-ion), press forward.

BDAG.en: 1. to move rapidly and decisively toward an objective, hasten, run, press on; 2. to harass someone, especially because of beliefs, persecute; 3. to cause to run or set in motion, drive away, drive out; 4. to follow in haste in order to find something, run after, pursue (physically or figuratively: pursue, strive for, seek after, aspire to something)
BDAG.pt: 1. mover-se rápida e decisivamente em direção a um objetivo, apressar-se, correr, avançar; 2. atormentar alguém, especialmente por causa de crenças, perseguir; 3. fazer correr ou pôr em movimento, afastar, expulsar; 4. seguir com pressa para encontrar algo, correr atrás, perseguir (fisicamente ou figurativamente: buscar, lutar por, aspirar a algo)

DEFINITION: an opinion, (a public) decree.
ORIGIN: From the base of dokeo; a law (civil, ceremonial or ecclesiastical).

BDAG.en: 1. a formal statement concerning rules or regulations that are to be observed (ordinance, decision, command); b. an imperial declaration (decree); 2. something that is taught as an established tenet or statement of belief, doctrine, dogma
BDAG.pt: 1. uma declaração formal concernente a regras ou regulamentos que devem ser observados (ordenança, decisão, comando); b. uma declaração imperial (decreto); 2. algo que é ensinado como um princípio ou declaração de crença estabelecida, doutrina, dogma

DEFINITION: to subject to regulations, decree; mid: to subject myself to regulations, be decree-ridden.
ORIGIN: From dogma; to prescribe by statute, i.e. (reflexively) to submit to, ceremonially rule.

BDAG.en: to put under obligation by rules or ordinances, obligate; (passive) submit to rules and regulations
BDAG.pt: colocar sob obrigação por regras ou ordenanças, obrigar; (passivo) submeter-se a regras e regulamentos

DEFINITION: to think, seem, appear, it seems.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb, doko dok'-o (used only in an alternate in certain tenses; compare the base of deiknuo) of the same meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or uncertainly).
USAGE: be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow.

BDAG.en: 1. to consider as probable, think, believe, suppose, consider (subjective opinion); 2. to appear to one’s understanding, seem, be recognized as (have the appearance; be influential, have a reputation)
BDAG.pt: 1. considerar como provável, pensar, crer, supor, considerar (opinião subjetiva); 2. parecer ao entendimento, parecer, ser reconhecido como (ter a aparência; ser influente, ter reputação)

DEFINITION: to put to the test, prove, examine; to distinguish by testing, approve after testing; to be fit.
ORIGIN: From dokimos; to test (literally or figuratively); by implication, to approve.
USAGE: allow, discern, examine, X like, (ap-)prove, try.

BDAG.en: 1. to make a critical examination of something to determine genuineness, put to the test, examine; 2. to draw a conclusion about worth on the basis of testing, prove, approve, accept as proved
BDAG.pt: 1. fazer um exame crítico de algo para determinar a autenticidade, pôr à prova, examinar; 2. tirar uma conclusão sobre o valor com base no teste, provar, aprovar, aceitar como provado

DEFINITION: (the process or result of) trial, proving, approval.
ORIGIN: From the same as dokimos; test (abstractly or concretely); by implication, trustiness.

BDAG.en: 1. a testing process, test, ordeal; 2. the experience of going through a test with special reference to the result, standing a test, character
BDAG.pt: 1. um processo de teste, prova, provação; 2. a experiência de passar por um teste com referência especial ao resultado, suportar uma prova, caráter

DEFINITION: a test, trial, what is genuine.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of dokime; a testing; by implication, trustworthiness.

BDAG.en: the process or means of determining the genuineness of something, testing, means of testing; genuineness as result of a test, genuine, without alloy
BDAG.pt: o processo ou meio de determinar a autenticidade de algo, teste, meio de teste; autenticidade como resultado de um teste, genuíno, puro

DEFINITION: approved, acceptable, tried.
ORIGIN: From dokeo; properly, acceptable (current after assayal), i.e. Approved.

BDAG.en: pert. to being genuine on the basis of testing, approved (by test), tried and true, genuine; pert. to being considered worthy of high regard, respected, esteemed; pert. to being valuable, precious
BDAG.pt: pert. a ser genuíno com base em teste, aprovado (por teste), provado e verdadeiro, genuíno; pert. a ser considerado digno de alta estima, respeitado, estimado; pert. a ser valioso, precioso

DEFINITION: a beam or spar of timber.
ORIGIN: From dechomai (through the idea of holding up); a stick of timber.

BDAG.en: a piece of heavy timber such as a beam used in roof construction or to bar a door, beam of wood
BDAG.pt: uma peça de madeira pesada, como uma viga usada na construção de telhados ou para trancar uma porta, trave de madeira

DEFINITION: treacherous, deceitful, fraudulent.
ORIGIN: From dolos; guileful.

BDAG.en: deceitful, treacherous (pertaining to violation of trust in effort to deceive).
BDAG.pt: enganoso, traiçoeiro (relativo à violação da confiança no esforço para enganar).

DEFINITION: to act deceitfully, deceive, use fraud.
ORIGIN: From dolios; to be guileful.

BDAG.en: deceive.
BDAG.pt: enganar.

DEFINITION: deceit, guile, treachery.
ORIGIN: From an obsolete primary verb, dello (probably meaning to decoy; compare deleazo); a trick (bait), i.e. (figuratively) wile.

BDAG.en: deceit, cunning, treachery (taking advantage through craft and underhanded methods).
BDAG.pt: engano, astúcia, traição (tirar vantagem através de métodos ardilosos e sorrateiros).

DEFINITION: to adulterate, corrupt, ensnare.
ORIGIN: From dolos; to ensnare, i.e. (figuratively) adulterate.

BDAG.en: to beguile by craft, falsify, adulterate (to make false through deception or distortion).
BDAG.pt: enganar pela astúcia, falsificar, adulterar (tornar falso através de engano ou distorção).

DEFINITION: a gift, present.
ORIGIN: From the base of didomi; a present.

BDAG.en: gift.
BDAG.pt: dádiva, presente.

DEFINITION: honor, renown; glory, an especially divine quality, the unspoken manifestation of God, splendor.
ORIGIN: From the base of dokeo; glory (as very apparent), in a wide application (literal or figurative, objective or subjective).

BDAG.en: brightness, splendor, radiance; greatness, splendor; honor, prestige, fame, renown (in general, or approbation/recognition of status/performance).
BDAG.pt: brilho, esplendor, radiância; grandeza, magnificência; honra, prestígio, fama, renome (em geral, ou aprovação/reconhecimento de status/desempenho).

DEFINITION: to render or esteem glorious (in a wide application).
ORIGIN: From doxa; to render (or esteem) glorious (in a wide application).
USAGE: (make) glorify(-ious), full of (have) glory, honour, magnify.

BDAG.en: to influence one’s opinion about another so as to enhance the latter’s reputation, praise, honor, extol; to cause to have splendid greatness, clothe in splendor, glorify.
BDAG.pt: influenciar a opinião sobre outra pessoa de modo a aumentar a reputação, louvar, honrar, exaltar; causar-lhe esplêndida grandeza, revestir de esplendor, glorificar.

DEFINITION: "gazelle" (an animal with large bright eyes), Dorcas, a Christian woman.
ORIGIN: Gazelle; Dorcas, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Dorcas, meaning gazelle (a name).
BDAG.pt: Dorcas, que significa gazela (um nome).

DEFINITION: the act of giving, a gift.
ORIGIN: From the base of didomi; a giving; by implication, (concretely) a gift.

BDAG.en: 1 gift; 2 giving
BDAG.pt: 1 dádiva; 2 dar/ato de dar

DEFINITION: a giver.
ORIGIN: From the base of didomi; a giver.

BDAG.en: giver.
BDAG.pt: doador.

DEFINITION: to bring into subjection, enslave, treat as a slave.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of doulos and ago; to be a slave-driver, i.e. To enslave (figuratively, subdue).

BDAG.en: enslave, subjugate (figuratively: direct the body for useful service, make it obey).
BDAG.pt: escravizar, subjugar (figurativamente: direcionar o corpo para serviço útil, fazê-lo obedecer).

DEFINITION: slavery, bondage.
ORIGIN: From douleuo; slavery (ceremonially or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 the state or condition of being held as chattel by another, slavery; 2 state or condition of being subservient, servility (figuratively extended)
BDAG.pt: 1 o estado ou condição de ser mantido como propriedade por outro, escravidão; 2 estado ou condição de ser subserviente, servilismo (extensão figurada)

DEFINITION: to be a slave, be subject to, obey, be devoted.
ORIGIN: From doulos; to be a slave to (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary).

BDAG.en: 1 to be owned by another, be a slave, be subjected; 2 to act or conduct oneself as one in total service to another, serve, obey (to personal beings or transcendent beings like God/Christ, or to things like sin/law)
BDAG.pt: 1 ser propriedade de outro, ser escravo, estar sujeito; 2 agir ou conduzir-se como alguém em serviço total a outro, servir, obedecer (a seres pessoais ou transcendentais como Deus/Cristo, ou a coisas como pecado/lei)

DEFINITION: a female slave, bonds-maid.
ORIGIN: Feminine of doulos; a female slave (involuntarily or voluntarily).

BDAG.en: female slave, bondwoman; used as an expression of humility by one of low rank when addressing someone of higher rank or a deity.
BDAG.pt: escrava, serva; usada como expressão de humildade por alguém de baixa posição ao se dirigir a alguém de patente superior ou a uma divindade.

DEFINITION: slavish, servile.
ORIGIN: Neuter of doulos; subservient.

DEFINITION: (a) (as adj.) enslaved, (b) (as noun) a (male) slave.
ORIGIN: From deo; a slave (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary; frequently, therefore in a qualified sense of subjection or subserviency).

BDAG.en: pert. to being under someone’s total control, slavish, servile, subject; male slave as an entity in a socioeconomic context (slave); one solely committed to another, slave, subject (applied to humans in relation to God or Christ, or pejoratively to sin).
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar sob o controle total de alguém, servil, sujeito; escravo masculino como entidade em um contexto socioeconômico (escravo); aquele inteiramente dedicado a outro, escravo, sujeito (aplicado a humanos em relação a Deus ou Cristo, ou pejorativamente ao pecado).

DEFINITION: to enslave, bring under subjection.
ORIGIN: From doulos; to enslave (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant.

BDAG.en: to make someone a slave, enslave a people; Pass: become a slave to someone; to make one subservient to one’s interests, cause to be like a slave, fig. ext. of mng. 1; Pass. to be bound (as a slave)
BDAG.pt: tornar alguém escravo, escravizar um povo; Passivo: tornar-se escravo de alguém; tornar alguém subserviente aos interesses de outrem, fazer com que pareça um escravo, extensão figurada do significado 1; Passivo: estar ligado (como escravo)

DEFINITION: a feast, banquet, reception.
ORIGIN: From dechomai; a reception, i.e. Convivial entertainment.

BDAG.en: reception, banquet.
BDAG.pt: recepção, banquete.

DEFINITION: a dragon or huge serpent; met: Satan.
ORIGIN: Probably from an alternate form of derkomai (to look); a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate).

BDAG.en: dragon, serpent, a sobriquet for the devil.
BDAG.pt: dragão, serpente, um epíteto para o diabo.

DEFINITION: to take hold of, grasp, catch.
ORIGIN: Perhaps akin to the base of drakon (through the idea of capturing); to grasp, i.e. (figuratively) entrap.

BDAG.en: to take by the handful, grasp by the hand, hence catch, seize someone.
BDAG.pt: agarrar com a mão cheia, apertar pela mão, consequentemente pegar, apoderar-se de alguém.

DEFINITION: as much as one can hold in the hand, a drachma (a Greek coin made of silver).
ORIGIN: From drassomai; a drachma or (silver) coin (as handled).

BDAG.en: drachma, a Greek silver coin, combining weight and value.
BDAG.pt: dracma, uma moeda de prata grega, combinando peso e valor.

DEFINITION: a sickle, a pruning hook.
ORIGIN: From drepo (to pluck); a gathering hook (especially for harvesting).

BDAG.en: an agricultural implement consisting of a curved blade and a handle, used for a variety of purposes, sickle
BDAG.pt: um implemento agrícola consistindo em uma lâmina curva e um cabo, usado para uma variedade de propósitos, foice

DEFINITION: a running, course, career, race.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of trecho; a race, i.e. (figuratively) career.

BDAG.en: movement on a path from one point to another, course (of heavenly bodies); carrying out of an obligation or task, course of life, mission.
BDAG.pt: movimento em um caminho de um ponto a outro, curso (de corpos celestes); cumprimento de uma obrigação ou tarefa, curso da vida, missão.

DEFINITION: Drusilla (born A.D. 39), daughter of Herod Agrippa to.
ORIGIN: A feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name); Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family.

BDAG.en: Drusilla (also the name of the Emperor Gaius’s sister), youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I, sister of Agrippa II; betrothed as a child to Antiochus Epiphanes of Commagene, but never married to him; married 53 a.d. to Azizus of Emesa, but left her husband and married Felix the procurator, to whom she bore a son, Agrippa.
BDAG.pt: Drusila (também o nome da irmã do Imperador Caio), filha mais nova de Herodes Agripa I, irmã de Agripa II; prometida em criança a Antíoco Epifânio da Comagena, mas nunca se casou com ele; casou-se em 53 d.C. com Aziz de Emesa, mas deixou o marido e casou-se com Félix, o procurador, a quem deu um filho, Agripa.

DEFINITION: (a) to be powerful, have (the) power, (b) to be able, to can.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; to be able or possible.
USAGE: be able, can (do, + -not), could, may, might, be possible, be of power.

BDAG.en: to possess capability (whether because of personal or external factors) for experiencing or doing someth., can, am able, be capable.
BDAG.pt: Possuir capacidade (seja por fatores pessoais ou externos) para experimentar ou fazer algo; poder, ser capaz.

DEFINITION: (a) physical power, force, might, ability, efficacy, energy, meaning (b) plur: powerful deeds, deeds showing (physical) power, marvelous works.
ORIGIN: From dunamai; force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous power (usually by implication, a miracle itself).
USAGE: ability, abundance, meaning, might(-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle(-s), power, strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work.

BDAG.en: gener. ‘capability’, with emphasis on function. 1 potential for functioning in some way, power, might, strength, force, capability. b specif., the power that works wonders. 3 a deed that exhibits ability to function powerfully, deed of power, miracle, wonder. 4 someth. that serves as an adjunct of power, resource. 5 an entity or being, whether human or transcendent, that functions in a remarkable manner, power as a personal transcendent spirit or heavenly agent/angel. 6 the capacity to convey thought, meaning.
BDAG.pt: Geralmente, 'capacidade', com ênfase na função. 1 Potencial para funcionar de alguma forma, poder, força, capacidade. b Especificamente, o poder que realiza prodígios. 3 Um feito que demonstra a capacidade de funcionar poderosamente, feito de poder, milagre, maravilha. 4 Algo que serve como um adjunto de poder, recurso. 5 Uma entidade ou ser, humano ou transcendente, que funciona de maneira notável, poder como um espírito pessoal transcendente ou agente celestial/anjo. 6 A capacidade de transmitir pensamento, significado.

DEFINITION: to empower, fill with power, strengthen.
ORIGIN: From dunamis; to enable.

BDAG.en: to cause someone to be able to do someth., enable.
BDAG.pt: Fazer com que alguém seja capaz de fazer algo, capacitar.

DEFINITION: (lit: a man who rules by force), a ruler, potentate; also: courtier, member of the court.
ORIGIN: From dunamai; a ruler or officer.

BDAG.en: One who is in a position to command others; ruler, sovereign (of God or humans); court official.
BDAG.pt: Aquele que está em posição de comandar outros; governante, soberano (de Deus ou humanos); funcionário da corte.

DEFINITION: to be powerful, have power, be able, be mighty.
ORIGIN: From dunatos; to be efficient (figuratively).

BDAG.en: To display capability, be effective, be able.
BDAG.pt: Demonstrar capacidade, ser eficaz, ser capaz.

DEFINITION: (a) of persons: powerful, able, (b) of things: possible.
ORIGIN: From dunamai; powerful or capable (literally or figuratively); neuter possible.
USAGE: able, could, (that is) mighty (man), possible, power, strong.

BDAG.en: able, capable, powerful; of transcendent beings (God, angelic beings); of prominent people; empowered; skilled, adept; strong, capable in something, to distinguish oneself in it; of things (weapons, commandments); possible; God's power.
BDAG.pt: capaz, competente, poderoso; de seres transcendentais (Deus, seres angelicais); de pessoas proeminentes; empoderado; habilidoso, adepto; forte, capaz em algo, destacar-se nisso; de coisas (armas, mandamentos); possível; o poder de Deus.

DEFINITION: to sink, set (as the sun).
ORIGIN: Or dumi doo'-mee prolonged forms of an obsolete primary duo doo'-o (to sink) to go "down".

BDAG.en: To go down, set (of the sun); metaphorically, to die.
BDAG.pt: Descer, pôr-se (do sol); metaforicamente, morrer.

DEFINITION: two.
ORIGIN: A primary numeral; "two".

BDAG.en: two (as an adjective or substance, including idiomatic phrases like 'two or three', 'two by two').
BDAG.pt: dois (como adjetivo ou substância, incluindo frases idiomáticas como 'dois ou três', 'dois a dois').

DEFINITION: like un- or mis- (as in unrest, misjudge), nullifies good sense or increases bad sense of a word.
ORIGIN: A primary inseparable particle of uncertain derivation; used only in composition as a prefix; hard, i.e. With difficulty.

BDAG.en: Inseparable prefix meaning un-, mis-, indicating difficulty or badness (opposite of εὖ-).
BDAG.pt: Prefixo inseparável significando não-, mal-, indicando dificuldade ou negatividade (oposto de εὖ-).

DEFINITION: difficult to carry, oppressive.
ORIGIN: From dus- and a derivative of bastazo; oppressive.

BDAG.en: burdensome or difficult to endure, hard to bear (burdens).
BDAG.pt: oneroso ou difícil de suportar, árduo de carregar (fardos).

DEFINITION: dysentery.
ORIGIN: From dus- and a comparative of entos (meaning a bowel); a "dysentery".

DEFINITION: difficult to interpret, hard to be understood.
ORIGIN: From dus- and a presumed derivative of hermeneuo; difficult of explanation.

BDAG.en: difficult to tell the meaning of something, hard to explain.
BDAG.pt: difícil de expressar o significado de algo, difícil de explicar.

DEFINITION: difficult, hard; of persons: hard to please.
ORIGIN: From dus- and kolon (food); properly, fastidious about eating (peevish), i.e. (genitive case) impracticable.

BDAG.en: difficult to fulfill or do, hard, difficult (of commandments); it is hard.
BDAG.pt: difícil de cumprir ou fazer, árduo, difícil (de mandamentos); é difícil.

DEFINITION: with difficulty, hardly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from duskolos; impracticably.

BDAG.en: hardly, with difficulty (entering the kingdom, attaining life, being saved, dying).
BDAG.pt: com dificuldade, arduamente (entrar no reino, alcançar a vida, ser salvo, morrer).

DEFINITION: a setting (as of the sun), by implication (the) western (region).
ORIGIN: From duno; the sun-set, i.e. (by implication) the western region.

BDAG.en: the action of appearing to sink and so disappear from view, going down, setting (of the sun), also as direction of the setting sun, west
BDAG.pt: o ato de parecer afundar e, assim, desaparecer da vista, ocaso, pôr do sol, também como direção do sol poente, oeste

DEFINITION: hard to understand.
ORIGIN: From dus- and a derivative of noieo; difficult of perception.

BDAG.en: hard to understand.
BDAG.pt: difícil de entender.

DEFINITION: evil report, defamation, words of ill omen.
ORIGIN: From a compound of dus- and pheme; defamation.

BDAG.en: defamation, slander, calumny (the act of detracting from or damaging another’s reputation).
BDAG.pt: difamação, calúnia (o ato de depreciar ou danificar a reputação de outrem).

DEFINITION: twelve; the usual way in which the Twelve apostles of Jesus are referred to.
ORIGIN: From duo and deka; two and ten, i.e. A dozen.

BDAG.en: twelve (including 'the twelve' referring to the disciples).
BDAG.pt: doze (incluindo 'os doze' referindo-se aos discípulos).

DEFINITION: twelfth.
ORIGIN: From dodeka; twelfth.

BDAG.en: twelfth in a series, twelfth
BDAG.pt: décimo segundo em uma série, décimo segundo

DEFINITION: the Twelve Tribes (of Israel).
ORIGIN: From dodeka and phule; the commonwealth of Israel.

DEFINITION: the roof (of a house), the top of the house.
ORIGIN: From demo (to build); properly, an edifice, i.e. (specially) a roof.

BDAG.en: the level surface of a flat roof, roof, housetop (proverbially: proclaim quite publicly).
BDAG.pt: a superfície plana de um telhado, telhado, eirado (proverbialmente: proclamar publicamente).

DEFINITION: a (free) gift, a gift (without repayment).
ORIGIN: From doron; a gratuity.

BDAG.en: that which is given or transferred freely by one pers. to another, gift, bounty, of God
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é dado ou transferido livremente de uma pessoa para outra, dom, dádiva, de Deus

DEFINITION: as a free gift, without payment, freely.
ORIGIN: Accusative case of dorea as adverb; gratuitously (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain.

BDAG.en: as a gift, without payment, gratis; undeservedly, without reason/cause; in vain, to no purpose
BDAG.pt: como um dom, sem pagamento, gratuitamente; imerecidamente, sem motivo; em vão, sem propósito

DEFINITION: to give, present, bestow.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from doron; to bestow gratuitously.

BDAG.en: to present someth. as a gift or confer a benefit, present, bestow
BDAG.pt: apresentar algo como um dom ou conferir um benefício, presentear, conceder

DEFINITION: a gift, a bestowment.
ORIGIN: From doreomai; a bestowment.

BDAG.en: gift, present
BDAG.pt: dádiva, presente

DEFINITION: a gift, present, a sacrifice.
ORIGIN: A present; specially, a sacrifice.

BDAG.en: gift, present
BDAG.pt: presente, dádiva

DEFINITION: an interjection, Ho! Ah! Ha! It is supposed to imply surprise, fear and indignation.
ORIGIN: Apparent imperative of eao; properly, let it be, i.e. (as interjection) aha!.

BDAG.en: an exclamatory particle expressing surprise or displeasure, ah!, ha!
BDAG.pt: partícula exclamativa expressando surpresa ou desagrado, ah!, ha!

DEFINITION: if.
ORIGIN: From ei and an; a conditional particle; in case that, provided, etc.; often used in connection with other particles to denote indefiniteness or uncertainty.
USAGE: before, but, except, (and) if, (if) so, (what-, whither-)soever, though, when (-soever), whether (or), to whom, (who-)so(-ever). See me.

BDAG.en: introduces a situation in which given X, Y will follow; as conj., marker of condition, if; used w. subjunctive to denote what is expected to occur; used w. the indicative (exx. in Dssm.); used w. other particles (e.g., ἐὰν καί, ἐὰν μή, ἐάνπερ, ἐάν τε…ἐάν τε); marker of the prospect of an action coordinated with another point of time; marker of the possibility of any number of occurrences of the same event, ever freq. in place of ἄν after relatives
BDAG.pt: introduz uma situação em que dado X, Y se seguirá; como conjunção, marcador de condição, se; usado com o subjuntivo para denotar o que se espera que ocorra; usado com o indicativo; usado com outras partículas (ex: ἐὰν καί, ἐὰν μή, ἐάνπερ, ἐάν τε…ἐάν τε); marcador da perspectiva de uma ação coordenada com outro ponto no tempo; marcador da possibilidade de qualquer número de ocorrências do mesmo evento, frequentemente no lugar de ἄν após pronomes relativos

DEFINITION: of himself, herself, itself.
ORIGIN: From a reflexive pronoun otherwise obsolete and the genitive case (dative case or accusative case) of autos; him- (her-, it-, them-, also (in conjunction with the personal pronoun of the other persons) my-, thy-, our-, your-) self (selves), etc..
USAGE: alone, her (own, -self), (he) himself, his (own), itself, one (to) another, our (thine) own(-selves), + that she had, their (own, own selves), (of) them(-selves), they, thyself, you, your (own, own conceits, own selves, -selves).

BDAG.en: reflexive pronoun: of himself, herself, itself, themselves
BDAG.pt: pronome reflexivo: de si mesmo, de si própria

DEFINITION: to allow, permit, let alone, leave.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; to let be, i.e. Permit or leave alone.
USAGE: commit, leave, let (alone), suffer. See also ea.

BDAG.en: 1 to allow someone to do someth., let, permit; 2 to refrain from bothering, detaining, or using, let go, leave alone
BDAG.pt: 1 permitir que alguém faça algo, deixar, consentir; 2 abster-se de incomodar, deter ou usar, soltar, deixar em paz

DEFINITION: seventy.
ORIGIN: From hebdomos and a modified form of deka; seventy.

BDAG.en: seventy
BDAG.pt: setenta

DEFINITION: seventy times.
ORIGIN: Multiple adverb from hebdomekonta; seventy times.

BDAG.en: seventy times
BDAG.pt: setenta vezes

DEFINITION: seventh.
ORIGIN: Ordinal from hepta; seventh.

BDAG.en: seventh
BDAG.pt: sétimo

DEFINITION: Eber, father of Peleg and son of Shelah.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Eber); Eber, a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Eber, son of Shelah
BDAG.pt: Eber, filho de Salá

DEFINITION: Hebrew, the Jewish language.
ORIGIN: From Eber; Hebraic or the Jewish language.

BDAG.en: pert. to the Hebrew people, Hebrew
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao povo hebreu, hebraico

DEFINITION: a Hebrew, particularly one who speaks Hebrew (Aramaic).
ORIGIN: From Eber; a Hebræan (i.e. Hebrew) or Jew.

BDAG.en: a Hebrew, 1 ethnic name for an Israelite, Hebrew in contrast to other nations; 2 Hebrew-/Aramaic-speaking Israelite in contrast to a Gk.-speaking Israelite, Hebrew-speaking Israelite
BDAG.pt: um hebreu, 1 nome étnico para um israelita, hebreu em contraste com outras nações; 2 israelita falante de hebraico/aramaico em contraste com um israelita falante de grego, israelita falante de hebraico

DEFINITION: the Hebrew language, or rather: Aramaic.
ORIGIN: From Eber; the Hebraistic (Hebrew) or Jewish (Chaldee) language.

BDAG.en: the Hebrew language (referring to Aramaic spoken in Palestine)
BDAG.pt: a língua hebraica (referindo-se ao aramaico falado na Palestina)

DEFINITION: in the Hebrew, or rather, in the Aramaic dialect.
ORIGIN: Adverb from Hebrais; Hebraistically or in the Jewish (Chaldee) language.

BDAG.en: in Hebrew/Aramaic
BDAG.pt: em hebraico/aramaico

DEFINITION: trans: to bring near; intrans: to come near, approach.
ORIGIN: From eggus; to make near, i.e. (reflexively) approach.
USAGE: approach, be at hand, come (draw) near, be (come, draw) nigh.

BDAG.en: approach, come near, draw near (in space); draw near in a temporal sense, come near, approach (in time)
BDAG.pt: aproximar-se, chegar perto (no espaço); aproximar-se no tempo, chegar perto (no tempo)

DEFINITION: to inscribe, to enter in a register.
ORIGIN: From en and grapho; to "engrave", i.e. Inscribe.

BDAG.en: 1 to record information, esp. names in official documents (write in, record); 2 to communicate a message in writing, write down, inscribe.
BDAG.pt: 1 registrar informações, especialmente nomes em documentos oficiais (escrever em, registrar); 2 comunicar uma mensagem por escrito, anotar, inscrever.

DEFINITION: under good security (adjective), guarantee (noun).
ORIGIN: From en and guion (a limb); pledged (as if articulated by a member), i.e. A bondsman.

BDAG.en: pert. to assurance for the fulfillment of something, under good security, as noun guarantee
BDAG.pt: pertencente à garantia para o cumprimento de algo, sob boa segurança, como substantivo garantia

DEFINITION: near (in place or time).
ORIGIN: From a primary verb agcho (to squeeze or throttle; akin to the base of agkale); near (literally or figuratively, of place or time).
USAGE: from, at hand, near, nigh (at hand, unto), ready.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being in close proximity spatially, near, close to; 2 pert. to being close in point of time, near; 3 pert. to being close as experience or event, close.
BDAG.pt: 1 pertencente a estar em proximidade espacial, perto, próximo; 2 pertencente à proximidade temporal, perto; 3 pertencente à proximidade como experiência ou evento, próximo.

DEFINITION: nearer.
ORIGIN: Neuter of the comparative of eggus; nearer.

DEFINITION: (a) to wake, arouse, (b) to raise up.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to the base of agora (through the idea of collecting one's faculties); to waken (transitively or intransitively), i.e. Rouse (literally, from sleep, from sitting or lying, from disease, from death; or figuratively, from obscurity, inactivity, ruins, nonexistence).
USAGE: awake, lift (up), raise (again, up), rear up, (a-)rise (again, up), stand, take up.

BDAG.en: 1 to cause someone to wake from sleep, wake, rouse; 2 to cease sleeping, wake up, awaken from sleep, pass. intr.; 3 to cause to stand up from a position lower than that of the person rendering assistance, raise, help to rise; 4 to move to a standing position, rise, get up, pass. intr.; 5 to cause to come into existence, raise up, bring into being; 6 to cause to return to life, raise up; 7 to enter into or to be in a state of life as a result of being raised, be raised, rise, pass. intr.; 8 to raise up from sickness, raise up=restore to health; 9 to change to a previous good state or condition, restore, erect (of buildings); 10 to move something from its position by exerting effort in overcoming resistance, lift up; 11 to move against in hostility, rise up, pass. intr. (of nations); 12 to make an appearance, appear, pass. intr.; 13 in a command to evoke movement from a fixed position, get up!, come! impv.
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer alguém acordar do sono, despertar, levantar; 2 cessar de dormir, acordar, despertar do sono, intransitivo; 3 fazer levantar-se de uma posição mais baixa, levantar, ajudar a levantar; 4 mover-se para uma posição de pé, levantar-se, erguer-se, intransitivo; 5 fazer vir à existência, levantar, trazer à existência; 6 fazer retornar à vida, ressuscitar; 7 entrar ou estar em um estado de vida como resultado de ter sido levantado, ser levantado, levantar-se, intransitivo; 8 levantar de uma doença, restaurar à saúde; 9 mudar para um estado ou condição anterior boa, restaurar, erguer (de edifícios); 10 mover algo de sua posição exercendo esforço contra resistência, levantar; 11 mover-se contra em hostilidade, levantar-se, intransitivo (de nações); 12 fazer uma aparição, aparecer, intransitivo; 13 em um comando para evocar movimento de uma posição fixa, levante-se!, venha! imperativo.

DEFINITION: a rousing, a rising (from death).
ORIGIN: From egeiro; a resurgence (from death).

BDAG.en: a coming back to life, resurrection, lit. ‘awakening’ of a dead person.
BDAG.pt: Um retorno à vida, ressurreição, literalmente ‘despertar’ de uma pessoa morta.

DEFINITION: hired to lie in wait, lying in wait.
ORIGIN: From en and a derivative of kathiemi; subinduced, i.e. Surreptitiously suborned as a lier-in-wait.

BDAG.en: pert. to having the task of obtaining information secretly, hired to lie in wait, spies.
BDAG.pt: Pertencente à tarefa de obter informações secretamente, contratado para espreitar, espiões.

DEFINITION: a renewal, dedication; the feast of rededication.
ORIGIN: Neuter plural of a presumed compound from en and kainos; innovatives, i.e. (specially) renewal (of religious services after the Antiochian interruption).

BDAG.en: festival of rededication known also as Hanukkah and the Feast of Lights.
BDAG.pt: Festival de reinauguração conhecido também como Chanucá e a Festa das Luzes.

DEFINITION: to consecrate, dedicate, renovate.
ORIGIN: From egkainia; to renew, i.e. Inaugurate.

BDAG.en: 1 to give newness to something, renew; 2 to bring about the beginning of something, ratify, inaugurate, dedicate.
BDAG.pt: 1 dar novidade a algo, renovar; 2 trazer o começo de algo, ratificar, inaugurar, dedicar.

DEFINITION: to call in (as a debt or demand), bring to account.
ORIGIN: From en and kaleo; to call in (as a debt or demand), i.e. Bring to account (charge, criminate, etc.).
USAGE: accuse, call in question, implead, lay to the charge.

BDAG.en: bring charges against, accuse someone
BDAG.pt: apresentar queixas contra, acusar alguém

DEFINITION: to leave behind, (in a good sense) let remain over or (in a bad sense) desert.
ORIGIN: From en and kataleipo; to leave behind in some place, i.e. (in a good sense) let remain over, or (in a bad sense) to desert.

BDAG.en: to cause something to remain or to exist after a point in time, leave of posterity; to separate connection with someone or something, forsake, abandon, desert; cease assembling
BDAG.pt: fazer com que algo permaneça ou exista após um ponto no tempo, deixar posteridade; separar a conexão com alguém ou algo, abandonar, desertar; cessar de se ajuntar

DEFINITION: to settle down in (a place), reside.
ORIGIN: From en and katoikeo; to settle down in a place, i.e. Reside.

BDAG.en: to live as a resident, live, reside
BDAG.pt: viver como residente, morar, residir

DEFINITION: to take pride in, glory in.
ORIGIN: From en and a derivative of kentron; to prick in, i.e. Ingraft.

BDAG.en: to cause (a shoot or bud: scion) to unite with the stock of a growing plant, graft of trees
