BDAG.pt: fazer com que (um broto ou gema: enxerto) se una ao tronco de uma planta em crescimento, enxertar árvores

DEFINITION: an accusation, charge.
ORIGIN: From egkaleo; an accusation, i.e. Offence alleged.
USAGE: crime laid against, laid to charge.

BDAG.en: an indictment or charge brought against someone through judicial proceedings, charge, accusation, legal term; the act or action of expressing disapproval, reproach
BDAG.pt: uma acusação formal ou queixa apresentada contra alguém através de procedimentos judiciais, acusação, imputação, termo legal; o ato ou ação de expressar desaprovação, repreensão

DEFINITION: to clothe myself (originally: to tie round in a knot).
ORIGIN: Middle voice from en and komboo (to gird); to engirdle oneself (for labor), i.e. Figuratively (the apron as being a badge of servitude) to wear (in token of mutual deference).

BDAG.en: to put or tie someth. on oneself, put on; clothe yourselves w. humility
BDAG.pt: Vestir-se ou amarrar algo em si mesmo; revestir-se de humildade.

DEFINITION: an incision, a cutting, break; met: an interruption, a hindrance.
ORIGIN: From egkopto; a hindrance.

BDAG.en: that which holds back the progress of someth., hindrance
BDAG.pt: Aquilo que impede o progresso de algo; impedimento, estorvo.

DEFINITION: to cut into, impede, detain.
ORIGIN: From en and kopto; to cut into, i.e. (figuratively) impede, detain.

BDAG.en: to make progress slow or difficult, hinder, thwart; interrupt
BDAG.pt: Tornar o progresso lento ou difícil, impedir, frustrar; interromper.

DEFINITION: self-mastery, self-restraint, self-control, continence.
ORIGIN: From egkrates; self-control (especially continence).

BDAG.en: restraint of one’s emotions, impulses, or desires, self-control
BDAG.pt: Restrição das emoções, impulsos ou desejos de alguém; autocontrole.

DEFINITION: to exercise self-control, be continent.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from egkrates; to exercise self-restraint (in diet and chastity).

BDAG.en: to keep one’s emotions, impulses, or desires under control, control oneself, abstain
BDAG.pt: Manter as emoções, impulsos ou desejos sob controle, controlar-se, abster-se.

DEFINITION: strong, master of, self-controlled.
ORIGIN: From en and kratos; strong in a thing (masterful), i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) self-controlled (in appetite, etc.).

BDAG.en: pert. to having one’s emotions, impulses, or desires under control, self-controlled, disciplined
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter as emoções, impulsos ou desejos sob controle, autocontrolado, disciplinado

DEFINITION: to judge in, to reckon among.
ORIGIN: From en and krino; to judge in, i.e. Count among.

BDAG.en: to make a judgment about something and classify it in a specific group, to class someone with someone
BDAG.pt: fazer um julgamento sobre algo e classificá-lo em um grupo específico, classificar alguém com alguém

DEFINITION: to hide in, mix with.
ORIGIN: From en and krupto; to conceal in, i.e. Incorporate with.

BDAG.en: to put into, and so out of sight, hide
BDAG.pt: colocar dentro, e assim fora de vista, esconder

DEFINITION: with child, pregnant.
ORIGIN: From en and the base of kuma; swelling inside, i.e. Pregnant.

BDAG.en: pregnant
BDAG.pt: Grávida.

DEFINITION: to rub in, anoint.
ORIGIN: From en and chrio; to rub in (oil), i.e. Besmear.

BDAG.en: to smear/rub on a substance such as salve or oil, smear on, anoint
BDAG.pt: Untar ou esfregar uma substância como bálsamo ou óleo; untar, ungir.

DEFINITION: I (only expressed when emphatic).
ORIGIN: A primary pronoun of the first person I (only expressed when emphatic).
USAGE: I, me. For the other cases and the plural see eme, emoi, emou, hemas, hemeis, hemin, hemon, etc.

BDAG.en: I, used w. a verb to emphasize the pers.; it is I; I am the one
BDAG.pt: Eu, usado com um verbo para enfatizar a pessoa; sou eu; sou aquele.

DEFINITION: to dash to the ground, level with the ground.
ORIGIN: From edaphos; to raze.

BDAG.en: to destroy or tear down by causing something to be brought to ground level, dash to the ground, and of a city raze to the ground
BDAG.pt: destruir ou derrubar, fazendo com que algo seja trazido ao nível do solo, lançar por terra, e no caso de uma cidade, arrasar completamente

DEFINITION: the base, ground, bottom.
ORIGIN: From the base of hedraios; a basis (bottom), i.e. The soil.

BDAG.en: the surface of the earth, ground
BDAG.pt: a superfície da terra, o chão

DEFINITION: sitting, seated; steadfast, firm.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of hezomai (to sit); sedentary, i.e. (by implication) immovable.

BDAG.en: pert. to being firmly or solidly in place, firm, steadfast
BDAG.pt: Relativo a estar firmemente ou solidamente no lugar; firme, estável.

DEFINITION: a foundation, stay, support.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of hedraios; a support, i.e. (figuratively) basis.

BDAG.en: that which provides a firm base for someth., perh. mainstay
BDAG.pt: Aquilo que fornece uma base firme para algo; talvez suporte principal.

DEFINITION: Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, father of Manasseh, and king of Judah (727-686 [?] B.C.).
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Chizqiyah); Ezekias (i.e. Hezekeiah), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Hezekiah
BDAG.pt: Ezequias.

DEFINITION: self-willed (arbitrary and unwarranted) piety.
ORIGIN: From ethelo and threskeia; voluntary (arbitrary and unwarranted) piety, i.e. Sanctimony.

DEFINITION: to accustom, the established custom.
ORIGIN: From ethos; to accustom, i.e. (neuter passive participle) customary.

BDAG.en: to conform to custom or tradition, accustom
BDAG.pt: conformar-se ao costume ou tradição, acostumar

DEFINITION: an ethnarch, a governor (not king) of a province.
ORIGIN: From ethnos and arche; the governor (not king) of a district.

BDAG.en: a title used with various meanings, but in general a person appointed to rule over a particular area or constituency on behalf of a king; head of an ethnic community/minority, ethnic head/leader
BDAG.pt: um título usado com vários significados, mas em geral uma pessoa nomeada para governar sobre uma área ou distrito particular em nome de um rei; chefe de uma comunidade/minoria étnica, líder étnico

DEFINITION: pagan, heathen, gentile; subst: a Gentile, non-Jew.
ORIGIN: From ethnos; national ("ethnic"), i.e. (specially) a Gentile.

BDAG.en: pert. to nationhood foreign to a specific national group, with focus on morality or belief, unbelieving, worldly, polytheistic; (as substantive) the non-Israelite/gentile in contrast to descendants of Abraham
BDAG.pt: pertencente à condição de nação estrangeira a um grupo nacional específico, com foco em moralidade ou crença, descrente, mundano, politeísta; (como substantivo) o não-israelita/gentio em contraste com os descendentes de Abraão

DEFINITION: in the manner of Gentiles, like the rest of the world.
ORIGIN: Adverb from ethnikos; as a Gentile.

BDAG.en: in the manner of the nations
BDAG.pt: à maneira das nações

DEFINITION: a race, people, nation; the nations, heathen world, Gentiles.
ORIGIN: Probably from etho; a race (as of the same habit), i.e. A tribe; specially, a foreign (non-Jewish) one (usually, by implication, pagan).

BDAG.en: 1 a body of persons united by kinship, culture, and common traditions, nation, people; 2 people groups foreign to a specific people group (the nations, gentiles, unbelievers)

ORIGIN: From eis and hodos; an entrance (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 place of entering, entrance; 2 act of arriving at a destination, entrance, access; 3 act of finding acceptance, acceptance.
BDAG.pt: 1 lugar de entrada, entrada; 2 ato de chegar a um destino, entrada, acesso; 3 ato de encontrar aceitação, aceitação.

DEFINITION: to leap into, rush into.
ORIGIN: From eis and pedao (to leap); to rush in.

BDAG.en: a rapid motion forward into, leap in, rush in.
BDAG.pt: Um movimento rápido para dentro, saltar para dentro, precipitar-se para dentro.

DEFINITION: to journey in(to), to go in(to), enter, intervene.
ORIGIN: From eis and poreuomai; to enter (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to enter into an area, go into, enter. Of the devil, who enters a person and takes possession. Of foods go into the mouth; into a person. In imagery come in, enter someone: grief. Abs. of desires.
BDAG.pt: Entrar em uma área, ir para dentro, entrar. Do diabo, que entra numa pessoa e a possui. De alimentos entrar na boca; em uma pessoa. Em sentido figurado, vir para dentro, entrar em alguém: tristeza. Absoluto de desejos.

DEFINITION: to run in, run into.
ORIGIN: From eis and trecho; to hasten inward.

BDAG.en: to make a quick visit in an area, run in.
BDAG.pt: Fazer uma visita rápida em uma área, correr para dentro.

DEFINITION: to lead into, bring in, announce.
ORIGIN: From eis and phero; to carry inward (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: generically ‘bring in, carry in’. 1 to bring into an area, bring in; 2 to cause someone to enter into a certain event or condition, bring in, fig. ext. of 1.
BDAG.pt: Genericamente, ‘trazer para dentro, carregar para dentro’. 1 trazer para uma área, trazer para dentro; 2 causar que alguém entre em um certo evento ou condição, trazer, extensão figurada de 1.

DEFINITION: then, thereafter, next (marking a fresh stage); therefore, then, furthermore.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a particle of succession (in time or logical enumeration), then, moreover.
USAGE: after that(-ward), furthermore, then. See also epeita.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being next in order of time, then, next (placed first); 2 a transition word to mark an addition to someth. just stated, furthermore, then, next.
BDAG.pt: 1 referente a ser o próximo em ordem de tempo, então, em seguida (colocado primeiro); 2 uma palavra de transição para marcar uma adição a algo que acabou de ser dito, além disso, então, em seguida.

DEFINITION: if, whether, or.
ORIGIN: From ei and te; if too.

DEFINITION: he that, if a man, whether any, whosoever.
ORIGIN: From ei and tis; if any.
USAGE: he that, if a(-ny) man('s thing, from any, ought), whether any, whosoever.

BDAG.en: 1. marker of a condition, existing in fact or hypothetical, if. 2. marker of an indirect question as content, that. 3. marker in causal clauses, when an actual case is taken as a supposition, where we also can use if instead of since. 4. marker of strong or solemn assertion, without apodosis (=in aposiopesis). 5. marker of direct and indirect questions (without particle following). 6. Used in combination w. other particles (e.g., εἰἄρα, εἴγε, εἰδὲκαί, εἰδὲμή).
BDAG.pt: 1. marcador de condição, existente de fato ou hipotética, se. 2. Marcador de pergunta indireta como conteúdo, que. 3. Marcador em cláusulas causais, quando um caso real é tomado como suposição, onde também podemos usar 'se' em vez de 'pois/já que'. 4. Marcador de afirmação forte ou solene, sem apodosia (=em aposiopese). 5. Marcador de perguntas diretas e indiretas (sem partícula seguinte). 6. Usado em combinação com outras partículas (ex: εἰἄρα, εἴγε, εἰδὲκαί, εἰδὲμή).

DEFINITION: from out, out from among, from, suggesting from the interior outwards.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition denoting origin (the point whence action or motion proceeds), from, out (of place, time, or cause; literal or figurative; direct or remote).
USAGE: after, among, X are, at, betwixt(-yond), by (the means of), exceedingly, (+ abundantly above), for(- th), from (among, forth, up), + grudgingly, + heartily, X heavenly, X hereby, + very highly, in,...ly, (because, by reason) of, off (from), on, out among (from, of), over, since, X thenceforth, through, X unto, X vehemently, with(-out). Often used in composition, with the same general import; often of completion.

BDAG.en: preposition meaning separation, from, out of, away from the place or thing from which separation takes place; denoting the direction from which something comes; denoting origin, cause, motive, reason; denoting severance of connection; denoting derivation; denoting effective cause; denoting a presupposition (reason/result); denoting means; denoting source from which something flows or comes; denoting material out of which something is made; denoting underlying rule or principle; marker for partitive genitive (part of a whole); used with verbs of supplying, receiving, consuming, or filling; denoting temporal sequence (from a starting time).
BDAG.pt: Preposição que significa separação, de, fora de, longe do lugar ou coisa da qual a separação ocorre; denotando a direção de onde algo vem; denotando origem, causa, motivo, razão; denotando corte de conexão; denotando derivação; denotando causa efetiva; denotando uma pressuposição (razão/resultado); denotando meio; denotando fonte de onde algo flui ou vem; denotando material de que algo é feito; denotando regra ou princípio subjacente; marcador para genitivo partitivo (parte de um todo); usada com verbos de suprir, receber, consumir ou encher; denotando sequência temporal (a partir de um tempo inicial).

DEFINITION: each (of more than two), every one.
ORIGIN: As if a superlative of hekas (afar); each or every.
USAGE: any, both, each (one), every (man, one, woman), particularly.

BDAG.en: one of an aggregate in a distributive sense, each, every, distributive pronoun
BDAG.pt: um de um agregado em sentido distributivo, cada um, todo, pronome distributivo

DEFINITION: at every time, always.
ORIGIN: As if from hekastos and tote; at every time.

BDAG.en: at any time, always
BDAG.pt: a qualquer tempo, sempre

DEFINITION: one hundred.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a hundred.

BDAG.en: one hundred
BDAG.pt: cem

DEFINITION: a hundred years old.
ORIGIN: From hekaton and etos; centenarian.

BDAG.en: a hundred years old
BDAG.pt: de cem anos de idade

DEFINITION: a hundred times.
ORIGIN: From hekaton and a presumed derivative of plasso; a hundred times.

BDAG.en: a hundred times as much, a hundredfold
BDAG.pt: cem vezes mais, cem vezes

DEFINITION: a centurion, a captain of one hundred men.
ORIGIN: Or hekatontarchos hek-at-on'-tar-khos; from hekaton and archo; the captain of one hundred men.

BDAG.en: a Roman officer commanding about a hundred men, centurion, captain
BDAG.pt: um oficial romano que comanda cerca de cem homens, centurião, capitão

DEFINITION: to throw (cast, put) out; to banish; to bring forth, produce.
ORIGIN: From ek and ballo; to eject (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: bring forth, cast (forth, out), drive (out), expel, leave, pluck (pull, take, thrust) out, put forth (out), send away (forth, out).

BDAG.en: force to leave, drive out, expel; cause to go or remove from a position, send out/away, release, bring out; cause someth. to be removed from someth., take out, remove; to pay no attention to, disregard; bring someth. about, cause to happen, bring
BDAG.pt: forçar a sair, expulsar, expelir; fazer sair ou remover de uma posição, enviar para fora/embora, libertar, trazer para fora; fazer com que algo seja removido de algo, tirar, remover; não prestar atenção, desconsiderar; trazer algo à tona, fazer acontecer, trazer

DEFINITION: (a) a way out, escape, (b) result, issue.
ORIGIN: From a compound of ek and the base of basis (meaning to go out); an exit (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: end point of a duration, end; outcome of an event or state, outcome; way out of some difficulty, a way out, end.
BDAG.pt: ponto final de uma duração, fim; resultado de um evento ou estado, desfecho; saída de alguma dificuldade, uma saída, fim.

DEFINITION: a throwing out, a jettisoning of cargo to lighten a ship.
ORIGIN: From ekballo; ejection, i.e. (specially) a throwing overboard of the cargo.

BDAG.en: generically 'to throw out of an area or object'; in our lit., as a nautical technical term: jettisoning, of a ship’s cargo to save the vessel in a storm.
BDAG.pt: geralmente 'lançar para fora de uma área ou objeto'; na nossa literatura, como termo técnico náutico: o ato de jogar fora (carga) de um navio para salvar a embarcação em uma tempestade.

DEFINITION: to give in marriage, marry.
ORIGIN: From ek and a form of gamisko (compare ekgamisko); to marry off a daughter.

BDAG.en: to arrange marriage for someone, give in marriage.
BDAG.pt: arrumar um casamento para alguém, dar em casamento.

DEFINITION: to give in marriage.
ORIGIN: From ek and gamisko; the same as ekgamizo.

DEFINITION: born of, a descendant, a grandchild.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of a compound of ek and ginomai; a descendant, i.e. (specially) grandchild.

BDAG.en: prim. sense ‘born of, sprung from’; usu. subst.: descendants, specifically grandchildren.
BDAG.pt: sentido primário 'nascido de, descendente de'; usualmente substantivado: descendentes, especificamente netos.

DEFINITION: to spend (give out) completely, exhaust.
ORIGIN: From ek and dapanao; to expend (wholly), i.e. (figuratively) exhaust.

BDAG.en: spend, exhaust (only fig. in pass. be spent of the sacrifice of one’s own life for someone).
BDAG.pt: gastar, exaurir (somente em sentido figurado na voz passiva: ser gasto, referindo-se ao sacrifício da própria vida por alguém).

DEFINITION: to take or receive, by implication to await, expect.
ORIGIN: From ek and dechomai; to accept from some source, i.e. (by implication) to await.

BDAG.en: to remain in a place or state and await an event or the arrival of someone, expect, wait.
BDAG.pt: permanecer em um lugar ou estado e aguardar um evento ou a chegada de alguém, esperar, estar à espera.

DEFINITION: perfectly evident, manifest.
ORIGIN: From ek and delos; wholly evident.

BDAG.en: quite evident, plain.
BDAG.pt: bastante evidente, claro.

DEFINITION: to be away from home, absent.
ORIGIN: From a compound of ek and demos; to emigrate, i.e. (figuratively) vacate or quit.

BDAG.en: 1 orig. of movement from a geographical area, ‘leave one’s country, take a long journey’; then fig. leave, get away from, the body. 2 ‘be in a strange land’, fig. be away abs.
BDAG.pt: 1 originalmente relativo ao movimento de uma área geográfica, 'deixar seu país, fazer uma longa viagem'; depois, figurativamente, deixar, afastar-se do corpo. 2 'estar em terra estranha', figurativamente estar ausente absolutamente.

DEFINITION: to give out, let; middle: to let out for own advantage.
ORIGIN: From ek and didomi; to give forth, i.e. (specially) to lease.

BDAG.en: let out for hire, lease.
BDAG.pt: alugar, arrendar.

DEFINITION: to narrate at length, declare.
ORIGIN: From ek and a compound of dia and hegeomai; to narrate through wholly.

BDAG.en: to provide detailed information when telling someth., tell (in detail).
BDAG.pt: fornecer informação detalhada ao contar algo, contar (em detalhes).

DEFINITION: to give justice over, defend, avenge, vindicate.
ORIGIN: From ekdikos; to vindicate, retaliate, punish.

BDAG.en: 1 to procure justice for someone, grant justice; 2 to inflict appropriate penalty for wrong done, punish, take vengeance for; 3 to carry out one’s obligations in a worthy manner, do justice to.
BDAG.pt: 1 procurar justiça para alguém, conceder justiça; 2 infligir penalidade apropriada por um erro cometido, punir, vingar; 3 cumprir as obrigações de maneira digna, fazer justiça a.

DEFINITION: (a) a defense, avenging, vindication, vengeance, (b) full (complete) punishment.
ORIGIN: From ekdikeo; vindication, retribution.

BDAG.en: meting out of justice, giving of justice; retaliation for harm done, vengeance; penalty inflicted on wrongdoers, abs. punishment.
BDAG.pt: aplicação da justiça, concessão de justiça; retaliação por dano causado, vingança; penalidade infligida aos malfeitores, punição absoluta.

DEFINITION: avenging, subst: an avenger (the word occurs frequently in the sense of a special advocate [champion] of a city).
ORIGIN: From ek and dike; carrying justice out, i.e. A punisher.

BDAG.en: pert. to justice being done so as to rectify wrong done to another, punishing, subst. one who punishes.
BDAG.pt: relativo à justiça sendo feita para retificar um erro cometido contra outro, punindo; substantivado, aquele que pune.

DEFINITION: to persecute, expel by persecuting, drive out, vex, harass.
ORIGIN: From ek and dioko; to pursue out, i.e. Expel or persecute implacably.

BDAG.en: 1 to use tactics that cause the departure of someone from a place, drive out; 2 to annoy persistently, persecute severely.
BDAG.pt: 1 usar táticas que causam a partida de alguém de um lugar, expulsar; 2 incomodar persistentemente, perseguir severamente.

DEFINITION: given out or over, surrendered.
ORIGIN: From ek and a derivative of didomi; given out or over, i.e. Surrendered.

BDAG.en: pert. to being handed over, given up, delivered up
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser entregue, cedido, remetido

DEFINITION: a receiving from, expectation.
ORIGIN: From ekdechomai; expectation.

BDAG.en: found nowhere else.
BDAG.pt: não encontrado em outro lugar.

DEFINITION: to put off, take off, strip off, with acc. of person or garment or both.
ORIGIN: From ek and the base of duno; to cause to sink out of, i.e. (specially as of clothing) to divest.

BDAG.en: 1 to remove clothing from the body, strip, take off 2 to remove by force, plunder
BDAG.pt: 1 remover a roupa do corpo, despir, tirar 2 remover à força, saquear

DEFINITION: (a) there, yonder, in that place, (b) thither, there.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; there; by extension, thither.

BDAG.en: 1 in ref. to a position in the immediate vicinity, there, in that place (the static aspect) 2 in ref. to a position relatively distant, there, to that place (the directional aspect)=ἐκεῖσε 1
BDAG.pt: 1 em referência a uma posição na proximidade imediata, ali, naquele lugar (o aspeto estático) 2 em referência a uma posição relativamente distante, ali, para aquele lugar (o aspeto direcional)=ἐκεῖσε 1

DEFINITION: thence, from that place.
ORIGIN: From ekei; thence.

BDAG.en: from there
BDAG.pt: de lá

DEFINITION: that one (or neut. that thing), often intensified by the article preceding.
ORIGIN: From ekei; that one (or (neuter) thing); often intensified by the article prefixed.
USAGE: he, it, the other (same), selfsame, that (same, very), X their, X them, they, this, those. See also houtos.

BDAG.en: pert. to an entity mentioned or understood and viewed as relatively remote in the discourse setting, that person, that thing, that (‘that over there’; opp. οὗτος ‘this’)
BDAG.pt: pertencente a uma entidade mencionada ou entendida e vista como relativamente remota no cenário do discurso, aquela pessoa, aquela coisa, aquele (‘aquele ali’; oposto a οὗτος ‘este’)

DEFINITION: thither, there, at that place.
ORIGIN: From ekei; thither.

BDAG.en: in ref. to attention directed toward a remote place or other side, there, to that place, thither
BDAG.pt: em referência à atenção dirigida a um lugar remoto ou outro lado, ali, para aquele lugar, para lá

DEFINITION: to seek out, seek out after, require.
ORIGIN: From ek and zeteo; to search out, i.e. (figuratively)investigate, crave, demand, (by Hebraism) worship.

BDAG.en: to exert effort to find out or learn someth., seek out, search for; to look for someth. with a view to securing it, desire, seek to get; to look for someone with a view to some kind of association, seek out, visit; to look for in expectation of fixing blame, look for, seek, in the judicial sense charge (to, with)
BDAG.pt: exercer esforço para descobrir ou aprender algo, procurar, buscar; procurar algo com o intuito de obtê-lo, desejar, buscar obter; procurar alguém com vista a algum tipo de associação, procurar, visitar; procurar na expectativa de atribuir culpa, procurar, buscar, no sentido judicial de acusar (alguém por algo)

DEFINITION: to be greatly astonished, be awe-struck.
ORIGIN: From ekthambos; to astonish utterly.

DEFINITION: full of astonishment, amazed.
ORIGIN: From ek and thambos; utterly astounded.

BDAG.en: utterly astonished
BDAG.pt: completamente espantado/assombrado

DEFINITION: cast out, exposed (to the elements), abandoned.
ORIGIN: From ek and a derivative of tithemi; put out, i.e. Exposed to perish.

BDAG.en: exposed, abandoned of infants
BDAG.pt: exposto, abandonado (referente a infantes)

DEFINITION: to clean (cleanse) out, clean thoroughly.
ORIGIN: From ek and kathairo; to cleanse thoroughly.

BDAG.en: 1 to remove as unclean, clean out. 2 to rid of someth. unclean, cleanse
BDAG.pt: 1 remover como impuro, limpar. 2 livrar de algo impuro, purificar

DEFINITION: to kindle, to be inflamed.
ORIGIN: From ek and kaio; to inflame deeply.

DEFINITION: to be faint, be weary.
ORIGIN: From ek and kakos; to be (bad or) weak, i.e. (by implication) to fail (in heart).

BDAG.en: lose heart
BDAG.pt: desanimar

DEFINITION: to pierce through (or deeply), transfix.
ORIGIN: From ek and the base of kentron; to transfix.

BDAG.en: pierce (someone, i.e., kill him)
BDAG.pt: perfurar (alguém, ou seja, matá-lo)

DEFINITION: to break off.
ORIGIN: From ek and klao; to exscind.

BDAG.en: to separate someth. from someth. with force, break off (of branches)
BDAG.pt: separar algo de algo com força, arrancar (de galhos)

DEFINITION: to shut out, exclude, separate.
ORIGIN: From ek and kleio; to shut out (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to exclude or withdraw from fellowship, shut out, exclude someone; to make no room for, exclude, shut out someth. = make it impossible
BDAG.pt: excluir ou retirar-se da comunhão, fechar a porta, excluir alguém; não dar espaço para, excluir, fechar algo = tornar impossível

DEFINITION: an assembly, congregation, church; the Church, the whole body of Christian believers.
ORIGIN: From a compound of ek and a derivative of kaleo; a calling out, i.e. (concretely) a popular meeting, especially a religious congregation (Jewish synagogue, or Christian community of members on earth or saints in heaven or both).

BDAG.en: a regularly summoned legislative body, assembly; a casual gathering of people, an assemblage, gathering; people with shared belief, community, congregation (of OT Israelites or Christians); the global community of Christians, (universal) church
BDAG.pt: um corpo legislativo regularmente convocado, assembleia; uma reunião casual de pessoas, ajuntamento, reunião; pessoas com crença em comum, comunidade, congregação (de Israelitas do AT ou cristãos); a comunidade global de cristãos, igreja (universal)

DEFINITION: (lit: to bend away from), to fall away from, turn away (from), deviate.
ORIGIN: From ek and klino; to deviate, i.e. (absolutely) to shun (literally or figuratively), or (relatively) to decline (from piety).
USAGE: avoid, eschew, go out of the way.

BDAG.en: to keep away from, steer clear of a pers., stay away from, avoid; turn aside (from) of those who turn away from seeking God’s interests
BDAG.pt: manter-se afastado de, evitar uma pessoa, afastar-se, evitar; desviar-se (de) daqueles que se afastam da busca pelos interesses de Deus

DEFINITION: to swim out (of the water).
ORIGIN: From ek and kolumbao; to escape by swimming.

BDAG.en: (dive overboard and) swim away
BDAG.pt: (saltar do navio e) nadar para longe

DEFINITION: to carry out (of the city gate for burial).
ORIGIN: From ek and komizo; to bear forth (to burial).

BDAG.en: carry out of a corpse being taken to a burial place outside a town.
BDAG.pt: conduzir para fora um cadáver que está sendo levado para um local de sepultamento fora da cidade.

DEFINITION: to cut off, cut down, cut out, to frustrate.
ORIGIN: From ek and kopto; to exscind; figuratively, to frustrate.
USAGE: cut down (off, out), hew down, hinder.

BDAG.en: to cut so as to sever, cut off/down (of a tree, branch, hand); to do away with, exterminate (figuratively of persons or things, root and branch).
BDAG.pt: cortar de modo a separar, cortar fora/abaixo (de uma árvore, galho, mão); abolir, exterminar (figurativamente de pessoas ou coisas, pela raiz).

DEFINITION: to hang from, hang upon (the lips of a speaker), to listen closely.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ek and kremannumi; to hang upon the lips of a speaker, i.e. Listen closely.

BDAG.en: to suspend something out from an area, hang out (active); to pay close attention to someone or something, hang on (middle voice, figurative).
BDAG.pt: suspender algo para fora de uma área, pendurar para fora (ativo); prestar muita atenção a alguém ou algo, ficar atento (voz média, figurado).

DEFINITION: to speak out, disclose, divulge.
ORIGIN: From ek and laleo; to divulge.

BDAG.en: to speak out about or publicize something, tell.
BDAG.pt: falar abertamente ou publicizar algo, contar.

DEFINITION: to shine forth (out).
ORIGIN: From ek and lampo; to be resplendent.

BDAG.en: to emit rays of light, shine (out); of a flame, blaze up.
BDAG.pt: emitir raios de luz, brilhar (para fora); de uma chama, inflamar-se.

DEFINITION: to forget entirely, make to forget.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ek and lanthano; to be utterly oblivious of.

BDAG.en: forget (altogether).
BDAG.pt: esquecer (completamente).

DEFINITION: to pick out for myself, choose, elect, select.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ek and lego (in its primary sense); to select.

BDAG.en: to pick out someone or something, choose (for oneself); to make a choice in accordance with significant preference, select someone/something for oneself; to gather in a crop.
BDAG.pt: escolher alguém ou algo, selecionar (para si mesmo); fazer uma escolha de acordo com uma preferência significativa, selecionar alguém/algo para si mesmo; colher uma safra.

DEFINITION: to leave out, leave off, by implication to cease.
ORIGIN: From ek and leipo; to omit, i.e. (by implication) cease (die).

BDAG.en: to be no longer in existence, fail, give out, be gone; to go away from a place, depart; to cease as state or event, fail, die out; to be deficient in one’s appearance, be inferior.
BDAG.pt: deixar de existir, falhar, esgotar-se, sumir; partir de um lugar, retirar-se; cessar como estado ou evento, falhar, extinguir-se; ser deficiente na aparência, ser inferior.

DEFINITION: chosen out, elect, choice, select, sometimes as subst: of those chosen out by God for the rendering of special service to Him (of the Hebrew race, particular Hebrews, the Messiah, and the Christians).
ORIGIN: From eklegomai; select; by implication, favorite.

BDAG.en: pert. to being selected, chosen; of Christians in particular, chosen; pert. to being esp. distinguished, elect; pert. to being considered best in the course of a selection, choice, excellent
BDAG.pt: Pertencente ao ser selecionado, escolhido; particularmente dos cristãos, escolhidos; pertinente a ser especialmente distinguido, eleito; pertinente a ser considerado o melhor no curso de uma seleção, escolha, excelente

DEFINITION: a choosing out, selecting, choice (by God).
ORIGIN: From eklegomai; (divine) selection (abstractly or concretely).

BDAG.en: a special choice, selection, choice, election (active sense); that which is chosen/selected (passive sense)
BDAG.pt: uma escolha especial, seleção, opção, eleição (sentido ativo); aquilo que é escolhido/selecionado (sentido passivo)

DEFINITION: to loose, release, unloose (as a bow-string), relax, enfeeble; pass: to be faint, grow weary.
ORIGIN: From ek and luo; to relax (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: be exhausted in strength, become weary, give out (especially from hunger); to lose courage.
BDAG.pt: esgotar as forças, ficar cansado, desfalecer (especialmente de fome); perder a coragem.

DEFINITION: to knead out, by anal. to wipe dry.
ORIGIN: From ek and the base of massaomai; to knead out, i.e. (by analogy) to wipe dry.

BDAG.en: to cause to become dry by wiping with a substance, wipe (feet with one’s hair or with a towel).
BDAG.pt: fazer secar limpando com uma substância, enxugar (pés com o cabelo ou com uma toalha).

DEFINITION: to hold up the nose in derision of.
ORIGIN: From ek and mukterizo; to sneer outright at.

BDAG.en: ridicule, sneer, (at) someone.
BDAG.pt: ridicularizar, zombar de alguém.

DEFINITION: to escape, get clear of, deviate, withdraw.
ORIGIN: From ek and neuo; (by analogy) to slip off, i.e. Quietly withdraw.

BDAG.en: to draw away from, turn aside, withdraw.
BDAG.pt: afastar-se de, desviar-se, retirar-se.

DEFINITION: to become sober (after drunkenness).
ORIGIN: From ek and nepho; (figuratively) to rouse (oneself) out of stupor.

BDAG.en: to become sober (literally); figuratively: come to one’s senses.
BDAG.pt: ficar sóbrio (literalmente); figurativamente: cair em si.

DEFINITION: willing, with right good will, voluntary, spontaneous.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative from hekon; voluntariness.

BDAG.en: pert. to doing something of one’s own volition, voluntary, as a volunteer
BDAG.pt: pertinente a fazer algo por própria vontade, voluntário, como um voluntário

DEFINITION: willingly, of one's own accord, spontaneously.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the same as hekousion; voluntarily.

BDAG.en: willingly; without compulsion, i.e. deliberately, intentionally

USAGE: about, after, against, + almost, X altogether, among, X as, at, before, between, (here-)by (+ all means), for (... Sake of), + give self wholly to, (here-)in(-to, -wardly), X mightily, (because) of, (up-)on, (open-)ly, X outwardly, one, X quickly, X shortly, (speedi-)ly, X that, X there(-in, -on), through(-out), (un-)to(-ward), under, when, where(-with), while, with(-in). Often used in compounds, with substantially the same import; rarely with verbs of motion, and then not to indicate direction, except (elliptically) by a separate (and different) preposition.

DEFINITION: to admit, approve, to be possible.
ORIGIN: Third person singular present of a compound of en and dechomai; (impersonally) it is accepted in, i.e. Admitted (possible).

BDAG.en: to be acceptable to one’s way of thinking, it is possible
BDAG.pt: ser aceitável à maneira de pensar, ser possível

DEFINITION: to be in one's own country, to be at home.
ORIGIN: From a compound of en and demos; to be in one's own country, i.e. Home (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to be in a familiar place, to be at home; (fig.) be at home in the body (i.e., physical life); be at home with the Lord (of the afterlife in heaven)
BDAG.pt: estar em um lugar familiar, estar em casa; (fig.) estar em casa no corpo (i.e., vida física); estar com o Senhor (na vida após a morte no céu)

DEFINITION: (somewhat rare) (of clothing: to put on another); mid: to put on (myself).
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of enduo; to invest (with a garment).

BDAG.en: to put on clothing, dress, put on someone with something; (mid.) dress oneself in something
BDAG.pt: vestir roupa, vestir, pôr algo em alguém; (médio) vestir-se com algo

DEFINITION: righteous, just.
ORIGIN: From en and dike; in the right, i.e. Equitable.

BDAG.en: 'based on what is right', hence just, deserved
BDAG.pt: 'baseado no que é justo', portanto justo, merecido

DEFINITION: the material of a building, a structure.
ORIGIN: From a compound of en and a derivative of the base of demos; a housing in (residence), i.e. Structure.

BDAG.en: primary meaning ‘interior structure’; in our literature probably = construction hence material
BDAG.pt: significado primário 'estrutura interior'; em nossa literatura, provavelmente = construção, portanto material

DEFINITION: to glorify, acknowledge the glory belonging to, recognize as glorious; pass: to be glorified in.
ORIGIN: From endoxos; to glorify.

DEFINITION: highly esteemed, splendid, glorious.
ORIGIN: From en and doxa; in glory, i.e. Splendid, (figuratively) noble.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being held in high esteem, honored, distinguished, eminent; 2 pert. to possessing an inherent quality that is not ordinary, glorious, splendid
BDAG.pt: 1 pertencente ao ser tido em alta estima, honrado, distinto, eminente; 2 pertencente ao possuir uma qualidade inerente que não é comum, glorioso, esplêndido

DEFINITION: apparel (esp. the outer robe).
ORIGIN: From enduo; apparel (especially the outer robe).

BDAG.en: 1 material of any kind manufactured to cover the body, garment, clothing; 2 covering in ref. to one’s inner life, covering
BDAG.pt: 1 material de qualquer tipo fabricado para cobrir o corpo, vestimenta, roupa; 2 cobertura em referência à vida interior, invólucro

DEFINITION: to fill with power, strengthen, make strong.
ORIGIN: From en and dunamoo; to empower.

BDAG.en: 1 to cause one to be able to function or do something, strengthen someone or something; 2 to become able to function or do something, become strong (pass. w. act. sense)
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer alguém capaz de funcionar ou fazer algo, fortalecer alguém ou algo; 2 tornar-se capaz de funcionar ou fazer algo, tornar-se forte (passivo com sentido ativo)

DEFINITION: to clothe; mid: to enter, creep into.
ORIGIN: From ennomos and duno; to sink (by implication, wrap (compare enduo) on, i.e. (figuratively) sneak.

BDAG.en: 1 to enter into an area through devious means or pretense, slip in; 2 to become introspective, retire within (fig. ext. of 1)
BDAG.pt: 1 entrar em uma área por meios desonestos ou pretexto, esgueirar-se; 2 tornar-se introspectivo, recolher-se para dentro (extensão figurada de 1)

DEFINITION: a putting on, investment (with clothing).
ORIGIN: From enduo; investment with clothing.

BDAG.en: 1 the act of putting on, putting on; 2 that which is put on, clothing
BDAG.pt: 1 o ato de vestir, vestir; 2 aquilo que é vestido, vestimenta

DEFINITION: to clothe or be clothed with (in the sense of sinking into a garment).
ORIGIN: From en and duno (in the sense of sinking into a garment); to invest with clothing (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 (act.) to put clothing or apparel on someone, dress, clothe someone; 2 (mid.) to put any kind of thing on oneself, clothe oneself in, put on, wear something; (metaph.) of the taking on of characteristics, virtues, intentions, etc.
BDAG.pt: 1 (ativo) vestir ou pôr vestuário em alguém, vestir alguém; 2 (médio) pôr qualquer tipo de coisa em si mesmo, vestir-se com, pôr, usar algo; (metafórico) de assumir características, virtudes, intenções, etc.

DEFINITION: an ambush, plot, treachery, fraud.
ORIGIN: Feminine from en and the base of hedraios; an ambuscade, i.e. (figuratively) murderous purpose.

BDAG.en: primary meaning ‘sitting in’, hence as act of concealment for surprise attack, ambush
BDAG.pt: significado primário 'sentar-se dentro', daí como ato de ocultação para ataque surpresa, emboscada

DEFINITION: to lie in wait (ambush) for, seek to entrap (hence: to defraud, deceive).
ORIGIN: From enedra; to lurk, i.e. (figuratively) plot assassination.

BDAG.en: 1 to conceal oneself in a suitable position for surprise attack, lie in wait for someone; 2 to use intrigue, plot
BDAG.pt: 1 ocultar-se em posição adequada para ataque surpresa, espreitar alguém; 2 usar intriga, conspirar

DEFINITION: lying in wait.
ORIGIN: Neuter of the same as enedra; an ambush, i.e. (figuratively) murderous design.

BDAG.en: deceit, = ἐνέδρα
BDAG.pt: engano, = ἐνέδρα

DEFINITION: to wrap up, roll up in (something), wind in.
ORIGIN: From ennomos and the base of heilisso; to enwrap.

BDAG.en: 1 to envelop an object by wrapping it in something, wrap (up) in something; 2 to encircle an object with confining material, confine in
BDAG.pt: 1 envolver um objeto enrolando-o em algo, embrulhar em algo; 2 cercar um objeto com material de confinamento, confinar em

DEFINITION: to be in, within.
ORIGIN: From ennomos and eimi; to be within (neuter participle plural).
USAGE: such things as... Have. See also eni.

BDAG.en: 1 to be inside an area or object, be in; 2 to be within the limits of realization, it is possible
BDAG.pt: 1 estar dentro de uma área ou objeto, estar em; 2 estar dentro dos limites da realização, é possível

DEFINITION: for the sake of, on account of, on account of which, wherefore, on account of what, why.
ORIGIN: Or heneken hen'-ek-en or heineken hi'-nek-en; of uncertain affinity; on account of.
USAGE: because, for (cause, sake), (where-)fore, by reason of, that.

DEFINITION: working, action, productive work, activity; in the NT, confined to superhuman activity.
ORIGIN: From energes; efficiency ("energy").

BDAG.en: the state or quality of being active, working, operation, action; deluding influence; productive power
BDAG.pt: o estado ou qualidade de estar ativo, funcionando, operação, ação; influência enganadora; poder produtivo

DEFINITION: to work, be operative, be at work, be made to work, accomplish; mid: to work, display activity.
ORIGIN: From energes; to be active, efficient.
USAGE: do, (be) effectual (fervent), be mighty in, shew forth self, work (effectually in).

BDAG.en: to put one’s capabilities into operation, work, be at work, be active, operate, be effective; to bring something about through use of capability, work, produce, effect
BDAG.pt: colocar as capacidades em operação, trabalhar, estar em operação, ser ativo, operar, ser eficaz; realizar algo através do uso de capacidade, trabalhar, produzir, efetuar

DEFINITION: a working, an effect, operation.
ORIGIN: From energeo; an effect.

BDAG.en: activity as expression of capability, activity (miraculous powers); activity as something that impacts on another, experience
BDAG.pt: atividade como expressão de capacidade, atividade (poderes miraculosos); atividade como algo que impacta em outro, experiência

DEFINITION: effective, productive of due result, at work.
ORIGIN: From en and ergon; active, operative.

BDAG.en: pert. to practical expression of capability, effective, active, powerful
BDAG.pt: pertencente à expressão prática de capacidade, eficaz, ativo, poderoso

DEFINITION: to confer a benefit on, to bless.
ORIGIN: From en and eulogeo; to confer a benefit on.

BDAG.en: to confer special benefits, act kindly, bless
BDAG.pt: conferir benefícios especiais, agir com bondade, abençoar

DEFINITION: (a) to have a grudge against, be angry (with), (b) pass. or mid: to be entangled, entangle myself.
ORIGIN: From en and echo; to hold in or upon, i.e. Ensnare; by implication, to keep a grudge.
USAGE: entangle with, have a quarrel against, urge.

BDAG.en: have a grudge against someone, bear ill-will; experience constraint, be subject to, be loaded down with
BDAG.pt: guardar rancor contra alguém, nutrir má vontade; experimentar constrangimento, estar sujeito a, ser sobrecarregado com

DEFINITION: prop. within, (of place) here, to here.
ORIGIN: From a prolonged form of en; properly, within, i.e. (of place) here, hither.

BDAG.en: pert. to a position relatively near the speaker, here; in this place
BDAG.pt: pertinente a uma posição relativamente próxima do falante, aqui; neste lugar

DEFINITION: to meditate upon, reflect upon, ponder.
ORIGIN: From a compound of en and thumos; to be inspirited, i.e. Ponder.

BDAG.en: to process information by thinking about it carefully, reflect (on), consider, think
BDAG.pt: processar informações pensando cuidadosamente sobre elas, refletir (sobre), considerar, pensar

DEFINITION: inward thought, reflection, plur: thoughts.
ORIGIN: From enthumeomai; deliberation.

BDAG.en: the process of considering someth., thought, reflection, idea
BDAG.pt: o processo de considerar algo, pensamento, reflexão, ideia

DEFINITION: is in, has place, can be.
ORIGIN: Contraction for the third person singular present indicative of eneimi; impersonally, there is in or among.

BDAG.en: to be or exist in a certain context, there is, in our lit. only w. a negative: there is not or no
BDAG.pt: ser ou existir em um certo contexto, há, em nossa literatura apenas com um negativo: não há ou ninguém

DEFINITION: a cycle of time, a year.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from a primary enos (a year); a year.

BDAG.en: a period of one year, year; more gener. a period of time other than a calendar year, year
BDAG.pt: um período de um ano, ano; mais geralmente um período de tempo diferente de um ano civil, ano

DEFINITION: to place in or upon; only in the intrans. tenses: to impend, be at hand, be present, threaten; as adj: present.
ORIGIN: From en and histemi; to place on hand, i.e. (reflexively) impend, (participle) be instant.

BDAG.en: to take place as an event, be here, be at hand, arrive, come; to be present as condition or thing at the time of speaking, be now, happen now; to be about to occur, be imminent, be impending
BDAG.pt: ocorrer como um evento, estar aqui, estar presente, chegar, vir; estar presente como condição ou coisa no momento da fala, ser agora, acontecer agora; estar prestes a ocorrer, ser iminente, estar pendente

DEFINITION: to invigorate, strengthen.
ORIGIN: From en and ischuo; to invigorate (transitively or reflexively).

BDAG.en: to recover from loss of strength, grow strong, regain one’s strength; to cause to recover from loss of strength, strengthen; urge someth. insistently
BDAG.pt: recuperar-se da perda de força, fortalecer-se, recuperar as forças; fazer recuperar-se da perda de força, fortalecer; instigar algo insistentemente

DEFINITION: ninth.
ORIGIN: Ordinal from ennea; ninth.

BDAG.en: ninth
BDAG.pt: nono

DEFINITION: nine.
ORIGIN: A primary number; nine.

BDAG.en: nine
BDAG.pt: nove

DEFINITION: ninety-nine.
ORIGIN: From a (tenth) multiple of ennea and ennea itself; ninety-nine.

BDAG.en: ninety
BDAG.pt: noventa

DEFINITION: dumb, speechless (as with amazement).
ORIGIN: From enneuo; dumb (as making signs), i.e. Silent from astonishment.

BDAG.en: primary meaning, pert. to lacking ability to speak, ‘mute’; then by extension speechless
BDAG.pt: significado primário, referente à falta de habilidade para falar, 'mudo'; depois por extensão sem palavras

DEFINITION: to nod at, beckon or communicate by gesture.
ORIGIN: From en and neuo; to nod at, i.e. Beckon or communicate by gesture.

BDAG.en: to signify by bodily movement, nod, make signs to someone
BDAG.pt: significar por movimento corporal, acenar com a cabeça, fazer sinais a alguém

DEFINITION: thinking, consideration; a thought, purpose, design, intention.
ORIGIN: From a compound of en and nous; thoughtfulness, i.e. Moral understanding.

BDAG.en: the content of mental processing, thought, knowledge, insight
BDAG.pt: o conteúdo do processamento mental, pensamento, conhecimento, percepção

DEFINITION: (a) legal, statutory, duly constituted, (b) under the law, obedient to the law.
ORIGIN: From en and nomos; (subjectively) legal, or (objectively) subject to.

BDAG.en: pertaining to being in accordance with law, legal, lawful; subject to law, obedient to law
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar de acordo com a lei, legal, lícito; sujeito à lei, obediente à lei

DEFINITION: nightly, neut. as adverb by night.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of en and nux; (adverbially) by night.

BDAG.en: pertaining to the period between sunset and sunrise, at night
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao período entre o pôr do sol e o nascer do sol, à noite

DEFINITION: to dwell in, be settled (stationary) in; met: to be indwelling.
ORIGIN: From en and oikeo; to inhabit (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to live, dwell (in)
BDAG.pt: morar, habitar (em)

DEFINITION: oneness, unity, unanimity.
ORIGIN: From heis; oneness, i.e. (figuratively) unanimity.

BDAG.en: a state of oneness or of being in harmony and accord, unity
BDAG.pt: um estado de unidade ou de estar em harmonia e acordo, união

DEFINITION: to disturb, cause tumult, trouble, annoy.
ORIGIN: From en and ochleo; to crowd in, i.e. (figuratively) to annoy.

BDAG.en: to interfere or bother to the point of causing discomfort, trouble, annoy
BDAG.pt: interferir ou incomodar a ponto de causar desconforto, perturbar, irritar

DEFINITION: involved in, held in, hence: liable, generally with dat. (or gen.) of the punishment.
ORIGIN: From enecho; liable to (a condition, penalty or imputation).
USAGE: in danger of, guilty of, subject to.

BDAG.en: caught in; 1 pert. to being held in or constrained, subject to; 2 pert. to being required to give an account for someth. held against one, liable, answerable, guilty
BDAG.pt: apanhado em; 1 pert. a estar detido ou constrangido, sujeito a; 2 pert. a ter que prestar contas por algo retido contra um, responsável, culpado

DEFINITION: an injunction, ordinance, precept.
ORIGIN: From entellomai; an injunction, i.e. Religious precept.

BDAG.en: that which is commanded as officially binding, commandment
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é comandado como oficialmente obrigatório, mandamento

DEFINITION: to embalm, prepare for burial.
ORIGIN: From a compound of en and taphos; to inswathe with cerements for interment.

BDAG.en: to prepare for burial, bury
BDAG.pt: preparar para o sepultamento, enterrar

DEFINITION: embalming, preparation of a body for burial.
ORIGIN: From entaphiazo; preparation for interment.

BDAG.en: the performance of what is customary for burial, preparation for burial or burial itself
BDAG.pt: a realização do que é costumeiro para o sepultamento, preparação para o sepultamento ou o próprio sepultamento

DEFINITION: to give orders (injunctions, instructions, commands).
ORIGIN: From en and the base of telos; to enjoin.

DEFINITION: hence, from this place, on this side and on that.
ORIGIN: From the same as enthade; hence (literally or figuratively); (repeated) on both sides.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to extension from a source near the speaker, from here; 2 pert. to the reason for, or source of, someth., fr. this
BDAG.pt: 1 pert. à extensão a partir de uma fonte próxima ao falante, daqui; 2 pert. à razão ou origem de algo, a partir disto

DEFINITION: (lit: approaching the king, hence a technical term), a petition, prayer, intercession.
ORIGIN: From entugchano; an interview, i.e. (specially) supplication.

BDAG.en: 1 a formal request put to a high official or official body, petition, request; 2 prayer, and chiefly an intercessory prayer
BDAG.pt: 1 um pedido formal feito a um alto funcionário ou corpo oficial, petição, solicitação; 2 oração, e principalmente uma oração intercessória

DEFINITION: (held precious, hence) precious, honored, honorable in rank.
ORIGIN: From en and time; valued (figuratively).
USAGE: dear, more honourable, precious, in reputation.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being highly regarded because of status or personal quality, honored, respected; 2 pert. to being esteemed as someth. of considerable worth, valuable, precious
BDAG.pt: 1 pert. a ser altamente considerado por status ou qualidade pessoal, honrado, respeitado; 2 pert. a ser estimado como algo de valor considerável, valioso, precioso

DEFINITION: an ordinance, injunction, command, law.
ORIGIN: From entellomai; injunction, i.e. An authoritative prescription.

BDAG.en: an order authorizing a specific action, writ, warrant; a mandate or ordinance, command (of OT law, of divine authorities, of Christ's precepts)
BDAG.pt: uma ordem que autoriza uma ação específica, mandado, alvará; um mandato ou ordenança, mandamento (da lei do AT, de autoridades divinas, dos preceitos de Cristo)

DEFINITION: belonging to the place, native, resident; subst: a citizen.
ORIGIN: From en and topos; a resident.

BDAG.en: pert. to belonging to a certain place, local; subst. the local residents
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a um certo lugar, local; substantivo: os residentes locais

DEFINITION: within, inside, the inside.
ORIGIN: From en; inside (adverb or noun).

BDAG.en: in, within, within the limits of; among you, in your midst; what is in the cup (content)
BDAG.pt: em, dentro, dentro dos limites de; entre vós, no vosso meio; o que está no copo (conteúdo)

DEFINITION: (a) to turn to confusion, put to shame, (b) mid: to reverence, regard.
ORIGIN: From en and the base of trope; to invert, i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) in a good sense, to respect; or in a bad one, to confound.

BDAG.en: to cause to turn (in shame), to shame; pass. be put to shame, be ashamed; to show deference to a pers., have regard for, respect
BDAG.pt: fazer voltar (em vergonha), envergonhar; voz passiva: ser envergonhado, envergonhar-se; mostrar deferência a uma pessoa, ter consideração, respeitar

DEFINITION: to nourish (sustain) on, be educated in.
ORIGIN: From en and trepho; (figuratively) to educate.

BDAG.en: to bring up, rear; then train in something
BDAG.pt: criar, educar; depois, treinar em algo

DEFINITION: trembling with fear, terrified.
ORIGIN: From en and tromos; terrified.

BDAG.en: pert. to being in a quivering condition because of exposure to an overwhelming or threatening circumstance, trembling
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a estar numa condição de tremor devido à exposição a uma circunstância avassaladora ou ameaçadora, a tremer

DEFINITION: respect, shame.
ORIGIN: From entrepo; confusion.

BDAG.en: the state of being ashamed, shame, humiliation; deference to a pers. in recognition of special status, respect, regard
BDAG.pt: o estado de estar envergonhado, vergonha, humilhação; deferência a uma pessoa em reconhecimento de status especial, respeito, consideração

DEFINITION: to revel (in), live luxuriously, riot.
ORIGIN: From en and truphao; to revel in.

BDAG.en: to take exuberant delight in, delight in; to engage in self-indulgent behavior, revel, carouse
BDAG.pt: ter deleite exuberante em, deleitar-se em; envolver-se em comportamento autodispensado, festejar, banquetear

DEFINITION: (a) to meet, encounter, hence: (b) to call (upon), make a petition, make suit, supplication.
ORIGIN: From en and tugchano; to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) confer with; by extension to entreat (in favor or against).

BDAG.en: to make an earnest request through contact with the pers. approached, approach or appeal to someone; plead for someone; pray; read (from encountering a book)
BDAG.pt: fazer um pedido sério através do contato com a pessoa abordada, aproximar-se ou apelar a alguém; advogar por alguém; orar; ler (a partir do sentido de encontrar um livro)

DEFINITION: to wrap up, roll round, envelop.
ORIGIN: From en and tulisso (to twist; probably akin to heilisso); to entwine, i.e. Wind up in.

BDAG.en: to wrap something around an object, wrap (up); fold up (of a cloth)
BDAG.pt: enrolar algo ao redor de um objeto, envolver (embrulhar); dobrar (um pano)

DEFINITION: to imprint, engrave.
ORIGIN: From en and a derivative of tupos; to enstamp, i.e. Engrave.

BDAG.en: to form letters or designs by incision, carve, impress
BDAG.pt: formar letras ou desenhos por incisão, esculpir, imprimir

DEFINITION: to insult, outrage, treat contemptuously, mock at.
ORIGIN: From en and hubrizo; to insult.

BDAG.en: to insult, outrage.
BDAG.pt: insultar, ultrajar.

DEFINITION: to dream (see visions) in sleep.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from enupnion; to dream.

BDAG.en: to dream, have visions in dreams.
BDAG.pt: sonhar, ter visões em sonhos.

DEFINITION: a dream, vision.
ORIGIN: From en and hupnos; something seen in sleep, i.e. A dream (vision in a dream).

BDAG.en: a dream
BDAG.pt: um sonho

DEFINITION: before the face of, in the presence of, in the eyes of.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of en and a derivative of optanomai; in the face of (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: before, in the presence (sight) of, to.

BDAG.en: pert. to a position in front of an entity, before someone or someth.; in the sight of, in the presence of, among; in the opinion/ judgment of; sin against someone; by the authority of, on behalf of
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a uma posição em frente de uma entidade, diante de alguém ou algo; à vista de, na presença de, entre; na opinião/julgamento de; pecar contra alguém; por autoridade de, em nome de

DEFINITION: Enosh (also Enos), son of Seth, and father of Cainan.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Enowsh); Enos (i.e. Enosh), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Enos, son of Seth.
BDAG.pt: Enos, filho de Sete.

DEFINITION: to take into ear, give ear to, listen to.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from a compound of en and ous; to take in one's ear, i.e. To listen.

BDAG.en: to listen carefully to what is said, give ear, pay attention to
BDAG.pt: escutar atentamente o que é dito, prestar atenção, dar ouvidos

DEFINITION: Enoch, son of Jared and father of Methuselah.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Chanowk); Enoch (i.e. Chanok), an antediluvian.

BDAG.en: Enoch, son of Jared, father of Methuselah.
BDAG.pt: Enoque, filho de Jarede, pai de Matusalém.

DEFINITION: six.
ORIGIN: A primary numeral; six.

BDAG.en: six.
BDAG.pt: seis.

DEFINITION: to announce publicly, proclaim.
ORIGIN: From ek and the base of aggelos; to publish, i.e. Celebrate.

BDAG.en: proclaim, report.
BDAG.pt: proclamar, relatar.

DEFINITION: to buy out, buy away from, ransom; mid: to purchase out, buy, redeem, choose.
ORIGIN: From ek and agorazo; to buy up, i.e. Ransom; figuratively, to rescue from loss (improve opportunity).

BDAG.en: to secure deliverance of, deliver, liberate; to gain something, esp. advantage or opportunity, make the most of; buy off (avoiding punishment)
BDAG.pt: assegurar a libertação de, livrar, libertar; obter algo, especialmente vantagem ou oportunidade, aproveitar ao máximo; comprar (evitando punição)

DEFINITION: to lead out, sometimes to death, execution.
ORIGIN: From ek and ago; to lead forth.

BDAG.en: to conduct from an area, lead out, bring out; to remove from a state or condition, free
BDAG.pt: conduzir para fora de uma área, liderar para fora, trazer para fora; remover de um estado ou condição, libertar

DEFINITION: to take out, remove; sometimes (mid): to choose, sometimes: to rescue.
ORIGIN: From ek and haireomai; actively, to tear out; middle voice, to select; figuratively, to release.

BDAG.en: to remove something from its place, take out, tear out; to deliver someone from peril or confining circumstance, set free, deliver, rescue
BDAG.pt: remover algo de seu lugar, tirar, arrancar; livrar alguém de perigo ou circunstância restritiva, pôr em liberdade, entregar, resgatar

DEFINITION: to lift up, remove, eject.
ORIGIN: From ek and airo; to remove.

BDAG.en: to exclude or remove someone from a group, remove, drive away
BDAG.pt: excluir ou remover alguém de um grupo, remover, expulsar

DEFINITION: to demand of, ask for, beg earnestly for.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ek and aiteo; to demand (for trial).

BDAG.en: to ask for with emphasis and with implication of having a right to do so, ask for, demand; to make an earnest request of someone, ask, plead
BDAG.pt: pedir com ênfase e com implicação de ter o direito de fazê-lo, pedir, exigir; fazer um pedido fervoroso a alguém, pedir, suplicar

DEFINITION: suddenly, unexpectedly.
ORIGIN: From ek and the base of aiphnidios; of a sudden (unexpectedly).

BDAG.en: suddenly, unexpectedly
BDAG.pt: de repente, inesperadamente

DEFINITION: to follow (out, up), to imitate.
ORIGIN: From ek and akoloutheo; to follow out, i.e. (figuratively) to imitate, obey, yield to.

BDAG.en: to accept as authoritative determiner of thought or action, obey, follow; to imitate behavior, follow, pursue, a way
BDAG.pt: aceitar como determinante autoritário de pensamento ou ação, obedecer, seguir; imitar o comportamento, seguir, perseguir um caminho

DEFINITION: six hundred.
ORIGIN: Plural ordinal from hex and hekaton; six hundred.

BDAG.en: six hundred
BDAG.pt: seiscentos

DEFINITION: to plaster, wash over; to wipe off, wipe out, obliterate.
ORIGIN: From ek and aleipho; to smear out, i.e. Obliterate (erase tears, figuratively, pardon sin).

BDAG.en: to cause to disappear by wiping a wipe away; wipe out, erase; remove so as to leave no trace, remove, destroy, obliterate
BDAG.pt: fazer desaparecer limpando; apagar, riscar; remover de modo a não deixar vestígios, remover, destruir, obliterar

DEFINITION: to leap up (for joy).
ORIGIN: From ek and hallomai; to spring forth.

BDAG.en: to spring free from a place, leap out; to spring up to a standing position, leap up
BDAG.pt: saltar para fora de um lugar, pular para fora; saltar para uma posição em pé, pular

DEFINITION: a rising up and out, resurrection.
ORIGIN: From exanistemi; a rising from death.

BDAG.en: the state or condition of coming up from among the dead, resurrection
BDAG.pt: o estado ou condição de ressurgir dentre os mortos, ressurreição

DEFINITION: to rise (spring) up out (of the ground).
ORIGIN: From ek and anatello; to start up out of the ground, i.e. Germinate.

BDAG.en: spring up of a quick-growing plant
BDAG.pt: brotação (de uma planta de crescimento rápido)

DEFINITION: (a) in trans. tenses: to raise up, cause to grow, (b) in intrans. tenses: to rise up from.
ORIGIN: From ek and anistemi; objectively, to produce, i.e. (figuratively) beget; subjectively, to arise, i.e. (figuratively) object.

BDAG.en: 1 to cause to stir from a position, raise up, awaken; 2 to beget progeny, raise up offspring; 3 to come to the fore, stand up (distinct from others) to speak; rise up of one who appears on the scene
BDAG.pt: 1 causar agitação de uma posição, levantar, despertar; 2 gerar prole, levantar descendência; 3 vir à tona, levantar-se (distinto dos outros) para falar; levantar-se alguém que aparece em cena

DEFINITION: to seduce wholly, deceive.
ORIGIN: From ek and apatao; to seduce wholly.

BDAG.en: to cause someone to accept false ideas about something, deceive, cheat; lead astray; deceive oneself
BDAG.pt: fazer alguém aceitar falsas ideias sobre algo, enganar, iludir; levar ao erro; enganar a si mesmo

DEFINITION: suddenly, unexpectedly.
ORIGIN: From ek and a derivative of the same as aiphnidios; of a sudden, i.e. Unexpectedly.

BDAG.en: 1 pertaining to something brought about in a very brief time, suddenly; 2 pertaining to something happening unexpectedly and without time for preparation, unexpectedly
BDAG.pt: 1 pertencente a algo trazido à existência em tempo muito breve, subitamente; 2 pertencente a algo que acontece inesperadamente e sem tempo para preparação, inesperadamente

DEFINITION: to be utterly without resource, be in despair.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ek and aporeo; to be utterly at a loss, i.e. Despond.

DEFINITION: to send away, send forth (a person qualified for a task).
ORIGIN: From ek and apostello; to send away forth, i.e. (on a mission) to despatch, or (peremptorily) to dismiss.

BDAG.en: 1 to send someone off to a locality or on a mission, send away, send off, send out; 2 to send off as an act of dismissal, send away; 3 to send something off in an official sense, send, dispatch
BDAG.pt: 1 enviar alguém para uma localidade ou em missão, mandar embora, despachar, enviar para fora; 2 mandar embora como ato de dispensa, despedir; 3 enviar algo em sentido oficial, mandar, expedir

DEFINITION: (a) to fit up, completely furnish, equip, furnish, supply, (b) to accomplish, finish.
ORIGIN: From ek and a derivative of artios; to finish out (time); figuratively, to equip fully (a teacher).

BDAG.en: 1 to bring something to an end, finish, complete; 2 to make ready for service, equip, furnish
BDAG.pt: 1 levar algo a um fim, terminar, completar; 2 preparar para o serviço, equipar, aparelhar

DEFINITION: to flash forth like lightning, gleam, be radiant.
ORIGIN: From ek and astrapto; to lighten forth, i.e. (figuratively) to be radiant (of very white garments).

BDAG.en: flash/gleam like lightning (figuratively of a white garment)
BDAG.pt: fulgurar/reluzir como um raio (figurativamente de um vestuário branco)

DEFINITION: immediately, instantly, at once.
ORIGIN: From ek and the genitive case singular feminine of autos (hora being understood); from that hour, i.e. Instantly.
USAGE: by and by, immediately, presently, straightway.

BDAG.en: at once, immediately, soon thereafter
BDAG.pt: de imediato, imediatamente, logo depois

DEFINITION: to raise up, arouse.
ORIGIN: From ek and egeiro; to rouse fully, i.e. (figuratively) to resuscitate (from death), release (from infliction).

BDAG.en: 1 to awaken someone from sleep, awaken; 2 to raise up from the dead, raise; 3 to bring to a sitting position, raise up; 4 cause to appear, bring into being; 5 give one higher status, elevate
BDAG.pt: 1 despertar alguém do sono, acordar; 2 ressuscitar dentre os mortos, levantar; 3 trazer a uma posição sentada, levantar; 4 fazer aparecer, trazer à existência; 5 dar a alguém um status mais elevado, elevar

DEFINITION: (originally: to shall go out), to go out (away), depart.
ORIGIN: From ek and eimi (to go); to issue, i.e. Leave (a place), escape (to the shore).

BDAG.en: to depart from an area, go out, go away; go on a journey; get to land
BDAG.pt: partir de uma área, sair, ir embora; embarcar em uma jornada; chegar a terra

DEFINITION: convince.
ORIGIN: From ek and elegcho; to convict fully, i.e. (by implication) to punish.

BDAG.en: to expose someone’s errors in devastating fashion: convict
BDAG.pt: expor os erros de alguém de forma devastadora: convencer/refutar

DEFINITION: (lit: to draw out of the right place, or to draw aside out of the right way), to entice.
ORIGIN: From ek and helkuo; to drag forth, i.e. (figuratively) to entice (to sin).

BDAG.en: to drag away, with connotation of initial reluctance, drag away taken in tow by his own desire(s)
BDAG.pt: arrastar para fora, com conotação de relutância inicial, arrastar para longe puxado pelo(s) seu(s) próprio(s) desejo(s)

DEFINITION: vomit (noun).
ORIGIN: From a comparative of ek and a presumed erao (to spue); vomit, i.e. Food disgorged.

BDAG.en: what has been vomited, vomit
BDAG.pt: o que foi vomitado, vômito

DEFINITION: to search diligently, to examine carefully (minutely).
ORIGIN: From ek and ereunao; to explore (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to make careful inquiry, try to find out concerning something
BDAG.pt: investigar cuidadosamente, tentar descobrir algo sobre algo

DEFINITION: to go or come out of.
ORIGIN: From ek and erchomai; to issue (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: come (forth, out), depart (out of), escape, get out, go (abroad, away, forth, out, thence), proceed (forth), spread abroad.

BDAG.en: to move out of or away from an area; go out, come out, go away, retire; appear; get up and go out/ready; discontinue an association, depart; get away fr. or out of a difficult situation, escape; depart in death, die; come fr. by way of ancestry, go out, proceed
BDAG.pt: mover-se para fora ou para longe de uma área; sair, vir para fora, ir embora, retirar-se; aparecer; levantar-se e sair/preparar-se; descontinuar uma associação, partir; escapar de ou sair de uma situação difícil; partir na morte, morrer; vir por linhagem ancestral, proceder

DEFINITION: it is permitted, lawful, possible.
ORIGIN: Third person singular present indicative of a compound of ek and eimi; so also exon ex-on' neuter present participle of the same (with or without some form of eimi expressed); impersonally, it is right (through the figurative idea of being out in public).

BDAG.en: to be authorized for the doing of something, it is right, is authorized, is permitted, is proper; to be within the range of possibility, it is possible
BDAG.pt: ser autorizado para a realização de algo, é certo, é autorizado, é permitido, é apropriado; estar dentro do alcance da possibilidade, é possível

DEFINITION: to examine, question, inquire at, search out.
ORIGIN: From ek and etazo (to examine); to test thoroughly (by questions), i.e. Ascertain or interrogate.

BDAG.en: try to find out by use of careful methods, which may include personal inquiry, scrutinize, examine, inquire; to inquire intensively, question, examine, [as legal term] question judicially
BDAG.pt: tentar descobrir por meio de métodos cuidadosos, o que pode incluir inquérito pessoal, perscrutar, examinar, inquirir; inquirir intensamente, questionar, examinar, [como termo legal] interrogar judicialmente

DEFINITION: to lead, show the way; met: to unfold, narrate, declare.
ORIGIN: From ek and hegeomai; to consider out (aloud), i.e. Rehearse, unfold.

BDAG.en: to relate in detail, tell, report, describe (chiefly narrative); to set forth in great detail, expound.
BDAG.pt: relatar em detalhes, contar, reportar, descrever (principalmente narrativo); expor em grande detalhe, explicar.

DEFINITION: sixty.
ORIGIN: The tenth multiple of hex; sixty.

BDAG.en: sixty.
BDAG.pt: sessenta.

DEFINITION: next in order, the next day, the following day, at the period immediately following.
ORIGIN: From echo (in the sense of taking hold of, i.e. Adjoining); successive.

BDAG.en: next in a series, in the next place (of time, always in NT: on the next day).
BDAG.pt: em seguida em uma série, em seguida (de tempo, sempre no NT: no dia seguinte).

DEFINITION: to sound out (forth) (referring either to the clearness or to the loudness of the sound).
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ek and echeo; to "echo" forth, i.e. Resound (be generally reported).

BDAG.en: trans., ‘cause to resound or be heard’; pass. be caused to sound forth, ring out
BDAG.pt: trans., 'fazer ressoar ou ser ouvido'; pass. ser feito para soar, ressoar

DEFINITION: condition, state, habit, use, especially: good condition of body or soul.
ORIGIN: From echo; habit, i.e. (by implication) practice.

BDAG.en: a state of maturity, maturity.
BDAG.pt: um estado de maturidade, maturidade.

DEFINITION: (lit: to remove from a standing position), (a) in trans. tenses: to astonish, amaze, (b) in intrans. tenses: to be astonished, amazed; to be out of mind, be mad.
ORIGIN: From ek and histemi; to put (stand) out of wits, i.e. Astound, or (reflexively) become astounded, insane.
USAGE: amaze, be (make) astonished, be beside self (selves), bewitch, wonder.

BDAG.en: to cause to be in a state in which things seem to make little or no sense, confuse, amaze, astound (trans.); be out of one’s normal state of mind, lose one’s mind (intr.); be amazed, be astonished (intr., weakened sense)
BDAG.pt: causar um estado em que as coisas parecem não fazer sentido, confundir, espantar, assombrar (trans.); estar fora do estado normal de espírito, perder o juízo (intrans.); ficar espantado, ficar maravilhado (intrans., sentido atenuado)

DEFINITION: to have strength for (a difficult task), be perfectly able.
ORIGIN: From ek and ischuo; to have full strength, i.e. Be entirely competent.

BDAG.en: to be fully capable of doing or experiencing something, be able, be strong enough, be in a position.
BDAG.pt: ser totalmente capaz de fazer ou experimentar algo, ser capaz, ser forte o suficiente, estar em posição.

DEFINITION: (a) an exit, going out, departure from a place; the exodus, (b) death.
ORIGIN: From ek and hodos; an exit, i.e. (figuratively) death.

BDAG.en: movement from one geographical area to another, departure, path, course; departure from among the living, euphemism for death
BDAG.pt: movimento de uma área geográfica para outra, partida, caminho, percurso; partida dentre os vivos, eufemismo para morte

DEFINITION: to destroy utterly, annihilate, exterminate, root out.
ORIGIN: From ek and olothreuo; to extirpate.

DEFINITION: (a) to consent fully, agree out and out, (b) to confess, admit, acknowledge (cf. the early Hellenistic sense of the middle: to acknowledge a debt), (c) to give thanks, praise.
ORIGIN: From ek and homologeo; to acknowledge or (by implication, of assent) agree fully.

BDAG.en: to indicate acceptance of an offer or proposal, promise, consent; to make an admission of wrong-doing/sin, confess, admit; to declare openly in acknowledgment, profess, acknowledge; to praise, in acknowledgment of divine beneficence and majesty.
BDAG.pt: indicar aceitação de uma oferta ou proposta, prometer, consentir; fazer uma admissão de erro/pecado, confessar, admitir; declarar abertamente em reconhecimento, professar, reconhecer; louvar, em reconhecimento da beneficência e majestade divinas.

DEFINITION: to adjure, put to oath; to exorcise.
ORIGIN: From ek and horkizo; to exact an oath, i.e. Conjure.

BDAG.en: to compel someone to do something by invoking a transcendent power, solemnly command; of expulsion of an evil spirit exorcise an evil spirit; to put someone under oath to warrant the truth of what is said, put under oath, adjure someone.
BDAG.pt: compelir alguém a fazer algo invocando um poder transcendente, ordenar solenemente; da expulsão de um espírito maligno, exorcizar um espírito maligno; colocar alguém sob juramento para garantir a veracidade do que é dito, fazer jurar, conjurar alguém.

DEFINITION: an exorcist, a caster out of evil spirits by the use of names or spells.
ORIGIN: From exorkizo; one that binds by an oath (or spell), i.e. (by implication) an "exorcist" (conjurer).

BDAG.en: one who drives out evil spirits by invocation of transcendent entities, exorcist.
BDAG.pt: aquele que expulsa espíritos malignos pela invocação de entidades transcendentes, exorcista.

DEFINITION: (a) to dig out, hence: to open up, (b) to gouge.
ORIGIN: From ek and orusso; to dig out, i.e. (by extension) to extract (an eye), remove (roofing).

BDAG.en: to extract something out of an area by force, tear out (eyes); dig through (a roof)
BDAG.pt: extrair algo de uma área à força, arrancar (olhos); escavar/perfurar (um telhado)

DEFINITION: to set at naught, ignore, despise.
ORIGIN: From ek and a derivative of the neuter of oudeis; to make utterly nothing of, i.e. Despise.
USAGE: set at nought. See also exoutheneo.

DEFINITION: to set at naught, ignore, despise.
ORIGIN: A variation of exoudenoo and meaning the same.
USAGE: contemptible, despise, least esteemed, set at nought.

DEFINITION: (a) power, authority, weight, especially: moral authority, influence, (b) in a quasi-personal sense, derived from later Judaism, of a spiritual power, and hence of an earthly power.
ORIGIN: From exesti (in the sense of ability); privilege, i.e. (subjectively) force, capacity, competency, freedom, or (objectively) mastery (concretely, magistrate, superhuman, potentate, token of control), delegated influence.
USAGE: authority, jurisdiction, liberty, power, right, strength.

BDAG.en: a state of control over something, freedom of choice, right; potential or resource to command, control, or govern, capability, might, power; the right to control or command, authority, absolute power, warrant; power exercised by rulers or others in high position by virtue of their office, ruling power, official power; bearer of ruling authority, human authorities, officials, government; powers of the spirit world; the sphere in which power is exercised, domain
BDAG.pt: um estado de controle sobre algo, liberdade de escolha, direito; potencial ou recurso para comandar, controlar ou governar, capacidade, poder; o direito de controlar ou comandar, autoridade, poder absoluto, legitimação; poder exercido por governantes ou outros em posição elevada em virtude de seu cargo, poder governante, poder oficial; portador de autoridade governante, autoridades humanas, funcionários, governo; poderes do mundo espiritual; a esfera em que o poder é exercido, domínio

DEFINITION: to exercise (wield) power (authority), pass: to be ruled, be held under authority.
ORIGIN: From exousia; to control.
USAGE: exercise authority upon, bring under the (have) power of.

BDAG.en: to have the right of control, have the right/power for something or over someone; specifically, the right or power to do with something as one sees fit
BDAG.pt: ter o direito de controle, ter o direito/poder sobre algo ou alguém; especificamente, o direito ou poder de fazer com algo como se vê por bem

DEFINITION: eminence, distinction, excellence.
ORIGIN: From a compound of ek and echo (meaning to stand out); prominence (figuratively).

BDAG.en: from ‘something that projects from a surface’; it is a short step to the idea of having special status, prominence ('excellence, advantage')
BDAG.pt: a partir de 'algo que se projeta de uma superfície'; é um pequeno passo para a ideia de ter um status especial, proeminência ('excelência, vantagem')

DEFINITION: to awaken out of sleep.
ORIGIN: From exupnos; to waken.

BDAG.en: wakeup, arouse (someone who is sleeping)
BDAG.pt: acordar, despertar (alguém que está dormindo)

DEFINITION: roused out of sleep.
ORIGIN: From ek and hupnos; awake.

BDAG.en: awake, aroused
BDAG.pt: acordado, desperto

DEFINITION: outside, without.
ORIGIN: Adverb from ek; out(-side, of doors), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: pert. to a position beyond an enclosure or boundary, outside; pert. to a position outside an area or limits, out
BDAG.pt: pertencente a uma posição além de um recinto ou limite, fora; pertencente a uma posição fora de uma área ou limites, para fora

DEFINITION: (a) from outside, from without, (b) outside, both as adj. and prep; with article: the outside.
ORIGIN: From exo; external(-ly).

BDAG.en: from outside; outside (as preposition); external, the external (as substitute for an adjective); outward, out (as result of action); on the outside (as noun)
BDAG.pt: de fora; fora de (como preposição); externo, o exterior (como substituto de adjetivo); para fora, para fora (como resultado de ação); do lado de fora (como substantivo)

DEFINITION: to drive out, expel, propel, thrust out; to drive out of the sea, drive on shore.
ORIGIN: Or exotho ex-o'-tho from ek and otheo (to push); to expel; by implication, to propel.

BDAG.en: to force to leave an area, push out, expel; to run or drive ashore, beach (mariner’s term)
BDAG.pt: forçar a sair de uma área, expulsar; encalhar, levar para a praia (termo náutico)

DEFINITION: outmost, outer, external.
ORIGIN: Comparative of exo; exterior.

BDAG.en: outside (in contrast to inside or in the middle); farthest, extreme
BDAG.pt: exterior (em contraste com o interior ou o meio); mais distante, extremo

DEFINITION: to take part in a festival, keep a feast (allegorically).
ORIGIN: From heorte; to observe a festival.

BDAG.en: celebrate a festival
BDAG.pt: celebrar um festival

DEFINITION: a festival, feast, periodically recurring.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a festival.

BDAG.en: a day or series of days marked by a periodic celebration or observance, festival, celebration (often specifically the Passover)
BDAG.pt: um dia ou série de dias marcados por uma celebração ou observância periódica, festival, celebração (frequentemente a Páscoa)

DEFINITION: a summons, a promise.
ORIGIN: From epaggello; an announcement (for information, assent or pledge; especially a divine assurance of good).

BDAG.en: declaration to do something with implication of obligation to carry out what is stated, promise, pledge, offer
BDAG.pt: declaração de fazer algo com a implicação de obrigação de cumprir o que foi dito, promessa, penhor, oferta

DEFINITION: to proclaim, to promise.
ORIGIN: From epi and the base of aggelos; to announce upon (reflexively), i.e. (by implication) to engage to do something, to assert something respecting oneself.

BDAG.en: to declare one's intention to do something with an obligation to carry it out; to promise or offer (of humans or God); to claim to be accomplished in something.
BDAG.pt: declarar a intenção de fazer algo com a obrigação de cumprir; prometer ou oferecer (de humanos ou de Deus); alegar ser realizado em algo.

DEFINITION: a promise.
ORIGIN: From epaggello; a self-committal (by assurance of conferring some good).

BDAG.en: a declaration of obligation to perform something; the content of what is promised.
BDAG.pt: uma declaração de obrigação de realizar algo; o conteúdo do que foi prometido.

DEFINITION: to bring upon; met: to cause to be imputed to.
ORIGIN: From epi and ago; to superinduce, i.e. Inflict (an evil), charge (a crime).

BDAG.en: to cause a state or condition to occur or be; to bring something upon someone, usually something bad (e.g., bringing grief or destruction).
BDAG.pt: causar que um estado ou condição ocorra ou seja; trazer algo sobre alguém, geralmente algo negativo (ex: trazer tristeza ou destruição).

DEFINITION: to contend earnestly for.
ORIGIN: From epi and agonizomai; to struggle for.

BDAG.en: to exert intense effort on behalf of something; to contend (often used with athletic imagery, emphasizing effort for a noble cause).
BDAG.pt: exercer um esforço intenso em nome de algo; batalhar (frequentemente usado com imagens atléticas, enfatizando o esforço por uma causa nobre).

DEFINITION: to gather together, pass: to crowd upon (some one), press around.
ORIGIN: From epi and athroizo (to assemble); to accumulate.

BDAG.en: to gather together in addition or besides; to increase in number.
BDAG.pt: ajuntar em adição ou além; aumentar em número.

DEFINITION: "praiseworthy", Epaenetus, a Christian of Rome.
ORIGIN: From epaineo; praised; Epaenetus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Epaenetus, one of the first Christians in Asia
BDAG.pt: Epeneto, um dos primeiros cristãos na Ásia
