DEFINITION: to praise, commend, applaud.
ORIGIN: From epi and aineo; to applaud.

BDAG.en: to express one’s admiration for or approval of a person, object, or event, praise
BDAG.pt: expressar admiração ou aprovação por uma pessoa, objeto ou evento, louvar

DEFINITION: commendation, praise, approval.
ORIGIN: From epi and the base of aineo; laudation; concretely, a commendable thing.

BDAG.en: the act of expressing admiration or approval; praise, approval, recognition (both from humans and God); something worthy of praise.
BDAG.pt: o ato de expressar admiração ou aprovação; louvor, aprovação, reconhecimento (tanto de humanos quanto de Deus); algo digno de louvor.

DEFINITION: to raise, lift up.
ORIGIN: From epi and airo; to raise up (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to cause to move upward, lift up, hold up; to offer resistance to, be in opposition, rise up; to suggest that one is better than one really is, be presumptuous, put on airs
BDAG.pt: fazer mover para cima, levantar, sustentar; oferecer resistência, opor-se, levantar-se; sugerir ser melhor do que realmente é, ser presunçoso, exibir-se

DEFINITION: to be ashamed, be ashamed of.
ORIGIN: From epi and aischunomai; to feel shame for something.

BDAG.en: to experience a painful feeling or sense of loss of status because of some particular event or activity, be ashamed
BDAG.pt: experimentar um sentimento doloroso ou de perda de status por causa de algum evento ou atividade particular, ter vergonha

DEFINITION: to beg, be a beggar, ask alms.
ORIGIN: From epi and aiteo; to ask for.

BDAG.en: to beg as a mendicant; to ask for more.
BDAG.pt: pedir esmola como um mendicante; pedir mais.

DEFINITION: to follow close after, accompany, dog; to imitate, pursue, be studious of.
ORIGIN: From epi and akoloutheo; to accompany.

BDAG.en: to use someone as a model for doing something, follow; to happen as result or appropriate event in connection with something, follow; to apply oneself to something with eager dedication, follow after, i.e. devote oneself to something
BDAG.pt: usar alguém como modelo para fazer algo, seguir; acontecer como resultado ou evento apropriado em conexão com algo, seguir; dedicar-se a algo com dedicação fervorosa, seguir, isto é, devotar-se a algo

DEFINITION: to listen to, hear favorably.
ORIGIN: From epi and akouo; to hearken (favorably) to.

BDAG.en: to pay close attention to what one is told with implication of being responsive, hear, listen to; to act appropriately in response to what one hears, heed, obey
BDAG.pt: prestar muita atenção ao que é dito com a implicação de ser responsivo, ouvir, escutar; agir apropriadamente em resposta ao que se ouve, atender, obedecer

DEFINITION: to listen to, hear, hearken to.
ORIGIN: From epi and the base of akroates; to listen (intently) to.

BDAG.en: listen to in the sense of overhearing
BDAG.pt: escutar no sentido de ouvir por acaso

DEFINITION: after, when, as soon as.
ORIGIN: From epi and an; a particle of indefinite contemporaneousness; whenever, as soon as.

BDAG.en: when, as soon as
BDAG.pt: quando, assim que

DEFINITION: necessarily; as subst: necessary things.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed compound of epi and anagke; (adverbially) on necessity, i.e. Necessarily.

BDAG.en: pert. to being essential in connection w. something, of a necessary nature
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser essencial em conexão com algo, de natureza necessária

DEFINITION: (a) nautical: to put out (from the shore), (lit: to take up a ship on to the high seas), (b) to go up, possibly: to go up again, return.
ORIGIN: From epi and anago; to lead up on, i.e. (technical) to put out (to sea); (intransitively) to return.

BDAG.en: to leave the shore so as to get into open water, go out, put out to sea; to go back toward some point or area, return
BDAG.pt: deixar a costa para entrar em águas abertas, sair, navegar; voltar para algum ponto ou área, retornar

DEFINITION: to remind, possibly: to remind again.
ORIGIN: From epi and anamimnesko; to remind of.

BDAG.en: to cause to remember, remind someone of something again. Pass: call to mind, remember something again
BDAG.pt: fazer lembrar, lembrar alguém de algo novamente. Passivo: trazer à mente, lembrar-se de algo novamente

DEFINITION: to rest upon, rely on, trust in.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and anapano; to settle on; literally (remain) or figuratively (rely).

BDAG.en: to be in a state or condition of repose, rest, take one’s rest; to find well-being or inner security, find rest, comfort, support
BDAG.pt: estar em estado ou condição de repouso, descansar, tomar repouso; encontrar bem-estar ou segurança interior, encontrar descanso, conforto, apoio

DEFINITION: to return, come back again.
ORIGIN: From epi and anerchomai; to come up on, i.e. Return.

BDAG.en: to come back to a point or area, return
BDAG.pt: voltar a um ponto ou área, retornar

DEFINITION: intrans. tenses: to rise up against.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and anistemi; to stand up on, i.e. (figuratively) to attack.

BDAG.en: to become active in forceful resistance or expression of hostility, rise up, rise in rebellion
BDAG.pt: tornar-se ativo em resistência forçada ou expressão de hostilidade, levantar-se, rebelar-se

DEFINITION: correction, reformation, setting straight (right) again.
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and anorthoo; a straightening up again, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (reformation).

BDAG.en: improvement
BDAG.pt: melhoramento, aperfeiçoamento

DEFINITION: (a) adv: on the top, above, (b) prep: on the top of, above, over, on, above, more than, superior to.
ORIGIN: From epi and ano; up above, i.e. Over or on (of place, amount, rank, etc.).

BDAG.en: above, over (marker of a position relatively higher whether contiguous or not); more than (in amount); superior in status (above, over).
BDAG.pt: acima, sobre (indicador de uma posição relativamente mais alta, quer contígua ou não); mais do que (em quantidade); superior em status (acima, sobre).

DEFINITION: to aid, relieve, do service, render help, be strong enough for.
ORIGIN: From epi and arkeo; to avail for, i.e. Help.

BDAG.en: to come to the aid of someone, help, aid; provide for
BDAG.pt: vir em auxílio de alguém, ajudar, socorrer; prover para

DEFINITION: sphere of duty, province.
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and archo (meaning a governor of a district, "eparch"); a special region of government, i.e. A Roman præfecture.

DEFINITION: a farm, estate, dwelling, habitation.
ORIGIN: From epi and an equivalent of aule; a hut over the head, i.e. A dwelling.

BDAG.en: property that serves as a dwelling place whether personally owned or by contract, farm, homestead, residence
BDAG.pt: propriedade que serve como local de habitação, seja de posse pessoal ou por contrato, fazenda, casa de campo, residência

DEFINITION: on the next day.
ORIGIN: From epi and aurion; occurring on the succeeding day, i.e. (hemera being implied) to-morrow.

BDAG.en: tomorrow; on the next day.
BDAG.pt: amanhã; no dia seguinte.

DEFINITION: in the very act.
ORIGIN: From epi and autos and (the dative case singular of) a derivative of phor (a thief); in theft itself, i.e. (by analogy) in actual crime.

BDAG.en: caught in the act (esp. of a thief or adulterer).
BDAG.pt: em flagrante (especialmente de um ladrão ou adúltero).

DEFINITION: Epaphras, Epaphroditus, a Colossian Christian, in captivity with Paul in Rome.
ORIGIN: Contracted from Epaphroditos; Epaphras, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Epaphras, a Christian of Colossae, founder of the church there.
BDAG.pt: Epafras, um cristão de Colossos, fundador da igreja lá.

DEFINITION: to foam out (a metaphor from the seaweed and refuse borne on the crest of waves), vomit forth.
ORIGIN: From epi and aphrizo; to foam upon, i.e. (figuratively) to exhibit (a vile passion).

BDAG.en: to cause to splash up like froth, cause to foam
BDAG.pt: fazer espirrar como espuma, fazer espumar

DEFINITION: Epaphras, Epaphroditus, a Colossian Christian, in captivity with Paul in Rome.
ORIGIN: From epi (in the sense of devoted to) and Aphrodite (Venus); Epaphroditus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Epaphroditus, messenger sent by the Phil. church to Paul.
BDAG.pt: Epafrodito, mensageiro enviado pela igreja de Filipos a Paulo.

DEFINITION: to arouse, stimulate, excite against.
ORIGIN: From epi and egeiro; to rouse upon, i.e. (figuratively) to excite against.

BDAG.en: to cause an activity to begin through provocation, arouse, excite, stir up; [Pass.] to be aroused against someone, also rise up, revolt against someone.
BDAG.pt: causar o início de uma atividade por provocação, despertar, excitar, agitar; [Pass.] ser despertado contra alguém, também levantar-se, revoltar-se contra alguém.

DEFINITION: of time: when, after; of cause: since, because; otherwise: else.
ORIGIN: From epi and ei; thereupon, i.e. Since (of time or cause).
USAGE: because, else, for that (then, -asmuch as), otherwise, seeing that, since, when.

BDAG.en: when, after (marker of time); because, since, for (marker of cause or reason); otherwise (with ellipsis for a different condition).
BDAG.pt: quando, depois (marcador de tempo); porque, visto que, pois (marcador de causa ou razão); caso contrário (com elipse para uma condição diferente).

DEFINITION: of time: when, now, after that; of cause: seeing that, forasmuch as.
ORIGIN: From epei and de; since now, i.e. (of time) when, or (of cause) whereas.
USAGE: after that, because, for (that, -asmuch as), seeing, since.

BDAG.en: marker of time at which, when, after; marker of cause or reason, (just) because
BDAG.pt: marcador de tempo no qual, quando, depois; marcador de causa ou razão, (simplesmente) porque

DEFINITION: since, forasmuch as.
ORIGIN: From epeide and per; since indeed (of cause).

BDAG.en: inasmuch as, since (a marker of cause or reason, intensified form of ἐπειδή).
BDAG.pt: visto que, já que (um marcador de causa ou razão, forma intensificada de ἐπειδή).

DEFINITION: to looked upon, regarded.
ORIGIN: And other moods and persons of the same tense; from epi and eido; to regard (favorably or otherwise).

DEFINITION: since indeed, seeing that.
ORIGIN: From epei and per; since indeed (of cause).

BDAG.en: inasmuch as, since indeed
BDAG.pt: na medida em que, já que de fato

DEFINITION: bringing in (besides or in addition), introduction, importation.
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and eisago; a superintroduction.

BDAG.en: the process of causing someth. to be present, bringing in (besides), introduction
BDAG.pt: o processo de fazer com que algo esteja presente, trazer (além), introdução

DEFINITION: then, thereafter, afterwards.
ORIGIN: From epi and eita; thereafter.

BDAG.en: being next in order of time, then, thereupon; being next in position of an enumeration of items, then
BDAG.pt: sendo o próximo em ordem de tempo, então, depois; sendo o próximo em posição de uma enumeração de itens, então

DEFINITION: beyond, on yonder side.
ORIGIN: From epi and (the accusative case plural neuter of) ekeinos; upon those parts of, i.e. On the further side of.

BDAG.en: at a more advanced point, farther on, beyond.
BDAG.pt: em um ponto mais avançado, mais adiante, além.

DEFINITION: to extend, mid. to stretch forward.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and ekteino; to stretch (oneself) forward upon.

BDAG.en: to exert oneself to the uttermost, stretch out, strain toward something.
BDAG.pt: esforçar-se ao máximo, estender-se, esforçar-se em direção a algo.

DEFINITION: to have on over (as a garment); mid: to put on myself in addition.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and enduo; to invest upon oneself.

BDAG.en: to put a garment on over an existing garment, put on (in addition)
BDAG.pt: vestir uma roupa sobre uma roupa existente, vestir (adicionalmente)

DEFINITION: a coat, outer wrap or tunic.
ORIGIN: From ependuomai; a wrapper, i.e. Outer garment.

BDAG.en: a garment put on over another garment, outer garment, coat
BDAG.pt: uma vestimenta colocada sobre outra, vestimenta exterior, casaco

DEFINITION: to come to, arrive, come on, come upon, attack.
ORIGIN: From epi and erchomai; to supervene, i.e. Arrive, occur, impend, attack, (figuratively) influence.

BDAG.en: to move to or upon a come, arrive; of the Holy Spirit come upon, from a superior position; to occur as an event or process happen; to come against someone with force, attack
BDAG.pt: mover-se para ou sobre, chegar; do Espírito Santo vir sobre, de uma posição superior; ocorrer como um evento ou processo; vir contra alguém com força, atacar

DEFINITION: to interrogate, question, demand of.
ORIGIN: From epi and erotao; to ask for, i.e. Inquire, seek.

BDAG.en: to put a question to, ask; to make a request, ask for; (with deities) inquire after God, i.e. after the thought, purpose, or will of God
BDAG.pt: fazer uma pergunta a, perguntar; fazer um pedido, pedir; (com divindades) inquirir a respeito de Deus, ou seja, sobre o pensamento, propósito ou vontade de Deus

DEFINITION: inquiry, request, appeal, demand; a profession, pledge.
ORIGIN: From eperotao; an inquiry.

BDAG.en: the content of asking, question; a formal request, appeal
BDAG.pt: o conteúdo do perguntar, pergunta; um pedido formal, apelo

DEFINITION: (a) trans: to hold forth, (b) intrans: to mark, pay attention (heed), note; to delay, stay, wait.
ORIGIN: From epi and echo; to hold upon, i.e. (by implication) to retain; (by extension) to detain; (with implication, of nous) to pay attention to.
USAGE: give (take) heed unto, hold forth, mark, stay.

BDAG.en: to maintain a grasp on someone or someth., hold fast; to be mindful or especially observant, hold toward, aim at, intr., fig. of mental processes; to remain at a place for a period of time, stop, stay, intr.
BDAG.pt: manter um aperto sobre alguém ou algo, agarrar-se firmemente; estar atento ou especialmente observador, manter-se em direção a, almejar, intransitivo, fig. de processos mentais; permanecer em um lugar por um período de tempo, parar, demorar-se, intransitivo.

DEFINITION: to insult, treat wrongfully, molest, revile.
ORIGIN: From a comparative of epi and (probably) areia (threats); to insult, slander.

BDAG.en: to treat someone in a despicable manner, threaten, mistreat, abuse
BDAG.pt: tratar alguém de maneira desprezível, ameaçar, maltratar, abusar

DEFINITION: on, to, against, on the basis of, at.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition; properly, meaning superimposition (of time, place, order, etc.), as a relation of distribution (with the genitive case), i.e. Over, upon, etc.; of rest (with the dative case) at, on, etc.; of direction (with the accusative case) towards, upon, etc.
USAGE: about (the times), above, after, against, among, as long as (touching), at, beside, X have charge of, (be-, (where-))fore, in (a place, as much as, the time of, -to), (because) of, (up-)on (behalf of), over, (by, for) the space of, through(-out), (un-)to(-ward), with. In compounds it retains essentially the same import, at, upon, etc. (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: on, upon, near (location/surface); on, in, above (contiguity); on, upon (direction); on, over (contact/goal attained); at, by, near (presence/occurrence); before (official proceeding); toward, on, at (movement/contact); across, over (motion across); to, upon (goal attained); up to, in the neighborhood of (closeness); to (person); to, toward (imagery of goal/objective); in blessing (manner); on, based on (basis for state/action); at, because of (feelings/opinions)
BDAG.pt: sobre, em cima de, perto de (localização/superfície); em, dentro de, acima de (contiguidade); sobre, em cima de (direção); sobre, em cima de (contato/objetivo alcançado); em, perto de (presença/ocorrência); perante (procedimento oficial); em direção a, sobre, em (movimento/contato); através, por cima de (movimento através); para, sobre (objetivo alcançado); até, nas proximidades de (proximidade); a (pessoa); para, em direção a (imagem de objetivo); em bênçãos (maneira); sobre, com base em (base para estado/ação); em, por causa de (sentimentos/opiniões)

DEFINITION: (a) to set foot on, step on, (b) to mount (a horse), board (a vessel).
ORIGIN: From epi and the base of basis; to walk upon, i.e. Mount, ascend, embark, arrive.
USAGE: come (into), enter into, go abroad, sit upon, take ship.

BDAG.en: to move up onto something, go up/upon, mount, board; embark; move to an area and be there, set foot in
BDAG.pt: mover-se para cima de algo, subir/ir sobre, montar, embarcar; embarcar; mover-se para uma área e estar lá, pisar em

DEFINITION: (a) to throw upon, cast over, (b) to place upon, (c) to lay, (d) intrans: to strike upon, rush.
ORIGIN: From epi and ballo; to throw upon (literal or figurative, transitive or reflexive; usually with more or less force); specially (with heautou implied) to reflect; impersonally, to belong to.
USAGE: beat into, cast (up-)on, fall, lay (on), put (unto), stretch forth, think on.

BDAG.en: to put on, throw over something on someone; lay on, put on; lay the hand on something; set to, throw oneself or beat upon; to be scheduled for someone’s possession, fall to, belong to; apply oneself earnestly to something, take something upon oneself, undertake
BDAG.pt: colocar sobre, jogar sobre algo em alguém; pousar, pôr sobre; pousar a mão sobre algo; lançar-se contra ou bater sobre; ser destinado à posse de alguém, cair para, pertencer a; aplicar-se seriamente a algo, assumir algo, empreender

DEFINITION: to put a burden on, be burdensome.
ORIGIN: From epi and bareo; to be heavy upon, i.e. (pecuniarily) to be expensive to; figuratively, to be severe towards.

DEFINITION: to place upon (a horse, mule).
ORIGIN: From epi and a reduplicated derivative of the base of basis (compare anabibazo); to cause to mount (an animal).

BDAG.en: to put someone on something, cause someone to mount; put on, place Jesus on the colt
BDAG.pt: colocar alguém sobre algo, fazer alguém montar; pôr em, colocar Jesus sobre o jumentinho

DEFINITION: to look with favor on, regard.
ORIGIN: From epi and blepo; to gaze at (with favor, pity or partiality).
USAGE: look upon, regard, have respect to.

BDAG.en: to look intently, look, gaze (of God into the depths); pay close attention to, show special respect for, gaze upon; look attentively at, with implication of personal concern for someone, look upon (of God’s loving care)
BDAG.pt: olhar fixamente, olhar, fitar (de Deus nas profundezas); prestar atenção, demonstrar respeito especial, fitar; olhar atentamente, com implicação de preocupação pessoal por alguém, olhar (do cuidado amoroso de Deus)

DEFINITION: that which is put on, a patch.
ORIGIN: From epiballo; a patch.

BDAG.en: a piece of cloth used to repair a hole in clothing, a patch
BDAG.pt: um pedaço de pano usado para remendar um buraco na roupa, um remendo

DEFINITION: to cry out to or against.
ORIGIN: From epi and boao; to exclaim against.

BDAG.en: to make a loud utterance, cry out loudly (of an aroused mob), yell, shout
BDAG.pt: fazer uma declaração em voz alta, gritar alto (de uma multidão agitada), bradar, gritar

DEFINITION: a plot, design against.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of epi and boulomai; a plan against someone, i.e. A plot.

BDAG.en: a secret plan to do something evil or cause harm, a plot against someone
BDAG.pt: um plano secreto para fazer algo maligno ou causar dano, uma conspiração contra alguém

DEFINITION: to take to wife after, marry a deceased brother's wife.
ORIGIN: From epi and a derivative of gamos; to form affinity with, i.e. (specially) in a levirate way.

BDAG.en: to become related by marriage, then marry as next of kin, usually brother-in-law of levirate marriage
BDAG.pt: tornar-se parente por casamento, depois casar como parente mais próximo, geralmente cunhado em casamento levirato

DEFINITION: (a) on the earth, belonging to the earth (as opposed to the sky), (b) in a spiritual sense, belonging to the earthly sphere, earthly (as opposed to heavenly).
ORIGIN: From epi and ge; worldly (physically or morally).

BDAG.en: pertaining to what is characteristic of the earth as opposed to heavenly, earthly (as adj. or subst.); pertaining to earthly things, with implication of personal gratification, worldly things
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que é característico da terra em oposição ao celestial, terreno (como adjetivo ou substantivo); pertencente a coisas terrenas, com implicação de gratificação pessoal, coisas mundanas

DEFINITION: to arise, spring up, arrive, come on.
ORIGIN: From epi and ginomai; to arrive upon, i.e. Spring up (as a wind).

BDAG.en: to happen, with implication of existence of a new condition, come to pass, of wind come up, of the night come on
BDAG.pt: acontecer, com implicação de existência de uma nova condição, ocorrer, de vento surgir, de a noite cair

DEFINITION: to come to know by directing attention to him or it, to perceive, discern, recognize; aor: to found out.
ORIGIN: From epi and ginosko; to know upon some mark, i.e. Recognize; by implication, to become fully acquainted with, to acknowledge.

BDAG.en: generally ‘know, understand, recognize’; to have knowledge of something or someone completely; to ascertain or gain information about something, learn, find out, notice, perceive, learn of, ascertain; to connect present information or awareness with what was known before, acknowledge acquaintance with, recognize, know again; to indicate that one values the person of another, acknowledge, give recognition to; to come to an understanding of, understand, know
BDAG.pt: geralmente 'saber, compreender, reconhecer'; ter conhecimento de algo ou alguém completamente; apurar ou obter informação sobre algo, aprender, descobrir, notar, perceber, tomar conhecimento de, apurar; conectar informação ou consciência presente com o que era conhecido antes, reconhecer familiaridade, reconhecer, conhecer de novo; indicar que se valoriza a pessoa de outro, reconhecer, dar reconhecimento a; chegar a uma compreensão de, compreender, saber

DEFINITION: knowledge of a particular point (directed towards a particular object); perception, discernment, recognition, intuition.
ORIGIN: From epiginosko; recognition, i.e. (by implication) full discernment, acknowledgement.

BDAG.en: knowledge, recognition in our lit. limited to transcendent and moral matters
BDAG.pt: conhecimento, reconhecimento, limitado em nossa literatura a assuntos transcendentais e morais

DEFINITION: an inscription, title, label.
ORIGIN: From epigrapho; an inscription.

BDAG.en: inscription, superscription of the ‘titulus’ fastened to a cross; ordinarily of a document incised on stone, but also of identifying notices on any kind of material
BDAG.pt: inscrição, sobrescrito do 'título' fixado a uma cruz; ordinariamente de um documento gravado em pedra, mas também de avisos de identificação em qualquer tipo de material

DEFINITION: to write upon, inscribe, imprint a mark on.
ORIGIN: From epi and grapho; to inscribe (physically or mentally).

BDAG.en: to form letters or words on any kind of surface, write on/in a lit.; to enter a name into a record, to record; fig. to be engaged in a work; Enroll
BDAG.pt: formar letras ou palavras em qualquer tipo de superfície, escrever em; inserir um nome em um registro, registrar; fig. estar engajado em um trabalho; alistar

DEFINITION: to show, display, point out, indicate; to prove, demonstrate.
ORIGIN: From epi and deiknuo; to exhibit (physically or mentally).

BDAG.en: to cause to be seen, show, point out; to claim a characteristic or quality for something, represent; to demonstrate that something is true, demonstrate, show
BDAG.pt: fazer ver, mostrar, apontar; reivindicar uma característica ou qualidade para algo, representar; demonstrar que algo é verdadeiro, demonstrar, mostrar

DEFINITION: to accept as true, to receive besides.
ORIGIN: From epi and dechomai; to admit (as a guest or (figuratively) teacher).

BDAG.en: to receive into one’s presence in a friendly manner, receive, welcome (with nuance of diplomatic courtesy); to acknowledge receptively, accept=not reject
BDAG.pt: receber em sua presença de maneira amigável, receber, dar as boas-vindas (com nuance de cortesia diplomática); reconhecer receptivamente, aceitar=não rejeitar

DEFINITION: to sojourn, be resident (temporarily, in a foreign city).
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and demos; to make oneself at home, i.e. (by extension) to reside (in a foreign country).

BDAG.en: to stay in a place as a stranger or visitor, be in town, stay; to go to the place where one normally lives, return home
BDAG.pt: permanecer em um lugar como estrangeiro ou visitante, estar na cidade, ficar; ir ao lugar onde se mora normalmente, voltar para casa

DEFINITION: to make an additional testamentary disposition, to furnish with additions.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and diatasso; to appoint besides, i.e. Supplement (as a codicil).

BDAG.en: to add to, with implication of supplementary or modifying instructions, legal t.t. add a codicil to a will
BDAG.pt: adicionar a, com a implicação de instruções suplementares ou modificadoras, termo legal: adicionar um codicilo a um testamento

DEFINITION: (a) trans: to hand in, give up, (b) intrans: to give way (to the wind).
ORIGIN: From epi and didomi; to give over (by hand or surrender).
USAGE: deliver unto, give, let (+ (her drive)), offer.

BDAG.en: 1 to make a transfer of someth., give, hand over, deliver; 2 to yield control of someth., give up/over, surrender
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer uma transferência de algo, dar, entregar; 2 ceder o controle de algo, entregar/render

DEFINITION: to set in order besides, put in order, correct.
ORIGIN: From epi and a derivative of orthos; to straighten further, i.e. (figuratively) arrange additionally.

BDAG.en: set right or correct in addition (to what has already been corrected)
BDAG.pt: corrigir ou emendar adicionalmente (ao que já foi corrigido)

DEFINITION: to sink, set, set during, go down.
ORIGIN: From epi and duno; to set fully (as the sun).

BDAG.en: to sink down, set (upon), esp. of the apparent movement of the sun when it ‘sets’
BDAG.pt: afundar, pôr-se (sobre), especialmente do movimento aparente do sol quando ele 'se põe'

DEFINITION: considerateness, forbearance, fairness, gentleness, mildness.
ORIGIN: From epieikes; suitableness, i.e. (by implication) equity, mildness.

BDAG.en: the quality of making allowances despite facts that might suggest reason for a different reaction, clemency, gentleness, graciousness, courtesy, indulgence, tolerance
BDAG.pt: a qualidade de fazer concessões apesar dos fatos que poderiam sugerir razão para uma reação diferente, clemência, gentileza, graça, cortesia, indulgência, tolerância

DEFINITION: gentle, mild, forbearing, fair, reasonable, moderate.
ORIGIN: From epi and eiko; appropriate, i.e. (by implication) mild.

BDAG.en: not insisting on every right of letter of law or custom, yielding, gentle, kind, courteous, tolerant
BDAG.pt: não insistir em todo direito da letra da lei ou costume, condescendente, gentil, bondoso, cortês, tolerante

DEFINITION: to seek after, desire, search for, make inquiries about.
ORIGIN: From epi and zeteo; to search (inquire) for; intensively, to demand, to crave.

BDAG.en: to try to find out something, search for, seek after a lit.; inquire, want to know; discuss, debate, dispute; to be seriously interested in or have a strong desire for a wish, wish for
BDAG.pt: tentar descobrir algo, procurar, buscar; inquirir, querer saber; discutir, debater, disputar; estar seriamente interessado ou ter um forte desejo por um desejo, desejar

DEFINITION: at the point of death, condemned to death.
ORIGIN: From epi and thanatos; doomed to death.

BDAG.en: pert. to being condemned to death, sentenced to death
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser condenado à morte, sentenciado à morte

DEFINITION: a laying on; an attack, assault.
ORIGIN: From epitithemi; an imposition (of hands officially).

BDAG.en: the superimposing of something on something, laying on (so Plut.) of hands
BDAG.pt: a superposição de algo sobre algo, imposição (como em Plutarco) de mãos

DEFINITION: to long for, covet, lust after, set the heart upon.
ORIGIN: From epi and thumos; to set the heart upon, i.e. Long for (rightfully or otherwise).

BDAG.en: 1 to have a strong desire to do or secure someth., desire, long for; 2 to have sexual interest in someone, desire
BDAG.pt: 1 ter um forte desejo de fazer ou obter algo, desejar, ansiar; 2 ter interesse sexual em alguém, desejar

DEFINITION: an eager desirer of.
ORIGIN: From epithumeo.

BDAG.en: one who desires, also in a pejorative sense, desirous of evil, do not be lustful
BDAG.pt: aquele que deseja, também em sentido pejorativo, desejoso do mal, não sejas cobiçoso

DEFINITION: desire, eagerness for, inordinate desire, lust.
ORIGIN: From epithumeo; a longing (especially for what is forbidden).

BDAG.en: a great desire for something, desire, longing, craving; desire for something forbidden or simply inordinate, craving, lust; of sexual desire
BDAG.pt: um grande desejo por algo, desejo, anseio, ânsia; desejo por algo proibido ou simplesmente desordenado, cobiça, luxúria; de desejo sexual

DEFINITION: to sit upon, cause to sit upon.
ORIGIN: From epi and kathizo; to seat upon.

BDAG.en: 1 sit or sit down (on) intr.; 2 set or put upon
BDAG.pt: 1 sentar ou sentar-se (sobre) intransitivo; 2 colocar ou pôr sobre

DEFINITION: (a) to call (name) by a supplementary (additional, alternative) name, (b) mid: to call upon, appeal to, address.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and kaleo; to entitle; by implication, to invoke (for aid, worship, testimony, decision, etc.).

BDAG.en: to call on, invoke for someth.; to address or characterize someone by a special term, call, give a surname; a request put to a higher judicial authority for review of a decision in a lower court, appeal; to invoke in an oath, call on someone as a witness
BDAG.pt: invocar, chamar em auxílio para algo; dirigir-se a ou caracterizar alguém com um termo especial, chamar, dar um sobrenome; um recurso submetido a uma autoridade judicial superior para revisão de uma decisão de um tribunal inferior, apelação; invocar em um juramento, chamar alguém como testemunha

DEFINITION: a covering, cloak, veil, pretext.
ORIGIN: From epikalupto; a covering, i.e. (figuratively) pretext.

BDAG.en: a stratagem for concealing something, cover, veil
BDAG.pt: uma estratagema para ocultar algo, cobertura, véu

DEFINITION: to put a cover on, cover up.
ORIGIN: From epi and kalupto; to conceal, i.e. (figuratively) forgive.

BDAG.en: to hide from view by covering, then by fig. extension as synonym for ‘forgive’ cover up
BDAG.pt: esconder da vista cobrindo, depois por extensão figurada como sinônimo de 'perdoar' encobrir

DEFINITION: on whom a curse has been invoked, accursed, doomed to destruction.
ORIGIN: From epi and a derivative of kataraomai; imprecated, i.e. Execrable.

BDAG.en: pert. to being under divine condemnation, cursed
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao estar sob condenação divina, amaldiçoado

DEFINITION: (a) dat: to be placed upon, be laid upon, lie upon, be imposed; to press upon, (b) absol: to press hard, be insistent, insist.
ORIGIN: From epi and keimai; to rest upon (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: impose, be instant, (be) laid (there-, up-)on, (when) lay (on), lie (on), press upon.

BDAG.en: to be at or in a place in contact with a surface, lie upon; to act upon through force or pressure, be urgent; to have the force of obligation, be imposed, be incumbent; keep on doing something, be urgent about; exist as possibility, be open
BDAG.pt: estar em ou num lugar em contato com uma superfície, jazar sobre; agir através de força ou pressão, ser urgente; ter a força de obrigação, ser imposto, ser incumbente; continuar a fazer algo, ser insistente sobre; existir como possibilidade, estar aberto

DEFINITION: an Epicurean, one who holds the tenets of Epicurus.
ORIGIN: From Epikouros (compare epikouria) (a noted philosopher); an Epicurean or follower of Epicurus.

BDAG.en: an Epicurean, a follower of Epicurus
BDAG.pt: um Epicurista, um seguidor de Epicuro

DEFINITION: succor (against foes), help, aid, assistance.
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and a (prolonged) form of the base of korasion (in the sense of servant); assistance.

BDAG.en: aid, help (implied)
BDAG.pt: auxílio, ajuda (implícito)

DEFINITION: to decree, give sentence, decide.
ORIGIN: From epi and krino; to adjudge.

BDAG.en: to come to a decision in a matter, decide, determine
BDAG.pt: chegar a uma decisão sobre uma questão, decidir, determinar

DEFINITION: to lay hold of, take hold of, seize (sometimes with beneficent, sometimes with hostile, intent).
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and lambano; to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively).
USAGE: catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on).

BDAG.en: to make the motion of grasping or taking hold of someth., take hold of, grasp, catch, sometimes w. violence; to take into custody, arrest; to pounce on someth. compromising, catch; take hold of in order to make one’s own, take hold of; be concerned with/about
BDAG.pt: fazer o movimento de agarrar ou tomar posse de algo, pegar, agarrar, capturar, às vezes com violência; tomar sob custódia, prender; avançar sobre algo comprometedor, capturar; pegar para fazer seu, tomar posse de; importar-se com/sobre

DEFINITION: to forget, neglect.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and lanthano; to lose out of mind; by implication, to neglect.

BDAG.en: to not have remembrance of someth., forget; to be inattentive to, neglect, overlook, care nothing about
BDAG.pt: não ter lembrança de algo, esquecer; ser desatento a, negligenciar, ignorar, não se importar com

DEFINITION: to call; mid: to choose for myself; pass: to be named.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and lego; to surname, select.

BDAG.en: to add someth. by way of identification, call/name (in addition); choose, select
BDAG.pt: adicionar algo como identificação, chamar/nomear (adicionalmente); escolher, selecionar

DEFINITION: to fail, fall short.
ORIGIN: From epi and leipo; to leave upon, i.e. (figuratively) to be insufficient for.

BDAG.en: ‘leave behind’, hence w. acc. as obj. also w. the mng. to not be enough, fail
BDAG.pt: ‘deixar para trás’, daí com acusativo como objeto também com o sentido de não ser suficiente, falhar

DEFINITION: forgetfulness, oblivion.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of epilanthanomai; negligence.

BDAG.en: forgetfulness
BDAG.pt: esquecimento

DEFINITION: remaining, that is left over, still left.
ORIGIN: From epi and loipoy; left over, i.e. Remaining.

BDAG.en: pert. to a part that remains from a whole, left, remaining
BDAG.pt: pertencente a uma parte que resta de um todo, restante, que sobrou

DEFINITION: solution, explanation, interpretation; release.
ORIGIN: From epiluo; explanation, i.e. Application.

BDAG.en: 'a setting free from something', then the act or process of explaining, explanation, interpretation
BDAG.pt: 'uma libertação de algo', depois o ato ou processo de explicar, explicação, interpretação

DEFINITION: to loose, release; to solve, settle, explain, interpret, decide.
ORIGIN: From epi and luo; to solve further, i.e. (figuratively) to explain, decide.

BDAG.en: to clarify something, explain, interpret; to come to a conclusion about a difficult matter, resolve, decide, settle (passive, of a dispute)
BDAG.pt: clarificar algo, explicar, interpretar; chegar a uma conclusão sobre um assunto difícil, resolver, decidir, assentar (passivo, de uma disputa)

DEFINITION: to testify earnestly, bear witness to.
ORIGIN: From epi and martureo; to attest further, i.e. Corroborate.

BDAG.en: to affirm that something is true, bear witness, attest
BDAG.pt: afirmar que algo é verdadeiro, testemunhar, atestar

DEFINITION: attention, care.
ORIGIN: From epimeleomai; carefulness, i.e. Kind attention (hospitality).

BDAG.en: careful attention displayed in discharge of obligation or responsibility, care, attention
BDAG.pt: atenção cuidadosa demonstrada no cumprimento de obrigação ou responsabilidade, cuidado, atenção

DEFINITION: to take care of, attend to.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and the same as melo; to care for (physically or otherwise).

BDAG.en: care for, take care of
BDAG.pt: cuidar de, tomar conta de

DEFINITION: carefully, diligently.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of epimeleomai; carefully.

BDAG.en: carefully, diligently
BDAG.pt: cuidadosamente, diligentemente

DEFINITION: (a) to remain, tarry, (b) to remain in, persist in.
ORIGIN: From epi and meno; to stay over, i.e. Remain (figuratively, persevere).

BDAG.en: to remain at or in the same place for a period of time, stay, remain; to continue in an activity or state, continue, persist (in), persevere
BDAG.pt: permanecer no ou em um mesmo lugar por um período de tempo, ficar, permanecer; continuar em uma atividade ou estado, continuar, persistir (em), perseverar

DEFINITION: to nod to, assent to, consent.
ORIGIN: From epi and neuo; to nod at, i.e. (by implication) to assent.

BDAG.en: give consent (by a nod)
BDAG.pt: dar consentimento (com um aceno)

DEFINITION: thought, purpose, design, intent.
ORIGIN: From epi and nous; attention of the mind, i.e. (by implication) purpose.

BDAG.en: the result of a thought process, thought, conception; inventiveness; intent
BDAG.pt: o resultado de um processo de pensamento, pensamento, concepção; inventividade; intenção

DEFINITION: to take an oath, swear falsely.
ORIGIN: From epiorkos; to commit perjury.

BDAG.en: to swear that something is true when one knows it is false, swear falsely, perjure oneself; to fail to do what one has promised under oath, break one’s oath
BDAG.pt: jurar que algo é verdade quando se sabe que é falso, jurar falsamente, perjurar-se; deixar de cumprir o que foi prometido sob juramento, quebrar o juramento

DEFINITION: sworn falsely, a perjurer.
ORIGIN: From epi and horkos; on oath, i.e. (falsely) a forswearer.

BDAG.en: perjurer
BDAG.pt: juramentador falso, perjuro

DEFINITION: following, next.
ORIGIN: Feminine singular participle of a comparative of epi and heimi (to go); supervening, i.e. (hemera or nux being expressed or implied) the ensuing day or night.

BDAG.en: the next day
BDAG.pt: o dia seguinte

DEFINITION: for the morrow, necessary, sufficient.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the same as epiousa; tomorrow's; but more probably from epi and a derivative of the present participle feminine of eimi; for subsistence, i.e. Needful.

BDAG.en: daily bread (as used in the Lord’s Prayer, variously interpreted)
BDAG.pt: pão nosso de cada dia (como usado na oração do Senhor, várias vezes interpretado)

DEFINITION: to fall upon, press upon, light upon, come over.
ORIGIN: From epi and pipto; to embrace (with affection) or seize (with more or less violence; literally or figuratively).
USAGE: fall into (on, upon) lie on, press upon.

BDAG.en: fall upon, press upon (causing damage); make contact approach impetuously/eagerly; to happen to, befall, of extraordinary events and misfortunes: come upon
BDAG.pt: cair sobre, pressionar sobre (causando dano); fazer contato aproximando-se impetuosamente/com avidez; acontecer a, sobrevir, de eventos e infortúnios extraordinários: vir sobre

DEFINITION: to strike at, to rebuke (with words).
ORIGIN: From epi and plesso; to chastise, i.e. (with words) to upbraid.

BDAG.en: strike at, rebuke, reprove
BDAG.pt: golpear, repreender, reprovar

DEFINITION: choke.
ORIGIN: From epi and pnigo; to throttle upon, i.e. (figuratively) overgrow.

DEFINITION: to long for, strain after, desire greatly, have affection for.
ORIGIN: From epi and potheo (to yearn); to dote upon, i.e. Intensely crave possession (lawfully or wrongfully).

BDAG.en: to have a strong desire for someth., with implication of need, long for, desire
BDAG.pt: ter um forte desejo por algo, com implicação de necessidade, ansiar, desejar

DEFINITION: eager longing (desire), strong affection.
ORIGIN: From epipotheo; a longing for.

BDAG.en: yearning desire for, longing
BDAG.pt: desejo ardente, anseio

DEFINITION: longed for, missed, greatly desired.
ORIGIN: From epi and a derivative of the latter part of epipotheo; yearned upon, i.e. Greatly loved.

BDAG.en: pert. to being earnestly desired, longed for, desired
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que é ardentemente desejado, ansiado, desejado

DEFINITION: longing, eager desire.
ORIGIN: From epipotheo; intense longing.

BDAG.en: longing, desire
BDAG.pt: anseio, desejo

DEFINITION: to travel, journey (to).
ORIGIN: From epi and poreuomai; to journey further, i.e. Travel on (reach).

BDAG.en: be on one’s way to, go/journey to
BDAG.pt: estar a caminho de, ir/jornada para

DEFINITION: to sew upon.
ORIGIN: From epi and the base of rhaphis; to stitch upon, i.e. Fasten with the needle.

DEFINITION: to throw (cast) (upon), as of cares.
ORIGIN: From epi and rhipto; to throw upon (literally or figuratively).

DEFINITION: bearing a mark, notable.
ORIGIN: From epi and some form of the base of semaino; remarkable, i.e. (figuratively) eminent.

BDAG.en: 1. of exceptional quality, splendid, prominent, outstanding 2. Also in a bad sense: notorious
BDAG.pt: 1. de qualidade excepcional, esplêndido, proeminente, notável 2. Também em sentido negativo: notório

DEFINITION: provision, nourishment, food.
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and a derivative of sitos; a provisioning, i.e. (concretely) food.

BDAG.en: provisions (as stock of food)
BDAG.pt: provisões (como estoque de alimentos)

DEFINITION: to look upon, visit, look out, select.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from epi and the base of skopos; to inspect, i.e. (by implication) to select; by extension, to go to see, relieve.

BDAG.en: 1. to make a careful inspection, look at, examine, inspect 2. to go to see a pers. with helpful intent, visit 3. to exercise oversight in behalf of, look after, make an appearance to help, of divine oversight
BDAG.pt: 1. fazer uma inspeção cuidadosa, olhar, examinar, inspecionar 2. ir ver uma pessoa com intenção de ajudar, visitar 3. exercer supervisão em favor, cuidar, fazer uma aparição para ajudar, de supervisão divina

DEFINITION: to raise a tent (over), dwell, spread a tabernacle over.
ORIGIN: From epi and skenoo; to tent upon, i.e. (figuratively) abide with.

BDAG.en: to use a place for lodging, take up quarters, take up one’s abode
BDAG.pt: usar um lugar como alojamento, pernoitar, estabelecer residência

DEFINITION: to overshadow, envelop.
ORIGIN: From epi and a derivative of skia; to cast a shade upon, i.e. (by analogy) to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence.

BDAG.en: to cause a darkened effect by interposing someth. between a source of light and an object, overshadow, cast a shadow; to cause a darkening, cover (mostly used for divine activity such as a cloud indicating God's presence)
BDAG.pt: causar um efeito de escurecimento ao interpor algo entre uma fonte de luz e um objeto, sombrear, projetar uma sombra; causar um escurecimento, cobrir (usado principalmente para atividade divina, como uma nuvem que indica a presença de Deus)

DEFINITION: to exercise oversight, care for, visit.
ORIGIN: From epi and skopeo; to oversee; by implication, to beware.

BDAG.en: to give attention to, look at, take care, see to it; to accept responsibility for the care of someone, oversee, care for; in a Christian sense, of the activity of church officials, be an overseer
BDAG.pt: dar atenção, olhar, tomar cuidado, providenciar; aceitar a responsabilidade pelo cuidado de alguém, supervisionar, cuidar; em sentido cristão, da atividade dos oficiais da igreja, ser um supervisor

DEFINITION: (a) visitation (of judgment), (b) oversight, supervision, overseership.
ORIGIN: From episkeptomai; inspection (for relief); by implication, superintendence; specially, the Christian "episcopate".
USAGE: the office of a "bishop", bishoprick, visitation.

BDAG.en: the act of watching over with special ref. to being present, visitation (of divine activity, salutary or unpleasant); position of responsibility, position, assignment; engagement in oversight, supervision, of leaders of Christian communities
BDAG.pt: o ato de vigiar, com referência especial à presença, visitação (de atividade divina, salutar ou desagradável); posição de responsabilidade, cargo, incumbência; envolvimento na supervisão, fiscalização, de líderes de comunidades cristãs

DEFINITION: (used as an official title in civil life), overseer, supervisor, ruler, especially used with reference to the supervising function exercised by an elder or presbyter of a church or congregation.
ORIGIN: From epi and skopos (in the sense of episkopeo); a superintendent, i.e. Christian officer in genitive case charge of a (or the) church (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: one who watches over, guardian; one who has the responsibility of safeguarding or seeing to it that someth. is done in the correct way, guardian (of Christ: guardian of souls); one who has a definite function or fixed office of guardianship and related activity within a group (including religious groups); the term was taken over in Christian communities in ref. to one who served as overseer or supervisor
BDAG.pt: aquele que vigia, guardião; aquele que tem a responsabilidade de salvaguardar ou garantir que algo seja feito da maneira correta, guardião (de Cristo: guardião das almas); aquele que tem uma função definida ou um ofício fixo de guarda e atividade relacionada dentro de um grupo (incluindo grupos religiosos); o termo foi adotado nas comunidades cristãs em referência àquele que servia como supervisor ou fiscal

DEFINITION: (lit: to draw over), mid: to become as uncircumcised.
ORIGIN: From epi and spao; to draw over, i.e. (with akrobustia implied) efface the mark of circumcision (by recovering with the foreskin).

DEFINITION: to know, know of, understand.
ORIGIN: Apparently a middle voice of ephistemi (with nous implied); to put the mind upon, i.e. Comprehend, or be acquainted with.

BDAG.en: to gain a firm mental grasp of something, understand; to acquire information about something, know, be acquainted with.
BDAG.pt: obter um firme domínio mental de algo, compreender; adquirir informação sobre algo, saber, estar familiarizado com.

DEFINITION: master, teacher, chief, commander.
ORIGIN: From epi and a presumed derivative of histemi; an appointee over, i.e. Commander (teacher).

BDAG.en: master (used as a title addressed to Jesus, nearly always by the disciples)
BDAG.pt: mestre (usado como um título dirigido a Jesus, quase sempre pelos discípulos)

DEFINITION: to send a message (by letter).
ORIGIN: From epi and stello; to enjoin (by writing), i.e. (genitive case) to communicate by letter (for any purpose).

BDAG.en: to send something to, inform/instruct by letter, also simply write.
BDAG.pt: enviar algo para, informar/instruir por carta, também simplesmente escrever.

DEFINITION: skillful, experienced, knowing.
ORIGIN: From epistamai; intelligent.

BDAG.en: pert. to being knowledgeable in a way that makes one effectual in the exercise of such knowledge, expert, learned, understanding.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser conhecedor de uma forma que o torne eficaz no exercício desse conhecimento, perito, erudito, entendido.

DEFINITION: to prop up, uphold, support, confirm, make stronger.
ORIGIN: From epi and sterizo; to support further, i.e. Reestablish.

BDAG.en: to cause someone to become stronger or more firm, strengthen, in our lit. of believers in connection with their commitment and resolve to remain true, esp. in the face of troubles
BDAG.pt: fazer com que alguém se torne mais forte ou mais firme, fortalecer, na nossa literatura de crentes em conexão com seu compromisso e resolução de permanecerem fiéis, especialmente diante de problemas

DEFINITION: a letter, dispatch, epistle, message.
ORIGIN: From epistello; a written message.

BDAG.en: letter, epistle.
BDAG.pt: carta, epístola.

DEFINITION: to muzzle, silence, stop the mouth.
ORIGIN: From epi and stoma; to put something over the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) to silence.

BDAG.en: to put something on the mouth, fig., to silence someone; also probably bridle, hinder, prevent
BDAG.pt: pôr algo na boca, figurado, silenciar alguém; também provavelmente refrear, impedir, prevenir

DEFINITION: (a) trans: to turn (back) to (towards), (b) intrans: to turn (back) (to [towards]); to come to myself.
ORIGIN: From epi and strepho; to revert (literally, figuratively or morally).

BDAG.en: to turn to; 1. to return to a point where one has been, turn around, go back; 2. to change direction, turn around; 3. to cause a person to change belief or course of conduct, turn (active transitive); 4. to change one’s mind or course of action, turn, return (intransitive active)
BDAG.pt: virar-se para; 1. retornar a um ponto onde se esteve, dar a volta, voltar; 2. mudar de direção, virar-se; 3. fazer com que uma pessoa mude de crença ou curso de conduta, converter (ativo transitivo); 4. mudar de opinião ou curso de ação, virar, retornar (ativo intransitivo)

DEFINITION: a turning (to God), conversion.
ORIGIN: From epistrepho; reversion, i.e. Morally, revolution.

BDAG.en: ‘turning (toward)’; 1. turning one’s attention to something, attention; 2. change of one’s way of thinking or believing, conversion
BDAG.pt: ‘virada (para)’; 1. voltar a atenção para algo, atenção; 2. mudança na forma de pensar ou crer, conversão

DEFINITION: to collect, gather together, assemble.
ORIGIN: From epi and sunago; to collect upon the same place.

BDAG.en: to bring together, gather (together)
BDAG.pt: reunir, ajuntar (junto)

DEFINITION: a gathering (collecting) together, assembling.
ORIGIN: From episunago; a complete collection; especially a Christian meeting (for worship).

BDAG.en: 1. a gathering together to or toward at some location, meeting, of a Christian group; 2. the action of assembling
BDAG.pt: 1. uma reunião para ou em direção a algum local, encontro, de um grupo cristão; 2. a ação de se reunir

DEFINITION: to run together again.
ORIGIN: From epi and suntrecho; to hasten together upon one place (or a particular occasion).

BDAG.en: run together of crowds
BDAG.pt: correrem juntos (referente a multidões)

DEFINITION: a gathering, concourse, tumult.
ORIGIN: From the middle voice of a compound of epi and sunistao; a conspiracy, i.e. Concourse (riotous or friendly).
USAGE: that which cometh upon, + raising up.

BDAG.en: a gathering together against established authority, uprising, disturbance, insurrection.
BDAG.pt: um ajuntamento contra a autoridade estabelecida, levante, perturbação, insurreição.

DEFINITION: dangerous, likely to fall.
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and sphallo (to trip); figuratively, insecure.

BDAG.en: pert. to causing mishap, unsafe, dangerous of a voyage in autumn.
BDAG.pt: relativo a causar infortúnio, inseguro, perigoso de uma viagem no outono.

DEFINITION: to persist, insist, be more urgent.
ORIGIN: From epi and ischuo; to avail further, i.e. (figuratively) insist stoutly.

BDAG.en: grow strong in the sense of having additional resources or being persistent in doing something, persist
BDAG.pt: fortalecer-se no sentido de ter recursos adicionais ou ser persistente em fazer algo, persistir

DEFINITION: to heap up, obtain a multitude of.
ORIGIN: From epi and soreuo; to accumulate further, i.e. (figuratively) seek additionally.

BDAG.en: ‘to pile up in addition’, then by fig. extension heap up
BDAG.pt: ‘acumular em adição’, então por extensão figurada amontoar

DEFINITION: instruction, command, order, authority.
ORIGIN: From epitasso; an injunction or decree; by implication, authoritativeness.

BDAG.en: authoritative directive, command, order, injunction; right or authority to command, authority.
BDAG.pt: diretiva autoritária, comando, ordem, injunção; direito ou autoridade para mandar, autoridade.

DEFINITION: to give order, command, charge.
ORIGIN: From epi and tasso; to arrange upon, i.e. Order.

BDAG.en: to command with authority, order, command.
BDAG.pt: ordenar com autoridade, ordenar, mandar.

DEFINITION: to complete, accomplish, perfect.
ORIGIN: From epi and teleo; to fulfill further (or completely), i.e. Execute; by implication, to terminate, undergo.

BDAG.en: to finish someth. begun, end, bring to an end, finish; to bring about a result according to plan or objective, complete, accomplish, perform, bring about; to cause someth. to happen as fulfillment of an objective or purpose, fulfill
BDAG.pt: terminar algo começado, finalizar, dar fim, concluir; concretizar um resultado de acordo com o plano ou objetivo, completar, realizar, efetuar, provocar; fazer com que algo aconteça como cumprimento de um objetivo ou propósito, realizar

DEFINITION: necessary, suitable, fit.
ORIGIN: From epitedes (enough); serviceable, i.e. (by implication) requisite.

BDAG.en: pert. to being made for an end or purpose, fit for, necessary.
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser feito para um fim ou propósito, apropriado para, necessário.

DEFINITION: to put, place upon, lay on; to add, give in addition.
ORIGIN: From epi and tithemi; to impose (in a friendly or hostile sense).
USAGE: add unto, lade, lay upon, put (up) on, set on (up), + surname, X wound.

BDAG.en: to place someth. on or transfer to (a place or object), lay/put upon; fig. inflict blows upon someone; bestow mercy upon someone; give someth. to someone; add; to set upon, attack, lay a hand on
BDAG.pt: colocar algo sobre ou transferir para (um lugar ou objeto), pousar/pôr sobre; figurado infligir golpes a alguém; conferir misericórdia a alguém; dar algo a alguém; acrescentar; atacar, assaltar, pôr a mão sobre

DEFINITION: to honor, to mete out due measure, to censure.
ORIGIN: From epi and timao; to tax upon, i.e. Censure or admonish; by implication, forbid.

BDAG.en: to express strong disapproval of someone, rebuke, reprove, censure also speak seriously, warn in order to prevent an action or bring one to an end; punish
BDAG.pt: expressar forte desaprovação a alguém, repreender, reprovar, censurar, também falar seriamente, advertir para prevenir uma ação ou trazê-la a um fim; punir

DEFINITION: punishment, penalty.
ORIGIN: From a compound of epi and time; properly, esteem, i.e. Citizenship; used (in the sense of epitimao) of a penalty.

BDAG.en: punishment
BDAG.pt: punição

DEFINITION: to turn to, commit, entrust; to allow, yield, permit.
ORIGIN: From epi and the base of trope; to turn over (transfer), i.e. Allow.
USAGE: give leave (liberty, license), let, permit, suffer.

BDAG.en: to allow someone to do someth., allow, permit; order, instruct
BDAG.pt: permitir que alguém faça algo, permitir, autorizar; ordenar, instruir

DEFINITION: power to decide, authority, commission.
ORIGIN: From epitrepo; permission, i.e. (by implication) full power.

BDAG.en: authorization to carry out an assignment, permission, a commission, full power
BDAG.pt: autorização para realizar uma tarefa, permissão, uma comissão, plenos poderes

DEFINITION: (a) (procurator) a steward, (b) (tutor) a guardian (appointed for an infant [under 14 perhaps] by the father or by a magistrate).
ORIGIN: From epi and tropos (in the sense of epitrope); a commissioner, i.e. Domestic manager, guardian.

BDAG.en: manager, foreman, steward; guardian
BDAG.pt: gerente, capataz, mordomo; guardião

DEFINITION: to attain, obtain, acquire.
ORIGIN: From epi and tugchano; to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) to attain.

BDAG.en: to be successful in achieving or gaining what one seeks, obtain, attain to, reach; obtain
BDAG.pt: ser bem-sucedido em alcançar ou obter o que se procura, conseguir, atingir, alcançar; obter

DEFINITION: to appear (as of a light in the heavens or from the heavens), shine upon.
ORIGIN: From epi and phaino; to shine upon, i.e. Become (literally) visible or (figuratively) known.

BDAG.en: to cause something to be seen, show; to provide illumination, give light to; to make one’s presence known, become apparent; show oneself, make an appearance.
BDAG.pt: fazer algo ser visto, mostrar; prover iluminação, dar luz; tornar a própria presença conhecida, tornar-se aparente; apresentar-se, fazer uma aparição.

DEFINITION: appearing, manifestation, glorious display.
ORIGIN: From epiphanes; a manifestation, i.e. (specially) the advent of Christ (past or future).

BDAG.en: 'appearing, appearance', especially the splendid appearance, as a technical term relating to transcendence it refers to a visible and often sudden manifestation of a hidden divinity; act of appearing, appearance (only of Christ’s appearing on earth, appearance in judgment); that which can ordinarily be seen, surface appearance.
BDAG.pt: 'aparecimento, aparência', especialmente a aparência esplêndida, como termo técnico referente à transcendência refere-se a uma manifestação visível e frequentemente súbita de uma divindade oculta; ato de aparecer, aparição (somente do aparecimento de Cristo na terra, aparição no juízo); aquilo que pode ser ordinariamente visto, aparência superficial.

DEFINITION: manifest, glorious, illustrious.
ORIGIN: From epiphaino; conspicuous, i.e. (figuratively) memorable.

BDAG.en: pert. to being resplendent, splendid, glorious, remarkable, probably suggesting light whose impact is esp. striking in its sudden appearance.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser resplandecente, esplêndido, glorioso, notável, provavelmente sugerindo luz cujo impacto é especialmente marcante em sua aparição súbita.

DEFINITION: to shine upon, give light to.
ORIGIN: A form of epiphaino; to illuminate (figuratively).

DEFINITION: to bring forward (against), impose, inflict.
ORIGIN: From epi and phero; to bear upon (or further), i.e. Adduce (personally or judicially (accuse, inflict)), superinduce.

BDAG.en: to bestow something on someone, bring, give, grant; bring something over and put it on someone, take to; to cause someone or something to undergo something adverse, bring (on/about), inflict; to add something on top of something, add; to bring charges or make accusations, bring, pronounce.
BDAG.pt: conceder algo a alguém, trazer, dar, outorgar; trazer algo sobre e pôr em alguém, levar a; fazer alguém ou algo sofrer algo adverso, trazer (sobre/ocasionar), infligir; adicionar algo em cima de algo, acrescentar; apresentar acusações ou fazer alegações, trazer, pronunciar.

DEFINITION: to call out, shout, clamor at.
ORIGIN: From epi and phoneo; to call at something, i.e. Exclaim.

BDAG.en: cry out (loudly) against someone; used with direct discourse following.
BDAG.pt: gritar (alto) contra alguém; usado com discurso direto a seguir.

DEFINITION: to dawn, be near commencing.
ORIGIN: A form of epiphauo; to begin to grow light.
USAGE: begin to dawn, X draw on.

BDAG.en: to grow towards or become daylight, shine forth, dawn, break, perhaps draw on (used for the Sabbath dawning or drawing on).
BDAG.pt: crescer em direção ou tornar-se dia, resplandecer, amanhecer, romper, talvez se aproximar (usado para o Sábado amanhecer ou se aproximar).

DEFINITION: to put one's hand to, to attempt.
ORIGIN: From epi and cheir; to put the hand upon, i.e. Undertake.

BDAG.en: set one’s hand to, endeavor, try (with infinitive); attempt something (with accusative); used of literary composition.
BDAG.pt: pôr a mão em, esforçar-se, tentar (com infinitivo); tentar algo (com acusativo); usado para composição literária.

DEFINITION: to pour upon.
ORIGIN: From epi and cheo (to pour).

BDAG.en: to cause to pour on or flow on, pour over, apply (something, e.g., oil and wine); to cause to flow into something, pour in (in the sense of add to something already contained in a vessel).
BDAG.pt: fazer derramar ou escorrer sobre, derramar sobre, aplicar (algo, ex: azeite e vinho); fazer escorrer para dentro de algo, despejar dentro (no sentido de adicionar a algo já contido em um recipiente).

DEFINITION: to supply, provide (perhaps lavishly), furnish.
ORIGIN: From epi and choregeo; to furnish besides, i.e. Fully supply, (figuratively) aid or contribute.

BDAG.en: to convey as a gift, give, grant; to provide (at one’s own expense), supply, furnish; to provide what is necessary for the well-being of another, support
BDAG.pt: transmitir como presente, dar, conceder; prover (às suas próprias custas), suprir, fornecer; prover o necessário para o bem-estar de outrem, sustentar

DEFINITION: supply, provision, equipment, support.
ORIGIN: From epichoregeo; contribution.

BDAG.en: assistance, support; a ligament that serves for support.
BDAG.pt: assistência, suporte; um ligamento que serve para suporte.

DEFINITION: to spread on, to anoint.
ORIGIN: From epi and chrio; to smear over.

BDAG.en: to apply a viscous substance, anoint, spread/smear (on); used of applying mud to eyes or applying seals to a stone.
BDAG.pt: aplicar uma substância viscosa, ungir, espalhar/barrar (sobre); usado para aplicar lama nos olhos ou aplicar selos em uma pedra.

DEFINITION: to build upon (above) a foundation.
ORIGIN: From epi and oikodomeo; to build upon, i.e. (figuratively) to rear up.

BDAG.en: to build something on something already built, build on to (of stones or building on a congregation); to engage in a building process of personal and corporate development, edify, build up/on.
BDAG.pt: construir algo sobre algo já construído, edificar sobre (de pedras ou construção de uma congregação); engajar-se em um processo de construção de desenvolvimento pessoal e corporativo, edificar, construir/aumentar.

DEFINITION: to force forward, run (a ship) aground.
ORIGIN: From epi and okello (to urge); to drive upon the shore, i.e. To beach a vessel.

BDAG.en: run aground (of a ship).
BDAG.pt: encalhar (de um navio).

DEFINITION: to name, impose a name on; pass: be named.
ORIGIN: From epi and onomazo; to name further, i.e. Denominate.

BDAG.en: call, name (used passively: you call yourself a Judean).
BDAG.pt: chamar, nomear (usado passivamente: você se chama judeu).

DEFINITION: to be an eyewitness of, behold, look upon.
ORIGIN: From epi and a derivative of optanomai; to inspect, i.e. Watch.

BDAG.en: to pay close attention to, watch, observe, see something (specifically conduct).
BDAG.pt: prestar atenção minuciosa, vigiar, observar, ver algo (especificamente a conduta).

DEFINITION: an eyewitness, spectator, looker-on.
ORIGIN: From epi and a presumed derivative of optanomai; a looker-on.

BDAG.en: one who sees to or attends to, with implication of careful scrutiny, a watchful observer; to have first-hand acquaintance with someth., with implication of special privilege, eyewitness (esp. as t.t. of the mysteries, to designate those who have been initiated into the highest grade of the mysteries)
BDAG.pt: aquele que cuida ou atende, com implicação de escrutínio cuidadoso, um observador vigilante; ter conhecimento em primeira mão de algo, com implicação de privilégio especial, testemunha ocular (especialmente como termo técnico dos mistérios, para designar aqueles que foram iniciados no mais alto grau dos mistérios)

DEFINITION: a word, so to speak.
ORIGIN: From epo; a word.

BDAG.en: word (used idiomatically, e.g., ὡς ἔ. εἰπεῖν, to qualify speech that might sound too assertive, so to speak, one might almost say; or perh. to effect a climax to use just the right word)
BDAG.pt: palavra (usada idiomaticamente, ex.: ὡς ἔ. εἰπεῖν, para qualificar um discurso que poderia soar muito assertivo, por assim dizer, poder-se-ia quase dizer; ou talvez para criar um clímax, usar a palavra certa)

DEFINITION: heavenly, celestial, in the heavenly sphere, the sphere of spiritual activities; met: divine, spiritual.
ORIGIN: From epi and ouranos; above the sky.

BDAG.en: generally 'heavenly'; 1 pert. to being in the sky or heavens as an astronomical phenomenon, celestial, heavenly; 2 pert. to being associated with a locale for transcendent things and beings, heavenly, in heaven (used as adj. or subst.)
BDAG.pt: geralmente 'celestial'; 1 relativo a estar no céu ou nos céus como um fenômeno astronômico, celeste, celestial; 2 relativo a estar associado a um local para coisas e seres transcendentes, celestial, no céu (usado como adjetivo ou substantivo)

DEFINITION: seven.
ORIGIN: A primary number; seven.

BDAG.en: seven (as a sacred number)
BDAG.pt: sete (como um número sagrado)

DEFINITION: seven times.
ORIGIN: Adverb from hepta; seven times.

BDAG.en: seven times (as a relatively large number)
BDAG.pt: sete vezes (como um número relativamente grande)

DEFINITION: seven thousand.
ORIGIN: From heptakis and chilioi; seven times a thousand.

BDAG.en: seven thousand
BDAG.pt: sete mil

DEFINITION: answer, bid, bring word, command.
ORIGIN: A primary verb (used only in the definite past tense, the others being borrowed from ereo, rheo, and phemi); to speak or say (by word or writing).
USAGE: answer, bid, bring word, call, command, grant, say (on), speak, tell. Compare lego.

DEFINITION: "beloved", Erastus, the name of two Christians.
ORIGIN: From erao (to love); beloved; Erastus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Erastus (a Christian at Corinth, designated as city treasurer; also a companion of Paul)
BDAG.pt: Erasto (um cristão em Corinto, designado como tesoureiro da cidade; também um companheiro de Paulo)

DEFINITION: to work, trade, perform, do, practice, commit, acquire by labor.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from ergon; to toil (as a task, occupation, etc.), (by implication) effect, be engaged in or with, etc.
USAGE: commit, do, labor for, minister about, trade (by), work.

BDAG.en: 1 to engage in activity that involves effort, work, intr. work, be active; Of financial enterprise: do business/trade with them; 2 to do or accomplish someth. through work, trans.; b practice, perform, officiate at; c bring about, give rise to as proceeds from work; d work (on); e work for/earn food
BDAG.pt: 1 engajar-se em atividade que envolve esforço, trabalhar, trabalhar intrinsecamente, ser ativo; Em empreendimento financeiro: negociar/fazer comércio com eles; 2 fazer ou realizar algo através do trabalho, trans.; b praticar, realizar, officiar em; c trazer à tona, gerar como rendimento do trabalho; d trabalhar (em); e trabalhar por/ganhar alimento

DEFINITION: working, activity, work, service, trade, business, gains of business, performance, practice.
ORIGIN: From ergates; occupation; by implication, profit, pains.

BDAG.en: 1 engagement in some activity or behavior with sustained interest, practice, pursuit of someth.; 2 manner of activity, working, function; 3 business activity, trade, business; 4 proceeds of work or activity profit, gain
BDAG.pt: 1 engajamento em alguma atividade ou comportamento com interesse sustentado, prática, busca de algo; 2 modo de atividade, funcionamento, função; 3 atividade comercial, comércio, negócio; 4 rendimento do trabalho ou atividade, lucro, ganho

DEFINITION: a field-laborer; then: a laborer, workman in general.
ORIGIN: From ergon; a toiler; figuratively, a teacher.

BDAG.en: one who is engaged in work, worker, laborer; in transf. sense, of apostles and teachers; one who effects someth. through work, a doer
BDAG.pt: aquele que está envolvido em trabalho, trabalhador, operário; em sentido transferido, de apóstolos e mestres; aquele que efetua algo através do trabalho, um realizador

DEFINITION: work, task, employment; a deed, action; that which is wrought or made, a work.
ORIGIN: From a primary (but obsolete) ergo (to work); toil (as an effort or occupation); by implication, an act.

BDAG.en: work; deed, action; manifestation, practical proof; deed, accomplishment (of God/Jesus, miracles; of humans, moral character); regular activity, work, occupation, task; product, undertaking, work (passive sense); thing, matter
BDAG.pt: trabalho; feito, ação; manifestação, prova prática; feito, realização (de Deus/Jesus, milagres; de humanos, caráter moral); atividade regular, trabalho, ocupação, tarefa; produto, empreendimento, obra (sentido passivo); coisa, assunto

DEFINITION: to stir up, arouse to anger, provoke, irritate, incite.
ORIGIN: From a presumed prolonged form of eris; to stimulate (especially to anger).

BDAG.en: to cause someone to react in a way that suggests acceptance of a challenge, arouse, provoke mostly in bad sense irritate, embitter; in a good sense of an encouraging example
BDAG.pt: causar em alguém uma reação que sugira aceitação de um desafio, despertar, provocar, na maioria das vezes em sentido negativo: irritar, amargurar; em sentido positivo, de um exemplo encorajador

DEFINITION: to stick fast, prop, fix firmly.
ORIGIN: Of obscure affinity; to prop, i.e. (reflexively) get fast.

BDAG.en: to stick in someth., jam fast, become fixed
BDAG.pt: fixar-se em algo, prender firmemente, ficar cravado

DEFINITION: (lit: to belch forth, hence) to utter, declare.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; to belch, i.e. (figuratively) to speak out.

BDAG.en: orig. ‘belch’, then to express forcefully someth. intelligible, utter, proclaim
BDAG.pt: originalmente 'arrotar', depois expressar com força algo inteligível, proferir, proclamar

DEFINITION: to search diligently, examine.
ORIGIN: Apparently from ereo (through the idea of inquiry); to seek, i.e. (figuratively) to investigate.

BDAG.en: see ἐραυνάω
BDAG.pt: ver ἐραυνάω

DEFINITION: (denoting speech in progress), (a) to say, speak; to mean, mention, tell, (b) to call, name, especially in the pass., (c) to tell, command.
ORIGIN: Probably a fuller form of rheo; an alternate for epo in certain tenses; to utter, i.e. Speak or say.

DEFINITION: a desert place, desert, uninhabited region.
ORIGIN: From eremos; solitude (concretely).

BDAG.en: uninhabited or lonely region, normally with sparse vegetation, desert
BDAG.pt: região desabitada ou solitária, normalmente com vegetação esparsa, deserto

DEFINITION: as an adj: deserted, desolate, waste; hence: the desert, to the east and south of Palestine; of a person: deserted, abandoned, desolate.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; lonesome, i.e. (by implication) waste (usually as a noun, chora being implied).

BDAG.en: as adj.: pert. to being in a state of isolation, isolated, desolate, deserted (of an area; of persons); as subst.: an uninhabited region or locality, desert, grassland, wilderness
BDAG.pt: como adjetivo: pertencente a um estado de isolamento, isolado, desolado, deserto (de uma área; de pessoas); como substantivo: uma região ou localidade desabitada, deserto, pastagem, ermo

DEFINITION: (a) to make desolate, bring to desolation, destroy, waste, (b) of a person: to strip, rob.
ORIGIN: From eremos; to lay waste (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: (bring to, make) desolate(-ion), come to nought.

BDAG.en: to make uninhabitable, lay waste, depopulate
BDAG.pt: tornar inabitável, devastar, despovoar

DEFINITION: a desolation, devastation.
ORIGIN: From eremoo; despoliation.

BDAG.en: state of being made uninhabitable, devastation, destruction, depopulation
BDAG.pt: estado de ser tornado inabitável, devastação, destruição, despovoamento

DEFINITION: to contend, dispute, wrangle, strive.
ORIGIN: From eris; to wrangle.

BDAG.en: quarrel, wrangle abs.
BDAG.pt: discutir, contender de forma absoluta

DEFINITION: (the seeking of followers and adherents by means of gifts, the seeking of followers, hence) ambition, rivalry, self-seeking; a feud, faction.
ORIGIN: Perhaps as the same as erethizo; properly, intrigue, i.e. (by implication) faction.

BDAG.en: strife, contentiousness, selfishness, selfish ambition. Pl. disputes or outbreaks of selfishness
BDAG.pt: luta, contenciosidade, egoísmo, ambição egoísta. Plural disputas ou surtos de egoísmo

DEFINITION: wool.
ORIGIN: Of obscure affinity; wool.

BDAG.en: wool
BDAG.pt: lã

DEFINITION: contention, strife, wrangling.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a quarrel, i.e. (by implication) wrangling.

BDAG.en: engagement in rivalry, esp. w. ref. to positions taken in a matter, strife, discord, contention; quarrels
BDAG.pt: envolvimento em rivalidade, especialmente com referência a posições assumidas em um assunto, discórdia, contenda; brigas

DEFINITION: a little young goat.
ORIGIN: From eriphos; a kidling, i.e. (genitive case) goat (symbolically, wicked person).

BDAG.en: kid, goat (diminutive of ἔριφος)
BDAG.pt: cabrito, cabra (diminutivo de ἔριφος)

DEFINITION: a young goat.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the same as erion (through the idea of hairiness); a kid or (genitive case) goat.

BDAG.en: kid, he-goat; (Pl.) goats
BDAG.pt: cabrito, bode; (Pl.) cabras

DEFINITION: Hermas, a Christian at Rome.
ORIGIN: Probably from Hermes; Hermas, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Hermas (a man's name)
BDAG.pt: Hermas (nome de homem)

DEFINITION: translation, interpretation, explanation.
ORIGIN: From the same as hermeneuo; translation.

BDAG.en: 1 capacity of doing translation, translation; 2 product of interpretive procedure, interpretation, exposition
BDAG.pt: 1 capacidade de fazer tradução, tradução; 2 produto de procedimento interpretativo, interpretação, exposição

DEFINITION: (a) to translate, explain, (b) to interpret the meaning of.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of Hermes (as the god of language); to translate.

BDAG.en: 1 to help someone understand a subject or matter by making it plain, explain, interpret; 2 to render words in a different language, translate
BDAG.pt: 1 ajudar alguém a entender um assunto ou matéria tornando-o claro, explicar, interpretar; 2 traduzir palavras em uma língua diferente

DEFINITION: (a) Hermes, the messenger and herald of the Greek gods, or rather the corresponding Lycaonian deity, (b) Hermes, a Roman Christian.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from ereo; Hermes, the name of the messenger of the Greek deities; also of a Christian.

BDAG.en: Hermes (the Greek god); (as a man’s name)
BDAG.pt: Hermes (o deus grego); (como nome de homem)

DEFINITION: "born of Hermes", Hermogenes, one who deserted Paul.
ORIGIN: From Hermes and ginomai; born of Hermes; Hermogenes, an apostate Christian.

BDAG.en: Hermogenes (a Christian fr. Asia)
BDAG.pt: Hermógenes (um cristão da Ásia)

DEFINITION: a creeping creature, reptile, especially a serpent.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of herpo (to creep); a reptile, i.e. (by Hebraism (compare remes)) a small animal.

BDAG.en: reptile; Esp. of a snake
BDAG.pt: réptil; Especialmente de uma serpente

DEFINITION: red.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; red, i.e. (with thalassa) the Red Sea.

BDAG.en: red (color of wine or blood) of roses, the Red Sea
BDAG.pt: vermelho (cor de vinho ou sangue) de rosas, o Mar Vermelho

DEFINITION: to come, go.

USAGE: accompany, appear, bring, come, enter, fall out, go, grow, X light, X next, pass, resort, be set.

BDAG.en: to move from one point to another, with focus on approach from the narrator’s perspective, come; of movement itself; come back, return; come before the judgment-seat of God; come in a hostile sense; to proceed on a course, with destination in view, go; to change place or position, with implication of being brought, be brought; to take place, come (of time or events); of making an appearance come before the public, appear
BDAG.pt: mover-se de um ponto a outro, com foco na aproximação da perspectiva do narrador, vir; do próprio movimento; voltar, retornar; comparecer diante do tribunal de Deus; vir em sentido hostil; prosseguir em um curso, com destino em vista, ir; mudar de lugar ou posição, com a implicação de ser trazido, ser trazido; ocorrer, acontecer (de tempo ou eventos); de fazer uma aparição vir à presença do público, aparecer

DEFINITION: (a) to ask (a question), question, (b) to request, make a request to, pray.
ORIGIN: Apparently from ereo (compare ereunao); to interrogate; by implication, to request.
USAGE: ask, beseech, desire, intreat, pray. Compare punthanomai.

BDAG.en: to put a query to someone, ask, ask a question; to ask for someth., ask, request
BDAG.pt: fazer uma pergunta a alguém, perguntar, fazer uma indagação; pedir algo, pedir, solicitar

DEFINITION: clothing, raiment, vestment, robe.
ORIGIN: From hennumi (to clothe); dress.

BDAG.en: clothing
BDAG.pt: vestimenta, roupa

DEFINITION: clothing, a garment.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of esthes; clothing (concretely).

DEFINITION: to eat, partake of food; met: to devour, consume (e.g. as rust does).
ORIGIN: Strengthened for a primary edo (to eat); used only in certain tenses, the rest being supplied by phago; to eat (usually literal).

BDAG.en: to take something in through the mouth, usually solids, but also liquids, eat; (used with other prep. expressions) eat with someone; (used absolutely) eat; (used with λαμβάνειν) receive and eat; (used with πίνω) to eat and drink (receive support, eat a meal, in contrast to fasting, ordinary daily activities, carefree/luxurious living)
BDAG.pt: ingerir algo pela boca, geralmente sólidos, mas também líquidos, comer; (usado com outras expressões preposicionais) comer com alguém; (usado absolutamente) comer; (usado com λαμβάνειν) receber e comer; (usado com πίνω) comer e beber (receber sustento, fazer uma refeição, em contraste com jejum, atividades diárias comuns, vida despreocupada/luxuosa)

DEFINITION: Esli, son of Naggai and father of Nahum.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (probably for Elyhow'eynay); Esli, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Esli, in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Esli, na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: are, be, have our being, have hope.

DEFINITION: a mirror, looking-glass (made of highly polished metal).
ORIGIN: From eis and a presumed derivative of optanomai; a mirror (for looking into).

BDAG.pt: espelho

DEFINITION: evening.
ORIGIN: Feminine of an adjective hesperos (evening); the eve (hora being implied).

DEFINITION: Hezron, son of Perez, father of Ram.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Chetsrown); Esrom (i.e. Chetsron), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Hezron, in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Hesrom, na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: be, have been, belong.

DEFINITION: are, belong, call, come, consist.
ORIGIN: Third person singular present indicative of eimi; he (she or it) is; also (with neuter plural) they are.
USAGE: are, be(-long), call, X can(-not), come, consisteth, X dure for a while, + follow, X have, (that) is (to say), make, meaneth, X must needs, + profit, + remaineth, + wrestle.

DEFINITION: be.
ORIGIN: Second person singular present imperative of eimi; be thou; also estosan es'-to-san, third person of the same let them be.

DEFINITION: last, at the last, finally, till the end.
ORIGIN: A superlative probably from echo (in the sense of contiguity); farthest, final (of place or time).
USAGE: ends of, last, latter end, lowest, uttermost.

BDAG.pt: geralmente 'último'; 1 pertencente a estar no limite mais distante de uma área, o mais distante, o último; 2 pertencente a ser o item final em uma série, o menor, o último no tempo; 3 pertencente à extrema distância em posição, valor ou situação, o último: o último, o menor, o mais insignificante

DEFINITION: extremely, utterly; to be at the extremity, to be in extremis, to be at the last grasp.
ORIGIN: Adverb from eschatos; finally, i.e. (with echo) at the extremity of life.

BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar no fim, finalmente; estar à beira da morte

DEFINITION: within, inside, with verbs either of rest or of motion; prep: within, to within, inside.
ORIGIN: From eis; inside (as preposition or adjective).

DEFINITION: (a) from within, from inside, (b) within, inside; with the article: the inner part, the inner element, (c) the mind, soul.
ORIGIN: From eso; from inside; also used as equivalent to eso (inside).

DEFINITION: inner; with the article: the part that is within.
