BDAG.en: inner (comparative of ἔσω)
BDAG.pt: interior (comparativo de ἔσω)

DEFINITION: a companion, comrade, friend.
ORIGIN: From etes (a clansman); a comrade.

BDAG.en: a person who has someth. in common with others and enjoys association, but not necessarily at the level of a φίλος or φίλη, comrade, companion, of a member of one’s group fellow-member; As a general form of address to someone whose name one does not know: my friend
BDAG.pt: uma pessoa que tem algo em comum com outros e desfruta de associação, mas não necessariamente ao nível de um amigo (φίλος ou φίλη), camarada, companheiro, de um membro do seu grupo, colega; Como uma forma geral de tratamento para alguém cujo nome não se sabe: meu amigo

DEFINITION: speaking another language; subst: one who speaks another language.
ORIGIN: From heteros and glossa; other- tongued, i.e. A foreigner.

BDAG.en: speaking a foreign language
BDAG.pt: falando uma língua estrangeira

DEFINITION: to teach different things, that is, different from the true or necessary teaching.
ORIGIN: From heteros and didaskalos; to instruct differently.

BDAG.en: to teach contrary to standard instruction, give divergent, i.e. divisive, instruction
BDAG.pt: ensinar contrariamente à instrução padrão, dar instrução divergente, ou seja, divisiva

DEFINITION: to be yoked with one different from myself, unequally yoked.
ORIGIN: From a compound of heteros and zugos; to yoke up differently, i.e. (figuratively) to associate discordantly.

BDAG.en: be unevenly yoked, be mismated (with someone)
BDAG.pt: estar desigualmente jugo, ser mal-acasalado (com alguém)

DEFINITION: (a) of two: another, a second, (b) other, different, (c) one's neighbor.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; (an-, the) other or different.
USAGE: altered, else, next (day), one, (an-)other, some, strange.

BDAG.en: other (distinct from some other item implied or mentioned); another (of two, or one of more than two); used interchangeably with ἄλλος; different in kind or class from what precedes
BDAG.pt: outro (distinto de algum outro item implícito ou mencionado); um outro (de dois, ou um de mais de dois); usado de forma intercambiável com ἄλλος; diferente em tipo ou classe do que precede

DEFINITION: otherwise, differently.
ORIGIN: Adverb from heteros; differently.

BDAG.en: differently, otherwise
BDAG.pt: de maneira diferente, de outro modo

DEFINITION: (a) of time: still, yet, even now, (b) of degree: even, further, more, in addition.
ORIGIN: Perhaps akin to etos; "yet," still (of time or degree).
USAGE: after that, also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any) longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet.

BDAG.en: yet, still (continuance); no longer (stopping); a little while longer (time not yet come); in addition, more (added number).
BDAG.pt: ainda, ainda (continuidade); não mais (parando); por mais um pouco de tempo (tempo ainda não chegado); além disso, mais (número adicionado).

DEFINITION: to make ready, prepare.
ORIGIN: From hetoimos; to prepare.
USAGE: prepare, provide, make ready. Compare kataskeuazo.

BDAG.en: to cause to be ready, put/keep in readiness, prepare (things, way, meal, place for someone).
BDAG.pt: fazer ficar pronto, pôr/manter em prontidão, preparar (coisas, caminho, refeição, lugar para alguém).

DEFINITION: foundation, firm footing; preparation, readiness.
ORIGIN: From hetoimazo; preparation.

BDAG.en: readiness, preparation.
BDAG.pt: prontidão, preparação.

DEFINITION: ready, prepared.
ORIGIN: From an old noun heteos (fitness); adjusted, i.e. Ready.

BDAG.en: ready, prepared (of things designed for a purpose; of persons).
BDAG.pt: pronto, preparado (de coisas destinadas a um propósito; de pessoas).

DEFINITION: readily.
ORIGIN: Adverb from hetoimos; in readiness.

BDAG.en: readily, be ready, be willing.
BDAG.pt: prontamente, estar pronto, estar disposto.

DEFINITION: a year.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a year.

BDAG.en: year.
BDAG.pt: ano.

DEFINITION: well, well done, good, rightly; also used as an exclamation.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a primary eus (good); (adverbially) well.

BDAG.en: well (as adverb, pert. to that which is good or beneficial, as applied to interpersonal relationship or experience); well done! excellent! (as interjection)
BDAG.pt: bem (como advérbio, referente ao que é bom ou benéfico, aplicado ao relacionamento interpessoal ou experiência); bem feito! excelente! (como interjeição)

DEFINITION: Eve, the first woman; wife of first man Adam.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Chavvah); Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first woman.

BDAG.en: Eve
BDAG.pt: Eva

DEFINITION: to bring good news, preach good tidings, with or without an object, expressing either the persons who receive the good news or the good news itself (the good news being sometimes expressed as a person).
ORIGIN: From eu and aggelos; to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel.
USAGE: declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel).

BDAG.en: bring good news, announce good news; mostly proclaim the divine message of salvation, proclaim the gospel; be proclaimed; have good news announced to one (of the gospel)
BDAG.pt: trazer boas novas, anunciar boas novas; principalmente proclamar a mensagem divina de salvação, proclamar o evangelho; ser proclamado; ter boas novas anunciadas a alguém (sobre o evangelho)

DEFINITION: the good news of the coming of the Messiah, the gospel; the gen. after it expresses sometimes the giver (God), sometimes the subject (the Messiah, etc.), sometimes the human transmitter (an apostle).
ORIGIN: From the same as euaggelizo; a good message, i.e. The gospel.

BDAG.en: good news (relating to God’s action in Jesus Christ); God’s good news to humans, good news as proclamation; details relating to the life and ministry of Jesus, good news of Jesus; a book dealing with the life and teaching of Jesus, a gospel account.
BDAG.pt: boas novas (relacionadas à ação de Deus em Jesus Cristo); boas novas de Deus para os humanos, boas novas como proclamação; detalhes relativos à vida e ministério de Jesus, boas novas de Jesus; um livro que trata da vida e ensinamento de Jesus, um relato evangélico.

DEFINITION: an evangelist, a missionary, bearer of good tidings.
ORIGIN: From euaggelizo; a preacher of the gospel.

BDAG.en: proclaimer of the gospel, evangelist
BDAG.pt: proclamador do evangelho, evangelista

DEFINITION: to give pleasure to, please (perhaps with the added idea of: rendering good service to).
ORIGIN: From euarestos; to gratify entirely.

BDAG.en: to do something or act in a manner that is pleasing or satisfactory, please, be pleasing; to experience pleasure, be pleased, take delight.
BDAG.pt: fazer algo ou agir de maneira agradável ou satisfatória, agradar, ser aprazível; experimentar prazer, ficar contente, deleitar-se.

DEFINITION: acceptable, well-pleasing (especially to God), grateful.
ORIGIN: From eu and arestos; fully agreeable.

BDAG.en: pleasing, acceptable (generally with reference to God, to whom something is acceptable).
BDAG.pt: agradável, aceitável (geralmente com referência a Deus, para quem algo é aceitável).

DEFINITION: acceptably, in a well-pleasing way.
ORIGIN: Adverb from euarestos; quite agreeably.

BDAG.en: in an acceptable manner.
BDAG.pt: de maneira aceitável.

DEFINITION: Eubulus, a Christian with Paul in Rome.
ORIGIN: From eu and boulomai; good-willer; Eubulus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Eubulus, a Christian in Rome; a presbyter in Corinth.
BDAG.pt: Eúbulo, um cristão em Roma; um presbítero em Corinto.

DEFINITION: (a) of noble birth, of high birth, (b) noble in nature.
ORIGIN: From eu and ginomai; well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or (figuratively) generous.

BDAG.en: pertaining to being of high status, well-born, high-born; pertaining to having the attitude ordinarily associated with well-bred persons, noble-minded, open-minded.
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser de alta posição, de boa linhagem, nobre; relativo a ter a atitude normalmente associada a pessoas bem-educadas, de mente nobre, de mente aberta.

DEFINITION: fair weather, good weather.
ORIGIN: Feminine from eu and the alternate of Zeus (as the god of the weather); a clear sky, i.e. Fine weather.

BDAG.en: 1 fair weather. 2 oft. in imagery, to represent peace and rest, then in the mng. tranquillity, peace
BDAG.pt: 1 bom tempo. 2 frequentemente em imagens, para representar paz e descanso, depois no sentido de tranquilidade, paz

DEFINITION: to be well-pleased, think it good, be resolved.
ORIGIN: From eu and dokeo; to think well of, i.e. Approve (an act); specially, to approbate (a person or thing).
USAGE: think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing.

BDAG.en: to consider something as good and therefore worthy of choice, consent, determine, resolve; to take pleasure or find satisfaction in something, be well pleased, take delight.
BDAG.pt: considerar algo como bom e, portanto, digno de escolha, consentir, determinar, resolver; ter prazer ou encontrar satisfação em algo, estar contente, deleitar-se.

DEFINITION: (a) good-will (good-pleasure), favor, feeling of complacency of God to man, (b) good-pleasure, satisfaction, happiness, delight of men.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of eu and the base of dokeo; satisfaction, i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish, purpose.
USAGE: desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good.

BDAG.en: 1 state or condition of being kindly disposed, good will of humans. 2 state or condition of being favored, favor, good pleasure. 3 desire, usually directed toward someth. that causes satisfaction or favor, wish, desire
BDAG.pt: 1 estado ou condição de ser bem-intencionado, boa vontade dos humanos. 2 estado ou condição de ser favorecido, favor, bom agrado. 3 desejo, geralmente direcionado a algo que causa satisfação ou favor, desejo, anseio

DEFINITION: good action, well-doing, benefiting, kind service.
ORIGIN: From euergetes; beneficence (genitive case or specially).

BDAG.en: the doing of that which is beneficial, doing of good or service; the content of beneficial service, good deed, benefit, a kindness
BDAG.pt: o ato de fazer o que é benéfico, a prática do bem ou serviço; o conteúdo do serviço benéfico, boa ação, benefício, uma gentileza

DEFINITION: to do good deeds, perform kind service, benefit.
ORIGIN: From euergetes; to be philanthropic.

BDAG.en: to render exceptional service, esp. to a community, do good to, benefit someone. Pass. be treated well
BDAG.pt: prestar um serviço excepcional, especialmente a uma comunidade, fazer o bem, beneficiar alguém. Passivo ser bem tratado

DEFINITION: a doer of good, a benefactor.
ORIGIN: From eu and the base of ergon; a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a philanthropist.

BDAG.en: benefactor as a title of princes and other honored pers., esp. those recognized for their civic contributions. Of God
BDAG.pt: benfeitor como título de príncipes e outras pessoas honradas, especialmente aquelas reconhecidas por suas contribuições cívicas. De Deus

DEFINITION: well-placed, ready for use.
ORIGIN: From eu and a derivative of tithemi; well placed, i.e. (figuratively) appropriate.

BDAG.en: orig. ‘well-placed’, then in ref. to that which is well suited for someth., fit, suitable, usable, convenient
BDAG.pt: originalmente 'bem-colocado', depois em referência ao que é bem adequado para algo, apto, conveniente, usável, cômodo

DEFINITION: immediately, soon, at once.
ORIGIN: Adverb from euthus; directly, i.e. At once or soon.
USAGE: anon, as soon as, forthwith, immediately, shortly, straightway.

BDAG.en: at once, immediately
BDAG.pt: de imediato, imediatamente

DEFINITION: to run a straight course.
ORIGIN: From euthus and dromos; to lay a straight course, i.e. Sail direct.

BDAG.en: of a ship run a straight course
BDAG.pt: de um navio, correr em linha reta

DEFINITION: to keep up spirit, be cheerful, be of good courage.
ORIGIN: From euthumos; to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully.

BDAG.en: be cheerful, cheer up, keep up one’s courage
BDAG.pt: estar alegre, animar-se, manter a coragem

DEFINITION: cheerful, having good courage.
ORIGIN: From eu and thumos; in fine spirits, i.e. Cheerful.
USAGE: of good cheer, the more cheerfully.

BDAG.en: cheerful, in good spirits
BDAG.pt: alegre, de bom ânimo

DEFINITION: (a) to make straight (of the direction, not the surface, of a road), (b) to guide, steer.
ORIGIN: From euthus; to straighten (level); technically, to steer.

BDAG.en: to cause something to be in a straight or direct line, straighten, make straight; to keep something on course, guide straight, steer
BDAG.pt: fazer com que algo esteja em linha reta ou direta, endireitar, tornar reto; manter algo no curso, guiar em linha reta, pilotar

DEFINITION: adj: (a) straight of direction, as opposed to crooked, (b) upright; adv: immediately.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from eu and tithemi; straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once.
USAGE: anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway.

BDAG.en: straight (adj.); immediately, at once (adv.)
BDAG.pt: reto, direto (adj.); imediatamente, de uma vez (adv.)

DEFINITION: straightness, uprightness.
ORIGIN: From euthus; rectitude.

BDAG.en: righteousness, uprightness
BDAG.pt: retidão, integridade

DEFINITION: to have a good (favorable) opportunity, have leisure; to devote leisure to.
ORIGIN: From eukairos; to have good time, i.e. Opportunity or leisure.

BDAG.en: to experience a favorable time or occasion for some activity, have time, leisure, opportunity
BDAG.pt: experimentar um tempo ou ocasião favorável para alguma atividade, ter tempo, lazer, oportunidade

DEFINITION: a convenient time, opportunity.
ORIGIN: From eukairos; a favorable occasion.

BDAG.en: favorable opportunity, the right moment
BDAG.pt: oportunidade favorável, o momento certo

DEFINITION: opportune, timely, suitable; perhaps sometimes: holiday, festival.
ORIGIN: From eu and kairos; well-timed, i.e. Opportune.

BDAG.en: well-timed, suitable (pert. to time)
BDAG.pt: oportuno, adequado (referente ao tempo)

DEFINITION: opportunely, in season, conveniently.
ORIGIN: Adverb from eukairos; opportunely.

BDAG.en: conveniently
BDAG.pt: convenientemente

DEFINITION: with easier labor.
ORIGIN: Comparative of a compound of eu and kopos; better for toil, i.e. More facile.

DEFINITION: reverence, fear of God, piety.
ORIGIN: From eulabes; properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely).

BDAG.en: the primary mng. relates to exercise of caution; in dealing with the transcendent realm one must be esp. cautious about giving offense to deities, hence ‘reverence, piety’, and in our lit. prob. only of reverent awe in the presence of God, awe, fear of God
BDAG.pt: o sentido primário relaciona-se ao exercício de cautela; ao lidar com o reino transcendente deve-se ser especialmente cauteloso em ofender divindades, daí 'reverência, piedade', e em nossa literatura provavelmente apenas de temor reverente na presença de Deus, assombro, temor de Deus

DEFINITION: to fear, be anxious, be cautious; to reverence.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from eulabes; to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be apprehensive; religiously, to reverence.

BDAG.en: 1 to be concerned about a matter, be concerned, be anxious; 2 to show reverent regard for, reverence, respect
BDAG.pt: 1 estar preocupado com um assunto, preocupar-se, estar ansioso; 2 mostrar consideração reverente por, reverenciar, respeitar

DEFINITION: (lit: handling well, hence) cautious, circumspect; hence: God-fearing, pious.
ORIGIN: From eu and lambano; taking well (carefully), i.e. Circumspect (religiously, pious).

BDAG.en: in our lit. only of relig. attitudes, devout, God-fearing
BDAG.pt: em nossa literatura apenas de atitudes religiosas, devoto, temente a Deus

DEFINITION: (lit: to speak well of) to bless; pass: to be blessed.
ORIGIN: From a compound of eu and logos; to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper).

BDAG.en: 1 to say someth. commendatory, speak well of, praise, extol; 2 to ask for bestowal of special favor, esp. of calling down God’s gracious power, bless; 3 to bestow a favor, provide with benefits
BDAG.pt: 1 dizer algo commendatório, falar bem de, louvar, exaltar; 2 pedir a concessão de favor especial, especialmente de invocar o poder gracioso de Deus, abençoar; 3 conceder um favor, prover com benefícios

DEFINITION: (used only of God), blessed (as entitled to receive blessing from man), worthy of praise.
ORIGIN: From eulogeo; adorable.

BDAG.en: in our lit. only (as predom. LXX) of God (and Christ) blessed, praised
BDAG.pt: em nossa literatura apenas (como predomina na LXX) de Deus (e Cristo) abençoado, louvado

DEFINITION: adulation, praise, blessing, gift.
ORIGIN: From the same as eulogeo; fine speaking, i.e. Elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess.
USAGE: blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech.

BDAG.en: 1 act of speaking in favorable terms, praise; 2 in an extended sense of ‘fine speaking’ ... used in a pejorative sense ... flattery; 3 act or benefit of blessing; 4 Since the concept of blessing connotes the idea of bounty, also bears the mng. generous gift, bounty
BDAG.pt: 1 ato de falar em termos favoráveis, louvor; 2 em sentido estendido de 'fala elegante' ... usado em sentido pejorativo ... bajulação; 3 ato ou benefício de bênção; 4 Uma vez que o conceito de bênção conota a ideia de generosidade, também tem o sentido de presente generoso, abundância

DEFINITION: willingly sharing, ready to impart, generous.
ORIGIN: From eu and a presumed derivative of metadidomi; good at imparting, i.e. Liberal.

BDAG.en: generous
BDAG.pt: generoso

DEFINITION: "victorious", Eunice, the mother of Timothy.
ORIGIN: From eu and nike; victorious; Eunice, a Jewess.

BDAG.en: Eunice, mother of Timothy
BDAG.pt: Evonice, mãe de Timóteo

DEFINITION: to think kindly of, to be favorable.
ORIGIN: From a compound of eu and nous; to be well- minded, i.e. Reconcile.

BDAG.en: be well-disposed, make friends to or with someone
BDAG.pt: ser bem-intencionado, fazer amizade com alguém

DEFINITION: good-will, kindliness; enthusiasm.
ORIGIN: From the same as eunoeo; kindness; euphemistically, conjugal duty.

BDAG.en: goodwill, kindly supportive feeling, favor, affection, benevolence; positive attitude, willingness (diplomatic context)
BDAG.pt: boa vontade, sentimento de apoio gentil, favor, afeição, benevolência; atitude positiva, disposição (contexto diplomático)

DEFINITION: to make into a eunuch, emasculate, castrate.
ORIGIN: From eunouchos; to castrate (figuratively, live unmarried).

BDAG.en: to cause someone to be a eunuch, castrate, emasculate, make a eunuch of (can be literal or figurative)
BDAG.pt: fazer de alguém um eunuco, castrar, emasculador, tornar eunuco (pode ser literal ou figurado)

DEFINITION: (a) a chamberlain, keeper of the bed-chamber of an eastern potentate, eunuch, (b) a eunuch, castrated person, or one who voluntarily abstains from marriage.
ORIGIN: From eune (a bed) and echo; a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer).

BDAG.en: a castrated male person, eunuch; a human male who, without a physical operation, is by nature incapable of begetting children, impotent male; a human male who abstains from marriage, without being impotent, a celibate
BDAG.pt: uma pessoa do sexo masculino castrada, eunuco; um homem que, sem operação física, é incapaz por natureza de gerar filhos, homem impotente; um homem que se abstém do casamento, sem ser impotente, um celibatário

DEFINITION: Euodia, or rather Euhodia, a Christian woman of Philippi.
ORIGIN: From the same as euodoo; fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Euodia, a Christian
BDAG.pt: Evódia, uma cristã

DEFINITION: to cause to prosper, pass: to have a happy (successful) journey, hence: to prosper.
ORIGIN: From a compound of eu and hodos; to help on the road, i.e. (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business affairs.

BDAG.en: have things turn out well, prosper, succeed (of persons, actions, or business)
BDAG.pt: ter as coisas darem certo, prosperar, ter sucesso (referente a pessoas, ações ou negócios)

DEFINITION: compliant, ready to obey.
ORIGIN: From eu and peitho; good for persuasion, i.e. (intransitively) complaint.

BDAG.en: compliant, obedient
BDAG.pt: complacente, obediente

DEFINITION: easily surrounding, encircling, easily distracted.
ORIGIN: From eu and a derivative of a presumed compound of peri and histemi; well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case).

BDAG.en: easily ensnaring, obstructing, constricting (of sin)
BDAG.pt: facilmente que enreda, que obstrui, que restringe (de pecado)

DEFINITION: good-doing, doing of good.
ORIGIN: From a compound of eu and poieo; well-doing, i.e. Beneficence.

BDAG.en: rendering of service, with implication of being generally recognized as laudable, well-doing; the content of well-doing, a good deed
BDAG.pt: prestação de serviço, com implicação de ser geralmente reconhecida como louvável, bom fazer; o conteúdo de fazer o bem, uma boa ação

DEFINITION: to have means, be prosperous, enjoy plenty.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hetoimazo and the base of poreia; (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means.

BDAG.en: to prosper financially, have plenty, be well off
BDAG.pt: prosperar financeiramente, ter fartura, estar bem de vida

DEFINITION: wealth, gain, plenty.
ORIGIN: From the same as euporeo; pecuniary resources.

BDAG.en: having the means for someth., ‘means’, then abundant means, prosperity
BDAG.pt: possuir os meios para algo, 'recursos', então meios abundantes, prosperidade

DEFINITION: beauty, gracefulness, comeliness.
ORIGIN: From a compound of eu and prepo; good suitableness, i.e. Gracefulness.

BDAG.en: fine appearance, beauty
BDAG.pt: boa aparência, beleza

DEFINITION: well-received, acceptable, welcome, pleasing.
ORIGIN: From eu and a derivative of prosdechomai; well-received, i.e. Approved, favorable.

BDAG.en: '(easily) acceptable, pleasant, welcome'; pert. to being capable of eliciting favorable acceptance, acceptable; pert. to being welcome in a situation, favorable
BDAG.pt: '(facilmente) aceitável, agradável, bem-vindo'; pert. a ser capaz de provocar aceitação favorável, aceitável; pert. a ser bem-vindo numa situação, favorável

DEFINITION: constantly attending to, devoted.
ORIGIN: From eu and the same as prosedreuo; sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service).

BDAG.en: pert. to being in constant attendance, constantly in service, constant
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar em constante comparecimento, constantemente em serviço, constante

DEFINITION: to look well, make a fair show (a good outward appearance, and so win good opinion).
ORIGIN: From a compound of eu and prosopon; to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display.

BDAG.en: make a good showing before people
BDAG.pt: fazer uma boa figura diante das pessoas

DEFINITION: to find, learn, discover, especially after searching.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary heuro (hyoo'-ro), which (together with another cognate form) heureo (hyoo-reh'-o) is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect to find (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: A prolonged form of a primary heuro (hyoo'-ro), which (together with another cognate form) heureo (hyoo-reh'-o) is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect to find (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to come upon someth. either through purposeful search or accidentally, find; to discover intellectually through reflection, observation, examination, or investigation, find, discover, transf. sense of 1; to attain a state or condition, find (for oneself), obtain.
BDAG.pt: encontrar algo seja por busca intencional ou acidentalmente, achar; descobrir intelectualmente através de reflexão, observação, exame ou investigação, achar, descobrir, sentido translatório de 1; atingir um estado ou condição, achar (para si), obter.

DEFINITION: Euroklydon, northeast wind.
ORIGIN: From Euros (the east wind) and kludon; a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter.

BDAG.en: Euroclydon, explained as the southeast wind, that stirs up waves; another form is εὐρυκλύδων=the wind that stirs up broad waves; only Ac 27:14 v.l., where εὐρακύλων (q.v.) is the correct rdg., and the two other forms are prob. to be regarded as scribal errors
BDAG.pt: Euroclídon, explicado como o vento sudeste que agita as ondas; outra forma é euriclídon = o vento que agita as ondas largas; apenas em At 27:14 v.l., onde euracúlon (v.g.) é a leitura correta, e as outras duas formas são provavelmente para serem consideradas erros de escriba.

DEFINITION: broad, spacious, wide.
ORIGIN: From eurus (wide) and chora; spacious.

BDAG.en: pert. to having ample room, broad, spacious, roomy (of a road) spacious; (a large room), in which one can live comfortably and unmolested
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a ter espaço amplo, largo, espaçoso, cômodo (de uma estrada) espaçoso; (um grande cômodo), no qual se pode viver confortavelmente e sem ser incomodado.

DEFINITION: piety (towards God), godliness, devotion, godliness.
ORIGIN: From eusebes; piety; specially, the gospel scheme.

BDAG.en: awesome respect accorded to God, devoutness, piety, godliness; Respect for deity, devotion; godly acts
BDAG.pt: Respeito impressionante concedido a Deus, devoção, piedade, temor a Deus; Respeito à divindade, devoção; atos de piedade.

DEFINITION: to be dutiful, pious, show piety towards, worship.

DEFINITION: "Zeus-given", Zenas, a Christian lawyer.
ORIGIN: Probably contracted from a poetic form of Zeus and doron; Jove-given; Zenas, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Zenas, a Christian and lawyer/legal expert
BDAG.pt: Zenás, um cristão e advogado/perito legal

DEFINITION: to seek, search for, desire, require, demand.

BDAG.en: try to find someth., seek, look for in order to find; to seek information, investigate, examine, consider, deliberate; to devote serious effort to realize one’s desire or objective, strive for, aim (at), try to obtain, desire, wish (for); ask for, request, demand
BDAG.pt: tentar encontrar algo, buscar, procurar a fim de achar; buscar informação, investigar, examinar, considerar, deliberar; devotar esforço sério para realizar um desejo ou objetivo, esforçar-se por, almejar, tentar obter, desejar, querer; pedir, solicitar, exigir

DEFINITION: a question, subject of inquiry, dispute.
ORIGIN: From zeteo; a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a debate.

BDAG.en: question, issue, argument (controversial)
BDAG.pt: questão, assunto, argumento (contencioso)

DEFINITION: a question, debate, controversy; a seeking, search.
ORIGIN: From zeteo; a searching (properly, the act), i.e. A dispute or its theme.

BDAG.en: a search for information, investigation; matter for dispute, controversial question, controversy; engagement in a controversial discussion, discussion, debate, argument
BDAG.pt: uma busca por informação, investigação; assunto para disputa, questão controversa, controvérsia; engajamento em discussão controversa, discussão, debate, argumentação

DEFINITION: spurious wheat, darnel; a plant that grows in Palestine which resembles wheat in many ways but is worthless.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; darnel or false grain.

BDAG.en: troublesome weed in grainfields, darnel, cheat (resembling wheat)
BDAG.pt: erva daninha incômoda em campos de grãos, joio, cizânia (semelhante ao trigo)

DEFINITION: Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel (Salathiel) and father of Abiud and Rhesa.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Zrubbabel); Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Zerubbabel (descendant of David, Persian governor)
BDAG.pt: Zorobabel (descendente de Davi, governador persa)

DEFINITION: darkness, murkiness, gloom.
ORIGIN: Akin to the base of nephos; gloom (as shrouding like a cloud).

BDAG.en: darkness ranging from partial to total state, with suggestion of foreboding, darkness, gloom; esp. darkness of the nether regions, gloom, and these regions themselves
BDAG.pt: escuridão que varia de parcial a total, com sugestão de presságio, trevas, penumbra; especialmente a escuridão das regiões infernais, trevas, e estas regiões em si

DEFINITION: a yoke; hence met: (a Jewish idea) of a heavy burden, comparable to the heavy yokes resting on the bullocks' necks; a balance, pair of scales.
ORIGIN: From the root of zeugnumi (to join, especially by a "yoke"); a coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales).

BDAG.en: a frame used to control working animals or, in the case of humans, to expedite the bearing of burdens, yoke; an instrument for determining weight, scale
BDAG.pt: estrutura usada para controlar animais de trabalho ou, no caso de humanos, para facilitar o transporte de fardos, jugo; instrumento para determinar peso, balança

DEFINITION: leaven, ferment, both lit. and met.
ORIGIN: Probably from zeo; ferment (as if boiling up).

BDAG.en: fermented dough, leaven; that which negatively permeates attitude or behavior, leaven fig. ext. of 1
BDAG.pt: massa fermentada, fermento; aquilo que permeia negativamente a atitude ou o comportamento, fermento estendido figurativamente do 1

DEFINITION: to leaven, ferment.
ORIGIN: From zume; to cause to ferment.

BDAG.en: to ferment, leaven
BDAG.pt: fermentar, levedar

DEFINITION: to capture alive, capture for life, enthrall.
ORIGIN: From the same as zoon and agreuo; to take alive (make a prisoner of war), i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare.

BDAG.en: capture alive (figuratively: win people for God's kingdom)
BDAG.pt: capturar vivo (figurativamente: ganhar pessoas para o reino de Deus)

DEFINITION: life, both of physical (present) and of spiritual (particularly future) existence.
ORIGIN: From zao; life (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: life; (in the phrase) in this life; end of life; life and breath; breath of life; living thing; necessary for life; transcendent life, life as God and Christ; means of sustenance, livelihood; course or mode of one’s life; life of the risen Christ; the life of believers (grace and holiness); life of salvation and glory; eternal life; the real, true life; hope of life; book of life; tree of life; crown of life; water of life; fountain of life.
BDAG.pt: vida; (na frase) nesta vida; fim da vida; vida e fôlego; fôlego de vida; ser vivo; necessário para a vida; vida transcendente, vida como Deus e Cristo; meio de sustento, subsistência; curso ou modo de vida; vida do Cristo ressurreto; a vida dos crentes (graça e santidade); vida de salvação e glória; vida eterna; a vida real, verdadeira; esperança de vida; livro da vida; árvore da vida; coroa da vida; água da vida; fonte da vida.

DEFINITION: a girdle, belt, waistband; because the purse was kept there, also: a purse.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to the base of zugos; a belt; by implication, a pocket.

BDAG.en: belt, girdle, in our lit. only of a man’s belt or girdle, unless the ref. is to heavenly beings (Rv). This belt is also used to hold money
BDAG.pt: cinto, faixa, na nossa literatura apenas o cinto ou faixa de um homem, a menos que a referência seja a seres celestiais (Apocalipse). Este cinto também é usado para guardar dinheiro

DEFINITION: to gird, put on the girdle, especially as preparatory to active work.
ORIGIN: From zone; to bind about (especially with a belt).

BDAG.en: to gird someone; to gird oneself.
BDAG.pt: cercar alguém (cingir); cingir-se.

DEFINITION: to preserve alive (lit: bring to birth), save.
ORIGIN: From the same as zoon and a derivative of ginomai; to engender alive, i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death.

BDAG.en: to cause to be alive, give life to, make alive; to cause to remain alive, keep/preserve alive.
BDAG.pt: fazer viver, dar vida, animar; fazer permanecer vivo, manter/preservar vivo.

DEFINITION: an animal, living creature.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of zao; a live thing, i.e. An animal.

BDAG.en: a living creature, wild or domesticated, but not including plants, animal in our lit. exclusive of human beings. a creature that transcends normal descriptive categories and is freq. composite, living thing/being. One isolated pass. in our lit. has ζῶα in the sense living creatures, including both humans and animals
BDAG.pt: uma criatura viva, selvagem ou domesticada, mas não incluindo plantas, animal em nossa literatura, exclusivo de seres humanos. uma criatura que transcende as categorias descritivas normais e é frequentemente composta, ser vivo/ente. Uma passagem isolada em nossa literatura tem ζῶα no sentido de criaturas vivas, incluindo humanos e animais

DEFINITION: to make that which was dead to live, cause to live, quicken.
ORIGIN: From the same as zoon and poieo; to (re-)vitalize (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to cause to live, make alive, give life to, especially in a transcendent sense (God, Christ, Spirit giving life to the dead or sustaining life); of things, circumstances, words (the law cannot do this, but the Word/wound can); to keep alive, sustain life (e.g., milk for a child).
BDAG.pt: fazer viver, animar, dar vida, especialmente em sentido transcendente (Deus, Cristo, Espírito dando vida aos mortos ou sustentando a vida); de coisas, circunstâncias, palavras (a lei não pode fazer isso, mas a Palavra/ferida pode); manter vivo, sustentar a vida (ex: leite para uma criança).

DEFINITION: or, than.
ORIGIN: A primary particle of distinction between two connected terms; disjunctive, or; comparative, than.
USAGE: and, but (either), (n-)either, except it be, (n-)or (else), rather, save, than, that, what, yea. Often used in connection with other particles. Compare especially ede, eper, etoi.

BDAG.en: particle; marker of an alternative, or, disjunctive particle; separating opposites; related and similar terms, where one can take the place of the other or one supplements the other; whether... or (in ἤτε... ἤτε); or (even, also) (ἤκαί); for καί (variant reading); either... or (ἤ...ἤ); either... or... or (ἤ...ἤ...ἤ); nor, or (in negative statements); how or what (interrogative); or do you suppose that? (rhetorical question); or is God... alone? (rhetorical question); or do you not know? (rhetorical question); whether... or (in πότερον...ἤ); whether... or... or... or (ἤ...ἤ...ἤ...ἤ); used with an interrogative word; than, rather than (comparison); nothing else than; what other... than; before (πρὶν ἤ)
BDAG.pt: partícula; marcador de alternativa, ou, partícula disjuntiva; separando opostos; termos relacionados e similares, onde um pode substituir o outro ou um complementa o outro; se... ou (em ἤτε... ἤτε); ou (até, também) (ἤκαί); em vez de καί (leitura variante); ou... ou (ἤ...ἤ); ou... ou... ou (ἤ...ἤ...ἤ); nem, ou (em declarações negativas); como ou o quê (interrogativo); ou você supõe que? (pergunta retórica); ou Deus é... somente? (pergunta retórica); ou você não sabe? (pergunta retórica); se... ou (em πότερον...ἤ); se... ou... ou... ou (ἤ...ἤ...ἤ...ἤ); usado com uma palavra interrogativa; do que, em vez de (comparação); nada além de; que outro... senão; antes (πρὶν ἤ)

DEFINITION: truly, surely.
ORIGIN: An adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of e; used only (in the New Testament) before men; assuredly.

BDAG.en: adv. truly; indeed (ἦμήν)
BDAG.pt: adv. verdadeiramente; de fato (ἦμήν)

DEFINITION: to command.
ORIGIN: From hegemon; to act as ruler.

BDAG.en: to exercise an administrative position, be leader, command, rule, order (especially of imperial legates/governors)
BDAG.pt: exercer uma posição administrativa, ser líder, comandar, governar, ordenar (especialmente de legados imperiais/governadores)

DEFINITION: rule, authority, sovereignty; a reign.
ORIGIN: From hegemon; government, i.e. (in time) official term.

BDAG.en: state of being in control over others in official capacity, chief command, direction, management of any high office (of imperial government or office of governor)
BDAG.pt: estado de estar no controle sobre outros em capacidade oficial, comando principal, direção, gestão de qualquer alto cargo (do governo imperial ou do cargo de governador)

DEFINITION: a leader, guide; a commander; a governor (of a province); plur: leaders.
ORIGIN: From hegeomai; a leader, i.e. Chief person (or figuratively, place) of a province.

BDAG.en: one who rules, esp. in a preeminent position, ruler; head imperial provincial administrator, governor in the provinces (esp. of procurators or prefects in Judaea)
BDAG.pt: aquele que governa, especialmente em posição proeminente, governante; administrador provincial imperial principal, governador nas províncias (especialmente de procuradores ou prefeitos na Judeia)

DEFINITION: (a) to lead, (b) to think, be of opinion, suppose, consider.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of a (presumed) strengthened form of ago; to lead, i.e. Command (with official authority); figuratively, to deem, i.e. Consider.
USAGE: account, (be) chief, count, esteem, governor, judge, have the rule over, suppose, think.

BDAG.en: to be in a supervisory capacity, lead, guide (often used of men in leading positions, officials, commanders, or heads of religious bodies); to engage in an intellectual process, think, consider, regard (e.g., consider it my duty, deem superfluous); look upon, consider someone or something (as) someone or something; esteem, respect
BDAG.pt: estar em capacidade de supervisão, liderar, guiar (frequentemente usado para homens em posições de liderança, oficiais, comandantes ou chefes de corpos religiosos); engajar-se em um processo intelectual, pensar, considerar, reputar (ex: considero meu dever, julgar supérfluo); olhar para, considerar alguém ou algo (como) alguém ou algo; estimar, respeitar

DEFINITION: gladly, pleasantly, with pleasure.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of the base of hedone; sweetly, i.e. (figuratively) with pleasure.

BDAG.en: gladly, with pleasure (e.g., to hear gladly, to tolerate gladly, to do gladly)
BDAG.pt: com prazer, alegremente (ex: ouvir com prazer, tolerar com prazer, fazer com prazer)

DEFINITION: already; now at length, now after all this waiting.
ORIGIN: Apparently from e (or possibly e) and de; even now.

BDAG.pt: um ponto de tempo anterior a outro ponto de tempo, agora, já, até agora. 2. marcador de culminação, finalmente. 3. marcador de proximidade lógica e imediatismo, de fato. 4. marcador de intensificação

DEFINITION: most gladly, most pleasantly.
ORIGIN: Neuter plural of the superlative of the same as hedeos; with great pleasure.

DEFINITION: pleasure, a pleasure, especially sensuous pleasure; a strong desire, passion.
ORIGIN: From handano (to please); sensual delight; by implication, desire.

BDAG.en: 1. state or condition of experiencing pleasure for any reason, pleasure, delight, enjoyment, pleasantness (often in a bad sense: evil pleasure). 2. pleasurable experience of sensation, agreeable taste
BDAG.pt: 1. estado ou condição de experimentar prazer por qualquer razão, prazer, deleite, gozo, agradabilidade (frequentemente em sentido pejorativo: prazer maligno). 2. experiência prazerosa de sensação, sabor agradável

DEFINITION: mint, peppermint.
ORIGIN: Neuter of the compound of the same as hedeos and osme; a sweet-scented plant, i.e. Mint.

BDAG.en: mint (garden plant).
BDAG.pt: hortelã (planta de jardim).

DEFINITION: habit, manner, custom, morals.

BDAG.pt: um padrão de comportamento ou prática que é habitual ou característico de um grupo ou indivíduo, costume, uso, hábito

DEFINITION: to have come, be present, have arrived.

BDAG.en: to be in a place as the result of movement to, have come, be present, of persons. 2. to make an appearance or come to pass, come, impers.
BDAG.pt: estar em um lugar como resultado de movimento para, ter chegado, estar presente, de pessoas. 2. fazer uma aparição ou acontecer, vir, impessoalmente

DEFINITION: Eli, God (Hebrew).

BDAG.pt: Eli, o pai (ou avô) de José, na genealogia de Jesus.

DEFINITION: Heli, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Eliy); Heli (i.e. Eli), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Eli, the father (or grandfather) of Joseph, in Jesus' genealogy.
BDAG.pt: Eli, o pai (ou avô) de José, na genealogia de Jesus.

DEFINITION: Elijah, an Israelite prophet.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Eliyah); Helias (i.e. Elijah), an Israelite.

BDAG.pt: Elias o Tisbita, um profeta.

DEFINITION: age, term of life; full age, maturity; stature.
ORIGIN: From the same as helikos; maturity (in years or size).

BDAG.en: 1. The period of time one's life continues, age, time of life (including youthfulness or old age). 2. The age sufficient for certain things, maturity (e.g., legal majority, age of strength). 3. Bodily stature.
BDAG.pt: 1. O período de tempo que a vida de alguém continua, idade, tempo de vida (incluindo juventude ou velhice). 2. A idade suficiente para certas coisas, maturidade (ex.: maioridade legal, idade de força). 3. Estatura corporal.

DEFINITION: of which size, of what size, how small, how much.
ORIGIN: From helix (a comrade, i.e. One of the same age); as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much.

BDAG.en: how great (in measure or extent).
BDAG.pt: quão grande (em medida ou extensão).

DEFINITION: the sun, sunlight.
ORIGIN: From hele (a ray; perhaps akin to the alternate of haireomai); the sun; by implication, light.

BDAG.en: the sun; can also mean heat of the sun or light of the sun.
BDAG.pt: o sol; também pode significar calor do sol ou luz do sol.

DEFINITION: a nail.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a stud, i.e. Spike.

BDAG.en: nail.
BDAG.pt: prego.

DEFINITION: our, us, we.
ORIGIN: Accusative case plural of ego; us.

DEFINITION: us, we ourselves.
ORIGIN: Nominative plural of ego; we (only used when emphatic).

BDAG.en: (See ἐγώ) we.
BDAG.pt: (Ver ἐγώ) nós.

DEFINITION: a day, the period from sunrise to sunset.
ORIGIN: Feminine (with hora implied) of a derivative of hemai (to sit; akin to the base of hedraios) meaning tame, i.e. Gentle; day, i.e. (literally) the time space between dawn and dark, or the whole aganaktesis hours (but several days were usually reckoned by the Jews as inclusive of the parts of both extremes); figuratively, a period (always defined more or less clearly by the context).
USAGE: age, + alway, (mid-)day (by day, (-ly)), + for ever, judgment, (day) time, while, years.

BDAG.en: 1. The period between sunrise and sunset, day (literal, opposed to night; figurative, e.g., period of human life). 2. Civil or legal day, including the night (period of time, or a specific point in time). Used in various temporal constructions (genitive, accusative, with prepositions) to indicate duration, point in time, or succession.
BDAG.pt: 1. O período entre o nascer e o pôr do sol, dia (literal, oposto a noite; figurado, ex.: período da vida humana). 2. Dia civil ou legal, incluindo a noite (período de tempo, ou um ponto específico no tempo). Usado em várias construções temporais (genitivo, acusativo, com preposições) para indicar duração, ponto no tempo ou sucessão.

DEFINITION: our, our own.
ORIGIN: From thnetos; our.

BDAG.en: our (used with nouns); what is ours (=the real riches).
BDAG.pt: nosso (usado com substantivos); o que é nosso (=as verdadeiras riquezas).

DEFINITION: I was.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of thriambeuo; I was.

DEFINITION: half dead.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of the base of hemisu and thnesko; half dead, i.e. Entirely exhausted.

BDAG.en: half dead
BDAG.pt: meio morto

DEFINITION: our, for us, we.
ORIGIN: Dative case plural of ego; to (or for, with, by) us.

DEFINITION: half.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to hama (through the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; (as noun) half.

BDAG.en: half
BDAG.pt: metade

DEFINITION: half an hour.
ORIGIN: From the base of hemisu and hora; a half-hour.

BDAG.en: a half hour
BDAG.pt: meia hora

DEFINITION: our company, us, we.
ORIGIN: Genitive case plural of ego; of (or from) us.

DEFINITION: agree, be, have charge of, hold, use.
ORIGIN: Imperfect of eimi; I (thou, etc.) Was (wast or were).
USAGE: + agree, be, X have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were.

DEFINITION: when, whenever, at which time.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; at which time.

BDAG.en: when, at the time when, whenever, as soon as
BDAG.pt: quando, no momento em que, sempre que, assim que

DEFINITION: than.
ORIGIN: From e and per; than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed).

BDAG.pt: ou (partícula comparativa)

DEFINITION: placid, gentle, mild.
ORIGIN: Probably from epos; properly, affable, i.e. Mild or kind.

BDAG.en: gentle, kind toward someone
BDAG.pt: gentil, bondoso para com alguém

DEFINITION: Er, son of Joshua and father of Elmadam.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Er); Er, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Er (name in genealogy)
BDAG.pt: Er (nome na genealogia)

DEFINITION: quiet, tranquil.
ORIGIN: Perhaps by transposition from eremos (through the idea of stillness); tranquil.

BDAG.en: quiet, tranquil, of life
BDAG.pt: quieto, tranquilo, de vida

DEFINITION: Herod; four persons are called by this name: Herod the Great, Herod Antipas, Herod Agrippa, and Herod Agrippa the younger.
ORIGIN: Compound of heros (a "hero") and eidos; heroic; Herod, the name of four Jewish kings.

BDAG.en: Herod (name of Idumaean princes)
BDAG.pt: Herodes (nome de príncipes idumeus)

DEFINITION: the Herodians, the partisans of Herod (Antipas).
ORIGIN: Plural of a derivative of Herodes; Herodians, i.e. Partisans of Herod.

BDAG.en: the Herodians, partisans of Herod the Great and his family
BDAG.pt: os Herodianos, partidários de Herodes, o Grande, e sua família

DEFINITION: Herodias (died after A.D. 40), daughter of Aristobulus and granddaughter of Herod to, wife, first, of her uncle Herod, second, of his half-brother, her uncle Herod Antipas.
ORIGIN: From Herodes; Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family.

BDAG.en: Herodias (name)
BDAG.pt: Herodias (nome)

DEFINITION: Herodion, a Christian in Rome, a relative of Paul.
ORIGIN: From Herodes; Herodion, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Herodion, a Jewish Christian, greeted Ro 16:11.
BDAG.pt: Herodião, um cristão judeu, saudado em Romanos 16:11.

DEFINITION: Isaiah, an Israelite prophet.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ysha'yah); Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Isaiah, the prophet (LXX; ...)
BDAG.pt: Isaías, o profeta (LXX; ...)

DEFINITION: Esau, elder son of Isaac the patriarch, brother of Jacob.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Esav); Esau, an Edomite.

BDAG.en: Esau. 'Dis-favored' by God Ro 9:13. Typical of an immoral and vulgar person Hb 12:16.
BDAG.pt: Essau. 'Desfavorecido' por Deus (Rm 9:13). Típico de uma pessoa imoral e vulgar (Hb 12:16).

DEFINITION: to rest from work, cease from altercation, be silent, live quietly.
ORIGIN: From the same as hesuchios; to keep still (intransitively), i.e. Refrain from labor, meddlesomeness or speech.
USAGE: cease, hold peace, be quiet, rest.

BDAG.en: 1. to relax from normal activity, rest, abstain from work. 2. to live a quiet life or refrain from disturbing activity, be peaceable/orderly. 3. to be free from being disturbed, have rest. 4. to refrain from saying something, be quiet, remain silent.
BDAG.pt: 1. relaxar da atividade normal, descansar, abster-se do trabalho. 2. viver uma vida quieta ou abster-se de atividade perturbadora, ser pacífico/ordenado. 3. estar livre de ser perturbado, ter descanso. 4. abster-se de dizer algo, ficar quieto, permanecer em silêncio.

DEFINITION: quietness, stillness, silence.
ORIGIN: Feminine of hesuchios; (as noun) stillness, i.e. Desistance from bustle or language.

BDAG.en: state of quietness without disturbance, quietness, rest. state of saying nothing or very little, silence.
BDAG.pt: estado de quietude sem perturbação, quietude, descanso. estado de não dizer nada ou muito pouco, silêncio.

DEFINITION: quiet, tranquil, peaceful.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of hedraios and perhaps echo; properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing).

BDAG.en: quiet, well-ordered (e.g., a peaceable and quiet life).
BDAG.pt: quieto, bem-ordenado (ex: uma vida pacífica e quieta).

DEFINITION: whether.
ORIGIN: From e and toi; either indeed.

DEFINITION: to be defeated, be overcome, be made inferior.
ORIGIN: From the same as hetton; to make worse, i.e. Vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower.

BDAG.en: 1. to be vanquished, be defeated, succumb. 2. to be made to feel less important, be treated worse.
BDAG.pt: 1. ser vencido, ser derrotado, sucumbir. 2. ser feito sentir-se menos importante, ser tratado pior.

DEFINITION: defect, loss, defeat, failure, shortcoming.
ORIGIN: From hettao; a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss.

BDAG.en: loss.
BDAG.pt: perda.

DEFINITION: lesser, inferior, weaker.
ORIGIN: Neuter of comparative of heka (slightly) used for that of kakos; worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb).

DEFINITION: let be.
ORIGIN: Third person singular imperative of eimi; let him (or it) be.

DEFINITION: to make a sound, give forth a sound, sound (when struck); to roar (as the sea).
ORIGIN: From echos; to make a loud noise, i.e. Reverberate.

BDAG.en: sound, ring out (of brass instruments). Roar, thunder of the sea.
BDAG.pt: soar, ressoar (de instrumentos de bronze). Rugido, trovão do mar.

DEFINITION: (a) a sound, noise, (b) a rumor, report.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. Roar; figuratively, a rumor.

BDAG.en: auditory impression of varying degrees of loudness, sound, tone, noise. information that is spread far and wide, report, news.
BDAG.pt: impressão auditiva de graus variados de volume, som, tom, ruído. informação que se espalha amplamente, boato, notícia.

DEFINITION: Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Thaddaeus, one of the Apostles.

BDAG.en: Thaddaeus
BDAG.pt: Tadeu

DEFINITION: (a) the sea, in contrast to the land, (b) a particular sea or lake, e.g. the sea of Galilee (Tiberias), the Red Sea.
ORIGIN: Probably prolonged from hals; the sea (genitive case or specially).

BDAG.en: sea (generically; specifically the Red Sea or the Mediterranean Sea); lake (Semitic usage, e.g., Lake of Gennesaret); the sand of the seashore as symbol of numberlessness; waves of the sea
BDAG.pt: mar (genericamente; especificamente o Mar Vermelho ou o Mar Mediterrâneo); lago (uso semítico, ex: Lago de Genesaré); a areia da praia como símbolo de incontabilidade; ondas do mar

DEFINITION: (properly: to warm, then) to cherish, nourish, foster, comfort.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to thallo (to warm); to brood, i.e. (figuratively) to foster.

BDAG.en: cherish, comfort (of children); care for (of a wife)
BDAG.pt: estimar, confortar (de crianças); cuidar (de uma esposa)

DEFINITION: Tamar, mother of Perez and Zerah by Judah, son of Jacob.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Tamar); Thamar (i.e. Tamar), an Israelitess.

BDAG.en: Tamar, daughter-in-law of Judah and mother of his twin sons Perez and Zerah
BDAG.pt: Tamar, nora de Judá e mãe de seus filhos gêmeos Perez e Zera

DEFINITION: to amaze; pass: to be amazed (almost terrified).
ORIGIN: From thambos; to stupefy (with surprise), i.e. Astound.

BDAG.en: be astounded; astound, amaze (passive voice used with active sense)
BDAG.pt: ficar espantado; espantar, admirar (voz passiva usada com sentido ativo)

DEFINITION: astonishment, amazement (allied to terror or awe).
ORIGIN: Akin to an obsolete tapho (to dumbfound); stupefaction (by surprise), i.e. Astonishment.

BDAG.en: a state of astonishment brought on by exposure to an unusual event, amazement, awe
BDAG.pt: um estado de assombro causado pela exposição a um evento incomum, espanto, admiração reverente

DEFINITION: deadly, mortal, fatal.
ORIGIN: From thanatos; fatal, i.e. Poisonous.

BDAG.en: deadly (e.g., deadly poison; death-dealing vermin)
BDAG.pt: mortal (ex: veneno mortal; bichos que causam morte)

DEFINITION: death-bringing, deadly.
ORIGIN: From (the feminine form of) thanatos and phero; death-bearing, i.e. Fatal.

BDAG.en: death-dealing
BDAG.pt: que causa a morte, letal

DEFINITION: death, physical or spiritual.
ORIGIN: From thnesko; (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: the termination of physical life, death (natural, as penalty, danger, manner of death, personified); transcendentally, spiritual or eternal death
BDAG.pt: a cessação da vida física, morte (natural, como penalidade, perigo, modo de morte, personificada); transcendentemente, morte espiritual ou eterna

DEFINITION: to put to death, subdue; pass: to be in danger of death, be dead to, be rid of, be parted from.
ORIGIN: From thanatos to kill (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify.

BDAG.en: to cause cessation of life, put to death; to cause total cessation of an activity, extirpate; to cause death that transcends the physical (spiritual or eternal death).
BDAG.pt: causar a cessação da vida, matar; causar a cessação total de uma atividade, extirpar; causar uma morte que transcende o físico (morte espiritual ou eterna).

DEFINITION: to bury.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. Inter.

BDAG.en: to bury (someone, something); to be buried.
BDAG.pt: enterrar (alguém, algo); ser enterrado.

DEFINITION: Terah, the father of Abraham.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Terach); Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of Abraham.

BDAG.en: Terah, father of Abraham.
BDAG.pt: Terá, pai de Abraão.

DEFINITION: to be courageous, confident, of good cheer.
ORIGIN: Another form for tharseo; to exercise courage.
USAGE: be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident. Compare tolmao.

BDAG.en: to have certainty in a matter, be confident, be courageous; to be able to depend on someone; be bold toward someone.
BDAG.pt: ter certeza sobre algo, estar confiante, ser corajoso; poder depender de alguém; ser ousado para com alguém.

DEFINITION: to be of good courage, good cheer, be bold.
ORIGIN: From tharsos; to have courage.
USAGE: be of good cheer (comfort). Compare tharrheo.

BDAG.en: to be firm or resolute in the face of danger or adverse circumstances, be enheartened, be courageous; have courage! don’t be afraid!
BDAG.pt: ser firme ou resoluto diante do perigo ou circunstâncias adversas, ser encorajado, ser corajoso; ter coragem! não ter medo!

DEFINITION: courage, confidence.
ORIGIN: Akin (by transposition) to thrasos (daring); boldness (subjectively).

BDAG.en: courage; to take courage.
BDAG.pt: coragem; tomar coragem.

DEFINITION: (a) concr: a marvel, wonder, (b) abstr: wonder, amazement.
ORIGIN: Apparently from a form of theaomai; wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract).

BDAG.en: an object of wonder, wonder, marvel; a wonder in special sense, portent, miracle; a state of wondering because one is extraordinarily impressed by something, wonder, amazement.
BDAG.pt: um objeto de assombro, maravilha, espanto; uma maravilha em sentido especial, portento, milagre; um estado de assombro por estar extraordinariamente impressionado com algo, assombro, pasmo.

DEFINITION: (a) intrans: to wonder, marvel, (b) trans: to wonder at, admire.
ORIGIN: From thauma; to wonder; by implication, to admire.
USAGE: admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder.

BDAG.en: to be extraordinarily impressed or disturbed by something, act. wonder, marvel, be astonished (in a good or bad sense); admire, wonder at, respect (persons); be marvelled at.
BDAG.pt: ser extraordinariamente impressionado ou perturbado por algo, agir maravilhado, espantado (em sentido bom ou mau); admirar, maravilhar-se, respeitar (pessoas); ser admirado.

DEFINITION: wonderful, admirable; subst: a wonder.
ORIGIN: From thauma; wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle.

BDAG.en: pert. to being a cause of wonder or worthy of amazement, wonderful, remarkable, admirable; wonderful things, wonders (substantive).
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser causa de espanto ou digno de admiração, maravilhoso, notável, admirável; coisas maravilhosas, prodígios (substantivo).

DEFINITION: to be wondered at, wonderful, marvelous.
ORIGIN: From thaumazo; wondered at, i.e. (by implication) wonderful.

BDAG.en: pert. to being a cause of wonder or worthy of amazement, wonderful, marvelous, remarkable (of God or things related to God).
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser causa de espanto ou digno de admiração, maravilhoso, incrível, notável (de Deus ou coisas relacionadas a Deus).

DEFINITION: a goddess.
ORIGIN: Feminine of theos; a female deity.

BDAG.en: a transcendent being conceived of as female and ordinarily understood as tutelary or source of special benefits to her devotees and therefore worthy of highest admiration and respect, god/goddess.
BDAG.pt: um ser transcendente concebido como feminino e ordinariamente entendido como tutelar ou fonte de benefícios especiais para seus devotos, sendo, portanto, digno da mais alta admiração e respeito, deusa.

DEFINITION: to see, behold, contemplate, look upon, view; to see, visit.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit.

BDAG.en: to have an intent look at something, to take something in with one's eyes, with implication that one is especially impressed, see, look at, behold (literally); be seen; be noticed, attract attention; to see for the purpose of visiting, come to see, visit; to perceive something above and beyond what is merely seen with the eye, see, behold, perceive.
BDAG.pt: olhar com intenção para algo, absorver algo com os olhos, com a implicação de estar especialmente impressionado, ver, olhar, contemplar (literalmente); ser visto; chamar a atenção; ver com o propósito de visitar, ir ver, visitar; perceber algo além do que é meramente visto com os olhos, ver, contemplar, perceber.

DEFINITION: to make a public show of, expose to public shame.
ORIGIN: From theatron; to expose as a spectacle.

BDAG.en: to put to shame, expose publicly (to reproach and affliction).
BDAG.pt: envergonhar, expor publicamente (a reprovação e aflição).

DEFINITION: (a) a theatre, a semi-circular stone building, generally open to the sky, (b) a spectacle, show.
ORIGIN: From theaomai; a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. General audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively).

BDAG.en: a place for seeing, esp. dramatic productions, theater; what one sees at a theater, a play, spectacle.
BDAG.pt: um lugar para ver, especialmente produções dramáticas, teatro; aquilo que se vê em um teatro, uma peça, espetáculo.

DEFINITION: brimstone, sulfur.
ORIGIN: Probably neuter of theios (in its original sense of flashing); sulphur.

BDAG.en: sulphur.
BDAG.pt: enxofre.

DEFINITION: divine; subst: the Deity.
ORIGIN: From theos.
USAGE: godlike (neuter as noun, divinity); divine, godhead.

BDAG.en: pert. to that which belongs to the nature or status of deity, divine; of persons who stand in close relation to, or reflect characteristics of, a deity, divine; gener., of that which exceeds the bounds of human or earthly possibility, supernatural.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à natureza ou status de divindade, divino; de pessoas que estão em estreita relação ou refletem características de uma divindade, divino; em geral, daquilo que excede os limites da possibilidade humana ou terrena, sobrenatural.

DEFINITION: divinity, divine nature.
ORIGIN: From theios; divinity (abstractly).

BDAG.en: the quality or characteristic(s) pert. to deity, divinity, divine nature, divineness.
BDAG.pt: a qualidade ou característica(s) pertencente(s) à divindade, divindade, natureza divina, caráter divino.

DEFINITION: of brimstone, sulfurous.
ORIGIN: From theion and eidos; sulphur-like, i.e. Sulphurous.

BDAG.en: sulphurous.
BDAG.pt: sulfuroso.

DEFINITION: an act of will, will; plur: wishes, desires.
ORIGIN: From the prolonged form of ethelo; a determination (properly, the thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree; abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination.

BDAG.en: what one wishes to happen, objective sense, what is willed; what one wishes to bring about by one’s own action; what one wishes to bring about by the activity of others; the act of willing or desiring, subjective sense, will.
BDAG.pt: o que se deseja que aconteça, sentido objetivo, aquilo que é querido; o que se deseja realizar através da própria ação; o que se deseja realizar através da atividade de outros; o ato de querer ou desejar, sentido subjetivo, vontade.

DEFINITION: a willing, will.
ORIGIN: From ethelo; determination (properly, the act), i.e. Option.

BDAG.en: the act of willing, will, of God
BDAG.pt: o ato de querer, a vontade, de Deus

DEFINITION: to will, wish, desire, be willing, intend, design.
ORIGIN: Thel'-o or thel'-o or in certain tenses theleo thel-eh'-o, and etheleo eth-el-eh'-o, which are otherwise obsolete; apparently strengthened from the alternate form of haireomai; to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas boulomai properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations), i.e. Choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to wish, i.e. Be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly); impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to delight in.
USAGE: desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean, please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly)).

BDAG.en: to have a desire for something, wish to have, desire, want; to have something in mind for oneself, of purpose, resolve, will, wish, want, be ready to do something; to take pleasure in, like; to have an opinion, maintain contrary to the true state of affairs; what can this mean?
BDAG.pt: ter um desejo por algo, querer ter, desejar, querer; ter algo em mente para si mesmo, de propósito, resolução, vontade, desejo, querer, estar pronto para fazer algo; ter prazer em, gostar; ter uma opinião, manter contrariamente à situação real das coisas; o que isto pode significar?

DEFINITION: (properly, an adj: belonging to the foundation), a foundation stone.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of tithemi; something put down, i.e. A substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: the supporting base for a structure, foundation; the basis for something taking place or coming into being, foundation (figurative extension of meaning)
BDAG.pt: a base de apoio para uma estrutura, fundação; a base para algo que ocorre ou vem a existir, fundamento (extensão figurada de significado)

DEFINITION: to found, lay the foundation (lit. and met.).
ORIGIN: From themelios; to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate.

BDAG.en: to provide a base for some material object or structure, lay a foundation, found, lit.; to provide a secure basis for the inner life and its resources, establish, strengthen, fig. ext. of mng.
BDAG.pt: fornecer uma base para algum objeto ou estrutura material, estabelecer uma fundação, fundar, literalmente; fornecer uma base segura para a vida interior e seus recursos, estabelecer, fortalecer, extensão figurada de sentido.

DEFINITION: taught by God, divinely instructed.
ORIGIN: From theos and didasko; divinely instructed.

BDAG.en: taught/instructed by God
BDAG.pt: ensinado/instruído por Deus

DEFINITION: to fight against God.
ORIGIN: From theomachos; to resist deity.

BDAG.en: fight against God, oppose God and God’s works
BDAG.pt: lutar contra Deus, opor-se a Deus e às obras de Deus

DEFINITION: fighting against God.
ORIGIN: From theos and machomai; an opponent of deity.

BDAG.en: fighting against God
BDAG.pt: lutando contra Deus

DEFINITION: God-breathed, inspired by God, due to the inspiration of God.
ORIGIN: From theos and a presumed derivative of pneo; divinely breathed in.

BDAG.en: inspired by God
BDAG.pt: inspirado por Deus

DEFINITION: (a) God, (b) a god, generally.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with ho) the supreme Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very.

BDAG.en: God (predominant NT use, often without the article); Christ, as one who manifests primary characteristics of deity; a god (nontranscendent, worthy of special reverence); the devil.
BDAG.pt: Deus (uso predominante no NT, muitas vezes sem artigo); Cristo, como aquele que manifesta características primárias de divindade; um deus (não transcendente, digno de especial reverência); o diabo.

DEFINITION: reverence for God, fear of God, godliness, piety.
ORIGIN: From theosebes; devoutness, i.e. Piety.

BDAG.en: reverence for God or set of beliefs and practices relating to interest in God, piety, godliness; religion.
BDAG.pt: Reverência a Deus ou conjunto de crenças e práticas relacionadas ao interesse em Deus, piedade, devoção; religião.

DEFINITION: devout, pious, God-fearing.
ORIGIN: From theos and sebomai; reverent of God, i.e. Pious.

BDAG.en: god-fearing, devout.
BDAG.pt: Temeroso de Deus, devoto.

DEFINITION: hating God, hateful to God.
ORIGIN: From theos and the base of stugnetos; hateful to God, i.e. Impious.

BDAG.en: god-detested, godforsaken (passive sense); hating God (active sense preferred in Ro 1:30).
BDAG.pt: Detestado por Deus, abandonado por Deus (sentido passivo); que odeia a Deus (sentido ativo preferido em Ro 1:30).

DEFINITION: deity, Godhead.
ORIGIN: From theos; divinity (abstractly).

BDAG.en: the state of being god, divine character/nature, deity, divinity, used as abstract noun for θεός
BDAG.pt: o estado de ser deus, caráter/natureza divina, divindade, divindade, usado como substantivo abstrato para θεός

DEFINITION: Theophilus, a friend of Luke of equestrian rank, to whom the Gospel and Acts are dedicated.
ORIGIN: From theos and philos; friend of God; Theophilus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Theophilus (a Christian of prominence; an elder in Corinth).
BDAG.pt: Teófilo (um cristão de destaque; um presbítero em Corinto).

DEFINITION: care, attention, especially medical attention (treatment); hence almost: healing; meton: those who render service.
ORIGIN: From therapeuo; attendance (specially, medical, i.e. Cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics.

BDAG.en: serving, service, care bestowed on another; the use of medical resources in treating the sick, treatment, esp. healing; = οἱ θεράποντες servants
BDAG.pt: servir, serviço, cuidado dispensado a outro; o uso de recursos médicos no tratamento dos doentes, tratamento, especialmente cura; = os servos

DEFINITION: to care for, attend, serve, treat, especially of a physician; hence: to heal.
ORIGIN: From the same as therapon; to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease).

BDAG.en: to render service or homage, serve a divinity; heal, restore; (of wounds) heal.
BDAG.pt: prestar serviço ou homenagem, servir a uma divindade; curar, restaurar; (de feridas) sarar.

DEFINITION: a servant, attendant, minister.
ORIGIN: Apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of theros; a menial attendant (as if cherishing).

BDAG.en: one who renders devoted service, esp. as an attendant in a cultic setting, attendant, aide, servant, servant (in our lit. only of Moses)
BDAG.pt: aquele que presta serviço dedicado, especialmente como atendente em um ambiente de culto, atendente, auxiliar, servo, servo (em nossa literatura apenas de Moisés)

DEFINITION: to reap, gather, harvest.
ORIGIN: From theros (in the sense of the crop); to harvest.

BDAG.en: to harvest a grain crop by reaping, reap, harvest; to gain results or benefits, reap (figuratively)
BDAG.pt: colher uma safra de grãos, ceifar, colher; obter resultados ou benefícios, colher (figurativamente)

DEFINITION: reaping, harvest; met: the harvest, crop.
ORIGIN: From therizo; reaping, i.e. The crop.

BDAG.en: the process (and time) of harvesting, harvest; crop to be harvested, harvest (figuratively)
BDAG.pt: o processo (e tempo) de colheita, colheita; safra a ser colhida, colheita (figurativamente)

DEFINITION: a reaper, harvester.
ORIGIN: From therizo; a harvester.

BDAG.en: reaper, harvester.
BDAG.pt: ceifador, colhedor.

DEFINITION: to warm; mid: to warm myself.
ORIGIN: From therme; to heat (oneself).

BDAG.en: warm oneself at a fire; dress warmly, keep warm (of clothing).
BDAG.pt: aquecer-se junto ao fogo; vestir-se com roupas quentes, manter-se aquecido (de vestuário).

DEFINITION: heat.
ORIGIN: From the base of theros; warmth.

BDAG.en: heat.
BDAG.pt: calor.

DEFINITION: summer.
ORIGIN: From a primary thero (to heat); properly, heat, i.e. Summer.

BDAG.en: summer.
BDAG.pt: verão.

DEFINITION: a Thessalonian.
ORIGIN: From Thessalonike; a Thessalonican, i.e. Inhabitant of Thessalonice.

BDAG.en: Thessalonian, an inhabitant of Thessalonica.
BDAG.pt: Tessalonicense, um habitante de Tessalônica.

DEFINITION: Thessalonica (modern Saloniki), an important city of the Roman province Macedonia.
ORIGIN: From Thessalos (a Thessalian) and nike; Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Thessalonica, a city in Macedonia on the Thermaic Gulf.
BDAG.pt: Tessalônica, uma cidade na Macedônia no Golfo Termaico.

DEFINITION: Theudas, a Jewish pretender of date about 4 B.C., otherwise unknown.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Theudas, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Theudas, the short form of a name compounded w. θεός, but perh. not Θεόδωρος, mentions a Jewish insurrectionist
BDAG.pt: Teudas, forma abreviada de um nome composto com θεός, mas talvez não Teodoro; menciona um insurrecionista judeu

DEFINITION: to look at, gaze, behold; to see, experience, discern; to partake of.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of theaomai (perhaps by addition of horao); to be a spectator of, i.e. Discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or intensively (acknowledge)).
USAGE: behold, consider, look on, perceive, see. Compare optanomai.

BDAG.en: to observe someth. with sustained attention, be a spectator, look at, observe, perceive, see; to come to the understanding of someth., notice, perceive, observe, find; undergo, experience
BDAG.pt: observar algo com atenção sustentada, ser espectador, olhar, notar, perceber, ver; chegar ao entendimento de algo, notar, perceber, observar, descobrir; sofrer, experimentar

DEFINITION: a viewing, a spectacle.
ORIGIN: From the same as theoreo; spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a spectacle.

BDAG.en: that which one looks at, spectacle, sight (especially of public spectacles, festivals).
BDAG.pt: aquilo que se olha, espetáculo, vista (especialmente de espetáculos públicos, festivais).

DEFINITION: a repository, receptacle; a case, sheath, scabbard.
ORIGIN: From tithemi; a receptacle, i.e. Scabbard.

BDAG.en: receptacle; grave; sheath for a sword.
BDAG.pt: receptáculo; sepulcro, túmulo; bainha para uma espada.

DEFINITION: (a) to give suck, (b) to suck.
ORIGIN: From thele (the nipple); to suckle, (by implication) to suck.

BDAG.en: to breast-feed an infant, nurse; to receive nourishment at the breast, suck, nurse.
BDAG.pt: amamentar um infante, nutrir; receber alimento ao seio, sugar, nutrir.

DEFINITION: female.
ORIGIN: From the same as thelazo; female.

BDAG.en: female, woman, girl; male and female.
BDAG.pt: fêmea, mulher, menina; masculino e feminino.

DEFINITION: hunting, entrapping; prey, game; a net, means of capture.
ORIGIN: From ther (a wild animal, as game); hunting, i.e. (figuratively) destruction.

BDAG.en: net, trap
BDAG.pt: rede, armadilha

DEFINITION: to hunt, seek to catch or entrap; met: to lay hold of.
ORIGIN: From thera; to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp at.

BDAG.en: to hunt, catch (fig.)
BDAG.pt: caçar, apanhar (figurado)

DEFINITION: to fight with wild beasts (i.e. wild beasts in human form); met: to be exposed to fierce hostility.
ORIGIN: From a compound of therion and machomai; to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men).

BDAG.en: be forced to fight with wild animals as a punishment, fight with wild animals; to be in a position of having to contend with adversaries, struggle with, contend with
BDAG.pt: ser forçado a lutar com animais selvagens como punição, lutar com animais selvagens; estar em posição de ter que contender com adversários, lutar contra, disputar com

DEFINITION: properly: a wild beast, hence: any animal; met: a brute.
ORIGIN: Diminutive from the same as thera; a dangerous animal.

BDAG.en: any living creature, excluding humans, animal, beast; wild animals; a reptile snake; animal-like beings of a transcendent kind; wicked person, someone w. a ‘bestial’ nature, beast, monster
BDAG.pt: qualquer criatura viva, excluindo humanos, animal, fera; animais selvagens; um réptil cobra; seres de tipo animal de natureza transcendente; pessoa perversa, alguém com natureza 'bestial', fera, monstro

DEFINITION: to store up, treasure up, save, lay up.
ORIGIN: From thesauros; to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up).

BDAG.en: to keep some material thing safe by storing it, lay up, store up, gather, save; to do something that will bring about a future event or condition, store up (fig.)
BDAG.pt: guardar algo material armazenando-o, acumular, guardar, juntar, salvar; fazer algo que resultará em um evento ou condição futura, acumular (fig.)

DEFINITION: a store-house for precious things; hence: a treasure, a store.
ORIGIN: From tithemi; a deposit, i.e. Wealth (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: a place where something is kept for safekeeping, repository (treasure box/chest, storehouse); that which is stored up, treasure (material things, transcendent things, the gospel)
BDAG.pt: um lugar onde algo é guardado para segurança, repositório (caixa/baú de tesouro, depósito); aquilo que é guardado, tesouro (coisas materiais, coisas transcendentais, o evangelho)

DEFINITION: to touch, handle, injure, harm.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of an obsolete primary thigo (to finger); to manipulate, i.e. Have to do with; by implication, to injure.

BDAG.en: to touch
BDAG.pt: tocar

DEFINITION: (a) to make narrow (strictly: by pressure); to press upon, (b) to persecute, press hard.
ORIGIN: Akin to the base of tribos; to crowd (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble.

BDAG.en: to press or crowd close against, press upon, crowd; to cause something to be constricted or narrow, press together, compress, make narrow; to cause to be troubled, oppress, afflict; (Pass.) be afflicted, distressed
BDAG.pt: pressionar ou apertar contra, pressionar, aglomerar; causar constrição ou estreiteza, comprimir, tornar estreito; causar aflição, oprimir, afligir; (Pass.) ser afligido, angustiado

DEFINITION: persecution, affliction, distress, tribulation.
ORIGIN: From thlibo; pressure (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble.

BDAG.en: trouble that inflicts distress, oppression, affliction, tribulation; inward experience of distress, affliction, trouble
BDAG.pt: problema que inflige angústia, opressão, aflição, tribulação; experiência interna de angústia, aflição, problema

DEFINITION: to die, be dying, be dead.
ORIGIN: A strengthened form of a simpler primary thano than'-o (which is used for it only in certain tenses); to die (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to pass from physical life, die; to lose one’s relationship w. God, die
BDAG.pt: passar da vida física, morrer; perder o relacionamento com Deus, morrer

DEFINITION: mortal, subject to death.
ORIGIN: From thnesko; liable to die.

BDAG.en: mortal, pert. to being subject to death (opp. immortal), mere human.
BDAG.pt: mortal, pertencente a estar sujeito à morte (oposto a imortal), mero ser humano.

DEFINITION: to disturb greatly, terrify, strike with panic; mid: to show agitation of mind.
ORIGIN: From thorubos; to be in tumult, i.e. Disturb, clamor.
USAGE: make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar.

BDAG.en: throw into disorder, act. (set the city in an uproar); disturb, agitate; pass. be troubled, distressed, aroused.
BDAG.pt: lançar na desordem, ativamente (causar alvoroço na cidade); perturbar, agitar; passivamente ser perturbado, aflito, agitado.

DEFINITION: (a) din, hubbub, confused noise, outcry, (b) riot, disturbance.
ORIGIN: From the base of throeo; a disturbance.

BDAG.en: a raising of voices that contributes to lack of understanding, noise, clamor; a state of confusion, confusion, unrest; a state or condition of varying degrees of commotion, turmoil, excitement, uproar
BDAG.pt: elevação de vozes que contribui para a falta de entendimento, ruído, clamor; um estado de confusão, desordem, inquietação; um estado ou condição de graus variados de comoção, tumulto, excitação, alvoroço

DEFINITION: to crush, break, shatter; met: to break down.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to crush.

BDAG.en: to cause something to be broken into pieces, break; to cause something to lose its validity, break; to cause to be oppressed, break, weaken, oppress
BDAG.pt: causar que algo se quebre em pedaços, quebrar; causar que algo perca a validade, quebrar; causar opressão, quebrar, enfraquecer, oprimir

DEFINITION: (lit: a nursling, hence probably) plur: cattle.
ORIGIN: From trepho; stock (as raised on a farm).

BDAG.en: (domesticated) animal, esp. a sheep or goat.
BDAG.pt: animal (doméstico), especialmente uma ovelha ou cabra.

DEFINITION: intrans: to lament, wail; trans: to bewail.
ORIGIN: From threnos; to bewail.

BDAG.en: express oneself in sorrowful tones, mourn, lament; sing a dirge; mourn for someone in ritual fashion.
BDAG.pt: expressar-se em tons de tristeza, chorar, lamentar; cantar um cântico fúnebre; lamentar alguém de forma ritual.

DEFINITION: wailing, lamentation, dirge.
ORIGIN: From the base of throeo; wailing.

BDAG.en: ritual expression of lament for the dead, a dirge; expression of grief, lamentation (general sense).
BDAG.pt: expressão ritual de lamento pelos mortos, um epitáfio/canto fúnebre; expressão de tristeza, lamentação (sentido geral).

DEFINITION: (underlying sense: reverence or worship of the gods), worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of threskos; ceremonial observance.

BDAG.en: expression of devotion to transcendent beings, esp. as it expresses itself in cultic rites, worship; Judean cultic tradition; Christianity.
BDAG.pt: expressão de devoção a seres transcendentes, especialmente como se manifesta em ritos de culto, adoração; tradição cultual judaica; Cristianismo.

DEFINITION: (refers probably to a careful observance of religious restrictions), religious (probably in a limited sense), devout.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of throeo; ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. Pious.

BDAG.en: religious.
BDAG.pt: religioso.

DEFINITION: (properly: to lead one as prisoner in a triumphal procession, hence) to lead around, make a show (spectacle) of, cause to triumph.
ORIGIN: From a prolonged compound of the base of throeo; and a derivative of haptomai (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory.

BDAG.en: lead in a triumphal procession (as a captive); exhibit in triumph (God's victory over hostile forces); triumph over; expose to shame; display, publicize.
BDAG.pt: conduzir em procissão triunfal (como cativo); exibir em triunfo (vitória de Deus sobre forças hostis); triunfar sobre; expor à vergonha; exibir, tornar público.
