DEFINITION: to condemn, pass sentence upon.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of dike; to adjudge against, i.e. Pronounce guilty.

BDAG.en: condemn, find/pronounce guilty
BDAG.pt: condenar, achar/pronunciar culpado

DEFINITION: to hunt down, follow closely.
ORIGIN: From kata and dioko; to hunt down, i.e. Search for.

BDAG.en: search for eagerly, hunt for (nearly always ‘pursue’ in a hostile sense)
BDAG.pt: procurar com avidez, caçar (quase sempre com o sentido de 'perseguir' em sentido hostil)

DEFINITION: to enslave.
ORIGIN: From kata and douloo; to enslave utterly.

BDAG.en: enslave, reduce to slavery
BDAG.pt: escravizar, reduzir à escravidão

DEFINITION: to overpower, quell, treat harshly.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of dunastes; to exercise dominion against, i.e. Oppress.

BDAG.en: oppress, exploit, dominate
BDAG.pt: oprimir, explorar, dominar

DEFINITION: to shame, disgrace, bring to shame, put to utter confusion, frustrate.
ORIGIN: From kata and aischunomai; to shame down, i.e. Disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush.

BDAG.en: dishonor, disgrace; put to shame; disappoint
BDAG.pt: desonrar, envergonhar; fazer passar vergonha; desapontar

DEFINITION: to burn up, consume entirely.
ORIGIN: From kata and kaio; to burn down (to the ground), i.e. Consume wholly.

BDAG.en: burn down, burn up, consume by fire
BDAG.pt: incendiar, queimar, consumir pelo fogo

DEFINITION: to veil, cover the head.
ORIGIN: From kata and kalupto; to cover wholly, i.e. Veil.

BDAG.en: cover, veil (active and passive); cover oneself w. a veil
BDAG.pt: cobrir, velar (ativo e passivo); cobrir-se com um véu

DEFINITION: to boast against, exult over.
ORIGIN: From kata and kauchaomai; to exult against (i.e. Over).

BDAG.en: to boast at the expense of another, boast against, exult over; to have a cause for boasting because of advantage in power, triumph over
BDAG.pt: vangloriar-se à custa de outro, gabar-se contra, exultar sobre; ter motivo para se gabar devido a uma vantagem de poder, triunfar sobre

DEFINITION: to recline (at table); more often: to keep bed, be lying ill (in bed).
ORIGIN: From kata and keimai; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal.

BDAG.en: to be in a recumbent position free from any activity, lie down (rest); of sick people; to recline (on a couch) for the purpose of dining, recline for a meal, dine
BDAG.pt: estar numa posição reclinada, livre de qualquer atividade, deitar-se (repousar); de pessoas doentes; reclinar-se (num divã) para comer, reclinar-se para uma refeição, jantar

DEFINITION: to break in pieces, break up.
ORIGIN: From kata and klao; to break down, i.e. Divide.

BDAG.en: break in pieces
BDAG.pt: quebrar em pedaços

DEFINITION: to shut up, confine.
ORIGIN: From kata and kleio; to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. Incarcerate.

BDAG.en: shut up, lock up
BDAG.pt: fechar, trancar

DEFINITION: to give as an inheritance, distribute by lot.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of a compound of kleros and didomi; to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate.

BDAG.en: to assign possession of, give (over) as rightful possession; to lay claim to someth. that has been assigned, take possession of, occupy
BDAG.pt: atribuir a posse de, dar (como) posse legítima; reivindicar algo que foi atribuído, tomar posse, ocupar

DEFINITION: to cause to recline at table; mid. and pass: to recline at table.
ORIGIN: From kata and klino; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table.

BDAG.en: to lay down (act. cause to lie down or sit down to eat); pass. in active sense (of a dead person; recline at dinner)
BDAG.pt: fazer deitar (fazer com que se deitem ou sentem para comer); passivo com sentido ativo (de uma pessoa morta; reclinar-se para o jantar)

DEFINITION: to flood over, overwhelm, inundate.
ORIGIN: From kata and the base of kludon; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge.

BDAG.en: flood, inundate
BDAG.pt: inundar, alagar

DEFINITION: a deluge, flood.
ORIGIN: From katakluzo; an inundation.

BDAG.en: flood, deluge, in our lit. only of the flood in Noah’s time
BDAG.pt: inundação, dilúvio, na nossa literatura apenas do dilúvio no tempo de Noé

DEFINITION: to follow after.
ORIGIN: From kata and akoloutheo; to accompany closely.

BDAG.en: follow; Fig. approach or attain the wisdom of someone
BDAG.pt: seguir; Fig. aproximar-se ou atingir a sabedoria de alguém

DEFINITION: to cut up, cut in pieces, mangle, wound.
ORIGIN: From kata and kopto; to chop down, i.e. Mangle.

BDAG.en: to cut in a rough manner, lacerate, cut; break in pieces
BDAG.pt: cortar de maneira grosseira, lacerar, cortar; quebrar em pedaços

DEFINITION: to cast down headlong, throw over a precipice.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of kremnos; to precipitate down.

BDAG.en: throw down (from) a cliff
BDAG.pt: arremessar (de) um penhasco

DEFINITION: punishment following condemnation, penal servitude, penalty.
ORIGIN: From katakrino; an adverse sentence (the verdict).

BDAG.en: judicial pronouncement upon a guilty person, condemnation, punishment, penalty
BDAG.pt: pronunciamento judicial sobre uma pessoa culpada, condenação, punição, penalidade

DEFINITION: to condemn, judge worthy of punishment.
ORIGIN: From kata and krino; to judge against, i.e. Sentence.

BDAG.en: pronounce a sentence after determination of guilt, pronounce a sentence on; sentence someone to death; consign to destruction
BDAG.pt: pronunciar uma sentença após determinar a culpa, pronunciar uma sentença sobre; sentenciar alguém à morte; consignar à destruição

DEFINITION: condemnation, censure.
ORIGIN: From katakrino; sentencing adversely (the act).

BDAG.en: a judicial verdict involving a penalty, condemnation
BDAG.pt: um veredito judicial que envolve uma penalidade, condenação

DEFINITION: to exercise authority over, overpower, master.
ORIGIN: From kata and kurieuo; to lord against, i.e. Control, subjugate.
USAGE: exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome.

BDAG.en: to bring into subjection, become master, gain dominion over, subdue; become master, gain power; to have mastery, be master, lord it (over), rule over someone or something
BDAG.pt: trazer para a sujeição, tornar-se mestre, ganhar domínio sobre, subjugar; tornar-se mestre, ganhar poder; ter domínio, ser mestre, dominar (sobre), governar sobre alguém ou algo

DEFINITION: to speak evil of, rail at, slander.
ORIGIN: From katalalos; to be a traducer, i.e. To slander.

BDAG.en: speak ill of, speak degradingly of, speak evil of, defame, slander
BDAG.pt: falar mal de, falar de forma depreciativa, falar mal, difamar, caluniar

DEFINITION: evil-speaking, backbiting, detraction, slander.
ORIGIN: From katalalos; defamation.

BDAG.en: the act of speaking ill of another, evil speech, slander, defamation, detraction
BDAG.pt: o ato de falar mal de outro, fala má, calúnia, difamação, detração

DEFINITION: slanderous, back-biting; subst: a railer, defamer.
ORIGIN: From kata and the base of laleo; talkative against, i.e. A slanderer.

BDAG.en: pert. to speaking ill of others, slanderous; Subst. slanderer
BDAG.pt: relativo a falar mal dos outros, calunioso; Substantivo: caluniador

DEFINITION: (a) to seize tight hold of, arrest, catch, capture, appropriate, (b) to overtake, (c) mid. aor: to perceived, comprehended.
ORIGIN: From kata and lambano; to take eagerly, i.e. Seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take.

BDAG.en: 1 to make something one’s own, win, attain; 2 to gain control of someone through pursuit, catch up with, seize; 3 to come upon someone, with implication of surprise, catch; 4 to process information, understand, grasp
BDAG.pt: 1 tornar algo seu, ganhar, alcançar; 2 obter controle sobre alguém através de perseguição, alcançar, capturar; 3 alcançar alguém, com implicação de surpresa, pegar; 4 processar informação, entender, apreender

DEFINITION: to enter in a list, register, enroll.
ORIGIN: From kata and lego (in its original meaning); to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol.

BDAG.en: to make a selection for membership in a group, be selected or be enrolled
BDAG.pt: fazer uma seleção para fazer parte de um grupo, ser escolhido ou ser matriculado/inscrito

DEFINITION: a remnant, small residue.
ORIGIN: From kataleipo; a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few.

BDAG.en: remnant
BDAG.pt: remanescente, resto

DEFINITION: to leave behind, desert, abandon, forsake; to leave remaining, reserve.
ORIGIN: From kata and leipo; to leave down, i.e. Behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining.

BDAG.en: to cause to be left in a place, leave (behind); to depart from a place, leave; to cease from some activity, leave to one side, give up; to cause something to remain in existence or be left over, leave over, remain; to leave something with design before departing, leave behind; to cause to be left to one’s own resources, leave (behind), desert; to set something aside in the interest of something else, leave, abandon, give up, neglect
BDAG.pt: causar que fique em um lugar, deixar (para trás); partir de um lugar, deixar; cessar de alguma atividade, deixar de lado, desistir; causar que algo permaneça em existência ou seja deixado, deixar sobrando, permanecer; deixar algo com intenção antes de partir, deixar para trás; fazer com que alguém seja deixado aos próprios recursos, deixar (para trás), abandonar; colocar algo de lado em favor de outra coisa, deixar, abandonar, desistir, negligenciar

DEFINITION: to stone down, stone to death, overwhelm with stones.
ORIGIN: From kata and lithazo; to stone down, i.e. To death.

BDAG.en: stone to death someone
BDAG.pt: apedrejar alguém até a morte

DEFINITION: reconciliation, restoration to favor.
ORIGIN: From katallasso; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. Restoration to (the divine) favor.

BDAG.en: reestablishment of an interrupted or broken relationship, reconciliation (with God)
BDAG.pt: restabelecimento de um relacionamento interrompido ou rompido, reconciliação (com Deus)

DEFINITION: to change, exchange, reconcile.
ORIGIN: From kata and allasso; to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference.

BDAG.en: reconcile (exchange of hostility for a friendly relationship); (of God) reconcile someone to himself; (passive) be reconciled, become reconciled (to God, or between human beings)
BDAG.pt: reconciliar (trocar hostilidade por uma relação amigável); (de Deus) reconciliar alguém consigo mesmo; (passivo) ser reconciliado, tornar-se reconciliado (com Deus, ou entre seres humanos)

DEFINITION: left behind; the rest, the remainder.
ORIGIN: From kata and loipoy; left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest).

BDAG.en: left, remaining (the rest of humanity)
BDAG.pt: deixado, restante (o resto da humanidade)

DEFINITION: an inn, lodging-place.
ORIGIN: From kataluo; properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e. (by implication) a lodging-place.

BDAG.en: lodging place (inn is possible, but more likely lodging or guest-room, or dining-room)
BDAG.pt: lugar de hospedagem (estadia é possível, mas mais provável que seja alojamento, quarto de hóspedes ou sala de jantar)

DEFINITION: (lit: to loosen thoroughly), (a) trans: to break up, overthrow, destroy, both lit. and met., (b) to unyoke, unharness a carriage horse or pack animal; hence: to put up, lodge, find a lodging.
ORIGIN: From kata and luo; to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially (compare kataluma) to halt for the night.
USAGE: destroy, dissolve, be guest, lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down.

BDAG.en: to detach (in demolition); destroy, demolish, dismantle (buildings, the temple of God); fig. tear down; to end the effect or validity of something, abolish, annul, make invalid (the law); to bring to an end, ruin, suppress (rulers); to cease what one is doing, halt, rest, find lodging
BDAG.pt: desprender (na demolição); destruir, demolir, desmantelar (edifícios, o templo de Deus); fig. derrubar; pôr fim ao efeito ou validade de algo, abolir, anular, invalidar (a lei); levar ao fim, arruinar, suprimir (governantes); cessar o que se está fazendo, parar, descansar, encontrar alojamento

DEFINITION: to understand, take in a fact about, consider carefully.
ORIGIN: From kata and manthano; to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully.

BDAG.en: observe (well), notice, learn
BDAG.pt: observar (bem), notar, aprender

DEFINITION: to give evidence (bear witness) against.
ORIGIN: From kata and martureo; to testify against.

BDAG.en: bear witness against
BDAG.pt: testemunhar contra

DEFINITION: to wait, stay (with), remain, abide, dwell.
ORIGIN: From kata and meno; to stay fully, i.e. Reside.

BDAG.en: stay, live (where they were staying); stay with someone
BDAG.pt: ficar, morar (onde estavam hospedados); ficar com alguém

DEFINITION: along, apart, in private.
ORIGIN: From kata and accusative case plural feminine of monos (with chora implied); according to sole places, i.e. (adverbially) separately.

BDAG.en: alone (adverbial)
BDAG.pt: sozinho (advérbio)

DEFINITION: a curse, an accursed thing.
ORIGIN: From kata (intensive) and anathema; an imprecation.

BDAG.en: that which is devoted or given over to a deity, hence accursed thing
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é devotado ou entregue a uma divindade, portanto, coisa amaldiçoada

DEFINITION: to curse, devote to destruction.
ORIGIN: From kata (intensive) and anathematizo; to imprecate.

BDAG.en: curse
BDAG.pt: amaldiçoar

DEFINITION: to use up, spend, consume (as with fire).
ORIGIN: From kata and analisko; to consume utterly.

BDAG.en: consume (of fire)
BDAG.pt: consumir (de fogo)

DEFINITION: (properly a medical term: to stupefy, hence) to burden, encumber.
ORIGIN: From kata and narkao (to be numb); to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive).

BDAG.en: burden, be a burden to
BDAG.pt: sobrecarregar, ser um fardo para

DEFINITION: to make a sign (by nodding the head).
ORIGIN: From kata and neuo; to nod down (towards), i.e. (by analogy) to make signs to.

BDAG.en: signal (usually by means of a nod) to someone (the message is added in the infinitive)
BDAG.pt: sinalizar (geralmente com um aceno) para alguém (a mensagem é acrescentada no infinitivo)

DEFINITION: to take note of, perceive, consider carefully, discern, detect, make account of.
ORIGIN: From kata and noieo; to observe fully.

BDAG.en: notice, observe carefully; to look at in a reflective manner, consider, contemplate; to think about carefully, envisage, think about, notice; Consider, contemplate
BDAG.pt: notar, observar atentamente; olhar de forma reflexiva, considerar, contemplar; pensar cuidadosamente, imaginar, notar; Considerar, contemplar

DEFINITION: (a) to come down, either from high land to lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to the coast; hence met: to arrive at, reach (destination), (b) of property: to come down (descend) by inheritance to an heir.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of anti; to meet against, i.e. Arrive at (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to get to a geographical destination, come (to), arrive (at), reach; to reach a condition or goal, fig. extension of 1 arrive at, attain, meet
BDAG.pt: chegar a um destino geográfico, vir (a), chegar (a), alcançar; atingir uma condição ou objetivo, extensão figurada de 1 chegar a, alcançar, encontrar

DEFINITION: deep sleep, torpor, insensibility, stupor.
ORIGIN: From katanusso; a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with neuo or even with nux)) stupor (lethargy).

BDAG.en: stupefaction (a spirit of stupor)
BDAG.pt: estupor/entorpecimento (espírito de estupor)

DEFINITION: met: to be pierced, stung, smitten.
ORIGIN: From kata and nusso; to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick").

BDAG.en: be pierced, stabbed fig., of the feeling of sharp pain connected w. anxiety, remorse, etc. (they were cut to the heart)
BDAG.pt: ser ferido, perfurado fig., do sentimento de dor aguda ligada à ansiedade, remorso, etc. (foram cortados no coração)

DEFINITION: to deem (count) worthy.
ORIGIN: From kata and axioo; to deem entirely deserving.

BDAG.en: to consider someone worthy to receive some privilege, benefit, or recognition, consider worthy
BDAG.pt: considerar alguém digno de receber algum privilégio, benefício ou reconhecimento, considerar digno

DEFINITION: to trample down, trample under foot (lit. and met.), spurn.
ORIGIN: From kata and pateo; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain.

BDAG.en: to tread so heavily as to injure, trample under foot; to look on with scorn, trample under foot, treat with disdain
BDAG.pt: pisar com força a ponto de ferir, pisotear; olhar com desprezo, tratar com desdém

DEFINITION: (in the Old Testament of the rest attained by the settlement in Canaan), resting, rest, dwelling, habitation.
ORIGIN: From katapauo; reposing down, i.e. (by Hebraism) abode.

BDAG.en: state of cessation of work or activity, rest; place of rest
BDAG.pt: estado de cessação de trabalho ou atividade, descanso; lugar de descanso

DEFINITION: (a) trans: to cause to rest, bring to rest; to cause to refrain, (b) intrans: to rest.
ORIGIN: From kata and pauo; to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist.

BDAG.en: to cause to cease, stop, bring to an end; to cause persons to be at rest, cause to rest; to cease some activity, stop, rest, intr.
BDAG.pt: fazer cessar, parar, pôr fim a; fazer com que pessoas repousem, fazer descansar; cessar alguma atividade, parar, descansar (intransitivo)

DEFINITION: (lit: that which is spread out downwards, that which hangs down), a curtain, veil, of that which separated the Holy of Holies from the outer parts of the temple at Jerusalem, also of an outer curtain at the entrance to the Holy Place in the same temple.
ORIGIN: From a compound of kata and a congener of petomai; something spread thoroughly, i.e. (specially) the door screen (to the Most Holy Place) in the Jewish Temple.

BDAG.en: curtain (in the temple, separating the holy of holies from the holy place or covering the entrance)
BDAG.pt: cortina (no templo, separando o Santo dos Santos do lugar santo ou cobrindo a entrada)

DEFINITION: to drink down, swallow, devour, destroy, consume.
ORIGIN: From kata and pino; to drink down, i.e. Gulp entire (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to drink down, swallow, swallow up; to destroy completely, in the figure of one devouring or swallowing someth.; to cause the end of someth., swallow up fig.
BDAG.pt: beber, engolir, tragar; destruir completamente, na figura de quem devora ou engole algo; causar o fim de algo, engolir (figurado)

DEFINITION: to fall down, fall prostrate.
ORIGIN: From kata and pipto; to fall down.

BDAG.en: fall (down)
BDAG.pt: cair (para baixo)

DEFINITION: to sail down (from the high seas to the shore).
ORIGIN: From kata and pleo; to sail down upon a place, i.e. To land at.

BDAG.en: sail down fr. the ‘high seas’ toward the coast, sail toward
BDAG.pt: navegar para baixo ('do alto mar') em direção à costa, navegar em direção a

DEFINITION: to exhaust by labor or suffering, wear out, overpower, oppress.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of ponos; to labor down, i.e. Wear with toil (figuratively, harass).

BDAG.en: to cause distress through oppressive means, subdue, torment, wear out, oppress
BDAG.pt: causar aflição por meios opressivos, subjugar, atormentar, desgastar, oprimir

DEFINITION: to sink in the sea, pass: to drown, be submerged.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of the same as Pontos; to plunge down, i.e. Submerge.

BDAG.en: ‘throw into the sea’, then gener. drown, pass. be sunk, be drowned
BDAG.pt: 'jogar no mar', depois genericamente afogar, passar a ser afundado, ser afogado

DEFINITION: cursing; a curse; meton: a doomed one.
ORIGIN: From kata (intensive) and ara; imprecation, execration.

BDAG.en: curse, imprecation
BDAG.pt: maldição, imprecação

DEFINITION: to curse.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from katara; to execrate; by analogy, to doom.

BDAG.en: to curse, execrate
BDAG.pt: amaldiçoar, execrar

DEFINITION: (a) to make idle (inactive), make of no effect, annul, abolish, bring to naught, (b) to discharge, sever, separate from.
ORIGIN: From kata and argeo; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively.
USAGE: abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void.

BDAG.en: to cause someth. to be unproductive, use up, exhaust, waste; to cause someth. to lose its power or effectiveness, invalidate, make powerless; to cause someth. to come to an end or to be no longer in existence, abolish, wipe out, set
BDAG.pt: fazer com que algo se torne improdutivo, esgotar, desperdiçar; fazer com que algo perca seu poder ou eficácia, invalidar, tornar ineficaz; fazer com que algo chegue ao fim ou deixe de existir, abolir, eliminar

DEFINITION: to number among, count with.
ORIGIN: From kata and arithmeo; to reckon among.

BDAG.en: to enumerate, count; to include as an entity in a group, count among (belong to)
BDAG.pt: enumerar, contar; incluir como entidade em um grupo, contar entre (pertencer a)

DEFINITION: (a) to fit (join) together; met: to compact together, (b) act. and mid: to prepare, perfect, for his (its) full destination or use, bring into its proper condition (whether for the first time, or after a lapse).
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of artios; to complete thoroughly, i.e. Repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust.
USAGE: fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.

BDAG.en: to cause to be in a condition to function well, put in order, restore; to restore to a former condition, put to rights; to adjust, complete, make complete; (passive) be trained, practiced; to prepare for a purpose, prepare, make, create, outfit; to furnish, equip
BDAG.pt: fazer com que esteja em condição de funcionar bem, pôr em ordem, restaurar; restaurar a uma condição anterior, consertar; ajustar, completar, tornar completo; (passivo) ser treinado, praticado; preparar para um propósito, preparar, fazer, criar, equipar; fornecer, aparelhar

DEFINITION: a preparing, an equipping.
ORIGIN: From katartizo; thorough equipment (subjectively).

BDAG.en: the process of perfecting, maturation
BDAG.pt: o processo de aperfeiçoamento, maturação

DEFINITION: a bringing to a condition of fitness, perfecting.
ORIGIN: From katartizo; complete furnishing (objectively).

BDAG.en: equipment, equipping
BDAG.pt: equipamento, aparelhamento

DEFINITION: to shake (the hand) up and down, wave; intrans: to beckon for silence.
ORIGIN: From kata and seio; to sway downward, i.e. Make a signal.

BDAG.en: to make rapid motions, shake, wave; to signal by a gesture, motion, make a sign
BDAG.pt: fazer movimentos rápidos, sacudir, acenar; sinalizar por um gesto, um movimento, fazer um sinal

DEFINITION: to dig down under, demolish, undermine.
ORIGIN: From kata and skapto; to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy.

BDAG.en: tear down, raze to the ground
BDAG.pt: derrubar, arrasar

DEFINITION: to build, construct, prepare, make ready.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of skeuos; to prepare thoroughly (properly, by external equipment; whereas hetoimazo refers rather to internal fitness); by implication, to construct, create.

BDAG.en: to make ready for some purpose, make ready, prepare; to bring a structure into being, build, construct, erect, create; to furnish, equip
BDAG.pt: preparar para algum propósito, deixar pronto, preparar; trazer uma estrutura à existência, construir, erguer, criar; prover, equipar

DEFINITION: to encamp, take up quarters, tabernacle, pitch tent, dwell.
ORIGIN: From kata and skenoo; to camp down, i.e. Haunt; figuratively, to remain.

BDAG.en: to provide with an abode, cause to dwell, take up an abode, live, settle
BDAG.pt: prover com uma morada, fazer habitar, tomar residência, viver, estabelecer-se

DEFINITION: a dwelling-place.
ORIGIN: From kataskenoo; an encamping, i.e. (figuratively) a perch.

BDAG.en: the act of taking up residence, taking up lodging; provision for shelter, a place to live
BDAG.pt: o ato de tomar residência, alojamento; provisão de abrigo, um lugar para viver

DEFINITION: to overshadow.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of skia; to overshade, i.e. Cover.

BDAG.en: overshadow
BDAG.pt: sombrear

DEFINITION: to view closely, inspect, spy out.
ORIGIN: From kataskopos; to be a sentinel, i.e. To inspect insidiously.

BDAG.en: spy out, lie in wait for
BDAG.pt: espiar, espreitar

DEFINITION: a spy, scout.
ORIGIN: From kata (intensive) and skopos (in the sense of a watcher); a reconnoiterer.

BDAG.en: a spy
BDAG.pt: um espião

DEFINITION: to deal craftily with, outwit.

DEFINITION: to strew or spread over; to lay low, overthrow.

DEFINITION: to pull down, drag away.
ORIGIN: From kata and suro; to drag down, i.e. Arrest judicially.

BDAG.en: drag (away by force)
BDAG.pt: arrastar (à força)

DEFINITION: to slaughter, kill off, slay.
ORIGIN: From kata and sphazo; to kill down, i.e. Slaughter.

DEFINITION: to seal up, secure with a seal.
ORIGIN: From kata and sphragizo; to seal closely.

BDAG.en: seal (up)

DEFINITION: a possession, holding fast.
ORIGIN: From katecho; a holding down, i.e. Occupancy.

BDAG.en: possession, taking into possession; holding back, restraining
BDAG.pt: posse, tomada de posse; contenção, restrição

DEFINITION: (a) to lay down, deposit, (b) mid: to lay down or deposit a favor, with the view of receiving one in return, seek favor.
ORIGIN: From kata and tithemi; to place down, i.e. Deposit (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: lay (down), place; grant, give (a favor)
BDAG.pt: deitar (abaixar), colocar; conceder, dar (um favor)

DEFINITION: a mutilation, spoiling.
ORIGIN: From a compound of kata and temno (to cut); a cutting down (off), i.e. Mutilation (ironically).

BDAG.en: mutilation, cutting in pieces
BDAG.pt: mutilação, corte em pedaços

DEFINITION: to strike down with an arrow.
ORIGIN: From kata and a derivative of toxon; to shoot down with an arrow or other missile.

BDAG.en: shoot down with a missile
BDAG.pt: abater com um projétil

DEFINITION: to run down.
ORIGIN: From kata and trecho; to run down, i.e. Hasten from a tower.

BDAG.en: run down
BDAG.pt: correr para baixo, atingir correndo

DEFINITION: to bear down, overpower; to give a vote or verdict, bring charges.
ORIGIN: From kata and phero (including its alternate); to bear down, i.e. (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a vote.

BDAG.en: bring down, cast against (vote/charges), get into a state of being (sink into sleep)
BDAG.pt: trazer para baixo, votar contra (acusação), entrar em um estado (afundar no sono)

DEFINITION: to flee for refuge (implying that the refuge is reached); aor. indicates moment of arrival.
ORIGIN: From kata and pheugo; to flee down (away).

BDAG.en: to get away from an area (flee), gain shelter from danger, take refuge
BDAG.pt: fugir de uma área (fugir), obter abrigo de um perigo, refugiar-se

DEFINITION: to destroy entirely.
ORIGIN: From kata and phtheiro; to spoil entirely, i.e. (literally) to destroy; or (figuratively) to deprave.

BDAG.en: destroy; ruin, corrupt (someone); be ruined, become useless
BDAG.pt: destruir; arruinar, corromper (alguém); ser arruinado, tornar-se inútil

DEFINITION: to kiss affectionately.
ORIGIN: From kata and phileo; to kiss earnestly.

BDAG.en: kiss someone in greeting or in farewell; (kiss) feet
BDAG.pt: beijar alguém em saudação ou despedida; (beijar) os pés

DEFINITION: to despise, scorn, and show it by active insult, disregard.
ORIGIN: From kata and phroneo; to think against, i.e. Disesteem.

BDAG.en: to look down on someone or something with contempt or aversion, despise, scorn, treat with contempt; to consider something not important enough, care nothing for, disregard, be unafraid of
BDAG.pt: olhar para baixo de alguém ou algo com desprezo ou aversão, desprezar, escarnecer, tratar com desprezo; considerar algo não importante o suficiente, não se importar, desconsiderar, não ter medo de

DEFINITION: a despiser, scorner.
ORIGIN: From kataphroneo; a contemner.

BDAG.en: despiser, scoffer
BDAG.pt: aquele que despreza, zombador

DEFINITION: to pour (down) upon.
ORIGIN: From kata and cheo (to pour); to pour down (out).

BDAG.en: pour out or down over

DEFINITION: under the earth, subterranean, infernal.
ORIGIN: From kata and chthon (the ground); subterranean, i.e. Infernal (belonging to the world of departed spirits).

BDAG.en: under the earth, subterranean (beings or powers)
BDAG.pt: debaixo da terra, subterrâneo (seres ou poderes)

DEFINITION: to use to the full, use up.
ORIGIN: From kata and chraomai; to overuse, i.e. Misuse.

BDAG.en: use (make full use of, misuse, use up)
BDAG.pt: usar (fazer uso completo de, usar mal, gastar)

DEFINITION: to cool, refresh.
ORIGIN: From kata and psucho; to cool down (off), i.e. Refresh.

BDAG.en: cool off, refresh
BDAG.pt: esfriar, refrescar

DEFINITION: full of images of idols, grossly idolatrous.
ORIGIN: From kata (intensively) and eidolon; utterly idolatrous.

BDAG.en: full of cult-images/idols
BDAG.pt: cheio de imagens de culto/ídolos

DEFINITION: opposite, in front (of), over against.
ORIGIN: From kata and enanti; directly opposite.

BDAG.en: opposite; before someone (in the sight of); opposite (marker of position)
BDAG.pt: em frente; diante de alguém (à vista de); oposto (indicador de posição)

DEFINITION: before the face of, over against.
ORIGIN: From kata and enopion; directly in front of.
USAGE: before (the presence of), in the sight of.

BDAG.en: in front of, right opposite: in the presence of God; before
BDAG.pt: em frente a, bem oposto a: na presença de Deus; diante de

DEFINITION: to have (exercise) power (authority) over.
ORIGIN: From kata and exousiazo; to have (wield) full privilege over.

BDAG.en: exercise authority, perhaps tyrannize over someone
BDAG.pt: exercer autoridade, talvez tiranizar sobre alguém

DEFINITION: to effect by labor, achieve, work out, bring about.
ORIGIN: From kata and ergazomai; to work fully, i.e. Accomplish; by implication, to finish, fashion.

BDAG.en: to bring about a result by doing someth., achieve, accomplish, do; to cause a state or condition, bring about, produce, create; to cause to be well prepared, prepare someone; to be successful in the face of obstacles, overpower, subdue, conquer
BDAG.pt: produzir um resultado através da ação, alcançar, realizar, fazer; causar um estado ou condição, produzir, criar; fazer com que algo esteja bem preparado, preparar alguém; ser bem-sucedido diante de obstáculos, subjugar, vencer

DEFINITION: to come down from sky to earth, or from high land to lower land (or to the coast), or from the high seas to the shore.

BDAG.en: to move in a direction considered the opposite of up but not necessarily with suggestion of a gradient, come down; to arrive at a place, arrive, put in, nautical t.t. of ships and those who sail in them
BDAG.pt: mover-se numa direção considerada oposta a 'para cima', mas não necessariamente com sugestão de inclinação, descer; chegar a um lugar, chegar, aportar, termo náutico para navios e seus tripulantes

DEFINITION: to eat up, eat till it is finished, devour, squander, annoy, injure.
ORIGIN: From kata and esthio (including its alternate); to eat down, i.e. Devour (literally or figuratively).

DEFINITION: (a) to make straight, (b) met: to put in the right way, direct.
ORIGIN: From kata and euthuno; to straighten fully, i.e. (figuratively) direct.

BDAG.en: gener. ‘make/keep straight’, lead, direct
BDAG.pt: geralmente, 'tornar/manter reto', conduzir, direcionar

DEFINITION: to rush, assault, rise up against.
ORIGIN: From kata and ephistemi; to stand over against, i.e. Rush upon (assault).

DEFINITION: (a) to hold fast, bind, arrest, (b) to take possession of, lay hold of, (c) to hold back, detain, restrain, (d) to hold a ship, keep its head.
ORIGIN: From kata and echo; to hold down (fast), in various applications (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: have, hold (fast), keep (in memory), let, X make toward, possess, retain, seize on, stay, take, withhold.

BDAG.en: to prevent the doing of something or cause to be ineffective, prevent, hinder, restrain; to adhere firmly to traditions, convictions, or beliefs, hold to, hold fast; to keep in one’s possession, possess; to keep within limits in a confining manner, confine; to take into one’s possession, occupy; lay claim to; hold course, nautical term, intransitive

BDAG.pt: falar contra; quase sempre como termo legal: apresentar acusações em tribunal perante um juiz humano: acusar alguém de algo; perante o tribunal de Deus; sem conotação legal acusar, repreender.

DEFINITION: an accusation, charge.

BDAG.en: accusation
BDAG.pt: acusação

DEFINITION: an accuser, prosecutor.
ORIGIN: From kata and agora; against one in the assembly, i.e. A complainant at law; specially, Satan.

BDAG.en: accuser
BDAG.pt: acusador

DEFINITION: a downcast countenance as a sign of sorrow, gloominess, gloom, dejection.

BDAG.en: gloominess, dejection
BDAG.pt: pessimismo, abatimento, tristeza profunda

BDAG.pt: comunicar; relatar, informar; ser informado, aprender; ensinar, instruir

DEFINITION: to rust; pass: to be rusted, tarnished.

BDAG.pt: enferrujar, tornar-se baço, corroer (de ouro e prata)

BDAG.pt: ter força ou capacidade para obter vantagem, ser dominante, prevalecer; ser capaz de; ter a capacidade de derrotar, vencer

BDAG.pt: morada, habitação

DEFINITION: to shear, cut the hair of; mid: to cut own hair, have hair cut.

DEFINITION: a word of command, a call, an arousing outcry.

BDAG.pt: sinal, (grito de) comando

DEFINITION: to command, order, direct, bid.

BDAG.pt: dar um comando, ordinariamente de natureza oficial, ordenar, mandar, instar

DEFINITION: vainglory, empty pride.

BDAG.pt: 1 uma autoavaliação vã ou exagerada, vaidade, presunção, ambição excessiva; 2 opinião vã ou sem valor, ilusão, engano, erro

DEFINITION: vainglorious, boastful.

BDAG.pt: geralmente 'vazio'; 1 relativo a estar sem algo material, vazio; 2 relativo a ser destituído de valor intelectual, moral ou espiritual, extensão figurada de sentido 'vazio'; 3 relativo a ser sem propósito ou resultado, em vão

DEFINITION: empty disputing, worthless babble.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of kenos and phone; empty sounding, i.e. Fruitless discussion.

DEFINITION: a sting, goad; met: of death.

DEFINITION: a centurion, an officer commanding about a hundred infantry in the Roman army.

DEFINITION: falsely, in vain, to no purpose.

BDAG.pt: advérbio de κενός: relativo a ser sem efeito ou sem propósito, de maneira vazia, inutilmente, em vão

DEFINITION: a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet, distinguishing them from other little letters, or a separation stroke between letters.

BDAG.pt: lit. 'chifre', então qualquer coisa que se projeta como um chifre, projeção, gancho como parte de uma letra, um serifa

DEFINITION: a potter.

DEFINITION: of clay, made by a potter, earthen.

DEFINITION: a pitcher, earthen vessel, jar.

DEFINITION: a tile; practically: the roof.

BDAG.en: 1 one who takes part in someth. with someone, companion, partner, sharer; 2 one who permits someone else to share in someth., sharer.
BDAG.pt: 1 aquele que toma parte em algo com alguém, companheiro, sócio, partilhador; 2 aquele que permite que outro compartilhe em algo, partilhador.

DEFINITION: (a) a bed, (b) a marriage bed; plur: repeated (immoral) sexual intercourse.
ORIGIN: From keimai; a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the male sperm.

BDAG.en: a structure for lying down, bed; specifically, the marriage-bed; sexual intercourse, seminal emission.
BDAG.pt: estrutura para deitar, leito; especificamente, leito conjugal; relações sexuais, emissão seminal.

DEFINITION: a bed-chamber.
ORIGIN: From koite; a bedroom.

BDAG.en: bedroom; used in titles like 'the one in charge of the bed-chamber' (chamberlain).
BDAG.pt: quarto de dormir; usado em títulos como 'o encarregado da câmara de dormir' (camareiro).

DEFINITION: crimson, scarlet, dyed with Kermes (coccum), the female coccus of the Kermes oak.
ORIGIN: From kokkos (from the kernel-shape of the insect); crimson-colored.

BDAG.en: red, scarlet; scarlet cloth or garment (often referring to a soldier's cloak or an apocalyptic color).
BDAG.pt: vermelho, escarlate; pano ou vestimenta escarlate (frequentemente referindo-se a um manto de soldado ou cor apocalíptica).

DEFINITION: a kernel, grain, seed.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed.

BDAG.en: generically 'grain, seed'; 1. the kernel of various plants, seed, grain (mustard, wheat); 2. formerly thought to be a berry (kermes insect), used for purplish-red dye; by metonymy applied to the color ('scarlet') or the dyed fabric
BDAG.pt: geralmente 'grão, semente'; 1. o caroço de várias plantas, semente, grão (mostarda, trigo); 2. antigamente considerado uma baga (inseto Kermes), usado para um corante vermelho-púrpura; por metonímia, aplicado à cor ('escarlate') ou ao tecido tingido

DEFINITION: to chastise, curtail, punish; mid: to cause to be punished.
ORIGIN: From kolos (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction).

BDAG.en: penalize, punish (actively or passively, often referring to divine judgment or hell).
BDAG.pt: penalizar, punir (ativa ou passivamente, muitas vezes referindo-se a julgamento divino ou inferno).

DEFINITION: flattery, with a view to advantage or gain.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of kolax (a fawner); flattery.

BDAG.en: flattery, flattering words
BDAG.pt: bajulação, palavras lisonjeiras

DEFINITION: chastisement, punishment, torment, perhaps with the idea of deprivation.
ORIGIN: From kolazo; penal infliction.

BDAG.en: infliction of suffering or pain in chastisement, punishment; transcendent retribution, punishment (of eternal punishment, of hell)
BDAG.pt: aplicação de sofrimento ou dor em castigo, punição; retribuição transcendente, castigo (de punição eterna, do inferno)

DEFINITION: to strike with the fist, buffet; hence: to mistreat violently.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the base of kolazo; to rap with the fist.

BDAG.en: to strike sharply, esp. with the hand, strike with the fist, beat, cuff; to cause physical impairment, torment (fig. extension, of painful attacks of an illness)
BDAG.pt: golpear firmemente, especialmente com a mão, bater com o punho, esbofetear; causar prejuízo físico, atormentar (extensão figurada, de ataques dolorosos de uma doença)

DEFINITION: (lit: to glue); hence: mid. and pass: to join myself closely, cleave, adhere (to), to keep company (with), of friendly intercourse.
ORIGIN: From kolla ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to join closely together, bind closely, unite; to be closely associated, cling to, attach to (literally, figuratively, of sins; join oneself to, become a follower/disciple of someone, cling to what is good)
BDAG.pt: unir estreitamente, ligar firmemente, associar; estar estreitamente associado, apegar-se, prender-se (literalmente, figurativamente, de pecados; unir-se, tornar-se seguidor/discípulo de alguém, apegar-se ao que é bom)

DEFINITION: eye salve.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of kollura (a cake; prob akin to the base of kollao); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster.

BDAG.en: eyesalve (a medical compound applied to the eyes)
BDAG.pt: colírio (um composto medicinal aplicado aos olhos)

DEFINITION: a money-changer, who changed heathen into Jewish money, for payment into the Temple treasury.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of kollubos (a small coin; probably akin to kollourion); a coin-dealer.

BDAG.en: money-changer
BDAG.pt: cambista

DEFINITION: (lit: to maim, mutilate), to cut short, shorten, abbreviate.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the base of kolazo; to dock, i.e. (figuratively) abridge.

BDAG.en: ‘mutilate, curtail’. 1 to cause someth. not to be full length, to shorten, lit., of stones 2 to reduce the duration of someth., shorten, fig. extension of 1: the last days
BDAG.pt: 'mutilar, abreviar'. 1 fazer com que algo não tenha o comprimento total, encurtar, literalmente, de pedras 2 reduzir a duração de algo, encurtar, extensão figurada de 1: os últimos dias

DEFINITION: Colossae, a town of the Roman province Asia, in the Lycus valley, near Laodicea and Hierapolis.
ORIGIN: Apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossae, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Colossae, once a flourishing city, later less important, in Phrygia in Asia Minor.
BDAG.pt: Colossos, uma vez uma cidade florescente, mais tarde menos importante, na Frígia, na Ásia Menor.

DEFINITION: Colossian.
ORIGIN: From Kolossai; a Colossaean, (i.e. Inhabitant of Colossae.

BDAG.en: Colossian, subst. ὁΚ. the Colossian
BDAG.pt: Colossense, substantivo ὁΚ. o colossense

DEFINITION: (a) sing. and plur: bosom; (sinus) the overhanging fold of the garment used as a pocket, (b) a bay, gulf.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy, a bay.

BDAG.en: var. mngs. in gener. lit. usage, freq. w. suggestion of curvature and the hollow so formed, as of a person’s chest, folds in a garment or a bay of the sea; our lit. contains no application of the term to anatomical parts uniquely female. 1 bosom, breast, chest 2 the fold of a garment, fold, formed as it falls from the chest over the girdle... this fold was used as a pocket. 3 a part of the sea that indents a shoreline, bay
BDAG.pt: várias acepções no uso literário em geral, frequentemente com sugestão de curvatura e o recesso assim formado, como o peito de uma pessoa, dobras em uma vestimenta ou uma baía do mar; nossa literatura não contém aplicação do termo a partes anatômicas unicamente femininas. 1 seio, peito, tórax 2 a dobra de uma vestimenta, prega, formada quando cai do peito sobre o cinto... esta prega era usada como um bolso. 3 uma parte do mar que se indentar em uma linha costeira, baía

DEFINITION: (properly: to dive, hence) to swim.
ORIGIN: From kolumbos (a diver); to plunge into water.

BDAG.en: 1 swim up and down, lit. ‘dive’ 2 swim
BDAG.pt: 1 nadar de um lado para o outro, literalmente 'mergulhar' 2 nadar

DEFINITION: (lit: a diving or swimming place), a pool.
ORIGIN: A diving-place, i.e. Pond for bathing (or swimming).

BDAG.en: pool, swimming-pool (used for bathing)
BDAG.pt: piscina, tanque de natação (usado para banho)

DEFINITION: a colony, a city settlement of Roman (soldier) citizens; a garrison city.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans.

BDAG.en: a city or town outside Italy whose inhabitants enjoyed special political privileges: colony, of Philippi in Macedonia, settled by Augustus
BDAG.pt: uma cidade ou vila fora da Itália cujos habitantes gozavam de privilégios políticos especiais: colônia, de Filipos na Macedônia, fundada por Augusto

DEFINITION: to wear the hair long, allow the hair to grow out.
ORIGIN: From kome; to wear tresses of hair.

BDAG.en: to wear long hair, let one's hair grow long
BDAG.pt: usar cabelo comprido, deixar o cabelo crescer

DEFINITION: hair, long hair.
ORIGIN: Apparently from the same as komizo; the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from thrix; which properly denotes merely the scalp).

BDAG.en: hair of a person’s head, (long) hair of women... κ. οὔλη curly hair
BDAG.pt: cabelo da cabeça de uma pessoa, cabelo (longo) de mulheres... κ. οὔλη cabelo encaracolado

DEFINITION: (a) act: to convey, bring, carry, (b) mid: to receive back, receive what has belonged to myself but has been lost, or else promised but kept back, or: to get what has come to be own by earning, recover.
ORIGIN: From a primary komeo (to tend, i.e. Take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain).

BDAG.en: 1 to convey someth. to a specific destination, bring... 2 to get back someth. that is one’s own or owed to one, get back, recover... 3 to come into possession of someth. or experience someth., carry off, get (for oneself), receive freq. as recompense
BDAG.pt: 1 levar algo a um destino específico, trazer... 2 reaver algo que é seu ou lhe é devido, recuperar... 3 vir a possuir algo ou experimentar algo, levar, obter (para si), receber frequentemente como recompensa

DEFINITION: in better health.
ORIGIN: Neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of komizo (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. Nice); figuratively, convalescent.

BDAG.en: better of sick persons: κ. ἔχειν begin to improve
BDAG.pt: melhor no caso de doentes: κ. ἔχειν começar a melhorar

DEFINITION: to whitewash, plaster over.
ORIGIN: From konia (dust; by analogy, lime); to whitewash.

BDAG.en: whitewash... a whitewashed wall... whitewashed tombs... w. implicit satire: the Pharisees are unwittingly a source of defilement
BDAG.pt: encalcar com cal... uma parede caiada... túmulos caiados... com sátira implícita: os fariseus são involuntariamente fonte de impureza

DEFINITION: dust.
ORIGIN: From the base of koniao and ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown about).

BDAG.en: dust... shake the dust from one’s feet... throw dust into the air... raise dust... A cloud of dust
BDAG.pt: poeira... sacudir a poeira dos pés... jogar poeira no ar... levantar poeira... Uma nuvem de poeira

DEFINITION: to abate, cease raging, be stilled.
ORIGIN: From kopos; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax.

BDAG.en: abate, stop, rest, cease... the wind fell
BDAG.pt: acalmar, parar, descansar, cessar... o vento cessou

DEFINITION: beating of the breast or head in lamentation, lamentation.
ORIGIN: From kopto; mourning (properly, by beating the breast).

BDAG.en: mourning, lamentation acc. to custom in many parts of the Mediterranean world this was accompanied by breast-beating
BDAG.pt: luto, lamentação de acordo com o costume em muitas partes do mundo mediterrâneo, isto era acompanhado de bater no peito

DEFINITION: a cutting in pieces, slaughter.
ORIGIN: From kopto; cutting, i.e. Carnage.

BDAG.en: cutting down, slaughter... return fr. the defeat of (i.e., fr. defeating) the kings
BDAG.pt: corte, matança... voltar da derrota dos (i.e., de derrotar) reis

DEFINITION: (a) to grow weary, (b) to toil, work with effort (of bodily and mental labor alike).
ORIGIN: From a derivative of kopos; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard.

BDAG.en: 1 become weary/tired... 2 to exert oneself physically, mentally, or spiritually, work hard, toil, strive, struggle
BDAG.pt: 1 ficar cansado/exaurido... 2 esforçar-se física, mental ou espiritualmente, trabalhar arduamente, labutar, lutar, esforçar-se

DEFINITION: (a) trouble, (b) toil, labor, laborious toil, involving weariness and fatigue.
ORIGIN: From kopto; a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication, pains.

BDAG.en: a state of discomfort or distress, trouble, difficulty; work, labor, toil; labor of love; reward for labor
BDAG.pt: um estado de desconforto ou aflição, dificuldade, labuta; trabalho, esforço, lida; trabalho de amor; recompensa pelo trabalho

DEFINITION: manure; a dung-hill.
ORIGIN: From kopros (ordure; perhaps akin to kopto); manure.

BDAG.en: manure pile
BDAG.pt: monte de esterco

DEFINITION: (a) to cut, cut off, strike, smite, (b) mid: to beat breast or head in lamentation, lament, mourn, sometimes with acc. of person whose loss is mourned.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief.
USAGE: cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail. Compare the base of tomoteros.

BDAG.en: cut (off); beat one’s breast as an act of mourning, mourn (greatly)
BDAG.pt: cortar (arrancar); bater no peito como ato de luto, lamentar (profundamente)

DEFINITION: a raven, crow.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from korennumi; a crow (from its voracity).

BDAG.en: crow, raven
BDAG.pt: corvo, gralha

DEFINITION: a little girl, a young girl; a girl, maiden.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of kore (a maiden); a (little) girl.

BDAG.en: girl, young woman (diminutive of κόρη)
BDAG.pt: menina, moça (diminutivo de κόρη)

DEFINITION: a gift, offering, anything consecrated to God.
ORIGIN: Korbanas (kor-ban-as') of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (qorban); a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. The room where the contribution boxes stood.

BDAG.en: something consecrated as a gift for God and closed to ordinary human use, gift to God, corban
BDAG.pt: algo consagrado como presente para Deus e fechado ao uso humano comum, dom para Deus, corban

DEFINITION: Korah, an Israelite.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Qorach); Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Korah, head of a rebellion against Moses
BDAG.pt: Coré, chefe de uma rebelião contra Moisés

DEFINITION: to fill, sate, glut, feed full, satisfy.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to cram, i.e. Glut or sate.

BDAG.en: satiate, fill; be satiated, have enough (literally: eaten enough; figuratively: think one has enough spiritual food)
BDAG.pt: satiar, encher; ser saciado, ter o suficiente (literalmente: ter comido o bastante; figurativamente: pensar que já se tem todo o alimento espiritual necessário)

DEFINITION: Corinthian, of Corinth.
ORIGIN: From Korinthos; a Corinthian, i.e. Inhabitant of Corinth.

BDAG.en: the Corinthian (inhabitant of Corinth)
BDAG.pt: o coríntio (habitante de Corinto)

DEFINITION: Corinth, in north-east Peloponnese, the capital of the Roman province Achaia.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece.

BDAG.en: Corinth a city in Greece on the isthmus of the same name.
BDAG.pt: Corinto, uma cidade na Grécia no istmo de mesmo nome.

DEFINITION: Cornelius, a centurion of the Roman army, stationed at Caesarea.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; Cornelius, a Roman.

BDAG.en: Cornelius, a Roman centurion in Caesarea by the sea
BDAG.pt: Cornélio, um centurião romano em Cesareia marítima

DEFINITION: a cor (a Hebrew measure equiv. to about 15 bushels).
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (kor); a cor, i.e. A specific measure.

BDAG.en: a Heb. dry measure ('רֹּכcor, kor'), a measure of capacity for grain, flour, etc.; acc. to Jos., Ant. 15, 314=ten Attic medimni, hence about 393 liters=about 4 hectoliters, or betw. ten and twelve bushels; measure Lk 16:7.
BDAG.pt: uma medida seca hebraica ('רֹּכcor, kor'), uma medida de capacidade para grãos, farinha, etc.; de acordo com Josefo, Ant. 15, 314 = dez medimnos áticos, ou seja, cerca de 393 litros = cerca de 4 hectolitros, ou entre dez e doze alqueires; medida em Lucas 16:7.

DEFINITION: to put into order; to decorate, deck, adorn.
ORIGIN: From kosmos; to put in proper order, i.e. Decorate (literally or figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick).

BDAG.en: 1 to put in order so as to appear neat or well organized, make neat/tidy... trim, of lamps. 2 to cause someth. to have an attractive appearance through decoration, adorn, decorate... b fig. a make beautiful or attractive inwardly, morally... b adorn, do credit to
BDAG.pt: 1 arrumar de modo a parecer limpo ou bem organizado, tornar limpo/arrumado... aparar, no caso de lâmpadas. 2 fazer com que algo tenha uma aparência atraente através de decoração, enfeitar, decorar... b fig. a tornar belo ou atraente internamente, moralmente... b adornar, dar crédito a

DEFINITION: earthly, worldly (belonging to the present earthly world as opposed to the heavenly and future).
ORIGIN: From kosmos (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt).

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to the earth as a physical phenomenon, earthly... 2 pert. to interests prevailing on earth, worldly, w. the implication of that which is at enmity w. God or morally reprehensible
BDAG.pt: 1 relativo à terra como um fenômeno físico, terreno... 2 relativo a interesses predominantes na terra, mundano, com a implicação daquilo que é contrário a Deus ou moralmente repreensível

DEFINITION: orderly, virtuous, decent, modest, well-ordered.
ORIGIN: From kosmos (in its primary sense); orderly, i.e. Decorous.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to having characteristics or qualities that evoke admiration or delight, an expression of high regard for pers., respectable, honorable pers.... 2 pert. to being appropriate for winning approval, appropriate, used w. an impers. noun, yet w. ref. to a pers., whose special status is prob. signalled thereby
BDAG.pt: 1 relativo a ter características ou qualidades que evocam admiração ou deleite, uma expressão de alta estima por uma pessoa, respeitável, honrosa... 2 relativo a ser apropriado para ganhar aprovação, apropriado, usado com um substantivo impessoal, mas com referência a uma pessoa, cujo status especial é provavelmente sinalizado por isso

DEFINITION: ruler of this world, that is, of the world as asserting its independence of God; used of the angelic or demonic powers controlling the sublunary world.
ORIGIN: From kosmos and krateo; a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan.

BDAG.en: world-ruler (used of world-ruling gods... Then gener. of spirit beings, who have parts of the cosmos under their control... of evil spirits)
BDAG.pt: dominador do mundo (usado para deuses dominadores do mundo... Então, geralmente, para seres espirituais que têm partes do cosmos sob seu controle... de espíritos malignos)

DEFINITION: the world, universe; worldly affairs; the inhabitants of the world; adornment.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of komizo; orderly arrangement, i.e. Decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)).

BDAG.en: 1 that which serves to beautify through decoration, adornment, adorning... 2 condition of orderliness, orderly arrangement, order... 3 the sum total of everything here and now, the world, the (orderly) universe... 4 the sum total of all beings above the level of the animals, the world... 5 planet earth as a place of inhabitation, the world
BDAG.pt: 1 aquilo que serve para embelezar através de decoração, adorno, adorno... 2 condição de ordem, arranjo ordenado, ordem... 3 a soma total de tudo o que está aqui e agora, o mundo, o universo (ordenado)... 4 a soma total de todos os seres acima do nível dos animais, o mundo... 5 o planeta terra como lugar de habitação, o mundo

DEFINITION: Quartus, a Christian, brother of Erastus the Corinthian.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Quartus, an otherwise unknown Christian
BDAG.pt: Quarto, um cristão de outra forma desconhecido

DEFINITION: (Aramaic) arise, stand up.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (quwm); cumi (i.e. Rise!).

DEFINITION: a guard, watch.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. A Roman sentry.

DEFINITION: to make light (in weight).
ORIGIN: From kouphos (light in weight); to unload.

BDAG.en: to lighten (used in LXX)
BDAG.pt: aliviar, tornar leve (usado na LXX)

DEFINITION: a large basket.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a (small) basket.

BDAG.en: basket, in the NT prob. a large, heavy basket, probably of var. sizes, for carrying things
BDAG.pt: cesto, no NT provavelmente um cesto grande e pesado, de vários tamanhos, para transportar coisas

DEFINITION: a bed, mattress, mat of a poor man.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; a mattress.

BDAG.en: mattress, pallet, the poor man’s bed
BDAG.pt: colchão, esteira, a cama do pobre

DEFINITION: to cry aloud, shriek.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat).

BDAG.en: to make a vehement outcry, cry out, scream, shriek; to communicate something in a loud voice, call, call out, cry
BDAG.pt: fazer um grito veemente, gritar, berrar, urrar; comunicar algo em voz alta, chamar, clamar, bradar

DEFINITION: drunken dissipation, surfeiting.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as harpazo; properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut).

BDAG.en: unbridled indulgence in a drinking party, drinking bout
BDAG.pt: indulgência sem freio em uma bebedeira, farra de bebida

DEFINITION: a skull.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of a derivative of the base of keras; a skull ("cranium").

BDAG.en: skull
BDAG.pt: crânio

DEFINITION: the fringe, edge, corner, tassel.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or tassel.

BDAG.en: edge, border, hem of a garment; tassel, which an Israelite was obligated to wear on the four corners of his outer garment
BDAG.pt: borda, orla, barra de uma vestimenta; borla, que um israelita era obrigado a usar nos quatro cantos de sua veste exterior

DEFINITION: strong, powerful, mighty.
ORIGIN: From kratos; powerful.

BDAG.en: strong, mighty (implied by context/related entry)
BDAG.pt: forte, poderoso (implícito pelo contexto/entrada relacionada)

DEFINITION: to strengthen, confirm; pass: to grow strong, become strong.
ORIGIN: From krataios; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor.

BDAG.en: to become strong.
BDAG.pt: fortalecer-se, tornar-se forte.

DEFINITION: to be strong, mighty, hence: to rule, be master, prevail; to obtain, take hold of; to hold, hold fast.

BDAG.pt: realizar algo superando obstáculos, alcançar; usar as mãos para estabelecer um contato firme, segurar com a mão; tomar controle de, apreender, dominar; sustentar ou servir de base para algo, apoiar; conter ou restringir de, impedir em uma ação; manter sob poder; aderir firmemente a, agarrar-se a; manter algo que lhe pertence; reter para si uma declaração; fazer com que uma condição continue, manter no lugar

BDAG.pt: forma de tratamento honorífica fortemente afirmativa, nobilíssimo, excelentíssimo, usada ao se dirigir a pessoas de vários status sociais

BDAG.pt: capacidade de exibir ou expressar força residente, poder; um produto específico de força residente, feito poderoso; exercício de habilidade governativa, poder, domínio, soberania

DEFINITION: to cry aloud, shout, exclaim.

DEFINITION: (a) a shout, cry, clamor, (b) outcry, clamoring against another.

BDAG.pt: um grito ou chamada alta, gritaria, clamor de pessoas excitadas; clamor de luto ou ansiedade, lamento, choro

DEFINITION: flesh; plur: pieces of flesh, kinds of flesh.
ORIGIN: Perhaps a primary word; (butcher's) meat.

BDAG.pt: carne.

DEFINITION: stronger, more excellent.

DEFINITION: stronger, more excellent.
ORIGIN: Comparative of a derivative of kratos; stronger, i.e. (figuratively) better, i.e. Nobler.

BDAG.en: pert. to being of high status, more prominent, higher in rank, preferable, better; pert. to having a relative advantage in value, more useful, more advantageous, better.
BDAG.pt: pert. a ser de status elevado, mais proeminente, de patente superior, preferível, melhor; pert. a ter uma vantagem relativa em valor, mais útil, mais vantajoso, melhor.

DEFINITION: to hang, hang up, suspend; mid: to be hanging, hang.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang.

BDAG.en: to cause to hang, trans. hang (up); dep. to hang down from some point, intrans., hang (figuratively, depend).
BDAG.pt: causar o ato de pendurar, trans. pendurar (em cima); dep. pendurar-se de algum ponto, intrans., pendurar (figurativamente, depender).

DEFINITION: a crag, precipice, steep bank.
ORIGIN: From kremannumi; overhanging, i.e. A precipice.

BDAG.en: steep slope or bank, cliff
BDAG.pt: encosta ou barranco íngreme, precipício

DEFINITION: a Cretan, an inhabitant of Crete.
ORIGIN: From Krete; a Cretan, i.e. Inhabitant of Crete.

BDAG.en: a Cretan, inhabitant of the island of Crete
BDAG.pt: um cretense, habitante da ilha de Creta

DEFINITION: Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of Paul.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a Christian.

BDAG.en: Crescens, a companion of Paul
BDAG.pt: Crescente, um companheiro de Paulo

DEFINITION: Crete, an island in the Mediterranean.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Crete
BDAG.pt: Creta

DEFINITION: barley.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; barley.

BDAG.en: barley, used in the preparation of cheap kinds of bread
BDAG.pt: cevada, usada na preparação de pães de qualidade barata

DEFINITION: made of barley.
ORIGIN: From krithe; consisting of barley.

BDAG.en: made of barley flour
BDAG.pt: feito de farinha de cevada

DEFINITION: (a) a judgment, a verdict; sometimes implying an adverse verdict, a condemnation, (b) a case at law, a lawsuit.
ORIGIN: From krino; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")).
USAGE: avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment.

BDAG.en: 1. legal action taken against someone, dispute, lawsuit; 2. content of a deliberative process, decision, decree; 3. action or function of a judge, judging, judgment; 4. legal decision rendered by a judge, judicial verdict; 5. proper recognition of someone’s rights, justice
BDAG.pt: 1. ação legal movida contra alguém, disputa, processo judicial; 2. conteúdo de um processo deliberativo, decisão, decreto; 3. ação ou função de um juiz, julgamento; 4. decisão judicial proferida por um juiz, veredito judicial; 5. justo reconhecimento dos direitos de alguém, justiça

DEFINITION: a lily growing wild, variously identified with the red anemone, the whole lily, the sword lily.
ORIGIN: Perhaps a prim word; a lily.

BDAG.en: lily
BDAG.pt: lírio

DEFINITION: (a) to judge, whether in a law-court or privately: sometimes with cognate nouns emphasizing the notion of the verb, (b) to decide, to think (it) good.
ORIGIN: Properly, to distinguish, i.e. Decide (mentally or judicially); by implication, to try, condemn, punish.
USAGE: avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.

BDAG.en: to make a right judgment; esp. pass an unfavorable judgment upon, criticize, find fault with, condemn; to make a judgment based on taking various factors into account, judge, think, consider, look upon; to come to a conclusion after a cognitive process, reach a decision, decide, propose, intend; to engage in a judicial process, judge, decide, hale before a court, condemn, also hand over for judicial punishment; to ensure justice for someone, see to it that justice is done.
BDAG.pt: fazer um juízo correto; especialmente passar um julgamento desfavorável sobre, criticar, achar falhas, condenar; fazer um julgamento baseado na consideração de vários fatores, julgar, pensar, considerar, ver; chegar a uma conclusão após um processo cognitivo, alcançar uma decisão, decidir, propor, tencionar; engajar-se em um processo judicial, julgar, decidir, levar a um tribunal, condenar, também entregar para punição judicial; garantir justiça para alguém, providenciar que a justiça seja feita.

DEFINITION: judging, judgment, decision, sentence; generally: divine judgment; accusation.
ORIGIN: Decision (subjectively or objectively, for or against); by extension, a tribunal; by implication, justice (especially, divine law).

BDAG.en: legal process of judgment, judging, judgment (esp. on the Last Day); often means judgment that goes against a person, condemnation, and the sentence that follows; a board of judges, court, specif. a local court; administration of what is right and fair, right in the sense of justice/righteousness.
BDAG.pt: processo legal de julgamento, ato de julgar, juízo (especialmente no Último Dia); frequentemente significa um julgamento contrário a uma pessoa, condenação, e a sentença que se segue; um corpo de juízes, tribunal, especificamente um tribunal local; administração do que é correto e justo, o direito no sentido de justiça/retidão.

DEFINITION: Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, converted and baptized by Paul.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian.

BDAG.en: Crispus, leader of the synagogue in Corinth, baptized by Paul.
BDAG.pt: Crispo, líder da sinagoga em Corinto, batizado por Paulo.

DEFINITION: criterion; a law-court; a law-case before an arbiter; a cause, controversy.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of krites; a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal.

BDAG.en: prim. ‘means for judging/trying, a standard’; a forum for justice, lawcourt, tribunal
BDAG.pt: primariamente ‘meio para julgar/examinar, um padrão’; um fórum de justiça, corte legal, tribunal

DEFINITION: a judge, magistrate, ruler.
ORIGIN: From krino; a judge (genitive case or specially).

BDAG.en: one who reaches a decision, passes judgment; one who has the right to render a decision in legal matters, a judge (of human beings or God/Christ); in a more general sense, judge, critic; one who rules in a special sense in the accounts of Israel’s theocratic period, ruler, traditionally rendered judge.
BDAG.pt: aquele que chega a uma decisão, que julga; aquele que tem o direito de proferir uma decisão em assuntos legais, um juiz (de seres humanos ou de Deus/Cristo); em um sentido mais geral, juiz, crítico; aquele que governa em um sentido especial nos relatos do período teocrático de Israel, governante, tradicionalmente traduzido como juiz.

DEFINITION: critical, able to judge or discern.
ORIGIN: From krites; decisive ("critical"), i.e. Discriminative.

BDAG.en: able to discern/judge (foll. by obj. gen.).
BDAG.pt: capaz de discernir/julgar (seguido pelo genitivo do objeto).

DEFINITION: to knock, beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to rap.

BDAG.en: to deliver a blow against something, strike, knock (in our literature only of knocking at a door).
BDAG.pt: desferir um golpe contra algo, bater, tocar à porta (em nossa literatura apenas no sentido de bater em uma porta).

DEFINITION: a cellar, vault, hidden place, crypt.
ORIGIN: Feminine of kruptos; a hidden place, i.e. Cellar ("crypt").

BDAG.en: a place for hiding or storing something, a dark and hidden place, a cellar.
BDAG.pt: um lugar para esconder ou armazenar algo, um lugar escuro e oculto, uma adega.

DEFINITION: hidden, secret; as subst: the hidden (secret) things (parts), the inward nature (character).
ORIGIN: From krupto; concealed, i.e. Private.

BDAG.en: pert. to being unknown because of being kept secret, hidden, secret; a hidden entity, something hidden.
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que não é conhecido por ser mantido em segredo, oculto, secreto; uma entidade oculta, algo escondido.

DEFINITION: to hide, conceal, lay up.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to conceal (properly, by covering).

BDAG.en: to keep from being seen, hide (things and persons); to withdraw from sight or knowledge, hide, keep secret; cause to disappear; hide in a safe place; to keep something from being divulged or discovered, conceal, hide.
BDAG.pt: manter fora da vista, esconder (coisas e pessoas); retirar da vista ou do conhecimento, ocultar, manter em segredo; fazer desaparecer; esconder em um lugar seguro; manter algo sem divulgar ou descobrir, ocultar, esconder.

DEFINITION: to be clear as crystal, brilliant like crystal.
ORIGIN: From krustallos; to make (i.e. Intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize").

BDAG.en: shine like crystal, be as transparent as crystal (of jasper).
BDAG.pt: brilhar como cristal, ser tão transparente quanto cristal (de jaspe).

DEFINITION: crystal.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of kruos (frost); ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock "crystal".

BDAG.en: rock-crystal (or possibly ice).
BDAG.pt: cristal de rocha (ou possivelmente gelo).

DEFINITION: in secret, secretly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from krupto; privately.

BDAG.en: adv. in secret.
BDAG.pt: advérbio: em segredo.

DEFINITION: (a) to acquire, win, get, purchase, buy, (b) to possess, win mastery over.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to get, i.e. Acquire (by any means; own).

BDAG.en: to gain possession of, procure for oneself, acquire, get; bring upon oneself (of misfortunes, etc.); possess.
BDAG.pt: obter posse de, procurar para si mesmo, adquirir, conseguir; atrair sobre si (de infortúnios, etc.); possuir.

DEFINITION: a piece of landed property, a field; plur: possessions, property, possibly landed property, property in land.
ORIGIN: From ktaomai; an acquirement, i.e. Estate.

BDAG.en: that which is acquired or possessed, generally of any kind; landed property, field, piece of ground.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é adquirido ou possuído, geralmente de qualquer tipo; propriedade fundiária, campo, pedaço de terra.

DEFINITION: a beast of burden (generally, a horse or mule) either for riding or for carrying loads on its back, or for yoking to a cart or carriage.
ORIGIN: From ktaomai; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal.

BDAG.en: a domestic animal capable of carrying loads, domesticated animal, pet, pack-animal, animal used for riding (mostly in pl. as collective, ‘flocks, herds’)
BDAG.pt: um animal doméstico capaz de transportar cargas, animal domesticado, animal de estimação, animal de carga, animal usado para montaria (principalmente no plural como coletivo, 'rebanhos, manadas')

DEFINITION: a possessor, owner.
ORIGIN: From ktaomai; an owner.

BDAG.en: owner of houses and lands
BDAG.pt: proprietário de casas e terras

DEFINITION: to create, form, shape, make, always of God.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to ktaomai (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer); to fabricate, i.e. Found (form originally).

BDAG.en: to bring something into existence, create, in our literature of God’s creative activity
BDAG.pt: trazer algo à existência, criar, na nossa literatura da atividade criativa de Deus

DEFINITION: (often of the founding of a city), (a) abstr: creation, (b) concr: creation, creature, institution; always of Divine work, (c) an institution, ordinance.
ORIGIN: From ktizo; original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 act of creation, creation; 2 the result of a creative act, that which is created, creature; 3 system of established authority that is the result of some founding action, governance system, authority system.
BDAG.pt: 1 ato de criação, criação; 2 o resultado de um ato criativo, aquilo que é criado, criatura; 3 sistema de autoridade estabelecida que é o resultado de alguma ação de fundação, sistema de governança, sistema de autoridade.

DEFINITION: a created thing, a creature.
ORIGIN: From ktizo; an original formation (concretely), i.e. Product (created thing).

BDAG.en: product of creative action, that which is created (by God), creature (created by God)
BDAG.pt: produto da ação criativa, aquilo que é criado (por Deus), criatura (criada por Deus)

DEFINITION: (often of the founder of a city), creator, God.
ORIGIN: From ktizo; a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things).

BDAG.en: Creator (of all things), God
BDAG.pt: Criador (de todas as coisas), Deus

DEFINITION: (lit: playing with dice, gaming, hence) trickery, sleight.
ORIGIN: From kubos (a "cube", i.e. Die for playing); gambling, i.e. (figuratively) artifice or fraud.

BDAG.en: craftiness, trickery (metaph. from dice-playing)
BDAG.pt: astúcia, engano (metafórico, vindo de jogar dados)

DEFINITION: (lit: steering, piloting), governing, government.
ORIGIN: From kubernao (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, i.e. (figuratively) directorship (in the church).

BDAG.en: administration, the plural indicates varieties of such leading positions in the ecclesial body of Christ
BDAG.pt: administração, o plural indica variedades de tais posições de liderança no corpo eclesial de Cristo

DEFINITION: a steersman, pilot; met: a guide, governor.
ORIGIN: From the same as kubernesis; helmsman, i.e. (by implication) captain.

BDAG.en: one who is responsible for the management of a ship, ship-master, pilot (of Christ, directs the destiny of humans)
BDAG.pt: aquele que é responsável pela administração de um navio, mestre de navio, piloto (de Cristo, dirige o destino dos humanos)

DEFINITION: in a circle round, round about.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the same as kukloi; from the circle, i.e. All around.

BDAG.en: all around, from all sides
BDAG.pt: por toda parte, de todos os lados

DEFINITION: to encircle, besiege, surround.
ORIGIN: From the same as kukloi; to encircle, i.e. Surround.

BDAG.en: to move so as to encircle an object, surround, encircle (w. hostile intent); to provide protection; to move full circle around an object, go around, circle round
BDAG.pt: mover-se para cercar um objeto, rodear, cercar (com intenção hostil); prover proteção; mover-se em círculo completo ao redor de um objeto, dar a volta, circular

DEFINITION: a circle, ring.
ORIGIN: As if dative case of kuklos (a ring, "cycle"; akin to kulioo); i.e. In a circle (by implication, of en), i.e. (adverbially) all around.

DEFINITION: a place of wallowing.
ORIGIN: From kulioo; a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. Filth.

BDAG.en: a rolling or wallowing (cf. κυλισμός)
BDAG.pt: um rolar ou revolvimento (cf. κυλισμός)

DEFINITION: to roll, roll along, wallow.
ORIGIN: From the base of kuma (through the idea of circularity; compare kukloi, heilisso); to roll about.

BDAG.en: to move an object by rolling it, roll (up); to move on a surface by turning over and over, roll (oneself)
BDAG.pt: mover um objeto rolando-o, rolar (para cima); mover-se sobre uma superfície virando repetidamente, rolar (a si mesmo)

DEFINITION: crippled, lame, especially in the hands.
ORIGIN: From the same as kulioo; rocking about, i.e. Crippled (maimed, in feet or hands).

BDAG.en: crippled, deformed (of a limb or person); the cripple, injured person (subst.)
BDAG.pt: mutilado, deformado (de um membro ou pessoa); o coxo, pessoa ferida (substantivo)

DEFINITION: a wave, surge, billow.
ORIGIN: From kuo (to swell (with young), i.e. Bend, curve); a billow (as bursting or toppling).

BDAG.en: wave; metaphorically: the inconstancy and stormy confusion of dissident teachers
BDAG.pt: onda; metaforicamente: a inconstância e confusão tempestuosa de mestres dissidentes

DEFINITION: a cymbal.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the base of kuma; a "cymbal" (as hollow).

BDAG.en: cymbal, a metal basin used in ritual observances, which produced a shrill sound when struck together
BDAG.pt: címbalo, uma bacia de metal usada em observâncias rituais, que produzia um som estridente quando tocada

DEFINITION: cumin, a plant used as a spice.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (compare kammon); dill or fennel ("cummin").

BDAG.en: cumin (the tiny fruits/seeds of the cumin herb)
BDAG.pt: cominho (os pequenos frutos/sementes da erva do cominho)

DEFINITION: a little dog, a house dog.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of kuon; a puppy.

BDAG.en: little dog, lap-dog, house-dog (sometimes without diminutive force)
BDAG.pt: cãozinho, cão de colo, cão doméstico (às vezes sem força diminutiva)

DEFINITION: a Cypriote, belonging to Cyprus.
ORIGIN: From Kupros; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. Inhabitant of Cyprus.

BDAG.en: a Cypriot, an inhabitant of Cyprus
BDAG.pt: um cipriota, um habitante de Chipre

DEFINITION: Cyprus, an island at the east end of the Mediterranean Sea.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Cyprus, an island in the bay formed by the south coast of Asia Minor and the Syrian coast
BDAG.pt: Chipre, uma ilha na baía formada pela costa sul da Ásia Menor e a costa Síria

DEFINITION: to bend, stoop down, bow the head.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of kuma; to bend forward.

BDAG.en: to bend (oneself) down
BDAG.pt: curvar-se para baixo

DEFINITION: belonging to Cyrene, a Cyrenaean.
ORIGIN: From Kurene; i.e. Cyrenaean, i.e. Inhabitant of Cyrene.

BDAG.en: a Cyrenian
BDAG.pt: um cireneu

DEFINITION: Cyrene, a district west of Egypt on the Mediterranean coast, forming with Crete a Roman province.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa.

BDAG.en: Cyrene, capital city of the N. African district of Cyrenaica (Pentapolis)
BDAG.pt: Cirene, cidade capital do distrito norte-africano da Cirenaica (Pentápolis)

DEFINITION: Cyrenius or Quirinius, governor of Syria.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman.

BDAG.en: imperial governor of Syria, mentioned in the NT in connection w. the census
BDAG.pt: governador imperial da Síria, mencionado no NT em conexão com o censo

DEFINITION: a lady.
ORIGIN: Feminine of kurios; Cyria, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: lady, mistress; used in addressing a definite person; (in 2J/3J) the elect lady (possibly referring to the congregation)
BDAG.pt: senhora, patroa; usada para se dirigir a uma pessoa definida; (em 2J/3J) a senhora eleita (possivelmente referindo-se à congregação)

DEFINITION: of the Lord, special to the Lord.
ORIGIN: From kurios; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus).

BDAG.en: pertaining to or belonging to the Lord, the Lord’s (e.g., Lord's Supper, Lord's day [Sunday])
BDAG.pt: pertencente ou relativo ao Senhor, do Senhor (ex: Ceia do Senhor, dia do Senhor [domingo])

DEFINITION: to have authority, rule over.
ORIGIN: From kurios; to rule.
USAGE: have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over.

BDAG.en: to be lord/master of; exercise authority or have control, rule; be master of, dominate (of things)
BDAG.pt: ser senhor/mestre de; exercer autoridade ou ter controle, governar; ser mestre de, dominar (de coisas)

DEFINITION: lord, master, sir; the Lord.
ORIGIN: From kuros (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title).

BDAG.en: lord, master (one who is in charge by virtue of possession, owner; one who is in a position of authority; Lord/God; Jesus)
BDAG.pt: senhor, mestre (aquele que está no comando por virtude de posse, proprietário; aquele que está em posição de autoridade; Senhor/Deus; Jesus)

DEFINITION: (a) abstr: lordship, (b) concr: divine or angelic lordship, domination, dignity, usually with reference to a celestial hierarchy.
ORIGIN: From kurios; mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively) rulers.

BDAG.en: essential nature of the Lord; majestic power wielded by the Lord, ruling power, lordship, dominion; a special class of angelic powers, dominions.
BDAG.pt: nature essencial do Senhor; poder majestoso exercido pelo Senhor, poder de domínio, senhorio; uma classe especial de poderes angélicos, dominações.

DEFINITION: to ratify, confirm, make valid, reaffirm, assure.
ORIGIN: From the same as kurios; to make authoritative, i.e. Ratify.

BDAG.en: to give sanction to something, confirm, ratify, validate, make legally binding; to come to a decision in a cognitive process, conclude, decide in favor of.
BDAG.pt: dar sanção a algo, confirmar, ratificar, validar, tornar legalmente vinculativo; chegar a uma decisão em um processo cognitivo, concluir, decidir a favor.

DEFINITION: a dog, universally despised in the East.
ORIGIN: A primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: dog; a cultically impure person, unqualified; an infamous person, dog (invective).
BDAG.pt: cão; uma pessoa cultualmente impura, inqualificada; uma pessoa infame, cão (injúria).

DEFINITION: a limb, member of a body; fig: a corpse, carcass.
ORIGIN: From the base of kolazo; a limb of the body (as if lopped).

BDAG.en: In LXX/NT, only plural: dead body, corpse, especially unburied.
BDAG.pt: Em LXX/NT, apenas no plural: corpo morto, cadáver, especialmente insepulto.

DEFINITION: to prevent, debar, hinder; with infin: from doing so and so.
ORIGIN: From the base of kolazo; to estop, i.e. Prevent (by word or act).
USAGE: forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand.

BDAG.en: to keep something from happening, hinder, prevent, forbid; to keep something back, refuse, deny, withhold.
BDAG.pt: impedir que algo aconteça, dificultar, prevenir, proibir; reter algo, recusar, negar, omitir.

DEFINITION: a village, country town.
ORIGIN: From keimai; a hamlet (as if laid down).
