BDAG.en: a relatively small community with a group of houses, village, small town; the inhabitants of a village.
BDAG.pt: uma comunidade relativamente pequena com um grupo de casas, aldeia, pequena cidade; os habitantes de uma aldeia.

DEFINITION: a large village, a city which in constitution has only the status of a village; a country town.
ORIGIN: From kome and polis; an unwalled city.

BDAG.en: lit. a city that ‘has only the position of a κώμη as far as its constitution is concerned’, in Mk 1:38 someth. like market-town
BDAG.pt: lit. uma cidade que 'tem apenas a posição de uma aldeia no que diz respeito à sua constituição', em Marcos 1:38 algo como cidade de mercado/vila grande

DEFINITION: a feasting, reveling, carousal.
ORIGIN: From keimai; a carousal (as if letting loose).

BDAG.en: orig. a festal procession in honor of Dionysus, then a joyous meal or banquet, in the NT only in a bad sense excessive feasting, carousing, revelry
BDAG.pt: originalmente uma procissão festiva em honra a Dionísio, depois uma refeição ou banquete alegre, no NT apenas em sentido negativo: festas excessivas, folia, libertinagem

DEFINITION: a gnat, mosquito, referred to proverbially as something small.
ORIGIN: Apparently a derivative of the base of kentron and a derivative of optanomai; a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis).

BDAG.en: gnat, mosquito.
BDAG.pt: mosquito, pernilongo.

DEFINITION: Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, south-west of Asia Minor.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Cos (an island in the Aegean Sea).
BDAG.pt: Cos (uma ilha no Mar Egeu).

DEFINITION: Cosam, son of Elmadam and father of Addi.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (compare qecem); Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Cosam (in the genealogy of Jesus).
BDAG.pt: Cosam (na genealogia de Jesus).

DEFINITION: (lit: blunted) dumb, dull, deaf.
ORIGIN: From kopto; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb).

BDAG.en: pert. to lack of speech capability, mute; pert. to lack of hearing capability, deaf; deaf and mute (fig. of cult images that neither hear nor answer).
BDAG.pt: relativo à falta de capacidade de fala, mudo; relativo à falta de capacidade auditiva, surdo; surdo-mudo (figurado para imagens de culto que nem ouvem nem respondem).

DEFINITION: (a) to obtain (receive) by lot, lot (turn) is, (b) to draw lots.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. Determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot.
USAGE: his lot be, cast lots, obtain.

BDAG.en: to obtain someth. as a portion, receive, obtain (by lot, or by divine will); to be selected through casting of lots, be appointed/ chosen by lot; to allot a portion or make an assignment by casting lots, cast lots.
BDAG.pt: obter algo como porção, receber, obter (por sorteio ou por vontade divina); ser escolhido através do lançamento de sortes, ser nomeado/escolhido por sorteio; sortear uma porção ou fazer uma designação lançando sortes, lançar sortes.

DEFINITION: Lazarus, Eliezer, (a) the beggar, (b) the brother of Martha and Mary, of Bethany.
ORIGIN: Probably of Hebrew origin (El'azar); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary).

BDAG.en: Lazarus (1. in J, brother of Mary and Martha, resident in Bethany in Judaea; 2. name of a beggar in a parable)
BDAG.pt: Lázaro (1. em João, irmão de Maria e Marta, residente em Betânia na Judeia; 2. nome de um mendigo em uma parábola)

DEFINITION: secretly, privately.
ORIGIN: Adverb from lanthano; privately.

BDAG.en: 1 (to do someth.) without others being aware, secretly, used as adv.; 2 (to do someth.) without going through proper channels, without the knowledge of, behind the back of, as prep. w. gen.
BDAG.pt: 1 (fazer algo) sem que os outros percebam, secretamente, usado como adv.; 2 (fazer algo) sem passar pelos canais apropriados, sem o conhecimento de, pelas costas de, como prep. com genitivo

DEFINITION: a sudden storm, squall, whirlwind, hurricane.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind (squall).

BDAG.en: whirlwind, hurricane; λ. ἀνέμου a fierce gust of wind
BDAG.pt: redemoinho, furacão; λ. de vento uma rajada forte de vento

DEFINITION: to kick.
ORIGIN: From adverb lax (heelwise); to recalcitrate.

BDAG.en: kick of draft animals, as a figure for unreasoning resistance
BDAG.pt: dar coices de animais de tração, como figura para resistência irracional

DEFINITION: (to talk, chatter in classical Greek, but in NT a more dignified word) to speak, say.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. Utter words.
USAGE: preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare lego.

BDAG.en: to make a sound, sound, give forth sounds/tones that form a kind of speech (esp. of inanimate things); to utter words, talk, speak (of persons), including having and using the faculty of speech, speaking/expressing oneself, communicating personally; to speak and thereby assert, proclaim, say something.
BDAG.pt: emitir um som, soar, produzir sons/tons que formam um tipo de fala (especialmente de coisas inanimadas); proferir palavras, falar, comunicar (de pessoas), incluindo ter e usar a faculdade da fala, falar/expressar-se, comunicar pessoalmente; falar e com isso afirmar, proclamar, dizer algo.

DEFINITION: (in classical Greek: babble, chattering) speech, talk; manner of speech, dialect.
ORIGIN: From laleo; talk.

BDAG.en: content of speech, speech, speaking; manner of expressing oneself, form of speech, way of speaking.
BDAG.pt: Conteúdo da fala, discurso, ato de falar; maneira de se expressar, forma de discurso, modo de falar.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), why.
ORIGIN: Or lamma lam-mah'; of Hebrew origin (mah with prepositional prefix); lama (i.e. Why).

BDAG.en: See λαμά, λεμά.
BDAG.pt: Ver λαμά, λεμά.

DEFINITION: (a) to receive, get, (b) to take, lay hold of.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas dechomai is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while haireomai is more violent, to seize or remove)).
USAGE: accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).

BDAG.en: to get hold of something by laying hands on or grasping something, directly or indirectly, take, take hold of, grasp, take in hand; to take away, remove; to take into one's possession, take, acquire; to lay hands on, seize; of feelings, emotions seize, come upon; of hunting and fishing: catch; to take payment, receive, accept, of taxes, etc.; to include in an experience, take up, receive; to make a choice, choose, select; to accept as true, receive; to enter into a close relationship, receive, make one's own, apprehend/comprehend mentally or spiritually; Special uses: show partiality/favoritism, take courage, try something, consult (take counsel); to be a receiver, receive, get, obtain; to take payment, receive a punishment; become acquainted with, experience, suffer something; used as a periphrasis for the passive (be edified, be circumcised, receive a mark, be reconciled, remember something, forget something, experience joy, be begun, have its beginning); receive something from someone.
BDAG.pt: pegar algo pousando as mãos ou agarrando algo, direta ou indiretamente, tomar, agarrar, apertar, pegar; tirar, remover; tomar posse, obter, adquirir; pôr as mãos, apreender; de sentimentos, emoções, tomar conta, sobrevir; de caça e pesca: pegar; receber pagamento, receber, aceitar, de impostos, etc.; incluir em uma experiência, acolher, receber; fazer uma escolha, escolher, selecionar; aceitar como verdadeiro, receber; entrar em um relacionamento íntimo, receber, fazer seu, apreender/compreender mental ou espiritualmente; Usos especiais: mostrar favoritismo/parcialidade, tomar coragem, experimentar algo, consultar (tomar conselho); ser um receptor, receber, obter, alcançar; receber pagamento, receber uma punição; tomar conhecimento de, experimentar, sofrer algo; usado como perífrase para o passivo (ser edificado, ser circuncidado, receber uma marca, ser reconciliado, lembrar-se de algo, esquecer algo, experimentar alegria, ser começado, ter seu início); receber algo de alguém.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Lemek); Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Lamech (father of Noah; in the genealogy of Jesus).
BDAG.pt: Lameque (pai de Noé; na genealogia de Jesus).

DEFINITION: a torch, lamp, lantern.
ORIGIN: From lampo; a "lamp" or flambeau.

BDAG.en: torch; celestial phenomena that resemble burning torches; lamp (with a wick and space for oil)
BDAG.pt: tocha; fenômenos celestiais que se assemelham a tochas ardentes; lâmpada (com pavio e espaço para azeite)

DEFINITION: shining, magnificent, bright, splendid.
ORIGIN: From the same as lampas; radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively, magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance).
USAGE: bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white.

BDAG.en: pert. to radiating light, bright (of heavenly bodies); pert. to being free of anything that impedes clear perception, clear, transparent; pert. to having a glistening quality (of garments, esp. white ones: bright, shining; of other objects: gleaming, bright); splendor (as a substantive).
BDAG.pt: pertencente à emissão de luz, brilhante (de corpos celestes); pertencente a ser livre de qualquer coisa que impeça a percepção clara, claro, transparente; pertencente a ter uma qualidade brilhante (de vestes, especialmente brancas: brilhante, resplandecente; de outros objetos: reluzente, brilhante); esplendor (como substantivo).

DEFINITION: splendor, brightness, brilliancy.
ORIGIN: From lampros; brilliancy.

BDAG.en: brightness, splendor (state of being splendid, shining); exceptional personal quality, distinction, brilliance (transf. sense of brilliance in uprightness, i.e. above and beyond the ordinary).
BDAG.pt: brilho, esplendor (estado de ser esplêndido, brilhante); qualidade pessoal excepcional, distinção, brilho (sentido transferido de brilho em retidão, ou seja, acima e além do comum).

DEFINITION: magnificently, sumptuously, splendidly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from lampros; brilliantly, i.e. Figuratively, luxuriously.

BDAG.en: splendidly.
BDAG.pt: esplendidamente.

DEFINITION: to shine, give light.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to beam, i.e. Radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to emit rays of light, shine (of a lamp, lightning flash); shine out, shine forth, gleam (light, a star, sun; of the face of the transfigured Jesus; of the light that shone forth at creation; of an angel); shine (figuratively, with φῶς, of God shining in our hearts).
BDAG.pt: emitir raios de luz, brilhar (de uma lâmpada, clarão de relâmpago); brilhar, resplandecer, reluzir (luz, uma estrela, sol; do rosto de Jesus transfigurado; da luz que surgiu na criação; de um anjo); brilhar (figurativamente, com φῶς, de Deus brilhando em nossos corações).

DEFINITION: to be hidden (concealed), lie hid, escape notice, sometimes with acc. of person from whom concealment takes place; to do so and so unconsciously, unknown to myself, to shut eyes to so and so.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly.
USAGE: be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.

BDAG.en: to succeed in avoiding attention or awareness, escape notice, be hidden; something is hidden from someone, escapes someone’s notice; (by implication) to do something without knowing it.
BDAG.pt: ter sucesso em evitar atenção ou consciência, escapar à observação, estar escondido; algo está escondido de alguém, escapa à atenção de alguém; (por implicação) fazer algo sem saber.

DEFINITION: hewn out of the rock.
ORIGIN: From a compound of las (a stone) and the base of xeros (in its original sense of scraping); rock-quarried.

BDAG.en: pert. to being hewn in rock, hewn (a tomb).
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser talhado na rocha, escavado (um túmulo).

DEFINITION: (a) a people, characteristically of God's chosen people, first the Jews, then the Christians, (b) sometimes, but rarely, the people, the crowd.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from demos, which denotes one's own populace).

BDAG.en: people, in a general sense; the mass of a community as distinguished from special interest groups; a body of people with common cultural bonds and ties to a specific territory, people as nation; people of God, people
BDAG.pt: povo, em sentido geral; a massa de uma comunidade distinguida de grupos de interesse específicos; um corpo de pessoas com laços culturais comuns e ligação a um território específico, povo como nação; povo de Deus, povo

DEFINITION: Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia, near Colossae and Hierapolis.
ORIGIN: From a compound of laos and dike; Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Laodicea (a city in Phrygia in Asia Minor).
BDAG.pt: Laodiceia (uma cidade na Frígia, na Ásia Menor).

DEFINITION: a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea.
ORIGIN: From Laodikeia; a Laodicean, i.e. Inhabitant of Laodicia.

BDAG.en: a Laodicean, inhabitant of Laodicea in Phrygia.
BDAG.pt: um laodiceu, habitante de Laodiceia na Frígia.

DEFINITION: the throat, gullet.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; the throat ("larynx").

BDAG.en: throat, gullet (orig. ‘larynx’)
BDAG.pt: garganta, esófago (originalmente, ‘laringe’)

DEFINITION: Lasea, a city in Crete, about the middle of the south coast.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Lasaea, a place in Crete.

BDAG.en: Lasaea, a city on the south coast of the island of Crete
BDAG.pt: Laseia, uma cidade na costa sul da ilha de Creta

DEFINITION: to burst asunder with a loud noise.
ORIGIN: A strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall).

BDAG.en: crash etc., erroneously thought to be the source of ἐλάκησεν
BDAG.pt: estrondo, etc., erroneamente tido como a fonte de ἐλάκησεν

DEFINITION: to hew stones, cut stones.
ORIGIN: From the same as the first part of laxeutos and the base of tomoteros; to quarry.

BDAG.en: to form a cavity or chamber by cutting away rock, hew out of a rock; to shape stones by cutting, hew, shape stones
BDAG.pt: formar uma cavidade ou câmara cortando rocha, talhar da rocha; moldar pedras cortando, talhar, dar forma a pedras

DEFINITION: service rendered to God, perhaps simply: worship.
ORIGIN: From latreuo; ministration of God, i.e. Worship.

BDAG.en: in cultic usage service/worship (of God)
BDAG.pt: no uso cultual, serviço/adoração (a Deus)

DEFINITION: to serve, especially God, perhaps simply: to worship.
ORIGIN: From latris (a hired menial); to minister (to God), i.e. Render religious homage.

BDAG.en: serve, in our lit. only of the carrying out of religious duties, esp. of a cultic nature, by human beings
BDAG.pt: servir, na nossa literatura apenas do cumprimento de deveres religiosos, especialmente de natureza cultual, por seres humanos

DEFINITION: an herb, garden plant, vegetable.
ORIGIN: From lachaino (to dig); a vegetable.

BDAG.en: edible garden herb, vegetable
BDAG.pt: erva de horta comestível, hortaliça

DEFINITION: Lebbaeus, a pet-name for Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus; the full form of the name is not known.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Lebbaeus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Lebbaeus, in the list of apostles as a variant reading for Thaddaeus
BDAG.pt: Lebbaeus, na lista dos apóstolos como variante textual para Tadeu

DEFINITION: properly: a division of the Roman army, numbering about 6,000 infantry with additional cavalry; hence: a very large number; a legion.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively).

DEFINITION: (denoting speech in progress), (a) to say, speak; to mean, mention, tell, (b) to call, name, especially in the pass., (c) to tell, command.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas epo and phemi generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while rheo is properly to break silence merely, and laleo means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean.
USAGE: ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter.

BDAG.en: to express oneself orally or in written form, utter in words, say, tell, give expression to (general sense); to express oneself in a specific way, say (ask, answer, order, command, recommend)
BDAG.pt: expressar-se oralmente ou por escrito, proferir em palavras, dizer, contar, dar expressão (sentido geral); expressar-se de uma maneira específica, dizer (perguntar, responder, ordenar, comandar, recomendar)

DEFINITION: a remnant, remainder.
ORIGIN: From leipo; a remainder.

BDAG.en: remnant
BDAG.pt: remanescente

DEFINITION: smooth, level, plain.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; smooth, i.e. "level".

BDAG.en: smooth, level (of a road)
BDAG.pt: liso, plano (de uma estrada)

DEFINITION: (earlier: to leave behind, abandon), (a) to be wanting, (b) mid: e.g. with gen: to come behind (in a race), be left behind in, fall short of (some standard), be wanting in.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to leave, i.e. (intransitively or passively) to fail or be absent.

BDAG.en: leave behind, fall short, be inferior, lack, be in need or want (of); be deficient in something that ought to be present, lack
BDAG.pt: deixar para trás, ficar aquém, ser inferior, carecer, estar em necessidade ou falta (de); ser deficiente em algo que deveria estar presente, faltar

DEFINITION: to act in the public service, render service, minister, in the widest sense, of some special public religious service, but also of the service of priests and Levites.
ORIGIN: From leitourgos; to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve).

BDAG.en: render special formal service, serve, render service (of cultic or ritual responsibilities, Christian services, officials of congregations, angels); confer a special material benefit, serve
BDAG.pt: prestar serviço formal especial, servir, prestar serviço (de responsabilidades cultuais ou rituais, serviços cristãos, oficiais de congregações, anjos); conferir um benefício material especial, servir

DEFINITION: a charitable gift, public service in the widest sense; service as of priest or Levite ritual.
ORIGIN: From leitourgeo; public function (as priest ("liturgy") or almsgiver).

BDAG.en: public service; service performed by an individual for the state or public cult; in our literature almost always used with some sort of religious connotation; service of a formal or public type, service of ritual and cultic services; fig. of the high-priestly office of Christ; other kinds of service to God; of officials in Christian congregations (the office); activities of a nonofficial person in the church service; acts that show forth Christian charity and other virtues; service of a personal nature, help, assistance.
BDAG.pt: serviço público; serviço realizado por um indivíduo para o estado ou culto público; em nossa literatura, quase sempre usado com algum tipo de conotação religiosa; serviço de tipo formal ou público, serviço de rituais e cultos; fig. do ofício sumo-sacerdotal de Cristo; outros tipos de serviço a Deus; de oficiais em congregações cristãs (o ofício); atividades de uma pessoa não oficial no serviço da igreja; atos que demonstram a caridade cristã e outras virtudes; serviço de natureza pessoal, ajuda, assistência.

DEFINITION: given to serving (ministration), ministering.
ORIGIN: From the same as leitourgeo; functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e. Beneficient.

BDAG.en: engaged in special service, of angels 'spirits in special service (to God)'.
BDAG.pt: engajado em serviço especial, de anjos 'espíritos em serviço especial (a Deus)'.

DEFINITION: a minister, servant, of an official character; of priests and Levites.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of laos and ergon; a public servant, i.e. A functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man).

BDAG.en: one who performs public service; one engaged in administrative or cultic service, servant, minister; one engaged in personal service, aide, assistant.
BDAG.pt: aquele que realiza serviço público; aquele engajado em serviço administrativo ou cultual, servo, ministro; aquele engajado em serviço pessoal, auxiliar, assistente.

DEFINITION: a towel, apron, coarse cloth.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, i.e. Apron.

BDAG.en: linen cloth, towel.
BDAG.pt: pano de linho, toalha.

DEFINITION: a scale, a scaly substance thrown off from the body.
ORIGIN: From lepo (to peel); a flake.

BDAG.en: scale (of fish); a thin flaky piece, scale (in a simile, used for sudden restoration of sight).
BDAG.pt: escama (de peixes); uma peça fina e escamosa, escama (em uma símile, usado para a restauração súbita da visão).

DEFINITION: leprosy.
ORIGIN: From the same as lepis; scaliness, i.e. "leprosy".

BDAG.en: a serious skin disease, possibly including leprosy (the term may refer to a variety of skin disorders).
BDAG.pt: uma doença de pele séria, possivelmente incluindo lepra (o termo pode se referir a uma variedade de distúrbios cutâneos).

DEFINITION: a leprous person, a leper.
ORIGIN: From the same as lepra; scaly, i.e. Leprous (a leper).

BDAG.en: pertaining to having a serious skin disorder, with a bad skin disease; substantively, a person with a bad skin disease.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter um distúrbio de pele sério, com uma doença de pele grave; substantivamente, uma pessoa com uma doença de pele grave.

DEFINITION: a small piece of money, probably the smallest piece of money.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of the same as lepis; something scaled (light), i.e. A small coin.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Levi, (a) an ancestor of Jesus, (b) another ancestor of Jesus, (c) third son of Jacob, the patriarch, and founder of a tribe named after him, (d) son of Alphaeus, and called Matthew, a revenue officer and one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Leviy); Levi, the name of three Israelites.

BDAG.en: Levi (son of Jacob; son of Melchi in Jesus' genealogy; son of Symeon in Jesus' genealogy; a disciple of Jesus; name of a high priest).
BDAG.pt: Levi (filho de Jacó; filho de Melqui na genealogia de Jesus; filho de Simeão na genealogia de Jesus; um discípulo de Jesus; nome de um sumo sacerdote).

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Levi, son of Alphaeus, the publican.
ORIGIN: A form of Leui; Lewis (i.e. Levi), a Christian.

DEFINITION: a Levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi; hence: a priest's assistant, an under priest, as the members of that tribe were charged with this duty.
ORIGIN: From Leui; a Levite, i.e. Descendant of Levi.

BDAG.en: a Levite, member of the tribe of Levi, esp. one who performed the lowlier services connected with the temple ritual.
BDAG.pt: um levita, membro da tribo de Levi, especialmente aquele que realizava os serviços mais humildes conectados com o ritual do templo.

DEFINITION: belonging to the tribe of Levi; Levitical.
ORIGIN: From Leuites; Levitic, i.e. Relating to the Levites.

BDAG.en: Levitical (pertaining to the Levitical priesthood).
BDAG.pt: Levítico (pertencente ao sacerdócio levítico).

DEFINITION: to whiten, to make white.
ORIGIN: From leukos; to whiten.

BDAG.en: make white (of clothes, whitened by a fuller); in imagery, make sins white; in apocalyptic figure, make robes white in the blood of the Lamb.
BDAG.pt: tornar branco (de roupas, alvejadas por um batedor); em imagens, tornar os pecados brancos; em figura apocalíptica, tornar as vestes brancas no sangue do Cordeiro.

DEFINITION: white, bright, brilliant.
ORIGIN: From luke ("light"); white.

BDAG.en: bright, shining, gleaming; white (of hair, goatskin, a pebble used for voting, wool, apocalyptic horses).
BDAG.pt: brilhante, reluzente, resplandecente; branco (de cabelo, pele de cabra, um seixo usado para votação, lã, cavalos apocalípticos).

DEFINITION: a lion.
ORIGIN: A primary word; a "lion".

BDAG.en: lion; metaphorically of a lion-hearted hero, the Messiah; symbol of rapacity.
BDAG.pt: leão; metaforicamente de um herói de coração de leão, o Messias; símbolo de rapacidade.

DEFINITION: forgetfulness, oblivion.
ORIGIN: From lanthano; forgetfulness.

BDAG.en: forgetfulness.
BDAG.pt: esquecimento.

DEFINITION: a trough, vat, winepress.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a trough, i.e. Wine-vat.

BDAG.en: a hollow container or vat, hence wine-press; figuratively, treading the wine-press (of judgment).
BDAG.pt: um recipiente ou tina oca, daí lagar de vinho; figurativamente, pisar o lagar (de julgamento).

DEFINITION: folly, nonsense, idle talk.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; twaddle, i.e. An incredible story.

BDAG.en: that which is totally devoid of anything worthwhile, idle talk, nonsense, humbug
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é totalmente desprovido de qualquer valor, conversa fiada, disparate, tolice

DEFINITION: a robber, brigand, bandit.
ORIGIN: From leizomai (to plunder); a brigand.

BDAG.en: robber, highwayman, bandit; revolutionary, insurrectionist, guerrilla
BDAG.pt: ladrão, salteador, bandido; revolucionário, insurrecionista, guerrilheiro

DEFINITION: a receiving.
ORIGIN: From lambano; receipt (the act).

DEFINITION: very; very much, exceedingly, greatly.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; much (adverbially).

BDAG.en: to a high degree, very, exceedingly.
BDAG.pt: em alto grau, muito, excessivamente.

DEFINITION: (Semitic word), frankincense, incense.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (lbownah); the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication) incense itself.

BDAG.en: frankincense, a white resinous gum, used both medicinally and for sacral purposes.
BDAG.pt: olíbano (incenso), uma goma resinosa branca, usada tanto medicinalmente quanto para fins sacros.

DEFINITION: frankincense, a censer.
ORIGIN: From libanos; frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning it.

BDAG.en: 1. (frank)incense; 2. censer, in which incense is burned.
BDAG.pt: 1. olíbano (incenso); 2. turíbulo, no qual o incenso é queimado.

DEFINITION: a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves; a synagogue at Jerusalem appears to have been reserved for them.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a Roman freedman.

BDAG.en: Freedperson, a designation for certain Israelites in Jerusalem who had their own synagogue (former slaves or their descendants)
BDAG.pt: Liberto, uma designação para certos israelitas em Jerusalém que tinham sua própria sinagoga (ex-escravos ou seus descendentes)

DEFINITION: "the west bank of the Nile", Libya, a region in N. Africa.
ORIGIN: Probably from lips; Libye, a region of Africa.

BDAG.en: Libya, a district in N. Africa between Egypt and Cyrene.
BDAG.pt: Líbia, um distrito no Norte da África entre o Egito e Cirene.

DEFINITION: to stone, pelt with stones.
ORIGIN: From lithos; to lapidate.

BDAG.en: stone someone; a means of capital punishment (especially for blasphemy); sometimes carried out by the populace.
BDAG.pt: apedrejar alguém; um meio de pena capital (especialmente por blasfêmia); às vezes executado pela população.

DEFINITION: made of stone.
ORIGIN: From lithos; stony, i.e. Made of stone.

BDAG.en: made of stone; fig. of the heart: stony, i.e., one without feeling.
BDAG.pt: feito de pedra; fig. sobre o coração: de pedra, ou seja, insensível/sem sentimento.

DEFINITION: to stone, cast stones (at), kill by stoning.
ORIGIN: From a compound of lithos and ballo; to throw stones, i.e. Lapidate.

BDAG.en: throw stones at someone; stone (to death).
BDAG.pt: atirar pedras em alguém; apedrejar (até a morte).

DEFINITION: a stone; met: of Jesus as the chief stone in a building.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: stone, in general; stone of a special kind (building stones, precious stones, jewels; millstones; large stones used to seal graves); stone images of the gods; fig. imagery relating to God’s people and the transcendent (e.g., living stones, cornerstone, stumbling stone).
BDAG.pt: pedra, em geral; pedra de tipo especial (pedras de construção, pedras preciosas, joias; pedras de moinho; grandes pedras usadas para selar sepulcros); imagens de pedra dos deuses; fig. imagens relativas ao povo de Deus e ao transcendente (ex: pedras vivas, pedra angular, pedra de tropeço).

DEFINITION: (adj: paved with stone), a mosaic pavement.
ORIGIN: From lithos and a derivative of stronnumi; stone-strewed, i.e. A tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed.

DEFINITION: to crush to powder, scatter like chaff.
ORIGIN: From likmos, the equivalent of liknon (a winnowing fan or basket); to winnow, i.e. (by analogy), to triturate.

BDAG.en: winnow; in NT context (Mt 21:44/Lk 20:18) interpreted by some as crush/destroy.
BDAG.pt: aventam; no contexto do NT (Mt 21:44/Lc 20:18) interpretado por alguns como esmagar/destruir.

DEFINITION: a harbor, port, haven.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a harbor.

BDAG.en: harbor; fig. to reach the harbor (as a goal after hardship).
BDAG.pt: porto; fig. alcançar o porto (como meta após a dificuldade).

DEFINITION: a lake.
ORIGIN: Probably from limen (through the idea of nearness of shore); a pond (large or small).

BDAG.en: a body of inland water, varying in size from lake to pool (e.g., Lake of Gennesaret); fig. a transcendent lake-like phenomenon (lake of fire or of salvation).
BDAG.pt: um corpo de água interior, variando em tamanho de lago a poça (ex: Mar da Galileia); fig. um fenômeno transcendente semelhante a um lago (lago de fogo ou de salvação).

DEFINITION: a famine, hunger.
ORIGIN: Probably from leipo (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of food.

BDAG.en: hunger; famine
BDAG.pt: fome; escassez de alimentos

DEFINITION: flax, linen.
ORIGIN: Probably a primary word; flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen".

BDAG.en: flax plant and products made from its fibers; lamp-wick; linen garment; fish-net
BDAG.pt: planta de linho e produtos feitos de suas fibras; pavio de lamparina; vestimenta de linho; rede de pesca

DEFINITION: Linus, a Christian in Rome.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from linon; Linus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Linus, Christian, possibly the first bishop of Rome
BDAG.pt: Lino, cristão, possivelmente o primeiro bispo de Roma

DEFINITION: (lit: fat), rich, sumptuous.
ORIGIN: From lipos (grease); fat, i.e. (figuratively) sumptuous.

BDAG.en: oily, fat; bright, radiant, luxurious, costly, rich (applied to peace)
BDAG.pt: oleoso, gordo; brilhante, radiante, luxuoso, custoso, rico (aplicado à paz)

DEFINITION: a pound (in weight, by Rom. standards).
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight.

BDAG.en: a (Roman) pound (unit of weight/money)
BDAG.pt: uma libra (romana) (unidade de peso/dinheiro)

DEFINITION: the south-west wind, and thus the quarter from which it comes.
ORIGIN: Probably from leibo (to pour a "libation"); the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter).

BDAG.en: the southwest (of a harbor)
BDAG.pt: o sudoeste (de um porto)

DEFINITION: a collection, collecting (of money), particularly of an irregular local contribution for religious purposes.
ORIGIN: From logos (in the commercial sense); a contribution.

DEFINITION: to reckon, count, charge with; reason, decide, conclude; think, suppose.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from logos; to take an inventory, i.e. Estimate (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on).

BDAG.en: to count, reckon, consider, think, deem, regard, suppose, reason, plan, hold a view, believe, intend, purpose
BDAG.pt: contar, calcular, raciocinar, considerar, achar, estimar, julgar, supor, planejar, ter uma opinião, crer, ter a intenção, propor

DEFINITION: (a) reasonable, rational, (b) metaphorical, as contrasted with the literal.
ORIGIN: From logos; rational ("logical").

BDAG.en: pertaining to being carefully thought through, thoughtful (applied to service, spiritual milk)
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que foi cuidadosamente pensado, atencioso, racional (aplicado ao serviço, leite espiritual)

DEFINITION: plur: oracles, divine responses or utterances (it can include the entire Old Testament).
ORIGIN: Neuter of logios; an utterance (of God).

BDAG.en: a saying, oracle (esp. divine sayings, words from Scripture, sayings of the Lord)
BDAG.pt: um dito, oráculo (especialmente ditos divinos, palavras das Escrituras, ditos do Senhor)

DEFINITION: eloquent, gifted with learning.
ORIGIN: From logos; fluent, i.e. An orator.

BDAG.en: eloquent, learned, cultured
BDAG.pt: eloquente, culto, instruído

DEFINITION: reasoning, thinking; a conception, device.
ORIGIN: From logizomai; computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit).

BDAG.en: the product of a cognitive process: calculation, reasoning, reflection, thought (often unfavorable); the capability of reasoning, reasoning power
BDAG.pt: o produto de um processo cognitivo: cálculo, raciocínio, reflexão, pensamento (muitas vezes desfavorável); a capacidade de raciocinar, poder de raciocínio

DEFINITION: to contend about words.
ORIGIN: From a compound of logos and machomai; to be disputatious (on trifles).

BDAG.en: to dispute about words, split hairs
BDAG.pt: disputar sobre palavras, ser minucioso em discussões verbais

DEFINITION: contention about words, an unprofitable controversy.
ORIGIN: From the same as logomacheo; disputation about trifles ("logomachy").

BDAG.en: word-battle, dispute about words
BDAG.pt: batalha de palavras, disputa sobre palavras

DEFINITION: a word (as embodying an idea), a statement, a speech.
ORIGIN: From lego; something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ).
USAGE: account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say(-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work.

BDAG.en: sound preaching; Christian teachings, the words of the gospel; an individual declaration or remark: assertion, declaration, speech; words uttered on various occasions, speeches or instruction; the ten commandments; connected discourse, a conversation, or parts of one and the same teaching; the subject under discussion, matter, thing generally; of literary or oratorical productions: treatise; computation, reckoning (formal accounting, settlement of an account, reflection, respect, reason, ground, motive); the independent personified expression of God, the Logos.
BDAG.pt: pregação sã; ensinamentos cristãos, as palavras do evangelho; uma declaração ou observação individual: afirmação, declaração, discurso; palavras proferidas em várias ocasiões, discursos ou instrução; os dez mandamentos; discurso conectado, uma conversação, ou partes de um mesmo ensinamento; o assunto em discussão, matéria, coisa em geral; de produções literárias ou oratórias: tratado; computação, cálculo (contabilidade formal, acerto de contas, reflexão, respeito, razão, fundamento, motivo); a expressão independente personificada de Deus, o Logos.

DEFINITION: a lance or spear.
ORIGIN: Perhaps a primary word; a "lance".

BDAG.en: spear, lance (perhaps spear-point).
BDAG.pt: lança (talvez ponta de lança).

DEFINITION: to revile a person to his face, abuse insultingly.
ORIGIN: From loidoros; to reproach, i.e. Vilify.

BDAG.en: revile, abuse (someone).
BDAG.pt: revidar, insultar (alguém).

DEFINITION: reviling, abuse.
ORIGIN: From loidoros; slander or vituperation.

BDAG.en: speech that is highly insulting, abuse, reproach, reviling (return abuse for abuse).
BDAG.pt: discurso altamente insultuoso, abuso, reprovação, injúria (retornar insulto por insulto).

DEFINITION: a railer, reviler, abuser.
ORIGIN: From loidos (mischief); abusive, i.e. A blackguard.

BDAG.en: reviler, abusive person.
BDAG.pt: injuriador, pessoa abusiva.

DEFINITION: (a) a pestilence, (b) a pestilent fellow.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a plague (literally, the disease, or figuratively, a pest).

BDAG.en: pestilence, plagues, diseases (as signs of the last time); public menace/enemy (pestilential person).
BDAG.pt: peste, pragas, doenças (como sinais dos últimos tempos); ameaça/inimigo público (pessoa pestilenta).

DEFINITION: left, left behind, the remainder, the rest, the others.
ORIGIN: Masculine plural of a derivative of leipo; remaining ones.
USAGE: other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest.

BDAG.en: remaining, left; other, rest of; (adverbially) from now on, in the future, finally, beyond that, in addition.
BDAG.pt: restante, o que sobrou; outro, o resto de; (adverbialmente) a partir de agora, no futuro, finalmente, além disso, em adição.

DEFINITION: finally, from now on, henceforth, beyond that.
ORIGIN: Neuter singular of the same as loipoy; something remaining (adverbially).
USAGE: besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then.

DEFINITION: from now on, henceforth, finally.
ORIGIN: Genitive case singular of the same as loipoy; remaining time.

DEFINITION: Lucas, Luke, Christian physician and writer of the Third Gospel and Acts.
ORIGIN: Contracted from Latin Lucanus; Lucas, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Luke (companion and co-worker of Paul, a physician, author of the third gospel and Acts).
BDAG.pt: Lucas (companheiro e colaborador de Paulo, médico, autor do terceiro evangelho e dos Atos).

DEFINITION: Lucius, (a) of Cyrene, an early Christian, in the church of Antioch, by some identified with the evangelist Luke, (b) a Christian with Paul at Corinth, by some identified with (a).
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; illuminative; Lucius, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Lucius (1. of Cyrene, a teacher or prophet at Antioch; 2. an otherwise unknown Christian)
BDAG.pt: Lúcio (1. de Cirene, mestre ou profeta em Antioquia; 2. um cristão desconhecido de outra forma)

DEFINITION: a bath (of water, not the vessel), water for washing, washing.
ORIGIN: From louo; a bath, i.e. (figuratively), baptism.

BDAG.en: bath, washing of baptism (often referring to a ceremonial cleansing).
BDAG.pt: banho, lavagem do batismo (frequentemente referindo-se a uma purificação cerimonial).

DEFINITION: (lit. or merely ceremonially), to wash, bathe (the body); mid: of washing, bathing one's self; met: to cleanse from sin.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to bathe (the whole person; whereas nipto means to wet a part only, and pluno to wash, cleanse garments exclusively).

BDAG.en: to use water to cleanse a body, wash, bathe; to use water in a cultic manner for purification, cleanse oneself; to cause to be purified, cleanse (act.)
BDAG.pt: usar água para limpar um corpo, lavar, banhar; usar água de maneira cultual para purificação, lavar-se; fazer ser purificado, limpar (ativo)

DEFINITION: Lydda, Diospolis, Lod (modern Ludd), a city on the way to Joppa within a day's journey of Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Lod); Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Lydda, a city southeast of Joppa on the road to Jerusalem
BDAG.pt: Lida, uma cidade a sudeste de Jope no caminho para Jerusalém

DEFINITION: Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi, native of Thyatira in Lydia (Asia Minor), and engaged in the clothing trade.
ORIGIN: Properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor).

BDAG.en: Lydia, a merchant from Thyatira in Lydia, converted by Paul in Philippi
BDAG.pt: Lídia, uma comerciante de Tiatira na Lídia, convertida por Paulo em Filipos

DEFINITION: Lycaonia, the country of the Lykaones, a district of Asia Minor, comprised within the Roman province Galatia and including the cities of Derbe and Lystra.
ORIGIN: Perhaps remotely from lukos; Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Lycaonia, a province in Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Licaônia, uma província na Ásia Menor

DEFINITION: in the Lycaonian language.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of Lukaonia; Lycaonistically, i.e. In the language of the Lycaonians.

BDAG.en: in (the) Lycaonian (language)
BDAG.pt: em (a língua) licaônia

DEFINITION: Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.
ORIGIN: Probably remotely from lukos; Lycia, a province of Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Lycia, a projection on the south coast of Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Lícia, uma projeção na costa sul da Ásia Menor

DEFINITION: a wolf, of perhaps a jackal; often applied to persons of wolfish proclivities.
ORIGIN: Perhaps akin to the base of leukos (from the whitish hair); a wolf.

BDAG.en: wolf, a fierce or vicious person (metaphorical)
BDAG.pt: lobo, uma pessoa feroz ou viciosa (metafórico)

DEFINITION: to outrage, maltreat, corrupt, defile.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from a probably derivative of luo (meaning filth); properly, to soil, i.e. (figuratively) insult (maltreat).

DEFINITION: to distress, to grieve.
ORIGIN: From lupe; to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad.
USAGE: cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry.

BDAG.en: to cause severe mental or emotional distress, vex, irritate, offend, insult, grieve, pain
BDAG.pt: causar sofrimento mental ou emocional severo, vexar, irritar, ofender, insultar, entristecer, causar dor

DEFINITION: pain of body or mind, grief, sorrow.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; sadness.

BDAG.en: pain of mind or spirit, grief, sorrow, affliction
BDAG.pt: dor da mente ou do espírito, pesar, tristeza, aflição

DEFINITION: "ending sorrow", Lysanias, a governor of Abilene.
ORIGIN: From lusis and ania (trouble); grief-dispelling; Lysanias, a governor of Abilene.

BDAG.en: Lysanias, tetrarch of Abilene
BDAG.pt: Lisânias, tetrarca de Abilene

DEFINITION: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman.

BDAG.en: Lysias (Claudius Lysias)
BDAG.pt: Lisias (Cláudio Lisias)

DEFINITION: dissolution, release; a loosing, divorce.
ORIGIN: From luo; a loosening, i.e. (specially), divorce.

BDAG.en: release, separation, (in marriage) a divorce
BDAG.pt: libertação, separação, (no casamento) um divórcio

DEFINITION: it is advantageous to, it profits.
ORIGIN: Third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of lusis and telos; impersonally, it answers the purpose, i.e. Is advantageous.

BDAG.en: be advantageous, be better, it profits
BDAG.pt: ser vantajoso, ser melhor, ser lucrativo

DEFINITION: Lystra, a Lycaonian city in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Lystra, a city in Lycaonia in Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Listra, uma cidade na Derbe da Ásia Menor

DEFINITION: the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom, the price of ransoming; especially the sacrifice by which expiation is effected, an offering of expiation.
ORIGIN: From luo; something to loosen with, i.e. A redemption price (figuratively, atonement).

BDAG.en: price of release, ransom (esp. also the ransom money for the manumission of slaves)
BDAG.pt: preço de libertação, resgate (especialmente o dinheiro de resgate para a alforria de escravos)

DEFINITION: to release on receipt of ransom; mid: to redeem, release by paying ransom, liberate.
ORIGIN: From lutron; to ransom (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to free by paying a ransom, redeem; to liberate from an oppressive situation, set free, rescue, redeem
BDAG.pt: libertar mediante pagamento de resgate, resgatar; libertar de uma situação opressiva, pôr em liberdade, salvar, redimir

DEFINITION: (in the Old Testament: ransoming from imprisonment for debt, or from slavery, release from national misfortune, etc.), liberation, deliverance, release.
ORIGIN: From lutroo; a ransoming (figuratively).

BDAG.en: experience of being liberated from an oppressive situation, redemption (ransoming, releasing)
BDAG.pt: experiência de ser libertado de uma situação opressiva, redenção (resgate, liberação)

DEFINITION: a redeemer, liberator, deliverer.
ORIGIN: From lutroo; a redeemer (figuratively).

BDAG.en: redeemer
BDAG.pt: redentor

DEFINITION: a lamp-stand.
ORIGIN: From luchnos; a lamp-stand (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: lampstand upon which lamps were placed or hung (not a candlestick)
BDAG.pt: candelabro sobre o qual lâmpadas eram colocadas ou penduradas (não um castiçal)

DEFINITION: a (portable) lamp.
ORIGIN: From the base of leukos; a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: lamp (of metal or clay); light of a lamp; (metaph.) the eye, the Spirit of God, the heavenly Jerusalem
BDAG.pt: lâmpada (de metal ou argila); luz de uma lâmpada; (metaforicamente) o olho, o Espírito de Deus, a Jerusalém celestial

DEFINITION: (a) to loose, untie, release, (b) met: to break, destroy, set at naught, contravene; to break up a meeting, annul.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to "loosen" (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-)loose, melt, put off. Compare rhegnumi.

BDAG.en: to undo something that is used to tie up or constrain, loose, untie (bonds, fetters); to set free something tied or similarly constrained, set free, loose, untie (a prisoner, animal, thing); to reduce something by violence into its components, destroy (a building); to do away with, destroy, bring to an end, abolish (commandments, laws)
BDAG.pt: desfazer algo que serve para amarrar ou restringir, soltar, desatar (laços, grilhões); libertar algo amarrado ou constrangido de forma semelhante, pôr em liberdade, soltar, desatar (um prisioneiro, animal, coisa); reduzir algo pela força aos seus componentes, destruir (um edifício); abolir, destruir, pôr fim, anular (mandamentos, leis)

DEFINITION: Lois, grandmother of Timothy.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Lois, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Lois, grandmother of Timothy.
BDAG.pt: Lóide, avó de Timóteo.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Lot, nephew of Abraham.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Lowt); Lot, a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Lot, son of Haran, nephew of Abraham; he lived in Sodom and was rescued from that doomed city, having led a virtuous life. His wife perished because, upon leaving the city, she looked back, contrary to God’s command.
BDAG.pt: Ló, filho de Harã, sobrinho de Abraão; viveu em Sodoma e foi resgatado daquela cidade condenada, tendo conduzido uma vida virtuosa. Sua esposa pereceu porque, ao deixar a cidade, olhou para trás, contrariando o comando de Deus.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Maath, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Probably of Hebrew origin; Maath, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Maath, in the genealogy of Jesus.
BDAG.pt: Maate, na genealogia de Jesus.

DEFINITION: Magadan, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare migdal); the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a place in Palestine.

DEFINITION: Magdalene, of Magdala, a place on the coast of the Sea of Galilee near Tiberias.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a derivative of Magdala; a female Magdalene, i.e. Inhabitant of Magdala.

BDAG.en: woman from Magdala, Magdalene, surname of a certain Mary, probably from the town of Magdala.
BDAG.pt: mulher de Magdala, Madalena, sobrenome de uma certa Maria, provavelmente da cidade de Magdala.

DEFINITION: magic.
ORIGIN: From mageuo; "magic".

BDAG.en: a rite or rites ordinarily using incantations designed to influence/control transcendent powers, magic; magic arts.
BDAG.pt: um rito ou ritos usando ordinariamente encantamentos destinados a influenciar/controlar poderes transcendentes, magia; artes mágicas.

DEFINITION: to practice sorcery or magic.
ORIGIN: From magos; to practice magic.

BDAG.en: practice magic.
BDAG.pt: praticar magia.

DEFINITION: a Magian, an (Oriental) astrologer, by implication a magician.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (Rab-Mag); a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by implication, a magician.

BDAG.en: a Magus, a (Persian then also Babylonian) wise man and priest, who was expert in astrology, interpretation of dreams and various other occult arts; magician.
BDAG.pt: um Mago, um sábio e sacerdote (persa e depois babilônico) perito em astrologia, interpretação de sonhos e várias outras artes ocultas; mágico.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Magog, sometimes as name of a people, sometimes as name of a country in the Old Testament, probably the Scythians; hence: used in apocalyptic literature.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Magowg); Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party.

BDAG.en: Magog, mentioned w. Gog among the enemies of God in the last days.
BDAG.pt: Magogue, mencionado com Gog entre os inimigos de Deus nos últimos dias.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Midian, generally taken to mean or to include the peninsula of Sinai.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Midyan); Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia.

BDAG.en: Midian, a people in Arabia; land of Midian is the place where Moses stayed for a while
BDAG.pt: Midiã, um povo na Arábia; a terra de Midiã é o lugar onde Moisés permaneceu por um tempo

DEFINITION: to make a disciple of, train in discipleship; pass: to be trained, discipled, instructed.
ORIGIN: From mathetes; intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. Enrol as scholar.

BDAG.en: 1 to be a pupil, with implication of being an adherent of the teacher intr., be or become a pupil or disciple; 2 to cause one to be a pupil, teach, trans. make a disciple of, teach
BDAG.pt: 1 ser um pupilo, com a implicação de ser um adepto do mestre intr., ser ou tornar-se um pupilo ou discípulo; 2 fazer com que alguém seja um pupilo, ensinar, trans. fazer um discípulo de, ensinar

DEFINITION: a learner, disciple, pupil.
ORIGIN: From manthano; a learner, i.e. Pupil.

BDAG.en: learner, pupil, disciple (one who engages in learning through instruction); disciple, adherent (one who is constantly associated with someone who has a pedagogical reputation or a particular set of views); esp. of the disciples of Jesus (The Twelve, or male/female followers generally); even after Jesus’ resurrection those who followed him were called μ. (almost = Christian).
BDAG.pt: aprendiz, aluno, discípulo (aquele que se dedica a aprender através da instrução); discípulo, adepto (aquele que está constantemente associado a alguém com reputação pedagógica ou um conjunto particular de visões); especialmente dos discípulos de Jesus (os Doze, ou seguidores masculinos/femininos em geral); mesmo após a ressurreição de Jesus, aqueles que O seguiam eram chamados μ. (quase = cristão).

DEFINITION: a female disciple, female Christian.
ORIGIN: Feminine from mathetes; a female pupil.

BDAG.en: (female) disciple.
BDAG.pt: discípula (feminino).

DEFINITION: (Hebrew) Methuselah, son of Enoch and father of Lamech.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Mthuwshelach); Mathusala (i.e. Methushelach), an antediluvian.

BDAG.en: Methuselah, son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah.
BDAG.pt: Matusalém, filho de Enoque e avô de Noé.

DEFINITION: Menna, Mainan, a proper name.
ORIGIN: Probably of Hebrew origin; Mainan, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Menna (variant of Μεννά).
BDAG.pt: Menã (variante de Μεννά).

DEFINITION: to be raving mad, speak as a madman.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from a primary mao (to long for; through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac".

BDAG.en: be mad, be out of one’s mind (beside having a demon and as a result of it: have no control over oneself); said to one who has brought incredible news ('you’re crazy') or whose enthusiasm seems to have outrun better judgment ('you’re out of your mind, you’re raving').
BDAG.pt: estar louco, estar fora de si (além de ter um demônio e como resultado disso: não ter controle sobre si mesmo); dito a alguém que trouxe notícias incríveis ('você está louco') ou cujo entusiasmo parece ter ultrapassado o bom senso ('você está fora de si, você está delirando').

DEFINITION: to bless, pronounce blessed or happy.
ORIGIN: From makarios; to beatify, i.e. Pronounce (or esteem) fortunate.

BDAG.en: to call or consider someone especially favored, call/consider blessed, happy, fortunate.
BDAG.pt: chamar ou considerar alguém especialmente favorecido, chamar/considerar abençoado, feliz, afortunado.

DEFINITION: happy, blessed, to be envied.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of the poetical makar (meaning the same); supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off.

BDAG.en: fortunate, happy (less focus on the transcendent dimension); privileged, blessed, fortunate, happy, privileged, from a transcendent perspective (the more usual sense: one on whom fortune smiles); privileged recipient of divine favor.
BDAG.pt: afortunado, feliz (menos foco na dimensão transcendente); privilegiado, abençoado, afortunado, feliz, privilegiado, de uma perspectiva transcendente (o sentido mais usual: aquele sobre quem a sorte sorri); beneficiário privilegiado do favor divino.

DEFINITION: regarding as happy, blessed, or enviable.
ORIGIN: From makarizo; beatification, i.e. Attribution of good fortune.

BDAG.en: pronouncement of being in receipt of special favor, blessing, of a quotation from the Psalms beginning with אַשְׁרֵי =μακάριος
BDAG.pt: declaração de estar em posse de favor especial, bênção, de uma citação dos Salmos que começa com אַשְׁרֵי =μακάριος

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Macedonia, a Roman province north of Achaia (Greece).
ORIGIN: From Makedon; Macedonia, a region of Greece.

BDAG.en: Macedonia, a Roman province
BDAG.pt: Macedônia, uma província romana

DEFINITION: a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. Inhabitant of Macedonia.

BDAG.en: a Macedonian
BDAG.pt: um macedônio

DEFINITION: a meat-market, marketplace.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin (macellum); a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop.

BDAG.en: meat market, food market
BDAG.pt: mercado de carne, mercado de alimentos

DEFINITION: at a distance, far away, remote, alien.
ORIGIN: Feminine accusative case singular of makros (hodos being implied); at a distance (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: far (away), at a relatively great distance (used adverbially or as a preposition)
BDAG.pt: longe (advérbio ou preposição), a uma distância relativamente grande

DEFINITION: from a (long) distance, afar.
ORIGIN: Adverb from makros; from a distance or afar.

BDAG.en: from far away, from a distance
BDAG.pt: de longe, a uma distância

DEFINITION: to suffer long, have patience, be forbearing, perseverance.
ORIGIN: From the same as makrothumos; to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient.
USAGE: bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure.

BDAG.en: to remain tranquil while waiting, have patience, wait; to bear up under provocation without complaint, be patient, forbearing; to delay
BDAG.pt: permanecer tranquilo enquanto espera, ter paciência, esperar; suportar a provocação sem reclamar, ser paciente, tolerante; demorar

DEFINITION: patience, forbearance, longsuffering.
ORIGIN: From the same as makrothumos; longanimity, i.e. (objectively) forbearance or (subjectively) fortitude.

BDAG.en: state of remaining tranquil while awaiting an outcome, patience, steadfastness, endurance; state of being able to bear up under provocation, forbearance, patience toward others
BDAG.pt: estado de permanecer tranquilo enquanto aguarda um resultado, paciência, firmeza, perseverança; estado de ser capaz de suportar a provocação, tolerância, paciência para com os outros

DEFINITION: with longsuffering, patiently.
ORIGIN: Adverb of a compound of makros and thumos; with long (enduring) temper, i.e. Leniently.

BDAG.en: patiently
BDAG.pt: pacientemente

DEFINITION: long, distant, far; of long duration.
ORIGIN: From mekos; long (in place (distant) or time (neuter plural)).

BDAG.en: pert. to taking a relatively long time, long; pert. to being relatively distant, far away, distant
BDAG.pt: pertencente a levar um tempo relativamente longo, longo; pertencente a ser relativamente distante, longe

DEFINITION: long-timed, long-lived.
ORIGIN: From makros and chronos; long-timed, i.e. Long-lived.

BDAG.en: long-lived
BDAG.pt: de vida longa

DEFINITION: weakness, illness, sickness.
ORIGIN: From malakos; softness, i.e. Enervation (debility).

BDAG.en: condition of bodily weakness, debility, weakness, sickness; condition of inner weakness, faint-heartedness, despondency, lack of energy
BDAG.pt: condição de fraqueza corporal, debilidade, doença; condição de fraqueza interior, desânimo, falta de energia

DEFINITION: (a) soft, (b) of persons: soft, delicate, effeminate.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; soft, i.e. Fine (clothing); figuratively, a catamite.

BDAG.en: pert. to being yielding to touch, soft, of things; pert. to being passive in a same-sex relationship, effeminate
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser maleável ao toque, macio, de coisas; pertencente a ser passivo em uma relação do mesmo sexo, efeminado

DEFINITION: Mahalaleel or Maleleel, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Mahalal'el); Maleleel (i.e. Mahalalel), an antediluvian.

BDAG.en: Maleleel (Gen 5:12), in the genealogy of Jesus Lk 3:37.
BDAG.pt: Maleleel (Gênesis 5:12), na genealogia de Jesus, Lucas 3:37.

DEFINITION: most of all, especially.
ORIGIN: Neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb mala (very); (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly.

BDAG.en: to an unusual degree, most of all, above all, especially, particularly, (very) greatly; marker of high level of certitude, most assuredly, certainly
BDAG.pt: em um grau incomum, acima de tudo, especialmente, particularmente, (muito) grandemente; marcador de alto nível de certeza, com toda a certeza, certamente

DEFINITION: more, rather.
ORIGIN: Neuter of the comparative of the same as malista; (adverbially) more (in a greater degree)) or rather.
USAGE: + better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather.

BDAG.en: to a greater or higher degree, more; for a better reason, rather, all the more; marker of an alternative to someth., rather in the sense instead (of someth.)
BDAG.pt: a um grau ou nível mais elevado, mais; por uma razão melhor, em vez disso, ainda mais; marcador de uma alternativa a algo, antes no sentido de em vez de (algo)

DEFINITION: Malchus, a servant of the high-priest at Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Melek); Malchus, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Malchus, slave of the high priest, whom Peter wounded when Jesus was arrested J 18:10.
BDAG.pt: Malco, servo do sumo sacerdote, a quem Pedro feriu quando Jesus foi preso em João 18:10.

DEFINITION: a grandmother.
ORIGIN: Of natural origin ("mammy"); a grandmother.

BDAG.en: grandmother (orig. 'mother')
BDAG.pt: avó (originalmente 'mãe')

DEFINITION: (Aramaic), riches, money, possessions, property.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (confidence, i.e. Wealth, personified); mammonas, i.e. Avarice (deified).

BDAG.en: wealth, property. Personified, ‘Mammon’.
BDAG.pt: riqueza, propriedade. Personificado, 'Mamon'.

DEFINITION: (Graecized form of Aramaic Menahem), Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas' court.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Manaen, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Manaen, one of the prophets and teachers in the Antioch church, described as Herod’s childhood companion (tetrarch).
BDAG.pt: Manaém, um dos profetas e mestres na igreja de Antioquia, descrito como companheiro de infância de Herodes (tetrarca).

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), Manasseh, (a) son of Joseph, founder of a tribe of Israel, (b) son of Hezekiah and father of Amon (Amos).
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Mnashsheh); Mannasses (i.e. Menashsheh), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Manasseh. 1 firstborn son of Joseph (father of a tribe). 2 son of Hezekiah, Hebrew king; in the genealogy of Jesus.
BDAG.pt: Manassés. 1 primogênito de José (pai de uma tribo). 2 filho de Ezequias, rei hebreu; na genealogia de Jesus.

DEFINITION: to learn; with adj. or nouns: to learn to be so and so; with acc. of person who is the object of knowledge; aor. sometimes: to ascertain.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, matheo, is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn (in any way).

BDAG.en: to gain knowledge or skill by instruction, learn; make the acquaintance of, learn about, come to know; to come to a realization, learn, appropriate to oneself (often through experience); hear
BDAG.pt: adquirir conhecimento ou habilidade por instrução, aprender; fazer conhecimento de, saber sobre, chegar a conhecer; chegar a uma percepção, aprender, apropriar-se (muitas vezes por experiência); ouvir

DEFINITION: raving madness, frenzy, insanity.
ORIGIN: From mainomai; craziness.

BDAG.en: madness, frenzy, delirium. Frequently used in a non-diagnostic sense of eccentric or bizarre behavior in word or action.
BDAG.pt: loucura, frenesi, delírio. Frequentemente usada em um sentido não diagnóstico para descrever comportamento excêntrico ou bizarro em palavras ou ações.

DEFINITION: (Hebrew), manna, the supernatural food eaten by the Israelites in the desert: of spiritual food.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (man); manna (i.e. Man), an edible gum.

BDAG.en: 'manna', often identified with the sweetish exudate of the manna tamarisk and related trees, produced by the sting of an insect; a food esp. associated with Israel’s experience, supplied to the Israelites during their wanderings; a heavenly food.
BDAG.pt: 'maná', frequentemente identificado com o exsudato adocicado do tamarisco de maná e árvores relacionadas, produzido pela picada de um inseto; um alimento especialmente associado à experiência de Israel, fornecido aos israelitas durante seu êxodo; um alimento celestial.

DEFINITION: to divine, practice soothsaying, suggesting the fraud involved in the practice.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of mainomai (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration); to divine, i.e. Utter spells (under pretense of foretelling.

BDAG.en: to practice divination, prophesy, divine, give an oracle; to consult a diviner, consult an oracle.
BDAG.pt: praticar adivinhação, profetizar, consultar oráculos, dar um oráculo; consultar um adivinho, consultar um oráculo.

DEFINITION: pass: to die, wither (like the grass).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away.

BDAG.en: to disappear gradually, die out, fade, disappear, wither (of plants, spirit, beauty); wither away (of a rich person)
BDAG.pt: desaparecer gradualmente, extinguir-se, desvanecer-se, sumir, murchar (de plantas, espírito, beleza); definhar (de uma pessoa rica)

DEFINITION: (Aramaic), either: Our Lord hath come, or: Our Lord cometh (will come, is at hand).
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come); maranatha, i.e. An exclamation of the approaching divine judgment.

DEFINITION: a pearl.
ORIGIN: From margaros (a pearl-oyster); a pearl.

BDAG.en: pearl; metaphorically, spiritual pearls of a martyr’s bonds; used in a proverb 'casting pearls before swine'
BDAG.pt: pérola; metaforicamente, pérolas espirituais das cadeias de um mártir; usado em um provérbio 'lançar pérolas diante dos porcos'

DEFINITION: Martha, sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany.
ORIGIN: Probably of Chaldee origin (meaning mistress); Martha, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Martha, sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany.
BDAG.pt: Marta, irmã de Maria e Lázaro de Betânia.

DEFINITION: Mary, Miriam, (a) the mother of Jesus, (b) of Magdala, (c) sister of Martha and Lazarus, (d) wife of Cleopas, (e) mother of John Mark, (f) a Christian woman in Rome.
ORIGIN: Or Mariam (mar-ee-am') of Hebrew origin (Miryam); Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females.

BDAG.en: Mary, specifically: 1. The mother of Jesus. 2. Mary Magdalene. 3. The 'other' Mary, mother of James and Joses. 4. Mary of Clopas. 5. Mary, sister of Martha. 6. The mother of John Mark. 7. An otherwise unknown Christian woman.
BDAG.pt: Maria, especificamente: 1. A mãe de Jesus. 2. Maria Madalena. 3. A 'outra' Maria, mãe de Tiago e Jose. 4. Maria de Clopas. 5. Maria, irmã de Marta. 6. A mãe de João Marcos. 7. Uma mulher cristã de outra forma desconhecida.

DEFINITION: Mark, who also had the Hebrew name John, son of Mary, nephew of Barnabas, coadjutor of Barnabas, Paul, and Peter.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; Marcus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Mark, a name found rather freq. (Diod S 11, 63, 1; Plut., ins, pap; Philo, Leg. ad Gai. 62; 294; Joseph.; Just., D. 141, 5; Ath. [ins]); surname of John (s. Ἰωάν(ν)ης 6), son of Mary of Jerusalem (s. Μαρία 6). Perh. introduced to Paul by Barnabas, his cousin (Col 4:10); he accompanied Paul and Barnabas on the so-called first missionary journey, but left them before it was completed, and later became the cause of an open break betw. them. Ac 12:12, 25; 15:37, 39. The same pers. is certainly referred to Phlm 24; 2 Ti 4:11; 1 Pt 5:13. Title of the second gosp. κατὰΜᾶρκον...
BDAG.pt: Marcos, um nome encontrado com relativa frequência...; sobrenome de João, filho de Maria de Jerusalém. Talvez apresentado a Paulo por Barnabé, seu primo; acompanhou Paulo e Barnabé na chamada primeira viagem missionária, mas os deixou antes de sua conclusão, e mais tarde se tornou a causa de uma separação aberta entre eles. A mesma pessoa é certamente referida em Filêmon, 2 Timóteo e 1 Pedro. Título do segundo evangelho, segundo Marcos...

DEFINITION: a crystalline stone, marble.
ORIGIN: From marmairo (to glisten); marble (as sparkling white).

BDAG.en: marble (so since Theophr., Lap. 9; Strabo 9, 1, 23; IG IV2/1, 109 III, 103 [III b.c.]; PLeid X, 10, 12; BGU 952, 10; EpJer 71; Jos., Bell. 4, 532; both masc. and fem. and neut. TestSol) as precious material Rv 18:12.
BDAG.pt: mármore (desde Teofrasto, etc.) como material precioso em Apocalipse 18:12.

DEFINITION: to witness, bear witness, give evidence, testify, give a good report.
ORIGIN: From martus; to be a witness, i.e. Testify (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness.

BDAG.en: to confirm or attest someth. on the basis of personal knowledge or belief, bear witness, be a witness. a to offer testimony... b to confirm bear witness to, declare, confirm... c to support one’s testimony with total selfgiving, eccl. usage w. regard to martyrdom bear witness, testify, be a witness (unto death), be martyred... 2 to affirm in a supportive manner, testify favorably, speak well (of), approve...
BDAG.pt: confirmar ou atestar algo com base em conhecimento ou crença pessoal, dar testemunho, ser uma testemunha. a oferecer testemunho... b confirmar, testemunhar, declarar, confirmar... c apoiar o testemunho com total entrega pessoal, uso eclesiástico em relação ao martírio, testemunhar, dar testemunho (até a morte), ser martirizado... 2 afirmar de maneira favorável, testemunhar favoravelmente, falar bem (de), aprovar...

DEFINITION: witness, evidence, testimony, reputation.
ORIGIN: From martus; evidence given (judicially or genitive case).

BDAG.en: confirmation or attestation on the basis of personal knowledge or belief, testimony a act of testifying testimony, testifying... b content of testimony... 2 testimony in court, testimony... 3 attestation of character or behavior, testimony, statement of approval... 4 testimony that invites death, a martyr’s death, martyrdom...
BDAG.pt: confirmação ou atestação baseada em conhecimento ou crença pessoal, testemunho a ato de testemunhar, testemunho... b conteúdo do testemunho... 2 testemunho em tribunal, depoimento... 3 atestação de caráter ou comportamento, testemunho, declaração de aprovação... 4 testemunho que convida à morte, morte de mártir, martírio...

DEFINITION: witness, evidence, testimony, proof.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of martus; something evidential, i.e. (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle).

BDAG.en: that which serves as testimony or proof, testimony, proof; tent of meeting, tent/tabernacle of testimony; martyrdom
BDAG.pt: aquilo que serve como testemunho ou prova, testemunho, prova; tenda de reunião, tabernáculo de testemunho; martírio

DEFINITION: (properly: to call (summon) to witness, and then absolutely) to testify, protest, asseverate; to conjure, solemnly charge.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from martus; to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation).

BDAG.en: to affirm something with solemnity, testify, bear witness; to urge something as a matter of great importance, affirm, insist, implore
BDAG.pt: afirmar algo com solenidade, testemunhar, dar testemunho; insistir em algo como de grande importância, afirmar, insistir, implorar

DEFINITION: a witness; an eye- or ear-witness.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a witness (literally (judicially) or figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr".

BDAG.en: one who testifies in legal matters, witness; one who affirms or attests, testifier, witness (transferred sense); one who witnesses at cost of life, martyr
BDAG.pt: aquele que testemunha em assuntos legais, testemunha; aquele que afirma ou atesta, testemunhador, testemunha (sentido transferido); aquele que testemunha ao custo da própria vida, mártir

DEFINITION: to bite, gnaw, chew.
ORIGIN: From a primary masso (to handle or squeeze); to chew.

DEFINITION: to flog, scourge, the victim being strapped to a pole or frame; met: to chastise.
ORIGIN: From mastix; to flog (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to beat with a whip or lash, whip, flog, scourge; afflict, torment, mistreat; to punish with discipline in mind, punish, chastise
BDAG.pt: bater com um chicote ou azorrague, açoitar, flagelar, açoitar; afligir, atormentar, maltratar; punir com disciplina em mente, castigar, disciplinar

DEFINITION: to flog, scourge, whip.
ORIGIN: From mastos; to whip (literally).

BDAG.en: strike with a whip; specifically of interrogation under torture, scourge
BDAG.pt: golpear com um chicote; especificamente de interrogatório sob tortura, açoitar

DEFINITION: (a) a scourge, lash, of leathern thongs with pieces of metal sewn up in them, (b) met: severe pains (sufferings), disease.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of massaomai (through the idea of contact); a whip (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a disease).
