BDAG.pt: um instrumento flexível usado para açoitar, chicote, azorrague; uma condição de grande aflição, tormento, sofrimento, extensão figurada do significado 1

DEFINITION: the breast, pap.
ORIGIN: From the base of massaomai; a (properly, female) breast (as if kneaded up).

BDAG.en: one of the mammillae, of a male, nipple; mammary gland or mamma of a female, breast
BDAG.pt: uma das mamilas, de um homem, mamilo; glândula mamária ou mama de uma fêmea, seio

DEFINITION: vain speaking, foolish talking.
ORIGIN: From mataiologos; random talk, i.e. Babble.

BDAG.en: empty, fruitless talk
BDAG.pt: conversa vazia, infrutífera

DEFINITION: a vain, empty talker.
ORIGIN: From mataios and lego; an idle (i.e. Senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. A wrangler.

BDAG.en: talking idly, subst. an idle talker, windbag
BDAG.pt: que fala inutilmente, substantivado como tagarela, falador

DEFINITION: vain, unreal, ineffectual, unproductive; practically: godless.
ORIGIN: From the base of maten; empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or (specially), an idol.

BDAG.en: pert. to being of no use, idle, empty, fruitless, useless, powerless, lacking truth
BDAG.pt: pertencente a não ter utilidade, vão, vazio, infrutífero, inútil, sem poder, carente de verdade

DEFINITION: vanity, emptiness, unreality, purposelessness, ineffectiveness, instability, frailty; false religion.
ORIGIN: From mataios; inutility; figuratively, transientness; morally, depravity.

BDAG.en: state of being without use or value, emptiness, futility, purposelessness, transitoriness
BDAG.pt: estado de estar sem uso ou valor, vazio, futilidade, falta de propósito, transitoriedade

DEFINITION: to become vain or foolish, be perverted.
ORIGIN: From mataios; to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally) wicked or (specially), idolatrous.

BDAG.en: render futile/worthless; pass. be given over to worthlessness, think about idle, worthless things, be foolish
BDAG.pt: tornar fútil/inútil; passivo: ser entregue à inutilidade, pensar em coisas vãs e inúteis, ser tolo

DEFINITION: in vain, in an unreal way, to no purpose.
ORIGIN: Accusative case of a derivative of the base of massaomai (through the idea of tentative manipulation, i.e. Unsuccessful search, or else of punishment); folly, i.e. (adverbially) to no purpose.

BDAG.en: in vain, to no end
BDAG.pt: em vão, sem propósito

DEFINITION: Matthew.
ORIGIN: A shorter form of machomai; Matthaeus (i.e. Matthitjah), an Israelite and a Christian.

DEFINITION: Matthan, an Israelite.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Mattan); Matthan (i.e. Mattan), an Israelite.

DEFINITION: Matthat, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Probably a shortened form of Mattathias; Matthat (i.e. Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites.

DEFINITION: Matthias.
ORIGIN: Apparently a shortened form of Mattathias; Matthias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite.

DEFINITION: Mattatha, an Israelite.
ORIGIN: Probably a shortened form of Mattathias (compare soterion); Mattatha (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Mattatha, son of Nathan, grandson of David; in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Matata, filho de Natã, neto de Davi; na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: Mattathias, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Mattithyah); Mattathias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite and a Christian.

BDAG.en: Mattathias, in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Matatias, na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: a short sword or dagger.
ORIGIN: Probably feminine of a presumed derivative of mache; a knife, i.e. Dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment.

BDAG.en: a relatively short sword or other sharp instrument, sword, dagger
BDAG.pt: uma espada relativamente curta ou outro instrumento cortante, espada, punhal

DEFINITION: (earlier: a battle, conflict, hence) in the sphere of words, etc: strife, contention, quarrel.
ORIGIN: From machomai; a battle, i.e. (figuratively) controversy.

BDAG.en: fighting, quarrels, strife, disputes
BDAG.pt: luta, brigas, discórdia, disputas

DEFINITION: to engage in battle, fight; hence: to strive, contend, dispute.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to war, i.e. (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute.

BDAG.en: to engage in physical combat, fight; to engage in heated dispute, without use of weapons, fight, quarrel, dispute
BDAG.pt: engajar-se em combate físico, lutar; envolver-se em disputa acalorada, sem uso de armas, brigar, discutir, disputar

DEFINITION: I, me, my.
ORIGIN: A shorter (and probably originally) from of eme; me.

DEFINITION: to boast, be arrogant, vaunt.
ORIGIN: From a compound of megas and aucheo (to boast; akin to auzano and kauchaomai); to talk big, i.e. Be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic).

BDAG.en: become proud, boast
BDAG.pt: tornar-se orgulhoso, vangloriar-se

DEFINITION: grand, magnificent, splendid.
ORIGIN: From megas; magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection.

BDAG.en: magnificent, splendid, grand (used only substantively for what impresses mind or spirit: greatness, sublimity; mighty deeds)
BDAG.pt: magnífico, esplêndido, grandioso (usado apenas substantivamente para o que impressiona a mente ou o espírito: grandeza, sublimidade; feitos poderosos)

DEFINITION: (divine) majesty or magnificence, glory.
ORIGIN: From megaleios; superbness, i.e. Glory or splendor.

BDAG.en: quality or state of being foremost in esteem, grandeur, sublimity, majesty; quality or state of experiencing high esteem because of awesome performance, impressiveness
BDAG.pt: qualidade ou estado de ser o principal em estima, grandiosidade, sublimidade, majestade; qualidade ou estado de experimentar alta estima devido a um desempenho impressionante, imponência

DEFINITION: magnificent, superb, transcendent, majestic.
ORIGIN: From megas and prepo; befitting greatness or magnificence (majestic).

BDAG.en: magnificent, sublime, majestic, impressive
BDAG.pt: magnífico, sublime, majestoso, impressionante

DEFINITION: (a) to enlarge, lengthen, (b) to increase, magnify, extol.
ORIGIN: From megas; to make (or declare) great, i.e. Increase or (figuratively) extol.

BDAG.en: cause to be large, make large/long, make great; exalt, glorify, magnify, speak highly of; increase, grow
BDAG.pt: fazer parecer grande, tornar grande/longo, engrandecer; exaltar, glorificar, magnificar, falar bem de; aumentar, crescer

DEFINITION: greatly, very much, vehemently.
ORIGIN: Adverb from megas; much.

BDAG.en: greatly, very (much), greatly (used to strengthen a verb)
BDAG.pt: grandemente, muito (usado para intensificar um verbo)

DEFINITION: (divine) majesty, greatness.
ORIGIN: From megas; greatness, i.e. (figuratively) divinity (often God himself).

BDAG.en: a state of greatness or preeminence, majesty, used only of God
BDAG.pt: um estado de grandeza ou preeminência, majestade, usado apenas para Deus

DEFINITION: large, great, in the widest sense.
ORIGIN: (including the prolonged forms, feminine megale, plural megaloi, etc.; compare also megistos, meizon); big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application).
USAGE: (+ fear) exceedingly, great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years.

BDAG.en: large, great (of any extension in space); suggesting spaciousness; pertaining to number; of age (young or old); above average in quantity; above standard in intensity (loud sound, strong wind, intense heat, surprising event, great emotion); relatively superior in importance (God, rulers, prominent people, sublime/important things, a great day); very great, extraordinary (superlative sense).
BDAG.pt: grande, vasto (de qualquer extensão no espaço); sugerindo amplitude; referente a número; de idade (jovem ou velho); acima da média em quantidade; acima do padrão em intensidade (som alto, vento forte, calor intenso, evento surpreendente, grande emoção); relativamente superior em importância (Deus, governantes, pessoas proeminentes, coisas sublimes/importantes, um grande dia); muito grande, extraordinário (sentido superlativo).

DEFINITION: greatness, vastness.
ORIGIN: From megas; magnitude (figuratively).

BDAG.en: quality of exceeding a standard involving physical magnitude, size; quality of exceeding a standard of excellence, greatness (especially of God's power or joy).
BDAG.pt: qualidade de exceder um padrão de magnitude física, tamanho; qualidade de exceder um padrão de excelência, grandeza (especialmente do poder ou alegria de Deus).

DEFINITION: a great one, a lord; a courtier, satrap, nobleman.
ORIGIN: Plural from megistos; grandees.

BDAG.en: a person of high rank, great man, courtier, magnate
BDAG.pt: uma pessoa de alta patente, grande homem, cortesão, magnata

DEFINITION: greatest.
ORIGIN: Superlative of megas; greatest or very great.

BDAG.en: superlative of μέγας: very great, extraordinary.
BDAG.pt: superlativo de μέγας: muito grande, extraordinário.

DEFINITION: to translate (from one language into another), interpret.
ORIGIN: From meta and hermeneuo; to explain over, i.e. Translate.

BDAG.en: to translate (explaining or rendering meaning).
BDAG.pt: traduzir (explicando ou transmitindo o sentido).

DEFINITION: deep drinking, drunkenness.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; an intoxicant, i.e. (by implication) intoxication.

BDAG.en: drunkenness, dissipation, revelry.
BDAG.pt: embriaguez, dissolução, folia.

DEFINITION: to cause to change its place, move out of its place; to translate, transfer, remove.
ORIGIN: Methistano meth-is-tan'-o from meta and histemi; to transfer, i.e. Carry away, depose or (figuratively) exchange, seduce.
USAGE: put out, remove, translate, turn away.

BDAG.en: to transfer from one place to another, remove, depose; to bring to a different point of view, turn away, mislead.
BDAG.pt: transferir de um lugar para outro, remover, depor; levar a um ponto de vista diferente, desviar, enganar.

DEFINITION: (a way of search after something, an inquiry; a method), scheming, craftiness, deceit.
ORIGIN: From a compound of meta and hodeuo (compare "method"); travelling over, i.e. Travesty (trickery).

BDAG.en: scheming, craftiness, wiles, stratagems (only in an unfavorable sense).
BDAG.pt: planejamento ardiloso, astúcia, artimanhas, estratagemas (somente em sentido desfavorável).

DEFINITION: confine, border, boundary.
ORIGIN: From meta and horion; bounded alongside, i.e. Contiguous (neuter plural as noun, frontier).

BDAG.en: boundary; also the region included by the boundaries
BDAG.pt: fronteira; também a região incluída pelos limites

DEFINITION: to make drunk; pass: to become drunk.
ORIGIN: A prolonged (transitive) form of methuo; to intoxicate.

BDAG.en: to cause to become intoxicated; (passive) to get drunk, become intoxicated.
BDAG.pt: fazer ficar intoxicado; (passivo) ficar bêbado, ficar embriagado.

DEFINITION: a drunkard.
ORIGIN: From methuo; tipsy, i.e. (as noun) a sot.

BDAG.en: drunkard
BDAG.pt: bêbado

DEFINITION: to be intoxicated with wine, be drunk.
ORIGIN: From another form of methe; to drink to intoxication, i.e. Get drunk.

BDAG.en: to drink to a point of intoxication, be drunk
BDAG.pt: beber até o ponto de intoxicação, estar bêbado

DEFINITION: greater, greatest.
ORIGIN: Neuter of meizon; (adverbially) in greater degree.

DEFINITION: greater.
ORIGIN: Continued comparative of meizon; still larger (figuratively).

BDAG.en: see μέγας
BDAG.pt: ver μέγας

DEFINITION: elder, greater, more.
ORIGIN: Irregular comparative of megas; larger (literally or figuratively, specially, in age).

BDAG.en: see μέγας
BDAG.pt: ver μέγας

DEFINITION: ink.
ORIGIN: Neuter of melas as noun; ink.

BDAG.en: see μέλας
BDAG.pt: ver μέλας

DEFINITION: black.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; black.

BDAG.en: black; ink
BDAG.pt: preto; tinta

DEFINITION: Melea, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Meleas, an Israelite.

DEFINITION: to devise, plan; practice, exercise myself in, study, ponder.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of melo; to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind.

BDAG.en: to work with something definite in mind, take care, endeavor; to improve by care or study, practice, cultivate, take pains; to fix one’s mind on something, think about, meditate upon
BDAG.pt: trabalhar com algo definido em mente, cuidar, esforçar-se; melhorar com cuidado ou estudo, praticar, cultivar, empenhar-se; fixar a mente em algo, pensar, meditar sobre

DEFINITION: honey.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; honey.

BDAG.en: honey; sweet; sign of fertility; healing remedy
BDAG.pt: mel; doce; sinal de fertilidade; remédio curativo

DEFINITION: belonging to bees, coming from bees.
ORIGIN: From meli; relating to honey, i.e. Bee (comb).

BDAG.en: pert. to the bee, (bee-)honeycomb, bee-hive
BDAG.pt: pertencente à abelha, (de) favo de mel, colmeia

DEFINITION: Melita (Malta), an island in the Mediterranean.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Melita, an island in the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Malta, an island located south of Sicily
BDAG.pt: Malta, uma ilha localizada ao sul da Sicília

DEFINITION: to intend, be about to; to delay, linger.
ORIGIN: A strengthened form of melo (through the idea of expectation); to intend, i.e. Be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity, probability, possibility, or hesitation).
USAGE: about, after that, be (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, intend, was to (be), mean, mind, be at the point, (be) ready, + return, shall (begin), (which, that) should (after, afterwards, hereafter) tarry, which was for, will, would, be yet.

BDAG.en: to take place at a future point of time and so to be subsequent to another event, be about to; be inevitable, be destined, inevitable; denoting an intended action: intend, propose, have in mind
BDAG.pt: ocorrer em um ponto futuro e, portanto, ser subsequente a outro evento, estar prestes a; ser inevitável, estar destinado, inevitável; denotar uma ação pretendida: pretender, propor, ter em mente

DEFINITION: a member or limb (of the body).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a limb or part of the body.

BDAG.en: a part of the human body, member, part, limb; a part as member of a whole, member (of the Christian community)
BDAG.pt: parte do corpo humano, membro, parte, rã; uma parte como membro de um todo, membro (da comunidade cristã)

DEFINITION: Melchi, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (melek with pronominal suffix, my king); Melchi (i.e. Malki), the name of two Israelites.

BDAG.en: Melchi, in the genealogy of Jesus (son of Jannai, father of Levi; or son of Addi, father of Neri)
BDAG.pt: Melqui, na genealogia de Jesus (filho de Janai, pai de Levi; ou filho de Addi, pai de Neri)

DEFINITION: Melchizedek, king and priest of Salem.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Malkiy-Tsedeq); Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High in the time of Abraham; a type of Christ as High Priest
BDAG.pt: Melquisedeque, rei de Salém e sacerdote do Deus Altíssimo na época de Abraão; um tipo de Cristo como Sumo Sacerdote

DEFINITION: it is a care, it is an object of anxiety, it concerns.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to be of interest to, i.e. To concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally, it matters).

BDAG.en: it is a care/concern, is of interest to someone; be a source of concern
BDAG.pt: ser uma preocupação/interesse para alguém; ser uma fonte de preocupação

DEFINITION: a parchment leaf, perhaps for notes.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin ("membrane"); a (written) sheep-skin.

BDAG.en: parchment, used for making of books or for sundry writing purposes
BDAG.pt: pergaminho, usado para fazer livros ou para diversos fins de escrita

DEFINITION: to blame, censure, find fault.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to blame.

BDAG.en: find fault with, blame
BDAG.pt: censurar, culpar

DEFINITION: blaming one's lot or destiny, discontented, complaining.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of memphomai and moira (fate; akin to the base of meros); blaming fate, i.e. Querulous (discontented).

BDAG.en: complaining about one's lot, discontented
BDAG.pt: queixoso sobre sua sorte, descontente

DEFINITION: an untranslatable particle, generally answered by de, each of the two introducing a clause intended to be contrasted with the other.
ORIGIN: A primary particle; properly, indicative of affirmation or concession (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with de (this one, the former, etc.).
USAGE: even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily. Often compounded with other particles in an intensive or asseverative sense.

BDAG.en: affirmative particle, often marking a concessive clause with a subsequent adversative clause (to be sure... but, on the one hand... on the other hand); or simply to separate thoughts
BDAG.pt: partícula afirmativa, frequentemente marcando uma oração concessiva com uma oração adversativa subsequente (certamente... mas, por um lado... por outro lado); ou simplesmente para separar pensamentos

DEFINITION: nay rather; indeed, truly, really.
ORIGIN: From Not Used and oun and ge; so then at least.

BDAG.en: particles used esp. in answers, to emphasize or correct; rather, on the contrary; Indeed; more than that
BDAG.pt: partículas usadas especialmente em respostas, para enfatizar ou corrigir; antes, pelo contrário; De fato; mais do que isso

DEFINITION: (a) indeed, really, (b) yet, however, nevertheless.
ORIGIN: From Not Used and toi; indeed though, i.e. However.

BDAG.en: really, actually; mostly adversative: though, to be sure, indeed; nevertheless; yet, despite that; but
BDAG.pt: realmente, de fato; principalmente adversativo: embora, com certeza, de fato; não obstante; ainda assim, apesar disso; mas

DEFINITION: to remain, abide, stay, wait; with acc: to wait for, await.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to stay (in a given place, state, relation or expectancy).
USAGE: abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain, stand, tarry (for), X thine own.

BDAG.en: remain, stay; continue to exist, remain, last, persist, continue to live; wait for, await; (intransitive sense) to remain in the same state
BDAG.pt: permanecer, ficar; continuar a existir, durar, persistir, continuar vivendo; esperar, aguardar; (sentido intransitivo) permanecer no mesmo estado

DEFINITION: to divide into parts, divide, part, share, distribute; mid: to share, take part in a partitioning; to distract.
ORIGIN: From meros; to part, i.e. (literally) to apportion, bestow, share, or (figuratively) to disunite, differ.
USAGE: deal, be difference between, distribute, divide, give participle

BDAG.en: divide, separate; share something with someone; divide (a person or state), become disunited; take a part; distribute, allot, assign, apportion
BDAG.pt: dividir, separar; compartilhar algo com alguém; dividir (pessoa ou estado), tornar-se desunido; tomar uma parte; distribuir, repartir, designar, atribuir

DEFINITION: care, worry, anxiety.
ORIGIN: From merizo (through the idea of distraction); solicitude.

BDAG.en: anxiety, worry, care (of life, of the world)
BDAG.pt: ansiedade, preocupação, cuidado (da vida, do mundo)

DEFINITION: to be over-anxious; with acc: to be anxious about, distracted; to care for.
ORIGIN: From merimna; to be anxious about.

BDAG.en: to be apprehensive, have anxiety, be anxious, be (unduly) concerned; to attend to, care for, be concerned about
BDAG.pt: estar apreensivo, ter ansiedade, estar ansioso, estar (excessivamente) preocupado; cuidar, tomar providências, estar interessado em

DEFINITION: (a) a part, division of a country, (b) a share, portion.
ORIGIN: Feminine of meros; a portion, i.e. Province, share or (abstractly) participation.

BDAG.en: a portion of a whole that has been divided, part; share, portion
BDAG.pt: uma porção de um todo que foi dividido, parte; quinhão, parte

DEFINITION: (a) a distributing, a distribution, (b) a parting, dividing, severance, separation.
ORIGIN: From merizo; a separation or distribution.

BDAG.en: division, separation; distribution, apportionment
BDAG.pt: divisão, separação; distribuição, repartição

DEFINITION: a divider, partitioner, distributor.
ORIGIN: From merizo; an apportioner (administrator).

BDAG.en: divider, arbitrator
BDAG.pt: divisor, árbitro

DEFINITION: a part, share, portion.
ORIGIN: From an obsolete but more primary form of meiromai (to get as a section or allotment); a division or share (literally or figuratively, in a wide application).
USAGE: behalf, course, coast, craft, particular (+ -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect, side, some sort(-what).

BDAG.en: part, portion (in contrast to the whole); component, element; region, district; side; piece; party; branch or line of business; matter, affair
BDAG.pt: parte, quinhão (em contraste com o todo); componente, elemento; região, distrito; lado; pedaço; facção, partido; ramo ou ramo de negócio; assunto, matéria

DEFINITION: (lit: midday, hence, the position of the sun at midday), the South.
ORIGIN: From mesos and hemera; midday; by implication, the south.

BDAG.en: midday, noon; the south.
BDAG.pt: meio-dia, meio-dia; o sul.

DEFINITION: to mediate, interpose, give bail.
ORIGIN: From mesites; to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify (as surety).

BDAG.en: guarantee, in the sense of settling a matter (by an oath)
BDAG.pt: garantir, no sentido de resolver um assunto (por meio de um juramento)

DEFINITION: (a) a mediator, intermediary, (b) a go-between, arbiter, agent of something good.
ORIGIN: From mesos; a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor).

BDAG.en: one who mediates between two parties to remove a disagreement or reach a common goal, mediator, arbitrator, of Christ
BDAG.pt: aquele que intermedeia entre duas partes para remover um desacordo ou alcançar um objetivo comum, mediador, árbitro, de Cristo

DEFINITION: midnight, the middle of the period between sunset and sunrise.
ORIGIN: Neuter of compound of mesos and nux; midnight (especially as a watch).

BDAG.en: midnight.
BDAG.pt: meia-noite.

DEFINITION: Mesopotamia, the Country between the (two) Rivers, i.e. the Euphrates and the Tigris.
ORIGIN: From mesos and potamos; Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and the Tigris; compare 'Aram Naharayim), a region of Asia.

BDAG.en: Mesopotamia (land between rivers).
BDAG.pt: Mesopotâmia (terra entre rios).

DEFINITION: middle, in the middle, between, in the midst of.
ORIGIN: From meta; middle (as an adjective or (neuter) noun).
USAGE: among, X before them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way.

BDAG.en: middle, in the middle (spatially or temporally)
BDAG.pt: meio, no meio (espacial ou temporalmente)

DEFINITION: a middle wall, partition wall, barrier.
ORIGIN: From mesos and toichos; a partition (figuratively).

BDAG.en: dividing wall.
BDAG.pt: parede divisória.

DEFINITION: mid-heaven, the middle of heaven, the zenith.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of mesos and ouranos; mid-sky.

BDAG.en: zenith (in midheaven).
BDAG.pt: zênite (em meio ao céu).

DEFINITION: to be in the middle, be advanced midway.
ORIGIN: From mesos; to form the middle, i.e. (in point of time), to be half-way over.

BDAG.en: be in/at the middle.
BDAG.pt: estar no/no meio.

DEFINITION: Messiah, the O.T. title corresponding to Christ.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (mashiyach); the Messias (i.e. Mashiach), or Christ.

BDAG.en: Messiah (Hellenized transliteration of the Hebrew/Aramaic for 'Anointed One').
BDAG.pt: Messias (transliteração helenizada do hebraico/aramaico para 'Ungido').

DEFINITION: full, filled with.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation.

BDAG.en: full (of space or characterized by something, e.g., full of vinegar, full of pretense)
BDAG.pt: cheio (de espaço ou caracterizado por algo, ex.: cheio de vinagre, cheio de hipocrisia)

DEFINITION: to fill.
ORIGIN: From mestos; to replenish, i.e. (by implication) to intoxicate.

BDAG.en: (pf. pass. ptc. μεμεστωμένος) fill with (e.g., full of new wine, speech fulfilled in action)
BDAG.pt: (particípio passado passivo μεμεστωμένος) encher com (ex.: cheio de mosto, discurso cumprido em ação)

DEFINITION: (a) gen: with, in company with, (b) acc: (1) behind, beyond, after, of place, (2) after, of time, with nouns, neut. of adjectives.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition (often used adverbially); properly, denoting accompaniment; "amid" (local or causal); modified variously according to the case (genitive association, or accusative succession) with which it is joined; occupying an intermediate position between apo or ek and eis or pros; less intimate than en and less close than sun).
USAGE: after(-ward), X that he again, against, among, X and, + follow, hence, hereafter, in, of, (up-)on, + our, X and setting, since, (un-)to, + together, when, with (+ -out). Often used in composition, in substantially the same relations of participation or proximity, and transfer or sequence.

BDAG.en: Preposition. Basic idea: ‘in the vicinity of’. A. With genitive: 1. Marker of placement, with, among, in company with someone or something. 2. Marker of association in general sense denoting the company within which something takes place, with someone. B. With accusative: 1. Marker of position: behind something. 2. Marker of time: after another point of time, after. 3. Of concrete objects, which serve as equipment.
BDAG.pt: Preposição. Ideia básica: ‘nas proximidades de’. A. Com genitivo: 1. Marcador de colocação, com, entre, em companhia de alguém ou algo. 2. Marcador de associação em sentido geral, denotando a companhia dentro da qual algo ocorre, com alguém. B. Com acusativo: 1. Marcador de posição: atrás de algo. 2. Marcador de tempo: depois de outro ponto no tempo, após. 3. De objetos concretos, que servem como equipamento.

DEFINITION: to change place (abode), leave, depart, remove, pass over.
ORIGIN: From meta and the base of basis; to change place.

BDAG.en: to transfer from one place to another, go/pass over; change from one state or condition to another state, pass, pass on
BDAG.pt: transferir de um lugar para outro, ir/passar; mudar de um estado ou condição para outro estado, passar, prosseguir

DEFINITION: to change; mid: to change mind.
ORIGIN: From meta and ballo; to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to turn about in opinion.

BDAG.en: pass, pass on, ext. of mng. 1 (to change one’s way of thinking, change)
BDAG.pt: passar, transmitir, extensão do sentido 1 (mudar a maneira de pensar, mudar)

DEFINITION: (usually: transfer, transport, and met: to a better mind), to turn about, change the position of; pass: to be brought back.
ORIGIN: From meta and harmozo; to lead over, i.e. Transfer (direct).

BDAG.en: to direct or bring from one area/direction to another, guide; to cause to undergo a change in state or condition, move, remove
BDAG.pt: dirigir ou trazer de uma área/direção para outra, guiar; causar uma mudança no estado ou condição, mover, remover

DEFINITION: (lit: to offer by way of change, offer so that a change of owner is produced), to share; sometimes merely: to impart, bestow.
ORIGIN: From meta and didomi; to give over, i.e. Share.

BDAG.en: give (a part of), impart, share
BDAG.pt: dar (uma parte de), impartir, compartilhar

DEFINITION: (a) change, transformation, (b) removal.
ORIGIN: From metatithemi; transposition, i.e. Transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law).

BDAG.en: removal to another place; change, transformation
BDAG.pt: remoção para outro lugar; mudança, transformação

DEFINITION: to change position, depart, remove.
ORIGIN: From meta and airo; to betake oneself, i.e. Remove (locally).

BDAG.en: go away w. indication of the place from which
BDAG.pt: ir embora com indicação do lugar de onde se parte

DEFINITION: mid: to summon to myself, send for.
ORIGIN: From meta and kaleo; to call elsewhere, i.e. Summon.

BDAG.en: call to oneself, summon
BDAG.pt: chamar para si, convocar

DEFINITION: trans: to move away, dislodge, remove.
ORIGIN: From meta and kineo; to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. Remove (figuratively).

BDAG.en: shift, remove
BDAG.pt: deslocar, remover

DEFINITION: (a) with gen: to take a share (part) of, share in, partake of, (b) with acc: to take after (later) or take instead.
ORIGIN: From meta and lambano; to participate; genitive case, to accept (and use).
USAGE: eat, have, be partaker, receive, take.

BDAG.en: to share or participate in someth., have a share in; to come into possession of someth., receive
BDAG.pt: compartilhar ou participar de algo, ter uma parte em; vir a possuir algo, receber

DEFINITION: participation, sharing in, receiving.
ORIGIN: From metalambano; participation.

DEFINITION: to change, transform, alter, exchange.
ORIGIN: From meta and allasso; to exchange.

BDAG.en: exchange
BDAG.pt: trocar

DEFINITION: (lit: to change one care or interest for another), to change mind (generally for the better), repent, regret.
ORIGIN: From meta and the middle voice of melo; to care afterwards, i.e. Regret.

BDAG.en: to have regrets about something, be very sorry, regret; to change one’s mind about something, change one’s mind, have second thoughts.
BDAG.pt: ter arrependimentos sobre algo, lamentar profundamente, arrepender-se; mudar de ideia sobre algo, mudar de opinião, ter segundas intenções.

DEFINITION: to transform, transfigure.
ORIGIN: From meta and morphoo; to transform (literally or figuratively, "metamorphose").

BDAG.en: transform, change in form (to change in a manner visible to others, be transfigured); to change inwardly in fundamental character or condition, be changed, be transformed
BDAG.pt: transformar, mudar de forma (mudar de maneira visível para os outros, ser transfigurado); mudar interiormente em caráter ou condição fundamental, ser mudado, ser transformado

DEFINITION: to repent, change mind, change the inner man (particularly with reference to acceptance of the will of God), repent.
ORIGIN: From meta and noieo; to think differently or afterwards, i.e. Reconsider (morally, feel compunction).

BDAG.en: change one’s mind; feel remorse, repent, be converted
BDAG.pt: mudar de ideia; sentir remorso, arrepender-se, ser convertido

DEFINITION: repentance, a change of mind, change in the inner man.
ORIGIN: From metanoeo; (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including reformation); by implication, reversal (of (another's) decision).

BDAG.en: a change of mind; repentance, turning about, conversion; remorse (regret for shortcomings and errors).
BDAG.pt: uma mudança de mente; arrependimento, virada, conversão; remorso (arrependimento por falhas e erros).

DEFINITION: meanwhile, afterwards, between.
ORIGIN: From meta and a form of sun; betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining.

BDAG.en: between, in the middle; in the meanwhile; afterward, next; between (denoting a reciprocal relation or difference).
BDAG.pt: entre, no meio; entretanto, no ínterim; depois, em seguida; entre (denotando uma relação recíproca ou diferença).

DEFINITION: to send after or for.
ORIGIN: From meta and pempo; to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite.

BDAG.en: Send for, summon someone.
BDAG.pt: Mandar buscar, convocar alguém.

DEFINITION: to turn, change, corrupt, pervert.
ORIGIN: From meta and strepho; to turn across, i.e. Transmute or (figuratively) corrupt.

BDAG.en: to cause a change in state or condition, change, alter something into something else, oft. its opposite; change or distort the gospel of Christ.
BDAG.pt: causar uma mudança de estado ou condição, mudar, alterar algo em outra coisa, frequentemente o oposto; mudar ou distorcer o evangelho de Cristo.

DEFINITION: to change the outward appearance (the dress, the form of presentment) of something, transfigure; to adapt.
ORIGIN: From meta and a derivative of schema; to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation).

BDAG.en: to change the form of something, transform, change; to feign to be what one is not, change/disguise oneself; to show a connection or bearing of one thing on another, apply to.
BDAG.pt: mudar a forma de algo, transformar, mudar; fingir ser o que não se é, mudar/disfarçar-se; mostrar uma conexão ou relação de uma coisa com outra, aplicar a.

DEFINITION: (a) to transfer, mid: to go over to another party, desert, (b) to change.
ORIGIN: From meta and tithemi; to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert.
USAGE: carry over, change, remove, translate, turn.

BDAG.en: change (the position of); to convey from one place to another, put in another place, transfer; to effect a change in state or condition, change, alter; to have a change of mind in allegiance, change one’s mind, turn away, desert.
BDAG.pt: mudar (a posição de); transportar de um lugar para outro, colocar em outro lugar, transferir; realizar uma mudança de estado ou condição, mudar, alterar; mudar de opinião em lealdade, mudar de ideia, afastar-se, desertar.

DEFINITION: afterwards.
ORIGIN: From meta and epeita; thereafter.

BDAG.en: afterwards.
BDAG.pt: depois.

DEFINITION: to have a share of, participate in, share, partake of, be a member of.
ORIGIN: From meta and echo; to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink).
USAGE: be partaker, pertain, take part, use.

BDAG.en: to have a part or share in something, share, have a share, participate; to partake of something in common with someone, eat, drink, enjoy, esp. w. foods.
BDAG.pt: ter uma parte ou quinhão em algo, compartilhar, ter uma parte, participar; participar de algo em comum com alguém, comer, beber, desfrutar, especialmente com alimentos.

DEFINITION: to raise on high, to be in suspense.
ORIGIN: From a compound of meta and a collateral form of airo or perhaps rather aer (compare "meteor"); to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively) suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious).

BDAG.en: be lifted up, be elevated; in our lit. only once, pass. and fig. do not be anxious, worried.
BDAG.pt: ser levantado, ser elevado; em nossa literatura apenas uma vez, passivo e figurado: não se inquietem, não se preocupem.

DEFINITION: change of abode, migration, deportation.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of a compound of meta and oikos; a change of abode, i.e. (specially), expatriation.

BDAG.en: removal to another place of habitation, deportation.
BDAG.pt: remoção para outro lugar de habitação, deportação.

DEFINITION: to transport, cause to migrate, remove.
ORIGIN: From the same as metoikesia; to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e colonize or exile.

BDAG.en: remove to another place of habitation, resettle; of forcible deportation.
BDAG.pt: remover para outro lugar de habitação, reassentar; referente a deportação forçada.

DEFINITION: sharing, partnership, fellowship.
ORIGIN: From metecho; participation, i.e. Intercourse.

BDAG.en: sharing, participation.
BDAG.pt: partilha, participação.

DEFINITION: a sharer, partner, associate.

DEFINITION: to measure (out), estimate.

DEFINITION: moderately, greatly, exceedingly.

BDAG.en: moderately, somewhat (litotes: not greatly).
BDAG.pt: moderadamente, um pouco (litotes: não grandemente).

DEFINITION: a measure, whether lineal or cubic; a measuring rod.
ORIGIN: An apparently primary word; a measure ("metre"), literally or figuratively; by implication, a limited portion (degree).

BDAG.pt: aquilo pelo qual algo é medido; um instrumento para medir, medida (de capacidade ou linear); o resultado da medição, quantidade, número (literal ou figurado).

DEFINITION: the forehead, front.
ORIGIN: From meta and ops (the face); the forehead (as opposite the countenance).

BDAG.en: forehead; used figuratively for a mark or sign placed there (e.g., a brand)
BDAG.pt: testa; usada figurativamente para uma marca ou sinal colocado ali (ex: uma marca de escravidão)

DEFINITION: as far as, until, even to.
ORIGIN: Or mechris (mekh-ris'); from mekos; as far as, i.e. Up to a certain point (as a preposition, of extent (denoting the terminus, whereas achri refers especially to the space of time or place intervening) or conjunction).

BDAG.en: until: in our lit. as prep. w. gen. and conj.
BDAG.pt: até: na nossa literatura como preposição com genitivo e conjunção

DEFINITION: not, that...not, lest (used for qualified negation).
ORIGIN: A primary particle of qualified negation (whereas ou expresses an absolute denial); (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas ou expects an affirmative one)) whether.
USAGE: any but (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not, nothing, that not, un(-taken), without. Often used in compounds in substantially the same relations. See also ean me, hina me, ou me, mekos, mekuno, men, me ouk.

BDAG.en: Used to introduce negative clauses, often equivalent to 'not'. It negates participles with a hypothetical sense, or in various constructions expressing purpose (so that not), prohibition (let not, do not), wishes/warnings (may it not be, should not), and in questions expecting a negative answer ('surely not?'). Also used in strengthened negation with οὐ (οὐ μή).
BDAG.pt: Usado para introduzir orações negativas, frequentemente equivalente a 'não'. Nega particípios com sentido hipotético, ou em várias construções expressando finalidade (para que não), proibição (não faça, não), desejos/advertências (que não seja, não deveria), e em perguntas que esperam uma resposta negativa ('certamente não?'). Também usado em negação reforçada com οὐ (οὐ μή).

DEFINITION: before, but, except.
ORIGIN: I.e. ean and me; if not, i.e. Unless.
USAGE: X before, but, except, if, no, (if, + whosoever) not.

BDAG.en: introduces a situation in which given X, Y will follow; as conj., marker of condition, if; used w. subjunctive to denote what is expected to occur; used w. the indicative (exx. in Dssm.); used w. other particles (e.g., ἐὰν καί, ἐὰν μή, ἐάνπερ, ἐάν τε…ἐάν τε); marker of the prospect of an action coordinated with another point of time; marker of the possibility of any number of occurrences of the same event, ever freq. in place of ἄν after relatives
BDAG.pt: introduz uma situação em que dado X, Y se seguirá; como conjunção, marcador de condição, se; usado com o subjuntivo para denotar o que se espera que ocorra; usado com o indicativo; usado com outras partículas (ex: ἐὰν καί, ἐὰν μή, ἐάνπερ, ἐάν τε…ἐάν τε); marcador da perspectiva de uma ação coordenada com outro ponto no tempo; marcador da possibilidade de qualquer número de ocorrências do mesmo evento, frequentemente no lugar de ἄν após pronomes relativos

DEFINITION: albeit not, lest, that.
ORIGIN: I.e. hina and me; in order (or so) that not.

BDAG.en: marker to denote purpose, aim, or goal (in order that, that); marker of objective (that); marker serving as substitute for the inf. of result (so that); marker of retroactive emphasis (that)
BDAG.pt: conjunção final, indicando propósito, objetivo (a fim de que, para que); marcador de objetivo (que); marcador substituto do infinitivo de resultado (de modo que); marcador de ênfase retroativa (que)

DEFINITION: anymore, at all, neither, never.
ORIGIN: I.e. ou and me; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all.
USAGE: any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise). Compare me ouk.

BDAG.en: objective negative adverb, denying the reality of an alleged fact; used typically with the indicative mood; functions as a negative response ('no'); marks negative propositions, negating single words or clauses ('not'); frequently used in litotes (understatement by double negative, e.g., 'not a few'); can serve as a periphrasis for certain verb concepts (e.g., οὐκ ἀγνοεῖν = 'to know quite well'); used in combination with other negatives to strengthen negation; used in questions expecting an affirmative answer ('not so?').
BDAG.pt: advérbio negativo objetivo, negando a realidade de um fato alegado; usado tipicamente com o modo indicativo; funciona como uma resposta negativa ('não'); marca proposições negativas, negando palavras ou cláusulas isoladas ('não'); frequentemente usado em litotes (eufemismo por dupla negação, ex: 'não poucos'); pode servir como perífrase para certos conceitos verbais (ex: οὐκ ἀγνοεῖν = 'saber muito bem'); usado em combinação com outras negativas para intensificar a negação; usado em perguntas esperando uma resposta afirmativa ('não é assim?').

DEFINITION: by no means, not at all.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a compound of me and amos (somebody); by no means.

BDAG.en: By no means, certainly not (adverb expressing a negative reaction).
BDAG.pt: De modo algum, certamente não (advérbio expressando uma reação negativa).

DEFINITION: and not, not even, neither…nor.
ORIGIN: From me and de; but not, not even; in a continued negation, nor.
USAGE: neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as).

BDAG.en: Negative disjunctive particle: and not, but not, nor; continuing a preceding negation (usually with μή). Can link two verbs sharing a negative, or link two clauses/verbs where each takes its own negation. Also functions as 'not even' in the apodosis of conditional sentences.
BDAG.pt: Partícula disjuntiva negativa: e não, mas não, nem; continuando uma negação anterior (geralmente com μή). Pode ligar dois verbos compartilhando uma negação, ou ligar duas orações/verbos onde cada um tem sua própria negação. Também funciona como 'nem mesmo' na apódose de frases condicionais.

DEFINITION: no one, none, nothing.
ORIGIN: Including the irregular feminine medemia may-dem-ee'-ah, and the neuter meden (may-den') from me and heis; not even one (man, woman, thing).
USAGE: any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay.

BDAG.en: as adj., pertaining to there not being any, no; as subst., a negative reference to an entity, event, or condition: nobody, nothing.
BDAG.pt: Como adjetivo, referente à inexistência de algo/alguém, nenhum; como substantivo, referência negativa a uma entidade, evento ou condição: ninguém, nada.

DEFINITION: not at any time, never.

DEFINITION: not yet.

BDAG.en: no longer, not from now on.

BDAG.pt: 1 mês; 2 lua nova (festa).

BDAG.pt: oferecer informação, informar, dar a conhecer, revelar; reportar; dar informação às autoridades

Also used in strengthened negation with οὐ (οὐ μή).
BDAG.pt: Usado para introduzir orações negativas, frequentemente equivalente a 'não'. Nega particípios com sentido hipotético, ou em várias construções expressando finalidade (para que não), proibição (não faça, não), desejos/advertências (que não seja, não deveria), e em perguntas que esperam uma resposta negativa ('certamente não?'). Também usado em negação reforçada com οὐ (οὐ μή).

BDAG.pt: 1 marcador de ponto de tempo negado indefinido, nunca; 2 marcador de propósito negado, que ... não, para que não.

DEFINITION: lest anywhere, lest perhaps.

BDAG.pt: um marcador que convida a uma resposta negativa à pergunta que introduz (um pouco mais enfático que o simples μή); talvez

DEFINITION: let alone, much less, much more.

DEFINITION: any.

BDAG.pt: causar que algo se torne ritualmente impuro, manchar, contaminar; causar que a pureza de algo seja violada por comportamento imoral, macular

DEFINITION: a mixture.

BDAG.pt: mistura, composto (de um unguento)

DEFINITION: to mix, mingle.

BDAG.pt: tamanho, medida ou quantidade relativamente limitada, pequeno, baixo (a de estatura); o pequeno, a criança (subst.)

DEFINITION: a Roman mile, measuring 1478.5 meters or 5820.9 feet.

DEFINITION: to imitate, follow.

DEFINITION: an imitator, follower.
ORIGIN: From mimeomai; an imitator.

DEFINITION: to remember, call to mind, recall, mention.

BDAG.pt: relembrar-se de informação da memória, lembrar, recordar, fazer-se lembrar; pensar e chamar a atenção para algo ou alguém, fazer menção de alguém; considerar cuidadosamente, lembrar, pensar, cuidar, ter em mente

DEFINITION: to hate, detest, love less, esteem less.

DEFINITION: (lit: repayment of price or payment of price due), reward, due punishment.

BDAG.pt: recompensa, seja favorável ou desfavorável, literalmente ‘pagamento de salários’ (a sentido favorável: recompensa; b sentido desfavorável: punição, retribuição)

DEFINITION: one who pays wages.

BDAG.pt: o sentido usual em ato de 'preço do contrato, aluguel' não é encontrado em nossa literatura, e o sentido de 'o que é alugado, uma casa alugada' é um significado não encontrado fora dela

DEFINITION: a hired servant, hireling.
ORIGIN: From misthoo; a wage-worker (good or bad).

BDAG.pt: homem contratado, de pescadores contratados

DEFINITION: Mitylene, the capital of the island of Lesbos in the northern Aegean sea.

ORIGIN: Including the comparative neoteros neh-o'-ter-os; a primary word; "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate.

BDAG.en: pert. to being in existence but a relatively short time, new, fresh; fig., of Christ (ever born anew in hearts); pert. to being superior in quality or state to what went before, new (e.g., new person, new covenant); pert. to being in the early stages of life, young; a person beginning to experience something, novice.
BDAG.pt: relativo a existir por um tempo relativamente curto, novo, fresco; fig., de Cristo (sempre renascendo nos corações); relativo a ser superior em qualidade ou estado ao que veio antes, novo (ex.: nova pessoa, nova aliança); relativo a estar nos estágios iniciais da vida, jovem; uma pessoa que começa a experimentar algo, noviço.

DEFINITION: a young bird, nestling; a young one.
ORIGIN: From neos; a youngling (nestling).

DEFINITION: youth, youthfulness.
ORIGIN: From neos; newness, i.e. Youthfulness.

BDAG.en: state of youthfulness, youth.
BDAG.pt: estado de jovialidade, juventude.

DEFINITION: (lit: newly-planted), newly converted to Christianity, recent convert.
ORIGIN: From neos and a derivative of phuo; newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte").

BDAG.en: newly planted in the Christian community, newly converted ('neophyte')
BDAG.pt: recentemente plantado na comunidade cristã, recém-convertido ('neófito')

DEFINITION: Nero.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor.

BDAG.pt: Nero, imperador romano (54–68 d.C.)

DEFINITION: to nod or beckon (as a sign).

DEFINITION: a cloud.
ORIGIN: From nephos; properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud.

BDAG.en: cloud; clouds bringing rain; dark clouds (as a comparison for a swarm); bright cloud (as a sign of God’s presence); clothed in a cloud; vehicle of Christ at his second coming; be under the cloud
BDAG.pt: nuvem; nuvens trazendo chuva; nuvens escuras (como comparação para um enxame); nuvem brilhante (como sinal da presença de Deus); vestido em uma nuvem; veículo de Cristo em sua segunda vinda; estar debaixo da nuvem

DEFINITION: Naphtali, son of Jacob, founder of a tribe which occupied territory.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Naphtaliy); Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine.

DEFINITION: a cloud; met: a dense crowd, a multitude, great company.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a cloud.

BDAG.en: cloud (as a symbol of darkness); fig. of a compact, numberless throng (host of witnesses)
BDAG.pt: nuvem (como símbolo de escuridão); fig. de uma multidão compacta e incontável (multidão de testemunhas)

DEFINITION: a kidney (as a general emotional center), the reins.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind.

BDAG.en: usu. pl. ‘kidneys’; by fig. ext. ... of the inner life mind ... who searches minds and hearts
BDAG.pt: usualmente no plural: 'rins'; por extensão figurada ... da vida interior, mente ... que investiga mentes e corações

DEFINITION: (lit: temple-sweeper), temple-warden; an honorary title.
ORIGIN: From a form of naos and koreo (to sweep); a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary.

BDAG.en: temple keeper; honorary temple keeper (title assumed by cities that built and maintained temples in honor of the emperor)
BDAG.pt: zelador do templo; zelador honorário do templo (título assumido por cidades que construíram e mantiveram templos em honra do imperador)

DEFINITION: associated with youth, youthful, juvenile.
ORIGIN: From the comparative of neos; appertaining to younger persons, i.e. Juvenile.

BDAG.en: youthful
BDAG.pt: juvenil, da juventude

DEFINITION: of affirmative swearing: by, with acc. of person or thing sworn by.
ORIGIN: Probably an intensive form of nai; a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as.

BDAG.en: marker pointing to the basis on which someth. is strongly affirmed, yes indeed, by w. acc. of pers. or thing by which one swears, affirms, or invokes sanction
BDAG.pt: marcador que aponta para a base sobre a qual algo é fortemente afirmado, sim de fato, acompanhado do acusativo da pessoa ou coisa pela qual se jura, afirma ou invoca sanção

DEFINITION: to spin.
ORIGIN: From neo (of like meaning); to spin.

BDAG.en: spin
BDAG.pt: fiar

DEFINITION: to be childlike, childish, infantile.
ORIGIN: From nepios; to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently.

BDAG.en: be (as) a child, fig. (in evil)
BDAG.pt: ser (como) uma criança, fig. (no mal)

DEFINITION: unlearned, unenlightened; noun: an infant, child.
ORIGIN: From an obsolete particle ne- (implying negation) and epos; not speaking, i.e. An infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian.

BDAG.en: a very young child, infant, child (lit.); fig.; one who is not yet of legal age, minor
BDAG.pt: uma criança muito nova, infante, criança (lit.); fig.; aquele que ainda não atingiu a maioridade legal, menor

DEFINITION: Nereus, a Christian in Rome.
ORIGIN: Apparently from a derivative of the base of naus (meaning wet); Nereus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Nereus (mythological name)
BDAG.pt: Nereu (nome mitológico)

DEFINITION: Neri, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Neriyah); Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Neri, in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Neri, na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: a little island, an islet.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of nesos; an islet.

BDAG.en: little island (diminutive of νῆσος)
BDAG.pt: pequena ilha (diminutivo de νῆσος)

DEFINITION: an island.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of naus; an island.

BDAG.en: island (Cyprus, Malta, Patmos)
BDAG.pt: ilha (Chipre, Malta, Patmos)

DEFINITION: fasting, the day of atonement.
ORIGIN: From nesteuo; abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement.

BDAG.en: 'fasting'. 1 the experience of being without sufficient food, going hungry gener.; 2 the act of going without food for a devotional or cultic purpose, fast
BDAG.pt: 'jejum'. 1 a experiência de estar sem comida suficiente, passar fome em geral; 2 o ato de abster-se de comida para um propósito devocional ou cultual, jejum

DEFINITION: to fast, abstain from food.
ORIGIN: From nestis; to abstain from food (religiously).

BDAG.en: to fast as a devotional rite, among Jews and Christians: as a sign of grief, Moses and Jesus fast for forty days and forty nights, with lamentation, as preparation for prayer, for baptism, with praying, to increase the power of his prayer, Jesus and his disciples do not fast, observe a fast, fast to God, fast for those who persecute you, pious Israelites used to fast twice a week, Christians on Wednesday and Friday, abstain from the world (figuratively)

DEFINITION: fasting, not eating.

BDAG.pt: não comendo, faminto

DEFINITION: sober, not intoxicated (with wine), temperate, vigilant.

DEFINITION: (lit: to be sober), to be calm (vigilant), circumspect.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity: to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet.

BDAG.en: prim. ‘be sober’; in the NT only fig. = be free fr. every form of mental and spiritual ‘drunkenness’, fr. excess, passion, rashness, confusion, etc. be well-balanced, self-controlled, be self-possessed under all circumstances, with praying, exercise self-restraint, to help you pray, exercise self-control for (your own) good, allusion to the self-control practiced by athletes
BDAG.pt: principalmente ‘ser sóbrio’; no NT apenas figurativamente = estar livre de toda forma de ‘embriaguez’ mental e espiritual, de excesso, paixão, imprudência, confusão, etc. ser equilibrado, autocontrolado, estar de posse de si em todas as circunstâncias, com oração, exercer autocontrole, para ajudar a orar, exercer autocontrole para (o seu próprio) bem, alusão ao autocontrole praticado por atletas

DEFINITION: Niger, a proper name.

BDAG.en: Niger (surname of Simeon the prophet)
BDAG.pt: Niger (sobrenome de Simeão, o profeta)

DEFINITION: Nicanor, a proper name.
ORIGIN: Probably from nikao; victorious; Nicanor, a Christian.

BDAG.pt: Nicandor, um dos sete assistentes da congregação de Jerusalém

DEFINITION: to conquer, be victorious, overcome, prevail, subdue.

USAGE: conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory.

BDAG.en: to win in the face of obstacles, be victor, conquer, overcome, prevail, intr. in a battle or contest, in a legal action; to overcome someone, vanquish, overcome, trans. act. w. the obj. in the acc., Christ has overcome the world, also said of Christians, overcome the evil one, the devil, win a victory over the soul, overcome evil with good; pass. be conquered, beaten, let oneself be overcome; to surpass in ability, outstrip, excel

DEFINITION: victory, a victorious principle.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success.

BDAG.pt: vitória, depois como abstrato para concreto o meio para ganhar uma vitória

DEFINITION: Nicodemus, a member of the Sanhedrin.
ORIGIN: From nikos and demos; victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Nicodemus, a member of the Sanhedrin who was favorable to Jesus and his cause
BDAG.pt: Nicodemos, membro do Sinédrio que era favorável a Jesus e à sua causa

DEFINITION: a Nicolaitan, possibly a follower of Nicolaus (a heretic at Ephesus).
ORIGIN: From Nikolaos; a Nicolaite, i.e. Adherent of Nicolaus.

BDAG.pt: Nicolaita, um seguidor de Nicolau, um fundador de seita de outra forma desconhecido

DEFINITION: Nicolaus, a Christian, probably not connected with the sect bearing the same name.
ORIGIN: From nikos and Laodikeus; victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic.

BDAG.en: Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch and one of the seven assistants of the Jerusalem church
BDAG.pt: Nicolau, um prosélito de Antioquia e um dos sete assistentes da igreja de Jerusalém

BDAG.pt: Nicópolis; a mencionada em Tito 3:12 e na subscrição de 1 Tm e Tg é geralmente considerada a N. em Epiro

DEFINITION: victory.
ORIGIN: From nike; a conquest (concretely), i.e. (by implication) triumph.

BDAG.en: late form for νίκη. victory; the prize of victory
BDAG.pt: forma tardia para vitória. vitória; o prêmio da vitória

DEFINITION: Nineveh, a city on the Tigris in Assyria.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Niynveh); Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria.

DEFINITION: a Ninevite, an inhabitant of Nineveh, a city on the Tigris in Assyria.
ORIGIN: From Nineui; a Ninevite, i.e. Inhabitant of Nineveh.

BDAG.en: Ninevite pl., people of Nineveh as examples of penitence, contrasted w. the contemporaries of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Ninuítas pl., povo de Nínive como exemplos de penitência, contrastado com os contemporâneos de Jesus

DEFINITION: a basin for washing hands or feet.
ORIGIN: From nipto; a ewer.

BDAG.en: foot-washing basin (implied by the root)

BDAG.en: to cleanse with use of water, wash; to provide generous service, wash feet
BDAG.pt: limpar com o uso de água, lavar; prestar um serviço generoso, lavar os pés

DEFINITION: to understand, think, consider, conceive, apprehend; aor. possibly: realize.
ORIGIN: From nous; to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed.

ORIGIN: From noieo; a perception, i.e. Purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself.

BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter nascido fora do casamento ou de origem servil e, portanto, sem status ou direitos legais, ilegítimo, bastardo

DEFINITION: (a) adj: connected with law, about law, (b) noun: a lawyer, one learned in the Law, one learned in the Old Testament.

BDAG.pt: pertencente a assuntos relacionados à lei, sobre a lei; pertencente ao estar bem informado sobre a lei, versado na lei, daí, substantivo, perito legal, jurista, advogado

DEFINITION: lawfully, rightfully.

DEFINITION: a custom, current coin.

BDAG.pt: dinheiro oficialmente introduzido no uso comum, moeda

DEFINITION: a teacher and interpreter of the Mosaic Law.
ORIGIN: From nomos and didaskalos; an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. A Rabbi.

BDAG.pt: instrutor da lei (para aqueles) que se desviam do ensino correto

DEFINITION: legislation, lawgiving.

BDAG.pt: literalmente ‘legislação’; depois também seu resultado, legislação, coletânea de leis

DEFINITION: (a) to ordain, lay down, give the sanction of law to, enact, (b) to base legally, regulate, direct.

BDAG.en: to function as a lawgiver, legislate; to enact on the basis of legal sanction, ordain, found by law
BDAG.pt: funcionar como legislador, legislar; promulgar com base em sanção legal, ordenar, fundar por lei

DEFINITION: a law-giver, legislator.
ORIGIN: From nomos and a derivative of tithemi; a legislator.

BDAG.en: lawgiver
BDAG.pt: legislador

DEFINITION: usage, custom, law; in NT: of law in general, plur: of divine laws; of a force or influence impelling to action; of the Mosaic law; meton: of the books which contain the law, the Pentateuch, the Old Testament scriptures in general.

DEFINITION: to be diseased, hence of mental or spiritual disease.

BDAG.pt: estar doente, indisposto (apenas figurativamente em nossa literatura); estar aflito com, ter um desejo mórbido por algo

DEFINITION: a trouble, disease, sickness.
ORIGIN: From noseo; an ailment.

BDAG.en: disease.
BDAG.pt: doença.

DEFINITION: a disease, malady, sickness.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability).

BDAG.pt: mal físico, doença, enfermidade; figurativamente (extensão do 1): vício, doença moral.

DEFINITION: a brood of young birds.
ORIGIN: From neossos; a brood (of chickens).

BDAG.en: nest; brood.
BDAG.pt: ninho; ninhada.

DEFINITION: a nestling, the young of birds.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of neossos; a birdling.

BDAG.en: the young of a bird
BDAG.pt: o filhote de um pássaro

DEFINITION: to rob; mid: to set apart for myself, appropriate for own benefit, purloin.

BDAG.pt: reservar para si, reter, de envolvimento em um tipo de operação de desvio (apropriação indevida)

DEFINITION: the south wind, the southern quarter.

BDAG.pt: um vento soprando de uma direção sul, vento sul, vento sudoeste; direção à direita ao se encarar o leste, sul (da direção em geral); de uma área ou país do sul

DEFINITION: a warning, admonition, counsel.

BDAG.en: counsel about avoidance or cessation of an improper course of conduct, admonition, instruction, warning, reproof.
BDAG.pt: aconselhamento sobre a evitação ou cessação de uma conduta imprópria, admoestação, instrução, advertência, repreensão.

DEFINITION: to admonish, warn, counsel, exhort.
ORIGIN: From the same as nouthesia; to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently.

BDAG.pt: aconselhar sobre a evitação ou cessação de uma conduta imprópria, admoestar, advertir, instruir.

DEFINITION: the new moon, first of the month.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a compound of neos and men (as noun by implication, of hemera); the festival of new moon.

BDAG.en: new moon (read by Tdf. Col 2:16; cf. νεομηνία)
BDAG.pt: lua nova (lido por Tdf. Col 2:16; cf. νεομηνία)

DEFINITION: wisely, discreetly, reasonably, sensibly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of nous and echo; in a mind-having way, i.e. Prudently.

BDAG.en: wisely, thoughtfully (of answering)
BDAG.pt: sabiamente, com reflexão (ao responder)

DEFINITION: the mind, the reason, the reasoning faculty, intellect.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of ginosko; the intellect, i.e. Mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning.

DEFINITION: Nympha, a Christian of Laodicea.

BDAG.en: Nymphas (a proper name, variant reading)
BDAG.pt: Nymphas (um nome próprio, leitura variante)

DEFINITION: (a) a bride, young wife, young woman, (b) a daughter-in-law.

DEFINITION: the bridechamber.
