BDAG.en: wedding hall; bridal chamber; bridegroom’s attendants
BDAG.pt: salão de casamento; câmara nupcial; assistentes do noivo

DEFINITION: adv. (a) of time: just now, even now; just at hand, immediately, (b) of logical connection: now then, (c) in commands and appeals: at this instant.
ORIGIN: A primary particle of present time; "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate.
USAGE: henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time). See also tanun, nuni.

BDAG.en: now (temporal marker with focus on the moment as such, at the present time, designating both a point of time as well as its extent, or as an adjective: the present, or substantively: the present time)
BDAG.pt: agora (marcador temporal com foco no momento em si, no tempo presente, designando tanto um ponto no tempo quanto sua extensão, ou como adjetivo: o presente, ou substantivamente: o tempo presente)

DEFINITION: but now.
ORIGIN: Or ta nun (tah noon) from neuter plural of ho and nun; the things now, i.e. (adverbially) at present.

DEFINITION: adv. (a) of time: just now, even now; just at hand, immediately, (b) of logical connection: now then, (c) in commands and appeals: at this instant.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of nun for emphasis; just now.

BDAG.en: now (emphatic form of νῦν, without change of meaning, often denoting the prevailing situation)
BDAG.pt: agora mesmo (forma enfática de νῦν, sem alteração de significado, muitas vezes denotando a situação prevalecente)

DEFINITION: the night, night-time.
ORIGIN: A primary word; "night" (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: night (period between sunset and sunrise; night as a condition, figuratively extended; time for rest from work)
BDAG.pt: noite (período entre o pôr do sol e o nascer do sol; noite como condição, extensão figurada; tempo de descanso do trabalho)

DEFINITION: to prick, pierce.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; to prick ("nudge").

BDAG.en: prick (to penetrate with a pointed instrument, ordinarily not a violent or deep piercing, prick, stab; to touch gently, nudge, poke to waken someone)
BDAG.pt: espetar/ferir (penetrar com um instrumento pontiagudo, geralmente não uma perfuração violenta ou profunda, picar, golpear; tocar gentilmente, cutucar, empurrar para acordar alguém)

DEFINITION: to nod in sleep, be drowsy, slumber.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of neuo; to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay.

BDAG.en: to be almost asleep, nod, become drowsy, doze; fig. be drowsy, idle (of retribution personified, destruction is not dozing)
BDAG.pt: estar quase a dormir, acenar com a cabeça, ficar sonolento, cochilar; fig. ser sonolento, indolente (referindo-se à retribuição personificada, a destruição não está a cochilar)

DEFINITION: a night and day, twenty-four hours.
ORIGIN: From nux and hemera; a day-and-night, i.e. Full day of twenty-four hours.

BDAG.en: a day and a night = 24 hours
BDAG.pt: um dia e uma noite = 24 horas

DEFINITION: Noah, a patriarch.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Noach); Noe, (i.e. Noach), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Noah (biblical figure)
BDAG.pt: Noé (figura bíblica)

DEFINITION: blunt, dull, hence spiritually; sluggish, remiss, slack.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of nothos; sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid.

BDAG.en: lazy, sluggish; sluggish in hearing = hard of hearing
BDAG.pt: preguiçoso, lento; lento para ouvir = de audição difícil

DEFINITION: the back (of men or animals).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; the back.

BDAG.en: back part of the body from the neck to the pelvis, back
BDAG.pt: parte traseira do corpo do pescoço à pélvis, costas

DEFINITION: hospitality, a lodging place.
ORIGIN: From xenos; hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment.

BDAG.en: hospitality, entertainment shown a guest; less frequently the place where the guest is lodged, guest room
BDAG.pt: hospitalidade, entretenimento oferecido a um hóspede; menos frequentemente o lugar onde o hóspede é alojado, quarto de hóspedes

DEFINITION: (a) to entertain a stranger, (b) to startle, bewilder.
ORIGIN: From xenos; to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be (make, appear) strange.

BDAG.en: to show hospitality, receive as a guest, entertain; to cause a strong psychological reaction through introduction of something new or strange, astonish, surprise; Pass. be surprised, wonder
BDAG.pt: mostrar hospitalidade, receber como hóspede, entreter; causar uma forte reação psicológica pela introdução de algo novo ou estranho, espantar, surpreender; Pass. ficar surpreso, maravilhar-se

DEFINITION: to entertain strangers, practice hospitality.
ORIGIN: From a compound of xenos and dechomai; to be hospitable.

BDAG.en: show hospitality
BDAG.pt: demonstrar hospitalidade

DEFINITION: alien, new, novel; noun: a guest, stranger, foreigner.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively, novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer.

BDAG.en: 1 adj. pertaining to being unfamiliar because of something being unknown, strange (a foreign/strange; b unheard of, surprising); 2 as subst. an entity involved in experience of unfamiliarity (a one who comes as a stranger; b a foreign country; c the host)
BDAG.pt: 1 adj. referente a algo desconhecido, estranho (a estrangeiro/estranho; b inaudito, surpreendente); 2 como substantivo, algo envolvido na experiência de unfamiliaridade (a um que vem como estranho; b um país estrangeiro; c o anfitrião)

DEFINITION: a sextarius (about a pint), a pitcher (of wood or stone).
ORIGIN: As if from xeo (properly, to smooth; by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. About a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher).

BDAG.en: a measure, about equal to 1/2 liter; but then it comes to mean simply pitcher, jug, without reference to the amount contained
BDAG.pt: uma medida, cerca de 1/2 litro; mas depois passou a significar simplesmente jarra, cântaro, sem referência à quantidade contida

DEFINITION: to dry up, parch, be ripened, wither, waste away.
ORIGIN: From xeros; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature.
USAGE: dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away).

BDAG.en: 1 to stop a flow... and so cause dryness, to dry, dry up (act. dry, dry out; pass. become dry, dry up, wither); 2 to become dry to the point of being immobilized, be paralyzed; 3 to become dry and therefore be ready for harvesting, be ripe
BDAG.pt: 1 interromper um fluxo... e assim causar secura, secar (ativo: secar; passivo: tornar-se seco, secar, murchar); 2 secar a ponto de ficar imobilizado, ser paralisado; 3 secar e, portanto, estar pronto para a colheita, estar maduro

DEFINITION: dry, withered; noun: dry land.
ORIGIN: From the base of xestes (through the idea of scorching); arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water).

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to total loss of moisture, dry, dried up (of wood, trees, plants, seeds, land); 2 pert. to being shrunken or withered and therefore immobile because of disease, withered, shrunken, paralyzed
BDAG.pt: 1 referente à perda total de umidade, seco, ressequido (de madeira, árvores, plantas, sementes, terra); 2 referente a estar encolhido ou murcho e, portanto, imóvel devido a doença, murcho, atrofiado, paralisado

DEFINITION: wooden.
ORIGIN: From xulon; wooden.

BDAG.en: Wooden (wooden cult images/idols; wooden vessels or equipment).
BDAG.pt: De madeira (imagens/ídolos de culto de madeira; utensílios ou equipamentos de madeira).

DEFINITION: anything made of wood, a piece of wood, a club, staff; the trunk of a tree, used to support the cross-bar of a cross in crucifixion.
ORIGIN: From another form of the base of xestes; timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance.

BDAG.en: 1 wood as a plant substance in unmanufactured form, wood; Pl. wood as building material; As fuel; 2 object made of wood (a pole; b club, cudgel; c a device for confining the extremities of a prisoner, stocks; c a wooden structure used for crucifixion, cross)
BDAG.pt: 1 madeira como substância vegetal em forma não manufaturada, lenha; Pl. madeira como material de construção; Como combustível; 2 objeto feito de madeira (a poste; b clava, porrete; c dispositivo para confinar as extremidades de um prisioneiro, cepo; c estrutura de madeira usada para crucificação, cruz)

DEFINITION: to shave, shear, cut off the hair.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the same as xulon (meaning a razor); to shave or "shear" the hair.

BDAG.en: To shave (mid.: have oneself shaved).
BDAG.pt: Rapar, barbear (médio: fazer-se rapar).

DEFINITION: the, the definite article.
ORIGIN: Including the feminine he (hay), and the neuter to (to) in all their inflections; the definite article; the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom).
USAGE: the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc.

BDAG.en: The (definite article, masculine singular nominative form, used here to describe its grammatical functions, especially with names of countries, rivers, seas, personal pronouns, possessive adjectives, adjectives, demonstrative pronouns, and in forming vocatives and substantive adjectives.)
BDAG.pt: O (Artigo definido, masculino singular nominativo, usado aqui para descrever suas funções gramaticais, especialmente com nomes de países, rios, mares, pronomes pessoais, adjetivos possessivos, adjetivos, pronomes demonstrativos e na formação de vocativos e adjetivos substantivados.)

DEFINITION: eighty.
ORIGIN: From ogdoos; ten times eight.

BDAG.en: Eighty.
BDAG.pt: Oitenta.

DEFINITION: the eighth, one of eight, with seven others.
ORIGIN: From oktos; the eighth.

BDAG.en: Eighth.
BDAG.pt: Oitavo.

DEFINITION: (properly: bulk, mass, hence) a weight, burden, encumbrance.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as agkale; a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. Burden (hindrance).

BDAG.en: 1. Material that is ponderously large, bulk. 2. That which hinders one from doing something, weight, burden, impediment (figurative extension of 1).
BDAG.pt: 1. Material pesadamente grande, volume. 2. Aquilo que impede alguém de fazer algo, peso, fardo, impedimento (extensão figurada de 1).

DEFINITION: this (referring to what is present).
ORIGIN: Including the feminine hede (hay'-deh), and the neuter tode (tod'-e) from ho and de; the same, i.e. This or that one (plural these or those); often used as a personal pronoun.

BDAG.en: Demonstrative pronoun referring to an entity viewed as present or near (often what follows, especially in the formula 'this is what... says'); can also refer to what precedes, or an unspecified entity ('such and such'); the neuter form stands before whole sentences/clauses or indirect questions.
BDAG.pt: Pronome demonstrativo referindo-se a uma entidade vista como presente ou próxima (frequentemente o que se segue, especialmente na fórmula 'isto é o que... diz'); pode também referir-se ao que precede, ou a uma entidade não especificada ('tal e tal'); a forma neutra antecede frases/orações inteiras ou perguntas indiretas.

DEFINITION: to journey, travel.
ORIGIN: From hodos; to travel.

BDAG.en: go, travel, make a trip (implying use of an established route)
BDAG.pt: ir, viajar, fazer uma viagem (com a implicação de usar uma rota estabelecida)

DEFINITION: to lead, guide; met: to instruct, teach.
ORIGIN: From hodegos; to show the way (literally or figuratively (teach)).

BDAG.en: 1. To assist in reaching a desired destination, lead, guide, literally. 2. To assist someone in acquiring information or knowledge, lead, guide, conduct, figuratively.
BDAG.pt: 1. Ajudar a alcançar um destino desejado, conduzir, guiar, literalmente. 2. Ajudar alguém a adquirir informação ou conhecimento, conduzir, guiar, condizer, figurativamente.

DEFINITION: a leader, guide; met: an instructor, teacher.
ORIGIN: From hodos and hegeomai; a conductor (literally or figuratively (teacher)).

BDAG.en: 1. One who leads the way in reaching a desired destination, guide, leader. 2. One who assists another in following a path, guide, leader, in imagery.
BDAG.pt: 1. Aquele que lidera o caminho para alcançar um destino desejado, guia, líder. 2. Aquele que auxilia outro a seguir um caminho, guia, líder, em sentido figurado.

DEFINITION: to travel, pursue a way, journey.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hodos and poreuomai; to be a wayfarer, i.e. Travel.

BDAG.en: travel, be on the way
BDAG.pt: viajar, estar no caminho

DEFINITION: a journey, journeying, travel.
ORIGIN: From the same as hodoiporeo; travel.

BDAG.en: walking, journey
BDAG.pt: caminhada, jornada

DEFINITION: a way, road, journey, path.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a road; by implication, a progress (the route, act or distance); figuratively, a mode or means.

BDAG.en: an established ‘way’ or ‘course’ such as a road or channel of a river; a way for traveling or moving from one place to another, way, road, highway; the action of traveling, way, trip, journey; course of behavior, way, way of life, fig. ext. of 1 and 2; the way, teaching in the most comprehensive sense, specif. of teaching and manner of life relating to Jesus Christ
BDAG.pt: um 'caminho' ou 'curso' estabelecido, como uma estrada ou canal de rio; um meio para viajar ou mover-se de um lugar para outro, caminho, estrada, via principal; a ação de viajar, caminho, viagem, jornada; curso de comportamento, modo, modo de vida, extensão figurada de 1 e 2; o caminho, o ensino no sentido mais abrangente, especificamente do ensino e modo de vida relacionados a Jesus Cristo

DEFINITION: a tooth.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the base of esthio; a "tooth".

BDAG.en: tooth
BDAG.pt: dente

DEFINITION: to torment, pain; mid. and pass: to be tormented, pained; to suffer acute pain, physical or mental.
ORIGIN: From odune; to grieve.

BDAG.en: to undergo physical torment, suffer pain; to experience mental and spiritual pain, be pained/distressed
BDAG.pt: sofrer tormento físico, sentir dor; experimentar dor mental e espiritual, estar aflito/angustiado

DEFINITION: pain, sorrow, distress, of body or mind.
ORIGIN: From duno; grief (as dejecting).

BDAG.en: physical suffering or misery, pain, woe; mental pain, distress
BDAG.pt: sofrimento ou miséria física, dor, aflição; dor mental, angústia

DEFINITION: lamentation, wailing, mourning, sorrow.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the base of duno; moaning, i.e. Lamentation.

BDAG.en: lamentation, mourning
BDAG.pt: lamentação, pranto

DEFINITION: called, that is to say.
ORIGIN: From the neuter of hos and the third person singular present indicative of eimi; which is.
USAGE: called, which is (make), that is (to say).

BDAG.en: The (definite article, masculine singular nominative form, used here to describe its grammatical functions, especially with names of countries, rivers, seas, personal pronouns, possessive adjectives, adjectives, demonstrative pronouns, and in forming vocatives and substantive adjectives.)
BDAG.pt: O (Artigo definido, masculino singular nominativo, usado aqui para descrever suas funções gramaticais, especialmente com nomes de países, rios, mares, pronomes pessoais, adjetivos possessivos, adjetivos, pronomes demonstrativos e na formação de vocativos e adjetivos substantivados.)

DEFINITION: Uzziah, son of Joram and father of Jotham, and king of Judah from about 785 to 746 B.C., an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Uzziyah); Ozias (i.e. Uzzijah), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Uzziah, Hebrew king
BDAG.pt: Uzias, rei hebreu

DEFINITION: to stink, be offensive.
ORIGIN: A primary verb (in a strengthened form).

BDAG.en: emit an odor, pleasant or unpleasant, to smell
BDAG.pt: emitir um odor, agradável ou desagradável, para cheirar

DEFINITION: (a) whence, from which place, (b) wherefore.
ORIGIN: From hos with the directive enclitic of source; from which place or source or cause (adverb or conjunction).

BDAG.en: from where, whence, from which (place or circumstance); for which reason, hence
BDAG.pt: de onde, donde, a partir de onde (lugar ou circunstância); por essa razão, portanto

DEFINITION: a linen cloth, a sheet, sail.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a sail.

BDAG.en: linen cloth, sheet, esp. of a sail (ὀθ. πλοίου a ship’s sail)
BDAG.pt: pano de linho, lençol, especialmente de uma vela (ὀθ. πλοίου, vela de um navio)

DEFINITION: a linen bandage, a wrapping.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of othone; a linen bandage.

BDAG.en: (linen) cloth, cloth wrapping
BDAG.pt: pano (de linho), envoltório de pano

DEFINITION: of one's family, domestic, intimate.
ORIGIN: From oikos; domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent.

BDAG.en: persons who are related by kinship or circumstances and form a closely knit group, members of a household (members of God’s household, those who belong to the household of faith)
BDAG.pt: pessoas relacionadas por parentesco ou circunstâncias e que formam um grupo coeso, membros de uma casa/família (membros da casa de Deus, aqueles que pertencem à casa da fé)

DEFINITION: a household (of servants).
ORIGIN: From oikeo; a fellow resident, i.e. Menial domestic.

BDAG.en: member of the household, then specifically house slave, domestic, and slave generally
BDAG.pt: membro da casa, e especificamente escravo doméstico, doméstico e escravo em geral

DEFINITION: to inhabit, dwell, indwell.
ORIGIN: From oikos; to occupy a house, i.e. Reside (figuratively, inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit.

BDAG.en: to reside in a place, live, dwell; to inhabit a place, dwell in (also transcendentally of God dwelling in unapproachable light)
BDAG.pt: residir em um lugar, viver, morar; habitar um lugar, morar (também de forma transcendente, de Deus habitando em luz inacessível)

DEFINITION: a prison cell.
ORIGIN: From oikeo; a tenement, i.e. (specially), a jail.

BDAG.en: an individual room in a dwelling, room, apartment; a room within a prison complex or a separate dwelling used for detention, quarters
BDAG.pt: um cômodo individual em uma habitação, quarto, apartamento; um quarto dentro de um complexo prisional ou uma habitação separada usada para detenção, alojamento

DEFINITION: a dwelling-place, habitation, abode.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of oikeo (equivalent to oikema); a residence (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: a place for living, dwelling, habitation (of angels; the glorified body of a transfigured Christian)
BDAG.pt: um lugar para viver, morada, habitação (de anjos; o corpo glorificado de um cristão transfigurado)

DEFINITION: a house, household, dwelling; meton: goods, property, means.
ORIGIN: From oikos; properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family (especially domestics).

BDAG.en: a structure used as a dwelling, house (literally as a building or figuratively of the body/heaven); a social unit within a dwelling, household, family
BDAG.pt: uma estrutura usada como morada, casa (literalmente como edifício ou figurativamente do corpo/céu); uma unidade social dentro de uma morada, casa, família

DEFINITION: one of a family, whether child or servant.
ORIGIN: From oikia; familiar, i.e. (as noun) relatives.

DEFINITION: to manage a household.
ORIGIN: From oikodespotes; to be the head of (i.e. Rule) a family.

BDAG.en: manage one’s household, keep house
BDAG.pt: administrar a própria casa, gerir o lar

DEFINITION: the master of a house.
ORIGIN: From oikos and despotes; the head of a family.
USAGE: goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house.

BDAG.en: master of the house, householder (used also figuratively of God)
BDAG.pt: mestre da casa, chefe de família (usado também em sentido figurado para Deus)

DEFINITION: to erect a building, build; fig. of the building up of character: to build up, edify, encourage.
ORIGIN: From the same as oikodome; to be a house-builder, i.e. Construct or (figuratively) confirm.

BDAG.en: to construct a building, build; build up again, restore; to construct in a transcendent sense, build (up the congregation/church); to help improve ability to function, strengthen, build up, make more able.
BDAG.pt: construir um edifício, edificar; reconstruir, restaurar; construir num sentido transcendente, edificar (a congregação/igreja); ajudar a melhorar a capacidade de funcionar, fortalecer, edificar, tornar mais capaz.

DEFINITION: (a) the act of building, (b) a building, (c) met: spiritual advancement, edification.
ORIGIN: Feminine (abstract) of a compound of oikos and the base of doma; architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation.

BDAG.en: process of building, building, construction; fig., of spiritual strengthening, edifying, edification, building up; a building as result of a construction process, building, edifice.
BDAG.pt: processo de construção, construção; fig., de fortalecimento espiritual, edificação; um edifício como resultado de um processo de construção, edifício.

DEFINITION: edifying.
ORIGIN: From the same as oikodome; confirmation.

BDAG.en: building, both as process and result, fig. edification
BDAG.pt: construção, tanto como processo quanto como resultado, fig. edificação

DEFINITION: to be a steward, manage a household.
ORIGIN: From oikonomos; to manage (a house, i.e. An estate).

BDAG.en: to manage a household, manage, administer, hold the office of an oikonomos, be manager; to administrate achievement of a project, manage, regulate, administer, plan
BDAG.pt: administrar uma casa, gerenciar, administrar, ocupar o cargo de oikonomos, ser gerente; administrar a concretização de um projeto, gerenciar, regular, administrar, planejar

DEFINITION: management of household affairs, stewardship, administration.
ORIGIN: From oikonomos; administration (of a household or estate); specially, a (religious) "economy".

BDAG.en: responsibility of management, management of a household, direction, office; state of being arranged, arrangement, order, plan; program of instruction, training
BDAG.pt: responsabilidade de gestão, administração de uma casa, direção, ofício; estado de estar arranjado, arranjo, ordem, plano; programa de instrução, treinamento

DEFINITION: a household manager, a steward, guardian.
ORIGIN: From oikos and the base of nomos; a house-distributor (i.e. Manager), or overseer, i.e. An employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the Gospel).

BDAG.en: manager of a household or estate, (house) steward, manager; public treasurer, treasurer; one who is entrusted with management in connection with transcendent matters, administrator
BDAG.pt: gerente de uma casa ou propriedade, mordomo (de casa), gerente; tesoureiro público; aquele encarregado da administração em conexão com assuntos transcendentais, administrador

DEFINITION: (a) a house, the material building, (b) a household, family, lineage, nation.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: house, dwelling, house of any large building (e.g., palace, house of prayer, prison-house), especially of God’s house (the temple or heavenly sanctuary); household, family; a whole clan or tribe of people descended from a common ancestor, house=descendants, nation; property, possessions, estate
BDAG.pt: casa, morada, casa de qualquer edifício grande (ex: palácio, casa de oração, casa de prisão), especialmente a casa de Deus (o templo ou santuário celestial); agregado familiar, família; um clã ou tribo inteira de pessoas descendentes de um ancestral comum, casa=descendentes, nação; propriedade, bens, patrimônio

DEFINITION: (properly: the land that is being inhabited, the land in a state of habitation), the inhabited world, that is, the Roman world, for all outside it was regarded as of no account.
ORIGIN: Feminine participle present passive of oikeo (as noun, by implication, of ge); land, i.e. The (terrene part of the) globe; specially, the Roman empire.

BDAG.en: The earth as the inhabited area (world); the Roman Empire (as an administrative unit); all inhabitants of the earth (humankind); the whole world (extraordinary use).
BDAG.pt: A terra como área habitada (mundo); o Império Romano (como unidade administrativa); todos os habitantes da terra (humanidade); o mundo inteiro (uso extraordinário).

DEFINITION: a keeper-at-home, a housekeeper.
ORIGIN: From oikos and ouros (a guard; be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e. Domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper").

DEFINITION: to pity, to have compassion on.
ORIGIN: Also (in certain tenses) prolonged oiktereo oyk-ter-eh'-o from oiktos (pity); to exercise pity.

BDAG.en: To have compassion on someone.
BDAG.pt: Ter compaixão de alguém.

DEFINITION: pity, compassion, favor, grace, mercy.
ORIGIN: From oikteiro; pity.

BDAG.en: Display of concern over another’s misfortune, pity, mercy, compassion (often used in the plural).
BDAG.pt: Demonstração de preocupação com a desgraça alheia, piedade, misericórdia, compaixão (frequentemente usado no plural).

DEFINITION: compassionate, merciful.
ORIGIN: From oikteiro; compassionate.

BDAG.en: Pertaining to being concerned about another’s unfortunate state or misery, merciful, compassionate (of God, sometimes humans).
BDAG.pt: Relativo a ter preocupação com o estado de infortúnio ou miséria alheia, misericordioso, compassivo (de Deus, às vezes de humanos).

DEFINITION: an excessive wine-drinker.
ORIGIN: From oinos and a derivative of the alternate of pino; a tippler.

BDAG.en: wine-drinker, drunkard
BDAG.pt: bebedor de vinho, bêbado

DEFINITION: wine.
ORIGIN: A primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (yayin)); "wine" (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: beverage made from fermented juice of the grape, wine; also used figuratively for God's wrath or spiritual intoxication; also the plant itself (vine/vineyard)
BDAG.pt: bebida feita do suco fermentado da uva, vinho; também usado figurativamente para a ira de Deus ou intoxicação espiritual; também a planta em si (videira/vinha)

DEFINITION: drunkenness, debauchery.

DEFINITION: to despise, hold in low esteem, make light of.

DEFINITION: a destroyer.

DEFINITION: to destroy, cause to perish.

DEFINITION: a whole burnt offering.

BDAG.pt: um sacrifício cultual no qual o animal era inteiramente consumido pelo fogo, holocausto

DEFINITION: perfect soundness, completeness.
ORIGIN: From holokleros; integrity, i.e. Physical wholeness.

BDAG.en: state of soundness or well-being in all parts, wholeness, completeness
BDAG.pt: estado de sanidade ou bem-estar em todas as partes, totalidade, completude

DEFINITION: complete in every part, sound, perfect, entire.
ORIGIN: From holos and kleros; complete in every part, i.e. Perfectly sound (in body).

DEFINITION: to howl, lament loudly, cry aloud, bewail.

DEFINITION: all, the whole, entire, complete.

DEFINITION: Olympas, a Christian man in Rome.

DEFINITION: an unripe fig, one which, not ripening in due time, grows through the winter and falls off in the spring.

DEFINITION: wholly, altogether, actually, really; with negative: not at all.

DEFINITION: to consort with, associate with, commune with; particularly, to talk (converse) with.

DEFINITION: intercourse, companionship, conversation, association.

BDAG.en: state of close association of persons, association, social intercourse, company; engagement in talk, conversation, speech or lecture to a group
BDAG.pt: estado de associação íntima de pessoas, associação, convívio social, companhia; envolvimento em conversa, diálogo, discurso ou palestra para um grupo.

DEFINITION: a mist or fog.

BDAG.pt: multidão, ajuntamento.

DEFINITION: an eye.

DEFINITION: to swear, take an oath, promise with an oath.

BDAG.en: to affirm the veracity of one’s statement by invoking a transcendent entity; swear, take an oath.
BDAG.pt: afirmar a veracidade da própria declaração invocando uma entidade transcendente; jurar, prestar um juramento.

DEFINITION: with one mind, unanimously, with one accord, at the same time.

BDAG.pt: estado de ter experiências em comum, semelhança; estado de ser semelhante em aparência, imagem, cópia; forma, aparência

DEFINITION: in like manner, similarly, in the same way, equally.

DEFINITION: making like, likeness, resemblance.

BDAG.pt: estado de ser semelhante, semelhança, aparência

BDAG.pt: qualquer instrumento que se usa para preparar ou pôr em ordem, ferramenta; um instrumento projetado para preparar para o engajamento militar, arma

DEFINITION: the act of seeing, a vision, appearance.
ORIGIN: From horao; the act of gazing, i.e. (externally) an aspect or (internally) an inspired appearance.

BDAG.en: organ of sight, eye, and hence sight, appearance, face; that which is seen, appearance, sight; vision in a transcendent mode
BDAG.pt: órgão da visão, olho, e daí visão, aparência, face; aquilo que é visto, aparência, vista; visão em modo transcendente

DEFINITION: visible.
ORIGIN: From horao; gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen.

BDAG.en: verbal adj. of ὁράω pert. to capability of being seen, visible
BDAG.pt: adjetivo verbal de ὁράω pertencente à capacidade de ser visto, visível

DEFINITION: to see, look upon, experience, perceive, discern, beware.
ORIGIN: Properly, to stare at (compare optanomai), i.e. (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); by extension, to attend to; by Hebraism, to experience; passively, to appear.

BDAG.en: to perceive by the eye, catch sight of, notice; to become visible, appear; to see someone in the course of making a friendly call, visit; to experience a condition or event, experience, witness; to be mentally or spiritually perceptive, perceive; to fix one’s gaze, look; to be alert or on guard, pay attention, see to it that; to accept responsibility for causing something to happen, look, see to, take care
BDAG.pt: perceber com os olhos, avistar, notar; tornar-se visível, aparecer; ver alguém ao fazer uma visita amigável; experimentar uma condição ou evento, vivenciar, testemunhar; ser mental ou espiritualmente perspicaz, perceber; fixar o olhar, olhar; estar alerta ou de guarda, prestar atenção, certificar-se de que; aceitar a responsabilidade por causar algo, olhar, providenciar, tomar cuidado

DEFINITION: anger, wrath, passion; punishment, vengeance.
ORIGIN: From oregomai; properly, desire (as a reaching forth or excitement of the mind), i.e. (by analogy), violent passion (ire, or (justifiable) abhorrence); by implication punishment.

BDAG.en: wrath, indignation, divine punitive judgment (often eschatological); storing up wrath (for oneself)
BDAG.pt: ira, indignação, juízo punitivo divino (frequentemente escatológico); acumular ira (para si mesmo)

DEFINITION: to irritate, provoke, be angry.
ORIGIN: From orge; to provoke or enrage, i.e. (passively) become exasperated.

BDAG.en: to be angry (used only in the passive voice in NT literature), followed by dative of person
BDAG.pt: estar irado, zangar-se (usado apenas na voz passiva na literatura do NT), seguido pelo dativo da pessoa

DEFINITION: inclined to anger, passionate.
ORIGIN: From orge; irascible.

BDAG.en: inclined to anger, quick-tempered
BDAG.pt: inclinado à ira, irascível, de pavio curto

DEFINITION: a fathom (the length of the outstretched arms).
ORIGIN: From oregomai; a stretch of the arms, i.e. A fathom.

BDAG.en: fathom (distance measured by a person’s arms stretched out horizontally), a nautical term
BDAG.pt: braça (distância medida com os braços de uma pessoa esticados horizontalmente), termo náutico

DEFINITION: to stretch forth, mid: to hanker after, long for, be eager for, aspire to.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare oros); to stretch oneself, i.e. Reach out after (long for).

BDAG.en: to seek to accomplish a specific goal, aspire to, strive for, desire (mid. ὀρέγομαι)
BDAG.pt: buscar realizar um objetivo específico, aspirar, esforçar-se, desejar (meio ὀρέγομαι)

DEFINITION: mountainous, hilly, the hill-country.
ORIGIN: From oros; mountainous, i.e. (feminine by implication, of chora) the Highlands (of Judaea).

BDAG.en: hilly, mountainous; (subst.) hill country, mountainous region
BDAG.pt: montanhoso, colinoso; (substantivado) região montanhosa, sertão

DEFINITION: strong desire, lust, appetite.
ORIGIN: From oregomai; excitement of the mind, i.e. Longing after.

BDAG.en: a condition of strong desire, longing, desire (used in an unfavorable sense)
BDAG.pt: uma condição de forte desejo, anseio, cobiça (usado em sentido desfavorável)

DEFINITION: to walk in a straight course, walk uprightly.
ORIGIN: From a compound of orthos and pous; to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward.

BDAG.en: to walk straight, upright; figuratively, to act rightly, be straightforward (in relation to the gospel truth)
BDAG.pt: andar direito, em linha reta; figurativamente, agir corretamente, ser reto (em relação à verdade do evangelho)

DEFINITION: upright, straight, direct.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of oros; right (as rising), i.e. (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively, honest), or (horizontally) level or direct.

BDAG.en: straight, upright, erect; correct, true (in belief or teaching)
BDAG.pt: reto, direito, ereto; correto, verdadeiro (em crença ou ensino)

DEFINITION: to cut straight; met: to handle correctly, teach rightly.
ORIGIN: From a compound of orthos and the base of tomoteros, to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message).

BDAG.en: to cut a path straight across country; figuratively, to guide the word of truth along a straight path
BDAG.pt: cortar um caminho reto através do país; figurativamente, guiar a palavra da verdade por um caminho reto

DEFINITION: to rise early, come in the morning.
ORIGIN: From orthros; to use the dawn, i.e. (by implication) to repair betimes.

BDAG.en: to be up or get up very early in the morning.
BDAG.pt: levantar-se ou levantar-se muito cedo pela manhã.

DEFINITION: morning.
ORIGIN: From orthros; relating to the dawn, i.e. Matutinal (as an epithet of Venus, especially brilliant in the early day).

BDAG.en: early in the morning.
BDAG.pt: de manhã cedo.

DEFINITION: early in the morning.
ORIGIN: From orthros; in the dawn, i.e. Up at day-break.

BDAG.en: early in the morning.
BDAG.pt: de manhã cedo.

DEFINITION: early dawn, day-break.
ORIGIN: From the same as oros; dawn (as sun-rise, rising of light); by extension, morn.

BDAG.en: period relatively early in the morning, dawn, early morning.
BDAG.pt: período relativamente no início da manhã, amanhecer, madrugada.

DEFINITION: rightly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from orthos; in a straight manner, i.e. (figuratively) correctly (also morally).

BDAG.en: rightly, correctly (pertaining to acting in conformity with a norm or standard).
BDAG.pt: corretamente, de modo certo (relativo a agir em conformidade com uma norma ou padrão).

DEFINITION: to separate, mark off by boundaries; to determine, appoint, designate.
ORIGIN: From horion; to mark out or bound ("horizon"), i.e. (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify.

BDAG.en: to set limits to, define, explain; to make a determination about, determine, appoint, fix, set (of time or things); appoint, designate, declare (of persons).
BDAG.pt: estabelecer limites, definir, explicar; fazer uma determinação sobre, determinar, nomear, fixar (de tempo ou coisas); nomear, designar, declarar (de pessoas).

DEFINITION: the boundaries of a place, hence: districts, territory.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary horos (a bound or limit); a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region).

BDAG.en: marker of division between two areas, boundary; mostly region, district.
BDAG.pt: marcador de divisão entre duas áreas, limite; na maioria das vezes região, distrito.

DEFINITION: to adjure by, charge solemnly by.
ORIGIN: From horkos; to put on oath, i.e. Make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin.

BDAG.en: to give a command to someone under oath, adjure, implore.
BDAG.pt: dar um comando a alguém sob juramento, conjurar, implorar.

DEFINITION: an oath.
ORIGIN: From herkos (a fence; perhaps akin to horion); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath).

BDAG.en: oath.
BDAG.pt: juramento.

DEFINITION: the taking of an oath, an oath.
ORIGIN: From a compound of horkos and a derivative of omnuo; asseveration on oath.

BDAG.en: the process of taking an oath, oath-taking, oath.
BDAG.pt: o processo de prestar juramento, o ato de jurar, juramento.

DEFINITION: to set in motion, to hasten on.
ORIGIN: From horme; to start, spur or urge on, i.e. (reflexively) to dash or plunge.

BDAG.en: to make a rapid movement from one place to another, rush (headlong).
BDAG.pt: fazer um movimento rápido de um lugar para outro, correr (de cabeça).

DEFINITION: a rapid motion forwards, onrush, assault.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a violent impulse, i.e. Onset.

BDAG.en: a psychological state of strong tendency, impulse, inclination, desire.
BDAG.pt: um estado psicológico de forte tendência, impulso, inclinação, desejo.

DEFINITION: a rushing on, impulse, violence.
ORIGIN: From horme; an attack, i.e. (abstractly) precipitancy.

BDAG.en: violent rush, onset.
BDAG.pt: ímpeto violento, investida.

DEFINITION: a bird, fowl.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ornis; a birdling.

BDAG.en: bird.
BDAG.pt: pássaro.

DEFINITION: a bird, a rooster or hen.
ORIGIN: Probably from a prolonged form of the base of oros; a bird (as rising in the air), i.e. (specially), a hen (or female domestic fowl).

BDAG.en: bird; specifically 'cock' or 'hen'; in NT only fem. hen. The action of the mother bird or specifically of the hen as a symbol of protecting care.
BDAG.pt: pássaro; especificamente 'galo' ou 'galinha'; no NT apenas feminino como galinha. A ação da ave-mãe ou especificamente da galinha como símbolo de cuidado protetor.

DEFINITION: a setting of boundaries, definite limit; plur: bounds.
ORIGIN: From a compound of the base of horion and a derivative of tithemi; a limit-placing, i.e. (concretely) boundary-line.

BDAG.en: fixed boundary. (God) determined the boundaries of their habitation.
BDAG.pt: fronteira fixa. (Deus) determinou os limites da sua habitação.

DEFINITION: a mountain, hill.
ORIGIN: Probably from an obsolete oro (to rise or "rear"; perhaps akin to airo; compare ornis); a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain): -hill, mount(-ain)..
USAGE: a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain); hill, mount(-ain).

BDAG.en: mountain, mount, hill; a relatively high elevation of land that projects higher than a 'bounos' (a minor elevation, hill). Used as the scene of outstanding events and places of solitude.
BDAG.pt: montanha, monte, colina; uma elevação relativamente alta do terreno que se projeta mais alto que um 'bounos' (uma elevação menor, colina). Usado como cenário de eventos notáveis e locais de solidão.

DEFINITION: to dig, dig out, excavate.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to "burrow" in the ground, i.e. Dig.

BDAG.en: to loosen material by digging, dig (up); to prepare a place for something by digging, dig out, prepare by digging; to make a hole in something by digging, dig (a hole).
BDAG.pt: soltar material cavando, cavar (para cima); preparar um lugar para algo cavando, escavar, preparar cavando; fazer um buraco em algo cavando, cavar (um buraco).

DEFINITION: bereaved, an orphan, fatherless, desolate.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; bereaved ("orphan"), i.e. Parentless.

BDAG.en: without parents, orphan; figuratively, orphaned (deprived of aid and comfort of one who serves as associate and friend).
BDAG.pt: sem pais, órfão; figurativamente, órfão (privado do auxílio e conforto de quem serve como associado e amigo).

DEFINITION: to dance.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from orchos (a row or ring); to dance (from the ranklike or regular motion).

BDAG.en: dance; of children at play.
BDAG.pt: dançar; de crianças brincando.

DEFINITION: usually rel. who, which, that, also demonstrative this, that.
ORIGIN: Including feminine he (hay), and neuter ho (ho) probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article ho); the relatively (sometimes demonstrative) pronoun, who, which, what, that.
USAGE: one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who(-m, -se), etc. See also hou.

BDAG.en: Relative pronoun (who, which, that); Demonstrative pronoun (this one). Used extensively in relative clauses, often exhibiting complex syntactic features like attraction, and can also function in indirect questions.
BDAG.pt: Pronome relativo (quem, qual, que); Pronome demonstrativo (este). Usado extensivamente em orações relativas, frequentemente exibindo características sintáticas complexas como atração, e também pode funcionar em perguntas indiretas.

DEFINITION: as often as, as many times as.
ORIGIN: Multiple adverb from hos; how (i.e. With an, so) many times as.

BDAG.en: As often as.
BDAG.pt: Sempre que; quantas vezes.

DEFINITION: holy, pious, godly, beloved of God.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; properly, right (by intrinsic or divine character; thus distinguished from dikaios, which refers rather to human statutes and relations; from hieros, which denotes formal consecration; and from hagios, which relates to purity from defilement), i.e. Hallowed (pious, sacred, sure).

BDAG.en: Pertaining to being without fault relative to deity, devout, pious, pleasing to God, holy; holy of God (as a standard).
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a estar sem culpa em relação à divindade, devoto, piedoso, agradável a Deus, santo; santo de Deus (como um padrão).

DEFINITION: holiness, godliness, piety.
ORIGIN: From hosios; piety.

BDAG.en: state of proper attitude toward God as exhibited in action, devoutness, piety, holiness
BDAG.pt: estado de atitude correta para com Deus conforme demonstrado em ação, devoção, piedade, santidade

DEFINITION: religiously, piously.
ORIGIN: Adverb from hosios; piously.

BDAG.en: In a manner pleasing to God, devoutly, uprightly.
BDAG.pt: De maneira agradável a Deus, devotamente, com retidão.

DEFINITION: a smell, odor, savor.
ORIGIN: From ozo; fragrance (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: odor, fragrance (pleasant or unpleasant), fig. quality affecting the mind as with an odor.
BDAG.pt: odor, fragrância (agradável ou desagradável), fig. qualidade que afeta a mente como um odor.

DEFINITION: how much, how great, how many, as great as, as much.
ORIGIN: By reduplication from hos; as (much, great, long, etc.) As.
USAGE: all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), (in-)asmuch as, so many as, that (ever), the more, those things, what (great, -soever), wheresoever, wherewithsoever, which, X while, who(-soever).

BDAG.en: as great, as far, as long as; how much (many), as much (many) as
BDAG.pt: tão grande, tão longe, tão longo quanto; quanto (muitos), tanta (coisa) quanto

DEFINITION: the very one who.
ORIGIN: From hos and per; who especially.

BDAG.en: just as, exactly as (see ὅς).
BDAG.pt: exatamente como, tal qual (ver ὅς).

DEFINITION: a bone.
ORIGIN: Or contracted ostoun (os-toon') of uncertain affinity; a bone.

BDAG.en: bone (pl. ὀστέα or contracted ὀστοῦν).
BDAG.pt: osso (plural ὀστέα ou contraído ὀστοῦν).

DEFINITION: whosoever, whichsoever, whatsoever.
ORIGIN: Including the feminine hetis (hay'-tis), and the neuter ho,ti (hot'-ee) from hos and tis; which some, i.e. Any that; also (definite) which same.
USAGE: X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what(-soever), whereas ye, (they) which, who(-soever). Compare hoti.

BDAG.en: any person who, whoever, every one who; who (to confirm a characteristic); sometimes takes the place of the simple relative ὅς.
BDAG.pt: qualquer pessoa que, quem quer que seja, todo aquele que; quem (para confirmar uma característica); às vezes substitui o relativo simples ὅς.

DEFINITION: made of clay, earthen.
ORIGIN: From ostrakon ("oyster") (a tile, i.e. Terra cotta); earthen-ware, i.e. Clayey; by implication, frail.

BDAG.en: made of earth/clay, earthen(ware) vessels; denoting breakableness (of vessels); of cultic images made of clay
BDAG.pt: feito de terra/barro, vasos de barro; denotando fragilidade (de vasos); de imagens cultuais feitas de barro

DEFINITION: the sense of smell, smelling.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of ozo; smell (the sense).

BDAG.en: sense of smell or organ of smell, nose
BDAG.pt: sentido do olfato ou órgão do olfato, nariz

DEFINITION: the loins.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; the loin (externally), i.e. The hip; internally (by extension) procreative power.

BDAG.en: the place where a belt or girdle is worn, waist, loins; the place of the reproductive organs, the loins (as source of descendants or power)
BDAG.pt: o lugar onde um cinto ou faixa é usada, cintura, lombos; o lugar dos órgãos reprodutivos, os lombos (como fonte de descendentes ou poder)

DEFINITION: when, whenever.
ORIGIN: From hote and an; whenever (implying hypothesis or more or less uncertainty); also causatively (conjunctionally) inasmuch as.
USAGE: as long (soon) as, that, + till, when(-soever), while.

BDAG.en: temporal particle: at the time that, whenever, when (conditional/repeated action); introducing an epexegetical statement
BDAG.pt: partícula temporal: no momento em que, sempre que, quando (ação condicional/repetida); introduzindo uma declaração epexegética

DEFINITION: when, at which time.
ORIGIN: From hos and te; at which (thing) too, i.e. When.
USAGE: after (that), as soon as, that, when, while.

BDAG.en: temporal particle: when (marker of a point of time that coincides with another point of time); as a substitute for a relative pronoun denoting time; as long as, while (marker of a period of time coextensive with another)
BDAG.pt: partícula temporal: quando (marcador de um ponto no tempo que coincide com outro ponto no tempo); como substituto para um pronome relativo que denota tempo; enquanto (marcador de um período de tempo coextensivo com outro)

DEFINITION: that, since, because; may introduce direct discourse.
ORIGIN: Neuter of hostis as conjunction; demonstrative, that (sometimes redundant); causative, because.
USAGE: as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, though, why.

BDAG.en: conjunction used for introducing reported speech or statements, often translated as 'that'; marker of causality, meaning 'because' or 'since'; used with demonstrative/interrogative pronouns to mean 'for this reason... that' or 'why? because...'; special uses include: with accusative and infinitive after certain verbs (e.g., θεωρεῖν), simple 'that' after ὡς (in later vernacular), and consecutive 'so that'.
BDAG.pt: conjunção usada para introduzir discurso relatado ou declarações, frequentemente traduzida como 'que'; marcador de causalidade, significando 'porque' ou 'visto que'; usada com pronomes demonstrativos/interrogativos para significar 'por esta razão... que' ou 'por que? porque...'; usos especiais incluem: com acusativo e infinitivo após certos verbos (ex: θεωρεῖν), simplesmente 'que' depois de ὡς (no vernáculo tardio), e consecutiva 'para que'.

DEFINITION: while.
ORIGIN: For the genitive case of hostis (as adverb); during which same time, i.e. Whilst.

BDAG.en: gen. sing. masc. and neut. of ὅστις (whoever/whatever)
BDAG.pt: genitivo singular masculino e neutro de ὅστις (quem quer que/o que quer que)

DEFINITION: not, no.
ORIGIN: Also (before a vowel) ouk (ook), and (before an aspirate) ouch (ookh) a primary word; the absolute negative (compare me) adverb; no or not.
USAGE: + long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, (can-)not, + nothing, + special, un(-worthy), when, + without, + yet but. See also ou me, mekos.

BDAG.en: objective negative adverb, denying the reality of an alleged fact; used typically with the indicative mood; functions as a negative response ('no'); marks negative propositions, negating single words or clauses ('not'); frequently used in litotes (understatement by double negative, e.g., 'not a few'); can serve as a periphrasis for certain verb concepts (e.g., οὐκ ἀγνοεῖν = 'to know quite well'); used in combination with other negatives to strengthen negation; used in questions expecting an affirmative answer ('not so?').
BDAG.pt: advérbio negativo objetivo, negando a realidade de um fato alegado; usado tipicamente com o modo indicativo; funciona como uma resposta negativa ('não'); marca proposições negativas, negando palavras ou cláusulas isoladas ('não'); frequentemente usado em litotes (eufemismo por dupla negação, ex: 'não poucos'); pode servir como perífrase para certos conceitos verbais (ex: οὐκ ἀγνοεῖν = 'saber muito bem'); usado em combinação com outras negativas para intensificar a negação; usado em perguntas esperando uma resposta afirmativa ('não é assim?').

DEFINITION: where, whither, when, in what place.
ORIGIN: Genitive case of hos as adverb; at which place, i.e. Where.

BDAG.en: adverb of place, originating as the genitive of ὅς (who, which); marks a position in space ('where'); can denote a location as a destination ('where, to which'); also marks a situation or set of circumstances ('in a situation where').
BDAG.pt: advérbio de lugar, originado como o genitivo de ὅς (quem, o qual); marca uma posição no espaço ('onde'); pode denotar um local como destino ('onde, para onde'); também marca uma situação ou conjunto de circunstâncias ('em uma situação onde').

DEFINITION: ah! ha! (an expression of wonder or surprise).
ORIGIN: A primary exclamation of surprise; "ah".

BDAG.en: interjection denoting amazement ('aha!'), also used to express scornful wonder or joy.
BDAG.pt: interjeição que denota espanto ('aha!'), também usada para expressar maravilha sarcástica ou alegria.

DEFINITION: alas! woe! (an expression of grief or denunciation).
ORIGIN: A primary exclamation of grief; "woe".

BDAG.en: interjection denoting pain or displeasure ('woe', 'alas'), often used with the dative of the person or thing concerned; can be used with the nominative and article as a vocative; can also function substantively as a state of intense hardship or distress ('woe', 'calamity').
BDAG.pt: interjeição que denota dor ou desagrado ('ai', 'miséria'), frequentemente usada com o dativo da pessoa ou coisa a que se refere; pode ser usada com o nominativo e artigo como vocativo; também pode funcionar como substantivo, referindo-se a um estado de intensa dificuldade ou aflição ('miséria', 'calamidade').

DEFINITION: by no means, not at all.
ORIGIN: Adverb from (the feminine) of oudeis; by no means.

BDAG.en: marker of emphatic negation: by no means
BDAG.pt: advérbio de negação enfática: de modo algum, nem pensar

DEFINITION: neither, nor, not even, and not.
ORIGIN: From ou and de; not however, i.e. Neither, nor, not even.
USAGE: neither (indeed), never, no (more, nor, not), nor (yet), (also, even, then) not (even, so much as), + nothing, so much as.

BDAG.en: negative conjunction, combination of οὐand δέ. 1 and not, nor joins neg. sentences or clauses to others of the same kind. 2 also not, not either, neither. 3 not even, Lat. ne … quidem
BDAG.pt: conjunção negativa, combinação de οὐ e δέ. 1 e não, nem une sentenças ou cláusulas negativas a outras do mesmo tipo. 2 também não, nem. 3 nem mesmo, Lat. ne … quidem

DEFINITION: no one, none, nothing.
ORIGIN: Including feminine oudemia (oo-dem-ee'-ah), and neuter ouden (oo-den') from oude and heis; not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. None, nobody, nothing.
USAGE: any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought.

BDAG.en: as an adj. no. 2 as a subst. a no one, nobody. b nonliterally worthless, meaningless, invalid. c the acc. in no respect, in no way
BDAG.pt: como adjetivo: nenhum. 2 como substantivo: a) ninguém, pessoa alguma. b) em sentido não literal: sem valor, sem sentido, inválido. c) acusativo: em nenhum aspecto, de modo algum

DEFINITION: never.
ORIGIN: From oude and pote; not even at any time, i.e. Never at all.
USAGE: neither at any time, never, nothing at any time.

BDAG.en: an indefnite negated point of time, never, w. pres.
BDAG.pt: um ponto de tempo negado indefinido, nunca, com o presente

DEFINITION: not yet, never before.
ORIGIN: From oude and po; not even yet.
USAGE: as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet.

BDAG.en: the negation of extending time up to and beyond an expected point, not yet, still not
BDAG.pt: a negação de estender o tempo até e além de um ponto esperado, ainda não

DEFINITION: no longer, no more.
ORIGIN: Also (separately) ouk eti (ook et'-ee) from ou and eti; not yet, no longer.
USAGE: after that (not), (not) any more, henceforth (hereafter) not, no longer (more), not as yet (now), now no more (not), yet (not).

BDAG.en: 1 the extension of time up to a point but not beyond, no more, no longer, no further lit., of time. 2 marker of inference in a logical process, then (accordingly) not
BDAG.pt: 1 a extensão do tempo até um ponto, mas não além, não mais, não mais, não adiante literalmente, de tempo. 2 marcador de inferência em um processo lógico, então (assim) não

DEFINITION: therefore, so then.
ORIGIN: From ou and oun; is it not therefore that, i.e. (affirmatively) hence or so.

BDAG.en: 1 inferential therefore, so, accordingly. 2 interrogative, when the question has inferential force, so then
BDAG.pt: 1 inferencial: portanto, assim, consequentemente. 2 interrogativo, quando a pergunta tem força inferencial: então?

DEFINITION: therefore, then, (and) so.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; (adverbially) certainly, or (conjunctionally) accordingly.
USAGE: and (so, truly), but, now (then), so (likewise then), then, therefore, verily, wherefore.

BDAG.en: a particle, never found at the beginning of a sentence. 1 inferential, denoting that what it introduces is the result of or an inference from what precedes, so, therefore, consequently, accordingly, then. 2 marker of continuation of a narrative, so, now, then
BDAG.pt: uma partícula, nunca encontrada no início de uma sentença. 1 inferencial, denotando que aquilo que introduz é o resultado ou uma inferência do que precede, então, portanto, consequentemente, de acordo. 2 marcador de continuação de uma narrativa, então, agora, pois

DEFINITION: not yet.
ORIGIN: From ou and po; not yet.
USAGE: hitherto not, (no...) As yet, not yet.

BDAG.en: not yet
BDAG.pt: ainda não

DEFINITION: a tail.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a tail.

BDAG.en: tail
BDAG.pt: cauda

DEFINITION: in heaven, belonging to heaven, heavenly, from heaven.
ORIGIN: From ouranos; celestial, i.e. Belonging to or coming from the sky.

BDAG.en: belonging to heaven, coming from or living in heaven, heavenly
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao céu, vindo ou habitando no céu, celestial

DEFINITION: from heaven, from the sky.
ORIGIN: From ouranos and the enclitic of source; from the sky.

BDAG.en: from heaven
BDAG.pt: do céu

DEFINITION: heaven, (a) the visible heavens: the atmosphere, the sky, the starry heavens, (b) the spiritual heavens.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the same as oros (through the idea of elevation); the sky; by extension, heaven (as the abode of God); by implication, happiness, power, eternity; specially, the Gospel (Christianity).

BDAG.en: heaven, sky; the host of heaven (stars); place of the atmosphere (clouds, birds); transcendent abode (dwelling place/throne of God); abode of angels; abode of the righteous dead; indirect reference to God.
BDAG.pt: céu, firmamento; o exército do céu (estrelas); lugar da atmosfera (nuvens, aves); morada transcendente (morada/trono de Deus); morada dos anjos; morada dos justos mortos; referência indireta a Deus.

DEFINITION: Urbanus, a Christian in Rome, fellow-worker of Paul.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; Urbanus (of the city, "urbane"), a Christian.

BDAG.en: Urbanus, addressee of a greeting, described as a co-worker in Christ.
BDAG.pt: Urbano, destinatário de uma saudação, descrito como colaborador em Cristo.

DEFINITION: Uriah, husband of Bathsheba the mother of Solomon.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin ('Uwriyah); Urias (i.e. Urijah), a Hittite.

BDAG.en: Uriah, husband of Bathsheba who, after his death, married David and bore Solomon to him; the wife of Uriah.
BDAG.pt: Urias, marido de Bate-Seba que, após sua morte, se casou com Davi e lhe gerou Salomão; a esposa de Urias.

DEFINITION: (a) the ear, (b) met: the faculty of perception.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; the ear (physically or mentally).

BDAG.en: the auditory organ, ear; mental and spiritual understanding, ear, hearing.
BDAG.pt: o órgão auditivo, ouvido; entendimento mental e espiritual, ouvido, audição.

DEFINITION: property, wealth, substance.
ORIGIN: From the feminine of on; substance, i.e. Property (possessions).

BDAG.en: that which exists and therefore has substance, property, wealth.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que existe e, portanto, tem substância, propriedade, riqueza.

DEFINITION: and not, neither, nor.
ORIGIN: From ou and te; not too, i.e. Neither or nor; by analogy, not even.
USAGE: neither, none, nor (yet), (no, yet) not, nothing.

BDAG.en: and not; neither... nor; neither... nor... nor.
BDAG.pt: e não; nem... nem; nem... nem... nem.

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Including nominative masculine plural houtoi (hoo'-toy), nominative feminine singular haute (how'-tay), and nominative feminine plural hautai (how'-tahee) from the article ho and autos; the he (she or it), i.e. This or that (often with article repeated).
USAGE: he (it was that), hereof, it, she, such as, the same, these, they, this (man, same, woman), which, who.

BDAG.en: this, this one (person or thing comparatively near at hand in the discourse material), directing attention to something here and now; sometimes used with a connotation of contempt; emphasizing a person already mentioned; referring to something that has immediately preceded; referring to a subject more remote in the paragraph but closer to the main referent; referring to what follows; resuming something previously mentioned with special emphasis; as an adjective, pertaining to an entity perceived as present or near in the discourse.
BDAG.pt: este, este aqui (pessoa ou coisa relativamente próxima no material do discurso), direcionando a atenção para algo aqui e agora; às vezes usado com conotação de desprezo; enfatizando uma pessoa já mencionada; referindo-se a algo que precedeu imediatamente; referindo-se a um assunto mais distante no parágrafo, mas mais próximo do referente principal; referindo-se ao que se segue; retomando algo previamente mencionado com ênfase especial; como adjetivo, pertinente a uma entidade percebida como presente ou próxima no discurso.

DEFINITION: thus, so, in this manner.
ORIGIN: Or (before a vowel houtos hoo'-toce adverb from houtos; in this way (referring to what precedes or follows).
USAGE: after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like(-wise), no more, on this fashion(-wise), so (in like manner), thus, what.

DEFINITION: by no means, not at all.
ORIGIN: Intensive of ou; not indeed.

BDAG.en: not (a strengthened form of οὐ); a simple negative, not; a negative reply, no, by no means; an interrogative word in questions that expect an affirmative answer, not?
BDAG.pt: Não (uma forma reforçada de οὐ); uma negação simples, não; uma resposta negativa, não, de modo algum; uma palavra interrogativa em perguntas que esperam uma resposta afirmativa, não?

DEFINITION: (a) a debtor, one who owes, one who is indebted, (b) one who has sinned against another (an Aramaism), a sinner.
ORIGIN: From opheilo; an ower, i.e. Person indebted; figuratively, a delinquent; morally, a transgressor (against God).

BDAG.en: one who is in debt in a monetary sense, debtor; one who is under obligation in a moral or social sense, one under obligation, one liable for; one who is guilty of a misdeed, one who is culpable, at fault
BDAG.pt: Aquele que está endividado em sentido monetário, devedor; aquele que está sob obrigação em sentido moral ou social, um obrigado, alguém responsável por; aquele que é culpado por um erro, o culpado, o responsável

DEFINITION: a debt, a duty, what is due.
ORIGIN: From opheilo; indebtedness, i.e. (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. (conjugal) duty.

BDAG.en: that which one owes in a financial sense, obligation; that which one ought to do, duty; failure to meet moral obligations
BDAG.pt: Aquilo que se deve em sentido financeiro, obrigação; aquilo que se deve fazer, dever; falha em cumprir obrigações morais

DEFINITION: that which is owed, a debt.
ORIGIN: From (the alternate of) opheilo; something owed, i.e. (figuratively) a due; morally, a fault.

BDAG.en: that which is owed in a financial sense, debt, one’s due; obligation in a moral sense, debt=sin
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é devido em sentido financeiro, dívida, o que é de direito; obrigação em sentido moral, dívida=pecado

DEFINITION: to owe, ought.
ORIGIN: Or (in certain tenses), its prolonged form opheileo (of-i-leh'-o) probably from the base of ophelos (through the idea of accruing); to owe (pecuniarily); figuratively, to be under obligation (ought, must, should); morally, to fail in duty.
USAGE: behove, be bound, (be) debt(-or), (be) due(-ty), be guilty (indebted), (must) need(-s), ought, owe, should. See also ophelon.

BDAG.en: to be indebted to someone in a financial sense, owe something to someone, be indebted; to be under obligation to meet certain social or moral expectations, owe (generally); to be constrained by circumstance, have to, ought
BDAG.pt: Estar endividado com alguém em sentido financeiro, dever algo a alguém, ser devedor; estar sob obrigação de satisfazer certas expectativas sociais ou morais, dever (geralmente); ser constrangido pela circunstância, ter que, dever

DEFINITION: O that! I wish! Would that!, followed by indicative.
ORIGIN: First person singular of a past tense of opheilo; I ought (wish), i.e. (interjection) oh that!.

BDAG.en: a fixed form, functioning as a particle to introduce unattainable wishes, o that, would that
BDAG.pt: uma forma fixa, funcionando como partícula para introduzir desejos inatingíveis, oxalá, quem dera

DEFINITION: advantage, gain, profit, help.
ORIGIN: From ophello (to heap up, i.e. Accumulate or benefit); gain.

BDAG.en: an advantage derived from something, benefit, good
BDAG.pt: uma vantagem derivada de algo, benefício, bem

DEFINITION: eye-service; service rendered only while the master watches.
ORIGIN: From ophthalmos and douleia; sight-labor, i.e. That needs watching (remissness).

DEFINITION: the eye; fig: the mind's eye.
ORIGIN: From optanomai; the eye (literally or figuratively); by implication, vision; figuratively, envy (from the jealous side-glance).

BDAG.en: eye as organ of sense perception; by metonymy for envy, malice; mental and spiritual understanding, eye, understanding
BDAG.pt: olho como órgão de percepção sensorial; por metonímia, inveja, malícia; entendimento mental e espiritual, visão, compreensão.

DEFINITION: a serpent, snake; used of the devil or Satan.
ORIGIN: Probably from optanomai (through the idea of sharpness of vision); a snake, figuratively, (as a type of sly cunning) an artful malicious person, especially Satan.

BDAG.en: a limbless reptile, snake, serpent; a person perceived as dangerous, snake; a symbolic figure, serpent (as a designation for the devil)
BDAG.pt: um réptil sem membros, cobra, serpente; uma pessoa percebida como perigosa, serpente; uma figura simbólica, serpente (como designação para o diabo)

DEFINITION: the brow, a ridge (of a mountain).
ORIGIN: Perhaps from optanomai (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision); the eye-"brow" or forehead, i.e. (figuratively) the brink of a precipice.

BDAG.en: eyebrow; then brow, edge of a cliff or hill
BDAG.pt: sobrancelha; depois, a testa, a borda de um penhasco ou colina.

DEFINITION: to trouble, torment, worry, vex.
ORIGIN: From ochlos; to mob, i.e. (by implication) to harass.

BDAG.en: to cause trouble by harassment, trouble, disturb
BDAG.pt: causar problemas por assédio, incomodar, perturbar.

DEFINITION: to gather a crowd, make a riot.
ORIGIN: From ochlos and poieo; to make a crowd, i.e. Raise a public disturbance.

BDAG.en: form a mob
BDAG.pt: formar uma turba/multidão.

DEFINITION: a crowd, multitude, the common people.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of echo (meaning a vehicle); a throng (as borne along); by implication, the rabble; by extension, a class of people; figuratively, a riot.
USAGE: company, multitude, number (of people), people, press.

BDAG.en: a relatively large number of people gathered together, crowd; the (common) people, populace; a group or company of people with common interests or of distinctive status; a large mass of people, horde, mass
BDAG.pt: um número relativamente grande de pessoas reunidas, multidão; o povo (comum), a população; um grupo ou companhia de pessoas com interesses comuns ou status distinto; uma grande massa de pessoas, horda, massa

DEFINITION: a fortress, strong defense, stronghold.
ORIGIN: From a remote derivative of echo (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely); a castle (figuratively, argument).

BDAG.en: a strong military installation, fortress
BDAG.pt: uma instalação militar forte, fortaleza

DEFINITION: a little fish.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of optos; a relish to other food (as if cooked sauce), i.e. (specially), fish (presumably salted and dried as a condiment).

BDAG.en: cooked food eaten w. bread; tidbit in general or specifically fish
BDAG.pt: comida cozida que se come com pão; iguaria em geral ou especificamente peixe

DEFINITION: late, in the evening.
ORIGIN: From the same as opiso (through the idea of backwardness); (adverbially) late in the day; by extension, after the close of the day.

BDAG.en: pert. to an advanced point of time in the day, usually between sunset and darkness, late; pert. specif. to the period between late afternoon and darkness, late in the day, evening; marker of a point of time subsequent to another point of time, after, with special ref. to lateness
BDAG.pt: pertencente a um ponto avançado do dia, geralmente entre o pôr do sol e a escuridão, tarde; pertencente especificamente ao período entre o fim da tarde e a escuridão, no final do dia, noite; marcador de um ponto no tempo subsequente a outro ponto no tempo, depois, com referência especial à tardiosidade

DEFINITION: the latter rain.
ORIGIN: From opse; later, i.e. Vernal (showering).

BDAG.en: pert. to a period of time that is relatively late, and esp. in connection with agricultural activity; in our lit. of rain that comes in spring, after the normal rains of the winter season have passed, late rain, spring rain
BDAG.pt: pertencente a um período de tempo relativamente tardio, e especialmente em conexão com atividade agrícola; em nossa literatura, referente à chuva que cai na primavera, após as chuvas normais da estação de inverno terem passado, chuva tardia, chuva da primavera

DEFINITION: late, evening.
ORIGIN: From opse; late; feminine (as noun) afternoon (early eve) or nightfall (later eve).

BDAG.en: as adj.: pert. to a point in time that is relatively later than another point of time, late; mostly subst.: the period between late afternoon and darkness, evening
BDAG.pt: como adjetivo: pertencente a um ponto no tempo relativamente posterior a outro ponto no tempo, tarde; na maioria das vezes como substantivo: o período entre o final da tarde e a escuridão, noite

DEFINITION: (a) the face, countenance, (b) the features, outward appearance.
ORIGIN: From optanomai; properly, sight (the act), i.e. (by implication) the visage, an external show.

BDAG.en: the experience of seeing something, seeing, sight; external or physical aspect of something, outward appearance, aspect; the front portion of the head or expression thereof, face, countenance; (pl.) chiefly the eyes, prob. means more generally face
BDAG.pt: a experiência de ver algo, visão, vista; aspecto externo ou físico de algo, aparência externa, aspeto; a porção frontal da cabeça ou a expressão dela, rosto, semblante; (plural) principalmente os olhos, provavelmente significa mais genericamente rosto

DEFINITION: pay, wages, salary, reward.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as opsarion; rations for a soldier, i.e. (by extension) his stipend or pay.

BDAG.en: 'ration-(money)' paid to a soldier, then pay, wages; compensation
BDAG.pt: 'ração-(dinheiro)' paga a um soldado, então soldo, salário; compensação
