DEFINITION: to come.
ORIGIN: Ho erchomenos (ho own kahee) ho ane kahee (ho er-khom'-en-os) a phrase combining ho with the present participle and imperfect of eimi and the present participle of erchomai by means of kai; the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. The Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ.
USAGE: which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be).

BDAG.en: The (definite article, masculine singular nominative form, used here to describe its grammatical functions, especially with names of countries, rivers, seas, personal pronouns, possessive adjectives, adjectives, demonstrative pronouns, and in forming vocatives and substantive adjectives.)
BDAG.pt: O (Artigo definido, masculino singular nominativo, usado aqui para descrever suas funções gramaticais, especialmente com nomes de países, rios, mares, pronomes pessoais, adjetivos possessivos, adjetivos, pronomes demonstrativos e na formação de vocativos e adjetivos substantivados.)

DEFINITION: to ensnare, entrap, entangle.
ORIGIN: From pagis; to ensnare (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to set a snare or trap, entrap (figuratively)
BDAG.pt: armar um laço ou armadilha, prender (figurativamente)

DEFINITION: a snare, trap (especially for catching birds) hence, met: stratagem, device, wile.
ORIGIN: From pegnumi; a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation).

BDAG.en: trap, snare; a device used to catch animals; that which causes one to be suddenly endangered or unexpectedly brought under control of a hostile force, trap, snare (figuratively); deadly snare
BDAG.pt: armadilha, laço; um dispositivo usado para capturar animais; aquilo que faz com que alguém seja subitamente perigoso ou inesperadamente posto sob o controle de uma força hostil, armadilha (figurativamente); laço mortal

DEFINITION: (a) suffering, affliction, (b) passion, emotion, (c) an undergoing, an enduring.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of pathos; something undergone, i.e. Hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence.

BDAG.en: that which is suffered or endured, suffering, misfortune; an inward experience of an affective nature, feeling, interest (in a bad sense)
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é sofrido ou suportado, sofrimento, infortúnio; uma experiência interior de natureza afetiva, sentimento, interesse (em um sentido negativo)

DEFINITION: one who has suffered or is subject to suffering.
ORIGIN: From the same as pathema; liable (i.e. Doomed) to experience pain.

BDAG.en: subject to suffering (of the Messiah)
BDAG.pt: sujeito a sofrimento (do Messias)

DEFINITION: that which befalls one, a passion, a suffering.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of pascho; properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence).

BDAG.en: that which is endured or experienced, suffering (physical sufferings of Christ); experience of strong desire, passion (especially sexual nature)
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é suportado ou vivenciado, sofrimento (sofrimentos físicos de Cristo); experiência de forte desejo, paixão (especialmente de natureza sexual)

DEFINITION: a boy's guardian or tutor, a slave who had charge of the life and morals of the boys of a family, not strictly a teacher.
ORIGIN: From pais and a reduplicated form of ago; a boy-leader, i.e. A servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("paedagogue")).

BDAG.en: boy-leader, the man, usu. a slave, whose duty it was to conduct a boy or youth to and from school and to superintend his conduct gener.; one who has responsibility for someone who needs guidance, guardian, leader, guide
BDAG.pt: condutor de menino, geralmente um escravo, cuja função era conduzir um menino ou jovem à escola e de volta, e supervisionar sua conduta em geral; aquele que tem responsabilidade por alguém que necessita de orientação, guardião, líder, guia

DEFINITION: a little boy, lad.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of pais; a little boy.

BDAG.en: child (also female); a youth, who is no longer a child; young slave.
BDAG.pt: criança (também do sexo feminino); um jovem que não é mais uma criança; jovem escravo.

DEFINITION: discipline; training and education of children, hence: instruction; chastisement, correction.
ORIGIN: From paideuo; tutorage, i.e. Education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction.

BDAG.en: the act of providing guidance for responsible living, upbringing, training, instruction, chiefly as it is attained by discipline, correction; the state of being brought up properly, training
BDAG.pt: o ato de fornecer orientação para uma vida responsável, criação, treinamento, instrução, principalmente conforme alcançado por disciplina, correção; o estado de ter sido criado adequadamente, treinamento

DEFINITION: an instructor, trainer; almost: a chastiser.
ORIGIN: From paideuo; a trainer, i.e. Teacher or (by implication) discipliner.

BDAG.en: instructor, teacher; corrector, one who disciplines.
BDAG.pt: instrutor, professor; corretor, aquele que disciplina.

DEFINITION: (a) to discipline, educate, train, (b) more severely: to chastise.
ORIGIN: From pais; to train up a child, i.e. Educate, or (by implication), discipline (by punishment).

BDAG.en: to provide instruction for informed and responsible living, educate; to assist in the development of a person’s ability to make appropriate choices, practice discipline, correct, give guidance; discipline w. punishment
BDAG.pt: fornecer instrução para uma vida informada e responsável, educar; auxiliar no desenvolvimento da capacidade de uma pessoa de fazer escolhas apropriadas, praticar disciplina, corrigir, dar orientação; disciplinar com punição

DEFINITION: from childhood, from early boyhood.
ORIGIN: Adverb (of source) from paidion; from infancy.

BDAG.en: from childhood.
BDAG.pt: desde a infância.

DEFINITION: a little child, an infant, little one.
ORIGIN: Neuter diminutive of pais; a childling (of either sex), i.e. (properly), an infant, or (by extension) a half-grown boy or girl; figuratively, an immature Christian.

BDAG.en: a child, normally below the age of puberty, child a very young child, infant, used of boys and girls; one who is open to instruction, child, fig. ext.; one who is treasured in the way a parent treasures a child, child, fig. ext.
BDAG.pt: uma criança, normalmente abaixo da puberdade, um bebê, criança muito jovem, usado para meninos e meninas; alguém aberto a instrução, criança, extensão figurada; alguém que é prezado como um pai prezaria um filho, criança, extensão figurada.

DEFINITION: a female slave, maidservant, maid, young girl.
ORIGIN: Feminine diminutive of pais; a girl, i.e. (specially), a female slave or servant.

BDAG.en: dim. of παῖς ‘girl’, in our lit. always of the slave class, female slave
BDAG.pt: diminutivo de παῖς 'menina', na nossa literatura sempre da classe escrava, escrava

DEFINITION: to play, sport (includes singing and dancing), play in the manner of children.
ORIGIN: From pais; to sport (as a boy).

BDAG.en: to engage in some activity for the sake of amusement, play, amuse oneself; play with someone.
BDAG.pt: engajar-se em alguma atividade por motivo de diversão, brincar, se divertir; brincar com alguém.

DEFINITION: (a) a male child, boy, (b) a male slave, servant; thus: a servant of God, especially as a title of the Messiah, (c) a female child, girl.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from paio; a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy), a girl, and (genitive case) a child; specially, a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God).
USAGE: child, maid(-en), (man) servant, son, young man.

BDAG.en: child. 1 a young pers. normally below the age of puberty, w. focus on age rather than social status, boy, youth; 2 one’s own immediate offspring, child as ‘son’ or ‘daughter’; 3 one who is committed in total obedience to another, slave, servant (of slaves and personal attendants; of those at a ruler’s court; of special relationships: humans as God’s servants, slaves; of Christ in his relation to God)
BDAG.pt: criança. 1 uma pessoa jovem normalmente abaixo da idade da puberdade, com foco na idade em vez do status social, menino, jovem; 2 sua própria descendência imediata, filho ou filha; 3 aquele que está totalmente obediente a outro, escravo, servo (de escravos e atendentes pessoais; daqueles na corte de um governante; de relações especiais: humanos como servos de Deus; de Cristo em sua relação com Deus)

DEFINITION: to strike, smite, sting.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than tupto); specially, to sting (as a scorpion).

BDAG.en: 1 to make violent contact by thrusting with someth., strike a w. a body part strike, hit; b w. sharp instruments strike, wound; c w. a stinger sting, of scorpions; 2 to inflict punishment, strike
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer contato violento empurrando com algo, golpear com uma parte do corpo, bater, atingir; b com instrumentos cortantes, ferir; c com um ferrão, picar (escorpiões); 2 infligir punição, golpear

DEFINITION: Pacatiana.
ORIGIN: Feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation; Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia.

DEFINITION: of old, long ago, in times past, former.
ORIGIN: Probably another form for palin (through the idea of retrocession); (adverbially) formerly, or (by relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient.
USAGE: any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to a point of time in the past, long ago, formerly; 2 pert. to a relatively long period of time, looking back fr. the present to a point of time in the past, for a long time; 3 pert. to a point of time within a relatively short time looking back from the present, already
BDAG.pt: 1 referente a um ponto no tempo passado, há muito tempo, antigamente; 2 referente a um período de tempo relativamente longo, olhando para trás a partir do presente até um ponto no passado, por muito tempo; 3 referente a um ponto no tempo dentro de um período relativamente curto olhando para trás a partir do presente, já

DEFINITION: old, ancient, not new or recent.
ORIGIN: From palai; antique, i.e. Not recent, worn out.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being in existence for a long time, old; 2 pert. to that which is obsolete or inferior because of being old, old, obsolete
BDAG.pt: 1 referente a existir por muito tempo, velho; 2 referente ao que está obsoleto ou inferior por ser velho, antigo, obsoleto

DEFINITION: oldness, obsoleteness.
ORIGIN: From palaios; antiquatedness.

BDAG.en: state of being superseded or obsolete, age, obsolescence
BDAG.pt: estado de estar substituído ou obsoleto, idade, obsolescência

DEFINITION: to make old, declare obsolete; pass: to grow old, become obsolete.
ORIGIN: From palaios; to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete.

BDAG.en: make old, declare/treat as obsolete; become old (often with the connotation of becoming useless)
BDAG.pt: tornar velho, declarar/tratar como obsoleto; tornar-se velho (muitas vezes com a conotação de se tornar inútil)

DEFINITION: wrestling, a wrestling bout; hence: a struggle, fight, conflict, contest.
ORIGIN: From pallo (to vibrate; another form for ballo); wrestling.

BDAG.en: engagement in a challenging contest (orig. ‘wrestling’), struggle against
BDAG.pt: engajamento em um concurso desafiador (originalmente 'luta'), luta contra

DEFINITION: a new birth, regeneration, renewal.
ORIGIN: From palin and genesis; (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration.

BDAG.en: state of being renewed, renewal (cosmic or eschatological sense); experience of a complete change of life, rebirth of a redeemed person
BDAG.pt: estado de ser renovado, renovação (sentido cósmico ou escatológico); experiência de uma mudança completa de vida, renascimento de uma pessoa redimida

DEFINITION: again, back, once more, further, on the other hand.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as pale (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand.

BDAG.en: back, again (return to a position/state or repetition); on the other hand, in turn; furthermore, thereupon (in a series/contrast)
BDAG.pt: de volta, de novo (retorno a uma posição/estado ou repetição); por outro lado, por sua vez; além disso, então (em uma série/contraste)

DEFINITION: all at once, all together.
ORIGIN: Dative case (adverb) of a compound of pas and plethos; in full multitude, i.e. Concertedly or simultaneously.

BDAG.en: all together (in unison, referring to a multitude)
BDAG.pt: todos juntos (em uníssono, referindo-se a uma multidão)

DEFINITION: very great, very much.
ORIGIN: From pas and polus; full many, i.e. Immense.

BDAG.en: very great (referring to extent)
BDAG.pt: muito grande (referente à extensão)

DEFINITION: Pamphylia, a Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pas and pura; every-tribal, i.e. Heterogeneous (chora being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Pamphylia, a province in the southern part of Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Panfília, uma província na parte sul da Ásia Menor

DEFINITION: an inn, khan, hotel.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed compound of pas and a derivative of dechomai; all-receptive, i.e. A public lodging-place (caravanserai or khan).

BDAG.en: inn, where a traveler may find a night’s lodging
BDAG.pt: estalagem, onde um viajante pode encontrar alojamento noturno

DEFINITION: an innkeeper, landlord, host.
ORIGIN: From the same as pandocheion; an innkeeper (warden of a caravanserai).

BDAG.en: inn-keeper
BDAG.pt: hospedeiro, estalajadeiro

DEFINITION: a festival assembly.
ORIGIN: From pas and a derivative of agora; a mass-meeting, i.e. (figuratively) universal companionship.

BDAG.en: an assemblage of many persons for a special occasion, festal gathering
BDAG.pt: uma assembleia de muitas pessoas para uma ocasião especial, ajuntamento festivo

DEFINITION: with one's whole household or family.
ORIGIN: Adverb from pas and oikos; with the whole family.

DEFINITION: complete armor, panoply.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pas and hoplon; full armor ("panoply").

BDAG.en: 1 the complete equipment of a heavy-armed soldier, full armor; 2 Purely metaphoric [full armor of God]
BDAG.pt: 1 o equipamento completo de um soldado de infantaria pesada, armadura completa; 2 Puramente metafórico [armadura de Deus]

DEFINITION: shrewdness, skill; hence: cunning, craftiness.
ORIGIN: From panougos; adroitness, i.e. (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry.

BDAG.en: cunning, craftiness, trickery, lit. ‘readiness to do anything’ (in an unfavorable sense)
BDAG.pt: astúcia, sagacidade, engano, literalmente 'prontidão para fazer qualquer coisa' (em sentido desfavorável)

DEFINITION: ready to do anything, crafty, skillful.
ORIGIN: From pas and ergon; all-working, i.e. Adroit (shrewd).

BDAG.en: clever, crafty, sly lit. ‘ready to do anything’ (in an unfavorable connotation)
BDAG.pt: esperto, ardiloso, astuto, literalmente 'pronto para fazer qualquer coisa' (com conotação desfavorável)

DEFINITION: from all sides, from all parts.
ORIGIN: Adverb (of source) from pantachou; from all directions.

BDAG.en: from every direction
BDAG.pt: de todas as direções

DEFINITION: everywhere, in all places.
ORIGIN: Genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of pas; universally.

BDAG.en: pert. to positions in any direction, everywhere
BDAG.pt: relativo a posições em qualquer direção, em todo lugar

DEFINITION: complete, entire, perfect, through all time.
ORIGIN: From pas and telos; full-ended, i.e. Entire (neuter as noun, completion).

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to meeting a very high standard of quality or completeness, completely, perfect, absolute; 2 pert. to unlimited duration of time, forever, for all time
BDAG.pt: 1 relativo ao cumprimento de um padrão muito alto de qualidade ou completude, completamente, perfeito, absoluto; 2 relativo à duração ilimitada de tempo, para sempre, para todo o tempo

DEFINITION: in every way, entirely, everywhere.
ORIGIN: Adverb (of manner) from pas; wholly.

BDAG.en: pert. to all possible considerations or positions, in every way
BDAG.pt: relativo a todas as considerações ou posições possíveis, de todas as maneiras

DEFINITION: from all sides, on all sides.
ORIGIN: Adverb (of source) from pas; from (i.e. On) all sides.

BDAG.en: pert. to extension fr. a source on all sides, from all directions, on all sides, entirely
BDAG.pt: relativo à extensão de uma fonte por todos os lados, de todas as direções, por todos os lados, inteiramente

DEFINITION: ruler of all, ruler of the universe, the almighty.
ORIGIN: From pas and kratos; the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign).

BDAG.en: the Almighty, All-Powerful, Omnipotent (One) only of God
BDAG.pt: o Todo-Poderoso, Todo-Potente, Onipotente (Aquele) somente de Deus

DEFINITION: always, at all times, ever.
ORIGIN: From pas and hote; every when, i.e. At all times.

BDAG.en: always, at all times
BDAG.pt: sempre, em todos os tempos

DEFINITION: wholly, entirely, in every way, by all means, certainly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from pas; entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event.
USAGE: by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely.

BDAG.en: 1 by all means, certainly, probably, doubtless; 2 totally, altogether; 4 at least
BDAG.pt: 1 por todos os meios, certamente, provavelmente, sem dúvida; 2 totalmente, completamente; 4 pelo menos

DEFINITION: gen: from; dat: beside, in the presence of; acc: alongside of.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition; properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of).
USAGE: above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side...by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with. In compounds it retains the same variety of application.

BDAG.en: from (origin, direction); by (agency); by (source/point of reference for asking/receiving/learning); beside/near (space); in the sight/judgment of; with (quality); during (time); in comparison to; because of; against/contrary to; less than/except for.
BDAG.pt: de/a partir de (origem, direção); por (agência); por/de (fonte/ponto de referência para perguntar/receber/aprender); ao lado de/perto de (espaço); à vista de/no julgamento de; com (qualidade); durante (tempo); em comparação com; por causa de; contra/contrário a; menos que/exceto por.

DEFINITION: to transgress, violate, depart, desert.
ORIGIN: From para and the base of basis; to go contrary to, i.e. Violate a command.

BDAG.en: to go aside, deviate from the way; to turn aside from an office; to transgress, break (a law, command) (actively or absolutely as 'to become a transgressor').
BDAG.pt: desviar-se, afastar-se do caminho; desviar-se de um ofício; transgredir, violar (uma lei, mandamento) (ativamente ou absolutamente como 'tornar-se um transgressor').

DEFINITION: to compare, arrive, land.
ORIGIN: From para and ballo; to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken.

BDAG.en: to throw to a point where an entity is positioned, throw to; to expose to hazard, give up; to put something beside something for the sake of comparison, compare; to come near to someone or something, approach.
BDAG.pt: lançar ou jogar para um ponto onde uma entidade está posicionada, jogar em; expor ao risco, entregar; colocar algo ao lado de algo para fins de comparação, comparar; aproximar-se de alguém ou algo, chegar perto.

DEFINITION: a transgression, overstepping, deviation.
ORIGIN: From parabaino; violation.

BDAG.en: act of deviating from an established boundary or norm, overstepping, transgression; violation of the law; Adam's transgression; become a transgressor.
BDAG.pt: ato de desviar-se de um limite ou norma estabelecida, ultrapassagem, transgressão; violação da lei; a transgressão de Adão; tornar-se um transgressor.

DEFINITION: a transgressor, law-breaker.
ORIGIN: From parabaino; a violator.

BDAG.en: violator, transgressor (of the law); sinner.
BDAG.pt: violador, transgressor (da lei); pecador.

DEFINITION: to urge, press, constrain by entreaties.
ORIGIN: From para and the middle voice of biazo; to force contrary to (nature), i.e. Compel (by entreaty).

BDAG.en: use force to accomplish something, urge strongly, prevail upon.
BDAG.pt: usar força para realizar algo, instar fortemente, persuadir/convencer.

DEFINITION: (a) a comparison, (b) a parable, often of those uttered by our Lord, (c) a proverb, an adage.
ORIGIN: From paraballo; a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage.

BDAG.en: something that serves as a model or example pointing beyond itself for later realization, type, figure; a narrative or saying designed to illustrate a truth especially through comparison or simile, comparison, illustration, parable, proverb, maxim.
BDAG.pt: algo que serve como modelo ou exemplo que aponta para além de si mesmo para realização posterior, tipo, figura; uma narrativa ou dito destinado a ilustrar uma verdade especialmente através de comparação ou símile, comparação, ilustração, parábola, provérbio, máxima.

DEFINITION: to expose myself to danger; to be adventuresome, reckless.
ORIGIN: From para and the middle voice of bouleuo; to misconsult, i.e. Disregard.

BDAG.en: be careless in relation to something, have no concern for one’s life.
BDAG.pt: ser descuidado em relação a algo, não se importar com a própria vida.

DEFINITION: a command, charge, injunction; a precept, rule of living.
ORIGIN: From paraggello; a mandate.

BDAG.en: an announcement respecting something that must be done, order, command, precept, advice, exhortation.
BDAG.pt: um anúncio sobre algo que deve ser feito, ordem, comando, preceito, conselho, exortação.

DEFINITION: to notify, command, charge, entreat solemnly.
ORIGIN: From para and the base of aggelos; to transmit a message, i.e. (by implication) to enjoin.

BDAG.en: to make an announcement about something that must be done, give orders, command, instruct, direct.
BDAG.pt: fazer um anúncio sobre algo que deve ser feito, dar ordens, comandar, instruir, dirigir.

DEFINITION: (a) to come on the scene, appear, come, (b) with words expressing destination: to present myself at, arrive at, reach.
ORIGIN: From para and ginomai; to become near, i.e. Approach (have arrived); by implication, to appear publicly.

BDAG.en: to be in movement so as to be present at a particular place, draw near, come, arrive, be present; to make a public appearance, appear; to come to help, stand by, come to the aid of
BDAG.pt: estar em movimento de modo a estar presente em um lugar particular, aproximar-se, vir, chegar, estar presente; fazer uma aparição pública, aparecer; vir em auxílio, apoiar, acorrer em ajuda

DEFINITION: to lead by, to pass by or away.
ORIGIN: From para and ago; to lead near, i.e. (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away.

BDAG.en: to move along and so leave a position, go away; to bring in something of a type foreign to the present condition or circumstance, bring in, introduce; to go past a reference point, pass by; to go out of existence, pass away, disappear
BDAG.pt: mover-se e assim deixar uma posição, afastar-se; trazer algo de um tipo estranho à condição ou circunstância presente, introduzir; passar por um ponto de referência, ultrapassar; deixar de existir, desaparecer, sumir

DEFINITION: to put to open shame, make a public example of, put to disgrace.
ORIGIN: From para and deigmatizo; to show alongside (the public), i.e. Expose to infamy.
USAGE: make a public example, put to an open shame.

BDAG.en: to disgrace someone publicly, expose, make an example of (often by punishment).
BDAG.pt: desgraçar alguém publicamente, expor, servir de exemplo (frequentemente por meio de punição).

DEFINITION: a park, a garden, a paradise.
ORIGIN: Of Oriental origin (compare pardec); a park, i.e. (specially), an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise").

BDAG.en: the garden of Eden, paradise; a transcendent place of blessedness, paradise.
BDAG.pt: o jardim do Éden, paraíso; um lugar transcendente de bem-aventurança, paraíso.

DEFINITION: to receive, accept, acknowledge.
ORIGIN: From para and dechomai; to accept near, i.e. Admit or (by implication) delight in.

BDAG.en: to acknowledge something to be correct, accept (a thing); to accept the presence of someone in a hospitable manner, receive, accept (a person)
BDAG.pt: reconhecer algo como correto, aceitar (uma coisa); aceitar a presença de alguém de maneira hospitaleira, receber, aceitar (uma pessoa)

DEFINITION: wrangling, constant arguing.
ORIGIN: From a compound of para and diatribo; misemployment, i.e. Meddlesomeness.

BDAG.en: waste of time in unimportant matters, useless occupation.
BDAG.pt: desperdício de tempo em assuntos sem importância, ocupação inútil.

DEFINITION: to hand over, pledge, hand down, deliver, commit, commend, betray, abandon.
ORIGIN: From para and didomi; to surrender, i.e yield up, intrust, transmit.
USAGE: betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison, recommend.

BDAG.en: hand over into the custody of (police and courts); surrender (military term); deliver up (often referring to arrest or betrayal, especially of Jesus); entrust for care or preservation; pass on/transmit (tradition); allow, permit (a condition to happen).
BDAG.pt: entregar à custódia (polícia e tribunais); render-se (termo militar); entregar (frequentemente referindo-se a prisão ou traição, especialmente de Jesus); confiar para cuidado ou preservação; transmitir (tradição); permitir, possibilitar (que algo aconteça).

DEFINITION: unexpected, strange, wonderful, astonishing.
ORIGIN: From para and doxa (in the sense of seeming); contrary to expectation, i.e. Extraordinary ("paradox").

BDAG.en: contrary to opinion or exceeding expectation, strange, wonderful, remarkable.
BDAG.pt: contrário à opinião ou excedendo a expectativa, estranho, maravilhoso, notável.

DEFINITION: a handing down or over, a tradition.
ORIGIN: From paradidomi; transmission, i.e. (concretely) a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law.

BDAG.en: handing down/over; surrender, arrest; the content of instruction that has been handed down, tradition (of teachings, commandments, narratives, etc.), especially the tradition preserved by the scribes and Pharisees or Christian teaching.
BDAG.pt: entrega/passagem; rendição, prisão; o conteúdo da instrução que foi transmitida, tradição (de ensinamentos, mandamentos, narrativas, etc.), especialmente a tradição preservada pelos escribas e fariseus ou o ensinamento cristão.

DEFINITION: to make jealous, provoke to jealously, provoke to anger.
ORIGIN: From para and zeloo; to stimulate alongside, i.e. Excite to rivalry.

BDAG.en: provoke to jealousy, make jealous (often in the sense of being untrue to God by turning to lesser divinities).
BDAG.pt: provocar ciúmes, fazer sentir ciúmes (muitas vezes no sentido de ser infiel a Deus ao se voltar para divindades inferiores).

DEFINITION: by the sea.
ORIGIN: From para and thalassa; along the sea, i.e. Maritime (lacustrine).

BDAG.en: (located) by the sea/lake, of places.
BDAG.pt: (localizado) junto ao mar/lago, de lugares.

DEFINITION: to look past, overlook, neglect.
ORIGIN: From para and theoreo; to overlook or disregard.

BDAG.en: to pay insufficient attention, with resulting deficiency in response, overlook, leave unnoticed, neglect.
BDAG.pt: prestar atenção insuficiente, com deficiência resultante na resposta, ignorar, deixar passar despercebido, negligenciar.

DEFINITION: a deposit, anything committed to one's charge or trust.
ORIGIN: From paratithemi; a deposit, i.e. (figuratively) trust.

BDAG.en: property entrusted to another, deposit (especially spiritual heritage entrusted to the orthodox Christian).
BDAG.pt: propriedade confiada a outro, depósito (especialmente herança espiritual confiada ao cristão ortodoxo).

DEFINITION: to admonish, advise, exhort.
ORIGIN: From para and aineo; to mispraise, i.e. Recommend or advise (a different course).

BDAG.en: to advise strongly, recommend, urge.
BDAG.pt: aconselhar fortemente, recomendar, instar.

DEFINITION: to beg off, make excuse, deprecate, refuse, reject, decline, shun, avoid.
ORIGIN: From para and the middle voice of aiteo; to beg off, i.e. Deprecate, decline, shun.

BDAG.en: to make a request, ask for, request (for oneself); to avert something by request or entreaty, excuse, decline, refuse, avoid, reject.
BDAG.pt: fazer um pedido, solicitar, pedir (para si mesmo); afastar algo por meio de pedido ou súplica, desculpar, recusar, evitar, rejeitar.

DEFINITION: to sit down beside, set beside.
ORIGIN: From para and kathizo; to sit down near.

BDAG.en: sit down beside someone.
BDAG.pt: sentar-se ao lado de alguém.

DEFINITION: (a) to send for, summon, invite, (b) to beseech, entreat, beg, (c) to exhort, admonish, (d) to comfort, encourage, console.
ORIGIN: From para and kaleo; to call near, i.e. Invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation).
USAGE: beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort(-ation), intreat, pray.

BDAG.en: to ask to come and be present (call to one's side); invite; summon to one's aid, call upon for help; to urge strongly, appeal to, urge, exhort, encourage; to make a strong request for something, implore, entreat; to instill someone with courage or cheer, comfort, encourage, cheer up; treat someone in an inviting or congenial manner (invite in, conciliate, be friendly to).
BDAG.pt: pedir que venha e esteja presente (chamar para o seu lado); convidar; convocar em auxílio, pedir ajuda; instar fortemente, apelar, exortar, encorajar; fazer um pedido veemente por algo, implorar, suplicar; infundir coragem ou alegria em alguém, consolar, encorajar, animar; tratar alguém de maneira convidativa ou amigável (convidar para entrar, conciliar, ser amigável).

DEFINITION: to cover (by hanging something beside), to hide.
ORIGIN: From para and kalupto; to cover alongside, i.e. Veil (figuratively).

BDAG.en: hide, conceal (figuratively).
BDAG.pt: esconder, ocultar (figurativamente).

DEFINITION: a trust or deposit.
ORIGIN: From a compound of para and katatithemi; something put down alongside, i.e. A deposit (sacred trust).

BDAG.en: something given for safekeeping, deposit.
BDAG.pt: algo dado para ser guardado em segurança, depósito.

DEFINITION: to be at hand, be present with, rest with.
ORIGIN: From para and keimai; to lie near, i.e. Be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy).

BDAG.en: to be present and ready for some purpose or action, be at hand, ready.
BDAG.pt: estar presente e pronto para algum propósito ou ação, estar à mão, estar pronto.

DEFINITION: a calling for, summons, hence: (a) exhortation, (b) entreaty, (c) encouragement, joy, gladness, (d) consolation, comfort.
ORIGIN: From parakaleo; imploration, hortation, solace.

BDAG.en: act of emboldening another (encouragement, exhortation); strong request, appeal, request; lifting of another’s spirits, comfort, consolation.
BDAG.pt: ato de encorajar outro (encorajamento, exortação); pedido veemente, apelo, solicitação; elevação do ânimo de outro, consolo, conforto.

DEFINITION: (a) an advocate, intercessor, (b) a consoler, comforter, helper, (c) Paraclete.
ORIGIN: An intercessor, consoler.

BDAG.en: advocate, lawyer, attorney, one who appears in another’s behalf, mediator, intercessor, helper
BDAG.pt: advogado, procurador, intercessor, aquele que defende os interesses de outro, mediador, auxiliar.

DEFINITION: a hearing amiss, by implication disobedience.
ORIGIN: From parakouo; inattention, i.e. (by implication) disobedience.

BDAG.en: refusal to listen and so be disobedient, unwillingness to hear, disobedience
BDAG.pt: recusa em ouvir e, consequentemente, em obedecer; relutância em escutar; desobediência.

DEFINITION: to accompany, follow closely, characterize, both lit. and met.; to investigate.
ORIGIN: From para and akoloutheo; to follow near, i.e. (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to.
USAGE: attain, follow, fully know, have understanding.

BDAG.en: to be closely associated w. someone viewed as an authority figure, follow lit. of direct discipleship; to be attendant upon, follow, accompany, attend; to conform to someone’s belief or practice by paying special attention, follow faithfully; to pay careful attention to someth. in a segment of time, follow a thing, follow a course of events, take note of
BDAG.pt: estar intimamente associado a alguém visto como autoridade, seguir literalmente no discipulado direto; estar presente, seguir, acompanhar, assistir; conformar-se à crença ou prática de alguém prestando atenção especial, seguir fielmente; prestar atenção cuidadosa a algo durante um período, seguir um assunto, acompanhar um curso de eventos, tomar nota de

DEFINITION: (a) to hear carelessly or incidentally, or to pretend not to hear, (b) to refuse to hear; to disobey, disregard.
ORIGIN: From para and akouo; to mishear, i.e. (by implication) to disobey.

BDAG.en: to listen to something when one is not personally addressed, overhear; to pay no attention to something that has been heard, ignore; refuse to listen to, disobey
BDAG.pt: ouvir algo sem ser endereçado pessoalmente, escutar sem querer; não dar atenção a algo que foi ouvido, ignorar; recusar-se a ouvir, desobedecer

DEFINITION: to stoop, peer in, look down, look intently.
ORIGIN: From para and kupto; to bend beside, i.e. Lean over (so as to peer within).

BDAG.en: to bend over for the purpose of looking, w. focus on satisfying one’s curiosity, take a look; to try to find out someth. intellectually, look (in, into) fig. ext. of 1
BDAG.pt: curvar-se com o propósito de olhar, com foco em satisfazer a curiosidade, dar uma olhada; tentar descobrir algo intelectualmente, investigar (dentro de algo) extensão figurada do primeiro sentido

DEFINITION: to take from, receive from, or: to take to, receive (apparently not used of money), admit, acknowledge; to take with me.
ORIGIN: From para and lambano; to receive near, i.e. Associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy, to assume an office; figuratively, to learn.

BDAG.en: take into close association, take with/along, take (along) to/into (a place), take someone aside (for private instruction), take (a wife) into one's home, take into custody, arrest, gain control of or receive jurisdiction over, take over, receive (a kingship, heritage), accept (Christ, the gospel, teaching)
BDAG.pt: tomar para associação íntima, levar junto, levar para (um lugar), chamar alguém para um lado (para instrução privada), receber (uma esposa) em casa, tomar sob custódia, prender, obter controle ou jurisdição sobre, assumir, receber (um reino, herança), aceitar (Cristo, o evangelho, ensinamento).

DEFINITION: to sail past or coast along.
ORIGIN: From para and the middle voice of lego (in its original sense); (specially), to lay one's course near, i.e. Sail past.

BDAG.en: coast along (a route)
BDAG.pt: navegar ao longo da costa (de um lugar).

DEFINITION: adjacent to the sea, on the coast.
ORIGIN: From para and hals; beside the salt (sea), i.e. Maritime.

BDAG.en: pert. to being (located) alongside the sea, the seacoast (as a noun)
BDAG.pt: pertencente ou situado ao lado do mar; o litoral (como substantivo).

DEFINITION: a change, variation, mutation.
ORIGIN: From a compound of para and allasso.
USAGE: transmutation (of phase or orbit), i.e. (figuratively) fickleness; variableness.

BDAG.en: change, variation
BDAG.pt: mudança, variação.

DEFINITION: to deceive, beguile, reason falsely, mislead.
ORIGIN: From para and logizomai; to misreckon, i.e. Delude.

BDAG.en: to deceive, delude; to reckon fraudulently, defraud, perh. distort
BDAG.pt: enganar, iludir; calcular fraudulentamente, defraudar, talvez distorcer

DEFINITION: afflicted with paralysis.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of paraluo; as if dissolved, i.e. "paralytic".

BDAG.en: lame person, paralytic (subst.)
BDAG.pt: pessoa coxa, paralítico (substantivo)

DEFINITION: to relax, enfeeble, weaken.
ORIGIN: From para and luo; to loosen beside, i.e. Relax (perfect passive participle, paralyzed or enfeebled).
USAGE: feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy.

BDAG.en: to cause to be feeble, undo, weaken, disable
BDAG.pt: causar debilidade, desfazer, enfraquecer, incapacitar

DEFINITION: to remain by, abide with; met: to persevere in.
ORIGIN: From para and meno; to stay near, i.e. Remain (literally, tarry; or figuratively, be permanent, persevere).

BDAG.en: remain, stay; to remain in a state or situation, remain, stay on; to continue in an official capacity, continue in an occupation/office; Continue in a state of being or quality
BDAG.pt: permanecer, ficar; permanecer em um estado ou situação, continuar; continuar em uma função oficial, prosseguir em uma ocupação/cargo; Continuar em um estado de ser ou qualidade

DEFINITION: to encourage, comfort, console, exhort.
ORIGIN: From para and the middle voice of a derivative of muthos; to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console.

BDAG.en: console, cheer up; console, comfort (especially in connection w. death or other tragic events)

DEFINITION: encouragement, comfort, consolation, exhortation.

BDAG.pt: encorajamento, conforto, consolação (aquilo que serve de encorajamento a quem está deprimido ou de luto)

DEFINITION: comfort, consolation, an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement.
ORIGIN: Neuter of paramuthia; consolation (properly, concretely).

BDAG.en: pert. to that which offers encouragement, esp. as consolation, means of consolation, alleviation
BDAG.pt: pertencente àquilo que oferece encorajamento, especialmente como consolo, meio de consolação, alívio

DEFINITION: to act contrary to law.

BDAG.pt: ilegalidade, maldade

DEFINITION: to embitter, provoke, irritate.

BDAG.en: to incite to anger, embitter, make angry, provoke. Pass. become embittered, be made angry. also without an acc., be disobedient, rebellious (toward God)
BDAG.pt: incitar à raiva, amargar, enfurecer, provocar. Passivo: tornar-se amargurado, ficar zangado. Também sem acusativo, ser desobediente, rebelde (contra Deus)

DEFINITION: a provocation, irritation, rebellion.
ORIGIN: From parapikraino; irritation.

BDAG.en: ‘embitterment’, then revolt, rebellion against God
BDAG.pt: “amarguramento”, depois revolta, rebelião contra Deus

DEFINITION: to fall away, fall back (into the unbelieving and godless ways of the old time).

BDAG.en: ‘fall beside’, then ‘go astray, miss’. Also abs. and in the sense to fail to follow through on a commitment, fall away, commit apostasy
BDAG.pt: “cair ao lado”, depois “perder o rumo, errar”. Também absoluto e no sentido de falhar no cumprimento de um compromisso, afastar-se, cometer apostasia

DEFINITION: to sail past (without stopping there).
ORIGIN: From para and pleo; to sail near.

DEFINITION: coming near, nearly resembling.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of para and the base of plesion (as adverb); close by, i.e. (figuratively) almost.

DEFINITION: similarly, in like manner, likewise.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the same as paraplesion; in a manner near by, i.e. (figuratively) similarly.

BDAG.en: similarly, likewise. in the sense in just the same way
BDAG.pt: semelhantemente, da mesma forma. No sentido de 'exatamente da mesma maneira'

DEFINITION: to go past, pass by, pass along by.
ORIGIN: From para and poreuomai; to travel near.

BDAG.en: 1 to move past a ref. point, go/pass by. 2 to make a trip, go (through)
BDAG.pt: 1 mover-se passando um ponto de referência, ir/passar por. 2 fazer uma viagem, ir (através)

DEFINITION: a falling away, lapse, slip, false step, trespass, sin.
ORIGIN: From parapipto; a side-slip (lapse or deviation), i.e. (unintentional) error or (wilful) transgression.

BDAG.en: in imagery of one making a false step so as to lose footing: a violation of moral standards, offense, wrongdoing, sin
BDAG.pt: na imagem de alguém dando um passo em falso de modo a perder o equilíbrio: uma violação dos padrões morais, ofensa, erro, pecado

DEFINITION: (lit: to flow past, glide past, hence) to be lost, perish, or merely: to drift away (fall away) from duty.
ORIGIN: From para and the alternate of rheo; to flow by, i.e. (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss).

BDAG.en: in imagery of flowing water (‘flow by’), be washed away, drift away
BDAG.pt: na imagem de água corrente ('fluir ao lado'), ser levado pela água, derivar

DEFINITION: marked amiss, marked at the side, marked with a sign.
ORIGIN: From para and the base of semaino; side-marked, i.e. Labelled (with a badge (figure-head) of a ship).

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being out of the ordinary, peculiar, odd. 2 pert. to being marked (on the side) so as to be distinguished, marked
BDAG.pt: 1 relativo a estar fora do comum, peculiar, estranho. 2 relativo a ser marcado (de lado) de modo a ser distinguido, marcado

DEFINITION: to prepare; mid: to prepare, make preparations.
ORIGIN: From para and a derivative of skeuos; to furnish aside, i.e. Get ready.

BDAG.en: to cause something to be ready, prepare, act and absolutely (used with Peter) desired to eat. While they were making preparations (sc. the meal), prepare oneself for something.
BDAG.pt: fazer com que algo esteja pronto, preparar, agir e absolutamente (usado com Pedro) desejou comer. Enquanto faziam os preparativos (ref. à refeição), preparar-se para algo.

DEFINITION: preparation, the day of preparation (for a Sabbath or feast).
ORIGIN: As if from paraskeuazo; readiness.

BDAG.en: preparation, specifically of a definite day, as the day of preparation for a festival; according to Israel’s usage it was Friday, on which day everything had to be prepared for the Sabbath. For Christians as well designated the sixth day of the week, Friday, and for Christians it is a fast day, as the day of Jesus’ death.
BDAG.pt: preparação, especificamente de um dia definido, como o dia de preparação para um festival; de acordo com o uso de Israel, era sexta-feira, dia em que tudo tinha de ser preparado para o sábado. Para os cristãos, designava o sexto dia da semana, sexta-feira, e é um dia de jejum, como o dia da morte de Jesus.

DEFINITION: to extend, prolong, continue.
ORIGIN: From para and teino (to stretch); to extend along, i.e. Prolong (in point of time).

BDAG.en: extend, prolong the speech.
BDAG.pt: estender, prolongar o discurso.

DEFINITION: to watch closely, to observe scrupulously.
ORIGIN: From para and tereo; to inspect alongside, i.e. Note insidiously or scrupulously.

BDAG.en: watch closely, observe carefully (active and middle forms); observe someone to see what the person does, watch (can take on the meaning watch maliciously, lie in wait for); stand guard, watch, guard the gates; carefully observe custom or tradition, observe scrupulously.
BDAG.pt: observar atentamente, vigiar cuidadosamente (formas ativa e média); observar alguém para ver o que a pessoa faz, vigiar (pode assumir o significado de vigiar maliciosamente, espreitar); montar guarda, vigiar, guardar os portões; observar cuidadosamente o costume ou a tradição, observar meticulosamente.

DEFINITION: observation, careful watching.
ORIGIN: From paratereo; inspection, i.e. Ocular evidence.

BDAG.en: act of watching or keeping an eye on someth. closely, observation. 2 act of following rules, observance of legal prescriptions, esp. of festivals
BDAG.pt: ato de vigiar ou manter um olho atento em algo de perto, observação. 2 ato de seguir regras, observância de prescrições legais, especialmente de festivais

DEFINITION: (a) to set (especially a meal) before, serve, (b) act. and mid: to deposit with, entrust to, (c) to bring forward, quote as evidence.
ORIGIN: From para and tithemi; to place alongside, i.e. Present (food, truth); by implication, to deposit (as a trust or for protection).
USAGE: allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before.

BDAG.en: place beside, place before; place something before someone, set before, frequently of food; set forth in teaching; entrust for safekeeping, give over, entrust, commend; cause something to happen to someone, do (to).
BDAG.pt: colocar ao lado, colocar à frente; colocar algo diante de alguém, servir, frequentemente de comida; apresentar no ensino; confiar para guarda, entregar, confiar, recomendar; fazer algo acontecer a alguém, fazer (a).

DEFINITION: to come by chance, chance to meet.

BDAG.en: happen to be near/present; anyone who comes by, those who happened to be there.
BDAG.pt: acontecer de estar perto/presente; qualquer um que passe, aqueles que por acaso estavam lá.

DEFINITION: adv. with force of adj: present, immediate, for the moment.

BDAG.en: on the spot, immediately, for the present (adverb); slight momentary trouble.
BDAG.pt: no local, imediatamente, por enquanto (advérbio); pequeno transtorno momentâneo.

DEFINITION: to turn aside, carry away, remove, cause to pass away; pass: to be misled, seduced.

BDAG.en: to convey someth. to a designated point, bring up; to take someth. away from a position, take/carry away; fig. lead or carry away fr. the path of truth, and so mislead; take away, remove
BDAG.pt: transportar algo a um ponto designado, trazer; tirar algo de uma posição, levar/carregar embora; figurativamente desviar ou levar para longe do caminho da verdade, e assim enganar; tirar, remover

DEFINITION: to be out of senses, be beside myself.

BDAG.en: spend the winter, to winter.

DEFINITION: wintering, spending the winter.

DEFINITION: instantly, immediately, on the spot.

DEFINITION: to be present, be near; to have come, arrived.

DEFINITION: brought in secretly, surreptitious.

BDAG.pt: pertinente a entrar em um grupo de maneira sorrateira, trazido secretamente, introduzido à força, esgueirado

DEFINITION: to enter secretly, come in by stealth.

BDAG.pt: entrar ao lado, esgueirar-se, entrar como questão secundária; Entrar com motivos indignos, entrar de mansinho

BDAG.pt: pertencente a ficar por um tempo em um lugar estranho ou estrangeiro, estar de passagem, residir temporariamente; em substantivo: estrangeiro, forasteiro, residente alienígena

DEFINITION: to pass by, pass away, pass out of sight; to be rendered void, become vain, neglect, disregard.
ORIGIN: From para and erchomai; to come near or aside, i.e. To approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causative) avert.

DEFINITION: a maiden, virgin; extended to men who have not known women.

BDAG.pt: alguém que nunca teve relações sexuais, virgem, pessoa casta; homem virgem, homem casto

DEFINITION: Parmenas, one of the original seven deacons at Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Probably by contraction for Parmenides (a derivative of a compound of para and meno); constant; Parmenas, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Parmenias, one of the seven appointees in Jerusalem.
BDAG.pt: Parmenas, um dos sete diáconos instituídos em Jerusalém.

DEFINITION: a passing by or through.
ORIGIN: From para and hodos; a by-road, i.e. (actively) a route.

BDAG.en: a way for travelers, passage, thoroughfare; the act of moving to a point of reference and continuing on one’s course, but with possibility of a stopover, passing by.
BDAG.pt: um caminho para viajantes, passagem, via; o ato de mover-se para um ponto de referência e continuar o curso, mas com possibilidade de uma parada, passando por.

DEFINITION: to dwell near, reside as a foreigner.

BDAG.pt: 1 habitar ou residir perto, morar nas proximidades, morar ao lado 2 habitar um lugar como estrangeiro, ser um estranho 3 também simplesmente habitar, viver em sem a conotação de ser um estranho

DEFINITION: a sojourning, a dwelling in a strange land.
ORIGIN: From paroikos; foreign residence.

BDAG.en: the state of being in a strange locality without citizenship, sojourn, stay, also in transf. sense of the foreign country itself; a cultic (Christian) group perceived as strangers, congregation, parish.
BDAG.pt: o estado de estar em um local estranho sem cidadania, estada, permanência, também no sentido transferido do próprio país estrangeiro; um grupo cultual (cristão) percebido como estranho, congregação, paróquia.

DEFINITION: foreign, alien, subst: a foreigner, sojourner.

BDAG.pt: estranho, estrangeiro, aquele que vive em um lugar que não é sua casa

DEFINITION: a cryptic saying, an allegory; a proverb, figurative discourse.

BDAG.pt: uma frase concisa, provérbio, ditado, máxima; uma comunicação breve contendo verdades destinadas a iniciados, um dito velado, uma figura de linguagem na qual ideias especialmente elevadas estão ocultas.

DEFINITION: given to wine, drunken, quarrelsome.
ORIGIN: From para and oinos; staying near wine, i.e. Tippling (a toper).

BDAG.en: pert. to one who is given to drinking too much wine, addicted to wine, drunken
BDAG.pt: relativo a quem tem o hábito de beber vinho em excesso, viciado em vinho, bêbado

DEFINITION: to have passed by.
ORIGIN: From para and oichomai (to depart); to escape along, i.e. Be gone.

BDAG.en: to be past, of time
BDAG.pt: estar passado, referindo-se ao tempo

DEFINITION: to resemble, be like.

BDAG.pt: ser muito semelhante a, assemelhar-se a

DEFINITION: like, similar.
ORIGIN: From para and homoios; alike nearly, i.e. Similar.

BDAG.en: pert. to being quite similar, like, similar.
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser bastante semelhante, como, similar.

DEFINITION: to sharpen, to stimulate, to provoke.

BDAG.pt: causar um estado de excitação interior, instigar, estimular, especialmente provocar a ira, irritar; passivo: tornar-se irritado, zangado

DEFINITION: stimulation, provocation, irritation, angry dispute.

BDAG.pt: 1 incitação à atividade, agitação, provocação 2 um estado de irritação expresso em argumento, desacordo acentuado 3 uma crise severa de uma doença, ataque de febre, especialmente no seu ponto alto: convulsão

DEFINITION: to provoke to anger, exasperate.

BDAG.en: make angry
BDAG.pt: irritar, enfurecer

DEFINITION: exasperation, wrath, irritation, indignation.

BDAG.en: state of being intensely provoked, angry mood, anger
BDAG.pt: estado de estar intensamente provocado, humor de raiva, raiva

DEFINITION: to stir up, incite, urge on.
ORIGIN: From para and otruno (to spur); to urge along, i.e. Stimulate (to hostility).

BDAG.en: stir up strong emotion against, arouse, incite someone
BDAG.pt: excitar forte emoção contra, despertar, incitar alguém

DEFINITION: (a) presence, (b) a coming, an arrival, advent, especially of the second coming of Christ.

BDAG.en: the state of being present at a place, presence; arrival as the first stage in presence, coming, advent; special technical sense of Christ's Messianic Advent in glory to judge the world at the end of this age
BDAG.pt: o estado de estar presente em um lugar, presença; chegada como primeiro estágio da presença, vinda, advento; sentido técnico especial da Vinda Messiânica de Cristo em glória para julgar o mundo no fim desta era

DEFINITION: prop: a dainty side-dish; meton: a plate, dish, platter.

DEFINITION: freedom, openness, especially in speech; boldness, confidence.

USAGE: bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly(-ness).

BDAG.en: a use of speech that conceals nothing and passes over nothing, outspokenness, frankness, plainness; openness to the public, before whom speaking and actions take place; a state of boldness and confidence, courage, confidence, boldness, fearlessness, esp. in the presence of persons of high rank
BDAG.pt: um uso da fala que não oculta nem omite nada, franqueza, abertura, clareza; abertura ao público, diante de quem ocorrem a fala e as ações; um estado de ousadia e confiança, coragem, confiança, audácia, destemor, especialmente na presença de pessoas de alta patente

DEFINITION: to speak freely, boldly; to be confident.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from parrhesia; to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor.

BDAG.en: express oneself freely, speak freely, openly, fearlessly; speak freely to or with someone; have the courage, venture; deal openly (boldly) with him
BDAG.pt: expressar-se livremente, falar livremente, abertamente, sem medo; falar livremente com alguém; ter a coragem, aventurar-se; lidar abertamente (ousadamente) com ele

DEFINITION: all, the whole, every kind of.
ORIGIN: Including all the forms of declension; apparently a primary word; all, any, every, the whole.
USAGE: all (manner of, means), alway(-s), any (one), X daily, + ever, every (one, way), as many as, + no(-thing), X thoroughly, whatsoever, whole, whosoever.

BDAG.en: each, every, any (pert. to totality with focus on its individual components); all people/men, everyone (w. a noun in the pl.); every one who, whoever; all (w. substantives); all things, everything (abs.); in all respects, in every way, altogether (adv.); any and every, every (any entity out of a totality)
BDAG.pt: cada um, todo, qualquer (pertencente à totalidade com foco em seus componentes individuais); todas as pessoas/homens, todos (no plural); todo aquele que, quem quer que seja; todos (com substantivos); todas as coisas, tudo (absoluto); em todos os aspectos, de todas as maneiras, completamente (advérbio); qualquer um e todo, cada um (qualquer entidade de uma totalidade)

DEFINITION: the Passover, the Passover supper or lamb.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare pecach); the Passover (the meal, the day, the festival or the special sacrifices connected with it).

BDAG.en: an annual Israelite festival commemorating Israel’s exodus from Egypt, the Passover; the lamb sacrificed for observance of the Passover, the Passover lamb; the Passover meal; in later Christian usage the Easter festival.
BDAG.pt: um festival anual israelita que comemora o êxodo de Israel do Egito, a Páscoa; o cordeiro sacrificado para a observância da Páscoa, o cordeiro pascal; a refeição de Páscoa; no uso cristão posterior, o festival da Páscoa (Easter).

DEFINITION: to be acted upon in a certain way, either good or bad; to experience ill treatment, suffer.
ORIGIN: Including the forms patho (path'-o), and pentho (pen'-tho), used only in certain tenses for it apparently a primary verb; to experience a sensation or impression (usually painful).

BDAG.en: to experience something, be treated (passive idea corresponding to active idea in ποιέω) of everything that befalls a person, whether good or ill. Developed usage leans toward unfavorable sense (suffer, endure). Also used to mean suffer death/be killed.
BDAG.pt: experimentar algo, ser tratado (ideia passiva correspondente à ideia ativa em ποιέω) de tudo o que acontece a uma pessoa, seja bom ou mau. O uso desenvolvido inclina-se para o sentido desfavorável (sofrer, suportar). Também usado no sentido de sofrer a morte/ser morto.

DEFINITION: Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; Patara, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Patara (a city in Lycia, on the southwest coast of Asia Minor).
BDAG.pt: Patara (uma cidade na Lícia, na costa sudoeste da Ásia Menor).

DEFINITION: to smite, strike (as with a sword), smite to death, afflict.
ORIGIN: Probably prolongation from paio; to knock (gently or with a weapon or fatally).

BDAG.en: to physically strike a blow, strike, hit; to inflict something disastrous, strike (figuratively); strike down, slay.
BDAG.pt: desferir fisicamente um golpe, bater, atingir; infligir algo desastroso, ferir (figuradamente); golpear mortalmente, matar.

DEFINITION: to tread, trample upon.
ORIGIN: From a derivative probably of paio (meaning a "path"); to trample (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to tread (on) with feet; to tread heavily with feet, trample (with destructive intent); move on foot, walk.
BDAG.pt: pisar com os pés; pisar com força com os pés, esmagar (com intenção destrutiva); mover-se a pé, andar.

DEFINITION: father, (Heavenly) Father, ancestor, elder, senior.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a "father" (literally or figuratively, near or more remote).

BDAG.en: the immediate biological ancestor, father; one from whom one is descended, forefather, ancestor; one who provides moral and intellectual upbringing, father; a title of respectful address, father; revered deceased persons with whom one shares beliefs or traditions, fathers, ancestors; the supreme deity, who is responsible for the origin and care of all that exists, Father, Parent; Father of Jesus Christ.
BDAG.pt: o ancestral biológico imediato, pai; alguém de quem se descende, antepassado, ancestral; aquele que provê educação moral e intelectual, pai; um título de endereço respeitoso, pai; pessoas falecidas reverenciadas com quem se compartilham crenças ou tradições, pais, ancestrais; a divindade suprema, responsável pela origem e cuidado de tudo o que existe, Pai, Progenitor; Pai de Jesus Cristo.

DEFINITION: Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean sea, south-west of Ephesus.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Patmus, an islet in the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean Sea, famous for the tradition that John had his ‘revelation’ here.
BDAG.pt: Patmos, uma pequena ilha rochosa no Mar Egeu, famosa pela tradição de que João teve sua 'revelação' ali.

DEFINITION: a patricide, a murderer of his father.
ORIGIN: From pater and the same as the latter part of metraloias; a parricide.

BDAG.en: one who kills his father, a patricide
BDAG.pt: aquele que mata seu pai, um parricida

DEFINITION: lineage, ancestry; a family, tribe.
ORIGIN: As if feminine of a derivative of pater; paternal descent, i.e. (concretely) a group of families or a whole race (nation).

BDAG.en: people linked over a relatively long period of time by line of descent to a common progenitor, family, clan, relationship; a relatively large body of people existing as a totality at a given moment and linked through ancestry and sociopolitical interests, people, nation; a division of a total people entity existing at a given moment, family
BDAG.pt: povo ligado por um período de tempo relativamente longo por descendência a um progenitor comum, família, clã, parentesco; um corpo relativamente grande de pessoas existindo como uma totalidade em um dado momento e ligadas por ancestralidade e interesses sociopolíticos, povo, nação; uma divisão de uma entidade total de povo existente em um dado momento, família

DEFINITION: a patriarch, head or founder of a family.
ORIGIN: From patria and archo; a progenitor ("patriarch").

BDAG.en: prime ancestor of a national entity, father of a nation, patriarch, of Hebr. patriarchs; ancestor
BDAG.pt: ancestral primordial de uma entidade nacional, pai de uma nação, patriarca, dos patriarcas hebraicos; ancestral

DEFINITION: ancestral, paternal, belonging to the fathers (ancestors).
ORIGIN: From pater; paternal, i.e. Ancestral.

BDAG.en: pert. to one’s ancestors, derived from / handed down by one’s father, paternal
BDAG.pt: pertencente aos seus antepassados, derivado de / transmitido pelo pai, paterno

DEFINITION: fatherland, one's native place.
ORIGIN: From parasemos; a father-land, i.e. Native town; (figuratively) heavenly home.

BDAG.en: 1. a relatively large geographical area associated with one’s familial connections and personal life, fatherland, homeland. 2. a relatively restricted area as locale of one’s immediate family and ancestry, home town, one’s own part of the country.
BDAG.pt: 1. uma área geográfica relativamente grande associada às suas conexões familiares e vida pessoal, pátria, terra natal. 2. uma área relativamente restrita como local da família imediata e ancestralidade, cidade natal, sua própria parte do país.

DEFINITION: "father's life", Patrobas, a Christian.
ORIGIN: Perhaps a contraction for Patrobios (a compound of pater and bios); father's life; Patrobas, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Patrobas recipient of a greeting.
BDAG.pt: Patrobas, destinatário de uma saudação.

DEFINITION: handed down by (from) one's ancestors, inherited.
ORIGIN: From pater and a derivative of paradidomi (in the sense of handing over or down); traditionary.

BDAG.en: inherited, handed down from one’s father or forefathers/ancestors
BDAG.pt: herdado, transmitido do pai ou dos antepassados/ancestrais

DEFINITION: of one's fathers, received from one's fathers.
ORIGIN: From pater; paternal, i.e. Hereditary.

BDAG.en: paternal, belonging to one’s father, inherited or coming from one’s father/ancestors.
BDAG.pt: paterno, pertencente ao pai, herdado ou vindo do pai/ancestrais.

DEFINITION: (Sergius) Paulus (a Roman proconsul), also Paul (an apostle).
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; (little; but remotely from a derivative of pauo, meaning the same); Paulus, the name of a Roman and of an apostle.

BDAG.en: Paul, the apostle of Jesus Christ; bore the Israelite name Saul as well as the Graeco-Roman Paul, probably born in Tarsus, Roman citizen. Educated in Mosaic tradition, initially a zealous Pharisee and foe of Christians, his perspective changed by a vision of Jesus Christ. Most prominent of the apostles to the nations/gentiles. Worked in Arabia, Syria, and Cilicia; traveled through Cyprus, Asia Minor, Macedonia, and Greece; planned a journey to Spain, but was arrested in Jerusalem. Reached Rome as a prisoner and was probably executed there.
BDAG.pt: Paulo, o apóstolo de Jesus Cristo; carregava o nome israelita Saulo, bem como o greco-romano Paulo, provavelmente nascido em Tarso, cidadão romano. Educado na tradição mosaica, inicialmente um fariseu zeloso e inimigo dos cristãos, sua perspectiva mudou por uma visão de Jesus Cristo. O mais proeminente dos apóstolos às nações/gentios. Trabalhou na Arábia Nabateia, Síria e Cilícia; viajou por Chipre, Ásia Menor, Macedônia e Grécia; planejou uma jornada missionária para a Espanha, mas foi preso em Jerusalém. Chegou a Roma como prisioneiro e foi provavelmente executado lá.

DEFINITION: (a) act: to cause to cease, restrain, hinder, (b) mid: to cease, stop, leave off.
ORIGIN: A primary verb ("pause"); to stop (transitively or intransitively), i.e. Restrain, quit, desist, come to an end.

BDAG.en: To cause something to stop or keep something from happening, stop, cause to stop, quiet, relieve, cure. To cease doing something, stop (oneself), cease. To cease from, have done with something. Absolutive: stop, cease, have finished, be at an end. Also of time elapse, come to an end.
BDAG.pt: Fazer algo parar ou impedir que algo aconteça, parar, fazer parar, acalmar, aliviar, curar. Cessar de fazer algo, parar (a si mesmo), cessar. Abster-se de, dar por findo com algo. Absoluto: parar, cessar, ter terminado, chegar ao fim. Também de o tempo passar, chegar ao fim.

DEFINITION: Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Paphus, a place in Cyprus.

BDAG.en: Paphos (Nea Paphos), a city on the west coast of Cyprus, the seat of the Roman proconsul. Paul visited the city on his so-called first missionary journey.
BDAG.pt: Pafos (Nea Pafos), uma cidade na costa oeste de Chipre, sede do procônsul romano. Paulo visitou a cidade em sua chamada primeira viagem missionária.

DEFINITION: to fatten, thicken; pass. fig: to become stupid, dull, unfeeling.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of pegnumi (meaning thick); to thicken, i.e. (by implication) to fatten (figuratively, stupefy or render callous).

BDAG.en: make fat, well-nourished. Pass. in act. sense become fat. fig. make impervious (orig. to water), make gross, dull. Pass. in act. sense become dull
BDAG.pt: Engordar, bem nutrido. Passivo no sentido ativo: tornar-se gordo. Figurado: tornar impermeável (originalmente à água), tornar grosseiro, obtuso. Passivo no sentido ativo: tornar-se obtuso

DEFINITION: a shackle, fetter for the feet.
ORIGIN: Ultimately from pous; a shackle for the feet.

BDAG.en: Fetter, shackle (in plural often with ἁλύσεις).
BDAG.pt: Grilhão, algema (no plural frequentemente com ἁλύσεις).

DEFINITION: level, low-lying, flat.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of pous (meaning the ground); level (as easy for the feet).

BDAG.en: Flat, level, either as opposed to 'steep', 'uneven' or in contrast to 'high', 'elevated'.
BDAG.pt: Plano, nivelado, seja em oposição a 'íngreme', 'irregular' ou em contraste com 'alto', 'elevado'.

DEFINITION: to travel on foot or by land.
ORIGIN: From the same as peze; to foot a journey, i.e. Travel by land.

BDAG.en: Travel by land in contrast to a sea-journey. The original meaning travel on foot is not impossible.
BDAG.pt: Viajar por terra em contraste com uma viagem marítima. O significado original de viajar a pé não é impossível.

DEFINITION: on foot, by land.
ORIGIN: Dative case feminine of a derivative of pous (as adverb); foot-wise, i.e. By walking.

BDAG.en: Adverb: by land (opposed to by ship), originally 'on foot'.
BDAG.pt: Advérbio: por terra (em oposição a de navio), originalmente 'a pé'.

DEFINITION: to obey one in authority, conform to advice, obey, follow.
ORIGIN: From a compound of peitho and archo; to be persuaded by a ruler, i.e. (genitive case) to submit to authority; by analogy, to conform to advice.

BDAG.en: Obey (God, the word of righteousness). Figuratively of heavenly bodies that obey the Creator. Absolutive: be obedient.
BDAG.pt: Obedecer (a Deus, à palavra da justiça). Figurativamente dos corpos celestes que obedecem ao Criador. Absoluto: ser obediente.

DEFINITION: persuasive, enticing, skilful.
ORIGIN: From peitho; persuasive.

BDAG.en: Persuasive, persuasive words of wisdom.
BDAG.pt: Persuasivo, palavras persuasivas de sabedoria.

DEFINITION: to persuade, to have confidence.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to convince (by argument, true or false); by analogy, to pacify or conciliate (by other fair means); reflexively or passively, to assent (to evidence or authority), to rely (by inward certainty).
USAGE: agree, assure, believe, have confidence, be (wax) conflent, make friend, obey, persuade, trust, yield.

BDAG.en: act. 1 cause to come to a particular point of view or course of action. a convince. b persuade, appeal to, also in an unfavorable sense cajole, mislead. c win over, strive to please. d conciliate, pacify, set at ease/rest. 2 The 2 pf. (w. plpf.) has pres. mng. a depend on, trust in. b be convinced, be sure, certain. 3 pass. and mid. a be persuaded, believe. b obey, follow. c be persuaded by someone, take someone’s advice or obey, follow someone. 4 perf. pass. to attain certainty in ref. to something, be convinced, certain
BDAG.pt: Ativo: 1 Fazer alguém chegar a um ponto de vista ou curso de ação particular. a convencer. b persuadir, apelar, também em sentido desfavorável: bajular, enganar. c conquistar, esforçar-se para agradar. d conciliar, pacificar, tranquilizar. 2 O 2. perfeito (com pretérito mais-que-perfeito) tem sentido presente: a confiar, depender de. b estar convencido, certo, seguro. 3 Passivo e médio: a ser persuadido, crer. b obedecer, seguir. c ser persuadido por alguém, aceitar o conselho ou obedecer/seguir alguém. 4 Perfeito passivo: atingir a certeza em referência a algo, estar convencido, certo

DEFINITION: to be hungry, needy, desire earnestly.
ORIGIN: From the same as penes (through the idea of pinching toil; "pine"); to famish (absolutely or comparatively); figuratively, to crave.

BDAG.en: 1 to feel the pangs of lack of food, hunger, be hungry. 2 desire someth. strongly, hunger for someth. fig. ext. of 1
BDAG.pt: 1 Sentir as dores da falta de alimento, ter fome, estar faminto. 2 Desejar algo fortemente, ter fome de algo (sentido figurado, extensão do 1)

DEFINITION: a trial, experiment, attempt.
ORIGIN: From the base of peran (through the idea of piercing); a test, i.e. Attempt, experience.

BDAG.en: an effort to accomplish something, attempt, trial, experiment, act. sense; experience won by attempting something, experience, pass. sense.
BDAG.pt: um esforço para realizar algo, tentativa, ensaio, experimento, sentido ativo; experiência obtida ao tentar algo, experiência, sentido passivo.

DEFINITION: to make proof of, to attempt, test, tempt.
ORIGIN: From peira; to test (objectively), i.e. Endeavor, scrutinize, entice, discipline.
USAGE: assay, examine, go about, prove, tempt(-er), try.

BDAG.en: to make an effort to do something, try, attempt; to endeavor to discover the nature or character of something by testing, try, make trial of, put to the test; to attempt to entrap through a process of inquiry, test; to entice to improper behavior, tempt.
BDAG.pt: fazer um esforço para fazer algo, tentar, experimentar; esforçar-se para descobrir a natureza ou o caráter de algo por meio de teste, experimentar, pôr à prova; tentar enredar através de um processo de inquérito, testar; incitar a um comportamento impróprio, tentar/seduzir (no sentido de levar ao pecado).

DEFINITION: (a) trial, probation, testing, being tried, (b) temptation, (c) calamity, affliction.
ORIGIN: From peirazo; a putting to proof (by experiment (of good), experience (of evil), solicitation, discipline or provocation); by implication, adversity.

BDAG.en: an attempt to learn the nature or character of something, test, trial; an attempt to make one do something wrong, temptation, enticement to sin.
BDAG.pt: uma tentativa de aprender a natureza ou o caráter de algo, teste, provação; uma tentativa de fazer alguém fazer algo errado, tentação, incitação ao pecado.

DEFINITION: mid: to try, attempt, endeavor.
ORIGIN: From peira; to test (subjectively), i.e. (reflexively) to attempt.

BDAG.en: to try to do someth., try, attempt, endeavor; to have an experience, to experience.
BDAG.pt: tentar fazer algo, tentar, experimentar, esforçar-se; ter uma experiência, experimentar.

DEFINITION: persuasion, conviction, a yielding to persuasion.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of peitho; persuadableness, i.e. Credulity.

BDAG.en: persuasion.
BDAG.pt: persuasão.

DEFINITION: the deep, the deep sea.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; deep or open sea, i.e. The main.

BDAG.en: open sea (as opposed to stretch of water near land), the open sea, the depths (of the sea); independent part of a whole body of water, sea.
BDAG.pt: mar aberto (em oposição à faixa de água perto da terra), o mar aberto, as profundezas (do mar); parte independente de um corpo inteiro de água, mar.

DEFINITION: to cut off with an ax, to behead.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of plesso (meaning an axe); to chop off (the head), i.e. Truncate.

BDAG.en: behead (with an ax), normally an act of capital punishment.
BDAG.pt: decapitar (com um machado), normalmente um ato de pena capital.

DEFINITION: the fifth.
ORIGIN: From pente; fifth.

BDAG.en: ordinal fifth; the fifth day.
BDAG.pt: o quinto ordinal; o quinto dia.

DEFINITION: to send, transmit, permit to go, put forth.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to dispatch (from the subjective view or point of departure, whereas hiemi (as a stronger form of eimi) refers rather to the objective point or terminus ad quem, and stello denotes properly, the orderly motion involved), especially on a temporary errand; also to transmit, bestow, or wield.

BDAG.en: to dispatch someone, usually for purposes of communication, send; to dispatch something through an intermediary, send.
BDAG.pt: despachar alguém, geralmente para fins de comunicação, enviar; despachar algo através de um intermediário, mandar.

DEFINITION: one who works for his living; a laborer, poor man.
ORIGIN: From a primary peno (to toil for daily subsistence); starving, i.e. Indigent.

BDAG.en: pert. to being obliged to work for a living, but not being reduced to begging, poor, needy.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à obrigação de trabalhar para viver, mas sem ser reduzido à mendicância, pobre, necessitado.

DEFINITION: a mother-in-law.
ORIGIN: Feminine of pentheros; a wife's mother.

BDAG.en: mother-in-law.
BDAG.pt: sogra.

DEFINITION: a father-in-law.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a wife's father.

BDAG.en: father-in-law.
BDAG.pt: sogro.

DEFINITION: to mourn, lament, feel guilt.
ORIGIN: From penthos; to grieve (the feeling or the act).

BDAG.en: to experience sadness as the result of some condition or circumstance, be sad, grieve, mourn; to engage in mourning for one who is dead, mourn over.
BDAG.pt: experimentar tristeza como resultado de alguma condição ou circunstância, estar triste, lamentar, chorar; engajar-se em luto por alguém que morreu, lamentar sobre.

DEFINITION: mourning, sorrow, sadness, grief.
ORIGIN: Strengthened from the alternate of pascho; grief.

BDAG.en: sorrow as experience or expression, grief, sadness, mourning
BDAG.pt: dor como experiência ou expressão, aflição, tristeza, luto

DEFINITION: needy, poor.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from the base of penes; necessitous.

BDAG.en: pert. to being in need of things relating to livelihood, poor, needy.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à necessidade de coisas relativas ao sustento, pobre, necessitado.

DEFINITION: five times.
ORIGIN: Multiplicative adverb from pente; five times.

BDAG.en: five times.
BDAG.pt: cinco vezes.

DEFINITION: five thousand.
ORIGIN: From pentakis and chilioi; five times a thousand.

BDAG.en: five thousand.
BDAG.pt: cinco mil.

DEFINITION: five hundred.
ORIGIN: From pente and hekaton; five hundred.

BDAG.en: five hundred.
BDAG.pt: quinhentos.

DEFINITION: five.
ORIGIN: A primary number; "five".

BDAG.en: five.
BDAG.pt: cinco.

DEFINITION: the fifteenth.
ORIGIN: From pente and kai and dekatos; five and tenth.

BDAG.en: fifteenth
BDAG.pt: décimo quinto

DEFINITION: fifty.
ORIGIN: Multiplicative of pente; fifty.

BDAG.en: fifty
BDAG.pt: cinquenta

DEFINITION: fiftieth, Pentecost, the second of the three great Jewish feasts.
ORIGIN: Feminine of the ordinal of pentekonta; fiftieth (hemera being implied) from Passover, i.e. The festival of "Pentecost".

BDAG.en: Pentecost (the festival celebrated on the fiftieth day after Passover)
BDAG.pt: Pentecostes (o festival celebrado no quinquagésimo dia após a Páscoa)

DEFINITION: confidence, trust, reliance.
ORIGIN: From the perfect of the alternate of pascho; reliance.

BDAG.en: trust, confidence (in others or in oneself); assurance about an outcome
BDAG.pt: confiança, segurança (em outros ou em si mesmo); certeza sobre um resultado

DEFINITION: indeed (adds force to the preceding word).
ORIGIN: From the base of peran; an enclitic particle significant of abundance (thoroughness), i.e. Emphasis; much, very or ever.

BDAG.en: enclitic particle, with intensive and extensive force
BDAG.pt: partícula enclítica, com força intensiva e extensiva

DEFINITION: over, on the other side, beyond.
ORIGIN: Apparently accusative case of an obsolete derivative of peiro (to "pierce"); through (as adverb or preposition), i.e. Across.

BDAG.en: on the other side (marker of a position across from something else, with intervening space); (as proper name) Perea
BDAG.pt: do outro lado (marcador de posição do outro lado de algo, com espaço intermediário); (como nome próprio) Pereia

DEFINITION: (a) a boundary, limit, extremity, (b) an end, conclusion.
ORIGIN: From the same as peran; an extremity.

BDAG.en: limit, end, boundary; the ends, limits (of the earth/world)
BDAG.pt: limite, fim, fronteira; as extremidades, limites (da terra/mundo)

DEFINITION: Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia.
ORIGIN: From purgos; fortified; Pergamus, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Pergamus or Pergamum, an important city in Mysia, in northwest Asia Minor.
BDAG.pt: Pérgamo ou Pérgamo, uma cidade importante na Mísia, noroeste da Ásia Menor.

DEFINITION: Perga, a city on the river Cestrus in the Roman province Pamphylia.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as Pergamos; a tower; Perga, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Perga, a city in Pamphylia, near the south coast of Asia Minor.
BDAG.pt: Perge, uma cidade na Panfília, perto da costa sul da Ásia Menor.

DEFINITION: about, concerning, around (denotes place, cause or subject).
ORIGIN: From the base of peran; properly, through (all over), i.e. Around; figuratively with respect to; used in various applications, of place, cause or time (with the genitive case denoting the subject or occasion or superlative point; with the accusative case the locality, circuit, matter, circumstance or general period).
USAGE: (there-)about, above, against, at, on behalf of, X and his company, which concern, (as) concerning, for, X how it will go with, ((there-, where-)) of, on, over, pertaining (to), for sake, X (e-)state, (as) touching, (where-)by (in), with. In comparative, it retains substantially the same meaning of circuit (around), excess (beyond), or completeness (through).

BDAG.en: Prep. with gen. and acc., generally meaning 'round about'; with gen. denotes object/person to which an activity/inward process refers (about, concerning); also used adverbially (finally, further(more)); with acc. generally refers to position (around, near), time (about, near), being occupied with, or regard/respect to.
BDAG.pt: Preposição com genitivo e acusativo, significando geralmente 'ao redor de'; com genitivo denota o objeto/pessoa a que uma atividade/processo interno se refere (sobre, a respeito de); também usada adverbialmente (finalmente, além disso); com acusativo refere-se geralmente à posição (ao redor, perto), tempo (por volta de, perto de), estar ocupado com, ou em relação/no que diz respeito a.

DEFINITION: to lead or carry about (or around), go about, traverse.
ORIGIN: From peri and ago; to take around (as a companion); reflexively, to walk around.

BDAG.en: To take or bring along, lead around (trans.); to travel about in various directions, go around, go about (intrans.).
BDAG.pt: Levar ou trazer consigo, conduzir ao redor (transitivo); viajar em várias direções, ir ao redor, circular (intransitivo).

DEFINITION: (a) to strip off, strip from, take away, (b) to cast off, cut adrift, cast loose.
ORIGIN: From peri and haireomai (including its alternate); to remove all around, i.e. Unveil, cast off (anchor); figuratively, to expiate.

BDAG.en: To take away from around something, take away, remove; to do away with, take away, remove.
BDAG.pt: Tirar de ao redor de algo, remover, retirar; abolir, tirar, eliminar.

DEFINITION: to flash (gleam) around like lightning.
ORIGIN: From peri and astrapto; to flash all around, i.e. Envelop in light.

BDAG.en: To shine brightly on an area that is all around a person, shine around (trans.); to shine brightly, shine (intrans.).
BDAG.pt: Brilhar intensamente sobre uma área que está ao redor de uma pessoa, cercar de luz (transitivo); brilhar intensamente, resplandecer (intransitivo).

DEFINITION: to cast around, wrap a garment about, put on; hence mid: to put on to myself, clothe myself, dress; to draw (a line).
ORIGIN: From peri and ballo; to throw all around, i.e. Invest (with a palisade or with clothing).
USAGE: array, cast about, clothe(-d me), put on.

BDAG.en: to encompass by erecting someth. around, lay, put around; to put on, esp. of articles of clothing, put on; to envelop someone in torture, thereby involving the pers. in misfortune
BDAG.pt: cercar erigindo algo ao redor, colocar, pôr em volta; vestir, especialmente artigos de vestuário, pôr (roupa); envolver alguém em tortura, envolvendo a pessoa em infortúnio

DEFINITION: to look around on, survey.
ORIGIN: From peri and blepo; to look all around.

DEFINITION: a wrapper, mantle, veil, cloak, covering.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of periballo; something thrown around one, i.e. A mantle, veil.

BDAG.en: an article of apparel that covers much of the body, covering, wrap, cloak, robe
BDAG.pt: uma peça de vestuário que cobre grande parte do corpo, cobertura, embrulho, capa, manto

DEFINITION: to bind (tie) around.
ORIGIN: peri and deo; to bind around one, i.e. Enwrap.
