BDAG.en: bind/wrap around something with something
BDAG.pt: atar/enrolar algo com algo

DEFINITION: to overdo, be a busybody, waste labor about (a thing).
ORIGIN: From peri and ergazomai; to work all around, i.e. Bustle about (meddle).

BDAG.en: to be intrusively busy, be a busybody, meddler; concern oneself about something
BDAG.pt: estar ocupado intrometidamente, ser intrometido, bisbilhoteiro; ocupar-se com algo

DEFINITION: of persons: over-careful; curious, meddling, a busy-body; of things: over-wrought; superfluous; curious, uncanny; subst: curious arts, magic.
ORIGIN: From peri and ergon; working all around, i.e. Officious (meddlesome, neuter plural magic).

BDAG.en: pert. to paying attention to matters that do not concern one, of persons, meddlesome, officious, curious, subst. a busybody; pert. to undue or misdirected curiosity, as in the practice of magic, belonging to magic
BDAG.pt: relativo a prestar atenção a assuntos que não lhe dizem respeito, de pessoas, intrometido, bisbilhoteiro, curioso, subst. um metidiço; relativo a curiosidade indevida ou mal direcionada, como na prática da magia, pertencente à magia

DEFINITION: to go around, move about, visit; to make a circuit, tack (as a ship).
ORIGIN: From peri and erchomai (including its alternate); to come all around, i.e. Stroll, vacillate, veer.
USAGE: fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about.

BDAG.en: to go about in various directions, go about, go from place to place; go around a reference point, make a circuit
BDAG.pt: andar em várias direções, vaguear, ir de lugar em lugar; contornar um ponto de referência, fazer um circuito

DEFINITION: (a) to contain (of a book containing subject matter); hence: it stands (has its content) thus, (b) to encompass, surround, get hold of, seize.
ORIGIN: From peri and echo; to hold all around, i.e. Include, clasp (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to enclose on all sides, surround, encircle; to take hold of completely, seize (of emotions/circumstances); to have something as content, contain (of a document)
BDAG.pt: cercar por todos os lados, rodear, circundar; tomar conta completamente, apoderar-se (de emoções/circunstâncias); conter algo (em um documento)

DEFINITION: to gird round; mid: to gird myself, generally for active work or travel.
ORIGIN: From peri and zonnumi; to gird all around, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to fasten on one's belt (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to put a belt or sash around, gird about; gird oneself
BDAG.pt: colocar um cinto ou faixa ao redor, cingir; cingir-se

DEFINITION: a putting around or on (as of ornaments).
ORIGIN: From peritithemi; a putting all around, i.e. Decorating oneself with.

BDAG.en: putting on or around as an act of wearing, putting on (ornaments)
BDAG.pt: ato de colocar ou vestir algo ao redor, colocar (ornamentos)

DEFINITION: in intrans. act. tenses: to stand around; mid: to avoid, shun.
ORIGIN: From peri and histemi; to stand all around, i.e. (near) to be a bystander, or (aloof) to keep away from.

BDAG.en: to encircle by standing around; to go around so as to avoid, avoid, shun
BDAG.pt: cercar ficando ao redor; dar a volta para evitar, evitar, esquivar-se

DEFINITION: that which is cleaned off, refuse.
ORIGIN: From a compound of peri and kathairo; something cleaned off all around, i.e. Refuse (figuratively).

BDAG.en: that which is removed as a result of a thorough cleansing, dirt, refuse, off-scouring; propitiatory offering, ransom
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é removido como resultado de uma limpeza completa, sujeira, detritos, escória; oferenda propiciatória, resgate

DEFINITION: to cover up, cover round about, veil round, blindfold.
ORIGIN: From peri and kalupto; to cover all around, i.e. Entirely (the face, a surface).

BDAG.en: to cover by putting something around, cover, conceal
BDAG.pt: cobrir colocando algo ao redor, cobrir, ocultar

DEFINITION: to lie about, surround; to be encompassed, surrounded, or clothed with, be in submission to.
ORIGIN: From peri and keimai; to lie all around, i.e. Inclose, encircle, hamper (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to be positioned around some object or area, be around, surround; to put something around, wear something, have something on
BDAG.pt: estar posicionado ao redor de algum objeto ou área, estar ao redor, cercar; colocar algo ao redor, vestir algo, ter algo vestido

DEFINITION: a helmet.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a compound of peri and kephale; encirclement of the head, i.e. A helmet.

BDAG.en: helmet (only in imagery of Christian virtues)
BDAG.pt: capacete (apenas em imagens de virtudes cristãs)

DEFINITION: having full power over, mastering, gaining control over.
ORIGIN: From peri and kratos; strong all around, i.e. A master (manager).

BDAG.en: having control in a situation, having power, being in command
BDAG.pt: ter controle em uma situação, ter poder, estar no comando

DEFINITION: to conceal, hide (by putting something around it).
ORIGIN: From peri and krupto; to conceal all around, i.e. Entirely.

DEFINITION: to encircle, surround, encompass.
ORIGIN: From peri and kukloo; to encircle all around, i.e. Blockade completely.

BDAG.en: surround, encircle (e.g., a beleaguered city)
BDAG.pt: cercar, rodear (ex: uma cidade sitiada)

DEFINITION: to shine around.
ORIGIN: From peri and lampo; to illuminate all around, i.e. Invest with a halo.

BDAG.en: shine around someone/something
BDAG.pt: brilhar ao redor de alguém/algo

DEFINITION: to leave behind; pass: to be left behind, remain, survive.
ORIGIN: From peri and leipo; to leave all around, i.e. (passively) survive.

DEFINITION: very sorrowful, greatly grieved.
ORIGIN: From peri and lupe; grieved all around, i.e. Intensely sad.

BDAG.en: very sad, deeply grieved
BDAG.pt: muito triste, profundamente aflito

DEFINITION: to wait for, await.
ORIGIN: From peri and meno; to stay around, i.e. Await.

BDAG.en: wait for (someone or something)
BDAG.pt: esperar por (alguém ou algo)

DEFINITION: round about, neighboring.
ORIGIN: Adverb from peri; all around, i.e. (as an adjective) circumjacent.

BDAG.en: (all) around
BDAG.pt: ao redor (de tudo)

DEFINITION: to dwell around, be neighboring to.
ORIGIN: From peri and oikeo; to reside around, i.e. Be a neighbor.

BDAG.en: to live near and around, be in the neighborhood of
BDAG.pt: viver perto e ao redor, estar nas vizinhanças de

DEFINITION: dwelling around; subst: a neighbor.
ORIGIN: From peri and oikos; housed around, i.e. Neighboring (used elliptically as a noun).

BDAG.en: living in the vicinity of others, living around, in the neighborhood; neighbors (subst.)
BDAG.pt: vivendo na vizinhança de outros, vivendo ao redor, nas proximidades; vizinhos (substantivo)

DEFINITION: costly, treasured, select, specially chosen.
ORIGIN: From the present participle feminine of a compound of peri and eimi; being beyond usual, i.e. Special (one's own).

BDAG.en: pert. to being of very special status, chosen, especial
BDAG.pt: pertencente a um status muito especial, escolhido, especial

DEFINITION: circumference, a portion circumscribed.
ORIGIN: From periecho; a being held around, i.e. (concretely) a passage (of Scripture, as circumscribed).

BDAG.en: content/wording of a written text/scripture or portion of written text/scripture
BDAG.pt: o conteúdo/a formulação de um texto escrito/escritura ou uma porção de texto escrito/escritura

DEFINITION: to walk, hence Hebraistically (in an ethical sense): to conduct life, live.
ORIGIN: From peri and pateo; to tread all around, i.e. Walk at large (especially as proof of ability); figuratively, to live, deport oneself, follow (as a companion or votary).

BDAG.en: to go here and there in walking, go about, walk around; to conduct one’s life, comport oneself, behave, live
BDAG.pt: andar de um lado para o outro ao caminhar, andar por aí, passear; conduzir a sua vida, portar-se, comportar-se, viver

DEFINITION: to put on a spit; met: to pierce, wound deeply.
ORIGIN: From peri and the base of peran; to penetrate entirely, i.e. Transfix (figuratively).

BDAG.en: pierce through, impale (figuratively: pierce oneself through with many a pang)
BDAG.pt: perfurar, empalar (figurativamente: perfurar-se com muitas dores)

DEFINITION: to fall into the midst of, be involved in, happen upon a place.
ORIGIN: From peri and pipto; to fall into something that is all around, i.e. Light among or upon, be surrounded with.

BDAG.en: to move toward something and hit against it, strike; to encounter at hazard, fall in with, fall into (hostile persons or discomfiting circumstances)
BDAG.pt: mover-se em direção a algo e bater contra isso, atingir; encontrar por acaso, topar com, cair em (pessoas hostis ou circunstâncias desanimadoras)

DEFINITION: to acquire, earn, purchase, make own, preserve alive.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from peri and poieo; to make around oneself, i.e. Acquire (buy).

BDAG.en: cause to remain over and above; 1. make secure for oneself, save/preserve (for oneself); 2. gain possession of something, acquire, obtain, gain for oneself; 3. effect some circumstance, bring (about) for someone.
BDAG.pt: causar que permaneça por sobra; 1. tornar seguro para si mesmo, salvar/preservar (para si mesmo); 2. obter posse de algo, adquirir, obter, ganhar para si mesmo; 3. efetuar alguma circunstância, trazer (à tona) para alguém.

DEFINITION: acquiring, obtaining, possessing, possession, ownership.
ORIGIN: From peripoieomai; acquisition (the act or the thing); by extension, preservation.

BDAG.en: experience of security, keeping safe, preserving, saving; experience of an event of acquisition, gaining, obtaining; that which is acquired, possessing, possession, property
BDAG.pt: experiência de segurança, manter a salvo, preservação, salvação; experiência de um evento de aquisição, ganho, obtenção; aquilo que é adquirido, posse, propriedade

DEFINITION: to tear off, as of garments.
ORIGIN: From peri and rhegnumi; to tear all around, i.e. Completely away.

DEFINITION: to distract, trouble greatly.
ORIGIN: From peri and spao; to drag all around, i.e. (figuratively) to distract (with care).

BDAG.en: to be pulled away from a reference point, be pulled/dragged away; to have one’s attention directed from one thing to another, become or be distracted, quite busy, overburdened.
BDAG.pt: ser puxado para longe de um ponto de referência, ser puxado/arrastado; ter a atenção direcionada de uma coisa para outra, ficar ou estar distraído, muito ocupado, sobrecarregado.

DEFINITION: abundance, superfluity.
ORIGIN: From perisseuo; surplusage, i.e. Superabundance.

BDAG.en: that which is beyond the regular or expected amount, surplus, abundance
BDAG.pt: aquilo que está além da quantidade regular ou esperada, excedente, abundância

DEFINITION: abundance, overflow.
ORIGIN: From perisseuo; a surplus, or superabundance.
USAGE: abundance, that was left, over and above.

BDAG.en: a condition of great plenty, abundance, fullness; that which remains above and beyond, what remains
BDAG.pt: uma condição de grande fartura, abundância, plenitude; aquilo que resta além do necessário, o que sobra

DEFINITION: (a) intrans: to exceed the ordinary (the necessary), abound, overflow; be left over, (b) trans: to cause to abound.
ORIGIN: From perissos; to superabound (in quantity or quality), be in excess, be superfluous; also (transitively) to cause to superabound or excel.
USAGE: (make, more) abound, (have, have more) abundance (be more) abundant, be the better, enough and to spare, exceed, excel, increase, be left, redound, remain (over and above).

BDAG.en: to be in abundance, abound (be more than enough, be left over; be present in abundance; be extremely rich or abundant, overflow; grow); cause to exist in abundance, cause to abound (greatly increase something, grant something richly); (pass.) receive something in great abundance.
BDAG.pt: estar em abundância, sobrar (ser mais que o suficiente, sobrar; estar presente em abundância; ser extremamente rico ou abundante, transbordar; crescer); fazer existir em abundância, causar abundância (aumentar muito algo, conceder algo ricamente); (pass.) receber algo em grande abundância.

DEFINITION: more, greater, excessive, abundant, exceedingly, vehemently; noun: preeminence, advantage.
ORIGIN: From peri (in the sense of beyond); superabundant (in quantity) or superior (in quality); by implication, excessive; adverbially (with ek) violently; neuter (as noun) preeminence.
USAGE: exceeding abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, exceedingly, very highly, beyond measure, more, superfluous, vehement(-ly).

BDAG.en: pert. to that which is not ordinarily encountered, extraordinary, remarkable; pert. to being extraordinary in amount, abundant, profuse (going beyond what is necessary; superfluous, unnecessary); in the comparative sense (substitute for μᾶλλον, πλείων).
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que não se encontra ordinariamente, extraordinário, notável; pertencente a ser extraordinário em quantidade, abundante, profuso (indo além do necessário; supérfluo, desnecessário); no sentido comparativo (substituto para μᾶλλον, πλείων).

DEFINITION: more abundantly, a great deal, far more.
ORIGIN: Neuter of perissoteros (as adverb); in a more superabundant way.
USAGE: more abundantly, a great deal, far more.

DEFINITION: greater, more, even more, more abundantly.
ORIGIN: Comparative of perissos; more superabundant (in number, degree or character).

BDAG.en: greater, more, even more (used w. a subst.; with focus on incremental aspect; neut. sing. as adv.).
BDAG.pt: maior, mais, ainda mais (usado com um substantivo; com foco no aspecto incremental; singular neutro como advérbio).

DEFINITION: more abundantly, much more.
ORIGIN: Adverb from perissoteros (g4055); more superabundantly.
USAGE: more abundant(-ly), X the more earnest, (more) exceedingly, more frequent, much more, the rather.

BDAG.en: (even) more comp.; to a much greater degree, far more, far greater; especially, elative, all the more.
BDAG.pt: mais (ainda) comparativo; em um grau muito maior, muito mais, bem maior; especialmente, elativo, com muito mais razão.

DEFINITION: greatly, exceedingly, abundantly, vehemently.
ORIGIN: Adverb from perissos; superabundantly.
USAGE: exceedingly, out of measure, the more.

BDAG.en: exceedingly, beyond measure, very.
BDAG.pt: excepcionalmente, além da medida, muito.

DEFINITION: a dove, pigeon.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a pigeon.

BDAG.en: pigeon or dove (bird of the family Columbidae), used symbolically for virtues or the Holy Spirit.
BDAG.pt: pombo ou pomba (ave da família Columbidae), usada simbolicamente para virtudes ou o Espírito Santo.

DEFINITION: to cut around, circumcise.
ORIGIN: From peri and the base of tomoteros; to cut around, i.e. (specially) to circumcise.

BDAG.en: 'to cut off around'; in our literature and the LXX, sometimes fig., only in the sense: to cut off the foreskin of the male genital organ, circumcise
BDAG.pt: 'cortar ao redor'; em nossa literatura e na LXX, às vezes figurado, apenas no sentido de: cortar o prepúcio do órgão genital masculino, circuncidar

DEFINITION: to place or put around, clothe; fig: to bestow, confer.
ORIGIN: From peri and tithemi; to place around; by implication, to present.
USAGE: bestow upon, hedge round about, put about (on, upon), set about.

BDAG.en: put/place around/on something around someone or something; to cause a state to exist relative to an object, put on/around, grant/bestow something to/on someone
BDAG.pt: colocar/pôr ao redor/sobre algo ao redor de alguém ou algo; causar um estado em relação a um objeto, vestir/colocar ao redor, conceder/dar algo a alguém

DEFINITION: circumcision.
ORIGIN: From peritemno; circumcision (the rite, the condition or the people, literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: circumcision of the foreskin, circumcision as a cultic rite; the state of having been circumcised; fig. of spiritual circumcision; one who is circumcised, abstract for concrete, usually plural those who are circumcised
BDAG.pt: circuncisão do prepúcio, circuncisão como rito de culto; o estado de ter sido circuncidado; fig. de circuncisão espiritual; aquele que é circuncidado, abstrato para concreto, geralmente no plural aqueles que são circuncidados

DEFINITION: to turn round, turn, change.
ORIGIN: From peri and the base of trope; to turn around, i.e. (mentally) to craze.

BDAG.en: to turn from one state to its opposite, turn
BDAG.pt: virar de um estado para o seu oposto, transformar

DEFINITION: to run around.
ORIGIN: From peri and trecho (including its alternate); to run around, i.e. Traverse.

BDAG.en: to be in motion around, run/move around; to be in rapid motion here and there in an area, run about, go about in
BDAG.pt: estar em movimento ao redor, correr/mover-se ao redor; estar em movimento rápido aqui e ali em uma área, correr por aí, vaguear em

DEFINITION: to carry around; pass: to be driven to and fro.
ORIGIN: From peri and phero; to convey around, i.e. Transport hither and thither.

BDAG.en: carry about, carry here and there; (figuratively) carry the name (of Christ, or of a Christian) about
BDAG.pt: carregar por aí, levar de um lado para o outro; (figurativamente) carregar o nome (de Cristo, ou de um cristão) consigo

DEFINITION: to examine on all sides, to despise.
ORIGIN: From peri and phroneo; to think beyond, i.e. Depreciate (contemn).

BDAG.en: to have disdain for, disregard, look down on, despise
BDAG.pt: ter desprezo por, desconsiderar, olhar de cima, desprezar

DEFINITION: neighboring; subst: the neighboring country, neighboring inhabitants.
ORIGIN: From peri and chora; around the region, i.e. Circumjacent (as noun, with ge implied vicinity).
USAGE: country (round) about, region (that lieth) round about.

BDAG.en: pert. to being around an area, neighboring; region around, neighborhood
BDAG.pt: relativo a estar ao redor de uma área, vizinho; região ao redor, vizinhança

DEFINITION: scrapings, offscourings, wiped-off filth.
ORIGIN: From a comparative of peri and psao (to rub); something brushed all around, i.e. Off-scrapings (figuratively, scum).

BDAG.en: that which is removed by the process of cleansing, dirt, off-scouring; ransom, scapegoat, sacrifice; term of polite self-depreciation
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é removido pelo processo de limpeza, sujeira, escória; resgate, bode expiatório, sacrifício; termo de polida autodepreciação

DEFINITION: to boast, vaunt myself.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from perperos (braggart; perhaps by reduplication of the base of peran); to boast.

BDAG.en: to heap praise on oneself, behave as a braggart, boast, brag
BDAG.pt: acumular elogios a si mesmo, comportar-se como um fanfarrão, gabar-se, vangloriar-se

DEFINITION: Persis, name of a Christian lady in Rome.
ORIGIN: A Persian woman; Persis, a Christian female.

BDAG.en: Persis, recipient of a greeting
BDAG.pt: Pérsis, destinatária de uma saudação

DEFINITION: last year, a year ago.
ORIGIN: Adverb from peras; the by-gone, i.e. (as noun) last year.

BDAG.en: last year, a year ago
BDAG.pt: ano passado, há um ano

DEFINITION: a bird, fowl.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of petomai; a flying animal, i.e. Bird.

BDAG.en: any kind of bird (wild or domestic), bird
BDAG.pt: qualquer tipo de ave (selvagem ou doméstica), pássaro

DEFINITION: to fly.
ORIGIN: Or prolongation petaomai (pet-ah'-om-ahee), or contracted ptaomai (ptah'-om-ahee) middle voice of a primary verb; to fly.

BDAG.en: fly
BDAG.pt: voar

DEFINITION: a rock, ledge, cliff, cave, stony ground.
ORIGIN: Feminine of the same as Petros; a (mass of) rock (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: bedrock or massive rock formations, rock as distinguished from stones; rocky ground with a thin layer of topsoil; in wordplay with the name Πέτρος
BDAG.pt: rocha matriz ou formações rochosas maciças, pedra distinta de seixos; solo rochoso com uma fina camada de solo superficial; em um jogo de palavras com o nome Pedro

DEFINITION: "a stone" or "a boulder", Peter, one of the twelve apostles.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a (piece of) rock (larger than lithos); as a name, Petrus, an apostle.

BDAG.en: surname of the head of the circle of Twelve Disciples, whose name was orig. Simon. ... leader of Jesus’ disciples, was spokesman for the Twelve...
BDAG.pt: Sobrenome do chefe do círculo dos Doze Discípulos, cujo nome era originalmente Simão. ... líder dos discípulos de Jesus, porta-voz dos Doze...

DEFINITION: rocky, stony.
ORIGIN: From petra and eidos; rock-like, i.e. Rocky.

BDAG.en: pert. to rocky area with little topsoil, rocky, stony ... rocky ground, over which a thin layer of soil is spread
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a área rochosa com pouca camada superficial de solo, rochoso, pedregoso ... solo pedregoso, sobre o qual uma fina camada de terra está espalhada

DEFINITION: rue, a plant used for flavoring or garnishing food.
ORIGIN: From pegnumi; rue (from its thick or fleshy leaves).

BDAG.en: rue (ruta chalepensis), mentioned among the garden herbs that are tithed
BDAG.pt: arruda (ruta chalepensis), mencionada entre as ervas de jardim que são dizimadas

DEFINITION: a fountain, spring, well, issue, flow.
ORIGIN: Probably from pegnumi (through the idea of gushing plumply); a fount (literally or figuratively), i.e. Source or supply (of water, blood, enjoyment) (not necessarily the original spring).

BDAG.en: a source of someth. that gushes out or flows, spring, fountain, flow ... source of life ... the spring of the water of life
BDAG.pt: uma fonte de algo que brota ou flui, nascente, fonte, fluxo ... fonte de vida ... a fonte da água da vida

DEFINITION: to fasten, pitch a tent.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which in its simpler form occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fix ("peg"), i.e. (specially) to set up (a tent).

BDAG.en: to make firm or stable by fixing in a place, make firm, fix ... to set up or erect a construction, put together, build ... to make solid or stiff, esp. of liquids, pass., intr. sense, of milk curdle ... congealed blood
BDAG.pt: tornar firme ou estável fixando em um lugar, firmar, fixar ... erguer ou montar uma construção, montar, edificar ... tornar sólido ou rígido, especialmente de líquidos, sentido passivo/intransitivo, de coalhar leite ... sangue coagulado

DEFINITION: the rudder of a ship.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a (presumed) derivative of pedon (the blade of an oar; from the same as pede); a "pedal", i.e. Helm.

BDAG.en: steering paddle, rudder
BDAG.pt: remo de direção, leme

DEFINITION: how large? how great?.
ORIGIN: A quantitative form (the feminine) of the base of pou; how much (as an indefinite), i.e. In size or (figuratively) dignity.

BDAG.en: correlative pron. ‘how large?’ but in our lit., in both places where it occurs, in an exclamation ... pert. to large size, how large ... pert. to extraordinary importance, how great
BDAG.pt: pronome correlativo 'quão grande?', mas em nossa literatura, em ambos os lugares em que ocorre, em uma exclamação ... referente a grande tamanho, quão grande ... referente a importância extraordinária, quão grande

DEFINITION: clay, mud.
ORIGIN: Perhaps a primary word; clay.

BDAG.en: clay (used in making pottery); mud, mire (soft mass produced when the ground is wet).
BDAG.pt: Barro/argila (usado na fabricação de cerâmica); lama, lodo (massa mole produzida quando o solo está molhado).

DEFINITION: a sack, wallet for carrying provisions.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a wallet or leather pouch for food.

BDAG.en: a leather pouch used by travelers, knapsack, traveler’s bag ... beggar’s bag. Such a bag was also used by shepherds
BDAG.pt: uma bolsa de couro usada por viajantes, alforje, saco de viagem ... bolsa de mendigo. Tal bolsa também era usada por pastores

DEFINITION: a cubit, about a foot and a half.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; the fore-arm, i.e. (as a measure) a cubit.

BDAG.en: orig. ‘forearm’ then cubit or ell as a measure of length (about 45–52 cm)
BDAG.pt: Originalmente 'antebraço', depois côvado ou vara como medida de comprimento (cerca de 45–52 cm)

DEFINITION: to lay hold of, apprehend, catch, arrest.
ORIGIN: Probably another form of biazo; to squeeze, i.e. Seize (gently by the hand (press), or officially (arrest), or in hunting (capture)).
USAGE: apprehend, catch, lay hand on, take. Compare piezo.

BDAG.en: to take firm hold of, grasp; to seize with intent to overpower or gain control (of humans or animals).
BDAG.pt: Agarrar firmemente, segurar; apreender com intenção de subjugar ou ganhar controle (de humanos ou animais).

DEFINITION: to press down, press together, as in a measure.
ORIGIN: Another form for piazo; to pack.

BDAG.en: press (down); (figuratively) to be so pinned/crushed
BDAG.pt: Pressionar (para baixo); (figurativamente) ser esmagado/calado

DEFINITION: persuasive speech.
ORIGIN: From a compound of a derivative of peitho and logos; persuasive language.

BDAG.en: persuasive speech, art of persuasion (in an unfavorable sense: specious arguments)
BDAG.pt: Discurso persuasivo, arte da persuasão (em sentido desfavorável: argumentos falaciosos)

DEFINITION: to make bitter, embitter; pass: to grow angry or harsh.
ORIGIN: From pikros; to embitter (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to cause to become bitter, make bitter (physically); to cause bitter feelings, embitter, make bitter (affective sense).
BDAG.pt: Fazer ficar amargo, tornar amargo (fisicamente); causar sentimentos amargos, amargurar, tornar amargo (sentido afetivo).

DEFINITION: bitterness, harshness, hence met: an embittered (resentful) spirit.
ORIGIN: From pikros; acridity (especially poison), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: state of being bitter to the taste, bitterness (lit.); state of being bitter in an affective sense, bitterness, animosity, anger, harshness (fig.).
BDAG.pt: Estado de ser amargo ao paladar, amargor (literal); estado de ser amargo em sentido afetivo, amargura, animosidade, raiva, aspereza (figurado).

DEFINITION: bitter, acrid, malignant.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from pegnumi (through the idea of piercing); sharp (pungent), i.e. Acrid (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: pert. to being bitter to taste, bitter (opp. sweet); pert. to being bitter in feeling or attitude, bitter, harsh
BDAG.pt: Relativo a ser amargo ao paladar, amargo (oposto a doce); relativo a ser amargo no sentimento ou atitude, amargo, áspero

DEFINITION: bitterly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from pikros; bitterly, i.e. (figuratively) violently.

BDAG.en: bitterly, ferociously (weep bitterly, roar ferociously)
BDAG.pt: Amargamente, ferozmente (chorar amargamente, rugir ferozmente)

DEFINITION: Pilate, a Roman procurator of Judea.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; close-pressed, i.e. Firm; Pilatus, a Roman.

BDAG.en: Pilate (Pontius P.), prefect of Judea 26–36 a.d.
BDAG.pt: Pilatos (Pôncio P.), prefeito da Judeia de 26 a 36 d.C.

DEFINITION: to swell, be inflamed.
ORIGIN: A reduplicated and prolonged form of a primary preo preh'-o which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fire, i.e. Burn (figuratively and passively, become inflamed with fever).

BDAG.en: to burn with fever or to become distended, swell up (medical term)
BDAG.pt: Arder com febre ou ficar distendido, inchar (termo médico)

DEFINITION: a tablet for writing.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of pinax; a tablet (for writing on).

BDAG.en: little (wooden) tablet esp. of a writing-tablet for notes
BDAG.pt: Pequena tabuleta (de madeira), especialmente uma tabuinha de escrita para anotações

DEFINITION: a plate, platter, disc, dish.
ORIGIN: Apparently a form of plax; a plate.

BDAG.en: a relatively flat large dish, platter, dish
BDAG.pt: Um prato relativamente plano e grande, travessa, ou vasilha

DEFINITION: to drink, imbibe.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of pio (pee'-o), which (together with another form) poo (po'-o) occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses; to imbibe (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to take in a liquid internally, drink; fig: submit to a severe trial or death (drink the cup).
BDAG.pt: ingerir um líquido internamente, beber; fig: submeter-se a uma provação severa ou à morte (beber o cálice).

DEFINITION: fatness, as of the olive; richness.
ORIGIN: From pion (fat; perhaps akin to the alternate of pino through the idea of repletion); plumpness, i.e. (by implication) richness (oiliness).

BDAG.en: state of oiliness, fatness (used of the rich sap/richness of a root, esp. of an olive tree).
BDAG.pt: estado de oleosidade, gordura (usado para a seiva rica/riqueza de uma raiz, especialmente de uma oliveira).

DEFINITION: to sell; pass: to be a slave to, be devoted to.
ORIGIN: A reduplicated and prolonged form of prao (prah'-o); (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses) contracted from perao (to traverse; from the base of peran); to traffic (by travelling), i.e. Dispose of as merchandise or into slavery (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to engage in vending, sell; pass: be sold; fig: to be sold into slavery to sin.
BDAG.pt: engajar-se em venda, vender; pass: ser vendido; fig: ser vendido como escravo ao pecado.

DEFINITION: to fall, fall under (as under condemnation), fall prostrate.
ORIGIN: A reduplicated and contracted form of peto (pet'-o); (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); probably akin to petomai through the idea of alighting; to fall (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: To move rapidly in a downward direction, fall, fall down; fall to the ground, fall to pieces, collapse; fall in a transcendent or moral sense, be ruined, go astray morally; fall dead; fall in battle; fall down as a sign of devotion or humility.
BDAG.pt: Mover-se rapidamente em direção descendente, cair, tombar; cair ao chão, desmoronar, colapsar; cair em sentido transcendente ou moral, ser arruinado, desviar-se moralmente; cair morto; cair em batalha; prostrar-se como sinal de devoção ou humildade.

DEFINITION: Pisidia, a country of Asia Minor, being the south-western part of the Roman province Galatia.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Pisidia, a mountainous region in central Asia Minor, west of the Taurus Mts., traversed by Paul.
BDAG.pt: Pisídia, uma região montanhosa na Ásia Menor central, a oeste das Montanhas Tauro, atravessada por Paulo.

DEFINITION: to believe, have faith in, trust in; pass: to be entrusted with.
ORIGIN: From pistis; to have faith (in, upon, or with respect to, a person or thing), i.e. Credit; by implication, to entrust (especially one's spiritual well-being to Christ).
USAGE: believe(-r), commit (to trust), put in trust with.

BDAG.en: 1. to consider something to be true and therefore worthy of one’s trust, believe (in) something, be convinced of something... 2. to entrust oneself to an entity in complete confidence, believe (in), trust, with implication of total commitment to the one who is trusted.
BDAG.pt: 1. considerar algo verdadeiro e, portanto, digno de confiança, crer (em) algo, estar convencido de algo... 2. confiar-se a uma entidade com confiança total, crer (em), confiar, com a implicação de um compromisso total com aquele em quem se confia.

DEFINITION: genuine, pure (of ointment), trustworthy.
ORIGIN: From pistis; trustworthy, i.e. Genuine (unadulterated).

BDAG.en: genuine, unadulterated (referring to quality); faithful, trustworthy (later meaning related to 'faith').
BDAG.pt: genuíno, puro (referindo-se à qualidade); fiel, confiável (sentido posterior relacionado à 'fé').

DEFINITION: faith, belief, trust, confidence; fidelity, faithfulness.
ORIGIN: From peitho; persuasion, i.e. Credence; moral conviction (of religious truth, or the truthfulness of God or a religious teacher), especially reliance upon Christ for salvation; abstractly, constancy in such profession; by extension, the system of religious (Gospel) truth itself.

BDAG.en: faithfulness, reliability, fidelity, commitment; a solemn promise/assurance, oath, troth; a token offered as a guarantee, proof, pledge; the state of believing on the basis of the reliability of the one trusted, trust, confidence, faith in the active sense ('believing').
BDAG.pt: fidelidade, confiabilidade, lealdade, compromisso; uma promessa/garantia solene, juramento; um sinal oferecido como garantia, prova, penhor; o estado de crer com base na confiabilidade daquele em quem se confia, confiança, fé no sentido ativo ('o ato de crer').

DEFINITION: trustworthy, faithful, believing.
ORIGIN: From peitho; objectively, trustworthy; subjectively, trustful.

BDAG.en: trustworthy, faithful, dependable, inspiring trust/faith; (passive aspect of believing); (of persons) trustworthy; (of God) one in whom we can have full confidence; (of things, esp. words) trustworthy, reliable; (of water) dependable, unfailing, plentiful; (of believers) trusting, cherishing faith/trust, believing, full of faith, faithful; (as subst.) a (Christian) believer.
BDAG.pt: digno de confiança, fiel, confiável, inspirador de confiança/fé; (aspecto passivo de crer); (de pessoas) confiável; (de Deus) aquele em quem podemos ter total confiança; (de coisas, especialmente palavras) digno de confiança, confiável; (de água) confiável, inesgotável, abundante; (de crentes) que confia, que preza a fé/confiança, que crê, cheio de fé, fiel; (como substantivo) um crente (cristão).

DEFINITION: to convince, establish, give assurance to; pass: to be assured of.
ORIGIN: From pistos; to assure.

BDAG.en: to act in a faithful manner, show oneself faithful (in something); to be sure about something because of its reliability, feel confidence, be convinced.
BDAG.pt: agir de maneira fiel, mostrar-se fiel (em algo); ter certeza de algo por causa da sua confiabilidade, sentir confiança, ficar convencido.

DEFINITION: to lead astray, deceive, cause to wander.
ORIGIN: From plane; to (properly, cause to) roam (from safety, truth, or virtue).
USAGE: go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way.

BDAG.en: to cause to go astray from a specific way, actively lead astray, cause to wander; mislead, deceive; to proceed without a sense of proper direction, go astray, be misled, wander about aimlessly; to go astray, be deluded; to wander away from the truth; to be mistaken in one’s judgment, deceive oneself; to be deceived, be misled; to let oneself be misled, deceived.
BDAG.pt: fazer desviar de um caminho específico, ativamente desviar, fazer vaguear; enganar, iludir; prosseguir sem um senso de direção adequada, desviar-se, ser enganado, vaguear sem rumo; desviar-se, ser iludido; desviar-se, perder o rumo; enganar-se no julgamento, iludir a si mesmo; ser enganado, ser ludibriado; deixar-se enganar, iludir.

DEFINITION: a wandering; fig: deceit, delusion, error, sin.
ORIGIN: Feminine of planos (as abstractly); objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety.

BDAG.en: wandering fr. the path of truth, error, delusion, deceit, deception to which one is subject; of an erroneous view of God, as exhibited in polytheism, resulting in moral degradation; the error of unprincipled pers.; the spirit of error
BDAG.pt: desvio do caminho da verdade, erro, ilusão, engano, artimanha ao qual se está sujeito; de uma visão errônea de Deus, como a exibida no politeísmo, resultando em degradação moral; o erro de pessoas sem princípios; o espírito de erro.

DEFINITION: a wanderer.
ORIGIN: From planos; a rover ("planet"), i.e. (figuratively) an erratic teacher.

BDAG.en: wanderer, roamer used as subst. and adj. in our lit. only in the combination ἀστέρες πλανῆται: wandering stars
BDAG.pt: Errante, vago usado como substantivo e adjetivo em nossa literatura apenas na combinação ἀστέρες πλανῆται: estrelas errantes.

DEFINITION: adj: misleading, deceiving, wandering; as subst: a deceiver, imposter.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader.

BDAG.en: pert. to causing someone to be mistaken as an adj., leading astray, deceitful; as subst. deceiver, impostor
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a fazer alguém se enganar como adjetivo, levando ao erro, enganoso; como substantivo, enganador, impostor.

DEFINITION: anything flat and broad, a flat stone.
ORIGIN: From plasso; a moulding-board, i.e. Flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: someth. with a flat surface; in our lit. a flat stone on which inscriptions could be made, tablet, of the tablets of the law
BDAG.pt: Algo com uma superfície plana; em nossa literatura, uma pedra chata na qual inscrições podiam ser feitas, tabuleta, das tábuas da lei.

DEFINITION: a thing formed or fashioned.
ORIGIN: From plasso; something moulded.

BDAG.en: that which is formed or molded, image, figure; handiwork
BDAG.pt: Aquilo que é formado ou moldado, imagem, figura; obra feita pelas mãos.

DEFINITION: to form, mould, as a potter his clay.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to mould, i.e. Shape or fabricate.

BDAG.en: to manufacture someth. by molding a soft substance, form, mold; esp. of God’s creative activity in forming humankind; to direct personal character or cultural formation, shape, in fig. ext. of 1: formation of mental things
BDAG.pt: Manufaturar algo moldando uma substância macia, formar, moldar; especialmente da atividade criativa de Deus na formação da humanidade; direcionar o caráter pessoal ou a formação cultural, moldar, em extensão figurada de 1: formação de coisas mentais.

DEFINITION: formed, molded; fig: feigned, made up, counterfeit.
ORIGIN: From plasso; moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false).

BDAG.en: pert. to being mentally constructed without a basis in fact, fabricated, false
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a ser construído mentalmente sem base factual, fabricado, falso.

DEFINITION: a street, public square, broad way.
ORIGIN: Feminine of platus; a wide "plat" or "place", i.e. Open square.

BDAG.en: wide road, street
BDAG.pt: Rua larga, avenida.

DEFINITION: breadth.
ORIGIN: From platus; width.

BDAG.en: extent from side to side, breadth, width; in imagery of the heart
BDAG.pt: Extensão de lado a lado, largura; em imagens do coração.

DEFINITION: to enlarge, make broad; met: of the growth of tenderness and love.
ORIGIN: From platus; to widen (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to cause someth. to be broad, make broad, enlarge, lit.; Fig., of warm affection (heart is open wide)
BDAG.pt: Fazer algo ser largo, tornar largo, ampliar, literalmente; Figurado, de afeto caloroso (coração se abre amplamente).

DEFINITION: broad, wide; subst: a street.
ORIGIN: From plasso; spread out "flat" ("plot"), i.e. Broad.

BDAG.en: pert. to great extent from side to side, broad, wide (of a gate or road)
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a grande extensão de lado a lado, largo, de grande extensão (de um portão ou estrada).

DEFINITION: braided hair, anything interwoven.
ORIGIN: From pleko; a plait (of hair).

BDAG.en: braided hair, w. focus on stylish coiffure
BDAG.pt: Cabelo trançado, com foco em penteado elegante.

DEFINITION: the greatest, the most, very great.
ORIGIN: Irregular superlative of polus; the largest number or very large.

DEFINITION: more excellent, very great, many.
ORIGIN: Or neuter pleion (pli'-on), or pleon (pleh'-on) comparative of polus; more in quantity, number, or quality; also (in plural) the major portion.
USAGE: X above, + exceed, more excellent, further, (very) great(-er), long(-er), (very) many, greater (more) part, + yet but.

BDAG.en: s. πολύς
BDAG.pt: Ver πολύς (mais).

DEFINITION: to weave together, plait, twist, braid.
ORIGIN: A primary word; to twine or braid.

BDAG.en: weave, plait (a wreath)
BDAG.pt: Tecer, trançar (uma coroa).

DEFINITION: to have more than enough; to abound, increase.
ORIGIN: From pleion; to do, make or be more, i.e. Increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound.
USAGE: abound, abundant, make to increase, have over.

BDAG.en: to become more and more, so as to be in abundance, be/become more or be/become great, be present in abundance, grow, increase, intr.; to have more than is necessary, have too much, intr.; to be responsible for increase, trans.
BDAG.pt: Tornar-se mais e mais, de modo a estar em abundância, ser/tornar-se mais ou tornar-se grande, estar presente em abundância, crescer, aumentar, intransitivo; ter mais do que o necessário, ter demais, intransitivo; ser responsável pelo aumento, transitivo.

DEFINITION: to take advantage of, overreach, defraud.
ORIGIN: From pleonektes; to be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach.
USAGE: get an advantage, defraud, make a gain.

BDAG.en: to take advantage of, exploit, outwit, defraud, cheat (of humans taking advantage of others; of Satan, pass.)
BDAG.pt: Tirar vantagem, explorar, enganar, defraudar, trapacear (de humanos tirando vantagem de outros; de Satanás, voz passiva).

DEFINITION: a covetous or avaricious person; one desirous of having more.
ORIGIN: From pleion and echo; holding (desiring) more, i.e. Eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder).

BDAG.en: one who desires to have more than is due, a greedy person
BDAG.pt: Aquele que deseja ter mais do que lhe é devido, uma pessoa gananciosa.

DEFINITION: covetousness, avarice, aggression, desire for advantage.
ORIGIN: From pleonektes; avarice, i.e. (by implication) fraudulency, extortion.

BDAG.en: the state of desiring to have more than one’s due, greediness, insatiableness, avarice, covetousness
BDAG.pt: o estado de desejar ter mais do que é devido, cobiça, insaciabilidade, avareza, avidez

DEFINITION: the side of the body.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a rib, i.e. (by extension) side.

BDAG.en: side, mostly of the human body; flat side of a stone
BDAG.pt: lado, principalmente do corpo humano; lado plano de uma pedra

DEFINITION: to sail, travel by sea, voyage.
ORIGIN: Another form for pleuo (plyoo'-o); which is used as an alternate in certain tenses; probably a form of pluno (through the idea of plunging through the water); to pass in a vessel.

BDAG.en: travel by sea, sail
BDAG.pt: viajar por mar, navegar

DEFINITION: a blow, stripe, wound; an affliction, plague.
ORIGIN: From plesso; a stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity.

BDAG.en: 1. a sudden hard stroke with some instrument, blow, stroke lit.; 2. wound caused by a blow, wound, bruise; 3. a sudden calamity that causes severe distress, blow in the sense ‘a blow of fate’, etc. fig. ext. of 1 and 2: plague, misfortune
BDAG.pt: 1. um golpe súbito e forte com algum instrumento, pancada, golpe literal; 2. ferida causada por um golpe, ferimento, contusão; 3. uma calamidade súbita que causa grande aflição, golpe no sentido de ‘golpe do destino’, etc. extensão figurada de 1 e 2: praga, infortúnio

DEFINITION: a multitude, crowd, great number, assemblage.
ORIGIN: From pletho; a fulness, i.e. A large number, throng, populace.

BDAG.en: 1. the fact or condition of being many, quantity/number; 2. a large amount, large number, multitude; 3. people, populace, population; 4. in the usage of cultic communities as a t.t. for the whole body of their members, fellowship, community, congregation
BDAG.pt: 1. o fato ou condição de ser muitos, quantidade/número; 2. uma grande quantidade, grande número, multidão; 3. povo, população; 4. no uso de comunidades cultuais como termo técnico para o corpo total de seus membros, irmandade, comunidade, congregação

DEFINITION: to increase, to be increased.
ORIGIN: From another form of plethos; to increase (transitively or intransitively).

BDAG.en: 1. to cause to become greater in number trans.: a. increase, multiply act.; b. be multiplied, grow, increase pass. in number; 2. to increase greatly in number, grow, increase intr.
BDAG.pt: 1. fazer tornar-se maior em número (transitivo): a. aumentar, multiplicar (ativo); b. ser multiplicado, crescer, aumentar (passivo) em número; 2. aumentar muito em número, crescer, aumentar (intransitivo)

DEFINITION: furnish, accomplish, fill, supply.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary pleo (pleh'-o) (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form pimplemi) to "fill" (literally or figuratively (imbue, influence, supply)); specially, to fulfil (time).

DEFINITION: a striker, contentious person, brawler.
ORIGIN: From plesso; a smiter, i.e. Pugnacious (quarrelsome).

BDAG.en: pugnacious person, bully
BDAG.pt: pessoa briguenta, valentão

DEFINITION: a flood.
ORIGIN: Prolonged from pletho; flood-tide, i.e. (by analogy) a freshet.

BDAG.en: the overflowing of a body of water, high water, flood
BDAG.pt: o transbordamento de um corpo d'água, maré alta, inundação

DEFINITION: however, nevertheless, but, except that, yet.
ORIGIN: From pleion; moreover (besides), i.e. Albeit, save that, rather, yet.
USAGE: but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than.

BDAG.en: used as conj.: marker of someth. that is contrastingly added for consideration: a. adversative but; b. only, nevertheless, but; c. only, in any case, on the other hand, but, breaking off a discussion and emphasizing what is important; d. except that; e. breaking off and passing to a new subject only, but. Used as prep. w. gen.: except, in ref. to pers. or thing
BDAG.pt: usado como conj.: marcador de algo adicionado em contraste para consideração: a. adversativo, mas; b. somente, todavia, mas; c. somente, em qualquer caso, por outro lado, mas, interrompendo uma discussão e enfatizando o que é importante; d. exceto que; e. interrompendo e passando para um novo assunto, somente, mas. Usado como preposição com genitivo: exceto, em referência a pessoa ou coisa

DEFINITION: full, abounding in, complete, completely occupied with.
ORIGIN: From pletho; replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete.

BDAG.en: filled, full (of things, containing all it will hold); of persons, full of a power, gift, feeling, characteristic quality, etc.; complete, full, in full (nothing lacking).
BDAG.pt: cheio, repleto (de coisas, contendo tudo o que pode conter); de pessoas, cheio de um poder, dom, sentimento, qualidade característica, etc.; completo, inteiro, em plenitude (sem nada faltar).

DEFINITION: (lit: to carry full), (a) to complete, carry out fully, (b) to fully convince, satisfy fully, (c) to fully believe.
ORIGIN: From pleres and phoreo; to carry out fully (in evidence), i.e. Completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish.
USAGE: most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of.

BDAG.en: fill (completely), fulfill (synonym of πληρόω, sometimes used as v.l.); fig. complement, aid; accomplish; be fully convinced, assured, certain.
BDAG.pt: encher (completamente), cumprir (sinônimo de πληρόω, ocasionalmente usado como variação textual); fig. complementar, auxiliar; realizar; estar totalmente convencido, assegurado, certo.

DEFINITION: full assurance, conviction, confidence.
ORIGIN: From plerophoreo; entire confidence.

BDAG.en: state of complete certainty, full assurance, certainty (also meaning fullness)
BDAG.pt: estado de certeza completa, plena segurança, convicção (também significando plenitude)

DEFINITION: to fill, fulfill, complete.
ORIGIN: From pleres; to make replete, i.e. (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc..
USAGE: accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (come), fully preach, perfect, supply.

BDAG.en: to fill in (impressions of stones); of sounds and odors: to fill a space; to fill someone's heart; of Christ: to pass through all cosmic spheres; to become filled or full (w. gen., dat., acc., or ἐν + dat.); to complete a period of time, fill up; to bring to completion (e.g., a begun activity, the gospel); to bring to a designed end, fulfill (a prophecy, promise, law, desire, duty, fate); to complete a number, have the number made complete; to carry out to the end (a ministry or course).
BDAG.pt: encher (marcas de pedras); de sons e odores: encher um espaço; encher o coração de alguém; de Cristo: passar por todas as esferas cósmicas; tornar-se cheio ou completo (com genitivo, dativo, acusativo, ou ἐν + dativo); completar um período de tempo; trazer a termo (ex: uma atividade iniciada, o evangelho); levar a um fim designado, cumprir (uma profecia, promessa, lei, desejo, dever, destino); completar um número; executar até o fim (um ministério ou percurso).

DEFINITION: (a) a fill, fullness; full complement; supply, patch, supplement, (b) fullness, filling, fulfillment, completion.
ORIGIN: From pleroo; repletion or completion, i.e. (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period).
USAGE: which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness.

BDAG.en: that which fills (up), e.g., a crew or cargo; that which makes something full/complete, supplement, complement (the church as the complement of Christ); a full number; sum total, fullness, even superabundance; act of fulfilling specifications, fulfillment (e.g., of the law); fullness of time.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que preenche (ou enche totalmente), ex: tripulação ou carga; aquilo que torna algo cheio/completo, suplemento, complemento (a igreja como o complemento de Cristo); um número completo; soma total, plenitude, até mesmo superabundância; ato de cumprir especificações, cumprimento (ex: da lei); plenitude do tempo.

DEFINITION: near, nearby, a neighbor.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of pelas (near); (adverbially) close by; as noun, a neighbor, i.e. Fellow (as man, countryman, Christian or friend).

BDAG.en: nearby, near, close (adverb); near, close to something (preposition with genitive); the one who is near or close (substantive).
BDAG.pt: próximo, perto, ao lado (advérbio); perto de algo (preposição com genitivo); aquele que está perto ou próximo (substantivo).

DEFINITION: satisfaction, indulgence.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of pletho; a filling up, i.e. (figuratively) gratification.

BDAG.en: process of securing complete satisfaction, satiety esp. w. food and drink, but also w. other types of enjoyment, satisfaction, gratification
BDAG.pt: processo de obter satisfação completa, saciedade, especialmente com comida e bebida, mas também com outros tipos de prazer, satisfação, gratificação

DEFINITION: to strike, smite.
ORIGIN: Apparently another form of plasso (through the idea of flattening out); to pound, i.e. (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity).

BDAG.en: to strike with force, strike (of flames of fire, of divinely-administered ‘blows’ or disasters)
BDAG.pt: golpear com força, ferir (de chamas de fogo, de 'golpes' ou desastres administrados divinamente)

DEFINITION: (a little boat, hence) a boat.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ploion; a boat.

BDAG.en: diminutive of πλοῖον, any kind of relatively small boat, small ship, boat, skiff
BDAG.pt: diminutivo de πλοῖον, qualquer tipo de barco relativamente pequeno, navio pequeno, barco, escafandro

DEFINITION: a ship, vessel, boat.
ORIGIN: From pleo; a sailer, i.e. Vessel.

BDAG.en: Primarily: ‘ship’ of any kind, though esp. a merchant ship. 1 a rather large sea-faring ship, ship. 2 a relatively small fishing vessel, such as would be used on Lake Gennesaret, boat. 3 quite general: a ship
BDAG.pt: Principalmente: 'navio' de qualquer tipo, embora especialmente um navio mercante. 1 um navio de grande porte para o mar, navio. 2 uma embarcação de pesca relativamente pequena, como a usada no Mar da Galileia, barco. 3 de forma geral: um navio

DEFINITION: a voyage, sailing.
ORIGIN: From pleo; a sail, i.e. Navigation.

DEFINITION: rich, abounding in, wealthy; subst: a rich man.
ORIGIN: From ploutos; wealthy; figuratively, abounding with.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to having an abundance of earthly possessions that exceeds normal experience, rich, wealthy. 2 pert. to being plentifully supplied with someth., abound (in), rich (in)
BDAG.pt: 1 relativo a ter uma abundância de bens terrenos que excede a experiência normal, rico, abastado. 2 relativo a estar abundantemente provido de algo, abundar (em), ser rico (em)

DEFINITION: richly, abundantly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from plousios; copiously.

BDAG.en: richly, abundantly
BDAG.pt: ricamente, abundantemente

DEFINITION: to become rich, be rich, abound in.
ORIGIN: From ploutizo; to be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich.

BDAG.en: 1 to be relatively high on a scale of opulence, be rich; aor. become rich; pf. have become rich. 2 to be plentifully supplied with someth., be rich, in imagery
BDAG.pt: 1 ser relativamente alto numa escala de opulência, ser rico; aoristo tornar-se rico; perfeito ter-se tornado rico. 2 ser abundantemente provido de algo, ser rico, em sentido figurado

DEFINITION: to make rich, cause to abound in, enrich.
ORIGIN: From ploutos; to make wealthy (figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 to cause to be relatively high on a scale of opulence, make wealthy. 2 to cause to abound in someth., make rich, in imagery: of spiritual riches
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer com que alguém esteja em um nível alto de opulência, enriquecer alguém. 2 fazer com que algo transborde, tornar rico, em sentido figurado: de riquezas espirituais

DEFINITION: riches, wealth, abundance, materially or spiritually.
ORIGIN: From the base of pletho; wealth (as fulness), i.e. (literally) money, possessions, or (figuratively) abundance, richness, (specially), valuable bestowment.

BDAG.en: 1 abundance of many earthly goods, wealth. 2 plentiful supply of someth., a wealth, abundance, fig. ext. of 1
BDAG.pt: 1 abundância de muitos bens terrenos, riqueza. 2 suprimento farto de algo, uma riqueza, abundância, extensão figurada de 1

DEFINITION: to wash.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of an obsolete pluo (to "flow"); to "plunge", i.e. Launder clothing.

BDAG.en: 1 to wash someth. other than a part of the body, wash. 2 free someth. of someth., free from, i.e. from the impurity of sin
BDAG.pt: 1 lavar algo que não seja uma parte do corpo, lavar. 2 libertar algo de algo, livrar de, isto é, da impureza do pecado

DEFINITION: wind, breath, spirit.
ORIGIN: From pneo; a current of air, i.e. Breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively, a spirit, i.e. (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, demon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy Spirit.
USAGE: ghost, life, spirit(-ual, -ually), mind. Compare psuche.

BDAG.en: spirit, spiritual state, state of mind, disposition; an independent noncorporeal being, spirit; God personally; good, or at least not expressly evil spirits or spirit-beings; Ghost; evil spirits; the Spirit of God, of the Lord (=God); the Spirit of Christ, of the Lord (=Christ); the Holy Spirit; the Spirit (as divine controlling influence); the Spirit of truth; the Spirit of life; the Spirit of faith; the Spirit of adoption; the Spirit of power; the Spirit of grace; a quickening spirit; the Spirit in contrast to the world/flesh/body/letter/human wisdom; spirit as accompanying power, life, or wisdom; spiritual conduct; the Spirit inspiring divine revelation; the Spirit showing variety in spiritual gifts.
BDAG.pt: espírito, estado espiritual, estado de espírito, disposição; um ser não corporal independente, espírito; Deus pessoalmente; espíritos bons, ou pelo menos não expressamente maus, ou seres espirituais; fantasma; espíritos malignos; o Espírito de Deus, do Senhor (=Deus); o Espírito de Cristo, do Senhor (=Cristo); o Espírito Santo; o Espírito (como influência controladora divina); o Espírito da verdade; o Espírito da vida; o Espírito da fé; o Espírito de adoção; o Espírito de poder; o Espírito da graça; um espírito vivificante; o Espírito em contraste com o mundo/carne/corpo/letra/sabedoria humana; espírito como poder, vida ou sabedoria acompanhante; conduta espiritual; o Espírito que inspira a revelação divina; o Espírito que manifesta a variedade nos dons espirituais.

DEFINITION: spiritual.
ORIGIN: From pneuma; non-carnal, i.e. (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (daemoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious.

BDAG.en: pert. to spirit as inner life of a human being, spiritual; in ref. to the divine spirit, having to do with the divine spirit, caused by or filled with the divine spirit, pert./corresponding to the divine spirit; pert. to (evil) spirits.
BDAG.pt: Pertencente ao espírito como a vida interior de um ser humano, espiritual; em referência ao espírito divino, relacionado ao espírito divino, causado ou preenchido pelo espírito divino, pertencente/correspondente ao espírito divino; pertencente a espíritos (maus).

DEFINITION: spiritually, in a spiritual way; from a spiritual point of view.
ORIGIN: Adverb from pneumatikos; non-physically, i.e. Divinely, figuratively.

BDAG.en: pert. to transcendent influence, spiritually, in a spiritual manner, in a manner caused by or filled with the Spirit; pert. to being consistent with transcendent influence, in keeping w. the spirit.
BDAG.pt: Pertencente à influência transcendente, espiritualmente, de maneira espiritual, de uma maneira causada ou preenchida pelo Espírito; pertencente a ser consistente com a influência transcendente, em harmonia com o espírito.

DEFINITION: to blow, breathe, as the wind.
ORIGIN: A primary word; to breathe hard, i.e. Breeze.

BDAG.en: to move as wind, blow; to emit an odor, breathe out; to breathe something out.
BDAG.pt: Mover-se como o vento, soprar; emitir um odor, exalar; exalar algo.

DEFINITION: to choke, throttle, strangle; hence: to drown.
ORIGIN: Strengthened from pneo; to wheeze, i.e. (causative, by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown).

BDAG.en: to apply pressure around the neck in order to kill, strangle; to cause something to be stifled, choke; pass. be choked, drown; fig. be choked by one’s work.
BDAG.pt: apertar ao redor do pescoço para matar, estrangular; fazer com que algo seja sufocado, sufocar; ser sufocado, afogar; fig. ser sufocado pelas obras.

DEFINITION: strangled (i.e. killed without letting out the blood).
ORIGIN: From pnigo; throttled, i.e. (neuter concretely) an animal choked to death (not bled).

BDAG.en: strangled, choked to death (of animals killed without having the blood drained from them, whose flesh the Israelites were forbidden to eat)
BDAG.pt: estrangulado, sufocado até a morte (de animais mortos sem que o sangue fosse drenado, cuja carne era proibida aos israelitas comer)

DEFINITION: (a) breath, (b) gust, breeze, wind.
ORIGIN: From pneo; respiration, a breeze.

BDAG.en: relatively rapid movement of air, wind; the process of breathing, breath; passes over to the meaning of spirit (of God’s breath/spirit).
BDAG.pt: movimento relativamente rápido do ar, vento; o processo de respirar, respiração; passa ao significado de espírito (da respiração/espírito de Deus).

DEFINITION: reaching to the feet (of a garment).
ORIGIN: From pous and another element of uncertain affinity; a dress (esthes implied) reaching the ankles.

BDAG.en: reaching to the feet (a robe reaching to the feet).
BDAG.pt: que chega aos pés (uma veste que chega aos pés).

DEFINITION: whence, from what place.
ORIGIN: From the base of posis with enclitic adverb of origin; from which (as interrogative) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause.

BDAG.en: from where, from which, whence (interrogative expression of extension from a local source, derivation from a source, or cause/reason: how, why).
BDAG.pt: de onde, de qual, donde (expressão interrogativa de extensão de uma fonte local, derivação de uma fonte, ou causa/razão: como, por quê).

DEFINITION: (a) to make, manufacture, construct, (b) to do, act, cause.
ORIGIN: Apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary; to make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct).
USAGE: abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), cast out, cause, commit, + content, continue, deal, + without any delay, (would) do(-ing), execute, exercise, fulfil, gain, give, have, hold, X journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform, provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, X secure, shew, X shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield. Compare prasso.

BDAG.en: A multivalent term: 1. to produce something material, make, manufacture, create (especially of God's creative activity); 2. to undertake or do something that brings about an event, state, or condition (do, cause, accomplish, prepare, etc.), perform miracles; 3. used with nouns as a periphrasis for simple verbs (e.g., make peace, wage war); 4. to give (a meal/banquet); 5. of natural processes (to yield fruit/produce water); 6. regarding capital (to yield a return, make money); 7. causality (to make/cause someone to do something); 8. to keep/celebrate a feast (Passover)
BDAG.pt: Um termo polivalente: 1. produzir algo material, fazer, fabricar, criar (especialmente da atividade criativa de Deus); 2. empreender ou fazer algo que resulta em um evento, estado ou condição (fazer, causar, realizar, preparar, etc.), realizar milagres; 3. usado com substantivos como perífrase para verbos simples (ex: fazer a paz, travar guerra); 4. servir (uma refeição/banquete); 5. de processos naturais (produzir fruto/gerar água); 6. em relação a capital (dar retorno, ganhar dinheiro); 7. causalidade (fazer/causar que alguém faça algo); 8. guardar/celebrar uma festa (Páscoa)

DEFINITION: a thing made, a work, workmanship.
ORIGIN: From poieo; a product, i.e. Fabric (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: that which is made, work, creation, in our literature only of the works of divine creation; we are (God’s) creation.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é feito, obra, criação; em nossa literatura apenas das obras da criação divina; nós somos (criação de Deus).

DEFINITION: a doing, making, performance.
ORIGIN: From poieo; action, i.e. Performance (of the law).

BDAG.en: the process of activity, doing, working; the product of activity, work, creation of the artist (of the Divine Artist).
BDAG.pt: o processo de atividade, fazer, trabalhar; o produto da atividade, obra, criação do artista (do Artista Divino).

DEFINITION: (a) a maker, poet, (b) a doer, carrier out, performer.
ORIGIN: From poieo; a performer; specially, a "poet".

BDAG.en: 1 one who does something by producing something, maker, then specifically poet. 2 one who does what is prescribed, a doer
BDAG.pt: 1 aquele que faz algo produzindo algo, criador, e especificamente poeta. 2 aquele que faz o que é prescrito, um executor

DEFINITION: various, of different colors, diverse, various.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; motley, i.e. Various in character.

BDAG.en: 1 pertaining to existence in various kinds or modes, diversified, manifold. 2 pertaining to existence in various aspects: many-colored, variegated; of persons, crafty, sly, deceitful
BDAG.pt: 1 referente à existência em vários tipos ou modos, diversificado, multifacetado. 2 referente à existência em vários aspectos: multicor, variegado; de pessoas, astuto, ardiloso, enganoso

DEFINITION: to shepherd, tend, herd; hence: to rule, govern.
ORIGIN: From poimen; to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser).

BDAG.en: 1 to serve as tender of sheep, herd, tend, (lead to) pasture. 2 to watch out for other people, to shepherd, of activity that protects, rules, governs, fosters, fig. ext. of 1: a in the sense of lead, guide, or rule. b protect, care for, nurture
BDAG.pt: 1 servir como pastor de ovelhas, apascentar, cuidar, (conduzir ao) pasto. 2 vigiar outras pessoas, pastorear, atividade que protege, governa, fomenta, extensão figurada de 1: a no sentido de liderar, guiar ou governar. b proteger, cuidar, nutrir

DEFINITION: a shepherd; hence met: of the feeder, protector, and ruler of a flock of men.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a shepherd (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: one who herds sheep, shepherd, sheep-herder; one who serves as guardian or leader, shepherd (figuratively, applied to God, Christ, or human leaders/pastors).
BDAG.pt: aquele que apascenta ovelhas, pastor; aquele que serve como guardião ou líder, pastor (figurativamente, aplicado a Deus, Cristo ou líderes humanos/pastores).

DEFINITION: a flock (of sheep or goats).
ORIGIN: Contraction from poimaino; a flock (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: flock, esp. of sheep. In imagery: w. ref. to Jesus’ disciples, to the church and to Jesus as its head
BDAG.pt: rebanho, especialmente de ovelhas. Em linguagem figurada: referente aos discípulos de Jesus, à igreja e a Jesus como seu chefe

DEFINITION: a little flock.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of poimne; a flock, i.e. (figuratively) group (of believers).

BDAG.en: an assemblage of a specific kind of animal, flock (especially of sheep); a defined group of persons under a leader, flock (figuratively, applied to the Christian community or disciples).
BDAG.pt: um ajuntamento de um tipo específico de animal, rebanho (especialmente de ovelhas); um grupo definido de pessoas sob um líder, rebanho (figurativamente, aplicado à comunidade cristã ou discípulos).

DEFINITION: of what sort?.
ORIGIN: From the base of pou and hoios; individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one.

BDAG.en: interrog. pron., in direct and indir. interrog. sentences. 1 interrogative ref. to class or kind, of what kind? 2 (= τίς) which, what?
BDAG.pt: pronome interrogativo, em frases interrogativas diretas e indiretas. 1 interrogativo referente a classe ou tipo, de que tipo? 2 (= τίς) qual, que?

DEFINITION: to make war, contend, fight, battle.
ORIGIN: From polemos.
USAGE: to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. To battle (literally or figuratively); fight, (make) war.

BDAG.en: to wage war, fight (actively or passively); to be in opposition to, be hostile.
BDAG.pt: travar guerra, lutar (ativa ou passivamente); opor-se, ser hostil.

DEFINITION: a war, battle, strife.
ORIGIN: From pelomai (to bustle); warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series).

BDAG.en: military conflict, war, battle, engagement; a state of hostility/antagonism, strife, conflict, quarrel (figuratively).
BDAG.pt: conflito militar, guerra, batalha, combate; um estado de hostilidade/antagonismo, discórdia, conflito, briga (figurativamente).

DEFINITION: a city, the inhabitants of a city.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as polemos, or perhaps from polus; a town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size).

BDAG.en: population center, city, town; (metaphorically) the (heavenly) city, New Jerusalem; inhabitants of a city (abstract for concrete).
BDAG.pt: centro populacional, cidade, urbe; (metaforicamente) a cidade (celestial), Nova Jerusalém; habitantes de uma cidade (abstrato pelo concreto).

DEFINITION: a ruler of a city, city magistrate.
ORIGIN: From polis and archo; a town-officer, i.e. Magistrate.

BDAG.en: a magistrate who formed part of a town or city council, city official.
BDAG.pt: um magistrado que fazia parte de um conselho municipal ou da cidade, funcionário da cidade.

DEFINITION: (a) commonwealth, polity; citizen body, (b) (the Roman) citizenship, citizen-rights, franchise.
ORIGIN: From polites ("polity"); citizenship; concretely, a community.

BDAG.en: 1. the right to be a member of a sociopolitical entity, citizenship; 2. a sociopolitical unit or body of citizens, state, people, body politic; 3. behavior in accordance with standards expected of a respectable citizen, way of life, conduct.
BDAG.pt: 1. o direito de ser membro de uma entidade sociopolítica, cidadania; 2. uma unidade sociopolítica ou corpo de cidadãos, estado, povo, corpo político; 3. comportamento de acordo com os padrões esperados de um cidadão respeitável, modo de vida, conduta.

DEFINITION: a form of government, citizenship.
ORIGIN: From politeuomai; a community, i.e. (abstractly) citizenship (figuratively).

BDAG.en: commonwealth, state.
BDAG.pt: comunidade (ou corpo político), estado.

DEFINITION: to live the life of a citizen, live.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of a derivative of polites; to behave as a citizen (figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1. to be a citizen, have one’s citizenship/home; 2. to administrate a corporate body, rule a state; 3. to conduct one’s life, live, lead one’s life.
BDAG.pt: 1. ser cidadão, ter sua cidadania/lar; 2. administrar um corpo corporativo, governar um estado; 3. conduzir a própria vida, viver, levar a própria vida.

DEFINITION: a citizen, fellow-citizen.
ORIGIN: From polis; a townsman.

BDAG.en: 1. one who lives in or comes from a city or country, citizen; 2. a member of one’s own sociopolitical group, fellow-citizen, compatriot.
BDAG.pt: 1. aquele que vive ou vem de uma cidade ou país, cidadão; 2. um membro do seu próprio grupo sociopolítico, concidadão, compatriota.

DEFINITION: many times, often, frequently.
ORIGIN: Multiplicative adverb from polus; many times, i.e. Frequently.

BDAG.en: many times, often, frequently.
BDAG.pt: muitas vezes, frequentemente.

DEFINITION: many times more, manifold.
ORIGIN: From polus and probably a derivative of pleko; manifold, i.e. (neuter as noun) very much more.

BDAG.en: far in excess of a quantity normally expected, many times as much, manifold.
BDAG.pt: muito além da quantidade normalmente esperada, muitas vezes mais, múltiplo.

DEFINITION: much-speaking, loquacity.
ORIGIN: From a compound of polus and logos; loquacity, i.e. Prolixity.

BDAG.en: speech of tedious length, much speaking, wordiness, long-windedness.
BDAG.pt: fala de comprimento tedioso, muita fala, prolixidade, loquacidade.

DEFINITION: in many parts (one at one time, another at another, and so on).
ORIGIN: Adverb from a compound of polus and meros; in many portions, i.e. Variously as to time and agency (piecemeal).

BDAG.en: of many parts, in various parts (with πολυτρόπως: ‘in various ways’ in prophetic writing).
BDAG.pt: de muitas partes, em várias partes (com πολυτρόπως: ‘de várias maneiras’ na escrita profética).

DEFINITION: much varied, manifold.
ORIGIN: From polus and poikilos; much variegated, i.e. Multifarious.

BDAG.en: pert. to being diversified, (very) many-sided
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser diversificado, (muito) multifacetado

DEFINITION: much, many; often.
ORIGIN: Including the forms from the alternate pollos; (singular) much (in any respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverbial, largely; neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely.
USAGE: abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -ly, while), long, many, much, oft(-en (-times)), plenteous, sore, straitly. Compare pleistos, pleion.

BDAG.en: much, large, great (in quantity, measure, or degree); many (plural); the majority/most (as a noun).
BDAG.pt: muito, grande (em quantidade, medida ou grau); muitos (plural); a maioria/a maior parte (como substantivo).

DEFINITION: very compassionate, of great mercy.
ORIGIN: From polus and splagchnon (figuratively); extremely compassionate.

BDAG.en: pertaining to a very high degree of affection and compassion for someone, sympathetic, compassionate, merciful (of God).
BDAG.pt: relativo a um grau muito elevado de afeto e compaixão por alguém, simpático, compassivo, misericordioso (de Deus).

DEFINITION: very costly, very precious, of great value.
ORIGIN: From polus and telos; extremely expensive.
USAGE: costly, very precious, of great price.

BDAG.en: pert. to being of great value or worth, ordinarily of relatively high degree on a monetary scale, (very) expensive, costly of ointment, clothing, stones, costly establishments. Metaph., of inward adornment (i.e. God appraises it at high value)
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser de grande valor ou mérito, ordinariamente de grau relativamente alto em escala monetária, (muito) caro, custoso de unguento, vestuário, pedras, estabelecimentos dispendiosos. Metaforicamente, de adorno interior (ou seja, Deus o avalia a alto valor)

DEFINITION: of great value, very costly, very precious.
ORIGIN: From polus and time; extremely valuable.

BDAG.en: pert. to being very high on a monetary scale, very precious, valuable of a pearl, of an ointment. Comp. the genuineness (δοκίμιον 2) of (your) faith which is more precious than gold
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser muito alto em escala monetária, muito precioso, valioso de uma pérola, de um unguento. Comparado com a autenticidade (δοκίμιον 2) da (sua) fé que é mais preciosa que ouro

DEFINITION: in many ways.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a compound of polus and tropos; in many ways, i.e. Variously as to method or form.

BDAG.en: adv. fr. πολύτροπος ‘various, manifold’, pert. to a variety of modes of expressing someth., in many ways
BDAG.pt: advérbio de πολύτροπος 'variado, múltiplo', pertencente a uma variedade de modos de expressar algo, de muitas maneiras

DEFINITION: a drink.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of pino; a beverage.

BDAG.en: someth. that satisfies thirst, a drink. Pl., of usual things to drink. In imagery (prob. in ref. to the Eucharist). The typological predecessor of the Eucharist in the OT is seen as the spiritual drink (fr. the spiritual rock that followed them)
BDAG.pt: algo que satisfaz a sede, uma bebida. Plural, de coisas habituais para beber. Em imagética (provavelmente em referência à Eucaristia). O predecessor tipológico da Eucaristia no AT é visto como a bebida espiritual (da rocha espiritual que os seguia)

DEFINITION: wickedness, iniquities.
ORIGIN: From poneros; depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins.

BDAG.en: in our lit. only in the ethical sense: state or condition of a lack of moral or social values, wickedness, baseness, maliciousness, sinfulness. W. ἁρπαγή, w. ἄνοια, w. δολιότης, w. κακία. In the Lord’s Prayer (v.l.). In a catalogue of vices. Cp. where vices are personified. πονηρία μεγάλη. Of children (who know nothing of the wickedness that ruins the life of people). In the objective gen. punishment for wickedness, the reward for wickedness. In gen. of quality (to be rendered as adj.; respectable Gk., but strongly influenced in our lit. by Semitic tradition): evil desire, confusion of wickedness, evil teachers or teachers of wickedness, the spiritual (things) of wickedness, the angel of wickedness. πλείονα πονηρίαν ποιεῖν act more wickedly. Pl., of the various kinds of evil-mindedness and individual expressions of it. αἱπ. ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἐμμένουσιν wickedness remains in their hearts (here the pl. could refer to the plurality of persons involved, since virtually only one kind of wickedness is meant). On πονηρεύεσθαι ποικίλαις πονηρίαις see. πονηρεύομαι.
BDAG.pt: em nossa literatura apenas no sentido ético: estado ou condição de falta de valores morais ou sociais, perversidade, baixeza, malícia, pecaminosidade. Com ἁρπαγή, com ἄνοια, com δολιότης, com κακία. Na Oração do Senhor (v.l.). Em um catálogo de vícios. Compara-se onde os vícios são personificados. Grande perversidade. De crianças (que nada sabem da perversidade que arruína a vida das pessoas). No genitivo objetivo, castigo pela perversidade, a recompensa pela perversidade. No genitivo de qualidade (a ser traduzido como adjetivo; grego respeitável, mas fortemente influenciado em nossa literatura pela tradição semítica): desejo maligno, confusão de maldade, mestres do mal ou mestres da perversidade, as coisas espirituais da perversidade, o anjo da perversidade. πλείονα πονηρίαν ποιεῖν agir mais perversamente. Plural, dos vários tipos de mentalidade perversa e suas expressões individuais. αἱπ. ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἐμμένουσιν a perversidade permanece em seus corações (aqui o plural pode se referir à pluralidade de pessoas envolvidas, visto que virtualmente apenas um tipo de perversidade é pretendido). Sobre πονηρεύεσθαι ποικίλαις πονηρίαις ver. πονηρεύομαι.

USAGE: bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness). See also poneroteros.

BDAG.en: Freq. in Gk. lit. the opp. of ἀγαθός/ καλός or χρηστός. 1 pert. to being morally or socially worthless, wicked, evil, bad, base, worthless, vicious, degenerate. a as adj. α of humans or transcendent beings. ὁπον. ἄνθρωπος. δοῦλος πον. γενεὰπον. Mt 12:34. ἄνδρες πον. rowdies, ruffians. People are called πονηροί in contrast to God. Of hostile spirits τὸπνεῦμα τὸπονηρόν. Pl. Of the evil spirit that contends w. the Holy Spirit for a place in the human soul. ἄγγελος πον. ὁπονηρὸς ἄρχων. β of things βουλή. διαλογισμοί. διδαχή. δόλος. ἐπιθυμία. ἔργον. ἔργα. θησαυρός. καρδία. καρδία πονηρὰἀπιστίας. καταλαλιά. Arrogant καύχησις. λόγοι π. Of the ὁδὸς τοῦθανάτου. ὀφθαλμὸς π. πρᾶγμα. ῥῆμα π. slanderous, evil word. συνείδησις π. evil, guilty conscience. Of a Christian’s name spurn the name as vile (i.e as held only by worthless persons). In the judgment of Christians a close connection w. sin is the chief characteristic of this age: ἐκ τοῦαἰῶνος τοῦἐνεστῶτος πονηροῦ. Cp. αἱἡμέραι πονηραί εἰσιν. B 2:1. Sg. b as subst. α wicked or evil-intentioned person, evildoer. ὁπονηρός (the art. is generic). Pl. πονηροὶκαὶἀγαθοί. Opp. οἱδίκαιοι. W. οἱἀχάριστοι. W. ἁμαρτωλοί. β ὁπονηρός the evil one=the devil (who is not defined as a sinner but as one who is morally destructive). ἐκ τοῦπονηροῦεἶναι be a child of the evil one. The gen. τοῦπονηροῦ can also be taken as masc.
BDAG.pt: Frequente na lit. grega, o oposto de ἀγαθός/ καλός ou χρηστός. 1 pertencente a ser moral ou socialmente inútil, perverso, mau, ruim, baixo, inútil, vicioso, degenerado. a como adjetivo. α de humanos ou seres transcendentes. ὁπον. ἄνθρωπος. δοῦλος πον. γενεὰπον. Mt 12:34. ἄνδρες πον. valentões, rufiões. Pessoas são chamadas πονηροί em contraste com Deus. De espíritos hostis τὸπνεῦμα τὸπονηρόν. Plural. Do espírito maligno que luta com o Espírito Santo por um lugar na alma humana. ἄγγελος πον. ὁπονηρὸς ἄρχων. β de coisas: βουλή. διαλογισμοί. διδαχή. δόλος. ἐπιθυμία. ἔργον. ἔργα. θησαυρός. καρδία. καρδία πονηρὰἀπιστίας. καταλαλιά. Arrogante καύχησις. λόγοι π. Da ὁδὸς τοῦθανάτου. ὀφθαλμὸς π. πρᾶγμα. ῥῆμα π. palavra injuriosa, má. συνείδησις π. consciência má, culpada. Do nome de um cristão, rejeitar o nome como vil (isto é, como mantido apenas por pessoas inúteis). No juízo dos cristãos, uma conexão estreita com o pecado é a principal característica desta era: ἐκ τοῦαἰῶνος τοῦἐνεστῶτος πονηροῦ. Compara-se αἱἡμέραι πονηραί εἰσιν. B 2:1. Singular. b como substantivo: uma pessoa má ou de intenção perversa, malfeitor. ὁπονηρός (o artigo é genérico). Plural. πονηροὶκαὶἀγαθοί. Oposto a οἱδίκαιοι. Com οἱἀχάριστοι. Com ἁμαρτωλοί. β ὁπονηρός o maligno = o diabo (que não é definido como pecador, mas como alguém que é moralmente destrutivo). ἐκ τοῦπονηροῦεἶναι ser filho do maligno. O genitivo τοῦπονηροῦ também pode ser tomado como masculino.
