BDAG.pt: abstrato para concreto embaixador, embaixadores (embaixada).

DEFINITION: to be the elder, to take precedence.
ORIGIN: From the base of presbuteros; to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher).

BDAG.en: be an ambassador/envoy, travel/work as an ambassador.
BDAG.pt: ser um embaixador/enviado, viajar/trabalhar como embaixador.

DEFINITION: an assembly of elders, the Sanhedrin, officers of the church assembly, presbytery.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of presbuteros; the order of elders, i.e. (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery".

BDAG.en: an administrative group concerned with the interests of a specific community, council of elders; as a council in connection with administration of Christian congregations, presbytery.
BDAG.pt: um grupo administrativo preocupado com os interesses de uma comunidade específica, conselho de anciãos; como um conselho em conexão com a administração de congregações cristãs, presbitério.

DEFINITION: elder, usually used as subst.; an elder, a member of the Sanhedrin, an elder of a Christian assembly.
ORIGIN: Comparative of presbus (elderly); older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter".

BDAG.en: pert. to being relatively advanced in age, older, old; a council/elder (in the church context).
BDAG.pt: relativo a ter idade relativamente avançada, mais velho, velho; um conselho/ancião (no contexto da igreja).

DEFINITION: an old man, an ambassador.
ORIGIN: From the same as presbuteros; an old man.

BDAG.en: old man, aged man
BDAG.pt: homem velho, homem idoso

DEFINITION: an aged woman.
ORIGIN: Feminine of presbutes; an old woman.

BDAG.en: old(er) woman, elderly lady
BDAG.pt: mulher velha, senhora idosa

DEFINITION: falling headlong, prone.
ORIGIN: From pro; leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), i.e. Head foremost.

BDAG.en: forward, prostrate, head first, headlong
BDAG.pt: para a frente, prostrado, de cabeça, precipitadamente

DEFINITION: to saw, saw through.
ORIGIN: A strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw); to saw in two.

BDAG.en: saw (in two) as a method of execution
BDAG.pt: serrar (ao meio) como método de execução

DEFINITION: formerly, before.
ORIGIN: Adverb from pro; prior, sooner.

BDAG.en: before, formerly (adverb); before (conjunction/preposition)
BDAG.pt: antes, anteriormente (advérbio); antes (conjunção/preposição)

DEFINITION: Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Prisca (Priscilla), tentmaker
BDAG.pt: Prisca (Priscila), fabricante de tendas

DEFINITION: Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of Priska; Priscilla (i.e. Little Prisca), a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Priscilla (a proper name)
BDAG.pt: Priscila (nome próprio)

DEFINITION: (a) of place: before, in front of, (b) of time: before, earlier than.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition; "fore", i.e. In front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to.
USAGE: above, ago, before, or ever. In the comparative, it retains the same significations.

BDAG.en: before, in front of, at; earlier than; above all, especially
BDAG.pt: antes, em frente de, em; mais cedo do que; acima de tudo, especialmente

DEFINITION: (a) trans: to lead forth; in the judicial sense, into court, (b) intrans. and trans: to precede, go before, (c) intrans: to go too far.
ORIGIN: From pro and ago; to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time (participle, previous)).

BDAG.en: to take or lead from one position to another by taking charge, lead forward, lead or bring out; to move ahead or in front of, go before, precede; to go or come ahead of someone
BDAG.pt: levar ou conduzir de uma posição para outra assumindo a liderança, conduzir para a frente, trazer para fora; mover-se adiante ou à frente, ir antes, preceder; ir ou chegar antes de alguém

DEFINITION: to propose; mid: to propose to myself, purpose.
ORIGIN: From pro and haireomai; to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend).

BDAG.en: to set something forth, bring or take out; to reach a decision beforehand, choose (for oneself), commit oneself to, prefer; undertake, determine, decide, make up one’s mind
BDAG.pt: apresentar algo, trazer ou tirar; chegar a uma decisão antecipadamente, escolher (para si), comprometer-se com, preferir; empreender, determinar, decidir, formar uma opinião

DEFINITION: to make a prior accusation.
ORIGIN: From pro and a derivative of aitia; to accuse already, i.e. Previously charge.

BDAG.en: to reach a charge of guilt prior to an implied time, accuse beforehand
BDAG.pt: chegar a uma acusação de culpa antes de um tempo implícito, acusar antecipadamente

DEFINITION: to hear beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and akouo; to hear already,i.e. Anticipate.

BDAG.en: hear beforehand
BDAG.pt: ouvir antecipadamente

DEFINITION: to sin previously.
ORIGIN: From pro and hamartano; to sin previously (to conversion).

BDAG.en: sin beforehand
BDAG.pt: pecar antecipadamente

DEFINITION: a porch, court before a building, vestibule.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed compound of pro and aule; a forecourt, i.e. Vestibule (alley-way).

BDAG.en: place in front of a house, forecourt, gateway
BDAG.pt: lugar em frente a uma casa, pátio frontal, portal

DEFINITION: to go forward, advance.
ORIGIN: From pro and the base of basis; to walk forward, i.e. Advance (literally, or in years).
USAGE: + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken.

BDAG.en: to make a forward movement, go ahead, advance; to make an advance in time, advance in years
BDAG.pt: fazer um movimento para a frente, ir adiante, avançar; fazer um avanço no tempo, avançar em anos

DEFINITION: to thrust forward, put forth (as of branches), produce.
ORIGIN: From pro and ballo; to throw forward, i.e. Push to the front, germinate.

BDAG.en: to cause to come forward, put forward; to send out new growth, put out foliage or fruit
BDAG.pt: fazer vir para a frente, colocar à frente; enviar novo crescimento, brotar folhagem ou fruto

DEFINITION: pertaining to sheep.
ORIGIN: From probaton; relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem.

BDAG.en: pert. to (a) sheep, sheep gate
BDAG.pt: pertencente a (ovelha), porta das ovelhas

DEFINITION: a little sheep.
ORIGIN: Probably neuter of a presumed derivative of probaino; something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: sheep; people of God, sheep
BDAG.pt: ovelha; povo de Deus, ovelhas

DEFINITION: to lead forward, lead on; met: to induce, incite, urge.
ORIGIN: From pro and a reduplicated form of biazo; to force forward, i.e. Bring to the front, instigate.

BDAG.en: cause to come forward; incite, urge on [beforehand], prompt, lead on to, train in, instruct, teach, inculcate
BDAG.pt: fazer vir para a frente; incitar, instar [antecipadamente], impulsionar, levar a, treinar em, instruir, ensinar, inculcar

DEFINITION: to provide, foresee.
ORIGIN: From pro and blepo; to look out beforehand, i.e. Furnish in advance.

DEFINITION: to happen (come about) previously.
ORIGIN: From pro and ginomai; to be already, i.e. Have previousy transpired.

BDAG.en: to originate in time before, be born earlier, happen or be done before
BDAG.pt: originar-se no tempo anterior, nascer mais cedo, acontecer ou ser feito antes

DEFINITION: to know beforehand, foreknow.
ORIGIN: From pro and ginosko; to know beforehand, i.e. Foresee.

BDAG.en: to know beforehand or in advance, have foreknowledge (of) something; choose beforehand; know from time past
BDAG.pt: saber de antemão ou com antecedência, ter pressentimento (de) algo; escolher antecipadamente; saber desde tempos passados

DEFINITION: foreknowledge, previous determination.
ORIGIN: From proginosko; forethought.

BDAG.en: foreknowledge; predetermination, of God’s omniscient wisdom and intention
BDAG.pt: conhecimento prévio; predeterminação, da sabedoria e intenção onisciente de Deus

DEFINITION: born before.
ORIGIN: From proginomai; an ancestor, (grand-)parent.

BDAG.en: parents, forebears, ancestors
BDAG.pt: pais, antepassados, ancestrais

DEFINITION: (a) to write previously (aforetime); to write above (already), (b) to depict or portray openly, (c) to designate beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and grapho; to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe.
USAGE: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime).

BDAG.en: to write in advance or before, write beforehand (in the same document); what is written before (in an older document); mark out, designate for something; to set forth for public notice, show forth/portray publicly, proclaim or placard in public
BDAG.pt: escrever antecipadamente ou antes, escrever de antemão (no mesmo documento); o que foi escrito antes (em um documento mais antigo); demarcar, designar para algo; expor para notificação pública, mostrar/retratar publicamente, proclamar ou afixar em público

DEFINITION: manifest to all, evident, very clear.
ORIGIN: From pro and delos; plain before all men, i.e. Obvious.

BDAG.en: pert. to something that is quite obvious, clear, evident, known (to all); make clear
BDAG.pt: pertencente a algo que é bem óbvio, claro, evidente, conhecido (por todos); tornar claro

DEFINITION: to give before, give forth, betray.
ORIGIN: From pro and didomi; to give before the other party has given.

BDAG.en: to be beforehand in giving, give in advance; to hand over in a treacherous manner, betray
BDAG.pt: ser o primeiro a dar, dar antecipadamente; entregar de maneira traiçoeira, trair

DEFINITION: a betrayer, traitor.
ORIGIN: From prodidomi (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands); a surrender.

BDAG.en: traitor, betrayer
BDAG.pt: traidor, aquele que trai

DEFINITION: a precursor, forerunner, advance guard.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of protrecho; a runner ahead, i.e. Scout (figuratively, precursor).

BDAG.en: pert. to being a precursor, going (lit. running) before, going ahead, also subst.
BDAG.pt: Pertinente a ser um precursor, indo (lit. correndo) adiante, indo à frente, também substantivo.

DEFINITION: to see beforehand, be mindful.
ORIGIN: From pro and eido; foresee.

DEFINITION: to hope before, be the first to hope.
ORIGIN: From pro and elpizo; to hope in advance of other confirmation.

BDAG.en: to be prior in hoping, hope before, be the first to hope
BDAG.pt: Ser anterior em esperança, esperar antes, ser o primeiro a esperar.

DEFINITION: to say previously, predict, proclaim, foretell.
ORIGIN: From pro and epo; to say already, to predict.
USAGE: forewarn, say (speak, tell) before. Compare proereo.

DEFINITION: to begin before.
ORIGIN: From pro and enarchomai; to commence already.

BDAG.en: begin (beforehand) so that the beginning lies in the past as contrasted w. the present
BDAG.pt: começar (antecipadamente) de modo que o começo fique no passado em contraste com o presente

DEFINITION: to promise beforehand.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pro and epaggello; to promise of old.

DEFINITION: to say already, predict, foretell.
ORIGIN: From pro and ereo; used as alternate of proepo; to say already, predict.

DEFINITION: to go forward, go on, advance; to go before, precede.
ORIGIN: From pro and erchomai (including its alternate); to go onward, precede (in place or time).
USAGE: go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on.

BDAG.en: to continue to advance, go forward, advance; to precede as leader/guide, go before; to precede so as to be ahead, come/go before someone, go on before or ahead; Arrive at a place before someone; to come to the fore, come out, proceed
BDAG.pt: Continuar a avançar, ir para a frente, avançar; preceder como líder/guia, ir à frente; preceder de modo a estar à frente, vir/ir antes de alguém, ir adiante ou à frente; Chegar a um lugar antes de alguém; vir à tona, sair, proceder.

DEFINITION: to prepare or appoint beforehand, predestine.
ORIGIN: From pro and hetoimazo; to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: prepare beforehand
BDAG.pt: Preparar de antemão.

DEFINITION: to preach the gospel beforehand, foretell good tidings.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pro and euaggelizo; to announce glad news in advance.

BDAG.en: proclaim good news in advance
BDAG.pt: Proclamar as boas novas antecipadamente.

DEFINITION: trans: to hold before; mid: to excuse myself; intrans: to project, excel, surpass, have preeminence.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pro and echo; to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel.

BDAG.en: to be in a prominent position, jut out, excel, be first; (in Ro 3:9) are we excelled? i.e. are we in a worse position? or have we lost our advantage?; have an advantage; hold someth. before oneself for protection
BDAG.pt: Estar em posição proeminente, projetar-se, sobressair, ser o primeiro; (em Ro 3:9) somos ultrapassados? ou seja, estamos em pior situação? ou perdemos nossa vantagem?; ter uma vantagem; manter algo diante de si para proteção.

DEFINITION: to lead onward by example, go before, prefer.
ORIGIN: From pro and hegeomai; to lead the way for others, i.e. Show deference.

BDAG.en: to go first and lead the way, go before and show the way; to be in a position of leadership, preside; (in Ro 12:10) try to outdo one another in showing respect, consider better, esteem more highly
BDAG.pt: Ir primeiro e mostrar o caminho, ir à frente e indicar o caminho; estar em posição de liderança, presidir; (em Ro 12:10) tentar superar um ao outro em demonstrar respeito, considerar melhor, estimar mais altamente.

DEFINITION: a setting forth, the show-bread; predetermination, purpose.
ORIGIN: From protithemai; a setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God.

BDAG.en: setting forth of someth. in public, setting forth, putting out, presentation; that which is planned in advance, plan, purpose, resolve, will
BDAG.pt: Exposição de algo em público, exposição, apresentação; aquilo que é planejado antecipadamente, plano, propósito, resolução, vontade.

DEFINITION: appointed before; a previously-appointed time.
ORIGIN: From pro and a derivative of tithemi; fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with hemera implied) a designated day.

BDAG.en: a point of time set in advance, appointed day, fixed/limited time
BDAG.pt: um ponto de tempo fixado antecipadamente, dia marcado, tempo determinado/limitado

DEFINITION: inclination, readiness, eagerness, willingness, promptness.
ORIGIN: From prothumos; predisposition, i.e. Alacrity.
USAGE: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.

BDAG.en: exceptional interest in being of service, willingness, readiness, goodwill
BDAG.pt: interesse excepcional em ser prestativo, disposição, prontidão, boa vontade

DEFINITION: eager, ready, willing, prompt.
ORIGIN: From pro and thumos; forward in spirit, i.e. Predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity.

BDAG.en: pert. to being eager to be of service, ready, willing, eager, of the spirit
BDAG.pt: relativo a estar ansioso para servir, pronto, disposto, ávido, do espírito

DEFINITION: readily, eagerly, with a ready mind, cheerfully.
ORIGIN: Adverb from prothumos; with alacrity.

BDAG.en: pert. to being eager to be of service, willingly, eagerly, freely
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao ser ávido por servir, voluntariamente, com entusiasmo, livremente

DEFINITION: to preside, rule over, give attention to, direct, maintain, practice diligently.
ORIGIN: From pro and histemi; to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise.

BDAG.en: to exercise a position of leadership, rule, direct, be at the head (of), manage, conduct; to have an interest in, show concern for, care for, give aid; Busy oneself with, engage in
BDAG.pt: exercer uma posição de liderança, governar, dirigir, estar à frente, administrar, conduzir; ter interesse em, mostrar preocupação com, cuidar, ajudar; Ocupar-se com, engajar-se em

DEFINITION: to provoke, stimulate, challenge, call out.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pro and kaleo; to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate.

DEFINITION: to announce beforehand, promise, predict.
ORIGIN: From pro and kataggello; to anounce beforehand, i.e. Predict, promise.

BDAG.en: to announce beforehand, foretell of prophetic utterance; give information concerning someth. beforehand, i.e. foretell someth.
BDAG.pt: anunciar antecipadamente, predizer por profecia; dar informação a respeito de algo previamente, isto é, prever algo

DEFINITION: to prepare or complete beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and katartizo; to prepare in advance.

BDAG.en: get ready, make arrangements for in advance
BDAG.pt: preparar, fazer arranjos antecipadamente

DEFINITION: to be set (placed, put) before, be already there.
ORIGIN: From pro and keimai; to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward).

BDAG.en: to be open to public view, be exposed; to be present before one, lie before, be present; to be subsequent to some point of time as prospect, of a goal or destination, lie or be set before someone; Also be in prospect
BDAG.pt: estar aberto à vista pública, estar exposto; estar presente diante de alguém, estar à frente, estar presente; ser subsequente a um ponto no tempo como perspectiva, de uma meta ou destino, estar ou ser posto diante de alguém; Estar em perspectiva

DEFINITION: to announce or preach beforehand, announce by herald.
ORIGIN: From pro and kerusso; to herald (i.e. Proclaim) in advance.

BDAG.en: proclaim publicly
BDAG.pt: proclamar publicamente

DEFINITION: progress, advancement.
ORIGIN: From prokopto; progress, i.e. Advancement (subjectively or objectively).

BDAG.en: a movement forward to an improved state, progress, advancement, furtherance
BDAG.pt: um movimento para a frente para um estado melhorado, progresso, avanço, fomento

DEFINITION: (originally of the pioneer cutting his way through brushwood), to advance, progress, make progress.
ORIGIN: From pro and kopto; to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along).
USAGE: increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax.

BDAG.en: to move forward to a final stage, of time be advanced, be far gone; to move forward to an improved state, progress, advance in what is good or in what is bad
BDAG.pt: mover-se para a frente para um estágio final, do tempo estar avançado, estar longe; mover-se para frente para um estado melhorado, progredir, avançar no que é bom ou no que é mau

DEFINITION: a prejudgment, prejudice, partiality, preference.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pro and krino; a prejudgment (prejudice), i.e. Prepossession.

BDAG.en: a judgment that involves taking a side beforehand, prejudgment, discrimination
BDAG.pt: um julgamento que envolve tomar partido antecipadamente, pré-julgamento, discriminação

DEFINITION: to establish or ratify before.
ORIGIN: From pro and kuroo; to ratify previously.

BDAG.en: make valid/ ratify in advance
BDAG.pt: tornar válido/ ratificar antecipadamente

DEFINITION: to take before, anticipate; pass: to be caught or overtaken, taken by surprise.
ORIGIN: From pro and lambano; to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise.

BDAG.en: to do something that involves some element of temporal priority, anticipate something; take it upon oneself, undertake; take, get of a meal; ascertain something by surprise, detect, overtake, surprise
BDAG.pt: fazer algo que envolve algum elemento de prioridade temporal, antecipar algo; assumir, empreender; pegar, tomar (uma refeição); averiguar algo por surpresa, detectar, alcançar, surpreender

DEFINITION: to tell (say) beforehand, forewarn, declare, tell plainly.
ORIGIN: From pro and lego; to say beforehand, i.e. Predict, forewarn.

BDAG.en: to say someth. in advance of an event, tell beforehand/ in advance; to say/express someth. at a point of time that is prior to another point of time, state beforehand/earlier
BDAG.pt: dizer algo antecipadamente a um evento, contar antes/antecipadamente; dizer/expressar algo em um ponto de tempo que é anterior a outro ponto de tempo, declarar previamente/anteriormente

DEFINITION: to predict, testify or protest beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and marturomai; to be a witness in advance i.e. Predict.

BDAG.en: to speak with solemn assurance about someth. that is to happen, bear witness to beforehand, predict someth.
BDAG.pt: falar com certeza solene sobre algo que vai acontecer, testemunhar antecipadamente, predizer algo

DEFINITION: to meditate beforehand, prepare, get up, premeditate.
ORIGIN: From pro and meletao; to premeditate.

BDAG.en: to prepare beforehand by giving careful thought and attention, practice beforehand, prepare
BDAG.pt: preparar antecipadamente dando pensamento e atenção cuidadosos, praticar previamente, preparar

DEFINITION: to be anxious beforehand, ponder beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and merimnao; to care (anxiously) in advance.

BDAG.en: to worry beforehand, concern oneself or be anxious beforehand
BDAG.pt: preocupar-se antecipadamente, preocupar-se ou ficar ansioso antecipadamente

DEFINITION: to take thought for beforehand, provide for, practice.
ORIGIN: From pro and noieo; to consider in advance, i.e. Look out for beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself).

BDAG.en: to give careful thought to, take thought for, take into consideration, have regard for; to think about beforehand in a solicitous manner, care for, provide for someone/something
BDAG.pt: dar pensamento cuidadoso, pensar em, levar em consideração, ter em conta; pensar antecipadamente de maneira solícita, cuidar, prover para alguém/algo

DEFINITION: forethought, foresight, provision for, providence.
ORIGIN: From pronoeo; forethought, i.e. Provident care or supply.

BDAG.en: thoughtful planning to meet a need, forethought, foresight, providence esp. with reference to divine beneficence; to make provision for someth., be concerned for or about someth.
BDAG.pt: planejamento atencioso para suprir uma necessidade, previsão, perspicácia, providência especialmente com referência à beneficência divina; prover para algo, preocupar-se ou cuidar de algo

DEFINITION: to see beforehand, foresee, see previously, be mindful of; mid: to pay regard to, set before me.
ORIGIN: From pro and horao; to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view.

BDAG.en: to see in advance, foresee with an eye to the future; to see at a time prior to the present, see previously; mid. have before one’s eyes, see before one
BDAG.pt: ver com antecedência, prever com vista ao futuro; ver em um tempo anterior ao presente, ver anteriormente; na voz média, ter diante dos olhos, ver à frente

DEFINITION: to foreordain, predetermine, mark out beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and horizo; to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively) predetermine.

BDAG.en: decide upon beforehand, predetermine, of God
BDAG.pt: decidir de antemão, predeterminar, a respeito de Deus

DEFINITION: to suffer previously.
ORIGIN: From pro and pascho; to undergo hardship previously.

BDAG.en: suffer previously
BDAG.pt: sofrer anteriormente

DEFINITION: to send forward, accompany, equip for a journey.
ORIGIN: From pro and pempo; to send forward, i.e. Escort or aid in travel.
USAGE: accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth.

BDAG.en: send forth; to conduct someone who has a destination in mind, accompany, escort; to assist someone in making a journey, send on one’s way with food, money, by arranging for companions, means of travel, etc.
BDAG.pt: enviar adiante; conduzir alguém que tem um destino em mente, acompanhar, escoltar; ajudar alguém em uma jornada, enviar com provisões, dinheiro, arranjando companheiros, meios de transporte, etc.

DEFINITION: falling forward, headlong.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pro and pipto; falling forward, i.e. Headlong (figuratively, precipitate).

BDAG.en: only fig. pert. to being impetuous, rash, reckless, thoughtless
BDAG.pt: apenas figurativamente referente a ser impetuoso, imprudente, temerário, irrefletido

DEFINITION: to make to go before, to cause to go before.
ORIGIN: From pro and poreuomai; to precede (as guide or herald).

BDAG.en: go on before
BDAG.pt: ir adiante

DEFINITION: advantageous for, at (denotes local proximity), toward (denotes motion toward a place).
ORIGIN: A strengthened form of pro; a preposition of direction; forward to, i.e. Toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. Pertaining to; with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. Near to; usually with the accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, i.e. Whither or for which it is predicated).
USAGE: about, according to, against, among, at, because of, before, between, (where-)by, for, X at thy house, in, for intent, nigh unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), X together, to (you) -ward, unto, with(-in). In the comparative case, it denotes essentially the same applications, namely, motion towards, accession to, or nearness at.

BDAG.en: preposition expressing direction 'on the side of', 'in the direction of': w. gen. 'from', dat. 'at', or acc. 'to'; marker of direction or aspect from which something is determined, to the advantage of, advantageous for; marker of closeness of relation or proximity (a of place near, at, by; b in addition to); marker of movement or orientation toward someone/something; marker of time near, at, or during; marker of goal (aiming) at or (striving) toward; of relationship (hostile or friendly), against, for (a hostile against; b friendly to, toward, with, before); to indicate a connection by marking a point of reference, with reference/regard to; in comparison with, to be compared to; expressing purpose; in adverbial expressions; by, at, near
BDAG.pt: preposição que expressa direção 'ao lado de', 'na direção de': com genitivo 'de', dativo 'em', ou acusativo 'para'; marcador de direção ou aspecto de onde algo é determinado, para a vantagem de, vantajoso para; marcador de proximidade de relação ou proximidade (a de lugar perto, em, ao lado de; b além de); marcador de movimento ou orientação em direção a alguém/algo; marcador de tempo perto, em, ou durante; marcador de objetivo (mirando) em ou (esforçando-se) em direção a; de relacionamento (hostil ou amigável), contra, para (a hostil contra; b amigável a, para com, com, diante de); para indicar uma conexão marcando um ponto de referência, com referência/respeito a; em comparação com, para ser comparado a; expressando propósito; em expressões adverbiais; por, em, perto de

DEFINITION: the day before the Sabbath.
ORIGIN: From pro and sabbaton; a fore-sabbath, i.e. The Sabbath-eve.
USAGE: day before the sabbath. Compare paraskeue.

BDAG.en: the day before the Sabbath, i.e. Friday
BDAG.pt: o dia anterior ao sábado, ou seja, sexta-feira

DEFINITION: to address by name, designate, accost.
ORIGIN: From pros and a derivative of agora (mean to harangue); to address, i.e. Salute by name.

BDAG.en: to say hello, greet; to refer to someone by name or some other term, call, name, designate
BDAG.pt: saudar, cumprimentar; referir-se a alguém pelo nome ou outro termo, chamar, nomear, designar

DEFINITION: to bring to, bring near; to come to or towards, approach.
ORIGIN: From pros and ago; to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach.

BDAG.en: bring into someone’s presence, bring (forward); fig. of Christ, who brings people to God; as a technical term of sacrificial procedure, bring, present, offer (cultic) worship to God; move toward a reference point, come near, approach
BDAG.pt: trazer à presença de alguém, trazer (adiante); fig. de Cristo, que traz as pessoas a Deus; como termo técnico de procedimento sacrificial, trazer, apresentar, oferecer culto (cultual) a Deus; mover-se em direção a um ponto de referência, chegar perto, aproximar-se

DEFINITION: approach, access, admission.
ORIGIN: From prosago (compare agoge); admission.

BDAG.en: a way of approach, access
BDAG.pt: um modo de aproximação, acesso

DEFINITION: to beg, ask earnestly, ask for in addition.
ORIGIN: From pros and aiteo; to ask repeatedly (importune), i.e. Solicit.

BDAG.en: beg
BDAG.pt: pedir esmola

DEFINITION: to go up to, come up to, go up further.
ORIGIN: From pros and anabaino; to ascend farther, i.e. Be promoted (take an upper (more honorable) seat).

BDAG.en: to go up from one level to another, go up, move up
BDAG.pt: subir de um nível para outro, subir, mover-se para cima

DEFINITION: to spend in addition.
ORIGIN: From pros and analisko; to expend further.

DEFINITION: to fill up by adding to, supply.
ORIGIN: From pros and anapleroo; to fill up further, i.e. Furnish fully.

BDAG.en: to fill up or replenish besides, supply someone’s wants
BDAG.pt: completar ou reabastecer além disso, suprir as necessidades de alguém

DEFINITION: to lay on besides, to undertake besides (mid.).
ORIGIN: From pros and anatithemai; to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult.

BDAG.en: to add something to an existing amount, add or contribute; to take up a matter with, consult with
BDAG.pt: adicionar algo a uma quantia existente, acrescentar ou contribuir; levar um assunto a, consultar com

DEFINITION: to utter additional threats.
ORIGIN: From pros and apeileo; to menace additionally.

BDAG.en: threaten further / in addition
BDAG.pt: ameaçar mais / adicionalmente

DEFINITION: to spend in addition.
ORIGIN: From pros and dapanao; to expend additionally.

BDAG.en: spend in addition
BDAG.pt: gastar a mais

DEFINITION: to want more, need in addition.
ORIGIN: From pros and deomai; to require additionally, i.e. Want further.

BDAG.en: to have need of something, need
BDAG.pt: ter necessidade de algo, necessitar

DEFINITION: (a) to await, expect, (b) to receive, welcome (originally: to house), (c) to accept.
ORIGIN: From pros and dechomai; to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence, or (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await (with confidence or patience).

BDAG.en: to receive favorably, take up, receive, welcome; refuse to accept, reject; to look forward to, wait for
BDAG.pt: receber favoravelmente, acolher, receber, dar as boas-vindas; recusar aceitar, rejeitar; esperar ansiosamente, aguardar

DEFINITION: to expect, wait for, await, think, anticipate.
ORIGIN: From pros and dokeuo (to watch); to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication, to await.
USAGE: (be in) expect(-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for.

BDAG.en: to give thought to something that is viewed as lying in the future, wait for, look for, expect
BDAG.pt: pensar em algo que se vê como estando no futuro, esperar, procurar, contar com

DEFINITION: expectation, waiting.
ORIGIN: From prosdokao; apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated.

BDAG.en: expectation of something that is to happen, whether good or bad, expectation
BDAG.pt: expectativa de algo que vai acontecer, seja bom ou mau, expectativa

DEFINITION: to permit one to approach, permit further.
ORIGIN: From pros and eao; to permit further progress.

BDAG.en: permit to go farther
BDAG.pt: permitir ir mais longe

DEFINITION: to approach, come near to.
ORIGIN: From pros and eggizo; to approach near.

BDAG.en: to move toward a reference point, approach, come near
BDAG.pt: mover-se em direção a um ponto de referência, aproximar-se, chegar perto

DEFINITION: to wait upon, minister to, have charge of.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pros and the base of hedraios; to sit near, i.e. Attend as a servant.

BDAG.en: to be beside so as to be in attendance, attend, serve, wait upon, lit. ‘sit near’
BDAG.pt: estar ao lado para estar em atendimento, assistir, servir, esperar, literalmente 'sentar perto'

DEFINITION: to work besides, to gain besides.
ORIGIN: From pros and ergazomai; to work additionally, i.e. (by implication) acquire besides.

BDAG.en: to earn in addition, make more
BDAG.pt: ganhar a mais, render mais

DEFINITION: to come up to, come to, come near (to), approach, consent (to).
ORIGIN: From pros and erchomai (including its alternate); to approach, i.e. (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to.
USAGE: (as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto).

BDAG.en: to move towards (physical movement); approach (to a deity's presence, cultic sense); of inanimate things, come upon; to apply oneself to something, turn to, occupy oneself with a thing
BDAG.pt: mover-se em direção a (movimento físico); aproximar-se (à presença de uma divindade, sentido cultual); de coisas inanimadas, sobrevir; aplicar-se a algo, voltar-se para, ocupar-se com algo

DEFINITION: (a) prayer (to God), (b) a place for prayer (used by Jews, perhaps where there was no synagogue).
ORIGIN: From proseuchomai; prayer (worship); by implication, an oratory (chapel).

BDAG.en: petition addressed to deity, prayer; a place of or for prayer, place of prayer
BDAG.pt: súplica dirigida à divindade, oração; um lugar de ou para oração, local de oração

DEFINITION: to pray, pray for, offer prayer.
ORIGIN: From pros and euchomai; to pray to God, i.e. Supplicate, worship.

BDAG.en: to petition deity, pray
BDAG.pt: suplicar à divindade, orar

DEFINITION: (a) to attend to, pay attention to, (b) to beware, be cautious, (c) to join, devote myself to.
ORIGIN: From pros and echo; (figuratively) to hold the mind (nous implied) towards, i.e. Pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to.
USAGE: (give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard.

BDAG.en: to be in a state of alert, be concerned about, care for, take care; to pay close attention to someth., pay attention to, give heed to, follow; to continue in close attention to someth., occupy oneself with, devote or apply oneself to
BDAG.pt: estar em estado de alerta, preocupar-se com, cuidar de, ter cuidado; prestar muita atenção a algo, prestar atenção, dar ouvidos, seguir; continuar em atenção próxima a algo, ocupar-se com, devotar-se ou aplicar-se a

DEFINITION: to fasten with nails, nail to.
ORIGIN: From pros and a derivative of helos; to peg to, i.e. Spike fast.

BDAG.en: nail (fast) something to something; crucify
BDAG.pt: crucificar; pregar (fixar) algo a algo

DEFINITION: (lit: that has come to), a proselyte, that is a non-Jew, who has been circumcised and has adopted the Jews' religion.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of proserchomai; an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte").

BDAG.en: one who has come over from polytheism to Judean religion and practice, convert.
BDAG.pt: aquele que se converteu do politeísmo para a religião e prática judaica, convertido.

DEFINITION: for a season, temporary.
ORIGIN: From pros and kairos; for the occasion only, i.e. Temporary.
USAGE: dur-(eth) for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal.

BDAG.en: lasting only for a time, temporary, transitory.
BDAG.pt: durando apenas por um tempo, temporário, transitório.

DEFINITION: to call to myself, summon.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pros and kaleo; to call toward oneself, i.e. Summon, invite.

BDAG.en: to call to or notify in order to secure someone’s presence; to call (to) God or Christ, to faith, etc. (divine invitation); to call in a legal or official sense; to call to a special task or office.
BDAG.pt: chamar ou notificar para garantir a presença de alguém; chamar a Deus ou a Cristo, à fé, etc. (convite divino); chamar em sentido legal ou oficial; chamar para uma tarefa ou ofício especial.

DEFINITION: to persist, persevere in, continue steadfast in; to wait upon.
ORIGIN: From pros and kartereo; to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor).
USAGE: attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually).

BDAG.en: to stick by or be close at hand, attach oneself to, wait on, be faithful to someone; to persist in something; busy oneself with, be busily engaged in, be devoted to; hold fast to, continue in, persevere in something
BDAG.pt: persistir ao lado de ou estar por perto, se apegar a, servir, ser fiel a alguém; persistir em algo; ocupar-se com, estar ativamente envolvido em, ser dedicado a; agarrar-se a, continuar em, perseverar em algo

DEFINITION: steadfastness.
ORIGIN: From proskartereo; persistancy.

BDAG.en: firm persistence in an undertaking or circumstance, perseverance, patience
BDAG.pt: persistência firme em um empreendimento ou circunstância, perseverança, paciência.

DEFINITION: a pillow or cushion.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed compound of pros and kephale; something for the head, i.e. A cushion.

BDAG.en: an object on which one may rest one’s head, pillow
BDAG.pt: um objeto sobre o qual se pode repousar a cabeça, travesseiro.

DEFINITION: to assign by lot, allot, associate with, follow as a disciple.
ORIGIN: From pros and kleroo; to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to associate with.

BDAG.en: to be in close association, be attached to, join someone
BDAG.pt: estar em estreita associação, ser ligado a, juntar-se a alguém

DEFINITION: partiality, an inclination towards.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pros and klino; a leaning towards, i.e. (figuratively) proclivity (favoritism).

BDAG.en: (see πρόσκλισις)
BDAG.pt: (ver πρόσκλισις)

DEFINITION: (lit: to glue one thing to another), to join (unite) closely, cleave (to), follow as an adherent.
ORIGIN: From pros and kollao; to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere.

BDAG.en: to adhere to closely, be faithfully devoted to, join someone (used intr. with the lit. sense ‘stick to’)
BDAG.pt: aderir intimamente, ser fielmente devotado a, juntar-se a alguém (usado intransitivamente com o sentido literal de 'aderir')

DEFINITION: a stumbling-block, an occasion for falling, a moral embarrassment.
ORIGIN: From proskopto; a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy.

BDAG.en: act of stumbling, stumbling itself; opportunity to experience inward pain or make a misstep, cause for offense, cause for making a misstep (obstacle, hindrance)
BDAG.pt: ato de tropeçar, o tropeço em si; oportunidade de experimentar dor interior ou dar um passo em falso, motivo de ofensa, causa para um tropeço (obstáculo, impedimento)

DEFINITION: a cause of stumbling, offense, shock.
ORIGIN: From proskopto; a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin.

BDAG.en: an occasion for taking offense or for making a misstep, fig.
BDAG.pt: uma ocasião para se ofender ou para dar um passo em falso, fig.

DEFINITION: to stumble, strike the foot against, beat upon, take offense at.
ORIGIN: From pros and kopto; to strike at, i.e. Surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. Trip up (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to cause to strike against something, strike against; to make contact with something in a bruising or violent manner, beat against, stumble; to experience or cause offense, take offense at, feel repugnance for, reject; give offense
BDAG.pt: fazer algo colidir, bater contra; fazer contato com algo de maneira contundente ou violenta, bater contra, tropeçar; experimentar ou causar ofensa, ofender-se, sentir repugnância, rejeitar; dar ofensa

DEFINITION: to roll to, roll up against.
ORIGIN: From pros and kulioo; to roll towards, i.e. Block against.

BDAG.en: roll (up to) something
BDAG.pt: rolar (até) algo

DEFINITION: to go down on knees to, do obeisance to, worship.
ORIGIN: From pros and a probable derivative of kuon (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand); to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore).

BDAG.en: to express in attitude or gesture one’s complete dependence on or submission to a high authority figure, (fall down and) worship, do obeisance to, prostrate oneself before, do reverence to, welcome respectfully
BDAG.pt: expressar em atitude ou gesto a completa dependência ou submissão a uma autoridade superior, (prostrar-se e) adorar, prestar homenagem, prostrar-se diante, fazer reverência, acolher respeitosamente.

DEFINITION: a worshipper.
ORIGIN: From proskuneo; an adorer.

BDAG.en: worshiper
BDAG.pt: adorador.

DEFINITION: to speak to, converse with.
ORIGIN: From pros and laleo; to talk to, i.e. Converse with.

BDAG.en: to communicate orally with someone, speak to, speak with, address
BDAG.pt: comunicar oralmente com alguém, falar a, falar com, dirigir-se a

DEFINITION: (a) to take to myself, (b) to take aside, (c) to welcome.
ORIGIN: From pros and lambano; to take to oneself, i.e. Use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality).

BDAG.en: to take someth. that meets a personal need, take, partake of food; to promote one’s own ends, exploit, take advantage of; to take or lead off to oneself, take aside; to extend a welcome, receive in(to) one’s home or circle of acquaintances; to take or bring along with oneself, take along
BDAG.pt: pegar algo que satisfaz uma necessidade pessoal, tomar, participar de comida; promover os próprios fins, explorar, tirar vantagem; levar ou conduzir para si, levar à parte; estender uma recepção, receber em casa ou no círculo de conhecidos; levar ou trazer consigo, acompanhar

DEFINITION: a receiving, a taking to one's self, acceptance.
ORIGIN: From proslambano; admission.

DEFINITION: to remain; to abide in, remain in, persist in, adhere to.
ORIGIN: From pros and meno; to stay further, i.e. Remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in.
USAGE: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with).

BDAG.en: to be steadfast in association, remain/stay with; to stay on at a place beyond some point of time, remain longer, further
BDAG.pt: ser firme em associação, permanecer/ficar com; permanecer em um lugar além de um certo ponto de tempo, ficar mais tempo, continuar

DEFINITION: to bring (a ship) to anchor at.
ORIGIN: From pros and a derivative of the same as horme (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at.

BDAG.en: come into harbor, come to anchor
BDAG.pt: chegar ao porto, ancorar

DEFINITION: to owe besides (in addition).
ORIGIN: From pros and opheilo; to be indebted additionally.

BDAG.en: owe besides, still owe (of debts outstanding)
BDAG.pt: dever a mais, ainda dever (de dívidas pendentes)

DEFINITION: to be displeased or offended with.
ORIGIN: From pros and a form of ochtheo (to be vexed with something irksome); to feel indignant at.

BDAG.en: to be very upset over someth. someone has done, be angry, offended, provoked
BDAG.pt: ficar muito chateado com algo que alguém fez, ficar zangado, ofendido, provocado

DEFINITION: very hungry.
ORIGIN: From pros and the same as peinao; hungering further, i.e. Intensely hungry.

BDAG.en: hungry
BDAG.pt: faminto

DEFINITION: to fasten to, applied to Christ's being fastened to the cross.
ORIGIN: From pros and pegnumi; to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross).

BDAG.en: fix/fasten to abs. nail to (a cross)
BDAG.pt: fixar/prender a abs. pregar (numa cruz)

DEFINITION: (a) to fall down before, (b) to beat against, rush violently upon.
ORIGIN: From pros and pipto; to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm).

BDAG.en: 1 to prostrate oneself before someone, fall down before/ at the feet of freq. in the gesture of a suppliant 2 to move with force against something, fall upon, strike against
BDAG.pt: 1 prosternar-se diante de alguém, cair diante/aos pés de alguém, frequência no gesto de um suplicante 2 mover-se com força contra algo, cair sobre, bater contra

DEFINITION: to attach to, take to oneself, to pretend.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pros and poieo; to do forward for oneself, i.e. Pretend (as if about to do a thing).

BDAG.en: 1 to engage in an action or gesture that gives the appearance of conveying specific intent, make/act as though, pretend 2 to act in response to, take notice (of)
BDAG.pt: 1 envolver-se em uma ação ou gesto que dá a aparência de transmitir intenção específica, fazer/agir como se, fingir 2 agir em resposta a, prestar atenção (em)

DEFINITION: to come to, approach.
ORIGIN: From pros and poreuomai; to journey towards, i.e. Approach (not the same as proporeuomai).

BDAG.en: to come up to, approach someone
BDAG.pt: aproximar-se de, chegar perto de alguém

DEFINITION: to dash against, as waves.
ORIGIN: From pros and rhegnumi; to tear towards, i.e. Burst upon (as a tempest or flood).

BDAG.en: s. προσρήσσω
BDAG.pt: cf. προσρήσσω

DEFINITION: (a) to instruct, command, (b) to appoint, assign.
ORIGIN: From pros and tasso; to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively) enjoin.

BDAG.en: to issue an official directive or make a determination, command, order, give instructions, determine
BDAG.pt: emitir uma diretriz oficial ou fazer uma determinação, ordenar, mandar, dar instruções, determinar

DEFINITION: a female guardian, protector, patroness.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a derivative of proistemi; a patroness, i.e. Assistant.

BDAG.en: a woman in a supportive role, patron, benefactor
BDAG.pt: uma mulher em papel de apoio, patrona, benfeitora

DEFINITION: to place (put) to, add; to do again.
ORIGIN: From pros and tithemi; to place additionally, i.e. Lay beside, annex, repeat.
USAGE: add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more.

BDAG.en: 1 to add to something that is already present or exists, add, put to ... Of the addition of a word, sentence, etc. ... Of faith ... Of persons who are added to a group already existing ... Of one deceased 2 to add as a benefit, provide, give, grant, do
BDAG.pt: 1 adicionar a algo que já está presente ou existe, somar, pôr em ... Da adição de uma palavra, frase, etc. ... Da fé ... De pessoas que são adicionadas a um grupo já existente ... De um falecido 2 adicionar como benefício, prover, dar, conceder, fazer

DEFINITION: to run to.
ORIGIN: From pros and trecho (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e. Hasten to meet or join.

BDAG.en: to run to or towards, run up (to)
BDAG.pt: correr para ou em direção a, correr até (alguém/algo)

DEFINITION: anything eaten with bread, especially fish or meat.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of pros and phago; something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. A relish (specially, fish; compare opsarion).

BDAG.en: a relish eaten with bread, fish (to eat)
BDAG.pt: um acompanhamento (petisco) comido com pão, peixe (para comer)

DEFINITION: (originally: newly slaughtered, freshly killed), recent, new.
ORIGIN: From pro and a derivative of sphazo; previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made.

BDAG.en: new, recent, not previously existing
BDAG.pt: novo, recente, não existente anteriormente

DEFINITION: recently, lately, newly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from prosphatos; recently.

BDAG.en: recently
BDAG.pt: recentemente

DEFINITION: (a) to bring to, (b) characteristically: to offer (of gifts, sacrifices, etc).
ORIGIN: From pros and phero (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e. Lead to, tender (especially to God), treat.
USAGE: bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.

BDAG.en: to bring someone or something to someone, bring, offer, present; to present something to someone by bringing it, bring, offer, present (of offerings, gifts etc.); to behave towards or deal with someone in a certain way, meet, deal with
BDAG.pt: trazer alguém ou algo a alguém, trazer, oferecer, apresentar; apresentar algo a alguém trazendo, trazer, oferecer, apresentar (de oferendas, presentes etc.); comportar-se ou lidar com alguém de certa maneira, encontrar, tratar

DEFINITION: pleasing, acceptable, grateful.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of pros and phileo; friendly towards, i.e. Acceptable.

BDAG.en: pleasing, agreeable, lovely, amiable
BDAG.pt: agradável, aprazível, amável

DEFINITION: an offering, sacrifice.
ORIGIN: From prosphero; presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice.

BDAG.en: the act of bringing as a voluntary expression (sacrificing, offering); that which is brought as a voluntary expression (present, gift), offering
BDAG.pt: o ato de trazer como expressão voluntária (sacrificar, oferecer); aquilo que é trazido como expressão voluntária (presente, dádiva), oferta

DEFINITION: to call to, summon; to call (out) to, address, give a speech to, harangue.
ORIGIN: From pros and phoneo; to sound towards, i.e. Address, exclaim, summon.

BDAG.en: to call out or speak to, call out, address; to call to oneself, call to, summon, with implication of shared interests
BDAG.pt: chamar em voz alta ou dirigir-se a, gritar, abordar; chamar para si, chamar, convocar, com implicação de interesses comuns

DEFINITION: a pouring upon, an effusion, a sprinkling.
ORIGIN: From a comparative of pros and cheo (to pour); a shedding forth, i.e. Affusion.

BDAG.en: act of putting liquid on something, pouring, sprinkling, spreading (the sprinkling of blood)
BDAG.pt: ato de colocar líquido sobre algo, derramar, aspersão, espalhar (a aspersão de sangue)

DEFINITION: to touch lightly.
ORIGIN: From pros and psauo (to touch); to impinge, i.e. Lay a finger on (in order to relieve).

BDAG.en: to reach out to touch, touch
BDAG.pt: estender a mão para tocar, tocar

DEFINITION: to favor specially, show partiality.
ORIGIN: From prosopoleptes; to favor an individual, i.e. Show partiality.

DEFINITION: an accepter of a face, a respecter of persons.
ORIGIN: From prosopon and lambano; an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality.

DEFINITION: partiality, favoritism.
ORIGIN: From prosopoleptes; partiality, i.e. Favoritism.

DEFINITION: the face, countenance, surface.
ORIGIN: From pros and ops (the visage, from optanomai); the front (as being towards view), i.e. The countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person.
USAGE: (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.

BDAG.en: the front part of the head (face, countenance); personal presence or relational circumstance; the outer surface of someth., face=surface; that which is present in a certain form or character to a viewer, external things, appearance

DEFINITION: appoint beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and tasso; to pre-arrange, i.e. Prescribe.

BDAG.pt: arranjar algo antes, fixar, determinar, reservar (antecipadamente)

DEFINITION: to stretch out, tie up (for scourging), extend before.

BDAG.en: stretch out before, stretch out, spread out
BDAG.pt: estender à frente, esticar, espalhar

DEFINITION: formerly, before.

BDAG.pt: pertencente a um período de tempo anterior a outro, mais antigo (anterior, precedente); anterior a outra pessoa/coisa em importância, superior, preferível, mais proeminente

DEFINITION: to purpose, design beforehand, determine.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pro and tithemi; to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine).

DEFINITION: to encourage, exhort, persuade.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pro and the base of trope; to turn forward for oneself, i.e. Encourage.

BDAG.en: to promote a particular course of action, urge (on), encourage, impel, persuade
BDAG.pt: promover um curso de ação particular, instar (a), encorajar, impelir, persuadir

DEFINITION: to run before, outrun, run in advance.
ORIGIN: From pro and trecho (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e. Outstrip, precede.

BDAG.en: run ahead; run on ahead
BDAG.pt: correr à frente; correr adiante

DEFINITION: to have been already, have been previously.
ORIGIN: From pro and huparcho; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously.

BDAG.en: exist before
BDAG.pt: existir antes

DEFINITION: a pretext, an excuse.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pro and phaino; an outward showing, i.e. Pretext.

BDAG.en: something said in defense of an action, actual motive or reason, valid excuse; falsely alleged motive, pretext, ostensible reason, excuse
BDAG.pt: algo dito em defesa de uma ação, motivo ou razão real, desculpa válida; motivo alegado falsamente, pretexto, razão ostensiva, desculpa

DEFINITION: to bring forth, produce.
ORIGIN: From pro and phero; to bear forward, i.e. Produce.

BDAG.en: to bring someth. forth, yield (the earth) yields the fruits; of bringing someth. out into the open
BDAG.pt: trazer algo à luz, produzir (a terra) os frutos; de trazer algo à vista

DEFINITION: prophecy, prophesying; the gift of communicating and enforcing revealed truth.
ORIGIN: From prophetes ("prophecy"); prediction (scriptural or other).

BDAG.en: act of interpreting divine will or purpose, prophetic activity; the gift of interpreting divine will or purpose, gift of prophesying; the utterance of one who interprets divine will or purpose, prophecy
BDAG.pt: ato de interpretar a vontade ou propósito divino, atividade profética; o dom de interpretar a vontade ou propósito divino, dom de profetizar; a declaração daquele que interpreta a vontade ou propósito divino, profecia

DEFINITION: to foretell, prophesy; to set forth matter of divine teaching by special faculty.
ORIGIN: From prophetes; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office.

BDAG.en: to proclaim an inspired revelation, prophesy; to tell about someth. that is hidden from view, tell, reveal; to foretell someth. that lies in the future, foretell, prophesy
BDAG.pt: proclamar uma revelação inspirada, profetizar; contar sobre algo que está oculto à vista, dizer, revelar; predizer algo que está no futuro, prever, profetizar

DEFINITION: a prophet (an interpreter or forth-teller of the divine will).
ORIGIN: From a compound of pro and phemi; a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet.

BDAG.en: a proclaimer or expounder of divine matters or concerns that could not ordinarily be known except by special revelation; a person inspired to proclaim or reveal divine will or purpose, prophet; by metonymy, the writings of prophets
BDAG.pt: um proclamador ou expositor de assuntos ou concernimentos divinos que normalmente não poderiam ser conhecidos exceto por revelação especial; uma pessoa inspirada a proclamar ou revelar a vontade ou propósito divino, profeta; por metonímia, os escritos dos profetas

DEFINITION: prophetic, uttered by a prophet.
ORIGIN: From prophetes; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic").

BDAG.en: pert. to inspired interpretation of the divine will, prophetic γραφαὶπρ. the writings of the prophets=the OT
BDAG.pt: pertencente à interpretação inspirada da vontade divina, profético; γραφαὶπρ. significando os escritos dos profetas, ou seja, o AT.

DEFINITION: a prophetess.
ORIGIN: Feminine of prophetes; a female foreteller or an inspired woman.

BDAG.en: the form corresponding to προφήτης prophet
BDAG.pt: a forma correspondente a προφήτης (profeta), referente a uma profetisa.

DEFINITION: to anticipate, forestall.
ORIGIN: From pro and phthano; to get an earlier start of, i.e. Anticipate.

BDAG.en: 1 to be ahead of someone in some activity, be ahead of, come before, anticipate; 2 to do someth. at a point of time prior to another point of time, do before/previously
BDAG.pt: 1 estar à frente de alguém em alguma atividade, antecipar; 2 fazer algo em um ponto de tempo anterior a outro, fazer antes/previamente.

DEFINITION: to put into the hand, to take into one's hand, to determine.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from pro and a derivative of cheir; to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose.

BDAG.en: to express preference of someone for a task, choose for oneself, select, appoint
BDAG.pt: expressar preferência por alguém para uma tarefa, escolher para si mesmo, selecionar, nomear.

DEFINITION: to choose or appoint beforehand.
ORIGIN: From pro and cheirotoneo; to elect in advance.

BDAG.en: choose/appoint beforehand
BDAG.pt: escolher/nomear antecipadamente

DEFINITION: Prochorus, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: From pro and choros; before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Prochorus, one of the seven appointees for special service in the church at Jerusalem
BDAG.pt: Prócoro, um dos sete nomeados para serviço especial na igreja de Jerusalém.

DEFINITION: the stern (of a ship).
ORIGIN: Feminine of prumnus (hindmost); the stern of a ship.

BDAG.en: the afterpart of a boat, stern (opp. πρῷρα)
BDAG.pt: a parte traseira de um barco, popa (oposto a proa).

DEFINITION: early in the morning, at dawn.
ORIGIN: Adverb from pro; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch.

BDAG.en: early, early in the morning; as the fourth watch of the night (three to six o’clock)
BDAG.pt: cedo, de manhã cedo; como a quarta vigília da noite (das três às seis horas)

DEFINITION: (early) morning.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a derivative of proi as noun; day-dawn.

BDAG.en: early part of the daylight period, (early) morning
BDAG.pt: primeira parte do período de luz do dia, (início da) manhã.

DEFINITION: early rain, early crops.
ORIGIN: From proi; dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season).

DEFINITION: belonging to the morning, early.
ORIGIN: From proi; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. Matutinal.

BDAG.en: pert. to early morning, early, belonging to the morning ὁἀστὴρ ὁπρ. the morning star, Venus
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao início da manhã, matinal, pertencente à manhã; ὁἀστὴρ ὁπρ. significa a estrela da manhã, Vênus.

DEFINITION: the prow (of a ship).
ORIGIN: Feminine of a presumed derivative of pro as noun; the prow, i.e. Forward part of a vessel.

BDAG.en: the forepart of a boat, bow, prow (opp. πρύμνα)
BDAG.pt: a parte dianteira de um barco, proa (oposto a popa).

DEFINITION: to have preeminence, be chief, be first.
ORIGIN: From protos; to be first (in rank or influence).

BDAG.en: to hold the highest rank in a group, be first, have first place
BDAG.pt: ocupar o posto mais alto em um grupo, ser o primeiro, ter o primeiro lugar.

DEFINITION: a chief (most honorable) seat.
ORIGIN: From protos and kathedra; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. Preeminence in council.

BDAG.en: a position or place indicative of special honor for the pers. occupying it, seat of honor, best seat
BDAG.pt: uma posição ou lugar indicativo de honra especial para a pessoa que o ocupa, assento de honra, melhor assento.

DEFINITION: the chief place at a banquet or table.
ORIGIN: From protos and klisia; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. Preeminence at meals.

BDAG.en: the place of honor at a dinner, beside the master of the house or the host
BDAG.pt: o lugar de honra em um jantar, ao lado do mestre da casa ou do anfitrião

DEFINITION: first, in the first place, before, formerly.
ORIGIN: Neuter of protos as adverb (with or without ho); firstly (in time, place, order, or importance).
USAGE: before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all).

BDAG.en: first, in the first place, before, earlier, to begin with (as adverb)
BDAG.pt: primeiro, em primeiro lugar, antes, mais cedo, para começar (como advérbio)

DEFINITION: first, before, principal, most important.
ORIGIN: Contracted superlative of pro; foremost (in time, place, order or importance).
USAGE: before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former.

BDAG.en: first of several (inclusive of time, set, or space); first, earliest, earlier (as adjective or adverb); foremost, most important, most prominent
BDAG.pt: primeiro de vários (incluindo tempo, conjunto ou espaço); primeiro, mais cedo, anterior (como adjetivo ou advérbio); proeminente, mais importante, mais destacado

DEFINITION: one who stands in the front rank, hence: a leader, ringleader, chief.
ORIGIN: From protos and histemi; one standing first in the ranks, i.e. A captain (champion).

BDAG.en: one who stands first, a person who is at the head of a group, leader, probably in the sense ringleader
BDAG.pt: aquele que está à frente, uma pessoa que está no comando de um grupo, líder, provavelmente no sentido de instigador/cabeça de um grupo

DEFINITION: the birthright, the rights of the first-born.
ORIGIN: From prototokos; primogeniture (as a privilege).

BDAG.en: privileges associated with being a firstborn, birthright, right of primogeniture of a firstborn son
BDAG.pt: privilégios associados ao ser primogênito, direito de primogenitura, direito de primogenitura de um filho primogênito

DEFINITION: first-born, eldest.
ORIGIN: From protos and the alternate of tikto; first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: firstborn, heir apparent; fig. firstborn of a new humanity
BDAG.pt: primogênito, herdeiro aparente; fig. primogênito de uma nova humanidade

DEFINITION: to stumble, fall, sin, err, transgress.
ORIGIN: A form of pipto; to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation).

BDAG.en: to lose one’s footing, stumble, trip; figuratively, to make a mistake, go astray, sin; to experience disaster, be ruined, be lost
BDAG.pt: perder o equilíbrio, tropeçar, vacilar; figurativamente, cometer um erro, desviar-se, pecar; sofrer um desastre, ser arruinado, ser perdido

DEFINITION: the heel.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; the heel (figuratively).

BDAG.en: heel
BDAG.pt: calcanhar

DEFINITION: a little wing, (anything like a wing) a battlement.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of pterux; a winglet, i.e. (figuratively) extremity (top corner).

BDAG.en: diminutive of πτέρυξ ‘wing’; tip or extremity of anything, end, edge (e.g., pinnacle or summit of the temple)
BDAG.pt: diminutivo de πτέρυξ ‘asa’; ponta ou extremidade de algo, fim, borda (ex.: pináculo ou cume do templo)

DEFINITION: a wing, pinion.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of petomai (meaning a feather); a wing.

BDAG.en: wing, of birds
BDAG.pt: asa, de aves

DEFINITION: winged; subst: a bird, fowl.
ORIGIN: Contraction for peteinon; a bird.

BDAG.en: pert. to having feathers, feathered, winged; (as a substantive) the birds
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter penas, emplumado, alado; (como substantivo) as aves

DEFINITION: to terrify, scare, strike with panic.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to the alternate of pipto (through the idea of causing to fall) or to petomai (through that of causing to fly away); to scare.

BDAG.en: terrify, frighten; (passive) be terrified, be alarmed, frightened, startled
BDAG.pt: aterrorizar, assustar; (passivo) ser aterrorizado, ficar alarmado, assustado, sobressaltado

DEFINITION: a fluttering, excitement, terror.
ORIGIN: From ptoeo; alarm.

BDAG.en: act of causing someone to be intimidated, terrifying, intimidation; or experience of being intimidated, fear, terror
BDAG.pt: ato de causar intimidação a alguém, terror, intimidação; ou experiência de ser intimidado, medo, terror

DEFINITION: Ptolemais, a coast city of Phoenicia, midway between Tyre and Caesarea.
ORIGIN: From Ptolemaios (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Ptolemais, a Phoenician seaport city
BDAG.pt: Ptolemaida, uma cidade portuária fenícia

DEFINITION: a simple wooden pitchfork; a winnowing-shovel or fan.
ORIGIN: From ptuo; a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle).

BDAG.en: a fork-like shovel, winnowing shovel (used to separate chaff from grain)
BDAG.pt: uma pá em forma de forquilha, pá de debulha (usada para separar a palha do grão)

DEFINITION: to frighten, terrify.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of ptuo (and thus akin to ptoeo); to frighten.

BDAG.en: (active) ‘frighten, scare’; (almost always passive) to let oneself be intimidated, be frightened, terrified
BDAG.pt: (ativo) 'assustar, amedrontar'; (quase sempre passivo) deixar-se intimidar, ficar assustado, aterrorizado

DEFINITION: spittle, saliva.
ORIGIN: From ptuo; saliva.

BDAG.en: saliva, spittle
BDAG.pt: saliva, cuspe

DEFINITION: to fold, roll up (as a scroll).
ORIGIN: Probably akin to petannumi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to petomai through the idea of expansion, and to ptuo through that of flattening; compare pateo); to fold, i.e. Furl a scroll.

BDAG.en: to put something away after use by folding one part over another, fold up, roll up, close (a scroll)
BDAG.pt: guardar algo após o uso dobrando uma parte sobre a outra, dobrar, enrolar, fechar (um rolo)

DEFINITION: to spit.
ORIGIN: A primary verb (compare ptusso); to spit.

BDAG.en: spit, spit out
BDAG.pt: cuspir, expelir com a boca

DEFINITION: a fall; a carcass, corpse, dead body.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of pipto; a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion).

BDAG.en: a dead body: animal or human, (dead) body, corpse, esp. of one killed by violence
BDAG.pt: um corpo morto: animal ou humano, (cadáver), especialmente de alguém morto pela violência

DEFINITION: a falling, a fall, ruin.
ORIGIN: From the alternate of pipto; a crash, i.e. Downfall (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: state or condition of falling, fall (lit. of a house collapsing); fig. downfall, destruction
BDAG.pt: estado ou condição de cair, queda (literalmente de uma casa desmoronando); figurado: ruína, destruição

DEFINITION: beggary, poverty, destitution.
ORIGIN: From ptocheuo; beggary, i.e. Indigence (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: state of being deficient in means of support, poverty
BDAG.pt: estado de carência de meios de subsistência, pobreza

DEFINITION: to be in poverty, be a beggar.
ORIGIN: From ptochos; to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to be or become poor as a beggar, be (extremely) poor; of Christ in ref. to renunciation of transcendent prosperity
BDAG.pt: ser ou tornar-se pobre como um mendigo, ser (extremamente) pobre; de Cristo em referência à renúncia da prosperidade transcendente

DEFINITION: poor, destitute, spiritually poor, either in a good sense (humble devout persons) or bad.
ORIGIN: From ptosso (to crouch); akin to ptoeo and the alternate of pipto); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. Pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas penes properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed).

BDAG.en: pert. to being economically disadvantaged, orig. ‘begging’, dependent on others for support, but also simply poor; pert. to being thrust on divine resources, poor; lacking in spiritual worth, fig. ext. of 1; pert. to being extremely inferior in quality, miserable, shabby

DEFINITION: the fist.
ORIGIN: From a primary pux (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing).

BDAG.en: fist; fist-fight, boxing
BDAG.pt: punho; briga de punhos, boxe

ORIGIN: From Putho (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying).

BDAG.en: orig. 'the Python' (serpent); later a spirit of divination, then also of ventriloquists; πνεῦμα πύθωνα: a spirit of divination or prophecy
BDAG.pt: originalmente 'o Pitão' (serpente); mais tarde um espírito de adivinhação, depois também de ventríloquos; πνεῦμα πύθωνα: um espírito de adivinhação ou profecia

DEFINITION: frequent, often, much.
ORIGIN: From the same as skenopoios; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently.

BDAG.en: occurring freq. at intervals, frequent, numerous; as adv. often, frequently; as adv. more often, more frequently and in an elative sense very often, quite frequently
BDAG.pt: ocorrendo em intervalos frequentes, frequente, numeroso; como advérbio: muitas vezes, frequentemente; como advérbio: mais frequentemente, e em sentido superlativo: muito frequentemente, bastante frequentemente

DEFINITION: to box, be a boxer.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the same as pugme; to box (with the fist), i.e. Contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to fight with fists, box
BDAG.pt: lutar com os punhos, boxear

DEFINITION: a gate.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. The leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: gate, door; in imagery... the narrow gate that leads into life; the gate of righteousness; the gate to the Lord
BDAG.pt: portão, porta; em linguagem figurada... o portão estreito que conduz à vida; o portão da justiça; o portão para o Senhor

DEFINITION: a large gate; a gateway, porch, vestibule.
ORIGIN: From pule; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule.

BDAG.en: an entrance that contains a gate or gates, gateway, entrance, gate esp. of the large, impressive gateways at the entrance of temples and palaces; a gateway consisting of a forecourt, gateway, entrance separated fr. the house by a court
BDAG.pt: uma entrada que contém um ou mais portões, portal, entrada, portão, especialmente os portões grandes e impressionantes na entrada de templos e palácios; um pátio de entrada que consiste em um vestíbulo, portal, entrada separada da casa por um pátio

DEFINITION: to ask, inquire, ascertain by inquiry, understand.
ORIGIN: Middle voice prolonged from a primary putho (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. Ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from erotao, which properly means a request as a favor; and from aiteo, which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from zeteo, which implies a search for something hidden; and from deomai, which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence).

BDAG.en: to seek to learn by inquiry, inquire, ask; to determine someth. by inquiry, learn by inquiry
BDAG.pt: buscar aprender por inquérito, perguntar, questionar; determinar algo por inquérito, aprender por inquérito

DEFINITION: fire; the heat of the sun, lightning; fig: strife, trials; the eternal fire.
ORIGIN: A primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning).

BDAG.en: fire (earthly fire; heavenly/divine fire as a means of judgment or manifestation; figuratively, discord)
BDAG.pt: fogo (fogo terreno; fogo celestial/divino como meio de julgamento ou manifestação; figurativamente, discórdia)

DEFINITION: a fire, pile of burning fuel.
ORIGIN: From pur; a fire (concretely).

BDAG.pt: uma pilha de material combustível ou até mesmo em chamas, uma fogueira; uma pira na qual alguém é queimado

DEFINITION: a tower, fortified structure.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle.

BDAG.en: a tall structure used as a lookout, tower; a tower-shaped building, farm building
BDAG.pt: uma estrutura alta usada como vigia, torre; um edifício em forma de torre, edifício de fazenda

DEFINITION: to be on fire, to be ill of a fever.
ORIGIN: From pura; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever.

BDAG.en: suffer with a fever
BDAG.pt: padecer de febre

DEFINITION: a fever, scorching heat.
ORIGIN: From puresso; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever).

BDAG.en: fever
BDAG.pt: febre

DEFINITION: fiery, glittering.
ORIGIN: From pura; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming.

BDAG.en: of the color of fire, fiery
BDAG.pt: da cor do fogo, ígneo

DEFINITION: pass: to burn, be set on fire, be inflamed; glow with heat, be purified by fire.
ORIGIN: From pur; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust).
USAGE: burn, fiery, be on fire, try.

BDAG.en: to cause to be on fire, burn a lit., of the fiery end of the world; fig. burn, be inflamed w. sympathy, readiness to aid, or indignation; to cause to be very hot, make red hot, cause to glow, heat thoroughly
BDAG.pt: causar que seja incendiado, queimar, incendiar (referente ao fim ígneo do mundo); figurativamente, queimar, inflamar-se com simpatia, prontidão em ajudar ou indignação; causar que fique muito quente, tornar incandescente, fazer brilhar, aquecer intensamente

DEFINITION: to be red, fire-colored.
ORIGIN: From purrhos; to redden (intransitively).

BDAG.en: to be (fiery) red of the color of the morning or evening sky
BDAG.pt: ser vermelho (ígneo), da cor do céu da manhã ou da noite

DEFINITION: red, fire-colored.
ORIGIN: From pur; fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored.

BDAG.en: wheat
BDAG.pt: trigo

DEFINITION: a burning, trial, fiery test.
ORIGIN: From puroo; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test).

BDAG.en: process of burning, burning; an intense degree of some painful occurrence or experience, burning ordeal fig. ext.
BDAG.pt: processo de queima, queima; um grau intenso de alguma ocorrência ou experiência dolorosa, provação ardente (sentido figurado)

DEFINITION: yet, even.
ORIGIN: Another form of the base of pos; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See medepo, mepo, oudepo, oupo, popote..
USAGE: yet, even; used only in the comparative. See medepo, mepo, oudepo, oupo, popote.

DEFINITION: to exchange or barter, to sell.
ORIGIN: Probably ultimately from pelomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. To sell.

BDAG.en: sell; be offered for sale, be sold
BDAG.pt: vender; ser oferecido para venda, ser vendido

DEFINITION: a colt, young ass, foal.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass.

BDAG.en: young animal, foal; horse (when standing alone without indication that it is a foal)
BDAG.pt: animal jovem, potro; cavalo (quando aparece sozinho sem indicação de que é um potro)

DEFINITION: at any time, ever.
ORIGIN: From po and pote; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time.

BDAG.en: ever, at any time; usu. used w. a neg. (never, not ever)
BDAG.pt: sempre, em algum momento; usualmente usado com uma negação (nunca)

DEFINITION: to harden, render callous, petrify.
ORIGIN: Apparently from poros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous).

BDAG.en: harden, petrify; in our lit. only fig., to cause someone to have difficulty in understanding or comprehending, harden, petrify, mostly of hearts; make dull/obtuse/blind, close the mind
BDAG.pt: endurecer, petrificar; em nossa literatura apenas figurativamente, fazer com que alguém tenha dificuldade em entender ou compreender, endurecer, petrificar, principalmente de corações; tornar embotado/obtuso/cego, fechar a mente

DEFINITION: a covering with a callous, blindness.
ORIGIN: From poroo; stupidity or callousness.

BDAG.en: hardening, dulling; in our lit. only fig. state or condition of complete lack of understanding, dullness, insensibility, obstinacy
BDAG.pt: endurecimento, insensibilização; em nossa literatura apenas figurativamente, estado ou condição de completa falta de entendimento, torpor, insensibilidade, obstinação

DEFINITION: hardly, by any means, perhaps.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the base of pou; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition.
USAGE: haply, by any (some) means, perhaps. See ei pos, mepos. Compare pos.

DEFINITION: how, in what manner, by what means.
ORIGIN: Adverb from the base of pou; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!.
USAGE: how, after (by) what manner (means), that. (Occasionally unexpressed in English).

BDAG.en: interrog. reference to manner or way, in what way? how?; in exclamations: how ... !
BDAG.pt: interrogativo referente a modo ou maneira, de que modo? como?; em exclamações: como...!

DEFINITION: Rahab, a Canaanitess, who rescued the Hebrew spies at Jericho.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Rachab); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess.

BDAG.en: Rahab, a prostitute in Jericho who, acc. to Josh 2, saved Israelite spies by hiding them. This courageous woman is cited as a model of faith, uprightness, and hospitality.
BDAG.pt: Raabe, uma prostituta em Jericó que, segundo Josué 2, salvou espiões israelitas ao escondê-los. Esta mulher corajosa é citada como modelo de fé, retidão e hospitalidade.

DEFINITION: Rabbi, master, teacher; a title of respect often applied to Christ.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (rab with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor.

BDAG.en: properly a form of address, and so throughout our lit., then an honorary title for outstanding teachers of the law: master, sir, rabbi.
BDAG.pt: propriamente uma forma de tratamento, e assim em toda a nossa literatura, depois um título honorífico para professores notáveis da lei: mestre, senhor, rabino.

DEFINITION: Rabbi, master, teacher; a title of respect often applied to Christ.
ORIGIN: Or rhabbouni (hrab-boo-nee') of Chaldee origin; corresponding to rhabbi.

BDAG.en: properly a heightened form of: my lord, my master.
BDAG.pt: propriamente uma forma intensificada de: meu senhor, meu mestre.

DEFINITION: to beat with rods, scourge.
ORIGIN: From rhabdos; to strike with a stick, i.e. Bastinado.

BDAG.en: to beat with a rod, beat (of the punishment known formally in Lat. legal terminology as admonitio as distinct from catigatio (a lashing) and verberatio (flogging with chains))
BDAG.pt: bater com uma vara, açoitar (da punição conhecida formalmente na terminologia jurídica latina como admonitio, distinta de catigatio (açoite) e verberatio (flagelação com correntes))

DEFINITION: a rod, staff, staff of authority, scepter.
ORIGIN: From the base of rhapizo; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty).

BDAG.en: a relatively slender piece of wood varying in length, rod, staff, stick gener.; also of a shepherd’s staff, traveler’s staff, ruler’s staff, scepter, or a stick as a means of punishment.
BDAG.pt: um pedaço de madeira relativamente esbelto de comprimento variável, vara, cajado, bastão em geral; também de cajado de pastor, bastão de viajante, cetro de governante, ou um pau como meio de punição.

DEFINITION: a rod holder, (a Roman) lictor (one holding the rod of office).
ORIGIN: From rhabdos and echo; a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. A Roman lictor (constable or executioner).

BDAG.en: orig. ‘staff-bearer’, then of the Roman ‘lictor’, roughly equiv. to constable, police officer
BDAG.pt: originalmente 'portador de bastão', depois do 'lictor' romano, aproximadamente equivalente a policial, oficial de polícia

DEFINITION: Ragau (or Reu), an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (r'uw); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Reu, son of Peleg and father of Serug (Gen 11:18–21), in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Reu, filho de Pelegue e pai de Serugue (Gênesis 11:18–21), na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: a careless action, an act of villainy.
ORIGIN: From a comparative of rhaidios (easy, i.e. Reckless) and ergon; easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime.

BDAG.en: orig. the action of one who endeavors to gain some personal end through clever or tricky means. From the sense ‘prank, knavery, roguish trick, slick deed’ it is but a short step to that of serious misdeed, crime, villainy
