BDAG.pt: orig. a ação de alguém que se esforça para obter algum fim pessoal por meios espertos ou traiçoeiros. Do sentido de 'travessura, trapaça, truque ardiloso, ato astuto' é um pequeno passo para o de erro grave, crime, vilania

DEFINITION: ease in doing, laziness, recklessness, wickedness.
ORIGIN: From the same as rhaidiourgema; recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity.

BDAG.en: in its less pejorative sense ῥ. suggests an easygoing approach to things in contrast to serious acceptance of responsibilties: ‘frivolity’, then an endeavor to gain some personal end through clever or tricky means, in effect a mild expr. for chichanery, wickedness, villainy, deceit, fraud, unscrupulousness
BDAG.pt: em seu sentido menos pejorativo, ῥ. sugere uma abordagem despreocupada das coisas em contraste com a aceitação séria das responsabilidades: 'frivolidade', depois um esforço para obter algum fim pessoal por meios espertos ou traiçoeiros, na prática uma expressão suave para traquinagem, maldade, vilania, engano, fraude, falta de escrúpulos

DEFINITION: empty (an expression of contempt).
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare reyq); O empty one, i.e. Thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification).

BDAG.en: a term of abuse/put-down relating to lack of intelligence, numskull, fool (in effect verbal bullying), derived fr. the Aramaic ‘empty one’.
BDAG.pt: um termo de abuso/insulto relacionado à falta de inteligência, cabeça-dura, tolo (na prática, bullying verbal), derivado do Aramaico 'vazio'.

DEFINITION: a piece of cloth, a remnant torn off.
ORIGIN: From rhegnumi; a "rag," i.e. Piece of cloth.

BDAG.en: 1 tattered garment, rag. 2 piece of cloth, patch
BDAG.pt: 1 vestimenta esfarrapada, trapo. 2 pedaço de pano, remendo

DEFINITION: Rama, a place in Ephraim, two hours north of Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ramah); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Rama, a city in the tribe of Benjamin, about 8 km north of Jerusalem.
BDAG.pt: Ramá, uma cidade na tribo de Benjamim, a cerca de 8 km ao norte de Jerusalém.

DEFINITION: to sprinkle, cleanse ceremonially by sprinkling.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of rhaino (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e. Asperse (ceremonially or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 to sprinkle liquid on someth., (be)sprinkle w. acc., of the rite of purification. 2 The mid. is found in our lit. w. the mng. to cleanse oneself of impurities, cleanse, purify.
BDAG.pt: 1 aspersar líquido sobre algo, borrifar com acusativo, referente ao rito de purificação. 2 O meio é encontrado em nossa literatura com o sentido de limpar-se de impurezas, limpar, purificar.

DEFINITION: sprinkling, purification.
ORIGIN: From rhantizo; aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively).

BDAG.en: sprinkling. The blood of Jesus is called αἷμα ῥαντισμοῦ (blood of sprinkling, i.e. blood that is sprinkled for atonement)
BDAG.pt: aspersão. O sangue de Jesus é chamado de αἷμα ῥαντισμοῦ (sangue de aspersão, ou seja, sangue que é aspergido para expiação)

DEFINITION: to strike with a rod, to strike with the palm of the hand.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of a primary rhepo (to let fall, "rap"); to slap.
USAGE: smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare tupto.

BDAG.en: lit., and almost always in non-biblical authors ‘strike with a club or rod’; but in the other places in our lit. the sense is clearly to strike with the open hand, esp. in the face, slap.
BDAG.pt: literalmente, e quase sempre em autores não bíblicos, 'golpear com um porrete ou vara'; mas nos outros lugares de nossa literatura o sentido é claramente golpear com a mão aberta, especialmente no rosto, esbofetear.

DEFINITION: a blow (with a stick or the palm of the hand).
ORIGIN: From rhapizo; a slap.
USAGE: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.

BDAG.en: 1 a blow inflicted by some instrument such as a club, rod, or whip, blow. 2 a blow on the face with someone’s hand, a slap in the face.
BDAG.pt: 1 um golpe infligido por algum instrumento como um porrete, vara ou chicote, golpe. 2 um golpe no rosto com a mão de alguém, um tapa no rosto.

DEFINITION: a needle.
ORIGIN: From a primary rhapto (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of rhapizo through the idea of puncturing); a needle.

BDAG.en: needle esp. one used for sewing
BDAG.pt: agulha, especialmente uma usada para costura

DEFINITION: Rahab, a Canaanitess, who rescued the Hebrew spies at Jericho.
ORIGIN: From the same as Rhaab; Rachab, a Canaanitess.

BDAG.en: Rahab, in the genealogy of Jesus, wife of Salmon and mother of Boaz
BDAG.pt: Raabe, na genealogia de Jesus, esposa de Salmon e mãe de Boaz

DEFINITION: Rachel, younger wife of the patriarch Jacob.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Rachel); Rachel, the wife of Jacob.

BDAG.en: Rachel, Jacob’s wife, mother of the people of Israel
BDAG.pt: Raquel, esposa de Jacó, mãe do povo de Israel

DEFINITION: Rebecca, wife of the patriarch Isaac.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ribqah); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac.

BDAG.en: Rebecca, wife of Isaac
BDAG.pt: Rebeca, esposa de Isaque

DEFINITION: a chariot.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. Four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding).

DEFINITION: Rephan, the Saturn of later mythology.
ORIGIN: By incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (Kiyuwn); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol.

BDAG.en: s. Ῥαιφάν.
BDAG.pt: Ver Ῥαιφάν.

DEFINITION: to flow, overflow with.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form rheuo (hryoo'-o) is used to flow ("run"; as water).

BDAG.en: to flow with liquid, in our lit. only in transf. sense a as symbol of transcendent blessing flow. b fig. in the sense of ‘have more than enough of’: (over)flow with τὶ (someth.)
BDAG.pt: fluir com líquido, em nossa literatura apenas em sentido translatício a como símbolo de bênção transcendente que flui. b fig. no sentido de 'ter mais do que o suficiente de': transbordar com algo

DEFINITION: command, make, say, speak of.
ORIGIN: For certain tenses of which a prolonged form ereo (er-eh'-o) is used; and both as alternate for epo; perhaps akin (or identical) with rheo (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. Speak or say.
USAGE: command, make, say, speak (of). Compare lego.

BDAG.en: to flow with liquid, in our lit. only in transf. sense a as symbol of transcendent blessing flow. b fig. in the sense of ‘have more than enough of’: (over)flow with τὶ (someth.)
BDAG.pt: fluir com líquido, em nossa literatura apenas em sentido translatício a como símbolo de bênção transcendente que flui. b fig. no sentido de 'ter mais do que o suficiente de': transbordar com algo

DEFINITION: Rhegium, a city in the south-west corner of Italy opposite Sicily (modern Reggio).
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy.

BDAG.en: Rhegium, a city and promontory in Bruttium, at the ‘toe’ of Italy, opposite the Sicilian city of Messina
BDAG.pt: Regio, uma cidade e promontório na Brútio, na 'ponta' da Itália, em frente à cidade siciliana de Messina

DEFINITION: what is broken, a ruin.
ORIGIN: From rhegnumi; something torn, i.e. A fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall).

BDAG.en: the event of reduction to a ruined state, wreck, ruin, collapse, lit. ‘breaking’
BDAG.pt: o evento de redução a um estado arruinado, naufrágio, ruína, colapso, literalmente 'quebra'

DEFINITION: to rend, break asunder; to break forth (into speech); to throw or dash down.
ORIGIN: Or rhesso (hrace'-so) both prolonged forms of rheko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of agnumi (see in katagnumi)) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; katagnumi being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and thrauo a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like luo) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions.

BDAG.en: 1 to cause to come apart or be in pieces by means of internal or external force, tear in pieces, break, burst τινά or τὶ (someone or someth.). Pass. be torn, burst. 2 to effect an action or intensify it by initially throwing off restraint, tear/break/let loose, break out in
BDAG.pt: 1 causar a separação ou desintegração por meio de força interna ou externa, rasgar em pedaços, quebrar, romper alguém ou algo. Passivo: ser rasgado, romper. 2 realizar uma ação ou intensificá-la ao inicialmente libertar-se de restrições, rasgar/quebrar/soltar, irromper em

DEFINITION: a thing spoken, (a) a word or saying of any kind, as command, report, promise, (b) a thing, matter, business.
ORIGIN: From rheo; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially); by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever.

BDAG.en: 1 that which is said, word, saying, expression, or statement of any kind. 2 oft. takes a special significance fr. the context: prophecy, prediction; Declaration of scripture; Command(ment), order, direction (esp. of God); Threat; speech, sermon, proclamation.
BDAG.pt: 1 aquilo que é dito, palavra, dito, expressão ou declaração de qualquer tipo. 2 frequentemente assume um significado especial do contexto: profecia, predição; Declaração das escrituras; Mandamento, ordem, direção (especialmente de Deus); Ameaça; fala, sermão, proclamação.

DEFINITION: Rhesa, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for Rphayah); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Rhesa, in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Resa, na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: an orator, public speaker, advocate.
ORIGIN: From rheo; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate.

BDAG.en: orig. ‘public speaker, orator’, then specif. a speaker in court, advocate, attorney
BDAG.pt: originalmente 'orador público', depois especificamente um orador em tribunal, advogado, procurador

DEFINITION: expressly, explicitly, in so many words.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of rheo; out-spokenly, i.e. Distinctly.

BDAG.en: pert. to what is stated or has been stated as being precisely so, expressly, explicitly
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao que é afirmado ou foi afirmado como sendo precisamente assim, expressamente, explicitamente

DEFINITION: a root, shoot, source; that which comes from the root, a descendent.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: the underground part of a plant, root; in imagery and transferred sense: the beginnings fr. which someth. grows (a family or nation); descendant of the Messiah
BDAG.pt: a parte subterrânea de uma planta, raiz; em imagens e sentido transferido: os inícios dos quais algo cresce (uma família ou nação); descendente do Messias

DEFINITION: to cause to take root; met: to plant, fix firmly, establish.
ORIGIN: From rhiza; to root (figuratively, become stable).

BDAG.en: ‘cause to take root’, mostly fig., ‘put on a firm foundation, fix firmly’ pass. be/become firmly rooted/fixed
BDAG.pt: fazer criar raízes, na maioria das vezes figurativamente, 'colocar sobre uma base firme, fixar firmemente' passivamente ser/tornar-se firmemente enraizado/fixado

DEFINITION: a glance, twinkle or flash of the eye; a rush of wind or flame; any rapid movement.
ORIGIN: From rhipto; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant).

BDAG.en: prim.: ‘a throwing, the swing or force by which someth. is thrust forward’. The focus on sudden speed readily becomes the major semantic component in ref. to a variety of objects: rapid movement, e.g. of the eyes; the ‘casting’ of a glance takes an extremely short time: in the twinkling of an eye
BDAG.pt: primariamente: 'um arremesso, o balanço ou a força pela qual algo é impulsionado para a frente'. O foco na velocidade súbita torna-se prontamente o principal componente semântico em referência a uma variedade de objetos: movimento rápido, e.g., dos olhos; o 'lançamento' de um olhar leva um tempo extremamente curto: num piscar de olhos

DEFINITION: to fan, generally to make a breeze.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of rhipto (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves).

BDAG.en: blow here and there, toss (of the wind)
BDAG.pt: soprar para cá e para lá, agitar (referente ao vento)

DEFINITION: to throw off or away, cast, hurl.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of rhipto; to toss up.

DEFINITION: to throw, cast, toss, set down; pass: to be dispersed.
ORIGIN: A primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of rhapizo, through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from ballo, which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from teino (see in ekteino), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse.

BDAG.en: to propel something with a forceful motion, throw (away, into the sea, down); expose newborn infants; put/lay something down; thrown down, prostrate, scattered (pass.)
BDAG.pt: impelir algo com movimento forte, jogar (fora, no mar, no chão); expor recém-nascidos; pousar/colocar algo; derrubado, prostrado, espalhado (voz passiva)

DEFINITION: Rehoboam, son of Solomon, and King of Israel.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Rchab'am); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Rehoboam, son and successor of Solomon
BDAG.pt: Roboão, filho e sucessor de Salomão

DEFINITION: Rhoda, a maidservant in the house of John Mark's mother at Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl.

BDAG.en: Rhoda (a slave in Mary's house; Hermas’ owner)
BDAG.pt: Roda (uma escrava na casa de Maria; proprietária de Hermas)

DEFINITION: Rhodes, an island in the Aegean sea, south-west of Asia Minor.
ORIGIN: Probably from rhodon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Rhodes, an island off the southwest point of Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Rodes, uma ilha ao largo do ponto sudoeste da Ásia Menor

DEFINITION: with a great noise, with a rushing sound.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. With a crash.

BDAG.en: pert. to noise made by someth. passing with great force and rapidity, with a rushing noise
BDAG.pt: relativo ao ruído feito por algo que passa com grande força e rapidez, com um som estrondoso

DEFINITION: a sword, scimitar; fig: war, piercing grief.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. A long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 'a large and broad sword' used by non-Greek-speaking peoples, esp. the Thracians; simply sword
BDAG.pt: ‘uma espada grande e larga’ usada por povos não gregos, especialmente os trácios; simplesmente espada

DEFINITION: Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob and founder of a tribe.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (r'uwben); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite.

DEFINITION: Ruth, a Moabitess and an ancestor of Christ.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ruwth); Ruth, a Moabitess.

BDAG.en: Ruth, a Moabite, with a leading role in the OT book of the same name
BDAG.pt: Rute, uma moabita, com papel principal no livro do AT com seu nome

DEFINITION: Rufus, a Christian man in Rome, probably to be identified with the brother of Alexander and son of Simon of Cyrene.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Rufus. 1 son of Simon of Cyrene and brother of Alexander. 2 recipient of a greeting. 3 a steadfast confessor w. Ignatius and Zosimus.
BDAG.pt: Rufus. 1 filho de Simão de Cirene e irmão de Alexandre. 2 destinatário de uma saudação. 3 um confessor firme com Inácio e Zósimo.

DEFINITION: the rush (of a moving body), a (crowded) street.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from rhoumai in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded).

BDAG.en: in later Gk. narrow street, lane, alley.
BDAG.pt: no grego posterior, rua estreita, viela, beco.

DEFINITION: to rescue, deliver (from danger or destruction).
ORIGIN: Middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to rheo (through the idea of a current; compare rhusis); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. Rescue.

BDAG.en: to rescue from danger, save, rescue, deliver, preserve.
BDAG.pt: resgatar do perigo, salvar, livrar, preservar.

DEFINITION: filth, pollution, defilement.
ORIGIN: From rhuparos; dirtiness (morally).

BDAG.en: moral defilement or corruption, moral uncleanness, vulgarity; esp. sordid avarice, greediness
BDAG.pt: defilement moral ou corrupção, impureza moral, vulgaridade; especialmente avareza sórdida, ganância

DEFINITION: filthy, defiled, dirty.
ORIGIN: From rhupos; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being dirty, filthy, soiled; 2 pert. to moral sordidness, unclean, defiled
BDAG.pt: 1 relativo a ser sujo, imundo, manchado; 2 relativo a sordidez moral, impuro, contaminado

DEFINITION: filth, filthiness, dirt, squalor.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity.

BDAG.en: prim. 'a filthy substance, dirt'; fig. uncleanness; a dark viscous juice
BDAG.pt: primariamente ‘uma substância suja, sujeira’; figurativamente impureza; um suco escuro e viscoso

DEFINITION: to be filthy; hence (morally): to be stained with sin.
ORIGIN: From rhupos; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally).

DEFINITION: a flowing, an issue.
ORIGIN: From rhoumai in the sense of its congener rheo; a flux (of blood).

BDAG.en: flowing, flow (of blood, hemorrhage)
BDAG.pt: fluxo, escoamento (de sangue, hemorragia)

DEFINITION: a wrinkle; fig: a spiritual defect, flaw.
ORIGIN: From rhoumai; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. A wrinkle (especially on the face).

BDAG.en: a wrinkle, in imagery, of the church.
BDAG.pt: uma ruga, em imagética, da igreja.

DEFINITION: Roman, Latin.
ORIGIN: From Rhomaios; Romaic, i.e. Latin.

BDAG.en: Roman, Latin.
BDAG.pt: Romano, Latino.

DEFINITION: Roman; subst: a Roman citizen.
ORIGIN: From Rhome; Romaean, i.e. Roman (as noun).

BDAG.en: pert. to the city of Rome or the Roman Empire, Roman (noun: the Roman, the Roman citizen, pl. the Romans as a people or Roman citizens).
BDAG.pt: pertencente à cidade de Roma ou ao Império Romano, Romano (substantivo: o Romano, o cidadão romano, pl. os romanos como povo ou cidadãos romanos).

DEFINITION: in the Latin language.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a presumed derivative of Rhome; Romaistically, i.e. In the Latin language.

BDAG.en: in the Latin language, in Latin.
BDAG.pt: na língua latina, em latim.

DEFINITION: Rome, the capital of Italy and the Rom. Empire (named after Romulus, the legendary founder).
ORIGIN: From the base of rhonnumi; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy.

BDAG.en: the capital city of the Roman Empire, Rome.
BDAG.pt: a cidade capital do Império Romano, Roma.

DEFINITION: to strengthen, render firm; imperative at the end of letters: farewell.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from rhoomai (to dart; probably akin to rhoumai); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye).

BDAG.en: in the act. (obsolete in NT times) ‘to strengthen’; the perf. pass. (in the sense ‘be strong’, farewell, goodbye
BDAG.pt: No ativo (obsoleto nos tempos do NT) 'fortalecer'; no perfeito passivo (no sentido de 'estar forte', adeus, despedida)

DEFINITION: thou hast forsaken me.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee or (shbaq with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. Shebakthani), a cry of distress.

BDAG.en: you have forsaken me
BDAG.pt: Tu me abandonaste

DEFINITION: Sabaoth, armies.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (tsaba' in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. Tsebaoth), a military epithet of God.

BDAG.en: Sabaoth (Greek transcription of צְבָאוֹת), Yahweh Lord of the Armies, Lord of Hosts
BDAG.pt: Sabaoth (transcrição grega de צְבָאוֹת), Senhor dos Exércitos, Senhor das Hostes

DEFINITION: a keeping of the Sabbath, a Sabbath rest.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of sabbaton; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven).

BDAG.en: sabbath rest, sabbath observance fig. a special period of rest for God’s people modeled after the traditional sabbath
BDAG.pt: Descanso sabático, observância do sábado, figurado: um período especial de descanso para o povo de Deus modelado após o sábado tradicional

DEFINITION: the Sabbath, the seventh day (of the week).
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (shabbath); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. The interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications.

BDAG.en: the seventh day of the week in Israel’s calendar, marked by rest fr. work and by special religious ceremonies, sabbath; a period of seven days, week
BDAG.pt: O sétimo dia da semana no calendário de Israel, marcado pelo descanso do trabalho e por cerimônias religiosas especiais, sábado; um período de sete dias, semana

DEFINITION: a fishing-net.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of satto (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing.

BDAG.en: a large net hanging vertically, with floats on the top and sinkers on the bottom, seine, dragnet
BDAG.pt: uma rede grande pendurada verticalmente, com boias no topo e pesos na parte inferior, arrastão, rede de arrasto

DEFINITION: a Sadducee, a member of the aristocratic party among the Jews, from whom the high-priests were almost invariably chosen.
ORIGIN: Probably from Sadok; a Sadducaean (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite.

BDAG.en: member of a major Israelite group, Sadducee
BDAG.pt: membro de um grupo israelita principal, Saduceu

DEFINITION: Zadok, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Tsadowq); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Zadok, in the genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Zadoque, na genealogia de Jesus

DEFINITION: to fawn upon, flatter, beguile; pass: to be perturbed.
ORIGIN: Akin to seio; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb).

BDAG.en: 1 prim., of dogs, ‘wag the tail’; hence to try to win favor by an ingratiating manner, fawn upon, flatter; 2 to cause to be emotionally upset, move, disturb, agitate
BDAG.pt: 1 primariamente, de cães, 'abanar o rabo'; daí tentar ganhar favor com um comportamento lisonjeiro, bajular, adular; 2 causar agitação emocional, mover, perturbar, agitar

DEFINITION: sack-cloth, a sign of mourning.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (saq); "sack"-cloth, i.e. Mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief).

BDAG.en: a coarse cloth made of animal (goat or camel) hair, sack, sackcloth
BDAG.pt: um tecido grosseiro feito de pelo de animal (cabra ou camelo), saco, pano de saco (silício)

DEFINITION: Shelah, an ancestor of Christ, also Salmon, an ancestor of Christ.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shelach); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Shelah, in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
BDAG.pt: Selá, na genealogia de Lucas para Jesus

DEFINITION: Salathiel, son of Jechoniah.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Sh'altiy'el); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Shealtiel, Salathiel, father of Zerubbabel
BDAG.pt: Salatiel, pai de Zorobabel

DEFINITION: Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus.
ORIGIN: Probably from salos (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus.

BDAG.en: Salamis, a large city on the east coast of the island of Cyprus visited by Paul
BDAG.pt: Salamina, uma cidade grande na costa leste da ilha de Chipre visitada por Paulo

DEFINITION: Salim, a place in Palestine.
ORIGIN: Probably from the same as saleuo; Salim, a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Salim
BDAG.pt: Salim

DEFINITION: to shake, excite, disturb in mind, stir up, drive away.
ORIGIN: From salos; to waver, i.e. Agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite.
USAGE: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.

BDAG.en: 1 to cause to move to and fro, shake, cause to waver/totter; pass. be shaken, be made to waver/totter; 2 to disturb inwardly, disturb, shake, fig. ext. of 1
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer mover-se para frente e para trás, abalar, fazer vacilar/cambalear; pass. ser abalado, ser feito vacilar/cambalear; 2 perturbar interiormente, abalar, agitar, fig. extensão de 1

DEFINITION: Salem, doubtless identical with Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shalem); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Salem. Calls Melchizedek king of Salem and interprets it as ‘King of peace’
BDAG.pt: Salém. Chama a Melquisedeque rei de Salém e interpreta como 'Rei da paz'

DEFINITION: Salmon, son of Nahshon and father of Boaz.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Salmown); Salmon, an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Salmon, father of Boaz and ancestor of Jesus in the genealogy.
BDAG.pt: Salmom, pai de Boaz e ancestral de Jesus na genealogia.

DEFINITION: Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete.
ORIGIN: Perhaps of similar origin to Salamis; Salmone, a place in Crete.

BDAG.en: Salmone, a promontory on the northeast corner of Crete.
BDAG.pt: Salmone, um promontório no canto nordeste de Creta.

DEFINITION: the tossing of the sea in a tempest; agitation, rolling.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of saino; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow.

BDAG.en: a rolling or tossing motion, surge, esp. of the waves in a rough sea; also of an earthquake
BDAG.pt: um movimento de rolamento ou agitação, vaga, especialmente das ondas em mar agitado; também de um terremoto

DEFINITION: a trumpet, the sound of a trumpet.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from salos (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet.

BDAG.en: 1 a wind instrument used esp. for communication, trumpet; 2 the sound made or signal given by a trumpet, trumpet-call, trumpet-sound
BDAG.pt: 1 um instrumento de sopro usado especialmente para comunicação, trombeta; 2 o som produzido ou sinal dado por uma trombeta, chamado de trombeta, som de trombeta

DEFINITION: to sound a trumpet.
ORIGIN: From salpigx; to trumpet, i.e. Sound a blast (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1 to produce the sound of a trumpet, blow a trumpet; 2 to publicize someth. with fanfare, to trumpet
BDAG.pt: 1 produzir o som de uma trombeta, tocar a trombeta; 2 divulgar algo com alarde, trombetear

DEFINITION: a trumpeter.
ORIGIN: From salpizo; a trumpeter.

BDAG.en: trumpeter.
BDAG.pt: trompeteiro.

DEFINITION: Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John, the apostles.
ORIGIN: Probably of Hebrew origin; Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess.

BDAG.en: Salome, one of the Galilean women who followed Jesus; possibly the wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John.
BDAG.pt: Salomé, uma das mulheres galileias que seguiram Jesus; possivelmente a esposa de Zebedeu e mãe de Tiago e João.

DEFINITION: Samaria, a small district of Palestine, bounded by Galilee on the north, and by Judaea on the south, and taking its name from the city of Samaria, the ancient capital of the kingdom of (northern) Israel.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shomrown); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine.

BDAG.en: Samaria, the Gk. form of the name, referring to the whole province in NT times.
BDAG.pt: Samaria, a forma grega do nome, referindo-se a toda a província nos tempos do Novo Testamento.

DEFINITION: a Samaritan, an inhabitant of the region of Samaria.
ORIGIN: From Samareia; a Samarite, i.e. Inhabitant of Samaria.

DEFINITION: (the region of) Samaria, a Samaritan woman.
ORIGIN: Feminine of Samareites; a Samaritess, i.e. Woman of Samaria.

DEFINITION: "Samos of Thrace", Samothrace, an island in the Aegean.
ORIGIN: From Samos and Thraike (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Samothrace, an island in the northern part of the Aegean Sea.
BDAG.pt: Samotrácia, uma ilha na parte norte do Mar Egeu.

DEFINITION: Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor, near Ephesus and Miletus.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Samos, an island off the west coast of Asia Minor.
BDAG.pt: Samos, uma ilha na costa oeste da Ásia Menor.

DEFINITION: Samuel, a prophet and judge in Isr.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shmuw'el); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Samuel, a major OT prophet who concludes the period of the Judges and begins the line of prophets.
BDAG.pt: Samuel, um grande profeta do Antigo Testamento que conclui o período dos Juízes e inicia a linhagem dos profetas.

DEFINITION: Samson, one of the Judges of Israel.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shimshown); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Samson, a judge in Israel.
BDAG.pt: Sansão, um juiz em Israel.

DEFINITION: a sandal.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of sandalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad.

BDAG.en: sandal, footwear consisting of a sole held on the foot by thongs.
BDAG.pt: sandália, calçado consistindo de uma sola presa ao pé por tiras.

DEFINITION: a plank, board.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a plank.

BDAG.en: board, plank; possibly referring to pieces of wreckage from a ship.
BDAG.pt: tábua, prancha; possivelmente referindo-se a pedaços de destroços de um navio.

DEFINITION: Saul, (a) the first king of Israel, (b) the Hebrew name of the Apostle to the Gentiles.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Sha'uwl); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul.

BDAG.en: Saul, 1) son of Kish and first king of Israel. 2) Hebrew name of the Apostle Paul.
BDAG.pt: Saul, 1) filho de Quis e primeiro rei de Israel. 2) nome hebraico do Apóstolo Paulo.

DEFINITION: rotten, useless, corrupt, depraved.
ORIGIN: From sepo; rotten, i.e. Worthless (literally or morally).

BDAG.en: rotten, putrid; of poor quality, bad (of fruits, fish, trees, stones); morally bad or evil (an evil word).
BDAG.pt: podre, putrefato; de má qualidade, ruim (de frutas, peixes, árvores, pedras); moralmente mau ou perverso (uma palavra má).

DEFINITION: Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian.
ORIGIN: Feminine of sappheiros; Sapphire, an Israelitess.

DEFINITION: sapphire, perhaps lapis lazuli.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (cappiyr); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem.

DEFINITION: a basket, generally of twisted cords.
ORIGIN: Apparently of Hebrew origin (sarag); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work.

BDAG.en: basket (so Aeneas Tact. 1348; Timocl. Com. [IV b.c.], Fgm. 14, 4 Kock [in Athen. 8, 339e; 9, 407e]; Lucian, Lexiph. 6; BGU 417, 14; PFlor 269, 7; PStras 37, 13) 2 Cor 11:33, where it is ‘clearly a rope-basket’
BDAG.pt: cesto (como em Eneias Tático 1348; Timocles Com. [IV a.C.], Fgm. 14, 4 Kock [em Ateneu 8, 339e; 9, 407e]; Luciano, Lexiph. 6; BGU 417, 14; PFlor 269, 7; PStras 37, 13) 2 Coríntios 11:33, onde é 'claramente um cesto de corda'

DEFINITION: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia.
ORIGIN: Plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Sardis, the ancient capital city of Lydia, in western Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Sardis, a antiga cidade capital da Lídia, na Ásia Menor ocidental

DEFINITION: sardine.
ORIGIN: From the same as sardios; sardine (lithos being implied), i.e. A gem, so called.

BDAG.en: sardine (late form of σάρδιον)
BDAG.pt: sardino (forma tardia de σάρδιον)

DEFINITION: carnelian, a precious stone.
ORIGIN: Properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (lithos being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called.

BDAG.en: a reddish precious stone, carnelian, sard(ius)
BDAG.pt: uma pedra preciosa avermelhada, cornalina, sard(us)

DEFINITION: sardonyx, a precious stone, white streaked with red.
ORIGIN: From the base of sardios and onux (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. The gem so called.

BDAG.en: sardonyx, a precious stone, w. difft. colors in parallel layers, a variety of agate
BDAG.pt: sardônio, uma pedra preciosa, com cores diferentes em camadas paralelas, uma variedade de ágata

DEFINITION: Zarephath, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Tsarphath); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Zarephath, a city on the Phoenician coast betw. Tyre and Sidon, where Elijah lived during a famine.
BDAG.pt: Zarefata, uma cidade na costa fenícia entre Tiro e Sidom, onde Elias viveu durante uma fome.

DEFINITION: pertaining to the flesh, carnal.
ORIGIN: From sarx; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate.

BDAG.en: pert. to being material or belonging to the physical realm, material, physical, human, fleshly; pert. to being human at a disappointing level of behavior or characteristics, (merely) human.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser material ou pertencer ao reino físico, material, físico, humano, carnal; pertencente a ser humano em um nível decepcionante de comportamento ou características, (meramente) humano.

DEFINITION: fleshly, consisting of flesh, carnal.
ORIGIN: From sarx; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft.

BDAG.en: pert. to being material or belonging to the physical realm, material, physical, human, fleshly; pert. to being human at a disappointing level of behavior or character, (merely) human, in ref. to the state or condition of a human being, with focus on being weak, sinful, or transitory
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser material ou pertencer ao reino físico, material, físico, humano, carnal; pertencente a ser humano em um nível decepcionante de comportamento ou caráter, (meramente) humano, em referência ao estado ou condição de um ser humano, com foco em ser fraco, pecaminoso ou transitório

DEFINITION: flesh, body, human nature, materiality; kindred.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of saroo; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such).

BDAG.en: the material that covers the bones of a human or animal body, flesh; the physical body as functioning entity, body; one who is or becomes a physical being, living being with flesh, human being; human/mortal nature, earthly descent; the outward side of life as determined by normal perspectives or standards, a transf. sense of 1 and 2.
BDAG.pt: o material que cobre os ossos de um corpo humano ou animal, carne; o corpo físico funcionando como entidade, corpo; aquele que é ou se torna um ser físico, ser vivo com carne, ser humano; natureza humana/mortal, descendência terrena; o lado externo da vida determinado por perspectivas ou padrões normais, um sentido transferido de 1 e 2.

DEFINITION: Serug, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Sruwg); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Serug, son of Reu and father of Nahor.
BDAG.pt: Serugue, filho de Reu e pai de Naor.

DEFINITION: to sweep, cleanse by sweeping.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of sairo (to brush off; akin to suro); meaning a broom; to sweep.

BDAG.en: to sweep by using a broom, sweep
BDAG.pt: varrer usando uma vassoura, varrer

DEFINITION: Sarah, the wife of Abraham.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Sarah); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham.

BDAG.en: Sarah, wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac
BDAG.pt: Sara, esposa de Abraão, mãe de Isaque

DEFINITION: Sharon, the maritime plain between Carmel and Joppa.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Sharown); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine.

DEFINITION: Satan.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (satan); Satan, i.e. The devil.

BDAG.en: literally 'adversary'; the Satan, the special enemy of God and all who belong to God, simply Satan, the Enemy; The Lawless One (Antichrist); one who incites to evil, causes sickness, hinders apostles, or causes false beliefs; Peter was called Satan by Jesus when he tempted Him to avoid the divine plan.
BDAG.pt: literalmente 'adversário'; o Satanás, o inimigo especial de Deus e de todos os que Lhe pertencem, simplesmente Satanás, o Inimigo; o Iníquo (Anticristo); aquele que incita ao mal, causa doenças, impede apóstolos ou causa falsas crenças; Pedro foi chamado Satanás por Jesus quando tentou desviá-lo do plano divino.

DEFINITION: the adversary, Satan, the devil.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin corresponding to ma'bad (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. The devil.

DEFINITION: seah, a (Hebrew) measure (equiv. to about one and a half pecks).
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (c'ah); a certain measure for things dry.

BDAG.en: a Hebrew dry measure holding about thirteen liters, a seah, a thirteen-liter measure
BDAG.pt: uma medida seca hebraica contendo cerca de treze litros, um 'seah', uma medida de treze litros

DEFINITION: Saul, the Jewish name of the apostle Paul.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin, the same as Saoul; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul.

BDAG.en: Saul, Grecized form of שָׁאוּל, the Hebrew name of the Apostle Paul
BDAG.pt: Saulo, forma grega de שָׁאוּל, o nome hebraico do Apóstolo Paulo

DEFINITION: (a) to extinguish, quench, (b) to suppress, thwart.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to cause to cease to function or exist, quench, put out (literally extinguish fire; figuratively, quench or stifle the spirit); to be extinguished or go out (of lamps or the fire of hell).
BDAG.pt: fazer cessar a função ou a existência, apagar, extinguir (literalmente apagar fogo; figurativamente, apagar ou sufocar o espírito); ser extinto ou apagar-se (de lâmpadas ou do fogo do inferno).

DEFINITION: you.
ORIGIN: Accusative case singular of su; thee.

BDAG.en: see σύ (you)
BDAG.pt: ver σύ (tu/você)

DEFINITION: of (to, for) yourself.
ORIGIN: Genitive case from se and autos, also dative case of the same, seautoi seh-ow-to', and accusative case seauton seh-ow-ton', likewise contracted sautou (sow-too'), sautoi (sow-to'), and sauton (sow-ton'), respectively of (with, to) thyself.

BDAG.en: yourself (reflexive pronoun of the second person singular, used only in gen., dat., and acc.)
BDAG.pt: a ti mesmo/você mesmo (pronome reflexivo da segunda pessoa do singular, usado apenas no genitivo, dativo e acusativo)

DEFINITION: to fear, to have reverential awe.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from a derivative of sebomai; to venerate, i.e. Adore.

BDAG.en: to show reverence to, worship.
BDAG.pt: mostrar reverência a, adorar.

DEFINITION: an object of worship or veneration.
ORIGIN: From sebazomai; something adored, i.e. An object of worship (god, altar, etc).

BDAG.en: something related to devotional activity, devotional object; cultic monuments.
BDAG.pt: algo relacionado à atividade devocional, objeto devocional; monumentos de culto.

DEFINITION: (official Greek equivalent of Augustus), venerated, august, a title of the Roman emperors; hence secondarily: Augustan, imperial.
ORIGIN: From sebazomai; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial.

BDAG.en: worthy of reverence, revered, august, as a translation of Latin Augustus and designation of the Roman emperor.
BDAG.pt: digno de reverência, reverenciado, augusto, como tradução do latim Augustus e designação do imperador romano.

DEFINITION: to reverence, worship, adore.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. Adore.

BDAG.en: worship (Pind.+; Pla., Phd. ...); to have a reverent attitude toward human beings, show reverence/respect for (Aeschyl. et al.)
BDAG.pt: adorar (Píndaro e outros; Platão, Fédon...); ter uma atitude reverente para com os seres humanos, demonstrar reverência/respeito por (Esquilo e outros)

DEFINITION: a chain.
ORIGIN: Probably from suro through its congener eiro (to fasten; akin to haireomai); a chain (as binding or drawing).

BDAG.en: pliable length of someth. used for binding, cord, rope, chain
BDAG.pt: comprimento flexível de algo usado para atar, corda, cabo, corrente

DEFINITION: a shaking (as an earthquake); a storm.
ORIGIN: From seio; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake.

BDAG.en: a violent shaking or commotion, shock, agitation, in our lit. only of natural phenomena, most commonly earthquake
BDAG.pt: um abalo violento ou comoção, choque, agitação, em nossa literatura apenas de fenômenos naturais, mais comumente terremoto

DEFINITION: to shake; fig: to agitate, stir up.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern).

BDAG.en: to cause to be in a state of commotion, shake, agitate. a lit. of things, esp. natural phenomena shake... Pass. of the earth be shaken, quake... b fig. ext. of a, stir up, set in motion; pass. be stirred of a city... Of mental agitation tremble
BDAG.pt: causar um estado de comoção, sacudir, agitar. a lit. de coisas, especialmente fenômenos naturais sacudir... Passivo da terra ser abalada, tremer... b fig. extensão de a, agitar, pôr em movimento; passivo ser agitado de uma cidade... De agitação mental tremer

DEFINITION: "second", Secundus, a Christian of Thessalonica.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Secundus, a name of Latin origin, a Christian of Thessalonica
BDAG.pt: Secundus, um nome de origem latina, um cristão de Tessalônica

DEFINITION: Seleucia, on the Syrian coast, the harbor of Syrian Antioch.
ORIGIN: From Seleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria.

BDAG.en: Seleucia, the port city of Antioch in Syria
BDAG.pt: Selêucia, a cidade portuária de Antioquia na Síria

DEFINITION: the moon.
ORIGIN: From selas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of haireomai, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon.

BDAG.en: moon; darkened in the time of tribulation
BDAG.pt: lua; escurecida no tempo da tribulação

DEFINITION: to be moonstruck, be epileptic (supposedly influenced by the moon).
ORIGIN: Middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of selene; to be moon-struck, i.e. Crazy.

BDAG.en: to experience epileptic seizures, be an epileptic ('moonstruck')
BDAG.pt: experimentar convulsões epilépticas, ser epiléptico ('atirado pela lua')

DEFINITION: Semein, an ancestor of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shim'iy); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite.

DEFINITION: the finest wheaten flour.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour.

BDAG.en: a high-grade wheat flour, flour of the best quality
BDAG.pt: farinha de trigo de alta qualidade, farinha da melhor qualidade

DEFINITION: venerable, honorable, grave, serious, dignified.
ORIGIN: From sebomai; venerable, i.e. Honorable.

BDAG.en: pert. to evoking special respect a of living entities a human beings worthy of respect/honor, noble, dignified, serious... b transcendent beings worthy of reverence, august, sublime, holy... b of characteristics, states of being, and things honorable, worthy, venerable, holy, above reproach
BDAG.pt: pertencente a evocar respeito especial a de seres vivos a seres humanos dignos de respeito/honra, nobres, dignos, sérios... b seres transcendentes dignos de reverência, augustos, sublimes, santos... b de características, estados de ser e coisas honrosas, dignas, veneráveis, santas, irrepreensíveis

DEFINITION: dignity, honor, gravity, seriousness.
ORIGIN: From semnos; venerableness, i.e. Probity.

BDAG.en: a manner or mode of behavior that indicates one is above what is ordinary and therefore worthy of special respect a of a human being dignity, seriousness, probity, holiness... b of a deity holiness
BDAG.pt: um modo ou maneira de se comportar que indica que alguém está acima do que é comum e, portanto, digno de respeito especial a de um ser humano dignidade, seriedade, probidade, santidade... b de uma divindade santidade

DEFINITION: Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman.

BDAG.en: Sergius, name of a Roman gens.
BDAG.pt: Sérgio, nome de uma gens romana.

DEFINITION: Seth, third son of Adam.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Sheth); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Seth, son of Adam and Eve and father of Enos.
BDAG.pt: Sete, filho de Adão e Eva e pai de Enos.

DEFINITION: Shem, a son of Noah.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shem); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Shem, son of Noah and father of Arphaxad.
BDAG.pt: Sem, filho de Noé e pai de Arfaxade.

DEFINITION: to signify, indicate, give a sign, make known.
ORIGIN: From sema (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate.

BDAG.en: to make known, report, communicate... to intimate someth. respecting the future, indicate, suggest, intimate... to provide an explanation for someth. that is enigmatic, mean, signify
BDAG.pt: fazer saber, relatar, comunicar... indicar algo a respeito do futuro, indicar, sugerir, insinuar... fornecer uma explicação para algo que é enigmático, significar

DEFINITION: a sign, miracle, indication, mark, token.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of semaino; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally.

BDAG.en: a sign or distinguishing mark whereby someth. is known, sign, token, indication; a signal previously agreed upon; a sign of things to come; an event that is an indication or confirmation of intervention by transcendent powers, miracle, portent (a miracle of divine origin, or one worked by Satan or his agents; portent terrifying appearances in the heavens).
BDAG.pt: Um sinal ou marca distintiva pela qual algo é conhecido, sinal, testemunho, indicação; um sinal previamente acordado; um sinal de coisas vindouras; um evento que é indicação ou confirmação da intervenção de poderes transcendentes, milagre, presságio (um milagre de origem divina, ou um realizado por Satanás ou seus agentes; aparições terríveis nos céus).

DEFINITION: to note, mark for myself.
ORIGIN: From semeion; to distinguish, i.e. Mark (for avoidance).

DEFINITION: today, now.
ORIGIN: Neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ho (t changed to s) and hemera; on the (i.e. This) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. At present, hitherto).

BDAG.en: today, this very day; serves to denote a limited period of time (now... in a little while)
BDAG.pt: hoje, neste dia mesmo; serve para denotar um período de tempo limitado (agora... daqui a pouco)

DEFINITION: to make corrupt, pass. become corrupt.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish.

BDAG.en: Decay, rot; be decayed (rotten wood); flesh decays; suffering an aural discharge; bear rotten fruit; (of the treasures of the rich) rot
BDAG.pt: apodrecer, decompor; estar apodrecido (madeira podre); a carne apodrece; sofrer corrimento auricular; dar fruto podre; (dos tesouros dos ricos) apodrecer

DEFINITION: silken, silk.
ORIGIN: From Ser (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. Silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric).

BDAG.en: see σιρικός (not provided in extract)
BDAG.pt: ver σιρικός (não fornecido no extrato)

DEFINITION: a moth.
ORIGIN: Apparently of Hebrew origin (cac); a moth.

BDAG.en: the moth, whose larvae eat clothing; (being eaten by moths as a symbol of feebleness and destruction); wood-worms
BDAG.pt: a traça, cujas larvas comem roupas; (ser comido por traças como símbolo de fraqueza e destruição); vermes da madeira

DEFINITION: moth-eaten.
ORIGIN: From ses and a derivative of bibrosko; moth-eaten.

BDAG.en: motheaten
BDAG.pt: comido por traças, roído por traças

DEFINITION: to strengthen.
ORIGIN: From sthenos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of histemi); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power).

BDAG.en: strengthen, make strong
BDAG.pt: fortalecer, tornar forte

DEFINITION: a jawbone, by implication cheek.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face.

BDAG.en: cheek (jawbone used historically)
BDAG.pt: bochecha (maxilar usado historicamente)

DEFINITION: intrans: to be silent, keep silence; trans: to keep secret; pass: to be kept secret.
ORIGIN: From sige; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively).

BDAG.en: to be silent, intr. (say nothing, keep still, keep silent); stop speaking, become silent; to keep something from becoming known, keep secret, conceal, trans.
BDAG.pt: estar em silêncio, intransitivo (não dizer nada, ficar quieto, ficar em silêncio); parar de falar, calar-se; manter algo sem que se torne conhecido, guardar segredo, ocultar, transitivo

DEFINITION: silence.
ORIGIN: Apparently from sizo (to hiss, i.e. Hist or hush); silence.

BDAG.en: the absence of all noise, whether made by speaking or by anything else, silence, quiet
BDAG.pt: a ausência de todo ruído, seja feito por fala ou por qualquer outra coisa; silêncio, quietude

DEFINITION: made of iron.
ORIGIN: From sideros; made of iron.

DEFINITION: of iron.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; iron.

BDAG.en: iron; metonymically for sword; red-hot iron
BDAG.pt: ferro; metonimicamente para espada; ferro em brasa

DEFINITION: Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Tsiydown); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Sidon, an ancient Phoenician royal city, on the coast betw. Berytus (Beirut) and Tyre
BDAG.pt: Sidom, uma antiga cidade real fenícia, na costa entre Berito (Beirute) e Tiro

DEFINITION: Sidonian, inhabitant of Sidon.
ORIGIN: From Sidon; a Sidonian, i.e. Inhabitant of Sidon.

BDAG.en: pert. to Sidon, Sidonian (adjective); the country around Sidon (noun a); the Sidonians (noun b)
BDAG.pt: pertencente a Sidom, sidoniano (adjetivo); a região ao redor de Sidom (substantivo a); os sidonianos (substantivo b)

DEFINITION: an assassin, murderer, bandit; one of the Sicarii.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans).

BDAG.en: one who is intent on killing someone as part of an organized subversive political program, dagger man, assassin, terrorist, name of the most extreme group among Judean nationalists, quite hostile to Rome
BDAG.pt: aquele que tem a intenção de matar alguém como parte de um programa político subversivo organizado, homem da adaga, assassino, terrorista, nome do grupo mais extremo entre os nacionalistas judeus, bastante hostil a Roma

DEFINITION: intoxicating drink.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (shekar); an intoxicant, i.e. Intensely fermented liquor.

BDAG.en: an alcoholic beverage. As a rule, differentiated from wine and mentioned with it; beer
BDAG.pt: uma bebida alcoólica. Como regra, diferenciada do vinho e mencionada com ele; cerveja

DEFINITION: Silas, a pet-form of the name Silvanus; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.
ORIGIN: Contraction for Silouanos; Silas, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Silas. A respected member of the church at Jerusalem who was prophetically gifted; later accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey
BDAG.pt: Silas. Um membro respeitado da igreja em Jerusalém que possuía dons proféticos; mais tarde acompanhou Paulo em sua segunda viagem missionária

DEFINITION: "sylvan", Silvanus, alt. form of the name Silas.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Silvanus; surely the same man who appears in Ac as Silas (q.v.)
BDAG.pt: Silvano; certamente o mesmo homem que aparece em Atos como Silas (v.g.)

DEFINITION: Siloam, a spring within the walls, in the south-east corner of Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shiloach); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem.

BDAG.en: Siloam, name of a water supply system in Jerusalem, through which the water of the spring Gihon became available for the Fortress of David. ἡκολυμβήθρα τοῦΣ. the pool of Siloam
BDAG.pt: Siloé, nome de um sistema de abastecimento de água em Jerusalém, através do qual a água da fonte de Giom se tornou disponível para a Fortaleza de Davi. ἡκολυμβήθρα τοῦΣ. o tanque de Siloé

DEFINITION: an apron worn by artisans.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. Narrow covering (apron).

BDAG.en: apron, such as is worn by workers w. σουδάριον
BDAG.pt: aventais, como o usado por trabalhadores com o sudário

DEFINITION: Simon, the name of several Israelites.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shim'own); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites.

BDAG.en: Simon; 1 surnamed Πέτροσ= Κηφᾶς, most prominent of the twelve disciples; 2 another of the twelve disciples, called ὁΚαναναῖος or (ὁ) ζηλωτής; 3 brother of Jesus; 4 a man of Cyrene; 5 father of Judas Iscariot; 6 Σ. ὁλεπρός Simon the leper; 7 a Pharisee; 8 a tanner in Joppa; 9 a magician; 10 a Gnostic in Corinth
BDAG.pt: Simão; 1 cognominado Pedro = Cefas, o mais proeminente dos doze discípulos; 2 outro dos doze discípulos, chamado o Cananeu ou o Zelote; 3 irmão de Jesus; 4 um homem de Cirene; 5 pai de Judas Iscariotes; 6 Simão, o leproso; 7 um fariseu; 8 um curtidor em Jope; 9 um mágico; 10 um gnóstico em Corinto

DEFINITION: Sinai, a mountain probably on the Sinai Peninsula.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Ciynay); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia.

BDAG.en: Sinai, name of a rocky mountain on the peninsula named after it. Mountain on which the law was given
BDAG.pt: Sinai, nome de uma montanha rochosa na península que leva seu nome. Montanha na qual a lei foi dada

DEFINITION: mustard (probably the shrub, not the herb).
ORIGIN: Perhaps from sinomai (to hurt, i.e. Sting); mustard (the plant).

BDAG.en: mustard plant. κόκκος σινάπεως: mustard seed, popularly viewed as the smallest of all seeds
BDAG.pt: planta de mostarda. κόκκος σινάπεως: semente de mostarda, popularmente vista como a menor de todas as sementes

DEFINITION: fine linen, a linen cloth.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. Bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it).

BDAG.en: fine cloth; fabric made from linen, linen cloth, of the cloth in which the body of Jesus was wrapped; a light piece of clothing like a chemise, shirt.
BDAG.pt: tecido fino; tecido feito de linho, pano de linho, referindo-se ao lençol em que o corpo de Jesus foi envolvido; uma peça de roupa leve como uma camisa, túnica.

DEFINITION: to sift, prove by trials, winnow.
ORIGIN: From sinion (a sieve); to riddle (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to sift by shaking in a sieve, sift (metaphorically).
BDAG.pt: peneirar agitando em uma peneira, peneirar (metaforicamente).

DEFINITION: a pit (for grain storage).
ORIGIN: From a derivative of sitos; grain-fed, i.e. Fattened.

BDAG.en: fattened, ὁμόσχος ὁσιτευτός the calf that has been fattened
BDAG.pt: engordado, ὁμόσχος ὁσιτευτός o bezerro que foi engordado

DEFINITION: fattened; subst: a fatling, cattle.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of sitos; grained, i.e. Fatted.

BDAG.en: fattened, subst. τὰσιτιστά cattle that have been fattened
BDAG.pt: engordado, substantivo τὰσιτιστά gado que foi engordado

DEFINITION: a measured portion of grain or food.
ORIGIN: From sitos and metron; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food).

BDAG.en: a measured allowance of grain/food, food allowance, ration. διδόναι τὸς. give out the food allowance
BDAG.pt: uma porção medida de grão/alimento, ração de comida. διδόναι τὸς. distribuir a ração de comida

DEFINITION: wheat, grain.
ORIGIN: Also plural irregular neuter sita (see'-tah) of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat.

BDAG.en: wheat, but also grain gener. κόκκος τοῦς. (seed of the grain); συνάγειν τὸν ς. εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην to gather the grain into the storehouse
BDAG.pt: trigo, mas também grão em geral. κόκκος τοῦς. (semente do grão); συνάγειν τὸν ς. εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην ajuntar o grão no celeiro

DEFINITION: Zion, a mountain of Jerusalem or the city of Jer.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Tsiyown); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant).

BDAG.en: Zion, of 1 Mt. Zion, a hill within the city of Jerusalem; 2 the city of Jerusalem; 3 the people of God (a the people of Israel; b the New Jerus. of prophetic promise)
BDAG.pt: Sião, de 1 Monte Sião, uma colina dentro da cidade de Jerusalém; 2 a cidade de Jerusalém; 3 o povo de Deus (a o povo de Israel; b a Nova Jerusalém da promessa profética)

DEFINITION: to keep silence, be silent, either voluntarily or involuntarily.
ORIGIN: From siope (silence, i.e. A hush; properly, muteness, i.e. Involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from sige, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like kophos properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water).

BDAG.en: to refrain from speaking or making a sound, keep silent, say nothing; to disrupt the process of speaking or making a sound, stop speaking, be/become quiet (of humans or metaph. of wind/waves).
BDAG.pt: abster-se de falar ou fazer som, ficar em silêncio, não dizer nada; interromper o processo de falar ou fazer som, parar de falar, calar-se (de humanos ou metaforicamente do vento/ondas).

DEFINITION: to cause to stumble, cause to sin, cause to become indignant, shock, offend.
ORIGIN: From skandalon; to entrap, i.e. Trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure).

BDAG.en: to cause to be brought to a downfall, cause to sin; be led into sin, fall away; to shock through word or action, give offense to, anger, shock.
BDAG.pt: causar uma queda, fazer pecar; ser levado ao pecado, apostatar; chocar por palavra ou ação, ofender, irritar, abalar.

DEFINITION: a stick for bait (of a trap), generally a snare, a stumbling block, an offense.
ORIGIN: Scandal; probably from a derivative of kampto; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. Snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin).
USAGE: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.

BDAG.en: a device for catching something alive, trap; an action or circumstance that leads one to act contrary to a proper course of action, temptation to sin; that which causes offense or revulsion, fault, stain.
BDAG.pt: um dispositivo para capturar algo vivo, armadilha; uma ação ou circunstância que leva alguém a agir contrariamente a um curso correto de ação, tentação para pecar; aquilo que causa ofensa ou repulsa, falha, mancha.

DEFINITION: to dig, excavate.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to dig.

BDAG.en: to dig into the ground, dig; to dig for agricultural purposes, cultivate.
BDAG.pt: cavar no chão, cavar; cavar para fins agrícolas, cultivar.

DEFINITION: anything scooped out, a light boat.
ORIGIN: A "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing).

BDAG.en: generally something that is concave or hollow.
BDAG.pt: geralmente algo que é côncavo ou oco.

DEFINITION: the leg (from the hip downwards).
ORIGIN: Apparently from skello (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank).

BDAG.en: leg.
BDAG.pt: perna.

DEFINITION: clothing, a covering, raiment.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of skepas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of skopos through the idea of noticeableness); clothing.

BDAG.en: that which serves as a cover and hence as a protection, covering (chiefly clothing, but also house).
BDAG.pt: aquilo que serve como cobertura e, consequentemente, como proteção, cobertura (principalmente vestuário, mas também casa).

DEFINITION: Sceva, an inhabitant of Ephesus.
ORIGIN: Apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scoevus), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Sceva (a proper name, high priest).
BDAG.pt: Sceva (um nome próprio, sumo sacerdote).

DEFINITION: tackle, fittings, equipment.
ORIGIN: From skeuos; furniture, i.e. Spare tackle.

BDAG.en: a collective for a variety of items that fall in the category of σκεῦος, equipment (of a ship’s gear or equipment).
BDAG.pt: um coletivo para uma variedade de itens que se enquadram na categoria de σκεῦος, equipamento (referente ao aparelhamento ou equipamento de um navio).

DEFINITION: a vessel to contain liquid; a vessel of mercy or wrath; any instrument by which anything is done; a household utensil; of ships: tackle.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively (specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband)).

BDAG.en: a material object used to meet some need in an occupation or other responsibility, gener. thing, object used for any purpose at all; a container of any kind, vessel, jar, dish, etc.; a human being exercising a function, instrument, vessel fig. ext. of 1 or 2.
BDAG.pt: um objeto material usado para satisfazer alguma necessidade em uma ocupação ou outra responsabilidade, coisa em geral, objeto usado para qualquer finalidade; um recipiente de qualquer tipo, vaso, jarra, prato, etc.; um ser humano exercendo uma função, instrumento, vaso (extensão figurada de 1 ou 2).

DEFINITION: a tent, booth, tabernacle, abode, dwelling, mansion, habitation.
ORIGIN: Apparently akin to skeuos and skia; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: a place of shelter, freq. of temporary quarters in contrast to fixed abodes of solid construction, tent, hut a gener. lodging, dwelling, of the tents of nomads... Metaph. David’s fallen dwelling of his ruined kingdom... of a movable cultic tent... Yahweh’s tabernacle... transcendent celestial tent, tent, dwelling metaph. ext. of 1. The earthly Tabernacle corresponds in Hb to another σκηνή: Christ as High Priest... God’s σκ.=dwelling is in heaven... eternal dwellings of the life to come
BDAG.pt: um lugar de abrigo, frequentemente alojamento temporário em contraste com moradas fixas de construção sólida, tenda, cabana, uma morada ou habitação em geral, das tendas dos nômades... Metaforicamente, a morada caída de Davi, de seu reino arruinado... de uma tenda cultual móvel... o Tabernáculo de Yahweh... tenda celestial transcendente, tenda, morada, extensão metafórica de 1. O Tabernáculo terreno corresponde no Hb a outra σκηνή: Cristo como Sumo Sacerdote... A σκηνή de Deus = morada no céu... moradas eternas da vida futura

DEFINITION: the feast of tabernacles, the great festival of the Jews, held in October.
ORIGIN: From skenos and pegnumi; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes).

BDAG.en: prim. ‘the setting up of tents’ or ‘construction of huts’; as name for the Festival of Booths/Tabernacles.
BDAG.pt: primariamente, 'o erguer de tendas' ou 'construção de cabanas'; como nome para a Festa das Tendas/Tabernáculos.

DEFINITION: making tents.
ORIGIN: From skene and poieo; a manufacturer of tents.

BDAG.en: maker of stage properties (Old Comedy usage); traditionally, tentmaker.
BDAG.pt: fabricante de adereços de palco (uso na Comédia Antiga); tradicionalmente, fabricante de tendas.

DEFINITION: a tent, tabernacle; fig: of the human body.
ORIGIN: From skene; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit).

BDAG.en: a temporary abode as opposed to a permanent structure, tent, lodging fig. ext. of the prim. mng ‘tent’, which is not found in our lit.: of the body... be in one’s tent, i.e. be physically alive
BDAG.pt: uma morada temporária em oposição a uma estrutura permanente, tenda, alojamento, extensão metafórica do significado primário de 'tenda', que não é encontrado em nossa literatura: do corpo... estar em sua tenda, ou seja, estar fisicamente vivo

DEFINITION: to dwell as in a tent, encamp, have tabernacle.
ORIGIN: From skenos; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion).

BDAG.en: live, settle, take up residence
BDAG.pt: viver, estabelecer-se, tomar residência

DEFINITION: a tent pitched, a dwelling, tabernacle.
ORIGIN: From skenoo; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul).

BDAG.en: gener. ‘lodging, dwelling’, in our lit. only metaph. habitation a of a people... b of God... c of the body... remain alive
BDAG.pt: geralmente 'alojamento, morada', em nossa literatura apenas metaforicamente habitação a de um povo... b de Deus... c do corpo... permanecer vivo

DEFINITION: a shadow, shade, thick darkness, an outline.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)).

BDAG.en: shade or shelter from light and any heat associated with it, shade... the shape cast by an object as it blocks rays of light, shadow... a mere representation of someth. real, shadow
BDAG.pt: sombra ou abrigo da luz e qualquer calor associado a ela, sombra... a forma projetada por um objeto ao bloquear os raios de luz, sombra... uma mera representação de algo real, sombra

DEFINITION: to leap (for joy), skip, bound.
ORIGIN: Akin to skairo (to skip); to jump, i.e. Sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus).

BDAG.en: exuberant springing motion, leap, spring about as a sign of joy; of sheep gaily skipping about; of the movements of a child in the womb, which are taken as an expression of joy; metaph. these waters at once calm and then billowing with suggestion of life
BDAG.pt: movimento de saltar exuberante, saltar, pular como sinal de alegria; de ovelhas pulando alegremente; dos movimentos de uma criança no ventre, que são tomados como expressão de alegria; metaforicamente, estas águas ao mesmo tempo calmas e depois ondulando com sugestão de vida

DEFINITION: hardness of heart, perverseness, obstinacy.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a compound of skleros and kardia; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception.

BDAG.en: an unyielding frame of mind, hardness of heart, coldness, obstinacy, stubbornness
BDAG.pt: uma mentalidade inflexível, dureza de coração, frieza, obstinação, teimosia

DEFINITION: hard, violent, harsh, stern.
ORIGIN: From the base of skelos; dry, i.e. Hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe).

BDAG.en: pert. to being externally hard or rough, hard (to the touch), rough; pert. to causing an adverse reaction because of being hard or harsh, hard, harsh, unpleasant, of words, rough (strong) winds; pert. to being difficult to the point of being impossible, hard; pert. to being unyielding in behavior or attitude, hard, strict, harsh, cruel, merciless; stubbornness
BDAG.pt: pert. a ser externamente duro ou áspero, duro (ao toque), áspero; pert. a causar uma reação adversa por ser duro ou severo, duro, severo, desagradável, de palavras, ventos fortes/ásperos; pert. a ser difícil ao ponto de ser impossível, difícil; pert. a ser inflexível em comportamento ou atitude, duro, rigoroso, severo, cruel, impiedoso; teimosia

DEFINITION: hardness, hardness of heart, obstinacy, perverseness.
ORIGIN: From skleros; callousness, i.e. (figuratively) stubbornness.

BDAG.en: hardness (of heart), stubbornness as a human characteristic; of the spirit of harshness, roughness with which the Holy Spirit cannot live
BDAG.pt: dureza (de coração), teimosia como característica humana; do espírito de aspereza, rudez com a qual o Espírito Santo não pode habitar

DEFINITION: stiff-necked, stubborn, obstinate.
ORIGIN: From skleros and trachelos; hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate.

BDAG.en: stiff-necked, stubborn
BDAG.pt: de cerviz dura, teimoso

DEFINITION: to harden, make hard, make stubborn.
ORIGIN: From skleros; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn.

BDAG.en: prim. ‘harden’; in our lit. only in fig. sense: to cause to be unyielding in resisting information, harden (act. with a human subject, w. God as subj.; pass. be or become hardened)
BDAG.pt: primariamente 'endurecer'; em nossa literatura apenas em sentido figurado: fazer com que seja inflexível em resistir à informação, endurecer (ativo com sujeito humano, com Deus como sujeito; passivo ser ou tornar-se endurecido)

DEFINITION: crooked, perverse, unfair, curved, tortuous.
ORIGIN: From the base of skelos; warped, i.e. Winding; figuratively, perverse.

BDAG.en: pert. to being bent, curved, or crooked as opposed to straight, crooked; pert. to being morally bent or twisted, crooked, unscrupulous, dishonest, etc., fig. extension of 1, harsh, unjust masters; someth. wrong
BDAG.pt: pert. a ser curvado, arqueado ou torto em oposição a reto, torto; pert. a ser moralmente inclinado ou distorcido, torto, inescrupuloso, desonesto, etc., extensão figurada de 1, senhores duros, injustos; algo errado

DEFINITION: a stake or thorn; fig: a sharp affliction.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the base of skelos and optanomai; withered at the front, i.e. A point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability).

BDAG.en: orig. ‘anything pointed’ such as a ‘(pointed) stake’, then someth. that causes serious annoyance thorn, splinter, etc., specif. of an injurious foreign body (Paul alludes to his illness in a thorn in the flesh)
BDAG.pt: originalmente 'qualquer coisa pontiaguda' como uma 'estaca (apontada)', depois algo que causa sério aborrecimento, espinho, lasca, etc., especificamente um corpo estranho prejudicial (Paulo alude à sua doença em um espinho na carne)

DEFINITION: to look at, regard attentively, take heed, beware, consider.
ORIGIN: From skopos; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard.
USAGE: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare optanomai.

BDAG.en: to pay careful attention to, look (out) for, notice (w. acc. of pers. or thing someone or someth.); keep one’s eyes on what can be seen; look out for one’s own interests; look to oneself, that... not; consider whether the light be darkness
BDAG.pt: prestar atenção cuidadosa, procurar, notar (com acusativo de pessoa ou coisa alguém ou algo); manter os olhos fixos no que pode ser visto; procurar os próprios interesses; cuidar de si mesmo, para que... não; considerar se a luz é trevas

DEFINITION: a watchman, a mark (on which to fix the eye).
ORIGIN: From skeptomai (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to skapto through the idea of concealment; compare skepasma); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal.

BDAG.en: goal, mark; press on toward the goal; set a mark
BDAG.pt: meta, alvo; avançar em direção à meta; estabelecer uma marca

DEFINITION: to disperse, scatter abroad (as of sheep); to dissipate, waste; to distribute alms.
ORIGIN: Apparently from the same as skorpios (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal.

BDAG.en: to cause a group or gathering to go in various directions, scatter, disperse; to distribute in various directions, scatter abroad, distribute
BDAG.pt: fazer com que um grupo ou ajuntamento se mova em várias direções, espalhar, dispersar; distribuir em várias direções, espalhar, distribuir

DEFINITION: a scorpion.
ORIGIN: Probably from an obsolete skerpo (perhaps strengthened from the base of skopos and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting).

BDAG.en: a species of vermin, scorpion; an extremely harmful person, scorpion
BDAG.pt: uma espécie de inseto nocivo, escorpião; uma pessoa extremamente prejudicial, escorpião

DEFINITION: full of darkness, dark.
ORIGIN: From skotos; opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted.

BDAG.en: dark, obscure.
BDAG.pt: escuro, obscuro.

DEFINITION: darkness; fig: spiritual darkness.
ORIGIN: From skotos; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: state of being devoid of light, darkness, gloom; darkening of the mind or spirit, darkness, fig. ext. of 1, of ignorance in moral and relig. matters
BDAG.pt: estado de ausência de luz, escuridão, trevas; escurecimento da mente ou espírito, trevas, extensão figurada de 1, de ignorância em matérias morais e religiosas

DEFINITION: to darken.
ORIGIN: From skotos; to obscure (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: be/become dark, be darkened (lit.); be/become inwardly darkened, fig. ext. of 1, of the organ of spiritual and moral perception
BDAG.pt: ficar/tornar-se escuro, ser escurecido (lit.); ficar/tornar-se interiormente escurecido, extensão figurada de 1, do órgão da percepção espiritual e moral

DEFINITION: darkness, either physical or moral.
ORIGIN: From the base of skia; shadiness, i.e. Obscurity (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: darkness, gloom, lit.; the state of being unknown, darkness, fig.; the state of spiritual or moral darkness, darkness, of darkening by sin, of the state of unbelievers and of the godless
BDAG.pt: escuridão, trevas, lit.; o estado de não ser conhecido, escuridão, fig.; o estado de escuridão espiritual ou moral, trevas, de escurecimento pelo pecado, do estado de descrentes e ímpios

DEFINITION: (lit. or met.) to darken.
ORIGIN: From skotos; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: primarily 'to cause to be dark, darken', in our literature only passive functioning intransitively: 1 be/become darkened, literally. 2 be/become darkened in mind, figuratively extended from 1.
BDAG.pt: Primariamente 'causar escuridão, escurecer', em nossa literatura apenas na voz passiva funcionando intransitivamente: 1 tornar-se/ficar escuro, literalmente. 2 tornar-se/ficar escurecido na mente, sentido figurado estendido do 1.

DEFINITION: refuse, dregs, dung.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of eis and kuon and ballo; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. Refuse (ordure).

BDAG.en: useless or undesirable material that is subject to disposal, refuse, garbage ('excrement, manure, garbage, kitchen scraps'). Specifically human excrement.
BDAG.pt: Material inútil ou indesejável sujeito a descarte, refugo, lixo ('excremento, esterco, lixo, restos de cozinha'). Especificamente excremento humano.

DEFINITION: a Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia (considered the wildest of barbarians).
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage.

BDAG.en: the Scythian, living in the region of the Black Sea, frequently viewed as the epitome of unrefinement or savagery.
BDAG.pt: O Cita, que vivia na região do Mar Negro, frequentemente visto como o epítome da grosseiria ou selvageria.

DEFINITION: gloomy, sad-countenanced.
ORIGIN: From skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of optanomai; angry-visaged, i.e. Gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance.

BDAG.en: pertaining to having a look suggestive of gloom or sadness, sad, gloomy, sullen, dark. Metaphorically of dark garments, reflecting the wearer’s state of mind.
BDAG.pt: Pertencente a ter uma aparência sugestiva de melancolia ou tristeza, triste, sombrio, taciturno, escuro. Metaforicamente aplicado a vestes escuras, refletindo o estado de espírito de quem as veste.

DEFINITION: to flay, trouble, annoy, vex.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass.

BDAG.en: 1 weary, harass. 2 trouble, bother, annoy someone. 3 trouble oneself (by taking an interest in).
BDAG.pt: 1 Cansar, atormentar. 2 Incomodar, perturbar, aborrecer alguém. 3 Incomodar-se (por se interessar por).

DEFINITION: arms stripped from a foe, spoils.
ORIGIN: Neuter from skullo; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. Booty.

BDAG.en: armor and weapons taken ('stripped') from the body of a slain enemy, then generally booty, spoils.
BDAG.pt: Armadura e armas tiradas ('despojadas') do corpo de um inimigo abatido, depois, genericamente, espólio, despojo.

DEFINITION: eaten by worms.
ORIGIN: From skolex and a derivative of bibrosko; worm-eaten, i.e. Diseased with maggots.

BDAG.en: eaten by worms.
BDAG.pt: comido por vermes.

DEFINITION: a gnawing worm; gnawing anguish.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm.

BDAG.en: worm. Symbol of insignificance and wretchedness. A never-dying worm shall torment the damned.
BDAG.pt: Verme. Símbolo de insignificância e miséria. Um verme que não morre atormentará os condenados.

DEFINITION: made of emerald, emerald-green.
ORIGIN: From smaragdos; consisting of emerald.

BDAG.en: pertaining to emerald, (of) emerald (both 'made of emerald' and 'emerald in color').
BDAG.pt: Pertencente à esmeralda, (de) esmeralda (tanto 'feito de esmeralda' quanto 'com cor de esmeralda').

DEFINITION: an emerald.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called.

BDAG.en: a bright green transparent precious stone, emerald.
BDAG.pt: Uma pedra preciosa transparente de cor verde brilhante, esmeralda.

DEFINITION: myrrh (used as an ointment and for embalming).
ORIGIN: Apparently strengthened for muron; myrrh.

BDAG.en: the resinous gum of the bush ‘balsamodendron myrrha’, myrrh: with incense and other aromatic substances. With gold and incense. With aloes (for embalming a corpse).
BDAG.pt: A goma resinosa do arbusto 'balsamodendron myrrha', mirra: com incenso e outras substâncias aromáticas. Com ouro e incenso. Com aloés (para embalsamar um corpo).

DEFINITION: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia.
ORIGIN: The same as smurna; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Smyrna (a prosperous commercial city on the west coast of Asia Minor).
BDAG.pt: Esmirna (uma próspera cidade comercial na costa oeste da Ásia Menor).

DEFINITION: of Smyrna.
ORIGIN: From Smurna; a Smyrnoean.

BDAG.en: coming from Smyrna, the Smyrnaean.
BDAG.pt: Vindo de Esmirna, o Esmirnense.

DEFINITION: to be like myrrh, to mingle with myrrh.
ORIGIN: From Smurna; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. Embitter (as a narcotic).

BDAG.en: treat with myrrh. Past participle passive: wine flavored with myrrh.
BDAG.pt: Tratar com mirra. Particípio perfeito passivo: vinho aromatizado com mirra.

DEFINITION: Sodom, an unidentified city in the Jordan Valley.
ORIGIN: Plural of Hebrew origin (Cdom); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Sodom, the city that was destroyed by God with fire and brimstone because of the sinfulness of its inhabitants. As an example of extraordinary sinfulness.
BDAG.pt: Sodoma, a cidade que foi destruída por Deus com fogo e enxofre por causa da pecaminosidade de seus habitantes. Como exemplo de pecado extraordinário.

DEFINITION: you.
ORIGIN: Dative case of su; to thee.

DEFINITION: Solomon, son of David King of Israel, and Bathsheba.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Shlomoh); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David.

BDAG.en: Solomon, son of Bathsheba and David, and the latter’s successor, known for his love of splendor and for his wisdom. Builder of the first temple in Jerusalem. Also a colonnade named for him in Herod’s temple.
BDAG.pt: Salomão, filho de Bate-Seba e Davi, e sucessor deste, conhecido pelo seu amor ao esplendor e pela sua sabedoria. Construtor do primeiro templo em Jerusalém. Também um pórtico com o seu nome no templo de Herodes.

DEFINITION: a cinerary urn, by anal. a coffin.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to the base of soreuo; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier.

BDAG.en: coffin, bier.
BDAG.pt: Caixão, liteira (leito funerário).

DEFINITION: yours, thy, thine.
ORIGIN: From su; thine.

BDAG.en: possessive pronoun of the second person singular, pertaining to you (the addressee), your, yours (singular). Serves to emphasize or to contrast.
BDAG.pt: Pronome possessivo da segunda pessoa do singular, referente a ti (o destinatário), teu, tua, seus (singular). Serve para enfatizar ou contrastar.

DEFINITION: you.
ORIGIN: Genitive case of su; of thee, thy.
USAGE: X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.

DEFINITION: a handkerchief, a head cloth (for the dead).
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. Towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse).

BDAG.en: face-cloth for wiping perspiration, corresponding somewhat to our ‘handkerchief’, probably simply a cloth.
BDAG.pt: Pano de rosto para enxugar o suor, correspondendo algo ao nosso 'lenço', provavelmente simplesmente um pano.

DEFINITION: "lily", Susanna, one of the women accompanying Jesus on His journeys.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (shuwshan feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess.

BDAG.en: Susanna, a benefactor in the service of Jesus and The Twelve.
BDAG.pt: Joana (Susana), uma benfeitora a serviço de Jesus e dos Doze.

DEFINITION: wisdom, insight, skill (human or divine), intelligence.
