ORIGIN: From sophos; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual).

BDAG.en: 1 the capacity to understand and function accordingly, wisdom. a natural wisdom that belongs to this world (contrasted with God’s wisdom). b transcendent wisdom that God imparts to those who are close to God (e.g., Solomon, Stephen, Paul). The gift of unveiling secrets.
BDAG.pt: 1 A capacidade de compreender e agir de acordo, sabedoria. Uma sabedoria natural que pertence a este mundo (em contraste com a sabedoria de Deus). b Sabedoria transcendente que Deus concede àqueles que estão próximos d'Ele (ex: Salomão, Estêvão, Paulo). O dom de desvendar segredos.

DEFINITION: to make wise, instruct; pass: to be skillfully devised.
ORIGIN: From sophos; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. Continue plausible error.

BDAG.en: To cause a person to develop understanding to a relatively sophisticated degree, make wise, teach, instruct (passive); to be skilled in formulating or creating something in an artful manner, concoct ingeniously or devise craftily.
BDAG.pt: Fazer com que uma pessoa desenvolva entendimento a um grau relativamente sofisticado, tornar sábio, ensinar, instruir (passivo); ser hábil em formular ou criar algo de maneira engenhosa, inventar astutamente ou arquitetar de forma ardilosa.

DEFINITION: wise, learned, cultivated, skilled, clever.
ORIGIN: Akin to saphes (clear); wise (in a most general application).

BDAG.en: Clever, skillful, experienced (pert. to doing something skillfully); wise, learned, having intelligence and education above the average; wise in that the wisdom is divine in nature and origin; God is called wise.
BDAG.pt: Esperto, hábil, experiente (relativo a fazer algo com habilidade); sábio, culto, possuindo inteligência e educação acima da média; sábio no sentido de que a sabedoria é de natureza e origem divina; Deus é chamado de sábio.

DEFINITION: Spain, roughly co-extensive with the modern country of the name.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe.

BDAG.en: Spain, the goal of a journey planned by Paul
BDAG.pt: Espanha, o objetivo de uma jornada planejada por Paulo

DEFINITION: to convulse, throw into spasms.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from spairo (to grasp; apparently strengthened from spao through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. Convluse with epilepsy.

BDAG.en: to tear, pull to and fro, rend; shake to and fro; an unclean spirit convulses the person in whom it dwells.
BDAG.pt: rasgar, puxar para lá e para cá, dilacerar; sacudir; um espírito imundo convulsiona a pessoa em quem reside.

DEFINITION: to swathe, wrap in swaddling clothes.
ORIGIN: From sparganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of sparasso meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom).

BDAG.en: To wrap in pieces of cloth used for swaddling infants, wrap up in cloths.
BDAG.pt: Enrolar em pedaços de pano usados para embrulhar recém-nascidos, envolver em panos.

DEFINITION: to live extravagantly, luxuriously; to be wanton.
ORIGIN: From spatale (luxury); to be voluptuous.

BDAG.en: to indulge oneself beyond the bounds of propriety, live luxuriously/voluptuously; (of sheep) be sportive.
BDAG.pt: dar-se a prazeres além dos limites da decência, viver luxuosamente/voluptuosamente; (de ovelhas) ser brincalhão.

DEFINITION: to draw (as a sword), pull.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to draw.

BDAG.en: to exert force so as to pull or draw, draw, pull (out); in our literature (as almost always in the LXX) only mid. in the sense draw a sword.
BDAG.pt: exercer força para puxar ou arrastar, puxar (para fora); na nossa literatura (como quase sempre na LXX) apenas no meio no sentido de sacar uma espada.

DEFINITION: anything wound up or coiled, a body (of soldiers), a cohort.
ORIGIN: Of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of haireomai in the sense of its cognate heilisso; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors).

BDAG.en: a military term; probably always cohort, the tenth part of a legion.
BDAG.pt: um termo militar; provavelmente sempre coorte, a décima parte de uma legião.

DEFINITION: to sow, spread, scatter.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from spao (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. Sow (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: sow seed; in imagery and metaphor: of appropriating the fruits of another’s labor; the word of God, the gospel et al. are sown; the body after burial is compared to a seed-grain; scatter, disperse.
BDAG.pt: semear; em imagens e metáforas: apropriar-se dos frutos do trabalho alheio; a palavra de Deus, o evangelho e outros são semeados; o corpo após o sepultamento é comparado a um grão de semente; espalhar, dispersar.

DEFINITION: a body-guardsman; an executioner.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. Military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman).

BDAG.en: A Roman soldier, primarily 'spy, scout', then courier, but also executioner.
BDAG.pt: Um soldado romano, primariamente 'espião, batedor', depois mensageiro, mas também executor.

DEFINITION: to pour out (as a drink offering), to make a libation.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend").

BDAG.en: offer a libation/drink-offering, in our lit. only pass. and fig. of the apostle who is about to be offered up, to shed his blood as a sacrifice
BDAG.pt: oferecer uma libação/oferta de bebida, na nossa literatura apenas passivo e figurado, referindo-se ao apóstolo que está prestes a ser oferecido, derramando seu sangue como sacrifício

DEFINITION: (a) seed, commonly of cereals, (b) offspring, descendents.
ORIGIN: From speiro; something sown, i.e. Seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting).

BDAG.en: the source from which someth. is propagated, seed; male seed or semen; posterity, descendants; genetic character, nature, disposition, character; spiritual descendants
BDAG.pt: a fonte da qual algo é propagado, semente; sêmen ou esperma masculino; posteridade, descendentes; caráter genético, natureza, disposição, caráter; descendentes espirituais

DEFINITION: a babbler, gossiper, one who picks up seeds and trifles as does a bird.
ORIGIN: From sperma and lego; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk).

BDAG.en: subst. of a kind of bird, the ‘rook’; in pejorative imagery of persons whose communication lacks sophistication and seems to pick up scraps of information here and there scrapmonger, scavenger.
BDAG.pt: substantivo de um tipo de pássaro, o 'gralhão'; em imagem pejorativa de pessoas cuja comunicação carece de sofisticação e parece recolher fragmentos de informação daqui e dali, catador de restos, varredor.

DEFINITION: to hasten, urge on, desire earnestly.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from pous; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. Urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly.

BDAG.en: to be in a hurry, hurry, hasten, intr.; to cause someth. to happen or come into being by exercising special effort, hasten, trans. or strive for; to be very interested in discharging an obligation, be zealous, exert oneself, be industrious
BDAG.pt: ter pressa, apressar-se, correr, intransitivo; fazer com que algo aconteça ou venha à existência exercendo esforço especial, apressar, transitivo ou esforçar-se por; ter grande interesse em cumprir uma obrigação, ser zeloso, esforçar-se, ser industrioso

DEFINITION: a cave, den, hideout.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of speos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort.

BDAG.en: primarily ‘cave’; as a robbers’ hideout; as a place of refuge; as a place of birth; of tombs.
BDAG.pt: primariamente 'caverna'; como esconderijo de ladrões; como lugar de refúgio; como lugar de nascimento; de sepulcros.

DEFINITION: a ledge of rock (over which the sea dashes), a reef.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea.

BDAG.en: used metaph. in Jd 12. The interpretation depends on which of two possible mngs. is preferred: 1 a rocky hazard hidden by waves, a rock washed by the sea, a (hidden) reef 2 that which soils or discolors, spot, stain
BDAG.pt: usado metaforicamente em Judas 12. A interpretação depende de qual dos dois significados possíveis é preferido: 1 um perigo rochoso escondido pelas ondas, uma rocha lavada pelo mar, um recife (escondido) 2 aquilo que suja ou descolora, mancha, nódoa

DEFINITION: to defile, spot, stain, soil.
ORIGIN: From spilos; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: stain, defile in our lit. only metaph.
BDAG.pt: manchar, macular em nossa literatura apenas metaforicamente

DEFINITION: a spot, fault, stain, blemish.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace.

BDAG.en: spot (in stones representing people w. serious faults); stain, blemish (of the church)
BDAG.pt: mancha (em pedras que representam pessoas com falhas sérias); mancha, defeito (da igreja)

DEFINITION: to be moved in the inward parts, to feel compassion.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from splagchnon; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity.

BDAG.en: have pity, feel sympathy, perh. τινός with or for someone
BDAG.pt: ter piedade, sentir simpatia, talvez com ou por alguém

DEFINITION: the inward parts; the heart, affections, seat of the feelings.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from splen (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy.

DEFINITION: a sponge.
ORIGIN: Perhaps of foreign origin; a "sponge".

BDAG.en: sponge
BDAG.pt: esponja

DEFINITION: ashes.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; ashes.

BDAG.en: ashes w. γῆ as a designation for someth. transitory
BDAG.pt: cinzas com γῆ como designação para algo transitório

DEFINITION: a sowing, by implication seed.
ORIGIN: From speiro; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage.

BDAG.en: prim. ‘the activity of sowing’ and fig. ‘procreation’, then by metonymy ‘that which is sown’, whence it also comes to mean seed
BDAG.pt: primariamente 'a atividade de semear' e fig. 'procriação', depois por metonímia 'aquilo que é semeado', de onde também chega a significar semente

DEFINITION: sown; neut. plur: sown fields.
ORIGIN: From sporos; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field.

BDAG.en: pert. to being sown, sown, subst. τὰσπόριμα standing grain, grain fields
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao ser semeado, semeado, subst. τὰσπόριμα grãos em pé, campos de grãos

DEFINITION: a sowing, seed (sown).
ORIGIN: From speiro; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown).

BDAG.en: store of seed (i.e. your store of things to distribute to the needy)
BDAG.pt: reserva de sementes (ou seja, sua reserva de coisas para distribuir aos necessitados)

DEFINITION: to make haste, to give diligence.
ORIGIN: From spoude; to use speed, i.e. To make effort, be prompt or earnest.
USAGE: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.

BDAG.en: 1 to proceed quickly, hurry, hasten 2 to speed up a process, expedite 3 to be especially conscientious in discharging an obligation, be zealous/eager, take pains, make every effort, be conscientious
BDAG.pt: 1 proceder rapidamente, apressar-se, correr 2 acelerar um processo, expedir 3 ser especialmente consciencioso no cumprimento de uma obrigação, ser zeloso/ansioso, empenhar-se, fazer todo o esforço, ser consciencioso

DEFINITION: diligent, earnest, zealous, eager.
ORIGIN: From spoude; prompt, energetic, earnest.

BDAG.en: pert. to being conscientious in discharging a duty or obligation, eager, zealous, earnest, diligent
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser consciencioso no cumprimento de um dever ou obrigação, ávido, zeloso, sério, diligente

DEFINITION: more diligently, earnestly, eagerly, zealously.
ORIGIN: Neuter of spoudaioteros as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. Very promptly.

DEFINITION: more diligent.
ORIGIN: Comparative of spoudaios; more prompt, more earnest.

DEFINITION: more earnestly, diligently, zealously.
ORIGIN: Adverb from spoudaioteros; more speedily, i.e. Sooner than otherwise.

DEFINITION: diligently, earnestly, zealously.
ORIGIN: Adverb from spoudaios; earnestly, promptly.

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to being quick in doing someth., with haste, w. focus on importance of what is done 2 pert. to being conscientious in discharging a duty or obligation, diligently, earnestly, zealously
BDAG.pt: 1 pertencente a ser rápido em fazer algo, com pressa, com foco na importância do que é feito 2 pertencente a ser consciencioso no cumprimento de um dever ou obrigação, diligentemente, seriamente, zelosamente

DEFINITION: (a) speed, haste, (b) diligence, earnestness, enthusiasm.
ORIGIN: From speudo; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness.

BDAG.en: 1 swiftness of movement or action, haste, speed 2 earnest commitment in discharge of an obligation or experience of a relationship, eagerness, earnestness, diligence, willingness, zeal
BDAG.pt: 1 rapidez de movimento ou ação, pressa, velocidade 2 compromisso sério no cumprimento de uma obrigação ou experiência de um relacionamento, ânsia, seriedade, diligência, boa vontade, zelo

DEFINITION: a (large, flexible) basket (for carrying provisions).
ORIGIN: From speiro (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle.

BDAG.en: basket, hamper
BDAG.pt: cesta, balaio

DEFINITION: (a) a stadium, one eighth of a Roman mile, (b) a race-course for public games.
ORIGIN: Or masculine (in plural) stadios (stad'-ee-os) from the base of histemi (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course.

BDAG.en: 1 a measure of distance of about 192 meters, stade, one-eighth mile 2 an area for public spectacles, arena, stadium
BDAG.pt: 1 uma medida de distância de cerca de 192 metros, estádio, um oitavo de milha 2 uma área para espetáculos públicos, arena, estádio

DEFINITION: an earthen jar (for racking off wine).
ORIGIN: From the base of histemi (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank.

BDAG.en: jar, pitcher (often used for storing liquids)
BDAG.pt: jarro, cântaro (frequentemente usado para armazenar líquidos)

DEFINITION: an insurrection, dissension; originally: standing, position, place.
ORIGIN: From the base of histemi; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy.

BDAG.en: condition of being in a certain position or state of affairs, existence, occurrence; movement toward a (new) state of affairs, uprising, riot, rebellion; lack of agreement respecting policy, strife, discord, disunion; difference in opinion, dispute
BDAG.pt: condição de estar em determinada posição ou estado de coisas, existência, ocorrência; movimento em direção a um (novo) estado de coisas, levante, motim, rebelião; falta de acordo sobre política, conflito, discórdia, desunião; diferença de opinião, disputa

DEFINITION: an Attic silver coin equal in value to the Jewish shekel.
ORIGIN: From the base of kauchesis; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin.

BDAG.en: the stater, a silver coin = four drachmas
BDAG.pt: o estáter, uma moeda de prata equivalente a quatro dracmas

DEFINITION: an upright stake, a cross (the Rom. instrument of crucifixion).
ORIGIN: From the base of histemi; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. Self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ.

BDAG.en: a pole to be placed in the ground and used for capital punishment, cross, a stake sunk into the earth in an upright position; the cross, with focus on the fate of Jesus Christ, the cross; the suffering/death which believers endure
BDAG.pt: um poste a ser colocado no chão e usado para punição capital, cruz, uma estaca afundada no chão em posição vertical; a cruz, com foco no destino de Jesus Cristo, a cruz; o sofrimento/morte que os crentes suportam

DEFINITION: to fix to the cross, crucify; fig: to destroy, mortify.
ORIGIN: From stauros; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness.

BDAG.en: to fasten to a cross, crucify; destroy through connection with the crucifixion of Christ, crucify, a transcendent sense in ext. of 1, of imitation of Christ; fig.
BDAG.pt: crucificar, prender a uma cruz; figurativamente, destruir através da conexão com a crucificação de Cristo, crucificar, num sentido transcendente de imitação de Cristo.

DEFINITION: a grape, cluster of grapes.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of stephanos; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined).

BDAG.en: (a bunch of) grapes
BDAG.pt: (um cacho de) uvas

DEFINITION: a head of grain.
ORIGIN: From the base of histemi; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk).

BDAG.en: the fruiting spike of a cereal grain, head or ear (of grain); spikenard flower
BDAG.pt: a espiga frutífera de um cereal, cabeça ou espiga (de grão); flor de nardo

DEFINITION: Stachys, a Christian man at Rome.
ORIGIN: The same as stachus; Stachys, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Stachys, recipient of a greeting
BDAG.pt: Estáquis, destinatário de uma saudação

DEFINITION: a flat roof of a house.
ORIGIN: Strengthened from a primary tegos (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof.

BDAG.en: roof
BDAG.pt: telhado

DEFINITION: to cover closely (so as to keep water out), generally to bear up under.
ORIGIN: From stege; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently).

BDAG.en: to keep confidential, cover, pass over in silence; to bear up against difficulties, bear, stand, endure
BDAG.pt: manter confidencial, cobrir, passar em silêncio; suportar dificuldades, aguentar, aguentar, suportar

DEFINITION: barren.
ORIGIN: A contraction from stereos (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile".

DEFINITION: to set, arrange; mid: to provide for, take care, withdraw from, hold aloof, avoid.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from the base of histemi; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with).

BDAG.en: to keep one's distance, keep away, stand aloof from someone; to shun something, avoid, try to avoid
BDAG.pt: manter distância, manter-se afastado, ficar distante de alguém; evitar algo, esquivar-se, tentar evitar

DEFINITION: a garland, wreath, crown.
ORIGIN: From the base of stephanos; a wreath for show.

BDAG.en: wreath/garland of flowers
BDAG.pt: grinalda/coroa de flores

DEFINITION: a groaning, sighing.
ORIGIN: From stenazo; a sigh.

BDAG.en: an involuntary expression of great concern or stress, sigh, groan, groaning
BDAG.pt: uma expressão involuntária de grande preocupação ou estresse, suspiro, gemido, lamentação

DEFINITION: to groan, expressing grief, anger, or desire.
ORIGIN: From stenos; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly.

BDAG.en: to express oneself involuntarily in the face of an undesirable circumstance, sigh, groan; to express discontent, complain
BDAG.pt: expressar-se involuntariamente diante de uma circunstância indesejável, suspirar, gemer; expressar descontentamento, queixar-se

DEFINITION: narrow, strait.
ORIGIN: Probably from the base of histemi; narrow (from obstacles standing close about).

BDAG.en: narrow (in reference to dimension)
BDAG.pt: estreito (em referência à dimensão)

DEFINITION: (to keep some one in a tight place), to press upon, cramp, restrain.
ORIGIN: From the same as stenochoria; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp.

BDAG.en: to confine or restrict to a narrow space, crowd, cramp, confine, restrict; fig. be confined, restricted; to be in a circumstance that seems to offer no way out, be distressed
BDAG.pt: confinar ou restringir a um espaço estreito, apertar, comprimir, confinar, restringir; fig. ser confinado, restringido; estar em uma circunstância que parece não oferecer saída, estar angustiado

DEFINITION: a narrow space, great distress, anguish.
ORIGIN: From a compound of stenos and chora; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity.

BDAG.en: a set of stressful circumstances, distress, difficulty, anguish, trouble
BDAG.pt: um conjunto de circunstâncias estressantes, aflição, dificuldade, angústia, problema

DEFINITION: solid, firm, steadfast.
ORIGIN: From histemi; stiff, i.e. Solid, stable (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: firm, hard, solid, strong; fig. steadfast, firm (of character)
BDAG.pt: firme, duro, sólido, forte; fig. constante, firme (de caráter)

DEFINITION: to strengthen, confirm, establish, settle.
ORIGIN: From stereos; to solidify, i.e. Confirm (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to render physically firm, make strong, make firm; fig. to cause to become firmer in such matters as conviction or commitment, strengthen
BDAG.pt: tornar fisicamente firme, fortalecer, firmar; fig. fazer com que se torne mais firme em questões como convicção ou compromisso, fortalecer

DEFINITION: a solid body, a support, strength, firmness.
ORIGIN: From stereoo; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability).

BDAG.en: the sky as a supporting structure, the firmament; state or condition of firm commitment, firmness, steadfastness
BDAG.pt: o céu como estrutura de sustentação, o firmamento; estado ou condição de firme compromisso, firmeza, constância

DEFINITION: "crowned", Stephanas, a Christian at Corinth.
ORIGIN: Probably contraction for stephanotos (crowned; from stephanoo); Stephanas, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Stephanas, a member of the church at Corinth
BDAG.pt: Estéfanas, membro da igreja em Corinto

DEFINITION: a crown, garland, honor, glory.
ORIGIN: From an apparently primary stepho (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, diadema), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: a wreath made of foliage or designed to resemble foliage and worn by one of high status or held in high regard, wreath, crown; that which serves as adornment or source of pride, adornment, pride, fig. ext. of 1; award or prize for exceptional service or conduct, prize, reward fig.
BDAG.pt: uma coroa feita de folhagem ou com aparência de folhagem, usada por alguém de alto status ou muito estimado, grinalda, coroa; aquilo que serve de adorno ou motivo de orgulho, adorno, orgulho, extensão figurada de 1; concessão ou prêmio por serviço ou conduta excepcional, prêmio, recompensa (fig.).

DEFINITION: Stephen, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem, and the first martyr.
ORIGIN: The same as stephanos; Stephanus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Stephen, one of the seven ‘assistants’ in Jerusalem
BDAG.pt: Estêvão, um dos sete 'assistentes' em Jerusalém

DEFINITION: to crown, adorn, decorate.
ORIGIN: From stephanos; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to encircle someone’s head with ornamental foliage, wreathe, crown; to recognize distinguished service or performance with an award, honor, reward, crown, fig. ext. of 1.
BDAG.pt: cercar a cabeça de alguém com folhagem ornamental, coroar, enfeitar com grinalda; reconhecer serviço ou desempenho distinto com um prêmio, honra, recompensa, coroa, extensão figurada de 1.

DEFINITION: the breast, chest.
ORIGIN: From histemi (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. Chest.

BDAG.en: chest, breast.
BDAG.pt: peito.

DEFINITION: to stand fast, stand firm, persevere.
ORIGIN: From the perfect tense of histemi; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere.

BDAG.en: to be in a standing position, stand; to be firmly committed in conviction or belief, stand firm, be steadfast.
BDAG.pt: estar em posição de pé, ficar de pé; estar firmemente comprometido em convicção ou crença, manter-se firme, ser inabalável.

DEFINITION: a setting firmly, steadfastness.
ORIGIN: From sterizo; stability (figuratively).

BDAG.en: a state of security, safe position; firm commitment to conviction or belief, steadfastness.
BDAG.pt: Um estado de segurança, posição segura; firme compromisso com a convicção ou crença, perseverança.

DEFINITION: (a) to fix firmly, direct myself towards, (b) generally met: to buttress, prop, support; to strengthen, establish.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of histemi (like stereos); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm.

BDAG.en: to fix firmly in a place, set up, establish, support, lit.; to cause to be inwardly firm or committed, confirm, establish, strengthen fig. ext. of 1.
BDAG.pt: fixar firmemente em um lugar, erguer, estabelecer, apoiar (literalmente); fazer com que seja interiormente firme ou comprometido, confirmar, estabelecer, fortalecer (extensão figurada de 1).

DEFINITION: a bed of leaves or rushes.
ORIGIN: From a primary stizo (to "stick", i.e. Prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service.

BDAG.en: mark, brand (often referring to scars or marks from service/suffering).
BDAG.pt: marca, estigma (frequentemente referindo-se a cicatrizes ou marcas de serviço/sofrimento).

DEFINITION: a moment, point of time, an instant.
ORIGIN: Feminine of stigma; a point of time, i.e. An instant.

BDAG.en: point; a moment (of time).
BDAG.pt: Ponto; um momento (no tempo).

DEFINITION: to shine, glisten, flash, be radiant.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. Flash intensely.

BDAG.en: to cast rays of light, shine, be radiant (of garments, gates).
BDAG.pt: emitir raios de luz, brilhar, ser radiante (de vestimentas, portões).

DEFINITION: a colonnade, portico.
ORIGIN: Probably from histemi; a colonnade or interior piazza.

BDAG.en: a roofed colonnade open normally on one side, portico.
BDAG.pt: uma colunata coberta, aberta normalmente em um lado, pórtico.

DEFINITION: a bough, branch of a tree.
ORIGIN: From a primary steibo (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed.

BDAG.en: See στιβάς (leaves, leafy branches).
BDAG.pt: Ver στιβάς (folhas, ramos frondosos).

DEFINITION: (a) plur: the heavenly bodies, (b) a rudiment, an element, a rudimentary principle, an elementary rule.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of stoicheo; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively).

BDAG.en: basic component of something, elements of substances underlying the natural world; fundamental principles or letters of the alphabet; transcendent powers that are in control over events in this world, elements, elemental spirits
BDAG.pt: componente básico de algo, elementos de substâncias subjacentes ao mundo natural; princípios fundamentais ou letras do alfabeto; poderes transcendentes que controlam os eventos neste mundo, elementos, espíritos elementares

DEFINITION: to be in rows, to walk by rule.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of steicho (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety.

BDAG.en: to be in line with a person or thing considered as standard for one's conduct, hold to, agree with, follow, conform with
BDAG.pt: estar em linha com uma pessoa ou coisa considerada padrão para a conduta, aderir a, concordar com, seguir, conformar-se com

DEFINITION: a long robe, worn by the upper classes in the East.
ORIGIN: From stello; equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity).

BDAG.en: a long, flowing robe (often worn by angels or glorified believers)
BDAG.pt: uma túnica longa e fluida (frequentemente vestida por anjos ou crentes glorificados)

DEFINITION: the mouth, speech, eloquence in speech, the point of a sword.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of tomoteros; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon).

BDAG.en: mouth (of humans, animals, or beings resembling humans); utterance, product of the organ of speech; geological fissure, edge/foremost part
BDAG.pt: boca (de humanos, animais ou seres com aparência humana); expressão, produto do órgão da fala; fissura geológica, borda/parte mais proeminente

DEFINITION: an opening, the stomach.
ORIGIN: From stoma; an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach".

BDAG.en: stomach
BDAG.pt: estômago

DEFINITION: warfare, military service; of Christian warfare.
ORIGIN: From strateuomai; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger).

BDAG.en: military engagement, expedition, campaign (also used figuratively for Christian warfare)
BDAG.pt: engajamento militar, expedição, campanha (também usado figurativamente para a guerra cristã)

DEFINITION: an expedition, an army, a company of soldiers.
ORIGIN: From strateuomai; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic).

BDAG.en: a military force, army, detachment of soldiers
BDAG.pt: uma força militar, exército, destacamento de soldados

DEFINITION: to wage war, fight, serve as a soldier; fig: of the warring lusts against the soul.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from the base of stratia; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations.

DEFINITION: (a) a general or leader of the army, (b) a magistrate or governor, (c) captain of the temple.
ORIGIN: From the base of stratia and ago or hegeomai; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (praetor), the chief (praefect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens.

BDAG.en: highest official in a Gr-Rom. city (praetor, chief magistrate); commander responsible for the temple in Jerusalem (captain of the temple)
BDAG.pt: oficial mais alto em uma cidade greco-romana (pretor, magistrado-chefe); comandante responsável pelo templo em Jerusalém (capitão do templo)

DEFINITION: an army; met: a host of angels, the hosts of heaven (i.e. the stars).
ORIGIN: Feminine of a derivative of stratos (an army; from the base of stronnumi, as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. An army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries.

BDAG.en: army, heavenly army of angels, host of heaven (heavenly bodies)
BDAG.pt: exército, exército celestial de anjos, hoste celestial (corpos celestes)

DEFINITION: a soldier.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of the same as stratia; a camper-out, i.e. A (common) warrior (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: soldier (literally or figuratively, like a soldier of Christ Jesus)
BDAG.pt: soldado (literalmente ou figurativamente, como um soldado de Jesus Cristo)

DEFINITION: to collect an army, enlist troops.
ORIGIN: From a compound of the base of stratia and lego (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. Enlist in the army.

BDAG.en: gather an army, enlist soldiers
BDAG.pt: reunir um exército, alistar soldados

DEFINITION: commander of the Roman emperor's body-guard.
ORIGIN: From stratopedon and archo; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a Praetorian praefect.

BDAG.en: military commander, commandant of a camp
BDAG.pt: comandante militar, comandante de um acampamento

DEFINITION: a military camp, an army.
ORIGIN: From the base of stratia and the same as pedinos; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops.

BDAG.en: lit. ‘camp’, then ‘body of troops, army’
BDAG.pt: lit. ‘acampamento’, depois ‘corpo de tropas, exército’

DEFINITION: to twist, torture; met: to twist or pervert language.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of strepho; to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert.

BDAG.en: to cause inward pain, torture, torment; to distort a statement so that a false mng. results, twist, distort
BDAG.pt: causar dor interior, torturar, atormentar; distorcer uma declaração para que resulte um falso significado, torcer, deturpar

DEFINITION: to turn, be converted, change, change direction.
ORIGIN: Strengthened from the base of trope; to twist, i.e. Turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).

BDAG.en: to change the position of someth. relative to someth. by turning a turn; turn around, turn toward; to carry someth. back to its previous location, bring back, return; to turn someth. into someth. else, turn, change; to turn away so as to dissociate oneself, turn intr.; to experience an inward change, turn, change
BDAG.pt: mudar a posição de algo em relação a algo, virando; virar-se, voltar-se para; levar algo de volta ao seu local anterior, trazer de volta, retornar; transformar algo em outra coisa, mudar, alterar; afastar-se para se dissociar, virar-se (intransitivo); experimentar uma mudança interna, virar, mudar

DEFINITION: to live luxuriously, revel, riot.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of strenos; to be luxurious.

BDAG.en: live in luxury, live sensually
BDAG.pt: viver em luxúria, viver sensualizadamente

DEFINITION: wantonness, luxury.
ORIGIN: Akin to stereos; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness).

BDAG.en: sensuality, luxury
BDAG.pt: sensualidade, luxo

DEFINITION: a small bird, sparrow.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of strouthos (a sparrow); a little sparrow.

BDAG.en: sparrow (diminutive)
BDAG.pt: pardal (diminutivo)

DEFINITION: to spread, make a bed.
ORIGIN: Or simpler stronnuo (strone-noo'-o), prolongation from a still simpler stroo (stro'-o), (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to stereos through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. Spread (as a carpet or couch).

DEFINITION: hateful, detestable, disgusting.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo (to hate); hated, i.e. Odious.

BDAG.en: loathsome, despicable
BDAG.pt: detestável, desprezível

DEFINITION: to be gloomy, have a somber countenance, be shocked.
ORIGIN: From the same as stugnetos; to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech).

BDAG.en: to be in state of intense dismay, be shocked, appalled; to have a dark or gloomy appearance, be or become gloomy, dark
BDAG.pt: estar em estado de intenso desalento, ficar chocado, horrorizado; ter uma aparência escura ou sombria, ficar ou tornar-se sombrio, escuro

DEFINITION: a pillar, support, column.
ORIGIN: From stuo (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of histemi); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support.

BDAG.en: a supporting portion, ordinarily cylindrical, of a structure, pillar, column; a person or community recognized for spiritual leadership, pillar, support
BDAG.pt: uma porção de suporte, ordinariamente cilíndrica, de uma estrutura, pilar, coluna; uma pessoa ou comunidade reconhecida pela liderança espiritual, pilar, suporte

DEFINITION: a Stoic.
ORIGIN: From stoa; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. Adherent of a certin philosophy.

BDAG.en: Stoic (see Στοϊκός)
BDAG.pt: Estoico (ver Στοϊκός)

DEFINITION: you (early mod. Eng. thou).
ORIGIN: The person pronoun of the second person singular; thou.
USAGE: thou. See also se, soi, sou; and for the plural humas, humeis, humin, humon.

BDAG.en: you (personal pronoun, second person singular, used for emphasis, contrast, or pleonastically)
BDAG.pt: tu/você (pronome pessoal, segunda pessoa do singular, usado para ênfase, contraste ou pleonasmo)

DEFINITION: kinship, kinfolk, relatives.
ORIGIN: From suggenes; relationship, i.e. (concretely) relatives.

BDAG.en: an extended family system, relationship, kinship concr. the relatives
BDAG.pt: um sistema familiar estendido, parentesco, afinidade, concretamente os parentes

DEFINITION: akin to, related; subst: fellow countryman, kinsman.
ORIGIN: From sun and genos; a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman.

BDAG.en: belonging to the same extended family or clan, related, akin to (used substantively for relative or compatriot)
BDAG.pt: pertencente à mesma família extensa ou clã, relacionado, aparentado (usado como substantivo para parente ou compatriota)

DEFINITION: permission, indulgence, concession.
ORIGIN: From a compound of sun and ginosko; fellow knowledge, i.e. Concession.

BDAG.en: permission to do something, concession, indulgence, pardon
BDAG.pt: permissão para fazer algo, concessão, indulgência, perdão

DEFINITION: to sit together or with.
ORIGIN: From sun and kathemai; to seat oneself in company with.

BDAG.en: sit with someone
BDAG.pt: sentar-se com alguém

DEFINITION: to cause to sit down with, sit down together.
ORIGIN: From sun and kathizo; to give (or take) a seat in company with.

BDAG.en: cause to sit down with someone; sit down with someone
BDAG.pt: fazer sentar-se com alguém; sentar-se com alguém

DEFINITION: to bear evil treatment along with.
ORIGIN: From sun and kakopatheo; to suffer hardship in company with.

BDAG.en: suffer together with someone
BDAG.pt: sofrer junto com alguém

DEFINITION: to endure adversity with (pass.).
ORIGIN: From sun and kakoucheo; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together.

DEFINITION: to call together.
ORIGIN: From sun and kaleo; to convoke.

BDAG.en: to summon persons to come together, summon, call to one’s side, summon
BDAG.pt: convocar pessoas para se reunirem, chamar, convocar para o seu lado, convocar

DEFINITION: to conceal closely, cover up wholly.
ORIGIN: From sun and kalupto; to conceal altogether.

BDAG.en: to keep something from being known by concealing it, conceal
BDAG.pt: manter algo desconhecido ao ocultá-lo, esconder

DEFINITION: to oppress, bend together.
ORIGIN: From sun and kampto; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict.

BDAG.en: (cause to) bend (the back)
BDAG.pt: (fazer) curvar (as costas)

DEFINITION: to go down with.
ORIGIN: From sun and katabaino; to descend in company with.

BDAG.en: to accompany someone in going down to, go down with someone (from a high place to a lower one)
BDAG.pt: acompanhar alguém ao descer para, descer com alguém (de um lugar alto para um lugar baixo)

DEFINITION: assent, agreement, concord, alliance.
ORIGIN: From sugkatatithemai; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with.

BDAG.en: agreement, union (of an agreement)
BDAG.pt: acordo, união (de um acordo)

DEFINITION: to deposit together, to agree with.
ORIGIN: Mid from sun and katatithemi; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with.

BDAG.en: agree with, consent to something, find oneself in agreement with something
BDAG.pt: concordar com, consentir com algo, encontrar-se em acordo com algo

DEFINITION: to condemn with, to vote (one) a place among.
ORIGIN: From sun and a compound of kata and psephizo; to count down in company with, i.e. Enroll among.

DEFINITION: to mix together, to agree with.
ORIGIN: From sun and kerannumi; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate.

BDAG.en: to bring about a blend by mixing various items, blend, unite; to effect a harmonious unit, compose
BDAG.pt: produzir uma mistura ao combinar vários itens, misturar, unir; produzir uma unidade harmoniosa, compor

DEFINITION: to move together, stir up, excite.
ORIGIN: From sparasso and kineo; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition).

BDAG.en: to stir up, move everything; arouse/excite someone
BDAG.pt: agitar, mover tudo; despertar/excitar alguém

DEFINITION: to enclose, shut in, make subject to.
ORIGIN: From sun and kleio; to shut together, i.e. Include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to.

BDAG.en: to catch by enclosing, close up together, hem in, enclose fish in a net; to confine to specific limits, confine, imprison
BDAG.pt: apanhar fechando, fechar junto, cercar, confinar peixes em uma rede; confinar a limites específicos, confinar, aprisionar

DEFINITION: a joint heir, participant.
ORIGIN: From sun and kleronomos; a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common.

BDAG.en: inheriting together with, mostly subst. co-heir
BDAG.pt: herdando juntamente com, na maioria das vezes como substantivo co-herdeiro

DEFINITION: to be a partaker with, have fellowship with, be an accomplice in.
ORIGIN: From sun and koinoneo; to share in company with, i.e. Co-participate in.
USAGE: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.

BDAG.en: to be associated with someone in some activity, be connected with something; to give a portion of what one has to another, share something with someone
BDAG.pt: ser associado a alguém em alguma atividade, estar conectado com algo; dar uma porção do que se tem a outro, compartilhar algo com alguém

DEFINITION: a partaker with, co-partner.
ORIGIN: From sun and koinonos; a co-participant.

BDAG.en: participant, partner
BDAG.pt: participante, parceiro

DEFINITION: to bear away together with, as in carrying away a corpse.
ORIGIN: From sun and komizo; to convey together, i.e. Collect or bear away in company with others.

BDAG.en: to gather in as harvest, bring in; to carry out burial arrangements, bury (a euphemistic fig. ext. of 1)
BDAG.pt: colher como colheita, trazer para dentro; realizar arranjos funerários, sepultar (uma extensão figurada eufemística de 1)

DEFINITION: to join together, combine, compare, interpret, explain.
ORIGIN: From sun and krino; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. Combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance).

BDAG.en: to bring things together so as to form a unit, combine; to draw a conclusion by comparing, compare; to clarify on the basis of a compatible relationship, explain, interpret
BDAG.pt: trazer coisas juntas para formar uma unidade, combinar; tirar uma conclusão comparando, comparar; clarificar com base em uma relação compatível, explicar, interpretar

DEFINITION: to be bowed together, bent double.
ORIGIN: From sun and kupto; to stoop altogether, i.e. Be completely overcome by.

BDAG.en: prim. ‘bend forwards, stoop’, then of a fixed bent-over position, act. intr. be bent over
BDAG.pt: principalmente 'curvar-se para a frente, inclinar-se', depois numa posição dobrada fixa, ativamente intr. estar curvado

DEFINITION: a coincidence, accident, chance.
ORIGIN: From a comparative of sun and kureo (to light or happen; from the base of kurios); concurrence, i.e. Accident.

BDAG.en: an unexpected conjunction of events, coincidence, chance
BDAG.pt: uma conjunção inesperada de eventos, coincidência, acaso

DEFINITION: to rejoice with, congratulate.
ORIGIN: From sun and chairo; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate.

BDAG.en: to experience joy in conjunction w. someone, rejoice with someone; to express pleasure over another’s good fortune, congratulate someone
BDAG.pt: experimentar alegria em conjunto com alguém, regozijar-se com alguém; expressar prazer pela boa sorte de outro, parabenizar alguém

DEFINITION: to pour together, to confuse, throw into confusion.
ORIGIN: Or sugchuno (soong-khoo'-no) from sun and cheo (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind).
USAGE: confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.

BDAG.en: lit. ‘pour together’, then by fig. ext. to cause dismay, confuse, confound, trouble, stir up; be in confusion; Confound, throw into consternation; Pass., intr. sense be amazed, surprised, excited, agitated
BDAG.pt: lit. 'derramar junto', depois por extensão figurada causar consternação, confundir, transtornar, agitar; estar em confusão; Confundir, lançar em consternação; Voz passiva, sentido intrínseco estar espantado, surpreendido, excitado, agitado

DEFINITION: to use together with, to associate with.
ORIGIN: From sun and chraomai; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common.

BDAG.en: to avail oneself of someth., make use of (pejorative application: take advantage of); to associate on friendly terms with, have dealings with someone
BDAG.pt: valer-se de algo, fazer uso de (aplicação pejorativa: tirar proveito de); associar-se em termos amigáveis com, ter relações com alguém

DEFINITION: confusion, disturbance.
ORIGIN: From sugcheo; commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance.

BDAG.en: confusion, tumult
BDAG.pt: confusão, tumulto

DEFINITION: to live together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and zao; to continue to live in common with, i.e. Co-survive (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to live with someone (of living with a sinner, or the believer’s life with the exalted Lord, or living with one’s wife, or polytheists); to live together and die together
BDAG.pt: viver com alguém (de viver com um pecador, ou a vida do crente com o Senhor exaltado, ou viver com a esposa ou politeístas); viver junto e morrer junto

DEFINITION: to yoke together, unite (as man and wife).
ORIGIN: From sun and the base of zeugos; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage).

BDAG.en: lit. ‘yoke together’, then gener. to make a pair, join together, pair, specif. of matrimony
BDAG.pt: lit. 'juntar sob o jugo', depois geralmente fazer um par, juntar, unir, especificamente do matrimônio

DEFINITION: to seek together, discuss, dispute.
ORIGIN: From sun and zeteo; to investigate jointly, i.e. Discuss, controvert, cavil.

BDAG.en: to carry on a discussion, discuss; to contend with persistence for a point of view, dispute, debate, argue; to ponder various aspects of a matter, reflect, meditate (in solitude)
BDAG.pt: manter uma discussão, discutir; contender com persistência por um ponto de vista, disputar, debater, argumentar; ponderar vários aspetos de um assunto, refletir, meditar (em solidão)

DEFINITION: mutual questioning, disputation.
ORIGIN: From suzeteo; mutual questioning, i.e. Discussion.

BDAG.en: a discussion in the course of which disputants persistently advocate/sponsor a particular point of view, dispute, discussion
BDAG.pt: uma discussão no decorrer da qual os disputantes defendem/patrocinam persistentemente um ponto de vista específico, disputa, discussão

DEFINITION: a disputer, as the Greek sophists.
ORIGIN: From suzeteo; a disputant, i.e. Sophist.

BDAG.en: disputant, debater
BDAG.pt: disputador, debatedor

DEFINITION: a yoke-fellow, colleague.
ORIGIN: From suzeugnumi; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: true comrade, lit. ‘yoke-fellow’
BDAG.pt: verdadeiro camarada, literalmente ‘companheiro de jugo’

DEFINITION: to make alive together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and zoopoieo; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to make alive together with someone (through union with Christ)
BDAG.pt: vivificar juntamente com alguém (através da união com Cristo)

DEFINITION: a sycamore tree, black mulberry tree.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (shaqam) in imitation of sukomoraia; a sycamore-fig tree.

BDAG.en: the mulberry tree, which is evidently differentiated fr. the sycamore
BDAG.pt: a amoreira, que é evidentemente diferenciada do sicômoro

DEFINITION: a fig tree.
ORIGIN: From sukon; a fig-tree.

BDAG.en: fig tree, ficus carica, much cultivated because of its sweet fruit, also growing wild
BDAG.pt: figueira, ficus carica, muito cultivada por causa de seu fruto doce, também crescendo selvagem

DEFINITION: the fig-mulberry tree, sycamore fig.
ORIGIN: From sukon and moron (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree.

DEFINITION: a (ripe) fig.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a fig.

BDAG.en: fruit of the fig tree, fig, esp. ripe fig
BDAG.pt: fruto da figueira, figo, especialmente figo maduro

DEFINITION: to accuse falsely, defraud.
ORIGIN: From a compound of sukon and a derivative of phaino; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort).
USAGE: accuse falsely, take by false accusation.

BDAG.en: accuse falsely, slander; put pressure on someone for personal gain, harass, squeeze, shake down, blackmail; secure something through intimidation, extort
BDAG.pt: acusar falsamente, difamar; pressionar alguém para ganho pessoal, assediar, extorquir; obter algo através de intimidação, coagir

DEFINITION: to plunder, lead captive; met: to make victim by fraud.
ORIGIN: From the base of sulao and (the reduplicated form of) ago; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce.

BDAG.en: to gain control of by carrying off as booty, make captive of, rob (in imagery of carrying someone away from the truth into the slavery of error)
BDAG.pt: tomar o controle levando como despojo, tornar cativo, roubar (em imagens de arrastar alguém para longe da verdade para a escravidão do erro)

DEFINITION: to rob, plunder, strip.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of sullo (to strip; probably akin to haireomai; compare skulon); to despoil.

BDAG.en: to rob, sack (as a dramatic fig. expr. for Paul’s procedure in accepting financial support)
BDAG.pt: roubar, saquear (como uma expressão figurada dramática para o procedimento de Paulo em aceitar apoio financeiro)

DEFINITION: to talk with, discuss.
ORIGIN: From sun and laleo; to talk together, i.e. Converse.

BDAG.en: to exchange thoughts with, talk/discuss/converse with someone
BDAG.pt: trocar pensamentos com, falar/discutir/conversar com alguém

DEFINITION: to collect, to take, by implication to take part with, to conceive.
ORIGIN: From sun and lambano; to clasp, i.e. Seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid.

BDAG.en: to take into custody a seize, grasp, apprehend, arrest; to capture (an animal), catch; to become pregnant, conceive, of a woman; to help by taking part with someone in an activity, support, aid, help
BDAG.pt: tomar sob custódia, apreender, agarrar, prender, deter; capturar (um animal), pegar; ficar grávida, conceber, de uma mulher; ajudar tomando parte com alguém numa atividade, apoiar, auxiliar, ajudar

DEFINITION: to collect, gather.
ORIGIN: From sun and lego in its original sense; to collect.

BDAG.en: to gather by plucking or picking, collect, gather (in), pick
BDAG.pt: recolher por arrancar ou apanhar, colecionar, ajuntar, colher

DEFINITION: to reason, reckon with myself, consider.
ORIGIN: From sun and logizomai; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. Deliberate.

BDAG.en: to ponder or discuss various possibilities relating to a matter, reason, discuss, debate
BDAG.pt: ponderar ou discutir várias possibilidades relativas a um assunto, raciocinar, discutir, debater

DEFINITION: to be moved to grief with (pass.).
ORIGIN: From sun and lupeo; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone.

DEFINITION: to come together, (of events) to come to pass.
ORIGIN: From sun and the base of basis; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. Concur (take place).

BDAG.en: to join someone in going somewhere, go along with; to occur as event or process, happen, come about
BDAG.pt: juntar-se a alguém em ir a algum lugar, ir junto; ocorrer como evento ou processo, acontecer, vir a ser

DEFINITION: properly: to throw together, hence: to ponder, come up with, encounter, with or without hostile intent; to dispute with; mid: to confer, consult with, contribute.
ORIGIN: From sun and ballo; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack.
USAGE: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.

BDAG.en: to engage in mutual pondering of a matter, converse, confer; to give careful thought to, consider, ponder; to draw a conclusion by comparing, compare; to come together at a point, meet, fall in with; to come into conflict w. someone a engage, fight someone; b quarrel, dispute; to be of assistance, help, be of assistance
BDAG.pt: engajar-se em ponderação mútua de um assunto, conversar, conferir; dar pensamento cuidadoso, considerar, ponderar; tirar uma conclusão comparando, comparar; encontrar-se em um ponto, reunir-se, encontrar; entrar em conflito com alguém ou engajar, lutar contra alguém; brigar, disputar; ser de assistência, ajudar, ser de assistência

DEFINITION: to reign together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and basileuo; to be co-regent (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to reign jointly, rule (as king) with someone
BDAG.pt: reinar conjuntamente, governar (como rei) com alguém

DEFINITION: (a) to unite or knit together, (b) to put together in reasoning, and so: to conclude, prove, (c) to teach, instruct.
ORIGIN: From sun and bibazo (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of basis); to drive together, i.e. Unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach.
USAGE: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.

BDAG.en: to bring together into a unit, unite (literally, of the body, which is held together by sinews, ligaments, joints; figuratively, unite, knit together); to draw a conclusion in the face of evidence, conclude, infer; to present a logical conclusion, demonstrate, prove; to advise by giving instructions, instruct, teach, advise
BDAG.pt: juntar em uma unidade, unir (literalmente, do corpo, que é mantido unido por tendões, ligamentos, juntas; figurativamente, unir, atar); tirar uma conclusão diante de evidências, concluir, inferir; apresentar uma conclusão lógica, demonstrar, provar; aconselhar dando instruções, instruir, ensinar, aconselhar

DEFINITION: to give advice, exhort; mid: to take counsel together, consult.
ORIGIN: From sun and bouleuo; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. Recommend, deliberate or determine.

BDAG.en: give advice on a course of action, advise, act; be involved with others in plotting a course of action, consult, plot; give careful thought to someth., meditate on, consider
BDAG.pt: dar conselho sobre um curso de ação, aconselhar, agir; estar envolvido com outros no planejamento de um curso de ação, consultar, tramar; refletir cuidadosamente sobre algo, meditar, considerar

DEFINITION: (a) a body of advisers (assessors) in a court, a council, (b) abstr: consultation, counsel, advice; resolution, decree.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of sumboulos; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. The provincial assessors or lay-court.

BDAG.en: the act of consulting or conferring, consultation, meeting; meeting of an official deliberative assembly, council session, meeting; the result reached by a deliberating group, plan, purpose; an official deliberative assembly as a body, council
BDAG.pt: o ato de consultar ou conferir, consulta, reunião; reunião de uma assembleia deliberativa oficial, sessão do conselho, reunião; o resultado alcançado por um grupo deliberativo, plano, propósito; uma assembleia deliberativa oficial como corpo, conselho

DEFINITION: an adviser, counselor.
ORIGIN: From sun and boule; a consultor, i.e. Adviser.

BDAG.en: adviser, counsellor
BDAG.pt: conselheiro, consultor

DEFINITION: Symeon, Simeon, the name of several Israelites, also a tribe of Isr.
ORIGIN: From the same as Simon; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites.

BDAG.en: Symeon, Simeon (a Semitic name)
BDAG.pt: Simeão (nome semítico)

DEFINITION: a fellow disciple.
ORIGIN: From a compound of sun and manthano; a co-learner (of Christianity).

BDAG.en: fellow-pupil, fellow-disciple
BDAG.pt: colega de estudo, companheiro de discípulo

DEFINITION: to testify or bear witness with.
ORIGIN: From sun and martureo; to testify jointly, i.e. Corroborate by (concurrent) evidence.

BDAG.en: to testify or bear witness with; gener. to provide supporting evidence by testifying, confirm, support by testimony
BDAG.pt: testemunhar ou dar testemunho com; geralmente fornecer evidência de apoio por meio de testemunho, confirmar, apoiar por testemunho

DEFINITION: to partake with, divide together with, have a share in.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from sun and merizo; to share jointly, i.e. Participate in.

DEFINITION: partaking with, subst. a joint partaker.
ORIGIN: From sun and metochos; a co-participant.

BDAG.en: having a share with another in some possession or relationship, sharing with someone in someth.
BDAG.pt: tendo uma parte com outro em alguma posse ou relacionamento, compartilhando com alguém em algo

DEFINITION: a fellow imitator.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of sun and mimeomai; a co-imitator, i.e. Fellow votary.

BDAG.en: one who joins others as an imitator, fellow-imitator
BDAG.pt: aquele que se junta a outros como imitador, colega imitador

DEFINITION: similar, conformed to.
ORIGIN: From sun and morphe; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar.

BDAG.en: pert. to having a similar form, nature, or style, similar in form as or to someth.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter uma forma, natureza ou estilo semelhante, semelhante em forma como ou a algo

DEFINITION: to bring to the same form with, conform.
ORIGIN: From summorphos; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate.

BDAG.en: to give the same form, pass. take on the same form
BDAG.pt: dar a mesma forma, passivo assumir a mesma forma

DEFINITION: to have a fellow feeling with, sympathize with.
ORIGIN: From sumpathes; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate.
USAGE: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.

BDAG.en: to have/show sympathy with, sympathize with (with dative of person or thing)
BDAG.pt: ter/mostrar simpatia com, simpatizar com (com dativo de pessoa ou coisa)

DEFINITION: sympathizing, compassionate.
ORIGIN: From sumpascho; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative.

BDAG.en: sympathetic, understanding
BDAG.pt: simpático, compreensivo

DEFINITION: to come together with, stand by one, help.
ORIGIN: From sun and paraginomai; to be present together, i.e. To convene; by implication, to appear in aid.

BDAG.en: come together (for a spectacle); come to the aid of someone
BDAG.pt: vir junto (para um espetáculo); vir em auxílio de alguém

DEFINITION: to invite, encourage along with others; pass: to share in encouragement with.
ORIGIN: From sun and parakaleo; to console jointly.

BDAG.en: encourage together; pass. receive encouragement or comfort together with you
BDAG.pt: encorajar em conjunto; pass. receber encorajamento ou consolo junto com você

DEFINITION: to take along as a companion.
ORIGIN: From sun and paralambano; to take along in company.

BDAG.en: take along with oneself someone; take along as adjunct
BDAG.pt: levar consigo alguém; levar como adjunto

DEFINITION: to remain or continue together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and parameno; to remain in company, i.e. Still live.

BDAG.en: stay with someone to help
BDAG.pt: permanecer com alguém para ajudar

DEFINITION: to be present together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and pareimi; to be at hand together, i.e. Now present.

BDAG.en: to be in a place together with others, be together, be present with someone; be present (together) with someone
BDAG.pt: estar em um lugar junto com outros, estar junto, estar presente com alguém; estar presente (junto) com alguém

DEFINITION: to suffer together with, sympathize.
ORIGIN: From sun and pascho (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize").

BDAG.en: to have the same thing happen to one, suffer with, also suffer the same thing as; to have understanding or sensitivity for others esp. in their troubles, have sympathy for
BDAG.pt: ter a mesma coisa acontecer a um, sofrer com, também sofrer o mesmo que; ter compreensão ou sensibilidade pelos outros, especialmente em seus problemas, ter simpatia por

DEFINITION: to send together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and pempo; to despatch in company.

BDAG.en: to send someone together with someone else, send with or at the same time
BDAG.pt: enviar alguém junto com outra pessoa, enviar com ou ao mesmo tempo

DEFINITION: to embrace completely.
ORIGIN: From sun and a compound of peri and lambano; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. Earnestly throw the arms about one.

BDAG.en: to throw one’s arms around, embrace
BDAG.pt: abraçar, envolver com os braços

DEFINITION: to drink together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and pino; to partake a beverage in company.

BDAG.en: drink with
BDAG.pt: beber com

DEFINITION: to fill completely; pass: to be completed.
ORIGIN: From sun and pleroo; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete).

BDAG.en: ‘fill up, fill completely’; become quite full (of a ship); to arrive as the timely moment for an event to take place, fulfill, approach, come (of time)
BDAG.pt: ‘encher, encher completamente’; ficar completamente cheio (de um navio); chegar como o momento oportuno para um evento ocorrer, cumprir, aproximar-se, vir (do tempo)

DEFINITION: to choke utterly, as weeds do plants; to crowd upon.
ORIGIN: From sun and pnigo; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd.

BDAG.en: to check the growth or well-being of someth. by pressure, choke (of plants); as a hyperbolic expr. for crowd around, press upon, someth. like almost crush
BDAG.pt: sufocar o crescimento ou bem-estar de algo por pressão, sufocar (de plantas); como expressão hiperbólica para cercar em multidão, pressionar, quase esmagar

DEFINITION: a fellow citizen.
ORIGIN: From sun and polites; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian).

BDAG.en: fellow-citizen/compatriot (fig. Christians become fellow-citizens of God’s people)
BDAG.pt: concidadão/compatriota (fig. cristãos tornam-se concidadãos do povo de Deus)

DEFINITION: to journey together with; to come together, assemble.
ORIGIN: From sun and poreuomai; to journey together; by implication, to assemble.

BDAG.en: to be in movement together with one or more persons, go (along) with; to gather with others in the same place, come together, flock
BDAG.pt: estar em movimento junto com uma ou mais pessoas, ir junto; reunir-se com outros no mesmo lugar, juntar-se, afluir

DEFINITION: a drinking party, company (guests at a party).
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of sumpino; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests.

BDAG.en: a party of people eating together, party, group
BDAG.pt: um grupo de pessoas comendo juntas, festa, grupo

DEFINITION: a fellow elder.
ORIGIN: From sun and presbuteros; a co-presbyter.

BDAG.en: one who is a ruling elder along with others, fellow-elder, fellow-minister
BDAG.pt: alguém que é um presbítero governante junto com outros, co-presbítero, co-ministro

DEFINITION: to bring together, collect; to be profitable to.
ORIGIN: From sun and phero (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage.
USAGE: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).

BDAG.en: to bring together into a heap, bring together; to be advantageous, help, confer a benefit, be profitable/useful
BDAG.pt: reunir em um monte, juntar; ser vantajoso, ajudar, conferir um benefício, ser proveitoso/útil

DEFINITION: to assent to, consent, confess, agree with.
ORIGIN: From sun and phemi; to say jointly, i.e. Assent to.

BDAG.en: concur, agree with
BDAG.pt: concordar, estar de acordo com

DEFINITION: one of the same tribe, a fellow country-man.
ORIGIN: From sun and a derivative of phule; a co-tribesman, i.e. Native of the same country.

BDAG.en: one who is a member of the same tribe or people group, compatriot; pl. one’s people
BDAG.pt: aquele que é membro da mesma tribo ou grupo de pessoas, compatriota; pl. seu povo

DEFINITION: grown together, united with.
ORIGIN: From sun and a derivative of phuo; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to.

BDAG.en: pert. to being associated in a related experience ('grown together') identified with someth.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar associado a uma experiência relacionada ('crescido junto') identificado com algo

DEFINITION: to grow together (pass.).
ORIGIN: From sun and phuo; passive, to grow jointly.

BDAG.en: grow up with someth. (passive with active force)
BDAG.pt: crescer junto com algo (voz passiva com sentido ativo)

DEFINITION: to call out with, to be in harmony, generally to agree.
ORIGIN: From sumphonos; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact).

BDAG.en: to be so alike or similar as to match, fit (in) with, match (with), agree with; to have common interests, be in agreement, in harmony; to have come to an agreement about someth., be of one mind, agree
BDAG.pt: ser tão semelhante ou similar a ponto de corresponder, encaixar-se, combinar (com), concordar com; ter interesses em comum, estar em acordo, em harmonia; ter chegado a um acordo sobre algo, ser de uma só mente, concordar

DEFINITION: harmony, agreement, concord.
ORIGIN: From sumphoneo; accordance.

BDAG.en: a state of shared interests, agreement
BDAG.pt: um estado de interesses compartilhados, acordo

DEFINITION: harmony of instruments, music.
ORIGIN: From sumphonos; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. A concert of instruments (harmonious note).

BDAG.en: music (the sound produced by several instruments); a group of performing musicians, band, orchestra; a wind instrument
BDAG.pt: música (o som produzido por vários instrumentos); um grupo de músicos executantes, banda, orquestra; um instrumento de sopro

DEFINITION: calling out together, agreeing.
ORIGIN: From sun and phone; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement).

BDAG.en: pert. to being in tune with, attuned to, harmonious; pert. to being in agreement, agreeing
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar em sintonia com, afinado com, harmonioso; pertencente a estar em acordo, concordando

DEFINITION: to compute, reckon up, count together.
ORIGIN: From sun and psephizo; to compute jointly.

BDAG.en: to calculate a total, count up, compute someth.
BDAG.pt: calcular um total, contar, computar algo

DEFINITION: of one accord.
ORIGIN: From sun and psuche; co-spirited, i.e. Similar in sentiment.

BDAG.en: lit. 'united in spirit', harmonious
BDAG.pt: lit. 'unido em espírito', harmonioso

DEFINITION: with, together with (expresses association with).
ORIGIN: A primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than meta or para), i.e. By association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc..
USAGE: beside, with. In composition it has similar applications, including completeness.

BDAG.en: with (marker of accompaniment and association, assistance, linkage/addition)
BDAG.pt: com (marcador de acompanhamento e associação, assistência, ligação/adição)

DEFINITION: to gather together, collect, assemble, receive with hospitality, entertain.
ORIGIN: From sun and ago; to lead together, i.e. Collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably).
USAGE: + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.

BDAG.en: to cause to come together, gather (things or persons); to effect renewed relations, bring together, reconcile; to bring together with, lead or bring (to); to extend a welcome to, invite/receive as a guest; to move to another position, advance, move
BDAG.pt: fazer vir junto, reunir (coisas ou pessoas); efetuar relações renovadas, reunir, reconciliar; trazer junto com, levar ou trazer (para); estender uma recepção a, convidar/receber como hóspede; mover-se para outra posição, avançar, mover-se

DEFINITION: an assembly, congregation, synagogue, either the place or the people gathered together in the place.
ORIGIN: From (the reduplicated form of) sunago; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church.

BDAG.en: a bringing together, assembling; a gathering place; a place of assembly, specifically the Jewish synagogue (place of worship, court, and punishment); the members of a synagogue (congregation); a synagogal meeting/gathering for worship; a group of persons who band together, band, gang (often hostile).
BDAG.pt: um juntar, assembleia; um lugar de reunião; um lugar de assembleia, especificamente a sinagoga judaica (lugar de adoração, tribunal e punição); os membros de uma sinagoga (congregação); uma reunião/ajuntamento sinagogal para adoração; um grupo de pessoas que se unem, bando, gangue (frequentemente hostil).

DEFINITION: to struggle in company with, aid.
ORIGIN: From sun and agonizomai; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant).

BDAG.en: to join with someone in a common effort, fight/contend along with someone, with focus on a supportive role help, assist
BDAG.pt: juntar-se a alguém em um esforço comum, lutar/contender junto com alguém, com foco em um papel de apoio, ajudar, auxiliar

DEFINITION: to compete together with others, cooperate vigorously with.
ORIGIN: From sun and athleo; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly.

BDAG.en: to contend/struggle along with someone (in spreading the gospel/for the faith).
BDAG.pt: contender/lutar junto com alguém (na propagação do evangelho/pela fé).

DEFINITION: to gather together, assemble.
ORIGIN: From sun and athroizo (to hoard); to convene.

BDAG.en: to cause to gather together as a group, gather, bring together; (Pass.) be gathered, meet, hold meetings for purposes of worship; to link with others in a common experience, unite with, be joined to
BDAG.pt: fazer com que se reúna como um grupo, reunir, juntar; (Passivo) ser reunido, encontrar-se, realizar reuniões para adoração; ligar-se a outros em uma experiência comum, unir-se a, ser juntado a

DEFINITION: to compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning.
ORIGIN: From sun and airo; to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account).

BDAG.en: lit. ‘raise up’ or ‘bind/yoke together’; in our lit. only in a commercial sense settle accounts, cast up accounts
BDAG.pt: literalmente 'levantar' ou 'atar/juntar'; em nossa literatura apenas em sentido comercial acertar contas, computar contas

DEFINITION: a fellow captive or prisoner.
ORIGIN: From sun and aichmalotos; a co-captive.

BDAG.en: fellow-prisoner
BDAG.pt: companheiro de prisão

DEFINITION: to accompany, follow together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and akoloutheo; to accompany.

BDAG.en: to accompany someone, freq. in the interest of maintaining an association, follow
BDAG.pt: acompanhar alguém, frequentemente no interesse de manter uma associação, seguir

DEFINITION: to be assembled together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and halizo (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. Convene.

DEFINITION: to go up with.
ORIGIN: From sun and anabaino; to ascend in company with.

BDAG.en: come/go up with someone
BDAG.pt: subir/ir com alguém

DEFINITION: to recline with (at table).
ORIGIN: From sun and anakeimai; to recline in company with (at a meal).
USAGE: sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).

BDAG.en: to recline at table with for the purpose of dining, eat with; the fellow guests/banqueters
BDAG.pt: reclinar-se à mesa com o propósito de jantar, comer com; os companheiros de mesa/banqueteadores

DEFINITION: to mingle together with, keep company with.
ORIGIN: From sun and a compound of ana and mignumi; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with.

BDAG.en: mingle, associate with
BDAG.pt: misturar-se, associar-se com

DEFINITION: to lie down to rest with, to be refreshed in spirit with.
ORIGIN: Middle from sun and anapano; to recruit oneself in company with.

BDAG.en: to relax in someone’s company, rest with someone
BDAG.pt: relaxar na companhia de alguém, descansar com alguém

DEFINITION: to meet, encounter, fall in with.
ORIGIN: From sun and a derivative of anti; to meet with; figuratively, to occur.

BDAG.en: meet; happen, of events
BDAG.pt: encontrar; acontecer, no caso de eventos

DEFINITION: a meeting with.
ORIGIN: From sunantao; a meeting with.

BDAG.en: a coming together at some point, meeting
BDAG.pt: um encontro em algum momento, reunião

DEFINITION: to lend a hand along with, take interest in (a thing) along with (others), assist jointly to perform some task, cooperate with, take share in, help, aid.
ORIGIN: From sun and antilambanomai; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. Co-operate (assist).

BDAG.en: take part with, come to the aid of, be of assistance to, help
BDAG.pt: tomar parte com, vir em auxílio de, ser de assistência a, ajudar

DEFINITION: to lead away with, carry along with (in good or bad sense according to context); mid: to conform myself willingly to.
ORIGIN: From sun and apago; to take off together, i.e. Transport with (seduce, passively, yield).

BDAG.en: to cause someone in conjunction with others to go astray in belief, lead away with; be led or carried away; adjust to a condition or circumstance, accommodate; join the company of others, associate with
BDAG.pt: fazer com que alguém se desvie da crença em conjunto com outros, levar junto; ser levado ou arrastado; ajustar-se a uma condição ou circunstância, acomodar-se; juntar-se ao grupo de outros, associar-se com

DEFINITION: to die together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and apothnesko; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to.

BDAG.en: die with
BDAG.pt: morrer com

DEFINITION: to destroy with, mid. to perish together.
ORIGIN: From sun and apollumi; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with.

BDAG.en: destroy with; be destroyed, perish with
BDAG.pt: destruir junto; ser destruído, perecer junto

DEFINITION: to send together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and apostello; to despatch (on an errand) in company with.

BDAG.en: to send someone together with someone else, send with
BDAG.pt: enviar alguém juntamente com outra pessoa, enviar com

DEFINITION: to fit together, compact.
ORIGIN: From sun and a derivative of a compound of harmos and lego (in its original sense of laying); to render close-jointed together, i.e. Organize compactly.

BDAG.en: join together so as to form a coherent entity, fit/join together
BDAG.pt: juntar para formar uma entidade coerente, encaixar/unir

DEFINITION: to seize and carry away.
ORIGIN: From sun and harpazo; to snatch together, i.e. Seize.

BDAG.en: take hold of forcibly, seize; (of a possessed person) be seized by an unclean spirit; (of a ship) be caught, torn away by the wind
BDAG.pt: agarrar à força, capturar; (de uma pessoa possuída) ser tomada por um espírito imundo; (de um navio) ser apanhado, ser arrancado pelo vento

DEFINITION: to cause to grow together, pass. to grow together.
ORIGIN: From sun and auzano; to increase (grow up) together.

DEFINITION: that which binds together; a band, bond.
ORIGIN: From sun and desmon; a joint tie, i.e. Ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control.

BDAG.en: that which binds together; that which holds someth. together, fastener; that which brings various entities into a unified relationship, uniting bond; a bond that confines/hinders, fetter; entities that are held together by a bond, bundle; band, college
BDAG.pt: aquilo que une; aquilo que mantém algo unido, fecho; aquilo que traz várias entidades para uma relação unificada, laço unificador; um laço que confina/atrapalha, grilhão; entidades mantidas juntas por um laço, feixe; banda, colégio

DEFINITION: to bind together; pass: to be bound together with, as of prisoners in chains.
ORIGIN: From sun and deo; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively).

BDAG.en: to bind so as to constrain or confine (with), bind (with); can also mean simply bind, imprison
BDAG.pt: atar de modo a restringir ou confinar (junto com), ligar (junto com); também pode significar simplesmente atar, aprisionar

DEFINITION: to join in approving, to glorify together.
ORIGIN: From sun and doxazo; to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. Similarly) with.

BDAG.en: to join with others in praising, join in praise; to honor together with, pass. be glorified with someone, share in someone’s glory
BDAG.pt: juntar-se a outros em louvar, juntar-se ao louvor; honrar juntamente com, passivo ser glorificado com alguém, compartilhar da glória de alguém

DEFINITION: a fellow slave, fellow servant; of Christians: a fellow worker, colleague.
ORIGIN: From sun and doulos; a co-slave, i.e. Servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine).

BDAG.en: one who, along with others, is in a relationship of total obedience to one master or owner, fellow-slave; a subordinate in total obedience to a ruler, slave; fellow-Christian
BDAG.pt: aquele que, juntamente com outros, está em um relacionamento de obediência total a um mestre ou dono, colega de escravidão; um subordinado em total obediência a um governante, escravo; colega cristão

DEFINITION: a running together, a concourse (esp. of a riotous gathering).
ORIGIN: From (the alternate of) suntrecho; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse.

BDAG.en: formation of a mob by persons running together, running together
BDAG.pt: formação de uma multidão por pessoas correndo juntas, ajuntamento apressado

DEFINITION: to raise along with.
ORIGIN: From sun and egeiro; to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to.

BDAG.en: to cause to emerge with from an inactive state, awaken with; to raise up with from death, physical or spiritual, raise with; of participating in the resurrection of Jesus
BDAG.pt: fazer emergir com de um estado inativo, despertar junto com; ressuscitar juntamente com da morte, física ou espiritualmente, elevar junto com; de participar da ressurreição de Jesus

DEFINITION: a council, tribunal; the Sanhedrin, the meeting place of the Sanhedrin.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of sun and the base of hedraios; a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal.

BDAG.en: a governing board, council; an official session of a council, council meeting; council meeting room, meeting room (Sanhedrin)
BDAG.pt: um corpo governante, conselho; uma sessão oficial de um conselho, reunião do conselho; sala de reunião do conselho, local de reunião (Sanedrim)

DEFINITION: the conscience, a persisting notion.
ORIGIN: From a prolonged form of suneido; co-perception, i.e. Moral consciousness.

BDAG.en: awareness of information about something, consciousness; the inward faculty of distinguishing right and wrong, moral consciousness, conscience; attentiveness to obligation, conscientiousness
BDAG.pt: consciência de informação sobre algo, consciência; a faculdade interna de distinguir o certo e o errado, consciência moral, consciência; atenção à obrigação, ser consciencioso

DEFINITION: to see together, to comprehend.
ORIGIN: From sun and eido; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of.
USAGE: consider, know, be privy, be ware of.

BDAG.en: 1. to share information or knowledge with, be privy to (in the sense ‘be implicated, be an accomplice’); 2. to be aware of information about something, to know, be conscious (I know with myself; i.e. I am conscious); consciousness in which one imparts information to oneself, conscience
