BDAG.pt: 1. compartilhar informação ou conhecimento com, estar a par de (no sentido de ‘estar implicado, ser cúmplice’); 2. estar ciente de informações sobre algo, saber, ter consciência (eu sei comigo mesmo; ou seja, estou consciente); consciência na qual se transmite informação a si mesmo, consciência

DEFINITION: to be with, come together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and eimi (including its various inflections); to be in company with, i.e. Present at the time.

BDAG.en: I (from εἰμί) be with; II (from εἶμι) come together
BDAG.pt: I (de εἰμί) estar com; II (de εἶμι) reunir-se

DEFINITION: to come together.
ORIGIN: From sun and eimi (to go); to assemble.

DEFINITION: to enter together with, embark with.
ORIGIN: From sun and eiserchomai; to enter in company with.
USAGE: go in with, go with into.

BDAG.en: to enter with, go into with someone
BDAG.pt: entrar com, ir para dentro com alguém

DEFINITION: a fellow traveler.
ORIGIN: From sun and the base of ekdemeo; a co-absentee from home, i.e. Fellow-traveller.

BDAG.en: traveling companion, with focus on official assignment
BDAG.pt: companheiro de viagem, com foco em designação oficial

DEFINITION: fellow-elect, fellow-chosen.
ORIGIN: From a compound of sun and eklegomai; chosen in company with, i.e. Co-elect (fellow Christian).

BDAG.en: pert. to being chosen together with, also chosen
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser escolhido juntamente com, também escolhido

DEFINITION: to compel, urge, force together.
ORIGIN: From sun and elauno; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation).

BDAG.en: to cause movement through constraint, drive, force, bring to something, in imagery
BDAG.pt: causar movimento por constrangimento, dirigir, forçar, trazer a algo, em sentido figurado

DEFINITION: to testify or bear witness together with.
ORIGIN: From sun and epimartureo; to testify further jointly, i.e. Unite in adding evidence.

BDAG.en: testify at the same time.
BDAG.pt: testemunhar ao mesmo tempo.

DEFINITION: to accompany, follow with.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from sun and a primary hepo (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with.

BDAG.en: accompany someone.
BDAG.pt: acompanhar alguém.

DEFINITION: to cooperate with, work together.
ORIGIN: From sunergos; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. Co-operate.

BDAG.en: to engage in cooperative endeavor, work together with, assist, help.
BDAG.pt: engajar-se em esforço cooperativo, trabalhar junto com, auxiliar, ajudar.

DEFINITION: a fellow worker, associate, helper.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of sun and the base of ergon; a co-laborer, i.e. Coadjutor.
USAGE: companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.

BDAG.en: helper, fellow-worker.
BDAG.pt: auxiliar, companheiro de trabalho.

DEFINITION: to come or go with, accompany; to come together, assemble.
ORIGIN: From sun and erchomai; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally).
USAGE: accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.

BDAG.en: to come together as a group, assemble, gather; to come/go with one or more persons, travel together with someone; to unite in an intimate relationship, come together in a sexual context.
BDAG.pt: vir junto como um grupo, reunir-se, ajuntar-se; ir/vir com uma ou mais pessoas, viajar junto com alguém; unir-se em um relacionamento íntimo, juntar-se em um contexto sexual.

DEFINITION: to eat with.
ORIGIN: From sun and esthio (including its alternate); to take food in company with.

BDAG.en: eat with someone.
BDAG.pt: comer com alguém.

DEFINITION: a putting together in the mind, hence: understanding, practical discernment, intellect.
ORIGIN: From suniemi; a mental putting together, i.e. Intelligence or (concretely) the intellect.

BDAG.en: the faculty of comprehension, intelligence, acuteness, shrewdness; understanding such as God grants to God’s own; the wisdom of the creator; the content of understanding or comprehension, insight, understanding.
BDAG.pt: a faculdade de compreensão, inteligência, perspicácia, sagacidade; entendimento tal como Deus concede aos Seus; a sabedoria do criador; o conteúdo da compreensão ou percepção, percepção, entendimento.

DEFINITION: intelligent, prudent, wise, understanding, discerning.
ORIGIN: From suniemi; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. Sagacious.

BDAG.en: pert. to being able to understand with discernment, intelligent, sagacious, wise, with good sense.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à capacidade de entender com discernimento, inteligente, sagaz, sábio, com bom senso.

DEFINITION: to consent, agree, be of one mind with, be willing.
ORIGIN: From sun and eudokeo; to think well of in common, i.e. Assent to, feel gratified with.
USAGE: allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.

BDAG.en: to join in approval, agree with, approve of, consent to, sympathize with.
BDAG.pt: juntar-se em aprovação, concordar com, aprovar, consentir, simpatizar com.

DEFINITION: to entertain together, pass. feast together.
ORIGIN: From sun and a derivative of a presumed compound of eu and a derivative of echo (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together.

BDAG.en: feast together.
BDAG.pt: festejar junto.

DEFINITION: to place over, rise together.
ORIGIN: From sun and ephistemi; to stand up together, i.e. To resist (or assault) jointly.

DEFINITION: (a) to press together, close, (b) to press on every side, confine, (c) to hold fast, (d) to urge, impel, (e) pass: to be afflicted with (sickness).
ORIGIN: From sun and echo; to hold together, i.e. To compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy.
USAGE: constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.

BDAG.en: to hold together as a unit, hold together, sustain; to close by holding together, stop, shut; to press in and around so as to leave little room for movement, press hard, crowd; to hold in custody, guard; to cause distress by force of circumstances, seize, attack, distress, torment; to occupy someone’s attention intensely; to provide impulse for some activity, urge on, impel; to hold within bounds so as to manage or guide, direct, control
BDAG.pt: segurar junto como uma unidade, sustentar; fechar ao segurar junto, parar, fechar; pressionar ao redor deixando pouco espaço para movimento, apertar, cercar; manter em custódia, guardar; causar aflição por força das circunstâncias, apoderar-se, atacar, afligir, atormentar; ocupar intensamente a atenção de alguém; fornecer impulso para alguma atividade, impulsionar; conter para gerenciar ou guiar, dirigir, controlar

DEFINITION: to delight inwardly in, congratulate.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from sun and the base of hedone; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. Feel satisfaction concerning.

BDAG.en: to experience joy in connection with, delight in
BDAG.pt: experimentar alegria em conexão com, deleitar-se em

DEFINITION: a custom, habit, practice.
ORIGIN: From a compound of sun and ethos; mutual habituation, i.e. Usage.

BDAG.en: a relationship in which the participants are compatible because of shared interests, friendship, fellowship, intimacy; a usage or practice that has become established or standard, custom
BDAG.pt: um relacionamento em que os participantes são compatíveis por causa de interesses compartilhados, amizade, comunhão, intimidade; um uso ou prática que se tornou estabelecido ou padrão, costume

DEFINITION: one of the same age.
ORIGIN: From sun and a derivative of helikia; a co-aged person, i.e. Alike in years.

BDAG.en: a person of one’s own age, a contemporary
BDAG.pt: uma pessoa da mesma idade, um contemporâneo

DEFINITION: to bury along with.
ORIGIN: From sun and thapto; to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin).

BDAG.en: bury (together) with; fig. of the believers being buried together w. their Lord in baptism
BDAG.pt: enterrar (junto) com; fig. dos crentes sendo sepultados juntamente com seu Senhor no batismo

DEFINITION: to break, break in pieces, crush, shatter.
ORIGIN: From sun and thlao (to crush); to dash together, i.e. Shatter.

BDAG.en: to crush in such a way that an object is put in pieces, crush (together), dash to pieces
BDAG.pt: esmagar de tal forma que um objeto seja reduzido a pedaços, esmagar (junto), estilhaçar

DEFINITION: to press on all sides, crowd upon.
ORIGIN: From sun and thlibo; to compress, i.e. Crowd on all sides.

BDAG.en: to crowd around so as to leave little room for movement, press together, press upon someone (of a crowd)
BDAG.pt: apertoar ao redor de modo a deixar pouco espaço para movimento, aglomerar-se, pressionar alguém (de uma multidão)

DEFINITION: to break in pieces, crush, thoroughly weaken.
ORIGIN: From sun and thrupto (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit.

BDAG.en: break in pieces; (figuratively) break someone’s heart
BDAG.pt: quebrar em pedaços; (figurativamente) quebrar o coração de alguém

DEFINITION: to consider, understand, perceive.
ORIGIN: From sun and hiemi (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously.

BDAG.en: to have an intelligent grasp of something that challenges one’s thinking or practice, understand, comprehend
BDAG.pt: ter uma compreensão inteligente de algo que desafia o pensamento ou a prática, entender, compreender

DEFINITION: to place together, commend, prove, exhibit; instrans: to stand with; to be composed of, cohere.
ORIGIN: Or (strengthened) sunistano (soon-is-tan'-o), or sunistemi (soon-is'-tay-mee) from sun and histemi (including its collateral forms); to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute.

BDAG.en: The basic semantic component refers to coherence or being in a state of close relationship. A. transitive: 1. to bring together by gathering, unite, collect; 2. to bring together as friends or in a trusting relationship by commending/recommending, present, introduce/recommend someone to someone else; 3. to provide evidence of a personal characteristic or claim through action, demonstrate, show, bring out something; 4. to bring into existence in an organized manner, put together, constitute, establish, prepare. B. intransitive: 1. to stand in close association with, stand with/by; 2. to be composed or compounded of various parts, consist; 3. to come to be in a condition of coherence, continue, endure, exist, hold together.
BDAG.pt: O componente semântico básico refere-se à coerência ou a um estado de relacionamento próximo. A. Transitivo: 1. reunir ajuntando, unir, colecionar; 2. juntar como amigos ou em relacionamento de confiança por meio de recomendação, apresentar, introduzir/recomendar alguém a alguém; 3. fornecer evidência de uma característica pessoal ou alegação através da ação, demonstrar, mostrar, evidenciar algo; 4. trazer à existência de maneira organizada, juntar, constituir, estabelecer, preparar. B. Intransitivo: 1. estar em associação estreita com, ficar ao lado de; 2. ser composto ou formado por várias partes, consistir; 3. chegar a um estado de coerência, continuar, perdurar, existir, manter-se unido.

DEFINITION: to journey with, accompany.
ORIGIN: From sun and hodeuo; to travel in company with.

BDAG.en: a. to take the same path, travel together with (lit.); b. metaph. of the Lord he was my traveling companion on the upright way
BDAG.pt: a. tomar o mesmo caminho, viajar junto com (literalmente); b. metaforicamente, do Senhor ele foi meu companheiro de viagem no caminho reto

DEFINITION: a journey in company, a company (of travelers).
ORIGIN: From a compound of sun and hodos ("synod"); companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan.

BDAG.en: a group of travelers, caravan
BDAG.pt: um grupo de viajantes, caravana

DEFINITION: to dwell with, live in wedlock with.
ORIGIN: From sun and oikeo; to reside together (as a family).

BDAG.en: live with someone (of man and wife)
BDAG.pt: viver com alguém (de marido e mulher)

DEFINITION: to build together, to build up together.
ORIGIN: From sun and oikodomeo; to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively).

BDAG.en: 1. to build up or construct of various parts, build up, of the various parts of a structure, from which the latter is built up (together); 2. to build in with other materials, build in

BDAG.en: Bodily, corporeally (often implying reality as opposed to figuratively).
BDAG.pt: Corporalmente, fisicamente (frequentemente implicando realidade em oposição a figurativamente).

DEFINITION: "of a safe father", Sopater, a Christian from Berea.
ORIGIN: From the base of sozo and pater; of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Sopater son of Pyrrhus. S. was a Christian in Beroia and Paul’s companion on his last journey to Jerusalem
BDAG.pt: Sopatro, filho de Pirro. Era um cristão em Beréia e companheiro de Paulo em sua última viagem a Jerusalém

DEFINITION: to heap up, load.
ORIGIN: From another form of soros; to pile up (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: To amass by setting one thing atop another, heap/pile up; to heap a place with, load up with (often figuratively, as being overwhelmed by sins).
BDAG.pt: Amontoar colocando uma coisa sobre a outra, acumular/empilhar; encher um lugar com, sobrecarregar com (frequentemente em sentido figurado, como estar sobrecarregado de pecados).

DEFINITION: "of safe strength", Sosthenes, the name of a ruler of a synagogue and of a Christian.
ORIGIN: From the base of sozo and that of sthenoo; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Sosthenes. 1. leader of a synagogue in Corinth at the time of Paul’s first missionary work in that city; 2. a 'brother' mentioned in the salutation 1 Cor 1:1, beside Paul himself
BDAG.pt: Sostenes. 1. líder de uma sinagoga em Corinto na época do primeiro trabalho missionário de Paulo naquela cidade; 2. um 'irmão' mencionado na saudação de 1 Coríntios 1:1, ao lado do próprio Paulo

DEFINITION: "of a safe father", Sosipater, a Christian.
ORIGIN: Prolongation for Sopatros; Sosipatrus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Sosipater, a relative of Paul who sends greetings in Romans.
BDAG.pt: Sosípatro, um parente de Paulo que envia saudações em Romanos.

DEFINITION: a savior, deliverer, preserver.
ORIGIN: From sozo; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ.

BDAG.en: One who rescues, savior, deliverer, preserver; used as a title for divinities, deified rulers, or notably applied to Christ.
BDAG.pt: Aquele que resgata, salvador, libertador, preservador; usado como título para divindades, governantes deificados, ou notavelmente aplicado a Cristo.

DEFINITION: welfare, prosperity, deliverance, preservation, salvation, safety.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a derivative of soter as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally).

BDAG.en: deliverance, preservation (focus on physical aspect: from impending death, esp. on the sea); salvation (focus on transcendent aspects, in connection w. Jesus Christ as Savior).
BDAG.pt: livramento, preservação (com foco no aspecto físico: da morte iminente, especialmente no mar); salvação (com foco nos aspectos transcendentais, em conexão com Jesus Cristo como Salvador).

DEFINITION: saving, bringing salvation; subst: salvation.
ORIGIN: Neuter of the same as soteria as (properly, concretely) noun; defender or (by implication) defence.

BDAG.en: pert. to salvation, saving, delivering, preserving, bringing salvation; neut. τὸ σωτήριον means of deliverance, then also the deliverance itself, in our literature of Messianic salvation and the one who mediates it.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à salvação, salvador, livrador, preservador, que traz salvação; o neutro τὸ σωτήριον significa meio de livramento e, então, o próprio livramento, na nossa literatura referente à salvação Messiânica e àquele que a media.

DEFINITION: to be of sound mind, be sober-minded, exercise self-control.
ORIGIN: From sophron; to be of sound mind, i.e. Sane, (figuratively) moderate.
USAGE: be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.

BDAG.en: to be able to think in a sound or sane manner, be of sound mind; to be prudent, with focus on self-control, be reasonable, sensible, serious, keep one’s head; esp. of women: be chaste, virtuous.
BDAG.pt: ser capaz de pensar de modo são ou sensato, ter a mente sã; ser prudente, com foco no autocontrole, ser razoável, sensato, sério, manter a cabeça no lugar; especialmente para mulheres: ser casta, virtuosa.

DEFINITION: to make sober-minded, admonish, control.
ORIGIN: From sophron; to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct.

BDAG.en: 'bring to one’s senses', to instruct in prudence or behavior that is becoming and shows good judgment, encourage, advise, urge.
BDAG.pt: 'trazer ao juízo', instruir em prudência ou comportamento que seja apropriado e demonstre bom senso, encorajar, aconselhar, exortar.

DEFINITION: self-control, self-discipline, prudence.
ORIGIN: From sophronizo; discipline, i.e. Self-control.

BDAG.en: the teaching of prudence, advice, improvement; exercise of prudence, moderation, self-discipline, prudence (= σωφροσύνη).
BDAG.pt: o ensino da prudência, conselho, melhoria; exercício da prudência, moderação, autodisciplina, prudência (= σωφροσύνη).

DEFINITION: soberly, with moderation, prudently.
ORIGIN: Adverb from sophron; with sound mind, i.e. Moderately.

BDAG.en: pert. to being prudent, soberly, moderately, showing self-control
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ser prudente, com sobriedade, moderadamente, demonstrando autocontrole

DEFINITION: soundness of mind, sanity; self-control, sobriety.
ORIGIN: From sophron; soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control.

BDAG.en: soundness of mind, reasonableness, rationality; practice of prudence, good judgment, moderation, self-control as exercise of care and intelligence appropriate to circumstances; esp. as a woman’s virtue: decency, chastity.
BDAG.pt: sã consciência, razoabilidade, racionalidade; prática da prudência, bom senso, moderação, autocontrole como exercício de cuidado e inteligência apropriados às circunstâncias; especialmente como virtude feminina: decência, castidade.

DEFINITION: of sound mind, self-controlled, temperate, sober-minded, modest, chaste.
ORIGIN: From the base of sozo and that of phren; safe (sound) in mind, i.e. Self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion).

BDAG.en: pert. to being in control of oneself, prudent, thoughtful, self-controlled; esp. of women: chaste, decent, modest.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar no controle de si mesmo, prudente, ponderado, autocontrolado; especialmente para mulheres: casto, decente, modesto.

DEFINITION: taverns; Three Taverns, the name of a village or town on the Appian Way, about thirty-three miles from Rome.
ORIGIN: Plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernoe.

BDAG.en: hut, inn, or shop (used only in the place name Three Taverns)
BDAG.pt: cabana, estalagem ou loja (usado apenas no nome do lugar Três Tavernas)

DEFINITION: "gazelle", Tabitha (also called Dorcas), a Christian woman.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare tsbiyah); the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female.

DEFINITION: that which has been arranged in order, a division, rank.
ORIGIN: From tasso; something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession.

BDAG.en: a clearly defined group, division, military detachment; a stage in a sequence, order, turn
BDAG.pt: um grupo claramente definido, divisão, destacamento militar; um estágio em uma sequência, ordem, turno

DEFINITION: appointed, arranged, fixed.
ORIGIN: From tasso; arranged, i.e. Appointed or stated.

BDAG.en: fixed, appointed (e.g., appointed day)
BDAG.pt: fixo, designado (ex: dia marcado)

DEFINITION: to endure severe hardship, be harassed, complain.
ORIGIN: From talaiporos; to be wretched, i.e. Realize one's own misery.

BDAG.en: torment, afflict; experience distress, endure sorrow/distress, be miserable, feel miserable, lament
BDAG.pt: atormentar, afligir; experimentar aflição, suportar tristeza/angústia, ser miserável, sentir-se miserável, lamentar

DEFINITION: hardship, misery, distress, toil.
ORIGIN: From talaiporos; wretchedness, i.e. Calamity.

BDAG.en: wretchedness, distress, trouble, misery; miseries (plural)
BDAG.pt: miséria, aflição, problema, desgraça; calamidades (plural)

DEFINITION: wretched, afflicted, miserable.
ORIGIN: From the base of talanton and a derivative of the base of peira; enduring trial, i.e. Miserable.

BDAG.en: miserable, wretched, distressed; wretched creature (subst.)
BDAG.pt: miserável, desgraçado, aflito; criatura miserável (substantivo)

DEFINITION: worth a talent, of a talent's weight.
ORIGIN: From talanton; talent-like in weight.

BDAG.en: weighing a talent (describing hailstones)
BDAG.pt: pesando um talento (descrevendo pedras de granizo)

DEFINITION: a balance, that which is weighed, a talent (about 3000 shekels in weight).
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of tlao (to bear; equivalent to phero); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent".

BDAG.en: a measure of weight varying in size; a unit of coinage talent, comparatively high value
BDAG.pt: uma medida de peso que varia em tamanho; uma unidade de moeda talento, de valor comparativamente alto

DEFINITION: (Aramaic), girl, little girl.
ORIGIN: Of Chaldee origin (compare taleh); the fresh, i.e. Young girl; talitha (O maiden).

BDAG.en: girl, little girl
BDAG.pt: menina, garotinha

DEFINITION: a store-chamber, secret chamber, closet; a granary, barn.
ORIGIN: Neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of tamias (a dispenser or distributor; akin to temno, to cut); a dispensary or magazine, i.e. A chamber on the ground-floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for retirement).

BDAG.en: place for the keeping of valuables, storeroom; gener. a room in the interior of a house, inner room
BDAG.pt: lugar para guardar valores, depósito; em geral, um aposento no interior de uma casa, quarto interior

DEFINITION: order, (a) regular arrangement, (b) appointed succession, (c) position, rank.
ORIGIN: From tasso; regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity.

BDAG.en: an arrangement of things in sequence, fixed succession/order; a state of good order, order, proper procedure; an assigned station or rank, position, post; an arrangement in which someone or something functions, arrangement, nature, manner, condition, outward aspect
BDAG.pt: um arranjo de coisas em sequência, sucessão/ordem fixa; um estado de boa ordem, ordem, procedimento adequado; uma estação ou patente designada, posição, posto; um arranjo em que alguém ou algo funciona, arranjo, natureza, modo, condição, aspecto exterior

DEFINITION: humble, lowly, in position or spirit (in a good sense).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition).
USAGE: base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly.

BDAG.en: lowly, undistinguished, of no account; servile in manner, pliant, subservient, abject; unpretentious, humble
BDAG.pt: de baixo status social ou relativamente incapaz de lidar com as coisas, humilde, sem distinção, insignificante; servil em maneiras, maleável, subserviente, abjeto; sem pretensões, humilde

DEFINITION: humility, lowliness of mind, modesty.
ORIGIN: From a compound of tapeinos and the base of phren; humiliation of mind, i.e. Modesty.
USAGE: humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind).

BDAG.en: humility, modesty
BDAG.pt: humildade, modéstia

DEFINITION: to make or bring low, humble, humiliate; pass: to be humbled.
ORIGIN: From tapeinos; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart).

BDAG.en: to cause to be at a lower point, lower; to cause someone to lose prestige or status, humble, humiliate, abase; to cause to be or become humble in attitude, humble, make humble in a favorable sense; to subject to strict discipline, constrain, mortify
BDAG.pt: causar estar em um ponto mais baixo, rebaixar; fazer alguém perder prestígio ou status, humilhar, rebaixar; fazer ser ou tornar-se humilde em atitude, humilhar, tornar humilde em sentido favorável; submeter a disciplina rigorosa, restringir, mortificar

DEFINITION: abasement (in spirit), low condition (in circumstances).
ORIGIN: From tapeinoo; depression (in rank or feeling).
USAGE: humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile.

BDAG.en: experience of a reversal in fortunes, humiliation as an experience; an unpretentious state or condition, lowliness, humility, humble station; a self-abasing demeanor, self-abasement, mortification
BDAG.pt: experiência de uma reviravolta nas fortunas, humilhação como experiência; um estado ou condição sem pretensões, pequenez, humildade, condição humilde; uma postura de auto-rebaixamento, auto-humilhação, mortificação

DEFINITION: to disturb, agitate, stir up, trouble.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; to stir or agitate (roil water).

BDAG.en: cause movement by shaking or stirring, shake together, stir up (of water); cause inward turmoil, stir up, disturb, unsettle, throw into confusion (of mental/spiritual agitation)
BDAG.pt: causar movimento agitando ou mexendo, sacudir junto, agitar (da água); causar tumulto interior, agitar, perturbar, desestabilizar, lançar em confusão (de agitação mental/espiritual)

DEFINITION: a disturbance, tumult, sedition, trouble.
ORIGIN: Feminine from tarasso; disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition.

BDAG.en: movement of someth. caused by stirring, stirring up of water; inward disturbance, perplexity, disquietude; upset of normal civic relations, disturbance, tumult, rebellion
BDAG.pt: movimento de algo causado por agitação, revolvimento de água; perturbação interna, perplexidade, inquietação; perturbação das relações cívicas normais, distúrbio, tumulto, rebelião

DEFINITION: a disturbance, commotion, trouble.
ORIGIN: Masculine from tarasso; a disturbance, i.e. (popular) tumult.

BDAG.en: a state of mental agitation; a state of civic unrest, disturbance, commotion
BDAG.pt: um estado de agitação mental; um estado de desordem cívica, distúrbio, comoção

DEFINITION: belonging to Tarsus, a Tarsian.
ORIGIN: From Tarsos; a Tarsean, i.e. Native of Tarsus.

BDAG.en: a person from Tarsus, a Tarsian (of Paul)
BDAG.pt: uma pessoa de Tarso, um tarsense (referente a Paulo)

DEFINITION: Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia.
ORIGIN: Perhaps the same as tarsos (a flat basket); Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Tarsus, capital of Cilicia in southeast Asia Minor, famous as a seat of Gk. learning
BDAG.pt: Tarso, capital da Cilícia no sudeste da Ásia Menor, famosa como centro de erudição grega

DEFINITION: to thrust down to Tartarus or Gehenna.
ORIGIN: From Tartaros (the deepest abyss of Hades); to incarcerate in eternal torment.

BDAG.en: hold captive in Tartarus
BDAG.pt: manter cativo no Tártaro

DEFINITION: (a) to assign, arrange, (b) to determine; mid: to appoint.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses); to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. Assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot).

BDAG.en: bring about an order of things by arranging, arrange, put in place (authority structure, position); give instructions as to what must be done, order, fix, determine, appoint
BDAG.pt: fazer surgir uma ordem de coisas arranjando, arranjar, colocar no lugar (estrutura de autoridade, posição); dar instruções sobre o que deve ser feito, ordenar, fixar, determinar, nomear

DEFINITION: a bull, an ox.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word (compare towr, "steer"); a bullock.

BDAG.en: bull, ox as a sacrificial animal
BDAG.pt: touro, boi como animal de sacrifício

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Nominative or accusative case neuter plural of houtos; these things.
USAGE: + afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, this, those, thus.

BDAG.en: tautá= ta auta, only as variant reading
BDAG.pt: tautá = ta auta, apenas como leitura variante

DEFINITION: even thus, so.
ORIGIN: Neuter plural of ho and autos as adverb; in the same way.

BDAG.en: = τὰ αὐτά (the same)
BDAG.pt: = τὰ αὐτά (o mesmo)

DEFINITION: hence, that, then, these, those.
ORIGIN: And tautas (tow'-tas) dative case and accusative case feminine plural respectively of houtos; (to or with or by, etc.) These.

DEFINITION: her.
ORIGIN: And tauten (tow'-tane), and tautes (tow'-tace) dative case, accusative case and genitive case respectively of the feminine singular of houtos; (towards or of) this.
USAGE: her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same).

DEFINITION: a burial, burial place.
ORIGIN: Feminine from thapto; burial (the act).

BDAG.en: burial; burial-place
BDAG.pt: sepultamento, enterro; lugar de sepultamento

DEFINITION: a burial-place, sepulcher, tomb, grave.
ORIGIN: Masculine from thapto; a grave (the place of interment).

BDAG.en: a site or receptacle for interment, grave, tomb of a dead person; anything that functions as a tomb
BDAG.pt: um local ou receptáculo para sepultamento, cova, túmulo de uma pessoa morta; qualquer coisa que funcione como tumba

DEFINITION: quickly, presently, perhaps.
ORIGIN: As if neuter plural of tachus (adverbially); shortly, i.e. (figuratively) possibly.

BDAG.en: marker expressing contingency ranging between probability and bare possibility, perhaps, possibly, probably
BDAG.pt: marcador que expressa contingência variando entre probabilidade e mera possibilidade, talvez, possivelmente, provavelmente

DEFINITION: soon, quickly, hastily.
ORIGIN: Adverb from tachus; briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly.

BDAG.en: quickly, at once, without delay, soon (positive sense); too quickly, too easily, hastily (remonstrative sense); more quickly, faster (comparative); as soon as possible (superlative: hōs tachista)
BDAG.pt: rapidamente, de uma vez, sem demora, logo (sentido positivo); depressa demais, com muita facilidade, precipitadamente (sentido de repreensão); mais rápido, mais velozmente (comparativo); o mais rápido possível (superlativo: hōs tachista)

DEFINITION: swift, quick, impending.
ORIGIN: From tachos; curt, i.e. Impending.

BDAG.en: pertaining to a very brief extent of time, with focus on speed of action, quick, in haste; pertaining to taking place without delay, coming soon, imminent, swift
BDAG.pt: pertencente a uma extensão de tempo muito breve, com foco na velocidade da ação, rápido, com pressa; pertencente a ocorrer sem demora, vindo em breve, iminente, rápido

DEFINITION: more swiftly, more quickly.
ORIGIN: Neuter singular of the comparative of tachus (as adverb); more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily.

BDAG.en: see tachéōs
BDAG.pt: ver tachéōs

DEFINITION: most swiftly, most quickly, as quickly as possible.
ORIGIN: Neuter plural of the superlative of tachus (as adverb); most quickly, i.e. (with hos prefixed) as soon as possible.

DEFINITION: quickness, speed; hastily, immediately.
ORIGIN: From the same as tachus; a brief space (of time), i.e. (with en prefixed) in haste.

BDAG.en: a very brief period of time, with focus on speed of an activity or event, speed, quickness, swiftness, haste; pertaining to a relatively brief time subsequent to another point of time, soon, in a short time
BDAG.pt: um período de tempo muito breve, com foco na velocidade de uma atividade ou evento, velocidade, rapidez, pressa; pertencente a um tempo relativamente breve subsequente a outro ponto no tempo, em breve, em pouco tempo

DEFINITION: quickly, speedily.
ORIGIN: Neuter singular of tachus (as adverb); shortly, i.e. Without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily.

DEFINITION: quick, swift, speedy, ready, prompt.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready.

BDAG.en: pertaining to a very brief period of time, with focus on speed of an activity or event, quick, swift, speedy; pertaining to a relatively brief time subsequent to another point of time, in a short time, soon
BDAG.pt: pertencente a um período de tempo muito breve, com foco na velocidade de uma atividade ou evento, rápido, veloz, expedito; pertencente a um tempo relativamente breve subsequente a outro ponto no tempo, em breve, em pouco tempo

DEFINITION: and (denotes addition or connection).
ORIGIN: A primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; both or also (properly, as correlation of kai).
USAGE: also, and, both, even, then, whether. Often used in composition, usually as the latter participle.

BDAG.en: enclitic particle; marker of close relationship between sequential states or events, and likewise, and so, so; marker of connection between coordinate nonsequential items (and); used as connecter of sentences and parts of sentences (as... so, not only... but also); marker with ascensive stress and serving without copulative force, even.
BDAG.pt: partícula enclítica; marcador de relação próxima entre estados ou eventos sequenciais, e assim, e então, assim; marcador de conexão entre itens coordenados não sequenciais (e); usado como conectivo de frases e partes de frases (assim como... assim, não só... mas também); marcador com ênfase ascensiva e servindo sem força copulativa, até mesmo.

DEFINITION: a wall, especially of a city.
ORIGIN: Akin to the base of tikto; a wall (as formative of a house).

BDAG.en: wall, esp. city wall
BDAG.pt: muralha, especialmente muralha da cidade

DEFINITION: a sign, certain proof.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of tekmar (a goal or fixed limit); a token (as defining a fact), i.e. Criterion of certainty.

BDAG.en: that which causes something to be known in a convincing and decisive manner, proof (demonstrative proof)
BDAG.pt: aquilo que faz algo ser conhecido de maneira convincente e decisiva, prova (prova demonstrativa)

DEFINITION: a little child.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of teknon; an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts).

BDAG.en: dim. of τέκνον; (little) child voc. pl. τεκνία; in our literature only in the voc. pl., used by Jesus in familiar, loving address to his disciples, or by a Christian apostle or teacher to his spiritual children
BDAG.pt: diminutivo de τέκνον; (pequena) criança voc. pl. τεκνία; em nossa literatura apenas no voc. pl., usado por Jesus em um endereço familiar e amoroso aos seus discípulos, ou por um apóstolo ou mestre cristão aos seus filhos espirituais

DEFINITION: to bear children, beget, rear a family.
ORIGIN: From a compound of teknon and the base of ginomai; to be a child-bearer, i.e. Parent (mother).

BDAG.en: bear/beget children
BDAG.pt: dar à luz/procriar filhos

DEFINITION: child bearing, the rearing of a family.
ORIGIN: From the same as teknogoneo; childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties).

BDAG.en: the bearing of children
BDAG.pt: o ato de dar à luz (geração de filhos)

DEFINITION: a child, descendent, inhabitant.
ORIGIN: From the base of timoria; a child (as produced).

BDAG.en: an offspring of human parents, child; descendants, posterity; one dear to another without genetic relationship (child, son); one who has the characteristics of another being, child of (e.g., children of Abraham, children of God); inhabitants of a city, children (Hebraism); a class of persons with a specific characteristic, children of (e.g., children of love, children of wrath)
BDAG.pt: uma prole de pais humanos, filho; descendentes, posteridade; alguém querido por outro sem relação genética (filho, meu filho); aquele que tem as características de outro ser, filho de (ex: filhos de Abraão, filhos de Deus); habitantes de uma cidade, filhos (hebraísmo); uma classe de pessoas com uma característica específica, filhos de (ex: filhos do amor, filhos da ira)

DEFINITION: to bring up children, rear young.
ORIGIN: From a compound of teknon and trepho; to be a childrearer, i.e. Fulfil the duties of a female parent.

BDAG.en: bring up children, i.e. care for them physically and spiritually
BDAG.pt: criar filhos, ou seja, cuidar deles física e espiritualmente

DEFINITION: a craftsman, a carpenter.
ORIGIN: From the base of timoria; an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood.

BDAG.en: one who constructs, builder, carpenter (worker in wood)
BDAG.pt: aquele que constrói, construtor, carpinteiro (trabalhador em madeira)

DEFINITION: perfect, (a) complete in all its parts, (b) full grown, of full age, (c) specially of the completeness of Christian character.
ORIGIN: From telos; complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with ho) completeness.

BDAG.en: attaining an end or purpose, complete; perfect, expert; mature, full-grown, adult; cult initiate, initiated; fully developed in a moral sense; perfect (of God)
BDAG.pt: atingir um fim ou propósito, completo; perfeito, perito; maduro, adulto; iniciado em ritos cultuais; plenamente desenvolvido em um sentido moral; perfeito (de Deus)

DEFINITION: perfectness, perfection, maturity.
ORIGIN: From teleios; (the state) completeness (mentally or morally).

BDAG.en: perfection, completeness (of love, of maturity)
BDAG.pt: perfeição, completude (do amor, da maturidade)

DEFINITION: (a) as a course, a race, or the like: to complete, finish (b) as of time or prediction: to accomplish, (c) to make perfect; pass: to be perfected.
ORIGIN: From teleios; to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character).

BDAG.en: to complete an activity, finish, accomplish; to overcome or supplant an imperfect state, bring to its goal/accomplishment; fulfill of prophecies, promises; of the perfection of upright persons who have gone on before, perfected; make perfect someone or something; consecrate, initiate.
BDAG.pt: completar uma atividade, terminar, realizar; superar ou suplantar um estado imperfeito, levar ao seu objetivo/realização; cumprir profecias, promessas; no que diz respeito à perfeição de pessoas justas que já partiram, aperfeiçoado; aperfeiçoar alguém ou algo; consagrar, iniciar.

DEFINITION: perfectly, completely, without wavering.
ORIGIN: Adverb from teleios; completely, i.e. (of hope) without wavering.

BDAG.en: fully, perfectly, completely, altogether.
BDAG.pt: totalmente, perfeitamente, completamente, inteiramente.

DEFINITION: completion, fulfillment, perfection.
ORIGIN: From phusioo; (the act) completion, i.e. (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution.

BDAG.en: perfection; fulfillment of a promise.
BDAG.pt: perfeição; cumprimento de uma promessa.

DEFINITION: a perfecter, completer, finisher.
ORIGIN: From teleioo; a completer, i.e. Consummater.

BDAG.en: one who brings something to a successful conclusion, perfecter.
BDAG.pt: aquele que leva algo a uma conclusão bem-sucedida, aperfeiçoador.

DEFINITION: to bring fruit to perfection, to bear perfect offspring.
ORIGIN: From a compound of telos and phero; to be a bearer to completion (maturity), i.e. To ripen fruit (figuratively).

BDAG.en: bear fruit to maturity.
BDAG.pt: dar fruto até a maturidade.

DEFINITION: to complete, to come to an end, to die.
ORIGIN: From a presumed derivative of teleo; to finish life (by implication, of bios), i.e. Expire (demise).

BDAG.en: come to an end; die.
BDAG.pt: chegar ao fim; morrer.

DEFINITION: a finishing, end, death.
ORIGIN: From teleutao; decease.

BDAG.en: end, a euphemism for death.
BDAG.pt: fim, um eufemismo para morte.

DEFINITION: (a) to end, finish, (b) to fulfill, accomplish, (c) to pay.
ORIGIN: From telos; to end, i.e. Complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt).
USAGE: accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform.

BDAG.en: to complete an activity or process, bring to an end, finish, complete; to carry out an obligation or demand, accomplish, perform, fulfill, keep; to pay what is due, pay
BDAG.pt: completar uma atividade ou processo, dar fim, terminar, concluir; cumprir uma obrigação ou demanda, realizar, desempenhar, manter; pagar o que é devido

DEFINITION: (a) an end, (b) event or issue, (c) the principal end, aim, purpose, (d) a tax.
ORIGIN: From a primary tello (to set out for a definite point or goal); properly, the point aimed at as a limit, i.e. (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination (literally, figuratively or indefinitely), result (immediate, ultimate or prophetic), purpose); specially, an impost or levy (as paid).
USAGE: + continual, custom, end(-ing), finally, uttermost. Compare phoros.

BDAG.en: end, termination, cessation; the last part of a process, close, conclusion, esp. of the last things, the final act in the cosmic drama; the goal toward which a movement is being directed, end, goal, outcome; last in a series, rest, remainder; revenue obligation, (indirect) tax, toll-tax, customs duties.
BDAG.pt: fim, término, cessação; a última parte de um processo, conclusão, especialmente das coisas derradeiras, o ato final no drama cósmico; o objetivo para o qual um movimento está sendo direcionado, fim, meta, resultado; o último de uma série, o restante; obrigação de receita, (imposto) indireto, pedágio, taxas alfandegárias.

DEFINITION: a publican, collector of taxes.
ORIGIN: From telos and oneomai; a tax-farmer, i.e. Collector of public revenue.

BDAG.en: tax-collector, revenue officer.
BDAG.pt: coletor de impostos, funcionário da receita.

DEFINITION: a tax-collector's office, toll-house.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of telones; a tax-gatherer's place of business.

BDAG.en: revenue/tax office.
BDAG.pt: escritório de receita/imposto.

DEFINITION: a wonder, portent, marvel.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen.

BDAG.en: someth. that astounds because of transcendent association, prodigy, portent, omen, wonder.
BDAG.pt: algo que espanta devido a uma associação transcendente, prodígio, presságio, presságio, maravilha.

DEFINITION: Tertius, who wrote the Epistle to the Romans at Paul's dictation.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; third; Tertius, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Tertius, a Christian helpful to Paul
BDAG.pt: Tércio, um cristão prestativo a Paulo

DEFINITION: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of Paul at Caesarea.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Tertullus, a Roman.

BDAG.en: Tertullus, attorney for those who accused Paul before Felix the procurator
BDAG.pt: Tertulo, advogado daqueles que acusaram Paulo perante o procurador Félix

DEFINITION: forty.
ORIGIN: The decade of tessares; forty.

BDAG.en: indec. forty, often of days
BDAG.pt: indec. quarenta, frequentemente de dias

DEFINITION: forty years of age.
ORIGIN: From tessarakonta and etos; of forty years of age.

DEFINITION: four.
ORIGIN: Or neuter tessara (tes'-sar-ah) a plural number; four.

BDAG.en: four
BDAG.pt: quatro

DEFINITION: fourteenth.
ORIGIN: From tessares and kai and dekatos; fourteenth.

BDAG.en: fourteenth
BDAG.pt: décimo quarto

DEFINITION: of the fourth day, four days since.
ORIGIN: From tessares; pertaining to the fourth day.

BDAG.en: happening on the fourth day
BDAG.pt: que acontece no quarto dia

DEFINITION: fourth.
ORIGIN: Ordinal from tessares; fourth.

BDAG.en: fourth
BDAG.pt: quarto

DEFINITION: a tetrarch (the governor of a fourth part of a region).
ORIGIN: From tessares and gonia; four-cornered, i.e. Square.

BDAG.en: pert. to having four sides and four right angles, (four)-square
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter quatro lados e quatro ângulos retos, (de) quatro cantos

DEFINITION: a group of four, a quaternion (a guard of four soldiers).
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of tetras (a tetrad; from tessares); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers.

BDAG.en: a detachment/squad of four soldiers
BDAG.pt: um destacamento/esquadrão de quatro soldados

DEFINITION: four thousand.
ORIGIN: From the multiplicative adverb of tessares and chilioi; four times a thousand.

BDAG.en: four thousand
BDAG.pt: quatro mil

DEFINITION: four hundred.
ORIGIN: Plural from tessares and hekaton.

BDAG.en: four hundred
BDAG.pt: quatrocentos

DEFINITION: of four months, a period of four months.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of tessares and men; a four months' space.

BDAG.en: lasting four months; the period of four months
BDAG.pt: durando quatro meses; o período de quatro meses

DEFINITION: four-fold, four times as much.
ORIGIN: From tessares and a derivative of the base of pleistos; quadruple.

BDAG.en: four times, fourfold
BDAG.pt: quatro vezes, quádruplo

DEFINITION: four-footed.
ORIGIN: From tessares and pous; a quadruped.

BDAG.en: four-footed, quadrupeds
BDAG.pt: quadrúpede, animais quadrúpedes

DEFINITION: to rule over as a tetrarch.
ORIGIN: From tetrarches; to be a tetrarch.

DEFINITION: a tetrarch, ruler over a fourth part of a region.
ORIGIN: From tessares and archo; the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch").

DEFINITION: to reduce to ashes, consume, destroy.
ORIGIN: From tephra (ashes); to incinerate, i.e. Consume.

BDAG.en: cover with or reduce to ashes
BDAG.pt: cobrir com cinzas ou reduzir a cinzas

DEFINITION: art, skill, trade, craft.
ORIGIN: From the base of tikto; art (as productive), i.e. (specially), a trade, or (generally) skill.

BDAG.en: skill, trade
BDAG.pt: habilidade, ofício

DEFINITION: a craftsman, artisan, architect, builder.
ORIGIN: From techne; an artisan; figuratively, a founder (Creator).

BDAG.en: craftsperson, artisan, designer (of God as architect)
BDAG.pt: artesão, artífice, projetista (de Deus como arquiteto)

DEFINITION: to make liquid; pass: to melt (away).
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to liquefy.

BDAG.en: to cause someth. to become liquid, melt (trans.); pass. melt (intr.), dissolve (intr.)
BDAG.pt: fazer com que algo se torne líquido, derreter (trans.); passivo derreter (intrans.), dissolver (intrans.)

DEFINITION: clearly, distinctly, plainly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a compound of a derivative of telos and auge; in a far-shining manner, i.e. Plainly.

BDAG.en: adv. of τηλαυγής, of a visual image (very) plainly/clearly
BDAG.pt: advérbio de τηλαυγής, de uma imagem visual (muito) claramente/nitidamente

DEFINITION: such as this, of persons so old, of things so great.
ORIGIN: Or feminine telikaute (tay-lik-ow'-tay) from a compound of ho with helikos and houtos; such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast.

BDAG.en: a demonstrative pron. correlative to ἡλίκος; 1 in ref. to size so great, so large; 2 in ref. to degree so great/important/mighty etc.
BDAG.pt: um pronome demonstrativo correlativo a ἡλίκος; 1 em referência a tamanho tão grande, tão vasto; 2 em referência a grau tão grande/importante/poderoso etc.

DEFINITION: to keep, guard, observe, watch over.
ORIGIN: From teros (a watch; perhaps akin to theoreo); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from phulasso, which is properly to prevent escaping; and from koustodia, which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), i.e. To note (a prophecy; figuratively, to fulfil a command); by implication, to detain (in custody; figuratively, to maintain); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried).
USAGE: hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch.

BDAG.en: 1. retain in custody, keep watch over, guard; 2. cause a state to continue, keep, hold, preserve; 3. persist in obedience, keep, observe, fulfill (especially law/teaching)
BDAG.pt: 1. reter sob custódia, vigiar, guardar; 2. fazer com que um estado continue, manter, reservar, preservar; 3. persistir em obediência, guardar, observar, cumprir (especialmente lei/doutrina)

DEFINITION: a prison; observance (as of precepts).
ORIGIN: From tereo; a watching, i.e. (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison.

BDAG.en: act of holding in custody, custody, imprisonment; a place for custody, prison; act of ensuring the well-being of another, care; act of persisting in obedience, keeping, observance
BDAG.pt: ato de manter sob custódia, custódia, prisão; lugar de custódia, prisão; ato de garantir o bem-estar de outrem, cuidado; ato de persistir na obediência, guarda, observância

DEFINITION: Tiberias, a town in Galilee on the western border of the sea called after it.
ORIGIN: From Tiberios; Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Tiberias, a city on the west shore of the Lake of Gennesaret
BDAG.pt: Tibériades, uma cidade na margem ocidental do Mar da Galileia

DEFINITION: Tiberius, the second Roman emperor (died A.D. 37).
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor.

BDAG.en: Tiberius, a Roman emperor
BDAG.pt: Tibério, um imperador romano

DEFINITION: to put, place, lay, set, fix, establish.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form of a primary theo (theh'-o) (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses) to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly, in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from histemi, which properly denotes an upright and active position, while keimai is properly reflexive and utterly prostrate).
USAGE: + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down.

BDAG.en: to put or place in a particular location, lay, set up, put (away); to explain in what figure of speech can we present (the Reign of God); to take off, give up (in John); to show deference to, bend the knee; to place before someone, serve; to have (in mind), make up (your) minds; to effect someth., arrange for someth.; to assign to some task or function, appoint, assign; to establish, give (of a law), fix, establish, set; to cause to undergo a change in experience/condition, make, consign (to something or someone)
BDAG.pt: colocar ou dispor em um local particular, deitar, erguer, pôr (de lado); explicar em que figura de linguagem podemos apresentar (o Reino de Deus); tirar, entregar (em João); mostrar deferência, dobrar os joelhos; colocar diante de alguém, servir; ter em mente, decidir-se; efetuar algo, arranjar algo; designar para alguma tarefa ou função, nomear, atribuir; estabelecer, dar (de uma lei), fixar, estabelecer; causar uma mudança na experiência/condição, fazer, consignar (a algo ou alguém)

DEFINITION: to bear, bring forth, produce, beget, yield.
ORIGIN: A strengthened form of a primary teko tek'-o (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively.
USAGE: bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.

BDAG.en: to cause to be born or come into the world, give birth (to), bear
BDAG.pt: fazer nascer ou vir ao mundo, dar à luz, gerar

DEFINITION: to pluck, to pluck off.
ORIGIN: Perhaps akin to the alternate of haireomai, and thus to suro; to pull off.

BDAG.en: pluck, pick (e.g., heads of wheat).
BDAG.pt: arrancar, colher (e.g., espigas de trigo).

DEFINITION: Timaeus, father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus.
ORIGIN: Probably of Chaldee origin (compare tame'); Timoeus (i.e. Timay), an Israelite.

DEFINITION: (a) to value at a price, estimate, (b) to honor, reverence.
ORIGIN: From timios; to prize, i.e. Fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere.

BDAG.en: set a price on, estimate, value; show high regard for, honor, revere.
BDAG.pt: estabelecer um preço, estimar, avaliar; mostrar alta consideração, honrar, reverenciar.

DEFINITION: a valuing, a price.
ORIGIN: From tino; a value, i.e. Money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy, esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself.

BDAG.en: of value; unique, God-given position of the ruler; heavenly possessions; honor conferred through compensation, honorarium, compensation; a right that is specially conferred, privilege; respectability, a place of honor, (honorable) office.
BDAG.pt: de valor; posição única, dada por Deus, do governante; posses celestiais; honra conferida através de compensação, honorário, indenização; um direito especialmente conferido, privilégio; respeitabilidade, um lugar de honra, (honrado) cargo.

DEFINITION: of great price, precious, honored.
ORIGIN: Including the comparative timioteros (tim-ee-o'-ter-os), and the superlative timiotatos (tim-ee-o'-tat-os) from time; valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved.
USAGE: dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.

BDAG.en: held in honor; pert. to being of exceptional value, costly, precious; held in honor, respected; pert. to high status that merits esteem, held in honor/high regard, respected
BDAG.pt: mantido em honra; referente a ser de valor excepcional, custoso, precioso; mantido em honra, respeitado; referente a alto status que merece estima, mantido em honra/alta consideração, respeitado

DEFINITION: preciousness, costliness, worth.
ORIGIN: From timios; expensiveness, i.e. (by implication) magnificence.

BDAG.en: richness, prosperity (abstract for concrete abundance of costly things).
BDAG.pt: riqueza, prosperidade (abstrato para abundância concreta de coisas custosas).

DEFINITION: Timothy, a Christian of Lystra, helper of Paul.
ORIGIN: From time and theos; dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Timothy, a friend, traveling companion and co-worker of Paul.
BDAG.pt: Timóteo, um amigo, companheiro de viagem e colaborador de Paulo.

DEFINITION: Timon, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.
ORIGIN: From time; valuable; Timon, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Timon, one of the seven persons appointed to release the apostles from papyrus-work relating to aid for widows.
BDAG.pt: Timão, uma das sete pessoas designadas para libertar os apóstolos do trabalho com papiro relativo à ajuda às viúvas.

DEFINITION: to punish, avenge myself on.
ORIGIN: From a comparative of time and ouros (a guard); properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. To avenge (inflict a penalty).

BDAG.en: punish someone, have someone punished.
BDAG.pt: punir alguém, fazer com que alguém seja punido.

DEFINITION: punishment, vengeance.
ORIGIN: From timoreo; vindication, i.e. (by implication) a penalty.

BDAG.en: punishment (inflicted by God).
BDAG.pt: punição (infligida por Deus).

DEFINITION: to pay, to pay a penalty.
ORIGIN: Strengthened for a primary tio (tee'-o) (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses) to pay a price, i.e. As a penalty.

BDAG.en: to experience retribution, pay, undergo a penalty.
BDAG.pt: experimentar retribuição, pagar, sofrer uma penalidade.

DEFINITION: any one, some one, a certain one or thing.
ORIGIN: An enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object.
USAGE: a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever).

BDAG.en: someone, anybody, somebody; some, a number of (people); a certain pers., etc.; nothing (in negative statements); each one; something, anything; some, any, a certain; a proper name; an adj. or adjectival pron.; to moderate an expr. that is too definite; some, considerable; several; to be a person of importance, to be somebody
BDAG.pt: alguém, qualquer um, alguém; alguns, um número de (pessoas); uma certa pessoa, etc.; nada (em declarações negativas); cada um; algo, qualquer coisa; algum, qualquer, um certo; um nome próprio; um adjetivo ou pronome adjetival; para moderar uma expressão muito definida; algum, considerável; vários; ser uma pessoa importante, ser alguém

DEFINITION: who, which, what, why.
ORIGIN: Probably emphatic of tis; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions).
USAGE: every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why.

BDAG.en: interrogative pronoun: who? which (one)? what? (used in direct, indirect, rhetorical questions; sometimes substituting the relative pronoun).
BDAG.pt: pronome interrogativo: quem? qual (deles)? o quê? (usado em perguntas diretas, indiretas e retóricas; às vezes substituindo o pronome relativo).

DEFINITION: Titius (surnamed Justus), a Christian.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard).

BDAG.en: inscription, notice on the cross, which gave the reason for condemnation
BDAG.pt: inscrição, aviso na cruz, que dava a razão para a condenação

DEFINITION: Titus, a Greek Christian, helper of Paul, perhaps also brother of Luke.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Titus. 1 friend and colleague of Paul, mentioned in our lit. only in Paul’s letters. As a Gentile Christian he accompanied Paul to a meeting at Jerusalem; Paul did not have him circumcised... 2 surnamed Justus
BDAG.pt: Tito. 1 amigo e colega de Paulo, mencionado em nossa literatura apenas nas cartas de Paulo. Como cristão gentio, acompanhou Paulo a uma reunião em Jerusalém; Paulo não o fez circuncidar... 2 apelidado de Justo

DEFINITION: an enclitic particle of asseveration used as a prefix or suff. in the N.T.
ORIGIN: Probably for the dative case of ho; an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth.
USAGE: (used only with other particles in the comparative, as kaitoige, mentoi, toigaroun, toinun, etc.)

BDAG.en: enclitic particle marker of emphasis on the reliability of a statement, let me tell you, surely, in our lit. only in the transition formula and furthermore, besides
BDAG.pt: partícula enclítica marcadora de ênfase na confiabilidade de uma declaração, deixe-me dizer, certamente, em nossa literatura apenas na fórmula de transição e além disso, ademais

DEFINITION: consequently, therefore, well then, so then.
ORIGIN: From toi and gar and oun; truly for then, i.e. Consequently.

BDAG.en: a particle introducing an inference, for that very reason, then, therefore
BDAG.pt: uma partícula que introduz uma inferência, por essa mesma razão, então, portanto

DEFINITION: indeed now, therefore, accordingly, well then.
ORIGIN: From toi and nun; truly now, i.e. Accordingly.

BDAG.en: a particle introducing an inference, hence, so, well (then), indeed
BDAG.pt: uma partícula que introduz uma inferência, por conseguinte, então, bem (então), de fato

DEFINITION: of this kind, such, such as follows.
ORIGIN: (including the other inflections); from a derivative of toi and de; such-like then, i.e. So great.

BDAG.en: such as this, of this kind, referring to what follows and w. suggestion of unusual aspect
BDAG.pt: tal como este, deste tipo, referindo-se ao que se segue e com sugestão de aspecto incomum

DEFINITION: of such a kind, such.
ORIGIN: (including the other inflections); from toi and houtos; truly this, i.e. Of this sort (to denote character or individuality).

BDAG.en: correlative adj. pert. to being like some pers. or thing mentioned in a context, of such a kind, such as this, like such
BDAG.pt: adjetivo correlativo pertinente a ser como alguma pessoa ou coisa mencionada em um contexto, de tal tipo, tal como este, como tal

DEFINITION: a wall.
ORIGIN: Another form of teichos; a wall.

BDAG.en: wall, in denunciatory expression whitewashed wall
BDAG.pt: muro, parede; em expressão de denúncia, muro caiado

DEFINITION: a bringing forth, birth, interest, usury.
ORIGIN: From the base of tikto; interest on money loaned (as a produce).

BDAG.en: interest on money loaned. compound interest
BDAG.pt: juros sobre dinheiro emprestado. juros compostos

DEFINITION: to dare, endure, be bold, have courage, make up the mind.
ORIGIN: From tolma (boldness; probably itself from the base of telos through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while tharrheo is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous.

BDAG.en: to show boldness or resolution in the face of danger, opposition, or a problem, dare, bring oneself to (do someth.)
BDAG.pt: demonstrar ousadia ou resolução diante do perigo, oposição ou um problema, ousar, animar-se a (fazer algo)

DEFINITION: more boldly, more freely, with more confidence.
ORIGIN: Neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of tolmao (as adverb); more daringly, i.e. With greater confidence than otherwise.

BDAG.en: rather boldly
BDAG.pt: com mais ousadia, mais audaciosamente

DEFINITION: a bold, daring man.
ORIGIN: From tolmao; a daring (audacious) man.

BDAG.en: bold, audacious pers.
BDAG.pt: pessoa ousada, audaciosa

DEFINITION: sharper, keener.
ORIGIN: Comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than kopto, as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen.

DEFINITION: a bow.
ORIGIN: From the base of tikto; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric).

BDAG.en: the bow as an archer’s weapon
BDAG.pt: o arco como arma de um arqueiro

DEFINITION: a topaz.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite.

BDAG.en: topaz, a bright yellow, more or less transparent precious stone
BDAG.pt: topázio, uma pedra preciosa amarelo brilhante, mais ou menos transparente

DEFINITION: a place, region, seat; an opportunity.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas chora is a large but participle locality), i.e. Location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard.
USAGE: coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.

BDAG.en: place, (particular) spot, scene; regions, districts; an abode: place, room to live, stay, sit etc.; the customary location of something; a transcendent site: esp. of the place to which one’s final destiny brings one; a specific point of reference in a book, place, passage; a position held in a group for discharge of some responsibility, position, office; a favorable circumstance for doing something, possibility, opportunity, chance; idiom: instead of (where something was said to them)
BDAG.pt: lugar, ponto (particular), cena; regiões, distritos; uma morada: lugar, espaço para viver, ficar, sentar, etc.; o local costumeiro de algo; um local transcendente: especialmente o lugar para onde o destino final de alguém conduz; um ponto específico de referência em um livro, lugar, passagem; uma posição ocupada em um grupo para cumprir alguma responsabilidade, cargo, ofício; uma circunstância favorável para fazer algo, possibilidade, oportunidade, chance; idiomatismo: em vez de (onde lhes foi dito)

DEFINITION: so great, so large, so long, so many.
ORIGIN: From tosos (so much; apparently from ho and hos) and houtos (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. Such (in quantity, amount, number of space).
USAGE: as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.

BDAG.en: so great, so large, so far, so much, so strong, etc.; so many (entities or events); so much, so great a (quantity); so long (time); so great/strong, to such extent; to such a degree of (negative sense); so much and no more; so much, as much (correlative degree, corresponding to ὅσῳ)
BDAG.pt: tão grande, tão extenso, tão distante, tanto, tão forte, etc.; tantos (entidades ou eventos); tanta, tão grande (quantidade); por tanto tempo (tempo); tão grande/forte, a tal ponto; a tal grau de (sentido negativo); tanto e não mais; tanto, quanto (grau correlativo, correspondente a ὅσῳ)

DEFINITION: then, at that time.
ORIGIN: From (the neuter of) ho and hote; the when, i.e. At the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution).

BDAG.en: at that time, then; of the future, then; of any time at all that fulfills certain conditions; then, thereupon (to introduce what follows in time)
BDAG.pt: naquele tempo, então; no futuro, então; de qualquer tempo que satisfaça certas condições; então, em seguida (para introduzir o que se segue no tempo)

DEFINITION: his.
ORIGIN: Properly, the genitive case of ho; sometimes used for toutou; of this person.

DEFINITION: on the contrary, on the other hand.
ORIGIN: Contraction for the neuter of ho and enantion; on the contrary.

DEFINITION: by name.
ORIGIN: Contraction for the neuter of ho and onoma; the name (is).

DEFINITION: that is to say.
ORIGIN: Contraction for touto and esti; that is.

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Neuter singular nominative or accusative case of houtos; that thing.
USAGE: here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore).

BDAG.en: (see οὗτος)
BDAG.pt: (ver οὗτος)

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Dative case plural masculine or neuter of houtos; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things).
USAGE: such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those.

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Accusative case singular masculine of houtos; this (person, as objective of verb or preposition).

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Genitive case singular masculine or neuter of houtos; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing).
USAGE: here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus.

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Accusative case plural masculine of houtos; these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition).

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Dative case singular masculine or neuter of houtos; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing).
USAGE: here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this.

DEFINITION: this; he, she, it.
ORIGIN: Genitive case plural masculine or neuter of houtos; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things).
USAGE: such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.

DEFINITION: a male goat.
ORIGIN: From the base of trogo; a he-goat (as a gnawer).

BDAG.en: he-goat (named among other sacrificial animals, esp. on the Day of Atonement)
BDAG.pt: bode (nomeado entre outros animais sacrificiais, especialmente no Dia da Expiação)

DEFINITION: a table, (a) for food or banqueting, (b) for money-changing or business.
ORIGIN: Probably contracted from tessares and peze; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest).

BDAG.en: structure or surface for placing things, table; of a cultic object (table of showbread); table for a meal; money changers' table/bank; metonymically: a meal, food
BDAG.pt: estrutura ou superfície para colocar coisas, mesa; de um objeto cultual (mesa dos pães da proposição); mesa para uma refeição; mesa/banco de cambistas; metonimicamente: uma refeição, comida

DEFINITION: a money-changer, banker.
ORIGIN: From trapeza; a money-broker or banker.

BDAG.en: money changer, banker
BDAG.pt: cambista, banqueiro

DEFINITION: a wound.
ORIGIN: From the base of titrosko (to wound; akin to the base of thrauo, tribos, trizo, etc.); a wound.

BDAG.en: a wound
BDAG.pt: uma ferida

DEFINITION: to wound.
ORIGIN: From trauma; to inflict a wound.

BDAG.en: to wound
BDAG.pt: ferir

DEFINITION: to take by the throat, to overthrow.
ORIGIN: From trachelos; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. To expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare).

BDAG.en: to lay bare, reveal (in the only occurrence, referring to eyes being laid bare before God)
BDAG.pt: pôr a descoberto, revelar (na única ocorrência, referindo-se aos olhos postos a descoberto diante de Deus)

DEFINITION: the neck.
ORIGIN: Probably from trecho (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life.

BDAG.en: neck, throat; metaphorically: risking one's neck, bowing the neck in obedience
BDAG.pt: pescoço, garganta; metaforicamente: arriscar o pescoço, curvar o pescoço em obediência

DEFINITION: rough, rugged, uneven.
ORIGIN: Perhaps strengthened from the base of rhegnumi (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy).

BDAG.en: rough, uneven (of mountains, stones, road)
BDAG.pt: áspero, irregular (de montanhas, pedras, estrada)

DEFINITION: Trachonitis, the north-east of the territory beyond Jordan.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of trachus; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria.

BDAG.en: Trachonitis (the district south of Damascus)
BDAG.pt: Trachonitis (o distrito ao sul de Damasco)

DEFINITION: three.
ORIGIN: Or neuter tria (tree'-ah) a primary (plural) number; "three".

BDAG.en: three
BDAG.pt: três

DEFINITION: to tremble (esp. with fear).
ORIGIN: Strengthened from a primary treo (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear.

BDAG.en: to shake involuntarily, tremble, quiver; to feel intensely the impact of something transcendent, tremble, be in awe
BDAG.pt: tremer involuntariamente, estremecer, vibrar; sentir intensamente o impacto de algo transcendente, tremer, estar em assombro

DEFINITION: to feed, nourish; to bring up, rear, provide for.
ORIGIN: A primary verb (properly, threpho; but perhaps strengthened from the base of trope through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. Fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear).

BDAG.en: to care for by providing food or nourishment, feed, nourish, support; to care for children by bringing them up, rear, bring up, train
BDAG.pt: cuidar provendo alimento ou nutrição, alimentar, nutrir, sustentar; cuidar de crianças criando-as, criar, educar, treinar

DEFINITION: to run, exercise myself, make progress.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho; compare thrix); which uses dremo drem'-o (the base of dromos) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to make rapid linear movement, run, rush, advance; to make an effort to advance spiritually or intellectually, exert oneself; to proceed quickly and without restraint, progress
BDAG.pt: fazer movimento linear rápido, correr, apressar-se, avançar; fazer um esforço para avançar espiritual ou intelectualmente, esforçar-se; prosseguir rapidamente e sem restrições, progredir

DEFINITION: a hole.
ORIGIN: The decade of treis; thirty.

BDAG.en: thirty
BDAG.pt: trinta

DEFINITION: three hundred.
ORIGIN: Plural from treis and hekaton; three hundred.

BDAG.en: three hundred
BDAG.pt: trezentos

DEFINITION: a thistle.
ORIGIN: From treis and belos; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop).

BDAG.en: of prickly weeds, esp. the thistle
BDAG.pt: de ervas daninhas espinhosas, especialmente o cardo

DEFINITION: a worn path, beaten way, road, highway.
ORIGIN: From tribo (to "rub"; akin to teiro, truo, and the base of tragos, trauma); a rut or worn track.

BDAG.en: a defined track or route, path (beaten path, path generally, fig. of established ways of conduct)
BDAG.pt: um caminho ou rota definidos, trilha (caminho batido, caminho em geral, fig. de maneiras estabelecidas de conduta)

DEFINITION: a period of three years.
ORIGIN: From a compound of treis and etos; a three years' period (triennium).

BDAG.en: a period of three years, three years
BDAG.pt: um período de três anos, três anos

DEFINITION: to cry, chirp, to grind the teeth.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy).

BDAG.en: to utter a shrill cry; gnash, grind (the teeth)
BDAG.pt: emitir um grito estridente; ranger, apertar (os dentes)

DEFINITION: lasting three months.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of treis and men as noun; a three months' space.

BDAG.en: (a period of) three months
BDAG.pt: (um período de) três meses

DEFINITION: three times.
ORIGIN: Adverb from treis; three times.

BDAG.en: three times, thrice
BDAG.pt: três vezes, três

DEFINITION: having three stories; subst: the third story.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of treis and stege as noun; a third roof (story).

DEFINITION: three thousand.
ORIGIN: From tris and chilioi; three times a thousand.

BDAG.en: three thousand
BDAG.pt: três mil

DEFINITION: third.
ORIGIN: Ordinal from treis; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly.

BDAG.en: third in a series; a third part of something, third, third part
BDAG.pt: terceiro em uma série; uma terceira parte de algo, terceiro, a terceira parte

DEFINITION: made of hair.
ORIGIN: From thrix; hairy, i.e. Made of hair (mohair).

BDAG.en: made of hair
BDAG.pt: feito de pelo/cabelo

DEFINITION: a trembling, quaking, fear.
ORIGIN: From tremo; a "trembling", i.e. Quaking with fear.

BDAG.en: trembling, quivering fr. fear
BDAG.pt: tremor, estremecimento por medo

DEFINITION: a turning, change, mutation.
ORIGIN: From an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e. Revolution (figuratively, variation).

BDAG.en: the process of turning, turn, turning, change
BDAG.pt: o processo de virar, volta, virada, mudança

DEFINITION: (a) way, manner, (b) manner of life, character.
ORIGIN: From the same as trope; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character.
USAGE: (even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way.

BDAG.en: the manner in which something is done, manner, way, kind, guise; the way in which a person behaves or lives, ways, customs, kind of life
BDAG.pt: a maneira pela qual algo é feito, modo, via, tipo, aparência; a maneira como uma pessoa se comporta ou vive, modos, costumes, tipo de vida

DEFINITION: to endure the ways of, put up with.
ORIGIN: From tropos and phoreo; to endure one's habits.

BDAG.en: bear/put up with (someone’s) manner, moods etc.
BDAG.pt: suportar/tolerar o modo, os humores, etc. (de alguém)

DEFINITION: food, nourishment, maintenance.
ORIGIN: From trepho; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages).

BDAG.en: nourishment, food
BDAG.pt: nutrição, alimento

DEFINITION: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia.
ORIGIN: From trophe; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Trophimus a companion of Paul on his last journey to Jerusalem
BDAG.pt: Trófimo, um companheiro de Paulo em sua última viagem a Jerusalém

DEFINITION: a nurse.
ORIGIN: From trepho; a nourisher, i.e. Nurse.

BDAG.en: nurse, possibly mother
BDAG.pt: nutriz, possivelmente mãe

DEFINITION: the track of a wheel, a track, path.
ORIGIN: From trochos; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct.

BDAG.en: wheel-track, course, way
BDAG.pt: trilha de roda, percurso, caminho

DEFINITION: a wheel, course.
ORIGIN: From trecho; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects.

BDAG.en: wheel, (in NT) course or round of existence
BDAG.pt: roda, (no NT) curso ou ciclo da existência

DEFINITION: a deep dish, platter, bowl.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl.

BDAG.en: bowl, dish
BDAG.pt: tigela, prato

DEFINITION: to gather (as of grapes), harvest.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage.

BDAG.en: gather in ripe fruit, esp. harvest (grapes)
BDAG.pt: colher frutas maduras, especialmente vindimar (uvas)

DEFINITION: a turtle-dove.
ORIGIN: From truzo (to murmur; akin to trizo, but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing).

BDAG.en: small pigeon, turtledove, as a sacrificial animal of poor people
BDAG.pt: pomba pequena, rola, como animal sacrificial dos pobres

DEFINITION: a hole, eye (of a needle).
ORIGIN: From a derivative of truo (to wear away; akin to the base of trauma, tribos and trogo); an orifice, i.e. Needle's eye.

BDAG.en: hole
BDAG.pt: buraco, abertura

DEFINITION: a hole; the eye of a needle.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of the base of trumalia; an aperture, i.e. A needle's eye.

BDAG.en: that which is bored, a hole
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é furado, um buraco

DEFINITION: Tryphaena, a Christian woman in Rome.
ORIGIN: From truphe; luxurious; Tryphoena, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Tryphena ('Dainty'), a Christian acknowledged by Paul for her work in the Lord’s service
BDAG.pt: Trifena ('Delicada'), uma cristã reconhecida por Paulo por seu trabalho no serviço do Senhor

DEFINITION: to live a luxurious life, live self-indulgently.
ORIGIN: From truphe; to indulge in luxury.

BDAG.en: to lead a life of self-indulgence, live for pleasure, revel, carouse; (of animals) be contented, well fed
BDAG.pt: levar uma vida de autogratificação, viver para o prazer, festejar, banquetear; (de animais) estar contente, bem alimentado

DEFINITION: effeminate luxury, softness, indulgent living.
ORIGIN: From thrupto (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. Luxury or debauchery.

BDAG.en: 1. self-indulgent lifestyle, indulgence, reveling; 2. a state of extraordinary ease and comfort, luxury, splendor; 3. a state of intense satisfaction, enjoyment, joy, delight
BDAG.pt: 1. estilo de vida de autogratificação, indulgência, folia; 2. um estado de conforto e facilidade extraordinários, luxo, esplendor; 3. um estado de satisfação intensa, desfrute, alegria, deleite

DEFINITION: Tryphosa, a Christian woman in Rome, perhaps a sister of Tryphaena.
ORIGIN: From truphe; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female.

BDAG.en: Tryphosa ('Luscious'), Christian recipient of a commendatory greeting
BDAG.pt: Trifosa ('Suculenta'), cristã destinatária de uma saudação elogiosa

DEFINITION: Troas, a city near the Hellespont (i.e. Dardanelles).
ORIGIN: From Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Troas, (the) Troad, a city and region in the northwest corner of Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Troas, a Troade, uma cidade e região no canto noroeste da Ásia Menor

DEFINITION: Trogyllium, a promontory somewhat to the south of Ephesus.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Trogyllium a promontory and town south of Ephesus in Asia Minor
BDAG.pt: Troglílio, um promontório e cidade ao sul de Éfeso, na Ásia Menor

DEFINITION: to eat, partake of a meal.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of trauma and tribos through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of trugon and trizo through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat.

BDAG.en: to bite or chew food, eat (audibly), of animals; of human beings, to eat (especially in context of close comradeship or Lord's Supper)
BDAG.pt: morder ou mastigar comida, comer (audivelmente), de animais; de seres humanos, comer (especialmente em contexto de camaradagem íntima ou Ceia do Senhor)

DEFINITION: (a) gen: to obtain, (b) absol: to chance, happen; ordinary, everyday, it may chance, perhaps.
ORIGIN: Probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of tikto through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with ei), i.e. Perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with ou, extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were).
USAGE: be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh...self, + special. Compare tupto.
