BDAG.en: 1. to experience some happening, meet, attain, gain, find, experience; 2. to prove to be in the result, happen, turn out
BDAG.pt: 1. experimentar algum acontecimento, encontrar, atingir, ganhar, achar, experimentar; 2. provar ser no resultado, acontecer, resultar

DEFINITION: to torture, break on the wheel, beat to death.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of tupto (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death.

BDAG.en: to torture with an instrument called τύμπανον; torment, torture gener.
BDAG.pt: torturar com um instrumento chamado τύμπανον (tambor/timbre); atormentar, torturar em geral

DEFINITION: (originally: the mark of a blow, then a stamp struck by a die), (a) a figure; a copy, image, (b) a pattern, model, (c) a type, prefiguring something or somebody.
ORIGIN: From tupto; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. A statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. A model (for imitation) or instance (for warning).
USAGE: en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.

BDAG.en: a mark made as the result of a blow or pressure, mark, trace; embodiment of characteristics or function of a model, copy, image; an object formed to resemble some entity, image, statue; a kind, class, or thing that suggests a model or pattern, form, figure, pattern; the content of a document, text, content; an archetype serving as a model, type, pattern, model; of the types given by God as an indication of the future, in the form of persons or things
BDAG.pt: uma marca feita como resultado de um golpe ou pressão, marca, vestígio; incorporação de características ou função de um modelo, cópia, imagem; um objeto formado para assemelhar-se a alguma entidade, imagem, estátua; um tipo, classe ou coisa que sugere um modelo ou padrão, forma, figura, modelo; o conteúdo de um documento, texto, conteúdo; um arquétipo servindo como modelo, tipo, padrão, modelo; dos tipos dados por Deus como indicação do futuro, na forma de pessoas ou coisas

DEFINITION: to beat, strike, wound, inflict punishment.
ORIGIN: A primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. Cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from paio and patasso, which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or plesso with the fist (or a hammer), or rhapizo with the palm; as well as from tugchano, an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience).

BDAG.en: to inflict a blow, strike, beat, wound; fig. strike, assault (misfortunes designated as blows coming fr. God; assault someone’s conscience)
BDAG.pt: infligir um golpe, bater, ferir, machucar; fig. golpear, atacar (infortúnios designados como golpes vindos de Deus; agredir a consciência de alguém)

DEFINITION: Tyrannus, an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.
ORIGIN: A provincial form of the derivative of the base of kurios; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian.

BDAG.en: Tyrannus, an Ephesian in whose hall Paul lectured
BDAG.pt: Tirannus, um efesino no salão do qual Paulo ensinava

DEFINITION: to agitate or disturb in mind, trouble.
ORIGIN: From turbe (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to thorubos); to make "turbid", i.e. Disturb.

BDAG.en: to cause to bestir; mid. or pass. in act. sense trouble oneself, be troubled, be agitated with or about someth.
BDAG.pt: causar agitação; voz média ou passiva em sentido ativo perturbar-se, ficar aflito, ficar agitado com ou sobre algo

DEFINITION: a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre.
ORIGIN: From Turos; a Tyrian, i.e. Inhabitant of Tyrus.

BDAG.en: the Tyrian
BDAG.pt: o Tiro (gentílico)

DEFINITION: Tyre, an ancient city, the capital of Phoenicia.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Tsor): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Tyre, a city in Phoenicia
BDAG.pt: Tiro, uma cidade na Fenícia

DEFINITION: blind, physically or mentally.
ORIGIN: From, tuphoo; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally).

BDAG.en: pert. to being unable to see, blind, lit.; pert. to being unable to understand, incapable of comprehending, blind, of mental and spiritual blindness in imagery, fig. ext. of mng.
BDAG.pt: pertencente à incapacidade de ver, cego, literal; pertencente à incapacidade de compreender, incapaz de assimilar, cego, de cegueira mental e espiritual em sentido figurado, ext. de sentido.

DEFINITION: to make blind, physically or mentally.
ORIGIN: From tuphlos; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure.

BDAG.en: to deprive of sight, to blind (in our lit. only in imagery or fig.)
BDAG.pt: privar da visão, cegar (em nossa literatura apenas em sentido figurado ou imagético)

DEFINITION: to puff up, make haughty; pass: to be puffed up, be haughty.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of tupho; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit.
USAGE: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.

BDAG.en: ‘becloud, delude’, but only in a fig. sense and quite predom., in our lit. exclusively, in the pass. (be puffed up, conceited; be blinded, become foolish; be mentally ill)
BDAG.pt: ‘nublar, iludir’, mas apenas em sentido figurado e predominante, em nossa literatura exclusivamente na voz passiva (ficar inchado de orgulho, presunçoso; ficar cego, tornar-se tolo; estar mentalmente doente)

DEFINITION: to raise smoke, smolder.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. Slowly consume without flame.

BDAG.en: to give off smoke, pass. smoke, smolder, glimmer
BDAG.pt: soltar fumaça, no passivo: fumegar, arder lentamente, brilhar fracamente

DEFINITION: violent, tempestuous, stormy.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of tupho; stormy (as if smoky).

BDAG.en: like a whirlwind, a typhoon, hurricane
BDAG.pt: como um redemoinho, um tufão, furacão

DEFINITION: Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of tugchano; fortuitous, i.e. Fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Tychicus, a man fr. the province of Asia who accompanied Paul on his journey to Jerusalem w. the collection
BDAG.pt: Tíquico, um homem da província da Ásia que acompanhou Paulo em sua jornada a Jerusalém com a coleta

DEFINITION: dark purple or blue, of the color of hyacinth.
ORIGIN: From huakinthos; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. Deep blue.

BDAG.en: hyacinth-colored, i.e. dark blue (dark red?) or violet
BDAG.pt: cor de jacinto, ou seja, azul escuro (ou vermelho escuro?) ou violeta

DEFINITION: jacinth, a precious stone of the color of hyacinth.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. Some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon.

BDAG.en: the jacinth or hyacinth, a precious stone (perhaps blue in color, something like the sapphire)
BDAG.pt: o jacinto ou a flor jacinto, uma pedra preciosa (talvez azulada, semelhante à safira)

DEFINITION: glassy, made of glass, transparent.
ORIGIN: From hualos; glassy, i.e. Transparent.

BDAG.en: of glass, transparent as glass
BDAG.pt: de vidro, transparente como vidro

DEFINITION: glass, crystal, clear transparent stone.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the same as huetos (as being transparent like rain); glass.

BDAG.en: some kind of crystalline stone, crystal; also a translucent substance with a silicate base, glass
BDAG.pt: algum tipo de pedra cristalina, cristal; também uma substância translúcida com base de silicato, vidro

DEFINITION: to run riot, to outrage, insult.
ORIGIN: From hubris; to exercise violence, i.e. Abuse.

BDAG.en: to treat in an insolent or spiteful manner, mistreat, scoff at, insult; abuse, outrage something
BDAG.pt: tratar de maneira insolente ou maliciosa, maltratar, escarnecer, insultar; abusar, ultrajar algo

DEFINITION: wantonness, insolence, an act of wanton violence.
ORIGIN: From huper; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. Insult, injury.

BDAG.en: 1 the quality or state of being insolent, insolence, arrogance, the act. sense 2 the experience of insolence, shame, insult, mistreatment, the pass. sense 3 damage caused by use of force, fig. hardship, disaster, damage caused by the elements
BDAG.pt: 1 a qualidade ou estado de ser insolente, insolência, arrogância, no sentido ativo 2 a experiência de insolência, vergonha, insulto, maus-tratos, no sentido passivo 3 dano causado pelo uso da força, fig. dificuldade, desastre, dano causado pelos elementos

DEFINITION: an insolent, insulting, or violent man.
ORIGIN: From hubrizo; an insulter, i.e. Maltreater.

BDAG.en: a violent, insolent pers.
BDAG.pt: uma pessoa violenta e insolente

DEFINITION: to be well, be in good health; to be right, reasonable, sound, pure, uncorrupted.
ORIGIN: From hugies; to have sound health, i.e. Be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine).
USAGE: be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).

BDAG.en: to be in good physical health, be healthy; as a formula in an epistolary greeting; to be sound or free from error, be correct, fig. in the Pastoral Epistles with reference to Christian teaching.
BDAG.pt: estar em boa saúde física, estar saudável; como fórmula em uma saudação epistolar; estar são ou livre de erro, ser correto, figurativamente nas Epístolas Pastorais com referência ao ensino cristão.

DEFINITION: (a) sound, healthy, pure, whole, (b) wholesome.
ORIGIN: From the base of auzano; healthy, i.e. Well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine).

BDAG.en: pert. to being physically well or sound, healthy, sound (of persons or members); sound, undamaged (of things); pert. to being uncorrupted or correct, fig. extension of 1, sound teaching or preaching.
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar fisicamente bem ou são, saudável, íntegro (de pessoas ou membros); são, sem danos (de coisas); pertencente a ser incorrupto ou correto, extensão figurada de 1, ensino ou pregação sã.

DEFINITION: wet, moist, of wood sappy.
ORIGIN: From the base of huetos; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh).

BDAG.en: pert. to being in a moist or yielding condition, moist, pliant, green (of fresh wood).
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar em uma condição úmida ou flexível, úmido, maleável, verde (de madeira fresca).

DEFINITION: a water pot, a pot or jar.
ORIGIN: From hudor; a water-jar, i.e. Receptacle for family supply.

BDAG.en: water jar
BDAG.pt: jarro de água

DEFINITION: to be only a water drinker.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hudor and a derivative of pino; to be a water-drinker, i.e. To abstain from vinous beverages.

BDAG.en: to prefer water for drinking, drink (only) water, indicative of an abstemious way of life.
BDAG.pt: preferir água para beber, beber (somente) água, indicativo de um modo de vida abstêmio.

DEFINITION: afflicted with dropsy.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hudor and a derivative of optanomai (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical".

BDAG.en: suffering from dropsy, edema.
BDAG.pt: sofrendo de hidropisia, edema.

DEFINITION: water.
ORIGIN: And genitive case, hudatos (hoo'-dat-os), etc. From the base of huetos; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: water. 1 in a material sense, as an element (of the ocean, the earth, the deluge, water for washing, water from a spring, etc.). 2 transcendent life-giving medium, water, figuratively.
BDAG.pt: água. 1 em sentido material, como um elemento (do oceano, da terra, do dilúvio, água para lavar, água de uma nascente, etc.). 2 meio transcendente que dá vida, água, figurativamente.

DEFINITION: rain.
ORIGIN: From a primary huo (to rain); rain, especially a shower.

BDAG.en: rain
BDAG.pt: chuva

DEFINITION: adoption, as a son into the divine family.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of huios and a derivative of tithemi; the placing as a son, i.e. Adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God).

BDAG.en: adoption, lit. a legal term; in our lit. only in a transferred sense of a transcendent filial relationship between God and humans: acceptance of Israel as God’s son, or acceptance of believers as God’s children with full rights.
BDAG.pt: adoção, literalmente um termo legal; em nossa literatura apenas em sentido translativo de um relacionamento filial transcendente entre Deus e os humanos: aceitação de Israel como filho de Deus, ou aceitação dos crentes como filhos de Deus com plenos direitos.

DEFINITION: a son, descendent.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship.

BDAG.en: prim. 'son': 1 a male who is in a kinship relationship (direct male issue, animal offspring, descendant); one who is legally adopted as a son. 2 a person related or closely associated as if by ties of sonship (pupil, follower, spiritual son); individual member of a coherent group; one whose identity is defined by relationship (e.g., sons of Abraham, sons of God, sons of the devil).
BDAG.pt: primariamente 'filho': 1 um homem que está em uma relação de parentesco (descendência masculina direta, descendência animal, descendente); aquele que é legalmente adotado como filho. 2 uma pessoa relacionada ou intimamente associada como por laços de filiação (aluno, seguidor, filho espiritual); membro individual de um grupo coerente; aquele cuja identidade é definida por um relacionamento (ex: filhos de Abraão, filhos de Deus, filhos do diabo).

DEFINITION: wood, timber, forest.
ORIGIN: Perhaps akin to xulon; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel.

BDAG.en: a dense growth of trees, forest; the woody part of a tree, wood, pile of wood, wood used for building, etc.; the stuff out of which a thing is made, material, matter, stuff (in our literature only earthly, perishable, non-divine matter... Humans, too, are made of such material; with connotation of that which is sinful, hostile to God)
BDAG.pt: crescimento denso de árvores, floresta; a parte lenhosa de uma árvore, lenha, pilha de madeira, madeira usada para construção, etc.; a matéria da qual algo é feito, material, substância (em nossa literatura apenas matéria terrena, perecível, não divina... Os seres humanos também são feitos desse material; com conotação daquilo que é pecaminoso, hostil a Deus)

DEFINITION: you.
ORIGIN: Accusative case of humeis; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition).

DEFINITION: you.
ORIGIN: Irregular plural of su; you (as subjective of verb).

BDAG.en: you (plural)
BDAG.pt: vós / vocês (plural)

DEFINITION: Hymenaeus, a heretical teacher at Ephesus.
ORIGIN: From Humen (the god of weddings); "hymeneal"; Hymeneus, an opponent of Christianity.

BDAG.en: Hymenaeus, handed over (with Alexander) to Satan because of defection from the true faith
BDAG.pt: Himenaios, entregue (com Alexandre) a Satanás por causa da deserção da fé verdadeira

DEFINITION: your, yours.
ORIGIN: From humeis; yours, i.e. Pertaining to you.

BDAG.en: possessive adjectival pronoun of the second person plural ‘your’ (largely replaced by the genitive of the personal pronoun); pertaining to persons addressed as possessors or recipients; your time; your teaching; your own property; one of your own number; by the mercy shown to you; by the pride that I have in you
BDAG.pt: pronome adjetivo possessivo da segunda pessoa do plural, 'vosso/seu'; pertencente a pessoas endereçadas como possuidores ou receptores; o vosso tempo; o vosso ensino; vossa própria propriedade; um dos vossos; pela misericórdia mostrada a vós; pelo orgulho que tenho em vós

DEFINITION: you.
ORIGIN: Irregular dative case of humeis; to (with or by) you.

DEFINITION: to sing, sing hymns to, praise.
ORIGIN: From humnos; to hymn, i.e. Sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song.

BDAG.en: to sing a song in a cultic setting, especially of praise and celebration; sing in praise to, sing in praise of someone (God); sing (a hymn)
BDAG.pt: cantar um cântico em um contexto cultual, especialmente de louvor e celebração; cantar em louvor a, cantar o louvor de alguém (Deus); cantar (um hino)

DEFINITION: a hymn, sacred song, song of praise to God.
ORIGIN: Apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of hudeo (to celebrate; probably akin to aido; compare abowt); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms).

BDAG.en: a song with religious content, hymn/song of praise esp. in honor of a deity
BDAG.pt: um cântico com conteúdo religioso, hino/cântico de louvor especialmente em honra a uma divindade

DEFINITION: you.
ORIGIN: Genitive case of humeis; of (from or concerning) you.

DEFINITION: to lead or bring under, to lead on slowly, to depart.
ORIGIN: From hupo and ago; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. Withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: go away, withdraw, go; to leave someone's presence, go away; to be on the move, especially in a certain direction; used especially of Christ and his going to the Father
BDAG.pt: ir embora, retirar-se, ir; deixar a presença de alguém, ir embora; estar em movimento, especialmente em certa direção; usado especialmente de Cristo e sua ida ao Pai

DEFINITION: obedience, submissiveness, compliance.
ORIGIN: From hupakouo; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission.

BDAG.en: a state of being in compliance, obedience (one listens and follows instructions) a gener., the obedience which every slave owes his master... predom. of obedience to God and God’s commands, abs. (opp. ἁμαρτία)... obediently, in obedience (toward God)... Of Christ’s obedience... subjective gen. of Christ’s obedience to God... of human beings’ obedience to the will of God as expressed in the gospel... of obedience to God’s chosen representatives, the apostle and his emissaries... the objective gen. obedience to Christ... reply made to a question, answer
BDAG.pt: um estado de conformidade, obediência (ouve e segue instruções) de forma geral, a obediência que todo escravo deve ao seu mestre... predomina a obediência a Deus e aos mandamentos de Deus, absoluta (oposto a ἁμαρτία)... obedientemente, em obediência (para com Deus)... Da obediência de Cristo... genitivo subjetivo da obediência de Cristo a Deus... da obediência dos seres humanos à vontade de Deus conforme expressa no evangelho... da obediência aos representantes escolhidos por Deus, o apóstolo e seus emissários... o genitivo objetivo da obediência a Cristo... resposta dada a uma pergunta, réplica

DEFINITION: to listen, hearken to, obey, answer.
ORIGIN: From hupo and akouo; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. To listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority.

BDAG.en: to follow instructions, obey, follow, be subject to... to be in compliance... to grant one’s request, hear (of God)... to answer a knock at the door, technically of the door-keeper, whose duty it is to listen for the signals of those who wish to enter, and to admit them if they are entitled to do so: open or answer (the door)
BDAG.pt: seguir instruções, obedecer, seguir, estar sujeito a... estar em conformidade... atender a um pedido, ouvir (de Deus)... atender a uma batida na porta, tecnicamente do porteiro, cujo dever é escutar os sinais daqueles que desejam entrar e admiti-los se tiverem direito: abrir ou atender (a porta)

DEFINITION: under the power of or subject to a man.
ORIGIN: From hupo and aner; in subjection under a man, i.e. A married woman.

BDAG.en: pert. to being legally bound to a man in marriage, married (the married woman)
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar legalmente ligada a um homem pelo casamento, casada (a mulher casada)

DEFINITION: to go to meet, to meet.
ORIGIN: From hupo and a derivative of anti; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. To encounter, fall in with.

BDAG.en: to go to meet someone a in a friendly sense meet... b in a hostile sense encounter, oppose
BDAG.pt: ir ao encontro de alguém a no sentido amigável, encontrar... b no sentido hostil, confrontar, opor-se

DEFINITION: a going to meet.
ORIGIN: From hupantao; an encounter or concurrence (with eis for infinitive, in order to fall in with).

BDAG.en: coming to meet... in our lit. only in the expr. to meet someone, and in a positive sense
BDAG.pt: vir ao encontro... em nossa literatura apenas na expressão ir ao encontro de alguém, e em sentido positivo

DEFINITION: goods, substance, property, possessions.
ORIGIN: From huparcho; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth.

BDAG.en: state or condition of existing or staying in existence, existence, subsistence... that which one has, property, possession. Pl. possessions, belongings
BDAG.pt: estado ou condição de existir ou permanecer em existência, existência, subsistência... aquilo que se tem, propriedade, posse. Plural: posses, pertences

DEFINITION: goods, that which one has, things which one possesseth, substance, that hast.
ORIGIN: Neuter plural of present participle active of huparcho as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. Property or possessions.
USAGE: goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.

DEFINITION: to begin, to be ready or at hand, to be.
ORIGIN: From hupo and archomai; to begin under (quietly), i.e. Come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb).

BDAG.en: to really be there, exist, be present, be at one’s disposal... to be in a state or circumstance, be as a widely used substitute in H. Gk. for εἶναι, but in some of the foll. pass. the sense ‘be inherently (so)’ or ‘be really’ cannot be excluded
BDAG.pt: estar realmente presente, existir, estar disponível... estar em um estado ou circunstância, ser um substituto amplamente usado no grego koiné para εἶναι, mas em algumas das passagens a seguir o sentido de ‘ser inerentemente (assim)’ ou ‘ser realmente’ não pode ser excluído

DEFINITION: to yield, submit to authority.
ORIGIN: From hupo and eiko (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender.

BDAG.en: prim. ‘withdraw, give way to’, then by fig. extension to yield to someone’s authority, yield, give way, submit
BDAG.pt: primariamente ‘retirar-se, ceder a’, depois por extensão figurada ceder à autoridade de alguém, ceder, render-se, submeter-se

DEFINITION: opposite to, adverse; subst: an adversary.
ORIGIN: From hupo and enantios; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. Opposed or (as noun) an opponent.

BDAG.en: mostly opposed, contrary, hostile (against someone). Subst. the opponent of God
BDAG.pt: majoritariamente oposto, contrário, hostil (contra alguém). Substantivado: o adversário de Deus

DEFINITION: over, beyond, on behalf of, for the sake of, concerning.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than.
USAGE: (+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very. In the comparative, it retains many of the above applications.

BDAG.en: a marker indicating that an activity or event is in some entity’s interest, for, in behalf of, for the sake of someone/someth.... after words that express a request, prayer, etc.... after words and expressions that denote working, caring, concerning oneself about... after expressions having to do w. sacrifice... gener. be for someone, be on someone’s side.... after expressions of suffering, dying, devoting oneself, etc. die for someone or someth.
BDAG.pt: um marcador indicando que uma atividade ou evento é de interesse de alguma entidade, para, em favor de, pelo bem de alguém/algo... após palavras que expressam um pedido, oração, etc.... após palavras e expressões que denotam trabalho, cuidado, preocupação com... após expressões relacionadas a sacrifício... geralmente significando ser a favor de alguém, estar do lado de alguém.... após expressões de sofrimento, morte, dedicação, etc. morrer por alguém ou algo

DEFINITION: lit: to raise beyond, uplift; mid: to lift myself up, exalt myself, be arrogant.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from huper and airo; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty.
USAGE: exalt self, be exalted above measure.

BDAG.en: to have an undue sense of one’s self-importance, rise up, exalt oneself, be elated
BDAG.pt: ter um senso exagerado de auto-importância, levantar-se, exaltar-se, ficar elado

DEFINITION: past the bloom of youth, of full age.
ORIGIN: From huper and the base of akmen; beyond the "acme", i.e. Figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth.

BDAG.en: past one’s prime, past marriageable age, past the bloom of youth OR at one’s sexual peak and may be applied to a woman or to a man, with strong passions
BDAG.pt: passado o auge, passado a idade de casar, passado o vigor da juventude OU no auge sexual, podendo ser aplicado à mulher ou ao homem, com paixões fortes

DEFINITION: (high) above.
ORIGIN: From huper and ano; above upward, i.e. Greatly higher (in place or rank).

BDAG.en: (high) above (functioning as a preposition with genitive)
BDAG.pt: (alto) acima (funcionando como preposição com genitivo)

DEFINITION: to increase exceedingly or beyond measure.
ORIGIN: From huper and auzano; to increase above ordinary degree.

BDAG.en: grow wonderfully, increase abundantly (figuratively, of faith)
BDAG.pt: crescer maravilhosamente, aumentar abundantemente (figurativamente, da fé)

DEFINITION: to transgress; to go beyond, overreach, defraud.
ORIGIN: From huper and the base of basis; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach.

BDAG.en: to go beyond a high point on a scale of linear extent, go beyond, transgress, break laws and commandments, trespass, sin
BDAG.pt: ultrapassar um ponto alto em uma escala de extensão linear, ir além, transgredir, violar leis e mandamentos, cometer transgressão, pecar

DEFINITION: beyond measure.
ORIGIN: Adverb from present participle active of huperballo; excessively.

BDAG.en: exceedingly, immeasurably, surpassingly, to a much greater degree
BDAG.pt: excessivamente, incomensuravelmente, ultrapassadoramente, em grau muito maior

DEFINITION: to throw over or beyond, to run beyond.
ORIGIN: From huper and ballo; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent).

BDAG.en: to attain a degree that extraordinarily exceeds a point on a scale of extent, go beyond, surpass, outdo, surpassing, extraordinary, outstanding
BDAG.pt: atingir um grau que excede extraordinariamente um ponto em uma escala de extensão, ir além, superar, sobressair, que excede, extraordinário, notável

DEFINITION: excess, surpassing excellence, preeminence; adv: exceedingly.
ORIGIN: From huperballo; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with eis or kata) pre- eminently.
USAGE: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.

BDAG.en: state of exceeding to an extraordinary degree a point on a scale of extent (excess, extraordinary quality/character); to an extraordinary degree, beyond measure, utterly
BDAG.pt: estado de exceder a um grau extraordinário um ponto em uma escala de extensão (excesso, qualidade/caráter extraordinário); extraordinariamente, além da medida, totalmente

DEFINITION: to overlook, take no notice of, disregard.
ORIGIN: From huper and eido; to overlook, i.e. Not punish.

BDAG.en: 2nd aorist of ὑπεροράω
BDAG.pt: 2º aoristo de ὑπεροράω

DEFINITION: beyond.
ORIGIN: From huper and the neuter plural of ekeinos; above those parts, i.e. Still farther.

BDAG.en: beyond (used with genitive)
BDAG.pt: além (usado com genitivo)

DEFINITION: to over-stretch, stretch out beyond the measure assigned to me.
ORIGIN: From huper and ekteino; to extend inordinately.

BDAG.en: stretch out beyond, we are overextending ourselves (beyond the limits set by God)
BDAG.pt: esticar além, estamos nos estendendo demais (além dos limites estabelecidos por Deus)

DEFINITION: to pour out so that it overflows.
ORIGIN: From huper and the alternate form of ekcheo; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow.

DEFINITION: to intercede for, make petition for.
ORIGIN: From huper and entugchano; to intercede in behalf of.

BDAG.en: to intercede in behalf of another, plead, intercede
BDAG.pt: interceder em favor de outro, suplicar, interceder

DEFINITION: to hold above, to rise above, to be superior.
ORIGIN: From huper and echo; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority.

BDAG.en: to be at a point higher than another on a scale of linear extent, rise above, surpass, excel, to be in a controlling position, have power over, be in authority (over), be highly placed, to surpass in quality or value, be better than, surpass, excel
BDAG.pt: estar em um ponto mais alto que outro em uma escala de extensão linear, erguer-se acima, superar, sobressair, estar em uma posição de controle, ter poder sobre, estar em autoridade (sobre), estar em posição elevada, superar em qualidade ou valor, ser melhor que, superar, sobressair

DEFINITION: pride, arrogance, disdain.
ORIGIN: From huperephanos; haughtiness.

BDAG.en: a state of undue sense of one’s importance bordering on insolence, arrogance, haughtiness, pride
BDAG.pt: um estado de senso indevido de importância beirando a insolência, arrogância, altivez, orgulho

DEFINITION: showing oneself above others.
ORIGIN: From huper and phaino; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty.

BDAG.en: arrogant, haughty, proud
BDAG.pt: arrogante, soberbo, orgulhoso

DEFINITION: to be more than conqueror, prevail mightily.
ORIGIN: From huper and nikao; to vanquish beyond, i.e. Gain a decisive victory.

BDAG.en: as a heightened form of νικᾶν prevail completely, we are winning a most glorious victory
BDAG.pt: como uma forma intensificada de vencer, prevalecer completamente, estamos vencendo uma vitória gloriosíssima

DEFINITION: immoderate, boastful, excessive, pompous.
ORIGIN: From huper and ogkos; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent.

BDAG.en: of excessive size, puffed up, swollen; also haughty, pompous, bombastic (of words)
BDAG.pt: de tamanho excessivo, inchado, enfatuado; também arrogante, pomposo, bombástico (de palavras)

DEFINITION: superiority, excellence, preeminence, authority.
ORIGIN: From huperecho; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character).

BDAG.en: projection, prominence; a state of excelling, superiority, preeminence; a state of high official rank, authority of prominent officials
BDAG.pt: projeção, proeminência; um estado de excelência, superioridade, preeminência; um estado de alta posição oficial, autoridade de oficiais proeminentes

DEFINITION: (a) intrans: to abound exceedingly, (b) dep: to overflow.
ORIGIN: From huper and perisseuo; to super-abound.

BDAG.en: to be very high on a scale of amount, be in great excess; intr. be present in (greater) abundance; to cause someone to superabound in someth., supply lavishly
BDAG.pt: estar muito alto em uma escala de quantidade, estar em grande excesso; intr. estar presente em (maior) abundância; fazer alguém superabundar em algo, suprir lavishly

DEFINITION: superabundantly, beyond measure.
ORIGIN: From huper and perissos; superabundantly, i.e. Exceedingly.

BDAG.en: beyond all measure
BDAG.pt: além de toda medida

DEFINITION: to abound exceedingly, be exceedingly abundant.
ORIGIN: From huper and pleonazo; to superabound.

BDAG.en: to experience extraordinary abundance, abound; of a vessel that becomes too full run over, overflow
BDAG.pt: experimentar abundância extraordinária, abundar; de um vaso que se enche demais, transbordar, inundar

DEFINITION: to exalt beyond measure.
ORIGIN: From huper and hupsoo; to elevate above others, i.e. Raise to the highest position.

BDAG.en: to raise to a high point of honor, raise, exalt; mid. raise oneself, rise
BDAG.pt: elevar a um alto ponto de honra, erguer, exaltar; meio. elevar-se, levantar-se

DEFINITION: to be overly proud, to have high thoughts.
ORIGIN: From huper and phroneo; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. Be vain or arrogant.

BDAG.en: think too highly of oneself, be haughty
BDAG.pt: pensar muito bem de si mesmo, ser arrogante

DEFINITION: an upper room, the upper part of a house.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of huper; a higher part of the house, i.e. Apartment in the third story.

BDAG.en: upper story, room upstairs, also of the tower-like room built on the flat roof of an oriental house
BDAG.pt: andar superior, cômodo no andar de cima, também do quarto em forma de torre construído no telhado plano de uma casa oriental

DEFINITION: to hold or put under, to undergo.
ORIGIN: From hupo and echo; to hold oneself under, i.e. Endure with patience.

BDAG.en: as a legal t.t. undergo punishment
BDAG.pt: como um termo legal, sofrer punição

DEFINITION: listening to, obedient, submissive.
ORIGIN: From hupakouo; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive.

BDAG.en: obedient
BDAG.pt: obediente

DEFINITION: to serve as a rower, to minister to, serve.
ORIGIN: From huperetes; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve.

BDAG.en: to render service, serve, be helpful
BDAG.pt: prestar serviço, servir, ser prestativo

DEFINITION: a servant, an attendant, (a) an officer, lictor, (b) an attendant in a synagogue, (c) a minister of the gospel.
ORIGIN: From hupo and a derivative of eresso (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable).

BDAG.en: one who functions as a helper, freq. in a subordinate capacity, helper, assistant (e.g. a physician’s assistant; the lictor beside the consul; attendants of a board or court; synagogue attendant; a king’s retinue; the apostles as assistants of Christ; believers generally as God’s servants/assistants)
BDAG.pt: aquele que funciona como ajudante, frequentemente em capacidade subordinada, auxiliar, assistente (ex: assistente de médico; o lictores ao lado do cônsul; assistentes de um conselho ou tribunal; atendente de sinagoga; comitiva de um rei; os apóstolos como assistentes de Cristo; crentes em geral como servos/auxiliares de Deus)

DEFINITION: sleep; fig: spiritual sleep.
ORIGIN: From an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to hupo through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor.

BDAG.en: sleep; in imagery wake from sleep, i.e. bid farewell to the works of darkness
BDAG.pt: sono; em imagens, acordar do sono, ou seja, despedir-se das obras das trevas

DEFINITION: by, under, about.
ORIGIN: A primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)).
USAGE: among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In the comparative, it retains the same general applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specially, covertly or moderately.

BDAG.en: prep. w. gen. marker of agency or cause, by; w. acc. a position below an object or another position, under, below; marker of that which is in a controlling position, under, under the control of, under obligation in ref. to power, rule, sovereignty, command, etc.; marker of the approximate time of a period, about
BDAG.pt: preposição com genitivo, marcador de agência ou causa, por; com acusativo, posição abaixo de um objeto ou outra posição, debaixo de, abaixo de; marcador daquilo que está em posição de controle, sob, sob o controle de, sob obrigação em relação a poder, domínio, soberania, comando, etc.; marcador do tempo aproximado de um período, por volta de

DEFINITION: to throw or put under; met: to subject, submit, suggest, whisper, prompt, suborn, instigate.
ORIGIN: From hupo and ballo; to throw in stealthily, i.e. Introduce by collusion.

BDAG.en: instigate (secretly), suborn someone/something
BDAG.pt: instigar (secretamente), subornar alguém/algo

DEFINITION: a writing-copy, an example, pattern.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hupo and grapho; an underwriting, i.e. Copy for imitation (figuratively).

BDAG.en: model, pattern to be copied in writing or drawing; a model of behavior, example
BDAG.pt: modelo, padrão a ser copiado na escrita ou desenho; um modelo de comportamento, exemplo

DEFINITION: (a) a figure, copy, (b) an example, model.
ORIGIN: From hupodeiknumi; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration).

BDAG.en: an example of behavior used for purposes of moral instruction, example, model, pattern (in a good sense); a warning example; an indication of someth. that appears at a subsequent time, outline, sketch, symbol
BDAG.pt: um exemplo de comportamento usado para fins de instrução moral, exemplo, modelo, padrão (em sentido positivo); um exemplo de advertência; uma indicação de algo que aparece em um tempo subsequente, esboço, rascunho, símbolo

DEFINITION: to show secretly, to show by tracing out, to teach, make known.
ORIGIN: From hupo and deiknuo; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish).

BDAG.en: show, indicate; to direct someone’s attention to something, indicate, point out; to give instruction or moral direction, show, give direction, prove, set forth
BDAG.pt: mostrar, indicar; direcionar a atenção de alguém para algo, indicar, apontar; dar instrução ou direção moral, mostrar, dar direção, provar, expor

DEFINITION: to receive as a guest, entertain hospitably, welcome.
ORIGIN: From hupo and dechomai; to admit under one's roof, i.e. Entertain hospitably.

BDAG.en: to receive hospitably, receive, welcome, entertain as a guest someone
BDAG.pt: receber hospitaleiramente, receber, dar as boas-vindas, entreter como hóspede alguém

DEFINITION: (lit: to bind under), mid: to put on feet, pass: to be shod.
ORIGIN: From hupo and deo; to bind under one's feet, i.e. Put on shoes or sandals.

BDAG.en: tie/bind beneath, put on, of footwear
BDAG.pt: atar/amarrar por baixo, calçar, no caso de calçados

DEFINITION: a sole bound under (the foot), a sandal.
ORIGIN: From hupodeo; something bound under the feet, i.e. A shoe or sandal.

BDAG.en: a leather sole that is fastened to the foot by means of straps, sandal
BDAG.pt: uma sola de couro que é presa ao pé por meio de tiras, sandália

DEFINITION: answerable to, liable to (brought under) the judgment of.
ORIGIN: From hupo and dike; under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned.

BDAG.en: pert. to being liable to judgment/punishment, answerable, accountable
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar sujeito a julgamento/punição, responsável, prestador de contas.

DEFINITION: a beast of burden, an ass or mule.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of hupo and zugos; an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey.

BDAG.en: draught animal, beast of burden (lit. ‘under the yoke’) hence ‘pack animal’ in our lit. donkey, ass
BDAG.pt: animal de tração, animal de carga (lit. ‘debaixo do jugo’) daí ‘animal de carga’; em nossa literatura, jumento, asno

DEFINITION: to under-gird, as to strengthen a ship against the waves.
ORIGIN: From hupo and zonnumi; to gird under, i.e. Frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck).

BDAG.en: undergird, brace, nautical t.t.: provide a ship w. cables that go around the outside of the hull, and under it, to give the ship greater firmness in a heavy sea
BDAG.pt: cingir, reforçar, termo náutico: prover um navio com cabos que passam pela parte externa do casco, e por baixo dele, para dar maior firmeza ao navio em mar agitado

DEFINITION: underneath, below, under.
ORIGIN: From hupo and kato; down under, i.e. Beneath.

BDAG.en: under, below (functions only as a prep. w. gen.)
BDAG.pt: debaixo, abaixo (funciona apenas como preposição com genitivo).

DEFINITION: to answer, reply, to answer on a stage, to pretend.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from hupo and krino; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend).

BDAG.en: pretend, make believe, dissemble. Abs. of behavior, to pretend to be someth. that one is not play a role, act a part, dissemble
BDAG.pt: fingir, fazer-se de, dissimular. Usado absolutamente em relação ao comportamento, fingir ser algo que não se é, desempenhar um papel, dissimular.

DEFINITION: (lit: stage-playing), a response, answer, hypocrisy, dissembling.
ORIGIN: From hupokrinomai; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy").

BDAG.en: in our lit. only in a neg. sense to create a public impression that is at odds with one’s real purposes or motivations, play-acting, pretense, outward show, dissembling (loanword in Engl. ‘hypocrisy’)
BDAG.pt: na nossa literatura apenas em sentido negativo, criar uma impressão pública que está em desacordo com os propósitos ou motivações reais, representação teatral, pretensão, aparência externa, dissimulação (empréstimo no inglês 'hipocrisia').

DEFINITION: (lit: a stage-player), a hypocrite, dissembler, pretender.
ORIGIN: From hupokrinomai; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite".

BDAG.en: in our lit. only metaph. actor, in the sense pretender, dissembler
BDAG.pt: na nossa literatura apenas metaforicamente ator, no sentido de simulador, dissimulador.

DEFINITION: (a) to take up, (b) to welcome, entertain, (c) to answer, (d) to suppose, imagine.
ORIGIN: From hupo and lambano; to take from below, i.e. Carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. Continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume).

BDAG.en: 1 to cause to ascend, take up. 2 to take someone under one’s care, receive as a guest, support. 3 to give an answer to what is said, reply. 4 to consider to be probable, assume, think, believe, be of the opinion (that), suppose
BDAG.pt: 1 fazer ascender, levar para cima. 2 tomar alguém sob seus cuidados, receber como hóspede, apoiar. 3 dar uma resposta ao que é dito, replicar. 4 considerar provável, assumir, pensar, crer, ser da opinião (de que), supor.

DEFINITION: to leave behind; pass: to be left surviving.
ORIGIN: From hupotrecho and leipo; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive).

BDAG.en: leave remaining pass. be left (remaining)
BDAG.pt: deixar remanescente; passivo ser deixado (restante).

DEFINITION: a vessel or trough beneath a winepress (to receive the juice).
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed compound of hupo and lenos; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. Lower wine-vat.

BDAG.en: a trough placed beneath the wine-press to hold the wine, wine trough, vat
BDAG.pt: um tonel colocado debaixo do lagar para receber o vinho, tina de vinho, tanque.

DEFINITION: to leave behind.
ORIGIN: A prolonged form for hupoleipo; to leave behind, i.e. Bequeath.

BDAG.en: to cause to remain subsequent to some temporal reference point, leave, leave behind
BDAG.pt: causar a permanecer subsequente a algum ponto de referência temporal, deixar, deixar para trás

DEFINITION: (a) to remain behind, (b) to stand ground, show endurance, (c) to endure, bear up against, persevere.
ORIGIN: From hupo and meno; to stay under (behind), i.e. Remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. Bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere.
USAGE: abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.

BDAG.en: 1 to stay in a place beyond an expected point of time, remain/stay (behind), while others go away. 2 to maintain a belief or course of action in the face of opposition, stand one’s ground, hold out, endure. 3 to wait for with persistence, wait for
BDAG.pt: 1 ficar em um lugar além de um tempo esperado, permanecer/ficar (para trás), enquanto outros partem. 2 manter uma crença ou curso de ação diante da oposição, manter-se firme, aguentar, perseverar. 3 esperar com persistência, aguardar.

DEFINITION: to remind; pass: to remember, call to mind.
ORIGIN: From hupo and mimnesko; to remind quietly, i.e. Suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory.
USAGE: put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.

BDAG.en: 1 to put another in mind of someth., act. a remind. b call to mind, bring up. 2 to recollect for oneself, pass. w. act. sense remember, think of
BDAG.pt: 1 colocar outra pessoa em mente de algo, ativamente a. lembrar. b trazer à memória, evocar. 2 recordar para si mesmo, passivo com sentido ativo, lembrar, pensar em.

DEFINITION: remembrance, recollection, putting in mind; a reminder.
ORIGIN: From hupomimnesko; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection.

BDAG.en: the act of calling to someone’s mind, reminding; the act of remembering, remembrance
BDAG.pt: o ato de trazer à mente de alguém, o ato de lembrar; o ato de recordar, recordação

DEFINITION: endurance, steadfastness, patient waiting for.
ORIGIN: From hupomeno; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy.

BDAG.en: the capacity to hold out or bear up in the face of difficulty, patience, endurance, fortitude, steadfastness, perseverance; the act or state of patient waiting for someone or someth., expectation
BDAG.pt: a capacidade de resistir ou suportar diante da dificuldade, paciência, resistência, fortaleza, firmeza, perseverança; o ato ou estado de espera paciente por alguém ou algo, expectativa

DEFINITION: to conjecture, suppose, suspect, deem.
ORIGIN: From hupo and noieo; to think under (privately), i.e. To surmise or conjecture.

BDAG.en: to form an opinion or conjecture on the basis of slight evidence, suspect, suppose
BDAG.pt: formar uma opinião ou conjectura com base em pouca evidência, suspeitar, supor

DEFINITION: a supposition, suspicion.
ORIGIN: From huponoeo; suspicion.

BDAG.en: opinion or conjecture based on slight evidence, suspicion, conjecture
BDAG.pt: opinião ou conjectura baseada em pouca evidência, suspeita, conjectura

DEFINITION: to sail under (i.e. under the lee of).
ORIGIN: From hupo and pleo; to sail under the lee of.

BDAG.en: sail under the lee of an island, i.e. in such a way that the island protects the ship fr. the wind
BDAG.pt: navegar sob o lado abrigado de uma ilha, isto é, de tal forma que a ilha proteja o navio do vento

DEFINITION: to blow underneath.
ORIGIN: From hupo and pneo; to breathe gently, i.e. Breeze.

BDAG.en: blow gently
BDAG.pt: soprar suavemente

DEFINITION: a footstool.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of hupo and pous; something under the feet, i.e. A foot-rest (figuratively).

BDAG.en: footstool; of the earth as God’s footstool; make someone a footstool for someone, i.e. subject one pers. to another
BDAG.pt: escabelo (banquinho para os pés); da terra como escabelo de Deus; fazer alguém um escabelo para alguém, isto é, sujeitar uma pessoa a outra

DEFINITION: (lit: an underlying), (a) confidence, assurance, (b) a giving substance (or reality) to, or a guaranteeing, (c) substance, reality.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hupo and histemi; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively).

BDAG.en: the essential or basic structure/nature of an entity, substantial nature, essence, actual being, reality; a plan that one devises for action, plan, project, undertaking, endeavor; the interp. situation, condition, also specif. frame of mind; guarantee of ownership/entitlement, title deed
BDAG.pt: a estrutura/natureza essencial ou básica de uma entidade, natureza substancial, essência, ser atual, realidade; um plano que se elabora para a ação, plano, projeto, empreendimento, esforço; a situação de interpretação, condição, também especificamente estado de espírito; garantia de posse/direito, título de propriedade

DEFINITION: to withdraw, draw back, keep back, shun, conceal.
ORIGIN: From hupo and stello; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve).

BDAG.en: 1. to draw back or disappear from a position (act. draw back, withdraw; mid. draw back); 2. to be hesitant in regard to someth. (mid. shrink back; shrink from, avoid; be timid about, keep silent about)
BDAG.pt: 1. retrair-se ou desaparecer de uma posição (ativo: retrair-se, retirar-se; médio: retrair-se); 2. hesitar em relação a algo (médio: recuar; afastar-se, evitar; ser tímido sobre, calar sobre)

DEFINITION: a letting down, a shrinking back.
ORIGIN: From hupostello; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy.

BDAG.en: the state of being timid, hesitancy, timidity.
BDAG.pt: o estado de ser tímido, hesitação, timidez.

DEFINITION: to turn back, return.
ORIGIN: From hupo and strepho; to turn under (behind), i.e. To return (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).

BDAG.en: turn back, return
BDAG.pt: virar para trás, retornar

DEFINITION: to spread under, strew under.
ORIGIN: From hupo and stronnumi; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet).

DEFINITION: subjection, submission, obedience.
ORIGIN: From hupotasso; subordination.

BDAG.en: the state of submissiveness, subjection, subordination, as opposed to setting oneself up as controller
BDAG.pt: o estado de submissão, sujeição, subordinação, em oposição a se colocar como controlador

DEFINITION: to place under, subject to; mid, pass: to submit, put myself into subjection.
ORIGIN: From hupo and tasso; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey.
USAGE: be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.

BDAG.en: to cause to be in a submissive relationship, to subject, to subordinate; pass. become subject, be subjected or subordinated, obey; subject oneself to someone; of submission involving recognition of an ordered structure (to a husband, parents, secular authorities, God, etc.).
BDAG.pt: causar um relacionamento de submissão, sujeitar, subordinar; na voz passiva, tornar-se sujeito, ser submetido ou subordinado, obedecer; sujeitar-se a alguém; de submissão que envolve o reconhecimento de uma estrutura ordenada (a um marido, pais, autoridades seculares, Deus, etc.).

DEFINITION: to put under, lay down, suggest to, put in mind.
ORIGIN: From hupo and tithemi; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest.

BDAG.en: to lay something down as expression of service, lay down; mid. to provide instruction, make known, teach something to someone.
BDAG.pt: depositar algo como expressão de serviço, depor; na voz média, fornecer instrução, fazer saber, ensinar algo a alguém.

DEFINITION: to run under shelter of.
ORIGIN: From hupo and trecho (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past.

BDAG.en: to run or sail under the lee of (nautical term).
BDAG.pt: correr ou navegar sob a proteção de (termo náutico).

DEFINITION: a pattern, example; a form, sample.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hupo and a derivative of tupos; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation.

BDAG.en: a pattern as a model prototype; as a basis for behavioral comparison standard.
BDAG.pt: um padrão como modelo, protótipo; como base para comparação de comportamento, padrão.

DEFINITION: to bear by being under, to endure.
ORIGIN: From hupo and phero; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship.

BDAG.en: to bear up under trouble or difficulty, submit to, endure; to bear something for the benefit of another, bear, bring, effect.
BDAG.pt: suportar problemas ou dificuldades, submeter-se, aguentar; suportar algo para benefício de outro, carregar, trazer, efetuar.

DEFINITION: to withdraw, retire, go back, retreat.
ORIGIN: From hupo and choreo; to vacate down, i.e. Retire quietly.

BDAG.en: of persons: to withdraw from a location, to go off, go away, retire; of things: to move from a position, move away.
BDAG.pt: de pessoas: retirar-se de um lugar, ir embora, afastar-se, retirar-se; de coisas: mover-se de uma posição, afastar-se.

DEFINITION: to strike under the eye, hence: to bruise, treat severely, discipline by hardship, molest, annoy, harass, worry, exhaust.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hupo and a derivative of optanomai; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions).

BDAG.en: to blacken an eye, give a black eye, strike in the face; to bring someone to submission by constant annoyance, wear down, or figuratively, slander/besmirch; to put under strict discipline, punish, treat roughly, torment.
BDAG.pt: esmurrar o olho, dar um olho roxo, bater no rosto; levar alguém à submissão por constante aborrecimento, desgastar, ou figurativamente, caluniar/difamar; submeter a disciplina rigorosa, punir, tratar com rudeza, atormentar.

DEFINITION: a hog, boar, or sow.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine").

BDAG.en: the female of the swine, sow.
BDAG.pt: a fêmea do porco, a porca.

DEFINITION: hyssop, a stalk or stem of hyssop.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin ('ezowb); "hyssop".

BDAG.en: the hyssop (a small bush w. blue flowers and highly aromatic leaves; used in purificatory sacrifices)
BDAG.pt: o hissopo (um pequeno arbusto com flores azuis e folhas altamente aromáticas; usado em sacrifícios de purificação)

DEFINITION: to fall behind, be lacking, fall short, suffer need, be inferior to.
ORIGIN: From husteros; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient).
USAGE: come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.

BDAG.en: to miss out on something through one’s own fault, to miss, fail to reach; to be in short supply, fail, give out, lack; to be in need, be needy, lack; to be lower in status, be less than, inferior to; to experience deficiency in something advantageous or desirable, lack, be lacking, go without, come short of.
BDAG.pt: perder algo por culpa própria, falhar, não alcançar; estar em escassez, falhar, esgotar-se, faltar; estar necessitado, ser carente, carecer; ser de status inferior, ser menor que, inferior a; experimentar deficiência em algo vantajoso ou desejável, carecer, faltar, passar sem, ficar aquém.

DEFINITION: (a) of things or persons: that which is lacking, a defect or shortcoming, (b) want, poverty.
ORIGIN: From hustereo; a deficit; specially, poverty.
USAGE: that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.

BDAG.en: the lack of what is needed or desirable, need, want, deficiency; used often with verbs meaning to supply or make up for a need.
BDAG.pt: a falta daquilo que é necessário ou desejável, necessidade, carência, deficiência; usado frequentemente com verbos que significam suprir ou compensar uma necessidade.

DEFINITION: poverty, want, need.
ORIGIN: A falling short, i.e. (specially), penury.

BDAG.en: the condition of lacking that which is essential, need, lack, poverty
BDAG.pt: a condição de carecer do que é essencial, necessidade, falta, pobreza

DEFINITION: lastly, afterward, later.
ORIGIN: Neuter of husteros as adverb; more lately, i.e. Eventually.

DEFINITION: later, latter, last.
ORIGIN: Comparative from hupo (in the sense of behind); later.

BDAG.en: pert. to being subsequent in a series, the second one, the latter; pert. to a point of time that is subsequent to another point of time, later, then, thereafter, finally, last
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser subsequente numa série, o segundo, o último (no sentido de posterior); relativo a um ponto no tempo subsequente a outro ponto no tempo, mais tarde, então, depois, finalmente, por último

DEFINITION: woven.
ORIGIN: From huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted.

BDAG.en: woven
BDAG.pt: tecido

DEFINITION: high, lofty.
ORIGIN: From hupsos; lofty (in place or character).

BDAG.en: pert. to considerable extension upward, tall, high; pert. to being arrogant, exalted, proud, haughty; pert. to being of high quality, noble, sublime
BDAG.pt: pertencente a uma considerável extensão para cima, alto, elevado; pertencente a ser arrogante, exaltado, orgulhoso, altivo; pertencente a ser de alta qualidade, nobre, sublime

DEFINITION: to be high-minded, proud.
ORIGIN: From a compound of hupselos and phren; to be lofty in mind, i.e. Arrogant.

BDAG.en: be proud, haughty
BDAG.pt: ser orgulhoso, altivo

DEFINITION: highest, most high, the heights.
ORIGIN: Superlative from the base of hupsos; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens.

BDAG.en: pert. to being the highest in a spatial sense, highest (heaven); pert. to being the highest in status, the Most High of God
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser o mais alto num sentido espacial, o mais alto (céu); relativo a ser o mais alto em status, o Altíssimo (de Deus)

DEFINITION: height, heaven; dignity, eminence.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of huper; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity.

BDAG.en: height; extent or distance upward; high place, mostly heaven; position of high status, high position; a lofty opinion of oneself, pride, arrogance.
BDAG.pt: altura; extensão ou distância para cima; lugar alto, na maioria das vezes o céu; posição de alto status, posição elevada; uma opinião elevada de si mesmo, orgulho, arrogância.

DEFINITION: (a) to raise on high, lift up, (b) to exalt, set on high.
ORIGIN: From hupsos; to elevate (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: to lift up spatially, lift up, raise high; to cause enhancement in honor, fame, position, power, or fortune, exalt; exalt oneself, consider oneself better than others.
BDAG.pt: levantar espacialmente, levantar, elevar no alto; causar aumento em honra, fama, posição, poder ou fortuna, exaltar; exaltar-se, considerar-se melhor que os outros.

DEFINITION: height, barrier, bulwark; presumption.
ORIGIN: From hupsoo; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively).

BDAG.en: as an astronomical term: the space above the horizon, the world above; that which postures arrogantly, arrogance, everything that rises up.
BDAG.pt: como um termo astronômico: o espaço acima do horizonte, o mundo superior; aquilo que se porta arrogantemente, arrogância, tudo o que se eleva.

DEFINITION: a glutton.
ORIGIN: From phago; a glutton.

BDAG.en: glutton.
BDAG.pt: glutão.

DEFINITION: to eat, partake of food; met: to devour, consume (e.g. as rust does); used only in fut. and 2nd aor. tenses.
ORIGIN: A primary verb (used as an alternate of esthio in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively).

DEFINITION: (a) act: to shine, shed light, (b) pass: to shine, become visible, appear, (c) to become clear, appear, seem, show myself as.
ORIGIN: Prolongation for the base of phos; to lighten (shine), i.e. Show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative).
USAGE: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.

BDAG.en: to shine or to produce light, shine; to become visible, appear; to become known, be recognized, be apparent, be revealed; to be known by appearance as opposed to underlying reality, appear as someth., appear to be someth.; to make an impression on the mind, have the appearance, seem
BDAG.pt: brilhar ou produzir luz, reluzir; tornar-se visível, aparecer; tornar-se conhecido, ser reconhecido, ser aparente, ser revelado; parecer algo em oposição à realidade subjacente; dar a impressão, ter a aparência, parecer

DEFINITION: Peleg, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Peleg); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch.

BDAG.en: Peleg, son of Eber and father of Reu
BDAG.pt: Pelegue, filho de Héber e pai de Reu

DEFINITION: apparent, clear, visible, manifest; adv: clearly.
ORIGIN: From phaino; shining, i.e. Apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally.
USAGE: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).

BDAG.en: pert. to being evident so as to be readily known, visible, clear, plainly to be seen, open, plain, evident, known; that which is exposed to general view or knowledge, (in) the open, public notice
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser evidente de modo a ser prontamente conhecido, visível, claro, facilmente visto, aberto, manifesto, evidente, conhecido; aquilo que está exposto à vista ou conhecimento geral, em público

DEFINITION: to make clear (visible, manifest), make known.
ORIGIN: From phaneros; to render apparent (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: cause to become visible, reveal, expose publicly; cause to become known, disclose, show, make known; become public knowledge, be disclosed, become known; show or reveal oneself; be made known.
BDAG.pt: fazer ficar visível, revelar, expor publicamente; fazer saber, desvendar, mostrar, tornar conhecido; tornar-se de conhecimento público, ser revelado, tornar-se sabido; mostrar-se ou revelar-se; ser tornado conhecido.

DEFINITION: clearly, openly, manifestly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from phaneros; plainly, i.e. Clearly or publicly.

BDAG.en: in plain view, openly, publicly; in sharp visual focus, clearly, distinctly; in a readily understood manner, clearly, plainly.
BDAG.pt: em plena vista, abertamente, publicamente; em foco visual nítido, claramente, distintamente; de maneira facilmente compreensível, clara e evidentemente.

DEFINITION: a manifestation, disclosure.
ORIGIN: From phaneroo; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment.

BDAG.en: disclosure, announcement.
BDAG.pt: revelação, anúncio.

DEFINITION: a torch, lantern, light.
ORIGIN: From phaino; a lightener, i.e. Light; lantern.

BDAG.en: a portable light, lamp (later, lantern).
BDAG.pt: uma luz portátil, lâmpada (mais tarde, lanterna).

DEFINITION: Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Pnuw'el); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Phanuel, father of Hanna(h)/Anna, a prophet
BDAG.pt: Fanuel, pai de Hanna(h)/Ana, um profeta

DEFINITION: to make visible, to become visible.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of phaino; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle).

BDAG.en: to become visible, appear (esp. of extraordinary phenomena); sight, spectacle, of a theophany
BDAG.pt: tornar-se visível, aparecer (especialmente de fenômenos extraordinários); visão, espetáculo, de uma teofania

DEFINITION: show, display, pomp, imagination.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of phantazo; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy").

BDAG.en: pomp, pageantry.
BDAG.pt: pompa, aparato.

DEFINITION: an apparition, ghost, spirit, phantom.
ORIGIN: From phantazo; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. Spectre.

BDAG.en: apparition, esp. ghost.
BDAG.pt: aparição, especialmente fantasma.

DEFINITION: a valley, ravine, chasm, cleft.
ORIGIN: Properly, strengthened from the base of peran or rather of rhegnumi; a gap or chasm, i.e. Ravine (winter-torrent).

BDAG.en: ravine, but also valley.
BDAG.pt: ravina, mas também vale.

DEFINITION: Pharaoh, the title of ancient Egyptian kings.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (Par'oh); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king.

BDAG.en: Pharaoh, title of Egyptian kings.
BDAG.pt: Faraó, título de reis egípcios.

DEFINITION: Perez, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Perets); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite.

BDAG.en: Perez, son of the patriarch Judah and of Tamar.
BDAG.pt: Perez, filho do patriarca Judá e de Tamar.

DEFINITION: a Pharisee, member of a Jewish religious sect.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (compare parash); a separatist, i.e. Exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary.

BDAG.en: Pharisee, member of the organized followers of the experts in interpreting the scriptures (scribes).
BDAG.pt: Fariseu, membro dos seguidores organizados dos especialistas na interpretação das escrituras (escribas).

DEFINITION: the use of medicine, drugs or spells.
ORIGIN: From pharmakeus; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: sorcery, magic; magic arts
BDAG.pt: feitiçaria, magia; artes mágicas

DEFINITION: sorcerer.
ORIGIN: From pharmakon (a drug, i.e. Spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician.

BDAG.en: maker of potions, magician
BDAG.pt: fabricante de poções, mágico

DEFINITION: a poisoner, sorcerer, magician.
ORIGIN: The same as pharmakeus.

BDAG.en: one skilled in arcane uses of herbs or drugs, probably poisoner; one who does extraordinary things through occult means, sorcerer, magician
BDAG.pt: aquele versado no uso arcano de ervas ou drogas, provavelmente envenenador; aquele que faz coisas extraordinárias por meios ocultos, feiticeiro, mágico

DEFINITION: report, tidings, information.
ORIGIN: From phemi (not the same as "phase", which is from phaino); a saying, i.e. Report.

BDAG.en: information concerning a crime, then generally information concerning a person or event, report, announcement, news
BDAG.pt: informação sobre um crime, depois, geralmente, informação sobre uma pessoa ou evento, relatório, anúncio, notícia

DEFINITION: to assert, affirm, profess.
ORIGIN: Prolongation from the same as phemi; to assert.

BDAG.en: to state something with confidence, say, assert, claim
BDAG.pt: afirmar algo com confiança, dizer, assertar, alegar

DEFINITION: a manger, feeding-trough, stall.
ORIGIN: From pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder).

BDAG.en: manger, crib; could possibly mean a stable or a feeding-place
BDAG.pt: manjedoura, cocho; pode significar um estábulo ou um lugar de alimentação

DEFINITION: worthless, wicked, base.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked.

BDAG.en: low-grade or morally substandard, base; relatively inferior in quality, ordinary
BDAG.pt: de baixa qualidade ou moralmente inferior, vil; relativamente inferior em qualidade, comum

DEFINITION: brightness, light, splendor, radiance.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to the base of phos (compare phtheggomai); brilliancy.

BDAG.en: light, radiance, of the moon
BDAG.pt: luz, claridade, da lua

DEFINITION: to spare, abstain, forbear.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently.

BDAG.en: to save from loss or discomfort, spare; to abstain from doing something, refrain
BDAG.pt: salvar de perda ou desconforto, poupar; abster-se de fazer algo, refrear

DEFINITION: sparingly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from participle of pheidomai; abstemiously, i.e. Stingily.

BDAG.en: in a scanty or meager manner, sparingly
BDAG.pt: de maneira escassa ou mesquinha, parcimoniosamente

DEFINITION: a mantle, cloak.
ORIGIN: By transposition for a derivative probably of phaino (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout).

DEFINITION: to carry, bear, bring; to conduct, lead; perhaps: to make publicly known.
ORIGIN: A primary verb.
USAGE: for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, oio (oy'-o); and enegko (en-eng'-ko) to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows)

BDAG.en: to move an object to a particular point, put, place; to cause to continue in a state or condition, sustain; to afford passage to a place, lead to; to bring a thought or idea into circulation, bring, utter, make a word, speech, announcement, charge, etc.; to demonstrate the reality of something, establish; to hold out in the face of difficulty, bear patiently, endure, put up with; to be productive, bear, produce.
BDAG.pt: mover um objeto a um ponto particular, pôr, colocar; fazer com que algo continue em um estado ou condição, sustentar; proporcionar passagem a um lugar, conduzir a; trazer uma ideia ou pensamento à circulação, trazer, proferir, fazer uma palavra, discurso, anúncio, ordem, etc.; demonstrar a realidade de algo, estabelecer; aguentar diante da dificuldade, suportar pacientemente, suportar, aguentar; ser produtivo, dar fruto, produzir.

DEFINITION: to flee, escape, shun.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish.

BDAG.en: to seek safety in flight, flee; to become safe from danger by eluding or avoiding it, escape; to keep from doing something by avoiding it because of its potential damage, flee from, avoid, shun, fig. ext. of 1, and in a moral sense; to cease being visible, vanish, disappear.
BDAG.pt: buscar segurança em fuga, fugir; tornar-se seguro de um perigo iludindo ou evitando-o, escapar; abster-se de fazer algo evitando-o por causa de seu potencial dano, fugir de, evitar, esquivar-se, sentido figurado e moral; deixar de ser visível, desaparecer, sumir.

DEFINITION: Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix, procurator of the Roman province Judea from an uncertain date (before A.D. 52 ?) till A.D. 59.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman.

BDAG.en: Antonius Felix, a freedman of the House of the Claudians and brother of Pallas, the favorite of the Emperor Claudius. In 52/53 a.d. F. became procurator of Palestine.
BDAG.pt: Antônio Félix, um liberto da Casa dos Cláudios e irmão de Pálas, o favorito do Imperador Cláudio. Em 52/53 d.C., F. tornou-se procurador da Judeia.

DEFINITION: a report, fame, saying.
ORIGIN: From phemi; a saying, i.e. Rumor ("fame").

BDAG.en: report, news.
BDAG.pt: relato, notícia.

DEFINITION: to declare, say.
ORIGIN: Properly, the same as the base of phos and phaino; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. Speak or say.

BDAG.en: to state something orally or in writing, say, affirm; to say something that provides a fuller explanation of a statement, mean by one’s statement.
BDAG.pt: afirmar algo oralmente ou por escrito, dizer, asseverar; dizer algo que fornece uma explicação mais completa de uma declaração, querer dizer com a sua declaração.

DEFINITION: Festus, a governor of Judea.
ORIGIN: Of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman.

BDAG.en: Porcius Festus, successor to Felix as procurator of Palestine
BDAG.pt: Pórcio Festo, sucessor de Félix como procurador da Palestina

DEFINITION: (a) to anticipate, precede, (b) to come, arrive.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. Anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at.

BDAG.en: to be beforehand in moving to a position, come before, precede; to get to or reach a position, have just arrived, then simply arrive, reach; to come to or arrive at a particular state, attain.
BDAG.pt: antecipar-se ao mover-se para uma posição, chegar antes, preceder; chegar ou alcançar uma posição, ter acabado de chegar, então simplesmente chegar, alcançar; chegar ou atingir um estado particular, alcançar.

DEFINITION: perishable, corruptible.
ORIGIN: From phtheiro; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable.

BDAG.en: subject to decay/destruction, perishable; of persons mortal; of things perishable
BDAG.pt: sujeito à decomposição/destruição, perecível; de pessoas mortal; de coisas perecível

DEFINITION: to speak aloud, utter.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to pheggos and thus to phemi; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim.

BDAG.en: lit. ‘produce a sound’, then ‘call out loudly’, gener. speak, utter, proclaim something, with focus on the act of utterance.
BDAG.pt: lit. ‘produzir um som’, depois ‘gritar alto’, geralmente falar, proferir, proclamar algo, com foco no ato da enunciação.

DEFINITION: to corrupt, spoil, destroy, ruin.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. To spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave).

BDAG.en: destroy, ruin, corrupt, spoil; pass. be ruined, be doomed to destruction; to cause deterioration of the inner life, ruin, corrupt; to inflict punishment, destroy in the sense ‘punish w. eternal destruction’; break rules of a contest, violate rules
BDAG.pt: destruir, arruinar, corromper, estragar; passivo ser arruinado, estar fadado à destruição; causar deterioração da vida interior, arruinar, corromper; infligir punição, destruir no sentido de ‘punir com destruição eterna’; quebrar as regras de uma competição, violar regras

DEFINITION: autumnal, in autumn, when fruit is expected.
ORIGIN: From derivative of phthino (to wane; akin to the base of phtheiro) and opora (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves).

BDAG.en: belonging to late autumn
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao final do outono

DEFINITION: a sound.
ORIGIN: From phtheggomai; utterance, i.e. A musical note (vocal or instrumental).

BDAG.en: any clear or distinct sound; a of musical instruments tone; b of the human voice
BDAG.pt: qualquer som claro ou distinto; a de instrumentos musicais (tom); b da voz humana

DEFINITION: to envy.
ORIGIN: From phthonos; to be jealous of.

BDAG.en: envy, be jealous; begrudge someone (the chance to); dislike someone, be resentful toward someone without the connotation of jealousy or a grudge
BDAG.pt: invejar, ser ciumento; negar a alguém (a chance de); desgostar de alguém, ser ressentido com alguém sem a conotação de ciúme ou rancor

DEFINITION: envy, a grudge, spite.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to the base of phtheiro; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. Jealousy (spite).

BDAG.en: envy, jealousy
BDAG.pt: inveja, ciúme

DEFINITION: corruption, destruction, decay, rottenness, decomposition.
ORIGIN: From phtheiro; decay, i.e. Ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: breakdown of organic matter, dissolution, deterioration, corruption, in the world of nature; destruction of a fetus, abortion; ruination of a pers. through an immoral act, seduction of a young woman; inward depravity, depravity; total destruction of an entity, destruction in the last days
BDAG.pt: desintegração da matéria orgânica, dissolução, deterioração, corrupção, no mundo da natureza; destruição de um feto, aborto; ruína de uma pessoa através de um ato imoral, sedução de uma jovem; depravação interna, depravação; destruição total de uma entidade, destruição nos últimos dias

DEFINITION: a shallow and flat bowl.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial").

BDAG.en: bowl, specifically a bowl used in offerings
BDAG.pt: taça, especificamente uma taça usada em oferendas

DEFINITION: loving that which is good.
ORIGIN: From philos and agathos; fond to good, i.e. A promoter of virtue.

BDAG.en: loving what is good
BDAG.pt: aquele que ama o que é bom

DEFINITION: Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia.
ORIGIN: From Philadelphos (the same as philadelphos), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Philadelphia, a city in Lydia (west central Asia Minor)
BDAG.pt: Filadélfia, uma cidade na Lídia (Ásia Menor centro-ocidental)

DEFINITION: brotherly love, love of Christian brethren.
ORIGIN: From philadelphos; fraternal affection.
USAGE: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.

BDAG.en: love of brother/sister (in our literature in the transf. sense of affection for a fellow-Christian)
BDAG.pt: amor fraterno (no nosso contexto, no sentido transferido de afeição por um companheiro cristão)

DEFINITION: loving like a brother, loving one's brethren.
ORIGIN: From philos and adephos; fond of brethren, i.e. Fraternal.

BDAG.en: having affection for an associate, having brotherly love, having mutual affection
BDAG.pt: aquele que tem afeição por um associado, que tem amor fraterno, que tem afeto mútuo

DEFINITION: loving men, (of a wife) loving her husband.
ORIGIN: From philos and aner; fond of man, i.e. Affectionate as a wife.

BDAG.en: having affection/love for a husband
BDAG.pt: que ama o marido, amorosa ao marido

DEFINITION: love of mankind, benevolence.
ORIGIN: From the same as philanthropos; fondness of mankind, i.e. Benevolence ("philanthropy").

BDAG.en: affectionate concern for and interest in humanity, (loving) kindness, of God; as a virtue of rulers
BDAG.pt: preocupação afetuosa e interesse pela humanidade, bondade (amorosa), de Deus; como uma virtude de governantes

DEFINITION: humanely, kindly.
ORIGIN: Adverb from a compound of philos and anthropos; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. Humanely.

BDAG.en: benevolently, kindly (to treat someone in kindly fashion)
BDAG.pt: benevolamente, gentilmente (tratar alguém de forma gentil)

DEFINITION: love of money, avarice, covetousness.
ORIGIN: From philarguros; avarice.

BDAG.en: love of money, avarice, miserliness (as the root of all evil)
BDAG.pt: amor ao dinheiro, avareza, mesquinhez (como a raiz de todos os males)

DEFINITION: money-loving, avaricious, covetous.
ORIGIN: From philos and arguros; fond of silver (money), i.e. Avaricious.

BDAG.en: fond of money, avaricious
BDAG.pt: apegado ao dinheiro, avarento

DEFINITION: self-loving, selfish.
ORIGIN: From philos and autos; fond of self, i.e. Selfish.

BDAG.en: loving oneself, selfish
BDAG.pt: que ama a si mesmo, egoísta

DEFINITION: to love (of friendship), regard with affection, cherish; to kiss.
ORIGIN: From philos; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. Have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while agapao is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as ethelo and boulomai, or as thumos and nous respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness).

BDAG.en: to have a special interest in someone or someth., freq. with focus on close association, have affection for, like, consider someone a friend; to kiss as a special indication of affection, kiss; like or love to do someth., hence do someth. often or customarily
BDAG.pt: ter um interesse especial por alguém ou algo, frequentemente com foco na associação íntima, ter afeição por, gostar, considerar alguém um amigo; beijar como uma indicação especial de afeto, beijar; gostar ou amar fazer algo, portanto fazer algo frequentemente ou costumeiramente

DEFINITION: loving pleasure.
ORIGIN: From philos and hedone; fond of pleasure, i.e. Voluptuous.

BDAG.en: pert to having a special interest in pleasure, loving pleasure
BDAG.pt: pertencente a ter um interesse especial em prazer, amante do prazer

DEFINITION: a kiss.
ORIGIN: From phileo; a kiss.

BDAG.en: a kiss
BDAG.pt: um beijo

DEFINITION: Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae.
ORIGIN: From phileo; friendly; Philemon, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Philemon (‘Affectionate-one’), a Christian, prob. at Colossae, a convert of Paul.
BDAG.pt: Filemom (‘Aquele Afetuoso’), um cristão, provavelmente em Colossos, um convertido de Paulo.

DEFINITION: "worthy of love", Philetus, an erring Christian at Ephesus.
ORIGIN: From phileo; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity.

BDAG.en: Philetus (‘Worthy-of-love’), an otherw. unknown dissident, mentioned w. Hymenaeus
BDAG.pt: Fileto (‘Digno de Amor’), um dissidente de outra forma desconhecido, mencionado com Himeneu

DEFINITION: friendship, affection, fondness, love.
ORIGIN: From philos; fondness.

BDAG.en: friendship, love foll. by the objective gen.
BDAG.pt: amizade, amor seguido pelo genitivo objetivo

DEFINITION: a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi.
ORIGIN: From Philippoi; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. Native of Philippi.

BDAG.en: person from Philippi, the Philippian
BDAG.pt: pessoa de Filipos, o filipense

DEFINITION: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia.
ORIGIN: Plural of Philippos; Philippi, a place in Macedonia.

BDAG.en: Philippi, a city in Macedonia
BDAG.pt: Filipos, uma cidade na Macedônia

DEFINITION: Philip, (a) one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, (b) tetrarch of the Ituraean and Trachonitic region, half-brother of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee, (c) one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem and a missionary.
ORIGIN: From philos and hippos; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites.
