BDAG.en: Philip (‘Fond-of-horses’), a common name in the Gr-Rom. world. In our lit.: 1 the tetrarch, son of Herod the Great and Cleopatra of Jerusalem; 2 The Philip mentioned Mt 14:3 and Mk 6:17; 3 the apostle, one of the Twelve; 4 one of the seven ‘assistants’ at Jerusalem; 5 the Asiarch
BDAG.pt: Filipe (‘Amante de cavalos’), um nome comum no mundo greco-romano. Em nossa literatura: 1 o tetrarca, filho de Herodes, o Grande, e Cleópatra de Jerusalém; 2 O Filipe mencionado em Mt 14:3 e Mc 6:17; 3 o apóstolo, um dos Doze; 4 um dos sete ‘auxiliares’ em Jerusalém; 5 o Asiarcha

DEFINITION: loving God.
ORIGIN: From philos and theos; fond of God, i.e. Pious.

BDAG.en: having special affection for God, devout in a play on words w. φιλήδονος
BDAG.pt: ter afeição especial por Deus, devoto em um jogo de palavras com φιλήδονος

DEFINITION: "student, scholar", Philologus, a Christian.
ORIGIN: From philos and logos; fond of words, i.e. Talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Philologus, an otherwise unknown Christian, recipient of a greeting.
BDAG.pt: Filólogo, um cristão de outra forma desconhecido, destinatário de uma saudação.

DEFINITION: love of dispute, contention.
ORIGIN: From philoneikos; quarrelsomeness, i.e. A dispute.

BDAG.en: 1 contentiousness. 2 dispute, argument.
BDAG.pt: 1 contenciosidade. 2 disputa, discussão.

DEFINITION: strife-loving, contentious.
ORIGIN: From philos and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to nikos); fond of strife, i.e. Disputatious.

BDAG.en: 1 quarrelsome, contentious. 2 in a favorable sense emulous, (in) eager (rivalry).
BDAG.pt: 1 briguento, contencioso. 2 em um sentido favorável, emulativo, (em) ávido (de rivalidade).

DEFINITION: love to strangers, hospitality.
ORIGIN: From philoxenos; hospitableness.

BDAG.en: hospitality (implied by the root)
BDAG.pt: hospitalidade (implícita pela raiz)

DEFINITION: hospitable, loving strangers.
ORIGIN: From philos and xenos; fond of guests, i.e. Hospitable.

BDAG.en: hospitable.
BDAG.pt: hospitaleiro.

DEFINITION: to love the chief place, desire preeminence.
ORIGIN: From a compound of philos and protos; to be fond of being first, i.e. Ambitious of distinction.

BDAG.en: to have a special interest in being in the leading position, wish to be first, like to be leader.
BDAG.pt: ter um interesse especial em estar na posição de liderança, desejar ser o primeiro, gostar de ser líder.

DEFINITION: friendly; subst: a friend, an associate.
ORIGIN: Properly, dear, i.e. A friend; actively, fond, i.e. Friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.).

BDAG.en: 1 pert. to having a special interest in someone (beloved, dear, and loving, kindly disposed, devoted). 2 subst., a friend (male in sing., sometimes generic in pl.), or in a special sense, a friend of God/Christ.
BDAG.pt: 1 relativo a ter um interesse especial por alguém (amado, querido, e amoroso, bondoso, devotado). 2 substantivo, um amigo (masculino no singular, às vezes genérico no plural), ou em um sentido especial, amigo de Deus/Cristo.

DEFINITION: love of wisdom, philosophy, in the NT of traditional Jewish theology.
ORIGIN: From philosophos; "philosophy", i.e. (specially), Jewish sophistry.

BDAG.en: philosophy, in our lit. only in one pass. and in a pejorative sense, w. κενὴἀπάτη, of erroneous teaching
BDAG.pt: filosofia, em nossa literatura apenas em uma passagem e em sentido pejorativo, com *kènē apatē* (vã fraude), referente a ensino errôneo

DEFINITION: a philosopher.
ORIGIN: From philos and sophos; fond of wise things, i.e. A "philosopher".

BDAG.en: philosopher of Epicureans and Stoics.
BDAG.pt: filósofo dos epicuristas e estoicos.

DEFINITION: tenderly loving, kindly affectionate to.
ORIGIN: From philos and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. Fraternal towards fellow Christian.

BDAG.en: loving dearly, devoted to one another in brotherly love.
BDAG.pt: amar muito, devotado um ao outro em amor fraternal.

DEFINITION: loving one's children.
ORIGIN: From philos and teknon; fond of one's children, i.e. Maternal.

BDAG.en: loving one’s children, esp. of women
BDAG.pt: amar seus filhos, especialmente no caso das mulheres

DEFINITION: to be zealous, strive eagerly, desire very strongly.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from a compound of philos and time; to be fond of honor, i.e. Emulous (eager or earnest to do something).

BDAG.en: have as one’s ambition, consider it an honor, aspire, w. focus on idea of rendering service
BDAG.pt: ter como ambição, considerar uma honra, aspirar, com foco na ideia de prestar serviço

DEFINITION: kindly, in a friendly manner.
ORIGIN: Adverb from philophron; with friendliness of mind, i.e. Kindly.

BDAG.en: in a friendly manner, hospitably
BDAG.pt: de maneira amigável, hospitaleiramente

DEFINITION: friendly, kindly, courteous.
ORIGIN: From philos and phren; friendly of mind, i.e. Kind.

BDAG.en: well-disposed, friendly, kind
BDAG.pt: bem-intencionado, amigável, bondoso

DEFINITION: to muzzle, to put to silence.
ORIGIN: From phimos (a muzzle); to muzzle.

BDAG.en: tie shut (specif. of shutting a mouth w. a muzzle); to silence, put to silence
BDAG.pt: atar (fechar) com um freio (especificamente de fechar a boca); silenciar, calar

DEFINITION: Phlegon, a Roman Christian man.
ORIGIN: Active participle of the base of phlox; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Phlegon (‘Blazer’), an otherw. unknown Christian
BDAG.pt: Flegon ('Queimador'), um cristão de outra forma desconhecido

DEFINITION: to inflame, fire with passion, set on fire, burn up.
ORIGIN: From phlox (g5395); to cause a blaze, i.e. Ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion).

BDAG.en: set on fire in imagery
BDAG.pt: incendiar em sentido figurado

DEFINITION: a flame.
ORIGIN: From a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze.

BDAG.en: flame
BDAG.pt: chama

DEFINITION: to gossip against, talk idly, make empty charges against, talk nonsense.
ORIGIN: From phluaros; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously.

BDAG.en: to indulge in utterance that makes no sense, talk nonsense (about), disparage
BDAG.pt: dar vazão a falas sem sentido, falar disparates (sobre), difamar

DEFINITION: prating, talking foolishly, babbling.
ORIGIN: From phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. Prater.

BDAG.en: gossipy
BDAG.pt: fofoqueiro

DEFINITION: fearful, dreadful, terrible.
ORIGIN: From phobos; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable.

BDAG.en: causing fear, fearful, terrible, frightful
BDAG.pt: causador de medo, temível, terrível, assustador

DEFINITION: to fear, dread, reverence, be afraid, terrified.
ORIGIN: From phobos; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. Revere.

BDAG.en: to be in an apprehensive state, be afraid, become frightened; fear someone or something; have a profound measure of respect for, have reverence, respect (especially fear of offending God).
BDAG.pt: estar num estado aprensivo, ter medo, ficar assustado; temer alguém ou algo; ter uma profunda medida de respeito, ter reverência, respeito (especialmente o medo de ofender a Deus).

DEFINITION: a terrible sight, cause of terror, an object of fear.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of phobeo; a frightening thing, i.e. Terrific portent.

BDAG.en: something unusual that causes fear, terrible sight/event, horror.
BDAG.pt: algo incomum que causa medo, visão/evento terrível, horror.

DEFINITION: (a) fear, terror, alarm, (b) the object or cause of fear, (c) reverence, respect.
ORIGIN: From a primary phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright.

BDAG.en: 1 intimidating entity, the act. causative sense a intimidation; b concretely, someth. terrible/awe-inspiring, a terror; 2 the product of an intimidating/alarming force, the pass. sense a fear, alarm, fright; b reverence, respect (toward God and Christ; toward humans, respect that is due officials; wife to husband).
BDAG.pt: 1 entidade intimidante, no sentido causativo: a intimidação; b concretamente, algo terrível/inspirador de temor, um terror; 2 o produto de uma força intimidante/alarmante, no sentido passivo: a) medo, alarme, susto; b) reverência, respeito (a Deus e a Cristo; a humanos, o respeito devido às autoridades; esposa a marido).

DEFINITION: Phoebe, a Christian woman in the church at Cenchreae.
ORIGIN: Feminine of phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of phos); Phoebe, a Christian woman.

BDAG.en: Phoebe, a Christian official, deaconess of the church in Cenchreae, recommended by Paul.
BDAG.pt: Febe, uma oficial cristã, diaconisa da igreja em Cencreia, recomendada por Paulo.

DEFINITION: Phoenicia, a northern coast strip of the Roman province Syria.
ORIGIN: From phoinix; palm-country; Phoenice (or Phoenicia), a region of Palestine.

BDAG.en: Phoenicia, the seacoast of central Syria, with Tyre and Sidon as the most important cities.
BDAG.pt: Fenícia, a costa central da Síria, tendo Tiro e Sidom como as cidades mais importantes.

DEFINITION: a palm tree, the date-palm.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a palm-tree.

BDAG.en: a seaport mentioned Ac 27:12.
BDAG.pt: um porto mencionado em Atos 27:12.

DEFINITION: a Phoenician (an inhabitant of Phoenicia), Phoenix (a city of Crete).
ORIGIN: Probably the same as phoinix; Phoenix, a place in Crete.

BDAG.en: a seaport mentioned Ac 27:12.
BDAG.pt: um porto mencionado em Atos 27:12.

DEFINITION: a murderer.
ORIGIN: From phonos; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which anthropoktonos does not necessarily imply; while sikarios is a special term for a public bandit).

BDAG.en: murderer.
BDAG.pt: assassino.

DEFINITION: to kill, murder.
ORIGIN: From phoneus; to be a murderer (of).

BDAG.en: murder, kill; Pass.: be put to death, die a violent death.
BDAG.pt: assassinar, matar; Passivo: ser morto, morrer de morte violenta.

DEFINITION: murder, slaughter, killing.
ORIGIN: From an obsolete primary pheno (to slay); murder.

BDAG.en: murder, killing; Anger as a cause; bloody deeds.
BDAG.pt: assassinato, morte; Raiva como causa; atos sangrentos.

DEFINITION: to carry, wear, bear constantly.
ORIGIN: From phoros; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment.

BDAG.en: to carry or bear habitually or for a considerable length of time, bear constantly/regularly, hence wear clothing; to identify habitually w. someth., bear, fig. ext. of 1.
BDAG.pt: carregar ou portar habitualmente ou por um longo período, portar constantemente/regularmente, daí vestir (roupas); identificar-se habitualmente com algo, suportar (sentido figurado, extensão do primeiro).

DEFINITION: (of Latin origin), Forum, Market, Market-Town.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Appios; a station on the Appian road.

BDAG.en: s. Ἀππίου φόρον.
BDAG.pt: cf. tributo de Ápio.

DEFINITION: a tax, tribute, especially on persons.
ORIGIN: From phero; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas telos is usually a general toll on goods or travel).

BDAG.en: that which is brought in as payment to a state, with implication of dependent status, tribute, tax.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é trazido como pagamento a um estado, com implicação de status de dependência: tributo, imposto.

DEFINITION: to load, burden; pass: to be laden.
ORIGIN: From phortos; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety).

BDAG.en: to load/burden someone with something, more exactly cause someone to carry something (in imagery, of the burden of keeping the law).
BDAG.pt: carregar/sobrecarregar alguém com algo, mais precisamente fazer alguém carregar algo (em imagens, como o fardo de guardar a lei).

DEFINITION: a burden; the freight of a ship.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of phortos; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service.

BDAG.en: that which constitutes a load for transport, load; that which is carried and constitutes a burden, burden, in imagery (of the oppressive burden of the law)
BDAG.pt: aquilo que constitui uma carga para transporte, carga; aquilo que é carregado e constitui um fardo, fardo, em sentido figurado (do fardo opressivo da lei)

DEFINITION: cargo.
ORIGIN: From phero; something carried, i.e. The cargo of a ship.

BDAG.en: esp. the cargo of a ship (goods for transport)
BDAG.pt: especialmente a carga de um navio (mercadorias para transporte)

DEFINITION: "prosperous, lucky", Fortunatus, a Christian.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian.

BDAG.en: Fortunatus. An otherwise unknown Christian of Corinth; a member of the delegation sent by the Roman church to Corinth.
BDAG.pt: Fortunato. Um cristão de Corinto de outra forma desconhecido; um membro da delegação enviada pela igreja romana a Corinto.

DEFINITION: a scourge, lash, whip.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative from the base of phragelloo; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment.

BDAG.en: whip, lash made of ropes (less lethal than the penal ‘flagellum’)
BDAG.pt: chicote, azorrague feito de cordas (menos letal que o 'flagelo' penal)

DEFINITION: to flagellate, scourge.
ORIGIN: From a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. Lash as a public punishment.

BDAG.en: flog, scourge, a punishment inflicted on slaves and provincials after a sentence of death had been pronounced on them.
BDAG.pt: açoitar, flagelar, um castigo infligido a escravos e provinciais após uma sentença de morte ter sido proferida contra eles.

DEFINITION: a hedge, fence, partition.
ORIGIN: From phrasso; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively).

BDAG.en: a structure for enclosing an area, fence, hedge; a wall that separates, partition (fig. ext. of 1, of the law)
BDAG.pt: uma estrutura para cercar uma área, cerca, sebe; um muro que separa, partição (extensão figurada de 1, da lei)

DEFINITION: to declare, explain, interpret.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to phrasso through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound.

BDAG.en: explain, interpret someth. mysterious
BDAG.pt: explicar, interpretar algo misterioso

DEFINITION: to stop, close up, obstruct.
ORIGIN: Apparently a strengthening form of the base of phren; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence).

BDAG.en: to close or keep from opening, shut, close (a lit.); fig. ext. of 1a: close or stop the mouth, so that the pers. must remain silent; to cause someth. to cease, block, bar
BDAG.pt: fechar ou impedir de abrir, fechar; ext. fig. de 1a: fechar ou calar a boca, para que a pessoa deva permanecer em silêncio; fazer algo cessar, bloquear, barrar

DEFINITION: a pit, well, cistern.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. A cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison).

BDAG.en: a construction consisting of a vertical shaft, covered with a stone, for water supply, a well; an opening that leads to the depths of the nether world, pit, shaft
BDAG.pt: uma construção que consiste em um poço vertical, coberto com uma pedra, para fornecimento de água, um poço; uma abertura que leva às profundezas do mundo inferior, fosso, poço

DEFINITION: to deceive the mind, impose upon.
ORIGIN: From phrenapates; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. Delude.

BDAG.en: mislead concerning the truth, deceive oneself
BDAG.pt: enganar no que diz respeito à verdade, enganar a si mesmo

DEFINITION: a deceiver, seducer.
ORIGIN: From phren and apate; a mind-misleader, i.e. Seducer.

BDAG.en: deceiver, misleader
BDAG.pt: enganador, sedutor

DEFINITION: the mind, intellect, thought, understanding.
ORIGIN: Probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb; compare phrasso); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties).

BDAG.en: the process of careful consideration, thinking, understanding (only in plural)
BDAG.pt: o processo de cuidadosa consideração, pensamento, compreensão (somente no plural)

DEFINITION: to be rough, to shiver, shudder.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. Shudder (fear).

BDAG.en: to tremble fr. fear, shudder
BDAG.pt: tremer de medo, estremecer

DEFINITION: (a) to think, (b) to think, judge, (c) to direct the mind to, seek for, (d) to observe, (e) to care for.
ORIGIN: From phren; to exercise the mind, i.e. Entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience).
USAGE: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.

BDAG.en: to have an opinion with regard to someth., think, form/hold an opinion, judge; to give careful consideration to someth., set one’s mind on, be intent on; to develop an attitude based on careful thought, be minded/disposed
BDAG.pt: ter uma opinião com respeito a algo, pensar, formar/manter uma opinião, julgar; dar consideração cuidadosa a algo, fixar a mente em, estar empenhado em; desenvolver uma atitude baseada em pensamento cuidadoso, estar inclinado/disposto

DEFINITION: the thought (that which is in the mind).
ORIGIN: From phroneo; (mental) inclination or purpose.

BDAG.en: the faculty of fixing one’s mind on someth., way of thinking, mind(-set), focus on strong intention aim, aspiration, striving
BDAG.pt: a faculdade de fixar a mente em algo, modo de pensar, mentalidade, foco em forte intenção, objetivo, aspiração, esforço

DEFINITION: understanding (which leads to right action), practical wisdom, prudence.
ORIGIN: From phroneo; mental action or activity, i.e. Intellectual or moral insight.

BDAG.en: the faculty of thoughtful planning, way of thinking, (frame of) mind; the ability to understand, understanding, insight, intelligence
BDAG.pt: a faculdade de planejamento atencioso, modo de pensar, (estrutura de) mente; a capacidade de compreender, entendimento, percepção, inteligência

DEFINITION: intelligent, prudent, sensible, wise.
ORIGIN: From phren; thoughtful, i.e. Sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while sophos denotes practical skill or acumen; and sunetos indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative).

BDAG.en: pert. to understanding associated w. insight and wisdom, sensible, thoughtful, prudent, wise
BDAG.pt: pertencente ao entendimento associado à percepção e sabedoria, sensato, pensativo, prudente, sábio

DEFINITION: wisely, sensibly, prudently.
ORIGIN: Adverb from phronimos; prudently.

BDAG.en: prudently, shrewdly
BDAG.pt: prudentemente, astutamente

DEFINITION: to be thoughtful, careful, give heed.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of phren; to exercise thought, i.e. Be anxious.

BDAG.en: to give sustained thought to someth., think of, be intent on, be careful/concerned about
BDAG.pt: dar pensamento sustentado a algo, pensar em, estar empenhado em, ser cuidadoso/preocupado com

DEFINITION: to guard, keep, as by a military guard.
ORIGIN: From a compound of pro and horao; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. To mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect.

BDAG.en: 1 to maintain a watch, guard, lit.; 2 to hold in custody, detain, confine; 3 gener. to provide security, guard, protect, keep
BDAG.pt: 1 manter a vigília, guardar, literalmente; 2 manter sob custódia, deter, confinar; 3 em geral, prover segurança, guardar, proteger, conservar

DEFINITION: to be wanton, insolent; to roar, rage.
ORIGIN: Akin to bruo, brucho; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult.

BDAG.en: fig., of people be arrogant, haughty, insolent
BDAG.pt: fig., de pessoas ser arrogante, altivo, insolente

DEFINITION: a dry stick for burning.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo (to roast or parch; akin to the base of phlox); something desiccated, i.e. A dry twig.

BDAG.en: 1 bush, shrub; 2 in the pl., pieces of dry wood/brushwood esp. for making fires
BDAG.pt: 1 arbusto; 2 no plural, pedaços de madeira seca/mato especialmente para fazer fogo

DEFINITION: Phrygia, an ethnic district in Asia Minor, the north-western part of which was in the Roman province Asia and the south-eastern part in the Roman province Galatia.
ORIGIN: Probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor.

BDAG.en: Phrygia, a large district in Central Asia Minor, whose boundaries varied considerably from time to time
BDAG.pt: Frígia, uma grande região na Ásia Menor Central, cujas fronteiras variavam consideravelmente de tempos em tempos

DEFINITION: Phygelus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia who deserted Paul.
ORIGIN: Probably from pheugo; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian.

BDAG.en: Phygelus, an otherwise unknown Christian in Asia who, acc. to 2 Ti 1:15, w. Hermogenes turned his back on Paul
BDAG.pt: Fígelo, um cristão de outra forma desconhecido na Ásia que, segundo 2 Tm 1:15, com Hermógenes deu as costas a Paulo

DEFINITION: flight, fleeing.
ORIGIN: From pheugo; a fleeing, i.e. Escape.

BDAG.en: flight
BDAG.pt: fuga

DEFINITION: a watching, keeping guard; a guard, prison; imprisonment.
ORIGIN: From phulasso; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: 1 the act of guarding, guarding; 2 the act of guarding embodied in a person, guard, sentinel; 3 the place where guarding is done, prison; 4 one of the periods of time into which the night was divided, a watch of the night
BDAG.pt: 1 o ato de guardar, guarda; 2 o ato de guardar corporificado em uma pessoa, guarda, sentinela; 3 o lugar onde a guarda é feita, prisão; 4 um dos períodos de tempo em que a noite era dividida, uma vigília noturna

DEFINITION: to imprison, deliver into custody.
ORIGIN: From phulax; to incarcerate.

BDAG.en: take into custody, imprison
BDAG.pt: deter, aprisionar, colocar sob custódia

DEFINITION: a phylactery, an amulet, a parchment capsule containing little parchment rolls with the Hebrew texts, affixed to the left upper arm or the forehead of men at morning prayer, and regarded as a protection (hence the name) against evil spirits.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a derivative of phulasso; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts.

BDAG.en: leather prayer band and case containing scripture passages, sometimes used as an amulet, prayer-band, prayer-case
BDAG.pt: tira de couro e estojo contendo passagens das Escrituras, às vezes usado como amuleto, banda de oração, estojo de oração

DEFINITION: a guard, keeper, sentinel.
ORIGIN: From phulasso; a watcher or sentry.

BDAG.en: guard, sentinel
BDAG.pt: guarda, sentinela

DEFINITION: (a) to guard, protect; mid: to be on guard, (b) act. and mid. of customs and regulations: to keep, observe.
ORIGIN: Probably from phule through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. Be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid.
USAGE: beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare tereo.

BDAG.en: to carry out sentinel functions, watch, guard; to protect by taking careful measures, guard, protect; to be on one’s guard against, look out for, avoid; to hold in reserve, keep, reserve; to continue to keep a law or commandment from being broken, observe, follow; to store up, lay up for oneself
BDAG.pt: executar funções de sentinela, vigiar, guardar; proteger tomando medidas cuidadosas, guardar, proteger; estar em guarda contra, observar, evitar; reservar, manter; continuar a impedir que uma lei ou mandamento seja quebrado, observar, seguir; armazenar, reservar para si mesmo

DEFINITION: a tribe or race of people.
ORIGIN: From phuo (compare phullon); an offshoot, i.e. Race or clan.

BDAG.en: a subgroup of a nation characterized by a distinctive blood line, tribe; a relatively large people group that forms a sociopolitical subgroup of the human race, nation, people
BDAG.pt: um subgrupo de uma nação caracterizado por linhagem distinta, tribo; um grupo de pessoas relativamente grande que forma um subgrupo sociopolítico da raça humana, nação, povo

DEFINITION: a leaf.
ORIGIN: From the same as phule; a sprout, i.e. Leaf.

BDAG.en: leaf; collectively foliage
BDAG.pt: folha; coletivamente folhagem

DEFINITION: a mass or lump, as of bread dough.
ORIGIN: From a prolonged form of phuro (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to phuo through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough.

BDAG.en: that which is mixed/kneaded, mixture/batch of dough; metaph. fresh dough containing no leaven; the dough-like mixture from which potters make their wares, lump
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é misturado/sovado, mistura/massa de pão; metaforicamente massa nova sem fermento; a mistura semelhante a massa da qual os oleiros fazem seus produtos, torrão

DEFINITION: natural, (a) according to nature, (b) merely animal.
ORIGIN: From phusis; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive.

BDAG.en: pert. to being in accordance w. the basic order of things in nature, natural; of animals, creatures of instinct; pert. to the natural character of an entity, natural characteristic/disposition
BDAG.pt: pertencente a estar de acordo com a ordem básica das coisas na natureza, natural; de animais, criaturas de instinto; pertencente ao caráter natural de uma entidade, característica/disposição natural

DEFINITION: naturally, by nature.
ORIGIN: Adverb from phusikos; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively.

BDAG.en: naturally, by instinct
BDAG.pt: naturalmente, por instinto

DEFINITION: to inflate, puff up; pass: to be puffed up, arrogant, proud.
ORIGIN: From phusis in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty).

BDAG.en: fig. to cause to have an exaggerated self-conception, puff up, make proud; pass. become puffed up or conceited, put on airs
BDAG.pt: fig. causar uma autopercepção exagerada, inchar, envaidecer; passivo tornar-se inchado ou presunçoso, ser arrogante

DEFINITION: nature, inherent nature, origin, birth.
ORIGIN: From phuo; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage.

BDAG.en: condition or circumstance as determined by birth, natural endowment/condition, nature, esp. as inherited fr. one’s ancestors; the natural character of an entity, natural characteristic/disposition; the regular or established order of things, nature; an entity as a product of nature, natural being, creature
BDAG.pt: condição ou circunstância determinada pelo nascimento, dote/condição natural, natureza, especialmente como herdada dos ancestrais; o caráter natural de uma entidade, característica/disposição natural; a ordem regular ou estabelecida das coisas, natureza; uma entidade como produto da natureza, ser natural, criatura

DEFINITION: a puffing up, pride, swelling.
ORIGIN: From phusioo; inflation, i.e. (figuratively) haughtiness.

BDAG.en: swelled-headedness, pride, conceit
BDAG.pt: cabeça inchada (arrogância), orgulho, presunção

DEFINITION: a plant, that which is planted.
ORIGIN: From phuteuo; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable.

BDAG.en: that which is planted, a plant.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é plantado, uma planta.

DEFINITION: to plant, set.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of phuo; to set out in the earth, i.e. Implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine.

BDAG.en: to plant (something, a vine, a tree, sticks); be planted in the sea.
BDAG.pt: plantar (algo, uma videira, uma árvore, estacas); ser plantado no mar.

DEFINITION: to grow, grow up, spring up.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. To swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: to grow (up), come up.
BDAG.pt: crescer, surgir.

DEFINITION: a burrow, hole, den, lair.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place.

BDAG.en: hole for animals, den, lair, hole (of a fox-hole).
BDAG.pt: toca para animais, covil, esconderijo, buraco (de raposa).

DEFINITION: to give forth a sound, hence: (a) of a cock: to crow, (b) of men: to shout, (c) trans: to call (to myself), summon; to invite, address.
ORIGIN: From phone; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation.

BDAG.en: to produce a voiced sound/tone, crow (of a cock), call/cry out, speak loudly, say with emphasis, use an attribution in speaking of a person (address as), call to oneself, summon, extend hospitality through invitation.
BDAG.pt: produzir um som vocalizado/tom, cacarejar (de um galo), chamar/gritar, falar alto, dizer com ênfase, usar uma atribuição ao falar de uma pessoa (endereçar como), chamar para si, convocar, estender hospitalidade através de convite.

DEFINITION: a sound, noise, voice, language, dialect.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to phaino through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language.

BDAG.en: to produce a voiced sound/tone, frequently with reference to intensity of tone; of animals: crow; of humans: call/cry out, speak loudly, say with emphasis; to use an attribution in speaking of a person, address as; to call to oneself, summon; to extend hospitality through invitation, invite; an auditory effect, sound, tone, noise; the faculty of utterance, voice; a verbal code shared by a community to express ideas and feelings, language.
BDAG.pt: Produzir um som/tom vocalizado, frequentemente com referência à intensidade do tom; de animais: cantar (galo); de humanos: chamar/gritar, falar em voz alta, dizer com ênfase; usar uma atribuição ao falar de uma pessoa, dirigir-se a ela como; chamar para si, convocar; estender hospitalidade através de convite, convidar; um efeito auditivo, som, tom, ruído; a faculdade de expressão, voz; um código verbal compartilhado por uma comunidade para expressar ideias e sentimentos, linguagem.

DEFINITION: light, a source of light, radiance.
ORIGIN: From an obsolete phao (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare phaino, phemi); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative).

BDAG.en: light in contrast to darkness; light in the physical realm; in a transcendent sense, the element and sphere of the divine; light that illuminates the spirit and soul of humans, the element in which the redeemed person lives; a verbal code shared by a community to express ideas and feelings, language.
BDAG.pt: Luz em contraste com a escuridão; luz no reino físico; em um sentido transcendente, o elemento e a esfera do divino; luz que ilumina o espírito e a alma dos humanos, o elemento em que a pessoa redimida vive; um código verbal compartilhado por uma comunidade para expressar ideias e sentimentos, linguagem.

DEFINITION: a light, an illuminator, perhaps the sun; a star; brilliancy.
ORIGIN: From phos; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy.

BDAG.en: light-giving body, esp. of heavenly bodies, specif. star; state of brightness or shining, splendor, radiance.
BDAG.pt: corpo que emite luz, especialmente corpos celestes, especificamente estrela; estado de brilho ou fulgor, esplendor, resplendor.

DEFINITION: (lit: light-bearing), radiant, the morning-star.
ORIGIN: From phos and phero; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively).

BDAG.en: light-bringing, light-giving (as adjective); only once as a substantive: prob. the morning star, the planet Venus.
BDAG.pt: que traz luz, que dá luz (como adjetivo); apenas uma vez como substantivo: provavelmente a estrela da manhã, o planeta Vênus.

DEFINITION: bright, luminous, full of light.
ORIGIN: From phos; lustrous, i.e. Transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively).

BDAG.en: shining, bright, radiant; illuminated, full of light.
BDAG.pt: resplandecente, brilhante, radiante; iluminado, cheio de luz.

DEFINITION: (a) to light up, illumine, (b) to bring to light, make evident, reveal.
ORIGIN: From phos; to shed rays, i.e. To shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.

BDAG.en: to function as a source of light, to shine, of God; to cause to be illumined, give light to, light (up), illuminate; to make known in reference to the inner life or transcendent matters and thus enlighten, enlighten, give light to, shed light upon; to bring to light, reveal.
BDAG.pt: funcionar como fonte de luz, brilhar, de Deus; fazer com que seja iluminado, dar luz, iluminar; tornar conhecido em referência à vida interior ou a assuntos transcendentes e assim iluminar, esclarecer, lançar luz sobre; trazer à luz, revelar.

DEFINITION: light, luster, illumination, enlightenment.
ORIGIN: From photizo; illumination (figuratively).

BDAG.en: illumination in the physical sense (of the moon, sun, daylight); in our lit. only in imagery: illumination for the inner life, enlightenment, light; bringing to light, revealing.
BDAG.pt: iluminação no sentido físico (da lua, do sol, da luz do dia); em nossa literatura apenas em sentido figurado: iluminação para a vida interior, esclarecimento, luz; trazer à luz, revelar.

DEFINITION: to rejoice, be glad; also a salutation: Hail.
ORIGIN: A primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. Calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well.
USAGE: farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.

BDAG.en: to be in a state of happiness and well-being, rejoice, be glad; a formalized greeting wishing one well, also in indicative, to use such a greeting (in effect, to express that one is on good terms w. the other); elliptically at the beginning of a letter greetings
BDAG.pt: estar em estado de felicidade e bem-estar, alegrar-se, regozijar-se; uma saudação formalizada desejando bem-estar a alguém, também no indicativo, usar tal saudação (na prática, expressar que se está em bons termos com o outro); elipticamente no início de uma carta, saudações

DEFINITION: hailstone.
ORIGIN: Probably from chalao; hail.

BDAG.en: hail
BDAG.pt: granizo

DEFINITION: to let down, lower, slacken, loosen.
ORIGIN: From the base of chasma; to lower (as into a void).

BDAG.en: let down (someth.), let down (nets), (nautical term) lower (the ship), let down (someone) in a basket
BDAG.pt: baixar (algo), lançar (redes), (termo náutico) arriar (o navio), descer (alguém) em uma cesta

DEFINITION: a Chaldean, an inhabitant of Chaldea.
ORIGIN: Probably of Hebrew or (Kasdiy); a Chaldoean (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates.

BDAG.en: Chaldean: land of the Chaldeans
BDAG.pt: Caldeu: terra dos Caldeus

DEFINITION: (a) hard, troublesome, (b) harsh, fierce.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from chalao through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. Dangerous, or (by implication) furious.

BDAG.en: troublesome, hard, difficult (hard times), hard to bear and penetrate deeply (of words), hard to deal with, violent, dangerous (of persons), bad, evil (of deeds)
BDAG.pt: problemático, duro, difícil (tempos difíceis), difícil de suportar e penetrar profundamente (de palavras), difícil de lidar, violento, perigoso (de pessoas), mau, perverso (de ações)

DEFINITION: to bridle, curb, restrain, sway.
ORIGIN: From a compound of chalinos and the reduplicated form of ago; to be a bit-leader, i.e. To curb (figuratively).

BDAG.en: bridle, hold in check (figuratively: the tongue, the body, desire; restrain oneself from something)
BDAG.pt: refrear, controlar (figuradamente: a língua, o corpo, o desejo; conter-se de algo)

DEFINITION: a bridle, bit.
ORIGIN: From chalao; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit).

BDAG.en: bit, bridle
BDAG.pt: freio, bridão

DEFINITION: brazen (i.e. of copper, bronze, brass).
ORIGIN: From chalkos; coppery.

BDAG.en: Copper coin, small change, also simply money
BDAG.pt: Moeda de cobre, troco pequeno, também simplesmente dinheiro

DEFINITION: a worker in brass or copper; a smith.
ORIGIN: From chalkos; a copper-worker or brazier.

BDAG.en: first ‘copper-smith’, then gener. (black)smith, metalworker
BDAG.pt: primeiro 'cooper-smith' (trabalhador em cobre), depois genericamente ferreiro, metalúrgico

DEFINITION: chalcedony, a small stone of various colors.
ORIGIN: From chalkos and perhaps eidos; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony".

BDAG.en: chalcedony, a precious stone
BDAG.pt: calcedônia, uma pedra preciosa

DEFINITION: a brazen (i.e. of copper, bronze, brass) vessel.
ORIGIN: Diminutive from chalkos; a copper dish.

BDAG.en: a container or object made of copper, brass, or bronze, bronze vessel, kettle
BDAG.pt: um recipiente ou objeto feito de cobre, latão ou bronze, vasilha de bronze, caldeirão

DEFINITION: orichalcum, a fine metal, or frankincense of a yellow color.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of chalkos and libanos (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre.

BDAG.en: an exceptionally fine type of metal or alloy (fine brass/bronze)
BDAG.pt: um tipo excepcionalmente fino de metal ou liga (bronze/latão fino)

DEFINITION: copper, brass, money; a brazen musical instrument.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from chalao through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it).

BDAG.en: a metal of various types, such as copper, brass, or bronze; anything made of such metal (a cult image of brass); copper coin, small change, also simply money
BDAG.pt: um metal de vários tipos, como cobre, latão ou bronze; qualquer coisa feita desse metal (uma imagem de culto de bronze); moeda de cobre, troco, ou simplesmente dinheiro

DEFINITION: on or to the ground.
ORIGIN: Adverb perhaps from the base of chasma through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. Prostrate.

BDAG.en: located on the ground, on the ground; to/on the ground (as objective of movement)
BDAG.pt: localizado no chão, no chão; para/no chão (como objetivo de movimento)

DEFINITION: Canaan, the whole of Palestine or Palestine west of the river Jordan.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Kna'an); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine.

BDAG.en: Canaan, in our lit. the land west of the Jordan, where the patriarchs lived
BDAG.pt: Canaã, na nossa literatura a terra a oeste do Jordão, onde os patriarcas viviam

DEFINITION: Canaanite, a Biblical and archaic name for Phoenician.
ORIGIN: From Chanaan; a Chanaanoean (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine.

BDAG.en: belonging to the land and people of Canaan, Canaanite
BDAG.pt: pertencente à terra e ao povo de Canaã, Cananeu

DEFINITION: joy, gladness, a source of joy.
ORIGIN: From chairo; cheerfulness, i.e. Calm delight.
USAGE: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).

BDAG.en: joy (the experience of gladness; a state of joyfulness; a person or thing that causes joy; a festive dinner or banquet)
BDAG.pt: alegria (a experiência de contentamento; um estado de alegria; uma pessoa ou coisa que causa alegria; um jantar ou banquete festivo)

DEFINITION: sculpture; engraving, a stamp, sign.
ORIGIN: From the same as charax; a scratch or etching, i.e. Stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue).

BDAG.en: a mark that is engraved, etched, branded, cut, imprinted, mark, stamp (in Rev of the mark of the Antichrist); an object fashioned by artistic skill involving alteration of a medium, thing formed, image
BDAG.pt: uma marca gravada, gravada a buril, marcada, cortada, impressa, marca, selo (em Apocalipse, a marca do Anticristo); um objeto moldado por habilidade artística envolvendo alteração de um meio, coisa formada, imagem

DEFINITION: an impression, representation, exact reproduction; a graving-tool.
ORIGIN: From the same as charax; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. An exact copy or (figuratively) representation).

BDAG.en: a mark or impression placed on an object; a reproduction, representation; a distinguishing mark, trademark; something produced as a representation, fig., of God; characteristic trait or manner, distinctive mark; an impression that is made, outward aspect, outward appearance, form.
BDAG.pt: uma marca ou impressão colocada sobre um objeto; uma reprodução, representação; uma marca distintiva, marca registrada; algo produzido como representação, fig., de Deus; um traço ou maneira característica, marca distintiva; uma impressão feita, aspecto exterior, aparência externa, forma.

DEFINITION: a palisade, mound for besieging.
ORIGIN: From charasso (to sharpen to a point; akin to grapho through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege).

BDAG.en: pointed stick/post used to fence in an area, stake; military installation involving use of stakes, palisade, entrenchment, siege-work
BDAG.pt: pau/poste pontiagudo usado para cercar uma área, estaca; instalação militar envolvendo o uso de estacas, paliçada, entrincheiramento, trabalho de cerco

DEFINITION: (a) to show favor to, (b) to pardon, forgive, (c) to show kindness.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from charis; to grant as a favor, i.e. Gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue.

BDAG.en: to give freely as a favor, give graciously; to cancel a sum of money that is owed, cancel; to show oneself gracious by forgiving wrongdoing, forgive, pardon; to give or grant someone to someone; show oneself to be gracious to someone
BDAG.pt: dar livremente como um favor, dar graciosamente; cancelar uma soma de dinheiro devida, cancelar; mostrar-se gracioso perdoando uma ofensa, perdoar, absolver; dar ou conceder alguém a alguém; mostrar-se gracioso para com alguém

DEFINITION: for the sake of, by reason of, on account of.
ORIGIN: Accusative case of charis as preposition; through favor of, i.e. On account of.
USAGE: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +...fore, X reproachfully.

BDAG.en: for the sake of, on behalf of, on account of (used as a preposition with the genitive).
BDAG.pt: pelo bem de, em nome de, por causa de (usado como preposição com o genitivo).

DEFINITION: (a) grace, as a gift or blessing brought to man by Jesus Christ, (b) favor, (c) gratitude, thanks, (d) a favor, kindness.
ORIGIN: From chairo; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude).
USAGE: acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).

BDAG.en: a winning quality or attractiveness that invites a favorable reaction, graciousness, attractiveness, charm, winsomeness; a beneficent disposition toward someone, favor, grace, gracious care/help, goodwill (often denoting God's undeserved gift); a practical application of goodwill, (a sign of) favor, gracious deed/gift, benefaction (on the part of humans or God); in Christian letters, used in fixed formulas for greeting and closing.
BDAG.pt: uma qualidade atraente ou atratividade que convida a uma reação favorável, graça, atratividade, charme, simpatia; uma disposição benéfica para com alguém, favor, graça, cuidado/ajuda graciosa, boa vontade (muitas vezes denotando o dom imerecido de Deus); uma aplicação prática de boa vontade, (um sinal de) favor, ato/dom gracioso, benefício (por parte de humanos ou de Deus); em cartas cristãs, usado em fórmulas fixas de saudação e encerramento.

DEFINITION: a gift of grace, an undeserved favor.
ORIGIN: From charizomai; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. Deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty.

BDAG.en: that which is freely and graciously given, favor bestowed, gift (of divine beneficence); spiritual possession of the believer; special gifts bestowed on individual Christians.
BDAG.pt: aquilo que é dado livre e graciosamente, favor concedido, dom (de beneficência divina); posse espiritual do crente; dons especiais conferidos a cristãos individuais.

DEFINITION: to make graceful, endow with grace.
ORIGIN: From charis; to grace, i.e. Indue with special honor.

BDAG.en: to cause to be the recipient of a benefit, bestow favor on, favor highly, bless, only with reference to divine grace.
BDAG.pt: fazer com que seja receptor de um benefício, conceder favor, favorecer grandemente, abençoar, apenas com referência à graça divina.

DEFINITION: Haran, a city in northwest Mesopotamia.
ORIGIN: Of Hebrew origin (Charan); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia.

BDAG.en: Haran, a place in Mesopotamia.
BDAG.pt: Haran, um lugar na Mesopotâmia.

DEFINITION: a sheet of paper (made of papyrus strips).
ORIGIN: From the same as charax; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over).

BDAG.en: papyrus, mostly taken in the sense of a sheet of paper, or a papyrus roll.
BDAG.pt: papiro, entendido na maioria das vezes como uma folha de papel, ou um rolo de papiro.

DEFINITION: a chasm, wide space.
ORIGIN: From a form of an obsolete primary chao (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval).

BDAG.en: chasm (lit. ‘a yawning’) of the unbridgeable space betw. Abraham and the place of torture
BDAG.pt: abismo (lit. ‘uma abertura’), o espaço intransponível entre Abraão e o lugar de tormento

DEFINITION: a lip, mouth, shore, edge, brink; meton: language, dialect.
ORIGIN: From a form of the same as chasma; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water).

BDAG.en: lip (used in speaking); shore, bank (of a river or the sea).
BDAG.pt: lábio (usado ao falar); margem, ribeira (de um rio ou do mar).

DEFINITION: to expose to winter cold, to drive with storm.
ORIGIN: From the same as cheimon; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale.

DEFINITION: a storm-brook, a winter torrent.
ORIGIN: From the base of cheimon and rheo; a storm-runlet, i.e. Winter-torrent.

BDAG.en: a stream of water that flows abundantly in the winter, winter torrent, ravine, wadi
BDAG.pt: um riacho de água que flui abundantemente no inverno, torrente de inverno, ravina, uádi

DEFINITION: a storm, tempest; winter, the rainy season.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of cheo (to pour; akin to the base of chasma through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. Winter.

BDAG.en: 1 stormy weather, bad weather, storm 2 the season of bad weather, winter
BDAG.pt: 1 tempo tempestuoso, mau tempo, tempestade 2 a estação de mau tempo, inverno

DEFINITION: the hand.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the base of cheimon in the sense of its congener the base of chasma (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument).

BDAG.en: hand 2 an acting agent, hand (of), fig. ext. of 1. In this sense the focus is on the person or thing as the source of an activity.
BDAG.pt: mão 2 um agente atuante, mão (de), extensão figurada de 1. Neste sentido, o foco está na pessoa ou coisa como fonte de uma atividade.

DEFINITION: to lead by the hand.
ORIGIN: From cheiragogos; to be a hand-leader, i.e. To guide (a blind person).

BDAG.en: take/lead by the hand
BDAG.pt: pegar/guiar pela mão

DEFINITION: one who leads a helpless person by the hand.
ORIGIN: From cheir and a reduplicated form of ago; a hand-leader, i.e. Personal conductor (of a blind person).
USAGE: some to lead by the hand.

BDAG.en: one who leads another by the hand, leader
BDAG.pt: aquele que conduz outro pela mão, guia

DEFINITION: a (handwritten) document, legal note, bond.
ORIGIN: Neuter of a compound of cheir and grapho; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. A manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)).

BDAG.en: a hand-written document, specif. a certificate of indebtedness, account, record of debts
BDAG.pt: um documento escrito à mão, especificamente um certificado de dívida, conta, registro de débitos

DEFINITION: done or made with hands, artificial.
ORIGIN: From cheir and a derivative of poieo; manufactured, i.e. Of human construction.

BDAG.en: made by human hands, of buildings (especially temples)
BDAG.pt: feito por mãos humanas, de construções (especialmente templos)

DEFINITION: to elect by show of hands, choose by vote, appoint.
ORIGIN: From a comparative of cheir and teino (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint.

BDAG.en: to elect or choose someone for definite offices or tasks; to appoint, install (when used of apostles choosing elders)
BDAG.pt: eleger ou escolher alguém para cargos ou tarefas definidas; nomear, instalar (quando usado de apóstolos escolhendo presbíteros)

DEFINITION: worse, more severe.
ORIGIN: Irregular comparative of kakos; from an obsolete equivalent cheres (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally).

BDAG.en: worse, more severe (comparative of κακός)
BDAG.pt: pior, mais severo (comparativo de κακός)

DEFINITION: Cherubim, heavenly beings who serve God.
ORIGIN: Plural of Hebrew origin (kruwb); "cherubim" (i.e. Cherubs or kerubim).

DEFINITION: a widow.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of chasma through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively.

BDAG.en: a woman whose husband has died, widow (also referring to a special class of widows in the church)
BDAG.pt: mulher cujo marido morreu, viúva (também referindo-se a uma classe especial de viúvas na igreja)

DEFINITION: yesterday.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto.

BDAG.en: yesterday
BDAG.pt: ontem

DEFINITION: a thousand, the number one thousand.
ORIGIN: From chilioi; one thousand ("chiliad").

BDAG.en: a group of a thousand, a thousand
BDAG.pt: um grupo de mil, mil

DEFINITION: a commander of a thousand men, a military tribune.
ORIGIN: From chilioi and archo; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. Colonel.

BDAG.en: military tribune, the commander of a cohort (roughly equivalent to major or colonel)
BDAG.pt: tribuno militar, o comandante de uma coorte (aproximadamente equivalente a major ou coronel)

DEFINITION: a thousand.
ORIGIN: Plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand.

BDAG.en: a thousand
BDAG.pt: mil

DEFINITION: Chios (modern Scio), an important island in the Aegean Sea, off the west central coast of Asia Minor.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean.

BDAG.en: Chios, an island in the Aegean Sea
BDAG.pt: Quios, uma ilha no Mar Egeu

DEFINITION: a tunic, garment, undergarment.
ORIGIN: Of foreign origin (kthoneth); a tunic or shirt.

BDAG.en: tunic, shirt, a garment worn next to the skin
BDAG.pt: túnica, camisa, uma veste usada junto à pele

DEFINITION: snow.
ORIGIN: Perhaps akin to the base of chasma (chalao) or cheimon (as descending or empty); snow.

BDAG.en: snow as symbol of perfect whiteness
BDAG.pt: neve como símbolo de brancura perfeita

DEFINITION: a short cloak, worn by military officers and soldiers.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a military cloak.

BDAG.en: a loose outer garment worn by men, then gener. a military cloak, mantle
BDAG.pt: uma veste exterior solta usada por homens, depois, geralmente, uma capa ou manto militar

DEFINITION: to mock, scoff, jest, jeer.
ORIGIN: From a derivative probably of cheilos; to throw out the lip, i.e. Jeer at.

BDAG.en: to engage in mockery, mock, sneer, scoff; to make fun of maliciously, mock, scoff at, sneer at
BDAG.pt: engajar-se em zombaria, zombar, escarnecer, ridicularizar; zombar maliciosamente, caçoar, escarnecer

DEFINITION: warm, tepid; of persons: lukewarm.
ORIGIN: From chlio (to warm); tepid.

BDAG.en: lukewarm
BDAG.pt: morno

DEFINITION: Chloe, probably with business connections either in Corinth or in Ephesus or in both.
ORIGIN: Feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloe, a Christian female.

BDAG.en: Chloe (an otherwise unknown woman)
BDAG.pt: Clóe (uma mulher até então desconhecida)

DEFINITION: green, pale green.
ORIGIN: From the same as Chloe; greenish, i.e. Verdant, dun-colored.

BDAG.en: yellowish-green, (light) green of plants; pale, greenish gray
BDAG.pt: amarelado-esverdeado, verde (claro) de plantas; pálido, cinza-esverdeado

DEFINITION: abbreviation for six hundred sixty-six.
ORIGIN: The 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (stigma as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60, and 6; 666 as a numeral.

DEFINITION: earthy, made of earth.
ORIGIN: From choos; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene.

BDAG.en: made of earth/dust, earthy
BDAG.pt: feito de terra/poeira, terrestre

DEFINITION: a choenix (a dry measure of less than a quart).
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a choenix or certain dry measure.

BDAG.en: a dry measure (for grain), approximately equivalent to one quart
BDAG.pt: medida seca (para grãos), aproximadamente equivalente a um quarto de galão

DEFINITION: a swine, hog, sow.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a hog.

BDAG.en: young swine, swine generally
BDAG.pt: suíno jovem, porco em geral

DEFINITION: to be melancholy, mad, angry.
ORIGIN: From chole; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric").

BDAG.en: be angry
BDAG.pt: estar zangado, enfurecer-se

DEFINITION: gall (a bitter herb).
ORIGIN: Feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as Chloe (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.).

BDAG.en: gall, bile; (figuratively) bitter gall (in idiom)
BDAG.pt: fel, bílis; (figurativamente) fel amargo (em expressão idiomática)

DEFINITION: earth, soil, dust.
ORIGIN: From the base of cheimon; a heap (as poured out), i.e. Rubbish; loose dirt.

BDAG.en: soil, dust (of the dust of the road or scattered in grief)
BDAG.pt: terra, poeira (da estrada ou espalhada em luto)

DEFINITION: Chorazin, a city of Galilee.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine.

BDAG.en: Chorazin (a place in Galilee)
BDAG.pt: Corazim (um lugar na Galileia)

DEFINITION: to lead a chorus (i.e. a group of performers), to defray the cost of a chorus.
ORIGIN: From a compound of choros and ago; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish.

BDAG.en: defray the expenses of something, provide, supply (originally: lead a chorus or pay its expenses)
BDAG.pt: arcar com as despesas de algo, prover, suprir (originalmente: liderar um coro ou pagar suas despesas)

DEFINITION: a dance, dancing.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. Round dance ("choir".

BDAG.en: rhythmic movements to the accompaniment of music, (choral) dance, dancing; a company of dancers, troop, band; a group of singers, chorus, choir
BDAG.pt: movimentos rítmicos ao som de música, dança (coral), ato de dançar; um grupo de dançarinos, tropa, banda; um grupo de cantores, coro

DEFINITION: to feed, fatten, fill, satisfy.
ORIGIN: From chortos; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance).

BDAG.en: to fill with food, feed, fill; to experience inward satisfaction in something, be satisfied
BDAG.pt: encher de comida, alimentar, fartar; experimentar satisfação interior em algo, estar satisfeito

DEFINITION: food, sustenance, provision.
ORIGIN: From chortazo; forage, i.e. Food.

BDAG.en: food for humans (pluralized, usually for animal fodder)
BDAG.pt: alimento para humanos (pluralizado, geralmente para forragem de animais)

DEFINITION: grass, herbage, growing grain, hay.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation.

BDAG.en: grass, hay; stalks of grain in their early, grass-like stages
BDAG.pt: erva, feno; caules de grãos em seus estágios iniciais, semelhantes a grama

DEFINITION: Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod.

BDAG.en: Chuza (an official of Herod Antipas)
BDAG.pt: Cuzas (um oficial de Herodes Antipas)

DEFINITION: to use, make use of, deal with, take advantage of.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from cheir, to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner.

BDAG.en: use, make use of, employ; act, proceed; treat a person in a certain way
BDAG.pt: usar, fazer uso de, empregar; agir, proceder; tratar uma pessoa de certa maneira

DEFINITION: to lend.
ORIGIN: Probably the same as the base of chraomai; to loan.

BDAG.en: lend (see κίχρημι)
BDAG.pt: emprestar (ver κίχρημι)

DEFINITION: need, necessity, business.
ORIGIN: From the base of chraomai or chre; employment, i.e. An affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution.
USAGE: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want.

BDAG.en: 1. that which should happen or be supplied because it is needed, need, what should be; 2. that which is lacking and needed, need, lack, want, difficulty; 3. the thing that is lacking and (therefore) necessary, necessary thing; 4. an activity that is needed, office, duty, service
BDAG.pt: 1. aquilo que deve acontecer ou ser fornecido porque é necessário, necessidade, o que deve ser; 2. aquilo que falta e é necessário, necessidade, falta, carência, dificuldade; 3. a coisa que falta e (portanto) é necessária, coisa necessária; 4. uma atividade necessária, ofício, dever, serviço.

DEFINITION: a debtor.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of chrao and opheiletes; a loan-ower, i.e. Indebted person.

BDAG.en: debtor (variant spelling of χρεοφειλέτης)
BDAG.pt: devedor (variante de χρεοφειλέτης)

DEFINITION: it is necessary, proper, fitting.
ORIGIN: Third person singular of the same as chraomai or chrao used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be.

BDAG.en: it is necessary, it ought
BDAG.pt: é necessário, deve-se.

DEFINITION: to need, have need of, want, desire.
ORIGIN: From chreia; to make (i.e. Have) necessity, i.e. Be in want of.

BDAG.en: (have) need (of)
BDAG.pt: (ter) necessidade (de).

DEFINITION: a thing that one uses or needs.
ORIGIN: Something useful or needed, i.e. Wealth, price.

BDAG.en: wealth in gener., property, wealth, means (pl.); any kind of currency, money (mostly pl., more rarely sing.)
BDAG.pt: riqueza em geral, propriedade, posses, recursos (plural); qualquer tipo de moeda, dinheiro (principalmente no plural, mais raramente no singular)

DEFINITION: (originally: to transact business), (a) act. of God: to warn; pass: to be warned by God (probably in response to an inquiry as to one's duty), (b) (to take a name from public business, hence) to receive a name, be publicly called.
ORIGIN: From chrema; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of chraomai), i.e. Divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of chreia) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title.
USAGE: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.

BDAG.en: impart a divine message, make known a divine injunction/warning; receive a warning; someth. is revealed or prophesied; to take/bear a name/title, to go under the name of, be called/named, be identified as
BDAG.pt: transmitir uma mensagem divina, tornar conhecido um preceito/aviso divino; receber um aviso; algo é revelado ou profetizado; assumir/carregar um nome/título, ser chamado/designado, ser identificado como

DEFINITION: a divine response, an oracle.
ORIGIN: From chrematizo; a divine response or revelation.

BDAG.en: a divine statement, answer (of a dream)
BDAG.pt: uma declaração divina, resposta (de um sonho)

DEFINITION: useful, profitable.
ORIGIN: From chresis; serviceable.

BDAG.en: useful, beneficial, advantageous
BDAG.pt: útil, benéfico, vantajoso.

DEFINITION: use (as in a sexual sense).
ORIGIN: From chraomai; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body).

BDAG.en: 1. the state of being used, use, usage; 2. the state of being useful, usefulness; 3. state of intimate involvement w. a pers., relations, function, esp. of sexual intercourse
BDAG.pt: 1. o estado de ser usado, uso, utilização; 2. o estado de ser útil, utilidade; 3. estado de envolvimento íntimo com uma pessoa, relações, função, especialmente de relação sexual.

DEFINITION: to be kind (full of service to others), gentle.
ORIGIN: Middle voice from chrestos; to show oneself useful, i.e. Act benevolently.

BDAG.en: be kind, loving, merciful (to someone)
BDAG.pt: ser bondoso, amoroso, misericordioso (para com alguém)

DEFINITION: a kind address; in a bad sense: plausible speaking.
ORIGIN: From a compound of chrestos and lego; fair speech, i.e. Plausibility.

BDAG.en: smooth, plausible speech
BDAG.pt: discurso suave, plausível

DEFINITION: useful, gentle, pleasant, kind.
ORIGIN: From chraomai; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals).

BDAG.en: generally ‘useful, beneficial’; pert. to that which causes no discomfort, easy; pert. to meeting a relatively high standard of value, fine; pert. to being morally good and benevolent, reputable, kind, loving, benevolent; (subst.) the quality of beneficence, kindness
BDAG.pt: geralmente 'útil, benéfico'; referente ao que não causa desconforto, fácil; referente ao cumprimento de um padrão de valor relativamente alto, bom; referente a ser moralmente bom e benevolente, respeitável, bondoso, amoroso, benevolente; (substantivo) a qualidade de beneficência, bondade

DEFINITION: goodness, uprightness, kindness, gentleness.
ORIGIN: From chrestos; usefulness, i.e. Morally, excellence (in character or demeanor).

BDAG.en: generally ‘usefulness, helpfulness’; uprightness in one’s relations with others, uprightness; the quality of being helpful or beneficial, goodness, kindness, generosity (of humans or God)
BDAG.pt: geralmente 'utilidade, prestatividade'; retidão nas relações com os outros, retidão; a qualidade de ser prestativo ou benéfico, bondade, gentileza, generosidade (de humanos ou de Deus)

DEFINITION: an anointing, unction.
ORIGIN: From chrio; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit.

BDAG.en: anointing, usually taken to mean anointing with the Holy Spirit.
BDAG.pt: unção, geralmente entendido como a unção com o Espírito Santo.

DEFINITION: a Christian.
ORIGIN: From Christos; a Christian, i.e. Follower of Christ.

BDAG.en: one who is associated w. Christ, Christ-partisan, Christian.
BDAG.pt: aquele que está associado a Cristo, partidário de Cristo, cristão.

DEFINITION: Anointed One; the Messiah, the Christ.
ORIGIN: From chrio; Anointed One, i.e. The Messiah, an epithet of Jesus.

BDAG.en: fulfiller of Israelite expectation of a deliverer, the Anointed One, the Messiah, the Christ (appellation); the personal name ascribed to Jesus, Christ.
BDAG.pt: cumpridor da expectativa israelita de um libertador, o Ungido, o Messias, o Cristo (apelação); o nome pessoal atribuído a Jesus, Cristo.

DEFINITION: to anoint, consecrate by anointing.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to chraomai through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service.

BDAG.en: to anoint, in our literature only in a fig. sense of an anointing by God setting a person apart for special service under divine direction; God anoints, Jesus the Christ, the prophets, the apostles or all Christians.
BDAG.pt: ungir, em nossa literatura apenas em sentido figurado de uma unção por Deus que aparta uma pessoa para um serviço especial sob direção divina; Deus unge, Jesus o Cristo, os profetas, os apóstolos ou todos os cristãos.

DEFINITION: to delay, tarry, linger, spend time.
ORIGIN: From chronos; to take time, i.e. Linger.

BDAG.en: to continue in a state or place, stay; to extend a state or an activity beyond an expected time, take time, linger, fail to come or stay away for a long time.
BDAG.pt: continuar em um estado ou lugar, permanecer; estender um estado ou uma atividade além do tempo esperado, demorar, tardar, deixar de vir ou ficar ausente por muito tempo.

DEFINITION: time, a particular time, season.
ORIGIN: Of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from kairos, which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from aion, which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay.
USAGE: + years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while.

BDAG.en: an indefinite period of time during which some activity or event takes place, time, period of time; a point of time consisting of an occasion for some event or activity, time, occasion; a period during which something is delayed, respite, delay.
BDAG.pt: um período de tempo indefinido durante o qual alguma atividade ou evento ocorre, tempo, período de tempo; um ponto no tempo que constitui uma ocasião para algum evento ou atividade, tempo, ocasião; um período durante o qual algo é adiado, um prazo, uma demora.

DEFINITION: to waste time, spend time, delay.
ORIGIN: From a presumed compound of chronos and the base of tribos; to be a time-wearer, i.e. To procrastinate (linger).

BDAG.en: to experience a duration of time, spend time, lose time.
BDAG.pt: experimentar uma duração de tempo, gastar tempo, perder tempo.

DEFINITION: golden, made of gold, adorned with gold.
ORIGIN: From chrusos; made of gold.

BDAG.en: made of/adorned with gold, golden; golden in color or appearance.
BDAG.pt: feito de/adornado com ouro, dourado; de cor ou aparência dourada.

DEFINITION: a piece of gold, golden ornament.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of chrusos; a golden article, i.e. Gold plating, ornament, or coin.

BDAG.en: gold as raw material, gold; object made of gold or adorned with gold: gold ornaments, jewelry; coined gold, money.
BDAG.pt: ouro como matéria-prima, ouro; objeto feito de ouro ou adornado com ouro: ornamentos de ouro, joias; ouro cunhado, dinheiro.

DEFINITION: adorned with a gold ring.
ORIGIN: From chrusos and daktulios; gold-ringed, i.e. Wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry.

BDAG.en: with a gold ring / rings on one’s finger(s).
BDAG.pt: com um ou mais anéis de ouro no(s) dedo(s).

DEFINITION: a topaz, a gem with a bright yellow color.
ORIGIN: From chrusos and lithos; gold-stone, i.e. A yellow gem ("chrysolite").

BDAG.en: probably a yellowish precious stone, yellow topaz, chrysolite.
BDAG.pt: provavelmente uma pedra preciosa amarelada, topázio amarelo, crisólito.

DEFINITION: a chrysoprase, gem of a golden-greenish color.
ORIGIN: From chrusos and prason (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase").

BDAG.en: a precious stone of golden-green color, chrysoprase
BDAG.pt: uma pedra preciosa de cor verde-dourada, crisoprásio

DEFINITION: gold, anything made of gold, a gold coin.
ORIGIN: Perhaps from the base of chraomai (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin.

BDAG.en: gold as raw material, gold; objects made of gold or adorned with gold: gold ornaments; gold thing, of a cult image; coined gold, money.
BDAG.pt: ouro como matéria-prima, ouro; objetos feitos de ouro ou adornados com ouro: ornamentos de ouro; coisa de ouro, de uma imagem de culto; ouro cunhado, dinheiro.

DEFINITION: to gild, to cover with gold.
ORIGIN: From chrusos; to gild, i.e. Bespangle with golden ornaments.

BDAG.en: to make golden, gild, adorn with gold.
BDAG.pt: fazer de ouro, dourar, adornar com ouro.

DEFINITION: the surface of the body, skin.
ORIGIN: Probably akin to the base of chraomai through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin).

BDAG.en: surface of the body, skin.
BDAG.pt: superfície do corpo, pele.

DEFINITION: lame, deprived of a foot, limping.
ORIGIN: Apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. Limping.

BDAG.en: lame, crippled
BDAG.pt: coxo, aleijado

DEFINITION: (a) a country or region, (b) the land, as opposed to the sea, (c) the country, distinct from town, (d) plur: fields.
ORIGIN: Feminine of a derivative of the base of chasma through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. A space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants).
USAGE: coast, county, fields, ground, land, region. Compare topos.

BDAG.en: country, land; (dry) land in contrast to the sea, land; a portion of land area, district, region, place; the open country in contrast to the city, country; land used for farming, field, cultivated land; a place or position in which an entity is located, place
BDAG.pt: país, terra; terra (seca) em contraste com o mar, terra; porção de área de terra, distrito, região, lugar; campo aberto em contraste com a cidade, campo; terra usada para agricultura, campo, terra cultivada; um lugar ou posição onde uma entidade está localizada, lugar

DEFINITION: (lit: to make room, hence) (a) to have room for, receive, contain, (b) to make room for by departing, go, make progress, turn myself.
ORIGIN: From chora; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively).
USAGE: come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive.

BDAG.en: to make movement from one place or position to another, go, go out/away, reach; to make an advance in movement, be in motion, go forward, make progress; to have room for, hold, contain; fig. of open-heartedness, grasp mentally, accept, comprehend, understand; permit, allow for (of a native condition)
BDAG.pt: mover-se de um lugar ou posição para outro, ir, sair/afastar-se, alcançar; avançar em movimento, estar em movimento, progredir; ter espaço para, conter, comportar; figurado de abertura de coração, apreender mentalmente, aceitar, compreender; permitir, dar margem para (de uma condição natural)

DEFINITION: (a) to separate, put apart, (b) mid. or pass: to separate myself, depart, withdraw.
ORIGIN: From chora; to place room between, i.e. Part; reflexively, to go away.

BDAG.en: to cause separation through use of space between, divide, separate, act.; to separate by departing from someone, separate, leave, pass. freq. in act. sense (separate (oneself), be separated (of divorce), be taken away, take one’s departure, go away)
BDAG.pt: causar separação pelo uso de espaço intermediário, dividir, separar, agir.; separar-se ao partir de alguém, separar, deixar, passar. frequente no sentido ativo (separar-(se), ser separado (de divórcio), ser levado, retirar-se, ir embora)

DEFINITION: a place, piece of land, field, property, estate.
ORIGIN: Diminutive of chora; a spot or plot of ground.
USAGE: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession.

BDAG.en: a piece of land other than a populated area, place, piece of land, field; a limited geographical area, (a city and its) environs
BDAG.pt: um pedaço de terra fora de uma área povoada, lugar, pedaço de terra, campo; uma área geográfica limitada, (uma cidade e seus) arredores

DEFINITION: apart from, separately from; without.
ORIGIN: Adverb from chora; at a space, i.e. Separately or apart from (often as preposition).

BDAG.en: used as an adv.: separately, apart, by itself; used as prep. w. gen.: without, apart from, independent(ly of) (separated from someone, far from someone, without someone; without making use of something, without expressing or practicing something; without possessing something, apart from the presence of something; without relation to or connection with something, independently of something; apart from)
BDAG.pt: usado como adv.: separadamente, à parte, por si só; usado como preposição com genitivo: sem, exceto, independentemente (de) (separado de alguém, longe de alguém, sem alguém; sem usar algo, sem expressar ou praticar algo; sem possuir algo, à parte da presença de algo; sem relação ou conexão com algo, independentemente de algo; à parte de)

DEFINITION: the north-west wind, and the quarter of the sky from which it comes.
ORIGIN: Of Latin origin; the north-west wind.

BDAG.en: an undefined area or location, place
BDAG.pt: uma área ou localização indefinida, lugar

DEFINITION: to sing, sing psalms; earlier: to play on a stringed instrument.
ORIGIN: Probably strengthened from psao (to rub or touch the surface; compare psocho); to twitch or twang, i.e. To play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes).

BDAG.en: to sing songs of praise, with or without instrumental accompaniment, sing, sing praise
BDAG.pt: cantar hinos de louvor, com ou sem acompanhamento instrumental, cantar, cantar louvor

DEFINITION: a psalm, song of praise, the Hebrew book of Psalms.
ORIGIN: From psallo; a set piece of music, i.e. A sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms.

BDAG.en: song of praise, psalm in accordance with OT usage
BDAG.pt: cântico de louvor, salmo de acordo com o uso do Antigo Testamento

DEFINITION: a false brother, pretend Christian.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and adephos; a spurious brother, i.e. Pretended associate.

BDAG.en: one who pretends to be a fellow-believer, but whose claim is belied by conduct toward fellow-believers, false brother, false member
BDAG.pt: aquele que finge ser um companheiro de fé, mas cuja alegação é desmentida pela conduta para com os companheiros de fé, falso irmão, falso membro

DEFINITION: a false or pretended apostle.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and apostolos; a spurious apostle, i.e. Pretended pracher.

BDAG.en: one who claims to be an apostle without the divine commission necessary for the work, false/spurious/bogus apostle
BDAG.pt: aquele que se diz apóstolo sem a comissão divina necessária para a obra, falso/espúrio/falso apóstolo

DEFINITION: false, deceitful, lying, untrue.
ORIGIN: From pseudomai; untrue, i.e. Erroneous, deceitful, wicked.

BDAG.en: pert. to being contrary to the truth, false, lying; subst. liar
BDAG.pt: relativo a ser contrário à verdade, falso, mentiroso; substantivo: mentiroso

DEFINITION: a false teacher, teacher of false things.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and didaskalos; a spurious teacher, i.e. Propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine.

BDAG.en: false/bogus teacher, quack teacher, of someone in the Christian community who pretends to be a qualified instructor, but whose teaching is contrary to the generally accepted tradition
BDAG.pt: falso/inepto mestre, charlatão instrutor, de alguém na comunidade cristã que finge ser um instrutor qualificado, mas cujo ensino é contrário à tradição geralmente aceita

DEFINITION: false-speaking, speaking lies.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and lego; mendacious, i.e. Promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine.

BDAG.en: speaking falsely, lying; subst. liars
BDAG.pt: falando falsamente, mentindo; substantivo: mentirosos

DEFINITION: to deceive, lie, speak falsely.
ORIGIN: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood.

BDAG.en: to tell a falsehood, lie abs.; to attempt to deceive by lying, tell lies to, impose upon
BDAG.pt: dizer uma falsidade, mentir absolutamente; tentar enganar mentindo, mentir para, impor a

DEFINITION: a false witness.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and a kindred form of martus; a spurious witness, i.e. Bearer of untrue testimony.

BDAG.en: one who gives false testimony, a false witness
BDAG.pt: aquele que dá falso testemunho, uma falsa testemunha

DEFINITION: to bear false witness, give false testimony.
ORIGIN: From pseudomartur; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. Offer falsehood in evidence.

BDAG.en: bear false witness, give false testimony
BDAG.pt: dar falso testemunho, prestar falso testemunho

DEFINITION: false witness, false testimony.
ORIGIN: From pseudomartur; untrue testimony.

BDAG.en: false witness
BDAG.pt: falso testemunho

DEFINITION: a false prophet; one who in God's name teaches what is false.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and prophetes; a spurious prophet, i.e. Pretended foreteller or religious impostor.

BDAG.en: one who falsely claims to be a prophet of God or who prophesies falsely, false/bogus prophet
BDAG.pt: aquele que falsamente afirma ser um profeta de Deus ou que profetiza falsamente, falso/espúrio profeta

DEFINITION: a lie, falsehood, untruth; false religion.
ORIGIN: From pseudomai; a falsehood.

BDAG.en: a lie, falsehood
BDAG.pt: uma mentira, falsidade

DEFINITION: a false Christ, pretended Messiah.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and Christos; a spurious Messiah.

BDAG.en: one who, in lying fashion, gives himself out to be the Anointed One, a bogus Messiah
BDAG.pt: aquele que, de modo mentiroso, se apresenta como o Ungido, um falso Messias

DEFINITION: under a false name, falsely called.
ORIGIN: From pseudes and onoma; untruly named.

BDAG.en: pert. to using a membership name falsely, falsely bearing a name, falsely called of the γνῶσις of heterodox Christians
BDAG.pt: relativo ao uso falso de um nome de adesão, falsamente ostentando um nome, falsamente chamado no sentido do conhecimento (gnosis) de cristãos heterodoxos

DEFINITION: a falsehood, lie, untruthfulness.
ORIGIN: From pseudomai; a fabrication, i.e. Falsehood.

BDAG.en: ‘lie, falsehood’ in our lit. in the sense engagement in lying, lying, untruthfulness, un-dependability
BDAG.pt: 'mentira, falsidade' no nosso léxico no sentido de envolvimento em mentira, mentir, não veracidade, inconfiabilidade

DEFINITION: a liar, deceiver.
ORIGIN: From pseudomai (g5574); a falsifier.

BDAG.en: liar
BDAG.pt: mentiroso

DEFINITION: to feel, touch, handle; to feel after, grope for.
ORIGIN: From the base of psallo (compare psephos); to manipulate, i.e. Verify by contact; figuratively, to search for.

BDAG.en: feel (about for), grope after; touch by feeling and handling, touch, handle; look for someth. in uncertain fashion, to feel around for, grope for
BDAG.pt: sentir (procurando), tatear; tocar por sentir e manusear, tocar, manusear; procurar algo de forma incerta, tatear procurando

DEFINITION: to reckon, compute, calculate.
ORIGIN: From psephos; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute.

BDAG.en: to add up digits and calculate a total, count (up), calculate, reckon ('w. pebbles'); to probe a number for its meaning, interpret, figure out
BDAG.pt: somar dígitos e calcular um total, contar, calcular, contar ('com seixos'); sondar um número quanto ao seu significado, interpretar, descobrir

DEFINITION: (a) a pebble, small stone, (b) hence, from their use in voting: a vote.
ORIGIN: From the same as pselaphao; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote.

BDAG.en: a pebble used in voting: a black one for conviction, a white one for acquittal, voting-pebble; a pebble serving as an amulet, amulet
BDAG.pt: um seixo usado na votação: um preto para condenação, um branco para absolvição, seixo de votação; um seixo servindo como amuleto, amuleto

DEFINITION: a whispering, secret slandering.
ORIGIN: From a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to pseudomai); whispering, i.e. Secret detraction.

BDAG.en: derogatory information about someone that is offered in a tone of confidentiality, (secret) gossip, tale-bearing
BDAG.pt: informação depreciativa sobre alguém oferecida em tom de confidencialidade, fofoca (secreta), maledicência

DEFINITION: a whisperer, secret slanderer.
